c.m: Very confusing. Makes 50 minute lectures feel like three hours. Make sure to go review the lecture contents after class.

Tough exams (both in terms of the quantity of details tested and the level of application), but he's very fair and explained concepts clearly in lectures. Funny guy. He makes it pretty clear what's important for exams, but his questions can be a little more applied than students are used to.

So bad. Direct quote from him in class : “I'm not going to answer that question because I have a tendency to say things that may confuse the students more” -moon. He pretty much summed it up. Professor Moon was a lovely professor. You could tell he cared for the students and he worked hard to explain things clearly, which he did. His midterm and final questions were fair as they followed the content and example questions he presented in class.

His section was well taught and he always did his best to go into detail. Some of his questions might seem weird at first but doing all of his weekly exercises and textbook exercises should be more than enough to do well for his section.

Moon is one of my favourite professors at McGill! His section of the course is pretty heavy, with many different proteins to memorize. Like with other biology courses, almost anything he talks about, even if only mentioned briefly, is testable material unless otherwise stated.

Prof. Moon is a little unclear sometimes but rewatching the lectures will make things more clear. His test questions were pretty difficult and detail oriented on the midterm but more fair on the final. He makes a lot of jokes and lectures are enjoyable to attend.
He is a great professor. He has a nice personality and makes a lot of jokes. He is clear and will go over something again if people don't understand it. Definitely recommend.
Only had him for online classes so I never saw him in person, but his slides and explanations were clear and not-at-all confusing. Would recommend.

Easiest class at McGill, got a 98 and didn't go a single time. So great to take when you need to be able to manage workload from other classes. No exams or tests just easy projects. The Prof is super super friendly and TAs are very reasonable.

Very passionate not only about the course, but about her teaching. However, lots of the theories we discussed that seemed to invite critical discussion we did not actually end up discussing. I enjoy feeling challenged by a course, and did not really get that in RELG 271. Very kind professor, and I still enjoyed the course!
One of the best profs I've had so far, has such a refreshing outlook on the content and gives creative assignments.

This was hands down my favorite class at McGill. The readings and assignments were engaging, the tests were chill, and overall the material was super interesting. The final project was so much fun and Prof Malladi is not only a great professor but also super kind and accomodating!

She is one of the easiest to reach and most reasonable profs Ive had in my time at McGill. You can tell she's well-versed in what shes teaching and cares about students. Talking to her if anyone is unsure about guidelines usually helps sort it out. One of the best I have had here

Professor Malladi is very friendly. She is willing to work with you and listen to any of your concerns, even though this is a big lecture class. She expects your papers to be at university level. However, she is always willing to help. She breaks down the large assignments so it is not all one large paper due at once. I would definitely recommend

One of my favorite classes. Having her for a small class probably contributed to the good experience because a lot of our learning was through class discussion on the material. Everyone who took the class was very positive towards it and she incorporated class feedback; she really wants to be a good teacher. LOTS of readings, though, so be aware.

Although she is flexible outside of class, her form of lecturing is very traditional and boring. The assignment instructions were always unclear to the point that many of us were solely relying on our TA to help us understand anything of what was being asked.

She's unclear as to what she wants in assignments, gives 2 lines of instructions (example: write a paper), and then students get penalized. Not detailed as to what she wants in papers, which causes us to lose marks. but she is a very nice person, she's sweet!

RELG 271

Lectures are long and unclear as Prof. Malladi rambles for an hour and a half about topics that don't connect well to the overall theme of the class. 

Disorganized classes. Lectures slides aren't posted beforehand, no proper assignment instructions. 

Would not recommend.
Midterms are not too hard. Truly tries to make content engaging and understandable.

Prof has interesting experience and is helpful. Very willing to explain concepts in different ways to help students understand.. but it helps to be at least vaguely familiar with probability and statistics. I enjoyed the group project.
Nice teacher. ok class. too much work
Learned a lot in this class. Prof was accessible outside of class hours and was really passionate about his course. It made me want to do more statistics-related courses.
Learned what I was lacking in math to feel confident about my quantitative skills. Lot of assignments but you also learn a lot from them. Would take again.

Prof Erlich is a great lecturer. He is always energetic, remaining funny and engaging while explaining complex topics. His slides are incredibly well organized and easy to follow. He's very helpful during office hours. The goat

Aaron is caring, knowledgeable, and smart. Many 1Ls find ILT challenging because it differs from what they have previously known / learning in other courses. I highly recommend Professor Mills for ILT. He teaches with heart and genuinely cares about his students' learning. His assignments are flexible and allow you to get creative while exploring concepts you're most interested in. He's a fair grader, but like all law courses, the B curve is real.

I still can't believe how Mills has managed to distill Anishinaabe Constitutionalism into a single semester, making it so accessible. Everything was thoughtfully planned from the carefully chosen readings to the course structure. Mills is also very accessible outside of class. I feel very grateful to have had the chance to learn from him.

I loved this class! It was structured very thoughtfully and the lectures were super engaging. Mills was also very accessible outside of class and open with questions in office hours. I would recommend everyone take this class if they have a chance!
A very hypocritical professor who grades arbitrarily. If you're not his favorite, prepare yourself for a B or B- (he said so himself!).

A disappointing professor, whose interesting perspectives cannot save a deep-rooted and unwarranted wickedness. This Professor grades examinations entirely arbitrarily; abandon hopes of stability. One of the best classes of my life. I learned a lot.

He is definitely really smart and a great lecturer, will tell you what to expect on the final. I just didn't like this class. He is kinda harsh though and a tough grader.

Lord Vetta is an absolute gem, comp360 is a difficult but highly rewording class. Would highly recommend!

Very hard course, but seems to care about her students.  Extremely smart woman who will bring forward issues that you had never thought about.  Be ready to put in a lot of work, but learn a lot.

One of the best professors I've had. He has structured the course in a way where stress levels are low compared to other courses. Clear lectures and interesting material. The easiest 300 level courses in electrical engineering. Mainly because of the way he structured the course. A very caring professor as well. Makes sure the entire class understood. This class is primarily for the group programming project you're gonna do the whole semester. Apart from that, the material is random soft.eng. stuff which he makes really boring and I skipped most of the lectures.

Prof Farah is very interesting and has a lot of stuff to say... His classes tend to be super long but what's great is that everything is recorded. He likes to engage with his students, create conversations, ask for their opinions, etc. Although the final was around 12 pages long, the rest of the course is pretty light and overall worth taking.

This class was interesting and for the most part has pretty fair work load. His lectures are great and he's a funny guy. Only had to write a few 500 word essays, but there was a 11 page final paper. He's kinda a tough grader though, and the first grade you get will probably be what you finish with.

Farah really tries to be fair and nice towards his students. He also tries to make students work on something they like: we had a great deal of freedom in our assignments which was really enjoyable. However, I regret that Farah is such a tough grader. If you had done perfectly the job, it was still not enough to get a good grade! Such a hard class

Engaging professor. Going to class is basically mandatory, but he makes it entertaining enough. Lots and lots of pop quizzes, but generally an easy enough course. I really enjoyed it, and would take another class with him again.

Ce prof est très engagé et sympa. Ses évaluations sont très variables dans leur niveau de difficulté, mais sont en général assez difficiles. Farah est amusant, passionné et un peu bizarre, pas toujours professionnel, mais en bref, un excellent professeur. Je prendrais ce cours plutôt pour lui que pour la matière (bien, mais pas fascinant).

Ce prof est fantastique. J'ai rigolé pendant tout le semestre. Très intéressant et connait super bien sa matière. Je recommande fortement ce court. Les évaluations ne sont pas difficiles si vous lisez les livres et allez aux cours.

Super bon cours, trÃ¨s intÃ©ressant. Il est un peu picky sur les examens mais c'est pas impossible de rÃ©ussir avec lui. Super pour des Ã©tudiants voulant en apprendre plis sur la littÃ©rature. Je recommande Ã  100%!!

Cours bien structuré, prof très sympathique, captivant et attentionné, toujours disponible en cas de besoin.  Cependant les explications données en cours sont parfois floues et les objectifs des devoirs maison et des examens peuvent manquer de clarté et de précision.
awesome teacher, very funny !
Poor lecturer, asks ambiguous questions and stubbornly refuses to consider the student's perspective.

no introduction to any of the material; never know what he is talking about; jumps from topic to topic; explains experiment after experiment without prefacing why or what they were looking for or how it is even relevant to the course- do not take this class if you don't have to.... will save hours of frustration.

Hardest exam I have ever taken. The material itself isn't that bad, but his question style is just awful. For example, you have 10 statements and then the choices are something like: a) 5 or less of these are true b) 3 of these are true c) 2 of these are true, etc. etc. bioc 311 is a joke compared to that class.

I liked this class and the material was interesting, but Dr Nepveu really seem to hate teaching. You don't want a teacher like that, he doesn't motivate you. He discuss the aspect of the course he like (instead of teaching concepts), jumping from one topic to the other, and it's really hard to know what you should focus on.

He uses handouts rather than ppt (which is a bad thing). Very confusing, jumps from topic to topic without telling you what hes talking about. Exam questions were also difficult. Definitely my least favourite prof in this course.

He's the only professor who uses handouts rather than ppts (which isnt a good thing). He tends to ramble as well jumping from one topic to the next. My least favourite prof in this section because I dont like his teaching style and his exam questions are very difficult.

He makes easy topics difficult because he doesn't introduce concepts beforehand. He tends to jump from one idea to another and I had to re-watch his lectures A LOT. That said, if you practice his past questions you'll be okay

Honestly his material is interesting. His way of presenting it is horrid. Describes experiments to you and doesn't tell you what they are for... There are no titles to any of his notes and he loves to jump from one experiment to another. Lectures are always confusing and resulted in terrible attendance. Avoid if you don't absolutely need the class.
This professor is not good. His material is useless (bacteriophage lambda nut ad qut operons... never even told us what it meant). You can study over 50 hour for the exam and barely pass.

Great at teaching, but the midterm questions are idescribably difficult, so much so that only those who have taken this class can understand! Be very careful about the way he words the questions...that's what gets you. Other than that, nice guy in class.

Speaks fast and in a disorganized manner but repeats herself a lot. Classes and readings are interesting. Powerpoints are not super helpful. She is accessible outside of class and will take the time necessary to make sure everything is understood correctly. Very fair.

Prof Klein is extremely engaging and empathetic. Stellar in her field. I went to speak to her many times during office hours and always left enriched and feeling better about the material and also law school generally. Highly recommend.

Klein provides a critical yet practical overview of criminal justice in Canada. Her readings are on the reasonable side for first year, and she annotates the readings with her own commentary to ensure you understand why a passage is important. Her lectures are engaging. She teaches to the middle of the class, helping those who don't grasp concepts.

Professor Klein is gold. Her lectures are not about going through the readings as she expects students to be prepared. She treats students as equals and pushes us to challenge "textbook knowledge" to form our own POV on important issues from the course. Class discussions are engaging. Exam was hell & she's a tough grader. Still worth it though!

Klein is a great person - she is passionate about criminal justice and clearly knows a lot. The readings are really interesting but can be repetitive. She unfortunately is horrible at giving lectures and often gets derailed by irrelevant questions. You spend a lot of time talking about how people feel and not a lot of time learning.

Klein is a very nice and caring professor. However, she rambles a lot, lacks organization, and strays from class material all the time. Frequently we would not talk about any of the assigned readings because she would let students go on and on about their random thoughts.

Best. Prof. Ever. Take Criminal Justice WITH NO ONE ELSE. Prof. Klein is an absolute GEM. She is engaging, energetic, extremely intelligent and a really great person. She is inspiring when you go see her in office hours, and she always pushes her students to think further. Exams are challenging but fair, and she gives food feedback! Seriously do it

You can tell how passionate she is about her field. However,  she would  changed the syllabus content then never do the content so each day was a surprise on what we would be taught. Secondly, her grading was random and tough for some assignments. I would be graded on criteria that wasn't even on the rubric. She never responded to emails too.

Prof Thain is super knowledgable. Her lectures can sometimes be very dense and theory heavy, and she relies a lot on class participation so you definitely need to do the readings. She is a tough grader but is more than happy to help in office hours, and is really reachable by email too.
Professor Thain is so cool. I always looked forward to her lectures and she is so, so kind and caring of her students. Would love to take another class with her!

Almost ten years after I graduated, I still think about Dr. Thain and what an academic force she is. This woman is jaw-droppingly smart AND deeply humble and compassionate. Her lecture content is so elevated and challenging yet she's so appreciative and caring of her students. Sounds cheesy, but her lectures and insights stay with you for life.
Alanna is amazing and she will change your life. Go to her office hours and talk to her! She is incredibly kind and knowledgeable. She also picks the best readings.

Phenomenal and so inspiring. I still think of Alanna and I'm finishing up grad school, she's that good. If you want to go to school to actually think critically and grow as a cultural studies scholar/thinker then she's an absolute must. To those who think she's intimidating, it's probably because she's incredibly smart and invested in her lectures.

I love Alanna Thain. If there was a major that was only classes taught by her, I'd switch today. The best prof on earth, adorable, beautiful, knows her stuff, smartest person alive. Won't hesitate to rip overrated film directors a new one. If you're feeling brave, ask her about Scorsese and get ready for the roast of a lifetime.

You dont need to be smart to understand and appreciate Thain, being interested is enough. Contrary to what a few have said, she is one of the least intimidating profs around. She also couldn't care less about marks but genuinely wants her students to get something out of her classes. Very smart, sensible and very fun. Absolutely worth taking.

Alanna Thain is one of the most brilliant professors at McGill. Granted, her lectures are wordy and dense, but she presents ideas in such an inspired and interesting way that if you have even the slightest interest in the topic you should find yourself enthralled. She's especially wonderful for those with a keen interest in Cultural Studies.
Terrible teacher. She writes an essay before class and then reads it out loud with pauses and inflections. Painfully boring and useless.
Very boring but easy questions on final

I had Sandra for HISP218 as well as 219 this semester and I just adore her. She is a passionate lecturer and her classes are always so interactive, it's easy to meet new people and make friends because it's a small group and she encourages you to sit with new people every week or so. HISP219 was a lot of work but I did really enjoy it!

The best professor I have ever had: inspiring, great pedagogue, profoundly passionate. The course HISP219 is intensive and worth 6 credits during one term so the course is demanding, requiring daily homework and evaluations almost every week. Nevertheless, it is all worth it and would love to take this class again and again.
Excellent. I absolutely recommend; the intensive intermediate course has a reputation for being tough, but if you put effort it in, its absolutely worth it.

Amazing professor. Super organised and genuinely wants her students to succeed. Her class is very welcoming, and you get to know everybody through speaking exercises. There is homework every day and frequent testing, but for an intensive course, I found it very manageable. The most anything is worth is 10%, so grades balance out easily.

One of the best profs I've had at McGill. EXTREMELY well organized, kind, accommodating, great at explaining things. You need to do your homework and participate in class, but the work is 100% worth it. By the end, my Spanish had improved DRASTICALLY, and our class felt like a family. I will miss her class, I HIGHLY reccommend it.

High expectations for students and it's definitely an intensive workload, but she goes above and beyond to support you in your learning and super available to help when needed. She creates an amazing class environment and as long as you put in the work you'll learn a ton and feel comfortable speaking and writing in Spanish. STRONG recommend

One of the best profs. Sweet and stern, like an amazing mother figure. She's engaging in lectures and cares that you understand--will stop class if she needs to. Uses many resources. Grades fairly. Our class felt like a family by the end of the semester. I miss her all the time.
Very helpful and paying attention to each individual's needs.

As an intensive class, we sure had a lot of material to cover, but that's what's good about that: each thing only counts for a little. The teacher's passionate, caring and wants us to succeed. Literally went from taking 0 Spanish to almost fluent -all credit to her! Adored her!!!

She was a great teacher. The content was a lot because it was an intensive class but if there was any confusion, she was committed to helping everyone understand. Once you prepare and do the homework before class, you'll do great. I wish she taught an advanced class similar to this.

Rey is ok. Yes the class is difficult but if you show up to lectures, listen and do the assignments yourself, you will do well. Most people don't show up. His homework is related to the course but much harder than the tests. He recycles questions so most people cheat on midterms, so make sure you have past tests but they are not enough to pass.

Professor Rey is one of the few professors in the department who emphasize the rigorous exactitude of proof. I respect that. However, I feel like he could improve on the quality of his teaching and that of his teaching assistants. Most of his teaching assistants went through the assignment solutions way too fast for an ordinary student to process.

When I took his CHEE 400, I though no way there could be a class worse than this. However, only Rey can beat himself, and CHEE 440 is even worse. He doesn't listen to any advises or requests from student. He has been teaching for such a long time but he is still the worst professor in chem eng. Assignments are long are not related to the class.
Horrible Professor, he just reads his powerpoint in class, doesn't answer questions and his exams have material that was not presented in class and or was only briefly mentioned in the textbook.

This is THE WORST class I have taken in chemical engineering at McGill. His lectures are extremely boring. His class lacks a structure. Information is everywhere and he just reads PowerPoint every class with minimum interaction. There hasn't been a single example or practice problem in class that he guided us through.

This guy has a very outdated way of teaching this course, he does not incorporate any programming into it, where the reality is, in our field, process modelling is never done by hand as he's teaching it. It is time to let go of the past and get with the times. Also, he is always surprised at the low attendance, yet he doesn't change his methods.

This is class itself is the hardest in the entire chemeng curriculum. But Rey makes it even more boring. He just can't teach. He may be a good guy in curving but who knows if he would curve again when the midterm has a mode of 90% (apparently most people are cheating). I only hope he keeps his principle of not failing anyone.

sooooo many typos, you'd think a professor at this level would be more professional. Also, his "typos" are usually mistakes he'd give you a big fat zero on if you were the one who made them in your solution. P.S : even his typo correction has typos, not even joking
Great guy, can't hear a word he is saying but material is straightforward.

Rey has a grandpa sense of humour, if you don't get it, then you probably didn't spend much time with your grandpa. He's really nice if you approach him after class and would answer any question. His exams were overrated, not too hard to score above the average in any of them. Final was a repetitive from the assignments and midterm 1, literally.

He is an amazing professor, very helpful.If you haven't taken 436, 536 or calculus,it will be difficult to understand what is going on so make sure you have completed these classes.Exams are based on his weekly assignments(which are optional, not to hand in) Study the assignments, exam is identical or similar (numbers are changed, that's it)NO BOOK

Harsh grader with little outline of expectations for coursework. Participation is a large chunk of the grade, but you have to really advocate for yourself for the TA or prof to notice you. Content is interesting, but coursework expectations are all over the place with little guidance or instruction.

Dr. Blue is incredible. I can't stress enough how impactful his guidance and instruction was for me in my undergraduate studies. He takes so much care in his work and the materials he ascribes have stayed with me long after I've read them. 1000% will be taking any course he teaches in the future.
This prof was not available during office hours. His lecturers were unhelpful and I found him inaccessible. Wasnt a good experience for me and wouldn't recommend or take again
Amazing! Highly recommend taking any class you can with Dr. Blue.
Dr. Ketchum is a great prof. Her lectures are super interesting and I've learned a lot in them. She's also incredibly helpful and understanding if you need support or accommodation.
Loved Dr. Ketchum, but wished lectures were more interactive! Anyone interested in learning the parallels of social justice and feminism should take this class!

Dr. Ketchum is super nice and accommodating, her classes are interesting, and she's always available for one-on-one discussion during office hours or after class. She gives great feedback and RELEASES GRADES SUPER FAST! Her class was an easy A but still thought-provoking - I highly highly recommend it!!
A fantastic professor, clearly cares about her students and what she teaches. Very accessible readings, just put in the effort and participate, and you will succeed.

Great lectures. There's music and you can tell she really cares about the field. Easy A. All lecture recordings have transcripts. So you can CTRL+F key terms during quizzes if you need to. She actually recommends CTRL+F in her emails. The only critique I have is, it would have been nice to see her face more regularly.

THE BEST CLASS AND PROF!! Dr. Ketchum made this class extremely accessible as an online class. She provided transcripts for all her lectures and lectures were given in an audio/podcast format. All quizzes were open book, multiple choice and you had multiple days to complete them. Everything was graded very fairly. TAKE HER AND THIS CLASS!!

super accommodating and understanding. Dr. Ketchum genuinely wants her students to do well! The class is very engaging as there are weekly discussions. The grading criteria are super clear, and the tests and assignments are doable if you are interested in the class + the prof gives a ton of feedback to improve

While the content was very insightful, the podcast format left few chances to engage with peers and prof, leaving one feeling rather disconnected from the course. Assignments were a perfect blend of interesting & challenging with the chance to explore a topic of choice, and quizzes were easy & open book. Take if you want a good intro to gsfs.

Professor Ketchum is an amazing professor, you can tell she really cares about her students, which means she is willing to give extensions, example test questions, easy quizzes, and is very accessible. The course itself was beyond interesting, the readings were easy, short, and very interesting. If you just pay attention you can get an A! 10/10

This was by far my favourite professor. She answered emails in minutes. The lectures were extremely relevant to real life, and I felt actually helped me more for my politics major than my politics classes did. Both the assignments and quizzes were fun to do, and I felt the grading was fair. She also made the class extremely accessible given covid.

Very sweet and caring, good prof, but the course title was super misleading. This class is about marginalized groups and discrimination more than anything else. Heavy on the SJW, less mental disorder-focused. If that's your thing, then I'd recommend, and she's super passionate and knowledgeable on those topics. Better for soci than psyc students.

This teacher was very nice in lecture, but overall very strict and unclear grading scheme. The quizzes we had were exclusively on in-class content and lectures were not recorded, so if you had the misfortune of missing out on a sentence she said, you had no way of knowing the right answer. Not a class you can breeze through.
Grading criteria was often unclear, yet generous.
She's approachable and really nice, but I left the class feeling like I didn't learn very much. Her lectures are solid, but the content becomes incredibly repetitive, and at times redundant.

Prof Dennis was super friendly and approachable. She tried to make the lectures very interactive, interesting, and was open to any feedback. There were very do-able weekly quizzes and discussion posts, plus a group research project

Professor Dennis was amazing! She really cares that every student understands what they're learning. The class was split into weekly quizzes and reading responses (both easy) and one semester long big group project. If you are into just writing a few papers and being done with the class this prob. isn't right for you. Very interactive and chill.

Fantastic conductor - not always the clearest beat patterns but he has a wealth of knowledge that is evident in the corrections he gives to different sections. Generally a really nice person as well and treats every member of the orchestra with respect. Does not tolerate unexcused absences and lateness.
Great conductor and well respected man. Just wished the rehearsals for Beethoven Orchestra were more organized beforehand by being informed what we were playing in rehearsal more in advance.

Conducting is not clear, many of his students are clearer conductors than him - 1 should be down! Beethoven 5 in 2018-2019 was absolutely horrid. Maybe he was good 20 years ago, but he needs to retire. He refuses to correct any intonation at all, particularly in the winds (prime examples: Chichester psalms, Sibelius 5, Mahler 5, Beethoven 5). Bad.

Professor Hauser is the reason I keep coming back to Beethoven Orchestra every semester! He is so knowledgeable and gives amazing feedback to the conductors that help them refine their skills. His comments are always helpful and never sound condescending.
Best conductor and teacher I've ever seen!

He is a great conductor who loves teaching. I agree that he hates lack of preparation, and rightfully so. My only complaint is that for "artistic" reasons he will often delay programming concerto performances of competition winners. The orchestra needs more experience with playing with soloists.
Not to be believed! Absolutely incredible! Nohrma!

I don't understand why the University brings an amazing conductor such as Maestro Hauser, and then gives us someone so bad to end the season. If it is true that the person who finished this McGill concert season will conduct the Opera in January, I will not be in Orchestra!!!!!!

Obviously the person below is one of the string players WHO CONSISTENTLY DOESN'T PRACTICE AND SHOWS UP TO REHEARSALS COMPLETELY UNPREPARED...I guess that's why the rest of the orchestra reveres this man as the best thing to ever happen to McGill Music...grow up and go practice!!

As a string player, have nothing but complaints. the rep he chooses is too difficult for the string section as a whole, isn't a clear conductor (I mean, is that a 4 or a 1??!!), and doesn't listen to what his players have to say.
I had him for a research project and he was very caring and took time to get to know his students and gives realistic advice. I would definitely recommend him!

He really wants his students to understand the course content and do well, and is genuinely one of the most caring professors I've had at uni. The assignments are very representative of examination questions. His grading scheme is more than fair, even offering to weight a midterm grade less if performance increases on the final. 10/10 recommend!

Such a lovely person. Super nice and caring and always happy to answer questions both in and outside class. Really wants students to succeed so provides lots of notes and practice problems. He is sometimes a little slow in class as he takes a long time to answer each question, but his teaching is quite good and very representative of his exams.

Prof Ali is one of the best profs in the department. He puts in 110% and will go out of his way to make sure you understand. If you mess up on evaluations he gives you chances to make up for them in other ones. His exams are very fair and delivers the content very nicely. Protect this man at all costs!

It's the first time he taught the class, so the content/notes weren't as clear as they could possibly be. However improvement was shown throughout the semester. He cares a lot about people doing well. Midterms and final we're very fair, tested exactly what was expected and graded very fairly. Enjoyable class overall !

He's a very caring teacher; and really wants his students to do well. It's his first time teaching this course, thus he wasn't super organized with notes. However, he's willing to sacrifice a lot of hours outside of class to help. Test 2 was easy and the first was a disaster for most of the class.... yet to do the final. I did learn a lot :)

This stands to be my favourite course in my undergrad. The lecture style is unconventional but very open to discussion, and she fosters an amazing atmosphere for collaboration and learning. Grading is reasonable, but be sure to engage deeply with the text and form your own opinions. Overall, I left this class with a greater understanding.
I love her, she is the gem of philosophy department.

professor al-saji is an amazing scholar, and her lectures (which were in podcast form) made the challenging material much clearer and added brilliant critiques and new perspectives. the participation scheme is flexible, and you are evaluated primarily on two papers, which are graded fairly with lots of feedback. highly recommend!!

Professor Al-Saji is absolutely brilliant and has such a rich perspective, her passion and expertise are inspiring. The class is very well-structured and isn't too difficult as long as you keep up with the readings. She is great about responding to students' questions/concerns quickly and thoroughly.

Prof. Al-Saji is brilliant and daring (epic critiques). One must take this course to simply hear her lecture on Fanon. To contextualize existentialism, most of the class is devoted to Sartre. Once that part is done, Beauvoir and Fanon redeem the class and you realize why reading Sartre was necessary. Short but very dense readings. Fair grading too.

Lectures were in podcast form, plus a flexible participating scheme that could involve in-person conferences. The material was hard like any philosophy course (we read Sartre, de Beauvoir, and Fanon), but she explained really well and the readings were mostly short. I wouldn't take this as an elective but for a phil degree I definitely recommend.

I just took PHIL 375 with Alia Al-Saji - probably my favourite class I've taken so far at McGill. Al-Saji is incredibly sweet, brilliant, critical, and very caring. (By critical I mean that she is not afraid to point out her critical thoughts on famous philosophers.) She is very self-assured. I would love to take many more classes with her!

The "A" in Al-Saji stands for AMAZING! She's a great lecturer and she definitely knows her stuff. She's extremely kind once you get to know her and always wants the best for you. Take her if you can--you won't regret it. However, keep in mind that this is not an easy A class. You'll definitely have to work for it! Read before coming to class!!!
Simply amazing.  Changed my relation to the world and to myself.  Intense work, but worth it.  Everyone should take this class.
Fantastic prof. Really kind and knows her stuff.
Dr. Sajjad explained the material very well. I wasn't sure how I will do in this course. Now in the midway, I'm pretty confident.
Highly recommended.

I had trouble with stats in psych but Prof Alia was very clear. I loved how she'd show the calculations in real time and provided practice exams. I had her in fall 2023, so I don't know if things have changed but the exams were online!
The lectures make sense and are usually not too intense. She does go rather slow, however its nice especially when you don't understand things. Also, she is very good at answering questions.
Its my best class so far. dr. sajjad makes the material very interesting. of what I heard her finals are hard. thats the only thing
Very Organized and accessible. Posts recordings which helped me a lot.

Very slow lectures and omit essential concepts. Did not prepare me well for MATH 324. Unwilling to be in person and switch everything to Zoom whenever there's a chance. The assignment solutions and lecture notes are full of errors and scratches.
This was my first stats course with little background in maths (I forgot most of it). Dr. Sajjad made this course accessible. Highly recommended.
Great Instructor.
Dr. Sajjad teaches this course as a story telling. You don't feel pressured but at the end you notice that you learnt a lot.

Really caring professor who wants her students to do well. It's a difficult class that requires lots of studying - quizzes were hard and tanked my grade, but I felt like by the end of the course I had a good grasp of the content.

I do not like this prof. Dont get me wrong her lectures are well thought out and she teaches well but she is not kind. Her class is fine but if ur looking to get extra help dont expect it to be a good experience

I had a lot of trouble with this class. One minute I thought I understood and the next moment the rules for chemistry seemed to change - a proton can move here but not there. Then suddenly a proton can move here but not there again.
I thought she was kind, but she really isn't once you start asking the tough questions.

Great teacher who genuinely cares about her students' well-being. The class is hard especially if you haven't taken chem before, and I struggled with developing the study/practice habits necessary to do well on the weekly quizzes. Participation points were counted, and she was very accessible outside of class. If you work hard, you should do well.

Specifically for AECH 110, this is a class that forces incoming freshman to work! Dr.Cherestes is kind and gives good feedback but only if you take the time to reach out to her. Otherwise prepare for some relatively punishing quizzes/exams if you don't prepare properly. If you take the time to properly study and revise, you should be fine.
She was kind to a certain extent. I would do the homework, come to class and still not understand a single word of her lectures. She teaches as if we already know the material
If you let me to describe her course, then I could say the grade I got was higher than what I got in FDSC 200 (totally open book course). The labs were interesting and there was no final.

She is definitely better for orgo than she is for gen chem; she still makes a couple mistakes in class here and there but overall good professor, only 1 lab report per term which was nice. Tests are fair and with many opportunities of getting partial credit on the exams. No final

She cares for students and is always ready to answer questions or address any confusion. Office hours are open for a lot of time periods and she is so patient and explains your confusing part from different perspectives. Lectures and tutorials are delivered clearly and problem-solving sessions are held for better preparation for the exam.

Amazing professor who explains things thoroughly, doing varied examples in class. Extremely caring, which was a surprise since she seemed quite indifferent during freshmen chemistry. Assignments made sense, and although the material is difficult, with a little effort it's actually fun.
Very nice and helpful, try not to be late to her classes though ;-;

Professor Soucé is incredibly kind, caring, and approachable, and it's clear she truly wants her students to succeed. The grading structure is very fair, and you can do well in the class if you stay on top of the material and put in the effort. I genuinely looked forward to her class each week and would take any course she teaches!

She's a REALLY NICE teacher. She cares and pays attention to every student in the class and gives useful feedback. Feel free to ask her questions because she will answer your questions patiently. The class is inspirational and helpful. Lots of homework and tests BUT acceptable bc she's just SO NICE and I really want to take another class of hers
rounded me up to an A
Amazing Amazing Prof. Very hard marker but it does not matter because she is so kind and nice!
One of the best professors I've met at McGill!

This was one of my more challenging classes this semester, as I struggled to keep up with the practice and homework assignments. She gives good feedback in the classroom and on assessments. Make sure to participate in class and complete all the online assignments/quizzes, as it will help your grade at the end of the semester!

This was my first time ever taking a French course (outside of things like Duolingo) and I really enjoyed it. The class relied a lot on participation and interacting with your classmates in French, which is very helpful for oral practice/comprehension. She is great at giving feedback and I thought the class was very fair.
She was so sweet and a great teacher. She will explain questions until you understand and offers lots of wise insight on learning french that I haven't thought of before.
Very patient and kind. Nice even when you mess up a lot.

Very kind and entertaining professor with interesting lectures. Prof Hepburn produces extremely intelligent insights into novels that I never would have thought of! Tests are based on lecture material and the books only, and the research project was a nice break from standard essays. My favourite class this semester by far!

Prof. Hepburn's course is exactly what I look for in a literature course! Read the texts, then show up to hear plenty of interesting insights into the works and their context. The evaluations are purposeful, there's no annoying busywork, he moves beyond doing a mere survey of the author/era, and his passion for the subject comes through clearly!

I have taken a number of classes with Hepburn at McGill and I have enjoyed every one. As a friend told me "as long as you attend lectures and do the reading you will do fine." This was true, especially for his midterms/ finals. He is an entertaining and informative lecturer and loves discussion! Highly recommend. I did not find him a harsh marker.

Prof Hepburn is clearly passionate about what he teaches. He is helpful and easily accessible, but reading is intense, and its crucial to stay up with the readings in his classes if you want a good grade.

Honestly baffled at some of the bad reviews. This is my second class with Hepburn & he's easily one of the best profs in the department. If you go to the lectures & do the readings you are almost guaranteed an A. One of the easiest graders (that doesn't mean you can get away with not trying- but the A is in sight every paper).

Never met someone so skilled at ruining great books. Hepburn will focus in on the most boring, banal aspects of great novels and go on for hours, and come assignments, expect you to regurgitate these incredibly bland ideas. Snobby, pretentious, uninteresting; the embodiment of everything I hate about academia
He holds amazing class discussions!

Super lovely human being- would definitely take again if I could but he mostly does Areas of Eng. 3 stuff (obvs) and I need to do more of other sections.
If you go to the lectures and read the novels you'll be fine.

kinda was disappointed by this class. reading list was great but the prof spent more time talking about his own very specific analyses rather than the books themselves, and the final exam was basically just regurgitating his ideas rather than formulating your own. also super tough grader and favors certain students

Don't get me wrong his class is really difficult to get an A in but this man is amazing and makes me want to work to meet his expectations. I'm in awe of how intelligent he is and how interesting he made books about old white people. His zoom background was his library of books and I believe that he's read them all because he's so well versed.
Awesome prof! Fun lectures, learned a lot from him!
Awsome prof. Explains really well and can clarify if needed. If you fall behind he runs down the content at office hours

I took Math 203 and it was such a great class.  Lectures were so funny and well organized, and Prof Russell was so helpful and caring in office hours. 10/10 reccomend this course.  The grading scheme made my life easy and I was rarely stressed.
Goated teacher. Teaches the material perfectly, is passionate, and actually makes statistics an interesting material.

Really takes the time to care about his students and does an amazing job at creating a respectful and interactive classroom environment. MATH 324 is a difficult course, especially with being moved into all in person, heavily weighted exams, but everything was explained very clearly and made the course overall an enjoyable experience.

Prof Oliver is hands down one of the best profs in the Math department. What surprises me is how consistently he has made himself available almost 24/7 for questions and OHs, which shows just how much he cares about the progress and learning experience of his students. I could go on forever.... truly a GOAT

The best teacher I've had at McGill. He is very good at explaining concepts through slides and examples. He really understands the material too, so when students have questions, he is always able to explain and vulgarize the answer. Always provides some recaps, reinforcing learning. If you're able to take a class he teaches, go for it!

I have to say that math324 itself is tough work but if you meet Prof. Oliver and try to catch up on material in every lecture and positively ask questions with him, you'll be fine
math203/math204  more focusing on " plug in play" trick  in the tools of statistics (confidence interval etc.)

fair exam, very patient and clear explanation in office hour and lecture .
Great lectures. The course was well organized. The evaluations were fair.
Shrier Netanyahu ong

evil questions on the phgy 210 final im shaking

His questions were not hard and were not meant to confuse you. Make sure to understand osmosis and tonicity and the calculations associated with them.

Only had him for 2-3 lectures, he's okay. He's not the best at explaining stuff, but it's not that complicated. I clearly underestimated this section for the exam, it was a bit more difficult than I thought it would be.

Shrier is one of the nicest people I've ever met. The university is truly lucky to have him. Best prof at McGill, by far. Great sense of humour, really nice to talk to and genuinely cares about his students. #Shrierforpresident

He's a very good prof in general. SOME of his exam questions were a LITTLE bit tough, but just really try to UNDERSTAND his material than plainly memorizing it (do that too, you need both to get an A in this course). He was definitely one of the better profs for this course. His content was interesting and fascinating. Definitely recommend him.
Good prof in general, his section is so short and easy that I don't remember much about him. Exam questions were pretty fair and he was clear
Really nothing special about this prof., nothing to remember about him either except that his exam questions were not that easy, despite his material being very easy.
Prof Fournier is very sweet, takes time to explain, and is very passionate about the section she teaches. Highly recommend.
Class not as hard as people make it out to be, if you study well, you will be fine. If you put in the work, you'll do well in the class. Final is expected
This class is Pass/Fail and very interesting! Perfect if you know nothing about personal finance. No exams. Focused on learning. Attendance graded.

Amanda is probably the best teacher at Desautels. She lets you know how hard her class is, but gives you all the support and info you need to do well. She has many office hours, and is helps you work through your difficulties. Lectures are extremely engaging. If I could take Amanda for every class, I would.

Out of all my professors at McGill, she seemed to be one of the few who genuinely cared about each student's success. She taught with enthusiasm, humour, and clarity, making it very easy for students to follow along. I would definitely recommend her.
Amanda is the best prof at McGill. This class is tough, but she prepares you for her exams. Exams are long and tough. If you go to office hours and practice her questions, you will do well.

Agree with every other positive review! You definitely have to work for your grade, but if you go to class it becomes really clear what's going to be on the exam, so there are not really any surprises. Do her practice, understand the theory/standards, and getting a good grade will just be a matter of how much effort you're willing to put in.

Such a great prof! The content was hard, but her lectures were funny, and the class felt like a family this semester. Definitely do the practice midterms many times to prep for the MT. And go to her office hours! She tells you how difficult and long the exams will be so it's not a surprise. You have to stay on top of it for this class

Amanda is an amazing prof. She made a dry class IFA 2 as interactive as possible. I usually walked away from each lecture already understanding the materials thanks to her teaching, which makes reviewing and practicing a lot easier. Overall, would highly recommend taking her classes. Pay attention to her *** as they will appear on the exams.
Dry class, hard exams. However, she made it my best experience at McGill.

Heavy lectures + fair but hard exams. Best prof in accounting so far, cares about make students learn. Stay up to date with the textbook practice questions, don't fall behind. Do the previous midterms at least thrice bc her midterm is very similar to it. Final was harder (cheat sheet was allowed). Write down her ***, they're actually in the exams

The class itself was ok. The PowerPoints were confusing, the info that was given would alternate in each side, it was not consistent which made it difficult to learn the content correctly for the exams. Even if you speak every class, you won't get full participation points, she wants you to say exactly what she thinks (movie analysis is subjective)

Prof Holmes is kind and knowledgeable on the historical context of Latin American cinema. The class was taught in Spanish and she was understanding that students had varying levels of the language proficiency when grading. She is very sweet and approachable and allowed for a lot of class discussion and analysis of films. I loved this class!

Nice person. bizarre boring tangents that seem to confuse even her; cool content turns dull. Misguided emphasis on participation, ironic with her inability to process interpretations different than her own. Her difficulties creating an interesting lecture are only outdone by her worst-in-class feedback and random grading. don't take.
Writing a warning rather than a review, but you can also go to her class to see for yourself. Disappointing lectures and ambiguous grading. Not the greatest combo. Actually, probably the worst combo.

I found this course really interesting--not too much reading, midterms weren't bad, and the group presentation was graded pretty leniently (unlike the papers...). I'm confused how she grades participation, it doesn't seem very accurate (which could go either good or bad). Overall I really enjoyed this course, I felt it was easier than 244 with her.

Holmes is very personable outside of class. Not great in class, though. An unreasonably difficult grader. Never gives any real feedback, or explains WHY you got the grade you did. Ridiculously high standards for participation. No room for debate, either. If your analysis of texts isn't exactly what she wants, you're flat out wrong.

exams not very difficult, as long as you study enough for it ! lots of outside of class time work for hisp 301, as lectures are based on discussion and she grades your participation. she gives great feedback on assignments and will change your grade if you fix stuff and resubmit- she wants her students to succeed and helps you do so!

Prof. Holmes is a nice person and the reading list was really interesting, but she's a bit of a tough grader--even with participation points. Overall I enjoyed the course and the final was very reasonable, it's not too hard to do well in the class even if you're not a native speaker.

Prof.Holmes is knowledgeable as professor and caring as person. I learned a lot from her and she gave feedback very timely. Her cinema course is a good portion of theory, socio-historical background and film analysis. The only thing that I find a bit disappointing is her quiz was needlessly specific and participation is all about being talkative.

The reading list for HISP 244 was wonderfully selected. The rest of the course was an utter disappointment. Professor Holmes is often superficial and simplistic with her ideas and it was so frustrating to sit through her lectures being like this. She's a nice person, though.

I took her for PSYC 337 in the summer. Her lectures are very clear and informative. Her exams were straightforward and there was a writing assignment every week so that your grade is not solely reliant on exams which is nice! She is such a nice prof, I wish I could take her again!
Took her in summer and was one of the best courses I've taken at McGill. Very clear in how she explains and makes it easy to understand harder topics.

Psyc337 is very loaded with content but Dr. Ravary handles it like a champ. It's super clear and easy to follow along. Super interesting material and class is structured nicely and grading is good too. Loved having her class in the summer!
she was such a nice prof, I would definitely recommend taking her. I wish she would teach more McGill classes!! her tests are quite fair plus the assignments are super easy.

Amanda Ravary is really in-touch with what it's like to be a student. Her lecturing style is super clear and reflects the content of the slides which she uploads before class. I definitely recommend taking PSYC 337 in the summer rather than in the winter if you can to benefit from her style of teaching as opposed to a prof like Anna Weinberg.

Such an amazing prof! This is one of the most interesting courses I've taken at McGill. Dr. Ravary is awesome at keeping lectures engaging and is clearly very passionate about her work. Highly recommend taking 337 with her!

Just about done her class and I can honestly say she's been my favorite prof so far. So incredibly sweet and passionate about the topic, handles tough topics with a lot of care, you can tell she really wants her students to succeed. Really interesting topics, textbook readings are fair game on exams but just know general concepts. RECOMMEND!!

I took the summer course for PSYC337 and she taught it. A really amazing prof who made the course super enjoyable and was just a really great teacher and lecturer. I only wish she taught more courses at McGill because I would love to have her again as a prof! Learned more in this course over a month than I have in many others over a full semester.

Disregard what the previous review said, it's FAKE. This instructor is D-tier at best. He has a big ego but no skills to back it. He flexes his PhD and P.Eng titles to prove legitimacy because that's all he has to hide his TOTAL ABSENCE of professional experience. This person is a net negative to McGill's department of mechanical engineering.

Amar Sabih is the kind of professor who makes you level up. His high-quality questions and concrete direction improved our rigor and decisions in our project. Highly recommend.

His exams are a lot harder than any other prof giving the same class, only realistic way to practice is to find the hardest old midterms (don't try to solve the easy one, it will not appear on his midterms lol) on Studocu and solve them, don't waste your time on tutorials or his classes, because they are useless. 

Emailing him is also useless!
Midterms and exams are far way tougher than in class exercies and tutorial . I don't know why .

The class is heavy!  I learned to design complex machine elements! :)
The course has a project that is a bit hard, but you will learn a lot.
Happy to get an A- at the end
Knowledgeable, Helpful, Fair.
one of the best engineering courses i have ever taken. Very useful.

Interesting prof. Difficult first midterm, easy second midterm and final. Changed grading scheme two days before the final to add participation but unironically helped my grade out because it lowered midterm weight. Pretty good prof.
The only lap with educational videos. TAs are Ok but need to spend more time with the students. Overall experience was good. Easy A !
Recommended. Uses grades to motivate us and lots of bonus grades. I suppose to get a B+, with bonus points, I got an A :))
Dr. Johnson is an incredible prof; taking a course with her is well worth your time.

Amin was an excellent professor when i took 556. He is caring and is always ready to help when asked. He is very good at building up to harder material, but requires that you pay attention. He also expects the class to actively participate occasionally.

The workload is very heavy, so i would recommend taking 556 only if you are motivated.

Great teacher who can be very nice, but the positive reviews about him on Reddit can be misleading. You'll likely end up frustrated by high demands and discouraged by his sometimes dismissive attitude.

Although Prof. Emad is knowledgeable, the amount of deliverables is way too heavy of a load. Given that this course is only 4 credits, the fact that he assigns a huge assignment and a 5000-8000 word report on an individual final project due the same week during exams is overkill. This year, ECSE 556 took more time than my other 3 courses combined.

Pr. Emad is the best teacher I've ever had, and the ECSE552 Deep Learning course was one of the most enjoyable and insightful course you'll find on AI. Diversified work, that doesn't add up to too much, overall very good balance. Definitely recommend this course and this teacher.
Great professor. Very knowledgeable. Would definitely recommend

Dr. Shmuel is a great professor and mentor. I did my senior thesis project with Dr. Shmuel and got to participate in a lot of cool experiments. He always replies to emails promptly and is very supportive of his students. I'd love to work with Dr. Shmuel again in the future.
Fantastic lecturer; she is engaging and really cares about her students doing well. She is super accessible outside of class and her office hours are always a lot of fun.

Dr. Blum was one of my favourite profs I've had. Her class is quite difficult especially if physical chemistry isn't your area of expertise. However, by doing all the practice questions she assigns and practice quizzes you can set yourself up to do well. She is very kind and she goes above and beyond to help students. Office hours are a big help!

This class is really difficult but Professor Blum is very good! If you don't understand something she will explain it to you over and over again until you understand and always available outside of class. All content on tests are basically the same as practice quizzes and problem sets and it is very easy to get partial marks!

For a not-so-interesting class, Dr. Blum did a really good job of teaching it. She's super helpful and accessible outside of class, and will make sure that you understand before moving on. Her tests are very fair (entirely based on the homework), so they're easy to do well on if you know your thermo.

Blum is awesome! Yes, it's a hard course but she cares a lot about her students and is so patient. All the past exams + key + worked solutions for problem sets are posted, and she grades REALLY fast (final was graded in just 5 days, and all quizzes are graded and released with feedback within 1h!) exams resembled the problem set questions a LOT.

Amy is a great prof and teaches well. The quizzes arent impossible but they do take up a lot of time. Dont let yourself fall behind in the practice questions because the material piles up fast, its not that difficult if you do the problems and ask questions but dont expect to be able to learn everything a few days before the exam.

I didn't really enjoy her class. Blum is an okay professor, but the content itself was bland, which made this class a drag. Her quizzes/exams were quite difficult, with averages tending towards B/B-. I agree; her class was very intensive. Honestly, I put the most hours into this course, yet I still got a mediocre grade. Oh well.

Good at conveying content but harsh with respect to grading. In a sense I personally found the course unnecessarily hard. Workload is much like a 4+ credit course but thankfully it's not since the class averages for exams/quizzes are 60s-70s (at times 50s), which are apparently considered normal. Responds to emails quickly though
Insane amount of work. Online quizzes were a nightmare.
She is a great prof, really helpful and wants to see her students do well. Problem sets are long but questions on the exam are usually very similar to homework/quizzes/past exams she gives you.
Very interesting course but grading was harsh. Prof Janzwood is very nice and understanding, however it felt nearly impossible to get an A or even an A- in the class sometimes.

I absolutely love Janzwood!! I had her for ENVR 203 and enjoyed it so much that I took POLI 350. Her classes do require effort, but as long as you do the readings and pay attention in class you'll be set. Do NOT skip lectures though, you'll regret it when it's time to take midterm/final.
I personally did not really enjoy the course at first, but professor Janzwood is incredible and made me look forward to going to class every week. She is genuinely incredible.

Amy consistently demonstrated that she genuinely cared about the course topic and the students' interest in it. She is deeply passionate, and though she uses two group projects, with one randomly assigned, she is very sweet and a really good lecturer.
Very harsh grading, assignments are interesting; however, concepts are difficult to grasp at times if you're not already familiar with them. Also, be ready to read!

During her lectures it fwelt as if she was just reading off of an essay. I did not like the way she would not respond to questions outside of class out of fairness but in reality that in itself is not fair. The midterm was chill and the assignment had a clear grading criteria unlike her counterpart in the later half of the course.

Prof Janzwood is a friendly and caring individual. The class is not hard to do well in, as most of the grade is based on smaller assignments. However, the stuff assigned didn't align with its grading worth in my opinion (like 400ish-word reflection worth 3% of the grade). Also found it hard to gage what was important to learn for midterm/final.

not terrible but a lot of useless assignments worth barely anything. the class material feels a little disorganized and it sometimes felt like high school (i.e class discussions, etc). we did get a crib sheet for the final which was great. it's not hard to do well but i was excited for this class and honestly didn't like it

Would absolutely recommend prof. Janzwood and this class! Though the first part of the course was somewhat theoretical, the later weeks were more concrete, and we notably conducted a UN simulation which was an interesting and innovative project.

The structure of the class was the best I've had at McGill. Every week builds on the next, creating a very rewarding knowledge background in GEP at the end of the class. Available for her students and is both very knowledgeable on environmental politics and passionate about the topic.
A real gem! Fountain of knowledge. Great man!

I feel like people only rate if they love or hate, so I want to provide something different! Good teacher, quick but thorough, sticks to the textbook, hard marker on compositions (but they all are), really nice, sweet woman, brought cookies for Christmas. Fun class, take her section!

I loved Professor Creech! This class was once a week and wasn't that work heavy. Just attend class and you'll be fine! Lecture were interesting and a mix of class discussions, discussion boards, one paper where you to summarize an article and a group presentation. Overall, Prof Creech was lovely:)

The class itself had way too much history covered in just one semester, and if you have little knowledge on basic south asian history it might be difficult to follow. However, the grading was easy and straight forward however some lectures were incredibly hard to stay focused in. Prof Farran is passionate on the topic which def adds points.

Not answering questions and removing quiz material from mycourses before the final. Lectures quite boring but she is very passionate and cares about what she teaches. Genuine person. Final exam was much easier than she made it seem and she does not grade tough.
I give her 5 stars
I enjoyed this course.  There were many good discussions and it gave me lots of things to think about
I took a class by Professor Farran last term.  I found her tough but fair a real genuine person

professor farran is the type of professor who you can tell really cares about her students and the Course material.  She really loves the subject and presents the material in an interesting way.  Always available to answer questions i would take another class by her again if I needed to!

High weekly workload and lots of boring readings. Her section of the course focused on religion/terms and it was hard to reconcile/organize with the actual history of the region, made it confusing and hard to stay motivated. Final was not bad, 100% free response. Not a GPA or semester ruiner, but wouldn't take again.

Do not trust these reviews. Was this the best class ever? No, but it was a fairly easy A. You are expected to attend lectures and open the mandatory readings. I say this with love:  if you feel this is asking too much, maybe reconsider why you're in university. If you're interested in the subject (I wasn't), don't let these reviews discourage you.
Easy class, 10/10. Everything is open book but the exam.

A VERY dense course that is difficult to keep up with if you have no pre-existing knowledge on South Asian history. The quizzes and study guides did little in helping set expectations for the exam. Only did well thanks to the grade getting curved. Overall easy enough to get a good grade, however I would not recommend taking this course.

Awesome class! Definitely the most interesting chem class I've taken. He talks a LOT about biological inspiration for materials chem and ties everything to real-world applications. There's no textbook but there are suggested readings for every lecture, and definitely show yp to class. Assessments are comprehensive and grading critera is clear.
WOOOO PROF TONE!!!!
Great prof!!
Not a difficult course. Professor makes it far harder than it needs to be. Would not take another course from this professor.

This was such an incredible course. My friends got sick of me repeating everything I learned; the class material was so engaging and so pertinent. I'm sure I'll use what I've learned in the future. I agree with the other review that this hardly felt like schoolwork. Prof. Tone is so awesome and really authentic, which I appreciated.

Honestly the best prof I have ever had, her teaching style is amazing and so engaging. Rated her average difficulty simply because I found her course so interesting that it almost didn't feel like school work lol. I wish I had taken more classes with her, I love everything about her and she is just so interesting to listen/talk to

Truly one of the best professors I have had the pleasure of learning from. Very knowledgeable and passionate. Makes the content engaging and values what students has to say. Ready to help and cares so much! Only good things to say!

Professor Tone was one of the nicest professors I've ever had. Intensely passionate about her subject and made me passionate about it as well even though I came into the class knowing nothing about the history of medicine. She was very understanding and her lectures were incredibly interesting and engaging.

Prof Tone is one of the best history teachers I've ever had. She clearly knows her stuff and her lectures are so interesting. She's always available for any problems you might have and she clearly cares about her students and their input. I didn't think I'd be interested in the history of medicine but it's one of my favourite topics now!

BEST seminar, Dr. Tone has high standards but is a fair grader and gives you every opportunity to do well in class. Read, go to class, speak in seminars and you will not only do well but will learn valuable skills for academic research and writing. One of the best classes I've taken at McGill.

My other absolute FAVOURITE prof McGill!! A MUST take :) It was genuinely the most rewarding class I've taken in university. She is *so* invested in her students and their work, I can confidently say that taking her class changed the way I approach research and write academic papers for the better. I would take her a 3rd time if I could!! A+ prof!!

Prof Warburton will go down as my fav professor at McGill. He is kind, understanding, knowledgeable and clearly passionate about the content.

The course was well-organized, interesting and useful. The homeworks were helpful (pass-fail), the exams were fair, although the weekly labs did take a while, they complemented the coursework really well.

It was his first time teaching electronics, and he did a super good job! Lectures and lecture notes were extremely clear, which made studying much easier. The course was heavy in terms of labs and assignments, but Prof. Warburton was empathetic and made it easier with pass/fail assignments. I learned a lot and recommend taking his class!
Informative lectures, great answers to student questions. Overall very good.

Content was very clearly explained in lectures AND on the slides (very detailed and include a lot of images to explain abstract concepts). lectures are very engaging, professor Warburton is an amazing lecturer, very eloquent, caring and just, He answers all questions and lectures often included live demos and board calculations!

Professor Warburton was very helpful and engaging in this intro-level physics class. If you participate in class and show interest, you will definitely achieve a good grade. He does many practical demonstrations and experiments for concepts that are harder to grasp.

As someone who isn't a physics major, I thoroughly enjoyed this class because it allowed me to ask questions about physics that have always intrigued me. It was a great opportunity to explore and satisfy my curiosity about the some physical concepts. The practice exam questions are great tool to prepare for exams.

Material was consistently connected to current and relevant experiences that were directly related to students or the instructor. This made the content uniquely engaging and original. Andreas Warburton encouraged discussion from students and took the time to learn the names of students that participated.
Definitely would recommend taking the course if you are looking for something interesting and not too difficult. Overall, a great professor and an interesting course.

The course has changed a lot from past years and is focused on the students. The material is not too tough and there is always support available online or in person. The grading is quite forgiving with feedback given at a reasonable time. Sample papers and guides also given for the midterms and final which show the level perfectly.  Recommended!

Andreas does his best to make sure the concepts were explained clearly and there was always active discussion in class, online or in his office hours regarding material or anything in general. The content itself was also fun! 

The grading is also made so that students can make the most of it and with just a little work a high grade is achievable.
This teacher has a terrible attitude and will randomly yell at you because you didn't go to a few useless classes. She will proceed to not grade your work and tell other students she will fail you.
Extremely rude and unprofessional professor. Makes you think how such a person could be teaching a course about teaching.
I think she's racist. Didn't even care about pronouncing one Asian student's name correctly.

Dianne and TA are both serious and responsible. She does seem strict, but with the high demand for participation, I did join every lesson in remote teaching. Even listening to others' presentations, everyone is asked to give encouragement or advice. This makes me more engaged in learning. The courses are solid and the grading is rigorous.

Dianne was one of the worst teachers I have had so far. She is extremely rude and entitled in her feedback and comments. She will do anything to feel superior and to bring you down. I seriously do not recommend her. She is not a nice person.

It speaks to the ridiculousness of McGill in general that this mandatory course is only taught by ONE professor each semester. Don't expect to come out of it prepared to teach anything. You also learn nothing about classroom management. So much pointless busywork but I disagree with the other comments that it's a difficult course.
She is a very tough grader and gives such rude feedback to explain why she took off marks. She is extremely rude to students in class and makes aggressive comments. STAY AWAY

This class is about assessment and she talks about the importance of providing clear rubrics to students. However, ironically enough, she herself does not apply this. No clear criteria is given in any of her work, and she expects two group presentations in a semester. We also do not get any feedback on our work, even when it's well past mid-term.
Greatest lecturer in the entire University for the hardest class I've ever taken, and I'd do it again!

Very much enjoyed his teaching style. Classes consisted of a short lecture where he would go over new material, and then the rest of class was for working on exercises to get a feel for the new topics and also some class discussion. He taught things that were actually useful and applicable to real world problems.

Andrew is amazing. Quantum Mech is hard, but he did an amazing job teaching it to a bunch of exhausted undergrads at 9:30 am. He's totally aware of the difficulty of the class too, once curving a midterm up by 20%. Really great guy, outstanding prof, definitely take QM with him.
Awesome awesome awesome. Best physics professor I've ever had. Highly recommended to spend your (rare) electives on a chance to take a course with Prof. Cumming.
Absolutely brilliant guy. He demands hard work but you'll learn a lot. One of the best physics profs I've had.
Brilliant

Wow.. hard class, but super interesting.  A little discouraging when you get a low 60 on the midterm but it's still an 'A' because the test was difficult!...  Great lectures & clear notes.  Term paper was interesting to write - good idea.  The assignments are hard, and long, but not out of reach - often interesting.
Tough material, but this guy is as good of a physics teacher as you are ever going to get. He's very helpful and understanding and he made the class interesting.

Teaches physics the way it's supposed to be taught. Sense of humor, makes the material interesting, excited about what he's teaching. But, his assignments are EXTREMELY difficult, often requiring 15-20 hrs every week, and are not good for learning the material. The text "Griffiths" sucks as well.
Great teacher, still very new at what he does though, but he tries very hard.
He is one of the knowledgable teacher but I think he doesn't know how to help a student in the class

I might only have had a handful of lectures by this prof, but holy moly he is one of the greatest profs I've ever had. He is an extremely good lecturer and is very passionate, knowledgeable and respected in his field, and it shows. I can't recommend this prof enough.

Great lecturer, I learned a lot from this class but I wish Dr. Gonzalez would either give better rubrics before assignments or give more detailed and constructive criticism for after assignments so we can learn for future assignments.
Great prof, super interesting, interacting, nice and very clear on his explanations. He is just great take his classes

He is an incredibly engaging speaker. I wish he could have taught us more frequently, because he is that much fun to listen to. His module was very straight-forward and easy to prepare for. An excellent prof!!
he's a nice, charming, funny man...and kinda sexy
No Comments
He is such a nice weirdo you cannot imagine. He is really interested in conservation and that makes his lectures interested to attend. He is quite a character!!!

The absolute best! He definitely knows what he's talking about and has a lot of experience with the animals he's teaching to you. He shows a lot of videos of him travelling the world or even in his home interacting with the animals you're learning about. He also provided prelecture videos instead of prelecture slides compared to the other profs.

My entire degree is now focused on Eco-Evo + fish Biology because of this guy. Incredibly passionate about what he teaches, cares about his students and gives you the resources you need to do well in his class. While I do think occasionally his exams focus too much on arbitrary details, if you pay enough attention, you'll be fine.
Very friendly, funny and upfront about test material, that said a lot of tested material felt unnecessary and gratuitous

Interesting and engaging lectures. The lectures were probably the easiest to follow in biol 111, but the content on the final seemed oddly specific and very demanding in terms of detail. Not to mention that we had to draw a WHOLE phylogeny at the end.

He's an amazing lecturer, speaks very well and explains really well. His lectures were by far my favourite, they are super engaging and interesting. He shows pictures and videos that he took and talks about his adventures to link them to course content. He also brings stuff to the lectures to show like fossils and other cool things.

Great prof and knows how to keep his students engaged. Very well spoken and seems to enjoy teaching and sharing his passion with students. He does put hard questions on tests though so beware but with the way he teaches its doable to get them correct.

He was a very very good lecturer, his lectures were fun, engaging, and he really cared about the materials that he was teaching. His examples and information was research he conducted which was cool.
