Absolute banger. Great prof. His lectures gave me immense pleasure even if I was not acquainted with biology at all before the course. Stark contrast with some other tedious prof who taught the other parts of the same course.

Professor Hendry is an amazing professor. I've never seen a teacher that's so passionate about what he's teaching. His pre-lecture videos show that he puts a lot of thought into what he's teaching. His classes are probably the most fun as well, he engages with the students a lot.Great professor and I'm glad I had him for my first semester at McGill

Hendry's lectures were fun because he really connected with the students and used his own research and pictures to mix into the material. I beliveved his content was the most straight forward because it was evolution and vertebrates. As long as his ego doesn't grow TOO much, he is undoubtedly the best professor in the Mech Eng department. Take his course, please.
Very easy to understand

For MECH201 Higgings is great. The course itself is very content heavy but all quizzes are online. Notes are posted. He is very engaged with his content and makes lectures engaging. The end of year project was pretty challenging but achievable - thanks to Higgings and TAs. Would highly recommend as a prof.

Best prof I have ever had. This man is super interesting, and he explains the material very well with great visuals. You can tell he's super passionate about engineering, and it carries on to students like me.
Amazing prof in the department of mech eng.

His class notes are excellent, and his lectures are inspirational. He brings real-world examples to the class and shows practical applications. Exams are very fair, and assignments help understand the material. Responsive to students in-person but might not reply to every email.

Overall, undoubtedly the best professor in the Mech Eng department.
Prof. Higgins is amazing, if you have him the course will be fun.

Awesome prof, super articulated and engaging in class. Perfect prof for an introductory mech eng course since we covered a lot of aspects of the field. Good drawing and notes, great lectures. He's also well respected for research and design teams involvement. Hope to take him again

I've taken 2 courses with Prof Higgins and he is by far the best. Im at the point where I'm experiencing withdrawal symptoms, he's that good. His lecturing is really engaging and he is an amazing human being with actual empathy. Fair.
Good prof but the stuff he teach are pretty random
super nice guy. incredibly understanding and you can tell he cares for his students:) would recommend!
Great professor. Really caring and is always willing to listen to feedback. The class was well taught.

Great prof! Gives very good lectures and is super considerate for extensions. First prof to ever reach out to me when I got a bad grade for an assignment. Would highly recommend taking a class with him.
He is the best professor. I really recommend his class!
I loved his class. If I can, I will take his class again. 100% suggest
Terrieble, horrible, unbearable, very terrible organization of information conveyed, he doesn't know how to convey the information, the lecture slides are very confusing
He was the best prof I had this semester. He genuinely tries to help you. I would recommend taking the course with him.

He is literally the best! Always has a ton of office hours, and very willing to help students succeed. Literally canceled the midterm because he had students telling him they were too stressed to handle it given COVID. Always posts solutions to assignments & past finals/midterms. His assignments are tough, but fair, and he'll help you if you need.

He is honestly the best prof I have had this semester. He is so caring and really wants students to succeed. His assignments are hard, but fair, and there is always a relatively similar example in class notes or tutorials.

Wonderful and funny prof. Loved the chance to do some creative writing. He's super open to student feedback. Even though this class was fairly "experimental," which I think some might have been put off by, you learn so much.

This was my favourite class I've taken at McGill. Prof Pipey is SO funny, very kind and knowledgeable, and very susceptible to peer pressure. Class tended to get derailed, but he took it in stride. He's very clever and treats his students as equals. Papers are hard but he really just wants you to write a structured essay so crack the code + ur good

Prof. Andrew Piper has funny and engaging lectures. He didn't really give any feedback though. The syllabus also says that we are graded on attendance and participation yet neither of those things ever seemed to be brought up so not sure how the mark for that was determined.

I loved Prof Piper's lectures, they were honestly the highlight of my academic week and the discussions always made you think. I really did not enjoy Piper's GERM259. He is clearly a very intelligent man and knows a lot about literary theory and German literature, but he is unorganized, vague, uninterested, and uncaring. Do yourself a favour and don't take this class. I don't want to be mean because he is a very intelligent prof, but being in his class as a student was not pleasant. Not very organized, and grading criteria (and grades for that matter) always unclear.

Prof. Piper is a genuinely kind and caring person as well as an absolutely brilliant, captivating lecturer. Esp. if you're a first year and are feeling lost/reduced to a number, this course is a must - classes with Prof. Piper were the only times that I felt remotely human this semester. He can make you work for the grade, but it is 100% worth it.

Charismatic and captivating. Prof Piper presents all the key ideas of each book with passion. Prof Piper not only goes over major themes, but also explores the methodology of textual analysis. Thus, his course is quite accessible to students with no previous exposure to literature. Also, prof Piper is the lord of German literature memes. Fun class.

Dr. Piper is such an engaging lecturer! He is brilliant and funny. Tests are easily doable as long as you go to class and take notes. If you are typically a good student, you will have no problem taking this class.

Such a discouraging class. No concrete feedback on how to improve. When it comes to participation, considering its an important component to his class, the least he could do is learn his 30 students' names
Avoid at all costs especially for advanced calculus
TERRIBLE....... Take at your own risk - you've been warned
Poor reviews are not hard. Andy puts a lot of work into the summary notes and office hour. Good guy if you ask him for help!

I see a lot of poor reviews but I thought he was a good prof overall. His lectures were pretty good in that he explained theoretical examples which were helpful for the exam. Assignments were hard but great prep (summary notes also very helpful). Overall, hard and fair exam, but he curved so no complaints here. Would take again

Overall a good prof who actually cares about his students. His lectures are clear and he's well prepared, and posts good notes online afterwards. Although very smart, a very poor teacher. The worst quality is that he is very arrogant and never accepts the fact that students perform poorly because of his horribly ineffective teaching methods. Prof. Wan definitely knows the material inside-out, and he thinks his students are on the same level of understanding. Both his midterm and final were heavily theoretical/conceptual questions. And yes, 15 brains working together isn't enough to solve his assignments.
the best math prof in mcgill

His heart is in the right place, he's a cool guy and he clearly knows his stuff, but he expects far too much from his students. Professor Wan is incapable of clearly explaining concepts in vector calculus and PDEs. Throughout most of his lectures, the class was confused about the material. Took a course with her a very long time ago. She was a fabulous teacher.
Excellent. Teaches very well but do not play with her. Very fair.
Cool

She's a great teacher who now teaches at the Lebanese American University Campus in Jbeil. She takes the time required to explain and won't stop helping you till you're on the same waves, on the same paths.
Excellent teacher! Took COMP202 with her when I was at McGill. She made me love CS. Amazing! I still remember her explaining in class.
Excellent teacher! Wish she still teaches at McGill!
Excellent prof! MUST take the course with her!
Excellent teaching skills. Makes everything sound simple and clarifies complex issues.

Best teacher! Excellent and very fair.
Prof. vanhaelen is very understanding, and her classes are always very interesting. I recommend taking a class with her if you're in art history

I just finished taking her Dutch Republic Visual Culture class, and it was my favourite at McGill so far. Her lectures are so interesting, and you can tell she knows so much about art history. I never would have thought I would learn so much about so many things that go well beyond what one would think is related to the Dutch Republic. So amazing!!
I loved this prof, the lectures were very interesting. Although there was a lot to memorise for tests, it was still accessible.

Very sweet profesor. There were some readings, essays and testing of knowledge. Overall diverse class. She teaches well and answers to questions nicely. I did get confused at times as to why certain pieces of art were choosen for the topic taught but overall would retake this prof for her good class.

She's very nice. Lectures were dense (PPT with 80-100+ slides) but were recorded and uploaded after class which made reviewing material for the midterm and final easier. She prepares and lets you know in advance what to expects on exams (form of long essays) and how it's graded. I'm not good at writing but still got 75-80% on the assignments.

Prof Vanhaelen was personable and clearly extremely passionate about the subject matter (Visual Culture of the Dutch Republic). Lectures were at times a little dry (especially if you're not super passionate about 17th century Dutch art) and evaluations were definitely not something you can do in one night (pretty dense, but not too many of them).

She is so sweet and knowledgeable! I sometimes felt like the lectures were dense but she is very helpful and willing to help everyone understand. I thought the grading was fair and the class breakdown was very manageable. She is accessible for questions and wants everyone to also fall in love with Dutch art.

Vanhaelen is an amazing professor. She is so sweet and knowledgeable about what she's discussing. She also has so much experience that she inserts little bits of information and facts that only someone with insane knowledge could know off the top of her head. I'm U0 and took her 300 level course but it was my fav/most easy.

Shook that there are no ratings more recent than 2019! Prof. Vanhaelen remains one of the most caring and respected profs in the department. In her 200 level classes she gives engaging lectures and readings, while as a research supervisor she shines in her ability to offer applicable feedback while supporting the personal growth of her students.
Such an engaging lecturer. I really love my class with her and find myself wanting to stay longer after class ends. The assignments arent too difficult either, and the grading isnt harsh at all.

Truly inspiring: knowledgeable and humble, rigorous and fair, thorough and understanding, creative and scholarly. She creates such a positive environment where everyone is encouraged to contribute (and take risks). Her assignments are diverse and engaging, her classes fun and interesting, her course life-changing for anyone working in education.

Dr. Galante is my favorite professor in Mcgill. Choose her courses without hesitation! Trust me! No heavy stress, and the types of assignments are interesting. The most important thing is her work will change your traditional opinions on Education and really helpful for your study or future career. It's really worthy to take her course!

I came here to tell everyone who can to take Prof. Galante's class, as it truly changed my outlook on education. I was very surprised to read some unkind comments. 
Prof. Galante is a true gem and McGill and future educators are lucky to have her. She led us to think critically and inspired us to aim for greatness. Truly an incredible prof.

The course load was good. She preaches that mental health is her priority and for everyone to feel free to rest at home when they are not well but mid semester completely rips the class for going to doctors during her class. She forces everyone to participate in activities at the start of every class which no one enjoys.

Her course is a required course for the MA non-thesis program, however, she seems not to like Canada and the department she's working for. Claimed as an immigrant, sometimes has cynical comments about Canadian styles etc. Well, if you take it for the sake of the requirement for your degree, I guess we have to endure her never-ending opinions.

A super prof! She's caring and will go out of her way to help students. Prof. Galante is so smart, wellspoken, and very humble. She creates a positive and inclusive environment where students feel comfortable taking risks. Plus, her classes are SO engaging and she makes the content relevant and applicable! I wish I could take more of her courses.

Anila is amazing! She's super caring of her students and really wants everyone to succeed, she is very flexible and willing to negotiate if you have issues. Her instructions can be unclear at times but she always makes sure you are on the right track for whatever she's asking for. Would definitely recommend if you are interested in teaching science

Education courses are typically really vague and kind of pointless. Not everything was worthwhile but this was definitely one of the best education department courses.

amazing professor,, she is very helpful and kind. you feel happy in her classes as she always smiles and respect her students. she always encourages me and tell me that i can do the job. she is just (great).
The best professor ever.  I loved her class and learned a lot.
very nice lady! take her!!

Dr. Asghar is fantastic.  She is warm and approachable while maintaining a clear professionalism.  Her courses were very demanding, but also very useful.  She respects her students and values their input both in an outside of the classroom.

Prof Animesh made really good videos of the material, which was perfect if you missed a class or didn't understand something in class. Take him

Professor Animesh is very kind and approachable. The material can feel confusing at first, but it becomes much clearer with practice. He actively seeks student feedback and is very helpful during office hours. Overall, he supports students well and makes the learning experience smoother over time.
very heavy accent ,cannot understand what he is saying and his slides are disorganized

idk where to start. makes you do the grading & has TAs check you were honest. just have them grade it from the start. doesn't post grades so you do the exam not knowing where you stand. ask for clarification & gets defensive when the class is confused too. surprised he's employed despite these reviews but mcgill doesn't care & protects their own.

You'll get anxiety from his lectures. His method of teaching is disorganized and he overcomplicates simple concepts with long ramblings that he will say won't be on the exam and isn't relevant. slides and lectures are extremely all over the place; very disorganized. the content isn't difficult but he rambles often and makes a simple concept 10x harder than it has to be. and he yells when he teaches

I have taken SQL before and I can say he is the worst professor to teach this class. Teaching wise the professor has a very poor ability to teach the conent.
Good Teacher! Not always structured but lectures are interesting.

Biggest grade is for a grant proposal (which he doesn't teach how to make). Had to make an announcement because so many students complained about grading feedback being vague. The class was very disorganized. There were 3 50min classes a week (at least 1 class was cancelled weekly with little to no notice). When students asked questions, Prof Das just turned the question back to the class for students to answer, which was not helpful. Can be condescending

Amazing Professor, funny, caring, and always puts the class in a good mood. He has a great sense of humor and his lectures are very interactive which makes them interesting and dynamic. My favorite class this semester!

Prof was funny, and the course material was interesting. I took it online so I can not speak to his in-person course, however, we were graded on few things. It is fairly reading-heavy, but as long as you are acquainted with the reading material you should be fine for examinations. Would recommend, and would certainly take a course with him again.

Prof Das is amazing. One of the best profs I've had at McGill. He really cares about his students and engages people in discussions even in larger classes. Take any class with him I highly recommend it.

The course topics are so cool. e.g. how environment interacts with your genes. Prof. Das also gives amazing lectures. Several readings can be difficult, but he gives very helpful summaries on the slides.

One of my favorite profs at McGill. Lectures and discussions are so funny! He even provided study guides before exams. He definitely wants his students to do well. The exam questions also allows you to think and relate concepts with your real life experience. Would like to take more courses with Bobby!
Bobby is the best prof ever! He is so sweet and although attendance isn't mandatory you should still attend. He makes my day and takes the time to get to know everyone. Highly recommend.

The course is challenging and really trains your deductive logic, so I find it intellectually rewarding. The assessment is entirely based on group work, so make sure you find some collaborative partners and start everything asap. The prof is caring, patient but it's just creepy that he may suddenly appear behind you and see what you do on laptop.

Heard some negative things about quant fin but R with her is really enjoyable. She's accessible during and outside class time and made a good balance between finance with coding teaching. She's really guiding you through everything

With a new class, there will always be glitches and the material covered wont be taught to perfection. Some lectures were a little dry, but still interesting if youre interested in the topic.
Dry as toast

I came into this class with an open mind, but don't think I have met a teacher that unprepared, all over the place and unclear. I was dubious about the lecture format at first, which was less structured than I was used to. But it turned out to be a great class in terms of my own self-awareness. Inspiring and fun.

I took her Communication class this semester, it was mandatory and it was terrible. She wants everyone to participate but she is very picky when reviewing material in class settings. I didn't think she cared about teaching, it was more like she posted all the course material online and the student had to follow it
She's a very helpful teacher.
she moves round-I like that

I took the Honours version of this course (MATH537); same as MATH437 but with different grading & you do the final project alone. This was one of my favorite courses ever, even though it was quite challenging without strong knowledge of prerequisites.

Not helpful, a little bit rude, require too much, dont take his course if you have any other options. He is the worst prof I met at McGill. Definitely a tough grader, hard to communicate, and gave a hard final. He announced the duration of final for major was 2.5hr two minutes before exam starts. Same final exam for major&honour

He expects A LOT out of his students, is a passionate and intense professor, and goes at a very fast pace. You need to know a lot about Nonlinear Dynamics to understand his stuff, since his part of the course is a blitz. Really nice and engaging professor! She goes over key concepts multiple times, and her lectures/slides are pretty easy to follow. The pace she teaches is easy to keep up with too, even though there is a lot. Throughout the semester there isn't really any work to do except keeping up with the content because the midterm and final are pretty tough.
Very large introductory class, wish they would've published guidelines about concepts to know before the course given it had no prerequisites.

Her lectures were super interesting and she made sure to involve all the students. The slides are very clear and she often gives some cool facts, I feel like I learned quite a lot. However her portion in the exam was hard and it was often mandatory to have super accurate details.

She was super nice and so passionate and engaging. Amazing lecturer, unfortunately her content for Biol 111 was so detailed and very specific. There were so many little things to remember and exams tested these tiny details instead of big concepts. But you will most likely enjoy her lectures, she is very interactive and joyful always!

Her lectures were not very clear, she jumped around a lot between points, and she did not explain a lot of the concepts well that were central to her lectures. Her questions on both the midterm and final were extremely detailed oriented, instead of the main concepts discussed in lectures. Was not fair and dropped my grade exponentially.

Prof. Hargreaves is a kind and knowledgeable lecturer; her passion radiates to her students. My major complaint is that there are so many specific, random memorization-based details tested on the exams; I also wish they would give answers to past exams and be clearer on testable content (as opposed to "study everything").

Prof. Hargreaves gives amazing, clear and interesting lectures. She clearly cares about her students, stays after class to answer questions, and most of all, loves what she teaches! Be prepared for specific and detailed questions on the exams though. Certainly the best of the four BIOL111 profs!

Super sweet and stays after class to ask questions, then adds the answers to the slides afterwards. Lecturing is clear and you can see how the concepts interrelate. Be ready for specific details on the exam.

Definitely my favourite professor out of the four I had in BIOL 111. Her slides and presentation style are very engaging and she made it very clear what topics and vocab she wanted us to know. The exams were tough and often involved lots of material that we had to know just by memorization, but overall a great prof.

I took BIOL111 last semester and Professor Hargreaves is the only professor who lectured live (the other 3 just played pre-recorded videos) and this made a huge difference in my ability to engage with the material. Content was super interesting, she is very well-spoken, and is clearly incredibly intelligent.

Her lectures are very well structured: one day asynchronous where she teaches and one day where we do activities to apply the lecture. The feedback on assignments is useful for future assignments. Cares a lot about her students. Guest speakers are unique and insightful. 
Interesting but challenging assignments

Anna Kim is single handedly the most inspiring professor I have head at McGill. She is genuine, hilarious, passionate and extremely knowledgable. Her class is an open space to ask all questions and learn alongside your peers. Each class involved group tasks and extremely engaging discussions. The reading work load is very light. She is amazing!

She is very nice and sweet but she's a tough grader. She doesn't give As but I think all the teachers in MGCR360 grade like that. One class per week was asynchronous which I liked. Anna is an amazing professor. She is caring and dedicated, makes class interesting, is very accessible and the workload is very (extremely) reasonable compared to other professors. I had so much fun in this class, and it was honestly pretty easy if you went to class, she gave a lot of homework, but there was no final

Super kind teacher. The course is definitely intensive, with homework every day, and tests every week (after the first few weeks). A little too obsessed in the way she teaches and examines. Gotta be on her good side. The course itself is an easy elective though.

Professor Tumino made class time fun by changing up the schedule with partner activities, kahoots, and music. She was always willing to help, was a fair grader, and kept the class interesting. The class was alright. You learn a lot of verb tenses so it does get harder. She does give a lot of work. Additionally, she tends to redo questions that were already were given as homework. So that's annoying. Overall, she is a really nice woman and understanding of her students.

She is nice and won't make you feel stupid for asking questions but class can be a bit slow-moving and the exercises you go over in class can be tedious. The pace is understandable because I guess the class is meant for people whose only italian background is the 1 or 2 semesters of Ital 1. If you're good and quick in italian you may get bored

She's truly an amazing professor. Very understanding and very thorough. Thanks to her, i can speak italian after 1.5 years of learning it. She makes class fun and interesting. Lots of homework but it only helps us learn material more! Would highly recommend taking a class with her!

Amazing prof! She made the class very fun and it was super interesting to learn the language. So kind and very helpful, she understands you are new to the language. Lots of homework, but if you come to class and study you'll get a good grade.

Anna Maria is a great prof and makes things fun for a language course. There are many things that go into your final grade so its less stressful. She is a tough marker in the sense that there are rarely part marks. If you put in the work then you will get an A

Anna Maria is one of the nicest, funniest profs at McGill. She really cares about her students and will work with the class to make sure everything is manageable. She also is willing to go over past material that enough students didn't understand during class time. The environment she creates in the classroom is open, welcoming, and fun.
Her questions are doable if you study well, sometimes she puts traps or asks specifics but definitely doable. Her lectures are beyond amazing and her final questions were good too

She is beyond amazing ! She made the respiration section very manageable and easy to understand, her lectures were very well organized, her explanations were very clear and straightforward, the examples she gives really help with overall understanding. I lover her french accent, and everything about her ! One of the best profs at Mcgill !!!

Dr. Lauzon taught the respiration section. She explained pretty well. Her content involved a lot of graphs to know and imo was pretty dry. Her questions do sometimes require understanding topics and not just memorizing them, but they are still fair overall.

She's so sweet and her respiratory section is well explained. Some of the concepts might not make any sense and you just have to be like it is what it is and LOTS of graphs. Her questions are pretty fair.

Extremely nice and caring woman, but her slides are paragraphs of text that make things more confusing to understand. She covers the same topics in random places throughout different lectures, making the organization of thoughts and notes extremely difficult. Questions on exams were not too bad but make sure to supplement the learning yourself.
Love her classes. Make respiration simple and easy to understand.

The respiration section is definitely not the easiest to understand but she explains things really well and wants to make sure everyone gets it. Super helpful, and has an awesome french accent. Her explanations were complicated.
excellent professor, straight forward exam questions.
she is nothing special. sometimes there are serious gaps in her explanations which make easy concepts hard to comprehend
The course was interesting but I found that the Prof was rude and condescending at times during email interactions. She could benefit to learn SBN values as they in nursing.

While Annie was available to answer questions via email, I found her responses could have been more approachable and supportive. Also, the class content felt very disorganized. The teacher does not reply to her emails, the TAs basically carried the course. She made changes to the final exam, LITERALLY 2 days prior to the final. Though the final was fair, the last-minute changes were unnecessary and merely raised anxiety among students. You can definitely survive.

Does not care about her students. Does not respond to her emails. Her content is a mess. Prof doesn't teach, only reads the slides without explanation, is inconsistent throughout her lectures, gives contradictory information, quizzes are not accurate and are erroneous, made last minute changes in the final exam (<48hrs before the exam she added 10 questions and removed us the ability to return to a question once it was answered)
A very modest mathematics education course. With such teachers and their shallow focus on concepts, McGill resembles McDonald's among Micheline restaurants.
She could have had a better job in the registration office. Really disappointed with McGill.

Prof. S pretends to be a savvy professor, but her math knowledge is limited to elementary school. Such a great teacher! Loved having her as prof!
Annie is a great professor! I recommend taking her seminars + courses at McGill.

She is super sweet and very caring. Her lectures are always 3 hours, but she really takes the time to teach us properly. She wants us to be great teachers, and so prepares us for it. Extremely easy class if you do the work. Loved her. <3
The best supervisor possible.
She is the perfect guide to a great research.

Wonderful professor, very well respected and one of the only women professors at our school! Cares a lot about issues and topics that do not get explored in architecture, including gender issues. Very helpful with writing tips and thorough in her comments. Definitely take her courses!

Prof. Adams is one of the best teachers I've had. The clarity of her lectures is unsurpassed and she transmits her passion on the subjects that truly interest her. I still think about her lecture on post-modernism and Disney World architecture.  Very approachable, helped me write many scholarship, admission essays by reading them many times over

Simply wonderful - brilliant, clear and eloquent. I was always fascinated by the insightful things she had to say. Enigmatic character. Workload for this class is manageable; make sure to do the readings consistently (otherwise the amount will be difficult to handle for the final). It was a real pleasure taking her class.

Ms. Adams does not have the intellectual means of her ambitions. She has the knack to reduce fascinating subjects to her own despicable understanding. She if you are inquisitive, sensitive and passionate, and I measure my every word, stay away.

Sitting through an Adams lecture is like reading a dictionary. It's informative, but it's dry and sounds like a podcast, with no interaction whatsoever. Her lecture's are well organized and clear, but emotionless and passionless.
An outstanding research methods seminar -- only wish I had taken it years ago.  And Brava on becoming Director of the school.
I don't understand how she could be a teacher. Poor teaching capacity.
Interesting readings. Narrow-minded professor. Hard to approach (she makes you feel you are wasting her time)

While he is clearly knowledgeable about the topic, he assumes students are able to participate at a similar level, and grades harshly. I would not recommend taking this course unless you are able to devote an above-average amount of time, to receive average grades. The course also has lots of assignments with little or inconsistent instruction.
he is a bit monotone so you have to make an effort to be interested in the course content. you get to write policy briefs in his course which is epic. takes ages to return grades to you.

Gives zero guidelines for any of the papers and grades extremely harshly with super vague feedback. It feels as though he rips you apart regardless of what you submit. Would not recommend to anyone to take this course. Group project worth 55% of your grade and he picks the teams.

Prof. Masi is admirable without a doubt. His lectures though... try not to fall asleep, ppts are heavy, he's quite monotone. The project/essay is ridiculous especially if you have to carry the whole thing yourself... study a lot for the final and you will pass. If you can avoid the class though, do so. You need to really be interested in this.
Terrible professor, don't understand how he is still allowed to teach. Tears you down with negative feedback for group projects and papers.

Hes a great prof that truly cares about his students, his office is always open for you to come in and ask questions. His lectures are boring though and not really necessary because he posts everything online. He grades a bit harshly in the assignment and project but the final exam is very long and he most likely curves it.

His lecture slides are more than 100 pages, with repetitive materials and that will confuse you! Group projects are graded harshly with very vague feedback because he does not have clear grading criteria. He is approachable outside of class, but with more confusing advice as well. He expects wayyy too much from his students from his awful lectures!

Not a good professor, so many slides with at least 100 per slide decks with a lot of useless information. He also has a monotone voice that truly does not make you want to attend class. Would not take again.
One of my worst classes. Disorganized professor, 150-slides long powerpoints, lots of reading, not diversified topics.

I haven't had Ricciardi for any courses in which he's been the exclusive or even primary lecturer, but I wanted to rate him anyway cause I think he's great. He gets really into whatever he's talking about, and he can be tremendously funny. He's lectured in other courses I've taken and I looked forward to it every time and was not disappointed.
he's clear in lectures, but grading is a bit harsh

Enjoyed this course and the prof but be sure to KEEP ALL YOUR GRADED ASSIGNMENTS! Mine and another student's grades for one assignment were entered as a zero, and no grades were posted online until after final grades were released. He refused to change my grade because I no longer had the graded copy, even though I had the assignment file.
Very good prof. Obviously enthusiastic about what he teaches. This was a great course.

Super easy class; however, professor is super unapproachable and despite clearly marking some information in the slides, incorrectly marks some answers on the tests which directly contradict information on slides. I hope I don't have to take another class with him honestly (and this is coming from someone who did well in the class with no effort)

Really good teacher, loves what he teaches. Presents material in an organized way, tells you exactly what to not study for exam, and midterm. He is an awesome professor and would definitly reccomend taking a class with him. Just be prepared for fast talking, so take lots of notes :)
LOVE HIM! very passionate, talks fast and with full enthusiasm. clear, helpful and sometimes humorous :)

Tony is pretty much everything you would want a professor to be. He is crystal clear, covers the important topics over and over again, and loves what he teaches. Tests are easy as long as you go to class and lab.

Dropped in on this class just for fun on the first day, but he made the material extremely interesting by including anecdotes and personal stories. He talks quite a lot, so be careful if you ask him questions, but he is very passionate and knows how to give an entertaining lecture.
Excellent prof, full of energy and enthusiasm.  Holds your attention from beginning to end.

Professor Chan has been a wonderful teacher. She is very accessible, holding office hours regularly and a weekly tea chat, and is very responsive to emails. Her lectures are organized well and she is a great speaker. She encourages students to engage with each other during class and easily balances lecturing with group/one-on-one discussions.

Amazing prof! It seems like there have been several negative comments here. I would say she's excellent for teaching senior math courses. She's so passionate when explaining difficult concepts and everything is so smooth. A withdraw is she assigns lots of (difficult!) HW, but perhaps that's the best way to learn maths! Recommendddddd!
Never have I ever wanted to drop a class solely due to the professor before. Too bad this is a required class or I would have.
learned alot, lots of homework

This was back in Fall 22 but the ratings are a bit low so figured I'd weigh in. She's a great lecturer, very nice, amazing course notes. Analysis 1 convinced me to go through with honours math so I am grateful to her. B+ average the semester I had her and I thought the evaluations (and the grading scheme, 40% final) were very fair.
Extremely time-consuming and excessive assignments. Lectures seem good until you take an exam in this class and realize your time would have been better spent skipping class and reading the textbook.
avoid at all costs

The Professor is a wonderful person and charismatic speaker. MATH 318, however, was an incredibly difficult class for me. Very abstract, but rich in depth. The course material is tricky, which is reflected in the assignment and test grades. Her lectures can also be hard to follow (if writing on paper, not a tablet). The flexible grading saved me!

Good lord was this course tough. 318 is definitely very content heavy and abstract. The topics are super interesting! But the grading and difficulty really throws it all off. I would only recommend this class if you have a great math/logic background and can consume large amounts of info very quickly and effectively. The final was killer.
MATH 564 was a positive turning point for me as a mathematician, and Prof. Tserunyan's kindness and openness to feedback made the process, albeit grueling, feel warm and fruitful
Prof is nice and funny and it's not her fault, it's the course that is too hard (for me)...I struggled a lot but thankfully the final only takes 35%.

Dr. Suvrathan is an amazing lecturer and an even better person. She is by far one of my favorite professors at McGill. I looked forward to her lectures and her sunny energy. Her section was the most engaging and she genuinely cares about her students and their education. I would definitely take one of her classes again.
Amazing lecturer, clearly passionate about the topic she teaches.
She's simply the sweetest professor and very committed to students' understanding and growth! I would highly recommend taking this course if you can!!

This is the best prof I have ever had. She is incredibly sweet and intelligent, making a difficult class digestible. She is very interested in the material and goes out of her way to ensure we understand the material. Her exam questions were not difficult, if you take the time to watch the lectures and understand the main concepts you will do fine.

One of if not the best prof I've had. Everybody loves her lectures because of how engaging she is with teaching the content and how much fun she has with it! Very clear, always will answer your questions, and she cares a lot about the success of students. I would highly recommend!!!

You can tell she is very passionate when lecturing and that she cares about her students!! Very talented at explaining difficult concepts in a way that one can understand, while being encouraging/motivating. I really enjoyed her teaching style

Prof Suvrathan is my favourite prof at McGill. She's so enthusiastic about what she teaches and is so sweet! She also makes grading criteria for an assignment very clear, and the projects she assigns are really fun!

A literal ray of sunshine in the blues of second year. So kind, so clear, so coherent. Her slides are thorough, she makes an effort to summarize main topics after each key concept, and she also has a lot of great studies that she draws in to complement the content.

Enthusiastic, knowledgeable and acknowledges when things are beyond their scope of expertise. Goes above and beyond to enthusiastically progress the class and actively participates in class discussion to guide students. Actively available after class.

I love this professor. One of the best I've had at McGill, if not the best. The lectures are already super interesting but she makes them even better. She explains concepts really clearly and even shows fun videos of the experiments she's talking about. Her teaching style is amazing. Love her!

Ara is an amazing teacher, and everyone in film knows and loves her. she's very opinionated, and although it's because she's passionate, she can push her opinions sometimes. She is very knowledgeable and very caring to her students -she was especially understanding when I told her I couldn't come to class because of illness, takes attendance tho

I loved the way this class was constructed- we learnt about the historical context of a movie, then watched it, and then discussed it. The prof is very interesting and knows what she's talking about. There is a lot to memorise but it is worth it.

Ara is a great professor - her lectures are engaging, and I always left the classroom feeling like I'd actually learnt something. Her assignments were very fair and evaluation/grading was much more generous than I expected. Absolutely take a class with her if you can - her courses are challenging, but definitely worth it.
Ara is a great teacher, and her passion is palpable. One thing I will say is the screenings being mandatory was way too much- cannot do 4 hours of class time

Will she absolutely rip into your film analysis despite never having done one in your life? Yes, she most definitely will. Will you say something in front of the class and she just say uh no that completely wrong and move on? Yes again. But you can tell she so passionate about classes. She has really great lectures and I did love her assignments.

The class material is interesting and the prof is very passionate, but there are 3 conferences throughout the semester and weekly MANDATORY screenings most weeks, and the two 1.5 hour lectures are not shortened to accommodate this extra time, but we are still only given 3 credits for the course despite attending class for up to 4.5 hours a week

Being from New York does not excuse self-righteousness. I'm from Queens, so Osterweil's attempts to justify her rude behaviour seem ridiculous. Acknowledging complaints she has received in the past, she will, in the next breath, claim to be misunderstood, though nice people usually do not have to convince others of their kindness.

Prof Osterweil is a great teacher - she is really knowledgable, and inspiring to listen to. Classes are discussion based, with no devices, so participation is important but it makes for a more engaging class. I found grading to be harsh, but generally fair with lots of detailed feedback given. Would definitely recommend her class.

IMO Ara is an excellent prof - she's engaged, passionate, and every knowledgeable. Much of the course is centred around discussion, so you really have to participate. She can seem tough at times and will disagree with you, but it is never in bad faith. She cares deeply about her students, gives plenty of feedback and is really encouraging!

Ara Osterweil is an incredible professor. She cares deeply about her students, gives incredible feedback, fosters community, and encourages creativity. In ENGL 443, we read experimental non-fiction works, wrote our own "fragments" for submission, and had total freedom on the final. I highly suggest taking any class with Ara-- she is wonderful.

He's such a sweetheart. I would definitely recommend him; his lectures were very clear, the readings were pretty interesting yet a bit heavy, and conferences were so interesting and a great place to discuss authors' theories. Even though he's known as a tough grader, once you understand what he wants, it's clearly easy to get at least B+/A-.

Hands down one of the best professors or educators I have ever had. Professor Abizadeh is engaging, intellectually-challenging, and inspiring. I thoroughly enjoyed every lecture. Although the content was dense and tough, and his no tech policy was initially scary, due to the style of examinations throughout the semester, I could see improvement.

Do not recommend if you care about your GPA. Unfortunate because the material is interesting, and no technology helps you remember and understand better. The grading was very harsh, and there were discrepancies between TA's. The "quizzes" in class have unrealistic expectations. Although the professor was engaging and knowledgeable.

Would recommend! Great professor and great lectures. No devices were allowed, so pen and paper. 4 quizzes in total, but he drops your lowest quiz (3 worth 20% each). 20% is conference participation/attendance, and 20% is your final paper. Readings are a huge part of the class, but as long as you understand the authors' ideas, they're not mandatory.

Hands down one of the best professors I've ever had.
Although the class was very reading-heavy, he never failed to make the lectures engaging. He is incredibly passionate about what he teaches and truly cares about his students' learning. He didn't allow devices in class, but I ended up really appreciating it and found myself more focused. 10/10.

The only course this semester in which I did not once get bored. It was intellectually stimulating and his lectures were engaging. Clearly he's passionate about the topics but also about teaching.

Some things to keep in mind: he only posts lecture outlines and his quizzes are difficult at first but with help and practice it's possible to do well.

He's such a sweetheart! It's clear he cares about the content and about his students' success. Don't be afraid to say you don't understand something he says, he's very open to re-explaining, especially during office hours. He was so much more helpful than my TA lol. He's opposed to technology but I got most of my readings as a PDF and it was fine.

he is a great professor, he clearly cares about the content he teaches and his lectures are interesting.There are lots of books to read though so its def a harder 200 level class, but overall it's super interesting. Lot of quizzes, final paper (not exam), but he drops your lowest quiz mark. 
he's a sweetheart, would recommend !!

Yes, good lectures, interesting information, engaging, but I wouldn't recommend this class. For a 200-level, the expectations are too high. I had a great TA, and I could sense they felt the same. It was clear people were struggling, yet nothing changed. Interesting content, but felt like I couldn't enjoy it b/c of the pace and grading.
A passionate teacher that makes you feel politics more than learn it.
the final exam is worth 70%, provided no lecture recordings, and lacked both organization and consistency. He never responds to discussions : avoid his classes

Honestly I just find myself very very lost during his lectures and in general he is not good at projecting nor teaching. I am really scared about the 70% final and he said we will not have any practice material.

Super knowledgeable, but lectures were slow and repetetive(maybe due to lack of material?) He spoke a lot about industry applications, which was cool.Assignments were super easy, and the final was a copy-paste of them. You could get away with skipping lectures, but you'd miss out on some great advice. Cool teacher, easy A.
lectures are lowkey philosophical. we were all stressed for the final but it was all application, no proofs.

This is one of the most interesting course I've taken at McGill. Archer is kind and approachable. The grading is fair with an average of A. You can tell he really cares about his students.
I especially liked when he'd sometimes drift off the syllabus to share thoughts on artificial intelligence and philosophical topics, sparked by course materials.

Very helpful and well-structured course. The content is extremely useful and clearly presented, making even the more complex topics approachable. The professor was very caring and always made time to support students, whether through office hours or thoughtful feedback. His dedication to teaching and student success really stood out.

I personally did not mind him. Yes the class could have been a lot more organized but I found that the topics were super interesting so I was very engaged during the lectures. Not super accessible outside of class and the assignments could have been more clear but it was not the worst thing in the world.
the worst professor ever. he cant teach

Very intriguing and useful course (but not easy). Prof. Yang did a lot to motivate and engage students: relevant visuals and applications, clear and detailed explanation of challenging math, continuous updates to course materials showing his commitment to rigor. Managing a large class while developing the curriculum, he did an excellent work.

He's not the best lecturer and was slow to give grades and fb (TA strike, maybe), but the material was very interesting and presented nicely. He was helpful during OH and gave cool projects. I don't get where all the hate's coming from, really. He referred us to the slides for study material (which is very reasonable) and did a final review session

One of the most well spoken profs I've ever had, which makes for very clear lectures. Concepts in PHGY311 can be confusing at times but his explanations are clear and his test questions are fair. Do the practice problems and you will do well.

Challenging class - few assignments but worth a lot. The TAs grade harshly. Lots of readings that are necessary for takehome assignments. You can't survive this class without readings/lectures. Salvatore is a little hard to understand. If you put in effort, it is possible to get well, but would definitely not want to put myself through it again!

Good prof overall but his accent is really heavy and sometimes made him very hard to understand. They grade pretty harshly depending on the TA grading you but in the end if you work well and keep up with the readings you can get a good grade.

The online aspect of this class detracted from it a bit, as it was all pre-recorded and a-synchronous but professor Salvatore held weekly Q/A sessions that were really helpful. Overall a really great prof and a fascinating subject

I agree with other reviews that he has great detailed slides. I had difficulty understanding his accent in a large echoey lecture hall, & depended heavily on slides to understand the content. I found the assigned reading was long and repetitive, but not difficult. Would not take again simply due to not understanding lectures well.

I attended his classes in the most ancient university of Oriental Studies in Europe, and his courses on Islam were an amazing intellectual experience, which provided impulse and orientation to the rest of my academic life
Really great professor. He is exceedingly knowledgeable about what he teaches and he cares about his students. He made the subject truly interesting. I enjoyed his class, and his teaching style.

One of the best experiences I had with a course. The class is demanding, but slides are very good and it is not difficult to follow. I also liked the Professor's style. He has some accent but he is very passionate when he lectures. He is also very helpful.
Excellent slides. Transitions could be improved but the class experience is superb. Prof is passionate and caring

He has a very thick accent which is tough to understand. His lectures are very difficult to follow and the entire time you feel a little confused. This made it difficult to answer the questions for the midterm paper. However, many of my friends are getting As in his class and the lectures are recorded so it's not too difficult.

Honestly hard to follow lectures and are graded heavily on 2 essay-type take-homes (40% midterm-60% Final). Readings are short though, so there is that but if you don't attend lectures, it's hard to answer the questions on your papers, bringing me back to how he's not the best lecturer.

Great prof, uses specification grading, so if you do all of the necessary essays, you will get an A. Very kind and understanding of how busy students are, does his best to have a variety of guest lecturers.

Excellent course.  Teaching staff is caring and available for help. If you are motivated to learn and succeed (and attempt using ethical frameworks that might not be intuitive to science students), you will get a good grade.

NSCI 300 was one of my favourite courses this semester, with many guest lecturers and interesting lecture topics. I thought that the assessment scheme was very fair. Dr. Yazdani is not only a very caring professor but also very intelligible and helpful.

Really interesting class! A broad range of topics are covered by different guest lecturers, and you can pick the topics you're interested in to write your papers on. Although there's quite a bit of writing involved, it's very doable if you put in the time and effort. Highly recommend for those interested in research ethics and/or medical debates.

Overall an interesting course that I really enjoyed. Lots of writing! Start writing commentaries as soon as possible, don't leave them until the end. The feedback you receive on your commentaries will be helpful for the final paper. Very possible to receive a good grade if you put in the time and work.

Took NSCI 300 in Winter 2019 as part of requirement. We had guest lecturers from so many different fields - I learned so much and it was one of my favourite courses in undergrad! You will definitely learn things you don't learn in other science courses. There's a quite a bit of writing involved, but you will do well as long as you put in the work!

Took NSCI300 as part of a requirement and it has been my favourite class of my undergrad - to the point that I TEAM TAed the next year. Neuroethics puts a new perspective on scientific knowledge. Don't have to go to all the classes, only really the ones that you write commentaries on. Be prepared to write!

Although I had no prior research experience before taking this course, Armin was very patient with me. More importantly, in addition to teaching me the lab techniques, Armin taught me a lot about research ethics and trained me to think critically. Overall, Armin was a very responsible and inspirational teacher who I would definitely recommend.

Took NSCI 300 in Winter of 2019 and was a TEAM fellow in Winter 2020. This class is an easy A if you don't leave your thought papers to the last minute and experiment with different ethical frameworks because this will help you with the midterm and the final. You won't get A if you don't do the work. Also, ask questions! Armin is very helpful!

Hilarious guy! You should NOT take his course if you are not confident in French, as he speaks very quickly, but is always happy to repeat info if asked. He is very funny and a very animated and effective lecturer, but his tests are QUITE difficult, and he expects a lot of specificity. If you go to class and take detailed notes you should be fine.

Honestly love this teacher!
I have to precise that he does speak fast so if you are not familiar with french, it's gonna be quite difficult.
But you can clearly see he loves the subjects that he teaches, goes back to things that were misunderstood and personnally the no powerpoint thing truly didn't bother me. Plus he's hilarious. Would recommend!

He does not use slides of any kind but he writes important points on the board. You definitely need to be good at writing notes while listening, but he is more than happy to repeat things for those who ask. He has a great sense of humour but can speak a little quickly, so make sure you're comfortable enough in French. Overall, would recommend!

He is definitely one of the most meticulous professors at McGill. In his class, expect to give long and detailed answers and to use all the knowledge you can gain. However, he is very knowledgeable, applies concepts in different examples, and makes sure all the students understand the course material. I would definitely recommend him.

This prof is absolutely terrible. He doesnt believe in power points or any notes at all for that matter. So get ready to type as fast as you can, since all he does is talk very fast and expect you to catch everything. The course tests are entirely memorization, and he marks extremely hard. Even if correct, he will not give full marks. DO NOT TAKE

Formatting of his content is very hard to understand, but once you get it, it's pretty easy and many of his questions or T/F. But he talks about how annoyed he is to be dealing with students in front of students, and weirdly annoyed that people in his class want to succeed... Still would retake though because he's easy lol

My second favourite prof of this course. So funny, spent like the first half of class once ranting about how premeds are annoying (which they are). Super chill exam questions, I studied more than I needed to for his section.

Not awesome but not awful either, his content is just horribly formatted. He talks about one experiment to another in his PPs and it feels like I am straight up studying different facts about either the cell cycle or cancer and not their process in details. Makes studying 10x harder due to lack of connections between his slides.
Really uninterested and boring lectures

Incredibly uninterested and uninteresting. Clearly a professor who sees teaching as an annoying requirement to his research and makes it clear to his class. Just memorize the textbook and you'll be fine sadly.
Boring, but explains well. Just make sure to memorise everything

Lectures are meandering and disorganized. He seems to have little interest in whether students actually learn the material: he responds to questions after class or request for office hours with "Read the textbook." However, he also can't be bothered to write test questions so most will be True/False. Don't count on recorded lectures.

Very rude prof. Slides are literally screenshots of the text and diagrams from the textbook. Refused to answer any questions during the midterm review, instead teling students to "read the textbook"  most of his questions on the midterm were poorly worded and True/False. You can tell this guy doesn't care about teaching.

Very interesting lectures, he has slides but explains beyond what's written on them, so it's good to take notes during class. However, he barely tests you on stuff that's not written on the slides. His section was about cancer and you can see that he knows well what he's talking about, made me want to pursue research in that area!
The worst professor in McGill
Very chill prof. Explains like a storyteller.

here's the deal, this may be one of the only people that you will actually learn from here. if your goal is to get a perfect gpa and move onto high society, i can't speak for whether you'll like his work. but if you have some desire to suck the juice out of life and find some sort of truth and break your mind down to its bones, then join.

As a person, he is amazing and I could listen to him teach all day. He is super interesting and very knowledgable about the topics he teaches. The problem is that we were only graded on the midterm and final, each worth 50%. He is a tough grader and gives zero feedback on the exams. I was expecting to do a lot better considering how much I studied.
In depth teaching.  Brilliant teacher
this is an incredible man. smartest man i have ever met

The TA does all the grading and responds to most of the questions (so if you need help go to himher first). The exam questions are provided before the exam so you do not really need to read the book (lectures are sufficient to do well). He can be hard to understand because of the accent, but he has such interesting things to say!!

Very interesting man who is extremely knowledgeable about world religions. His lectures were poorly attended, but I have no idea why! This man is one of my favourite McGill profs who should be respected for his knowledge. Do not take this course for an easy A unless you truly have an interest in world religions and are willing to study a bit.

This course is so easy, I only had some difficulty in the first part of the course,Which includes Hinduism,Taoism,Buddhism and Confucianism, Bcz I didn't know a single thing about them before taking this class.The second part is super easy and you can watch some youtube vids if you hate reading the book, this way everything will stick to your head

It's a shame nobody goes to class. While his accent is a bit hard to understand at times, you get used to it. Very wise man, an expert in the field. Class is incredibly easy. 1/3 midterm, 1/3 research paper, 1/3 non-cumulative final. As long as you go to the conferences, and memorize the terms you will get an A.
Brilliant man. Learned so much from this class, even though it was incredibly easy. Barely need the required book and don't need to attend class. You'll learn a lot about life if you do though.

He's a great person, but the way he structured consumer behavior was horrible. There were readings, pop quizzes, a midterm, a project, and additional lectures to watch. It was so hard to follow and I lost interest halfway through the semester. I wish I took this class with someone else. All of my friends agree. VERY ambiguous grading as well.

One of my favourite teachers I've had, and you can tell he is very knowledgeable in the field. He is so caring towards his students, and gives everyone an opportunity to participate. His slides are very unorganized, but the content is easy to review on your own. The midterm was very fair, and there is one big group project throughout the semester.
The professor is very nice and easy to get in contact with and his materials were interesting. However, despite his very detailed rubric, his grading is very tough.

He is such a nice prof and genuinely cares about his student's wellbeing. There are weekly "pop quizzes" but they help you stay on track with the course content. He is really knowledgable in consumer behaviour and it is a really interesting topic. I definitely recommend this class with this prof!
He prepares you well for his class through his pop quizes .
nice guy, fairly chill concepts once you wrap your head around it

Talks slower than the other profs for CHEM110 but his section moves fast so you need to keep up with the content vids. He's perfectly decent as a person and teacher, he just ended up with difficult material which made his section more annoying. Some of his content didn't get reviewed but was on the final, so seriously, ask questions when confused.

He seems to care about his students and wants us all to succeed. His content was pretty straightforward once you understood it, but that required a bit of extra research out of class as his lectures and videos weren't always clear. Overall, just very kind and gives fair exam questions.

He had the hardest section of CHEM 110 in my opinion (the most new content from highschool) but he did a great job teaching it. Some parts in concept videos were hard to understand and had to be rewatched many times or required further research, overall he's very kind and teaches difficult concepts well.

His pre-lecture videos and content were difficult to understand and it took further research to fully grasp the material his section presented. It also felt like we did not get through a lot during lecture. Note that attendance is mandatory once a week for review sessions, but these won't matter if you get an 100% on 7/9 quizzes.
His passion towards teaching students shows through. Despite covering the most difficult part of CHEM110, I get more encouragement by his teaching style and genuine care towards students.
Very good lecturer. Always ready to answer questions in class in a clear way without talking down.

He's funny and his voice won't make you sleepy, but mediocre at explaining things in the videos and not very good at explaining things during lectures. He's also a bit disorganized sometimes. His content is definitely the hardest part of CHEM 110, so have videos from the Organic Chemistry Tutor on standby.

His video lessons were a bit longer than the others but he did go over plenty of questions so that was good. The in class questions he did did not line up with the in class questions we were given so it was a little annoying in figuring out if we did things right. He does answer questions in class very well.

His lecture is great. Be careful, this course is much harder than you thought. Gives extremely difficult exam though say want everyone got an A. This is a good wish! Very unclear grading cateria. Harsh grader!

I know you are probably not taking this class by choice is just mandatory for a couple programs. Imma tell you right now its a terrible class loool a ridiculous amounts of slides and test are just always a bruh moment. Final is deadly bc he is so specific with what he asks and there is more than 1000 slides you will need to memorize.
Good professor, lot of slides but he would curve you into incredibly high marks. Dont feel stress during reading the contents, you would get a good mark.
Get ready to memorize 1000+ slides to get a decent grade for final. If u can choose to not take this course by ANY chance then just dont take it. literally just take anybody else

To start, he simply reads his slides during lectures, which makes the class monotonous and not at all engaging. There were also about 1400 slides by the end of the course, which the prof tells you to memorize for tests. You can imagine how that would play out...
All the grades are on tests, get ready for 150 formulas. Such a mess

I had him for MIMM211, an introductory microbiology class.. Professor Cousineau is a greater teacher and makes the content interesting. He wants his students to do well and he is super genuine. The midterm had a few tricks, but nonetheless a fair exam. Textbook not necessary, lectures recorded.
Professor Cousineau is the best professor I've ever had in the MIMM department. He genuinely loves teaching and cares for his students. He also gives fair exams.
Extremely caring prof, and that's what I like. Properly records lectures, gives helpful sample questions, gives fair test questions, and is friendly to every student without exception.

He's the best professor I've had so far at McGill. His lectures are clear and he has detailed slides that contain all the information you need to know Before the midterm he posted sample multiple choice questions with a paragraph explaining why each answer was correct. He's also a really nice guy and would chat with students before and after class

Cousineau is by far my favourite professor in the entire MIMM department. He is passionate about what he teaches (as a result he will answer every question to no end) and genuinely cares. Introduce yourself once and he WILL remember you. I've seen him stay behind over an hour to answer questions that weren't even about his lecture. Would rate 6/5!!

Great professor. Has an accent, but tries extra hard to be clear. The general consensus is that his material is well understood. Exam is straightforward, gives practice questions. He arranges slides so that they have most of your notes, and is therefore able to spend more time on difficult topics.
Super easy midterm if you review well. Very clear, seems like a really nice guy. I don't know if there is a textbook but you really don't need it
Down to earth genuine prof. Cares about his students. Entertaining lectures which keeps people from getting distracted. Nothing but good things to say about Dr. Gentil.

Just like any other regular core course, there is some amount of work to be done. It is often very clear on what and how you will be graded and you will always be tested on what you were taught, no surprises. Concepts are well explained in class. If you can learn the material as you would for any other class, this class is relatively light.

Professor Gentil is a very nice and likable guy. He explains the content well enough however, the course material is broad and dry in many ways. He has a bit of a French accent, how it is nothing terrible. Overall, the course was poor, but the professor was good.
Great class, the professor does a great job despite the material's dry nature. The course covers a wide breadth of content and is reflected in the difficulty of the exams.

Dr. Robaire is an absolute sweetheart. He genuinely cares about his students and was generally very supportive throughout the 4 months. He made sure to promptly respond to e-mail and address any issues in class. Albeit his slightly disorganized teaching style, he was always happy to answer questions and repeat as needed.

A very sweet and approachable professor who wants the best for his students. His exam requires you to study the material well. Long answers can sometimes be tricky, but marking was not too harsh. Presentation was very clear about what they wanted and not marked harsh either. A great prof who really loves his job and his students!
Good guy, gave chocolates in the midterm. Heavy lectures, lots of slides and material. Ask details in tests. Expert in endocrine and reproductive system.

Not the easiest class nor the hardest. Very nice prof, very approachable! The midterm was super easy but the final was hard (not because of this prof, but because of Culty and Zorytha). He never asks on difficult concepts and asks the basic stuffs! NTCs are really helpful!

I think the midterm was fair. He didn't ask tough questions at all, but you did have to know your material (not much of memorization, just understanding). Many concepts are very hard in this course and it seems that we don't have much time to go into details for every concept (but he won't ask for those things on the exam).
Whatever this man teaches immediately becomes unbearable to sit through. Dry, dense, disorganized, and horrifyingly unclear. Avoid this course at all cost.

Yeah, I honestly don't know which has more material to study: PHAR 303 or PATH 300. This prof didn't help things. Basically just memorize massive amounts of info, all disorganized and both overlaps and conflicts with the other profs teachings.
Agree to the previous comment. This is probably the most disorganized course at McGill. Talks about everything, expects you to know everything, with nothing explained. Avoid if you are in PHAR minor.
Not an enjoyable course. 100 useless slides per lecture. REally hard to know what to memorize and what not, and it was impossible to acutally know everything. This course was way too broad
Good lectures, available online, fair exam questions

This class was extremely boring and un-inspirational. I have taken many drawing classes in the past and very excited for this one, but it was by far the worst art class I have ever taken. I have never seen anybody before her capable of making an art class this bad.
Great prof! Expect to be pushed to do your best.  If you put in the effort you will do well!
strict drawing teacher that really knows her stuff. Is patient in that mean-but actually nice lady type of way

I took drawing 1 thinking it was going to be fun but i was so wrong.. this class is hard! do not expect easy grades.. i've worked hours on drawings that i got 7/10 on. She's also really mean and always has bad things to say about your drawing.. she loves to hear herself talk and rambles on forever about things that nobody understands!! avoid!
No Comments
She's got a tough attitude but knows her stuff. She is great to listen to and enjoys her Coca-cola more than anyone I know.
A lot of work but worth the effort...Really nice teacher

Great prof and a really engaging class. Almost half of grade is assignments which is a godsend. He and the TAs aren't afraid of giving full marks if you earn it. Just do the readings and speak up in class for the participation grades!
The course materials provided were organized and clear but what the course covered was so monotonous and boring that made me stop going to class.

Course is 'hard' because it makes you think. Very fair grader - usually only docking a mark or so if you've got the whole question wrong but shown effort in thinking. He's extremely patient, really good in terms of clarity (he repeats himself in various ways to make things clear). Altogether my favourite prof of the semester. Always approachable!
Hard to understand him and make possibly interesting material very boring.  I showed up to every class before him and I hardly go to any because I'm guaranteed to fall asleep.

Really nice and funny professor. The assignments were challenging at times, but the course overall wasn?t that hard. No text required, but the handouts are very clear. I really enjoyed this course. Made me love Semantics more!
Lovely, lovely prof.  The material isn't easy but he's clear, organized, helpful, intelligent, and amusing.  Very rewarding class.
No Comments

She is great
- Lectures were clear and informative, the course is useful and interesting
- Programming assignments taught me a lot
- Grading is fair, reasonable averages on tests
Prof clearly passionate and knowledgeable about the subject, but lecture slides are very unclear and assignments often ambiguous.

Professor Kemme was great, her lectures are very clear.  First part of the course is SQL queries only. The material of the second half of the course demands computation. had cheatsheets for exams(easy).A significant portion of your grade depends on a group(3-4)project, that has 4 different parts to it.very useful course for work, highly recommand.

The course itself is challenging regardless of the instructors. I don't regret taking this course since she is passionate and kind. You need time for 2 300-level courses to do well in COMP 512. So, choose your courses wisely, and know programming in multi-threading and Java(intermediate level). COMP 409 is more helpful than COMP 310.

Quizzes, Written assignments, Programming Assignments and Midterms... Programming assignments are incredibly tough and will make you regret choosing this class.
Topics are incredibly important, but prepare to work a lot.

So much homework, feels like a 6 credit course. I spent more time doing assignments for this class than all of my other classes combined. Her lectures were ok but not recorded and she sped through many topics. Quiz questions weren't even on her slides so that made no sense.
Group project so vague and intense. Ain't no way this is a 4 credit course.

I feel that Bettina is a nice person but the amount of content that's packed in...
Lots of group and team projects. If you don't finish them ahead of time, you are doomed.
The exam was brutal. Way harder than the mock exams. Glad the grading was a bit more lenient.

EXTREMELY mixed. I don't think she's the worst but things could have been MUCH better. Pop quizzes felt unfair (all-or-nothing MCQ). Abit messy/unclear when doing in-class examples. Cool material, it shows she knows her stuff on DBSMs, but WAY too much, more than a 3-credit course. Not generous with extensions. I would CAREFULLY take again as prof.
Lots of work for a 3 credit course. Very unclear instructions and just a horribly designed final exam. However, there is very important information about databases that you learn.

I don't understand the point reviews. It isn't changing or improving the system and there aren't options for students to avoid experiencing this teacher. 
The lack of teaching/hard grading made it clear that "being smarter" was more important than seeing people succeed. The material was easy but she made it seem so complicated for no reason.

2 required textbooks. Attendance is taken every class. Lots of group assignments that she doesn't correct until the semester is over and leaves more than 1 paragraph of comments. The mid term looked like the final with over 100 questions. You will never leave this class before 8:45 pm. This is ONLY the tip of the iceberg. Beware of Beverley!
Classes are poorly thought, rushes through subjects and material is unclear. Gives very little feedback on assignments, if any at all.
Amazing professor! Very caring and understanding. I enjoyed the subjects discussed in class. She understand the fact that we are in a pandemic and she took our needs seriously.

Considering she has been teaching this class for a long time she is a mediocre teacher at best. How many slides, videos, articles and acts can you read along with the text book. She can't control her class, we never get through the slides or rushed through. Assignments are not clear. She knows her stuff I will give her that but can't teach.

WORST group project I've ever had in my life!!! We worked on it so EARLY ON in the semester, took multiple days off from studying and essay writing to work on the project, WE STILL FAILED! if she doesn't like your faces forget it. redeemed myself from my essay and final. wouldn't recommend her...

If you like to sit all the way in the back of auditorium classrooms don't bother going to her lecture she literally only speaks to those in the first few rows like the others don't exsist! But she does in-class exercises every other week that can be done in groups. I'm sure there are better teachers but do what you have to do you'll get a B

Advice is to work on the group project EARLY. Between filming and editing it can be time consuming. It will leave you with no time to do the individual essay. But do the essay properly and put effort she will give you 80 % + on it. Compared to other teachers her content is EASY. Seriously the "pop quizzes" are done in groups and she gives 10/10

She's okay. Don't expect to have answers to ANY of your questions. She avoids all questions in person says she's ''too busy'' and rarely answers emails. Exams all MC memorize chps + powerpoints, 3000 word essay and group project sum up the class. Be very precise for group project - mention everything she asks for or she gives a 0 in that category.

Hopefully there won't be another class taught by her , Can't believe that she's in Health and Social Services , like come on seriously? Highly Unsuitable to be a "professor" & in Health & Social Services Industry
What a great prof!  Highly recommend!

If you have a physics/math background, this course will be very easy for you. I did not. Because of this, I really struggled at times. Bill is the most engaging and enthusiastic prof I had in my first semester at mcgill, his lectures are recorded, but still worth attending. You will learn a lot in this class. Final was tough. Memorize every slide.
