Just take this course. Easiest course I've ever taken at McGill, hands down. To those who were complaining about lots of class material--seriously? that work was not even 1/4th the work I had to do for all my other classes. Trust me, it's a bird course. his exam questions are REALLY easy

Great prof, this was an awesome class if you're interested in learning about how things in the world work. Probably my most enjoyable class this semester. Yes, the exam is hard because of the amount of material that you are required to memorize but assignments are an easy average booster.

This prof is a great prof! Whenever I went to his office hours, he would spend as much time as I needed to explain everything I was confused about. He truly cares about his student, and the course is pretty easy! I studied a day for the final and ended up with an A.

Yeah so if you're looking for an easy class I would definitely avoid this one. It's alot of memorization of obscure facts that are hidden in the slides. So unless you know you can memorize 737 slides in excruciating detail, you're gonna have a bad time.

Professor Coish is incredibly enthusiastic about his subject, and is excited for his students to find similar enthusiasms. He tries to be connect with students (experiments you can do in bars to show off and so forth), and is very clear. Great elective.

Recommended! Enthusiastic, funny professor. Provides help at office hours. For exams, read the notes, and do the practice exams! Occasional trivia questions do show up but in general very straightforward. I'm an arts major with no physics background at all and I ended up with 90+%.
memorize everything on his slides. even the most random facts that you think aren't important. he's a great prof and he made us ice cream!! :D

An assignment every two weeks can be annoying but if you put in the time you can ace em. Midterm was a breeze since it didn't cover too much.  Enthusiastic professor who tries his best to make the course interesting, and succeeds. Final was trickier only because of the amount of material. Memorize every detail on his slides, they cover everything.

I actually found Prof Ditto to be refreshing from other psych profs. He presented the material in his lectures as though he was conversing with the class. He didn't just read slides like a lot of other profs do. He's very helpful and approachable as well.

Nice guy and clear slides. Quite a lot of reading material and emphasis on the small details. There are quizzes that can help boost your mark as long as you do them carefully. Some of his questions can be ambiguous and tricky but that is every psyc class in general.

He's well-meaning but not a great prof. He doesn't speak clearly and midway through I decided not to listen to lectures and just use the textbook and lecture slides. If you are good at learning on your own then you can do well in this course. It's not hard material-anyone can understand it. He's sweet and will answer questions during the exam!

This class is so boring, worst Psyc class I've ever taken. Prof. Ditto seems nice and can be quite funny but his lectures are dull and it's difficult to understand the point he's trying to make. Exams are very difficult even though they're MC. Class is recorded which is its only saving grace. Textbook is awfully boring and repetitive.

He is really just an awful prof. The lectures are super boring and difficult to follow. He has trouble getting to the point. He makes you read the book cover-to-cover and it's pretty much the worst textbook I've ever had to read. The exams are difficult and have random questions. This was truly an awful class. Exercise caution.

I think Prof Ditto is a sincere, well-meaning, and intelligent prof. However, he has difficulty speaking clearly and coherently. This class is unnecessarily boring. I think Prof Ditto will improve, but for now his class is not worth taking. Exams are  fair but challenging. Textbook was also poor choice.(Health Psychology by Taylor and Sirois)
best class!

Blaine Ditto is an underrated prof. He is a really nice guy who sincerely loves what he does and he is always willing to go the extra mile to help his students! He even brought donuts into class a couple times! Though he sometimes goes off into tangents when he lectures he usually makes it to his point eventually. Overall, take his classes!
No Comments
Disapointed in this class... thought it would be great but it was so boring....

Blane is an easy-going and caring professor. He makes sure to make his students feel welcomed and understood. He always takes the time to answer questions and really makes the content clear for everyone to understand. He definitely doesn't hand out A's, but he always wants to see his students succeed.
lots of pretty difficult readings and the lectures don't help because they just consist in him reading quotes from the readings. still it's an overall pretty okay class

i personally didn't like Benedicto but the class was just not my cup of tea either. he's not terrible but the lectures are a bit weird and useless. same thing with the conferences, the TA was not helpful at all. the take-home tests are not terrible though and the questions are pretty specific. he does bring in pop culture, just not a huge fan

Conferences were very relaxed and participation wasn't mandatory. The midterm and exam are worth the same (35% each) which I find odd, and I there could have been clearer guidelines for the midterm. Also, I could've gotten an A without attending (the graded works are essentially summarizing). Overall I enjoyed the class and I'd take it again.

He is delightful. His lectures get tough but are always engaging, and he makes an effort to connect the content to modern pop culture. He is respectful and encouraging of working through disagreements or questions about the content, which is really important for this type of course. He's also really funny, and loves to give movie recs!

Professor Benedicto is exceptionally kind, and his use of pop culture during the lectures was great, especially because most of the readings are challenging. My only problem was with his slides since he didn't use his own words but instead quotes from the readings, making them hard to follow.

I learned so much from this class, the readings were very hard at times but the lectures did help. The material was always interesting, and the tests weren't too bad. As for the conferences, you don't have to participate except for a group project. The TAs were great as well!

I really like Bobby and his use of pop culture, but I was not fond of his lecture slides. He did not use his own words, and instead took quotes out of the readings, which were oftentimes confusing. Great conversations in conferences even if I disagreed with the majority. I think everyone should take this course and try to gain a new perspective.

For a 3 hour lecture, the time has never flown by so fast. He is an extremely engaging lecturer that explores topics relevant to current culture. The grading criteria from the TAs for the conference presentation were very broad and weren't explained well. I would take this prof again, one of my favorite classes this semester.
Best teacher I have had at McGill. Incredibly knowledgable and funny, with lots of pop culture references. Would recommend even if you aren't a GSFS major or minor.

Prof. Benedicto is an incredible lecturer and was able to explain conceptually challenging material in very clear and engaging ways. The readings can be quite difficult, yet as long as you attend the lectures, it shouldn't be difficult to keep up. There are few assignments, and they are graded clearly and fairly.

Lectures are unimaginably incoherent, and he doesn't follow the textbook. Content was interesting enough, and as long as you do the assignments and the practice tests you'll be fine, exams are pretty easy and identical to the practice ones he hands out.

Very inconsiderate and lazy, literally played recordings of his online lectures in class instead of teaching. Course isn't difficult if you memorize all the assignments by heart, but the professor is terrible.

Legendary Vincent. Actually knows that you have other classes beside his and that you might not care about fluids. Graded by quizzes with no final exam. Do the assignments and you will have no problem passing this class.

Professor Chu is such a nice guy, but his lectures are just not worth it, it is so unclear and will not teach you most of the things you need about this class. From my opinion, if you do your assignment very carefully in CIVE 281 and understand everything about it, you will pass with a descent grade in this course.

Sweet guy who seems to know his stuff but not an amazing teacher. The 8:30 lectures really put you off, I learned everything from this class from the book and by doing the assignments. The class's more abt memorizing the assignments than understanding mechanics. It's also useless for EE majors, it should be removed. Good thing I took it online.

CIVE 281 is such a hard course. The material is very tedious and you don't learn anything except trying to copy and memorize assignments. This is one of those courses that are plain horrible. Try to take it during COVID and use the internet.

CIVE 281 is a required course in the Electrical Engr curriculum but is so useless that you will not need it for anything in your entire degree at McGill or after. It makes no sense to make this a prereq for ECSE362. This course is very difficult, proff doesnt help and is purely unnecessary. Help out new students by taking this course of curriculum.
He is an excellent prof in teaching and research.
Worst course I have taken at McGill. This course simply makes no sense and is useless.

I have him for cive 281. I had to teach myself the whole course, I feel bad for those that are not that gifted in physics. I am pretty talented in physics and still struggled with this prof. Good luck

Boring lectures (he just reads off slides), long assignments, and unclear expectations for exams. Slow grading, and very little time to improve (got MT1 back an hour before MT2, posted solutions to last assignment 2 days before the final). Had no office hours, unreachable by email. Always telling us how busy he was, didn't have time to spend on us.
It was hard to pay attention in Prof. Siwick's lectures because I sat in the front row and kept getting lost in his dreamy eyes. Wawaweewah.

Prof. Siwick is definitely a good person. He is passionate about the course as well as his research. However, I strongly hope he will improve with his pedagogy, especially his way of talking in class--too many pet phrases. You could literally hear tons of "so"s, "and"s and "umm.."s in every class, which could be distracting and make it very boring.

There is a lab report due every week, and they all have to be done by Python. But if you can work well with your partners, it's actually quite easy to get a decent grade. But honestly, I don't think his lectures are very helpful, you can basically learn all the things from your textbook. Also, brutal final quiz.

Showed up first class and showed up for final quiz. Got A. The class is heavily based on labs, so do yourself a favor and get a good lab partner. as for final quiz, get ready to punch in numbers in the calculator and thats about it. Quite an easy class. Tho be ready to hear the words "robust, right, ok?" in class.(said that alot during first class)

Pretty solid, goes through material super slowly (almost too slowly) but at least you feel like you understand. Gave a practice quiz that greatly resembled the real quiz. Lab reports are long and tedious, but not hard necessarily. Extensive use of python for data analysis. The average was a 75% on the quiz, B+ in the course.

Professor Siwick is easy to follow in class but I find it difficult to see a "big picture" when he is explaining concepts. I often have to refer to the textbook and write a giant TL;DR in his notes. That being said, he is funny, enthusiastic professor, and I still enjoyed attending lectures.
good prof, unfortunately I listened to his lectures sped up which made his habit of saying 'ok?' and  'alright?' repeatedly even more obnoxious

Excellent, nice, friendly prof!!! Very detailed, clear, and interesting lectures. He is very hard working to make this course (at least in his sections) better and has tried his best to give us a better understanding in the materials. Well, this class is mandatory to take, but just enjoy your time with him! :D

By far the best prof I have ever had at McGill. He is so smart and is so good at passing knowledge on to students. His lectures are clear and very informative, without being too long/boring. For someone who never loved chemistry, he definitely helped me warm up to it. Great guy, also super nice and funny. Keeps you interested in material.

Best. Prof. Ever!!!!! he is truly wonderful. I lit took his class as an elective 2 yrs ago but I still visit him in office hours sometimes. I learnt a lot from him and have sm respect for him. Lectures are basically story time w note taking, he is so funny and engaging & literally knows everyone's names in a huge class. Great prof!!

Best professor I have ever had. He is super passionate about his field and makes every lecture interesting (I never skipped a class). He is also super approachable and gets to know his students by name. The grading is very fair, and detailed outlines are provided for the tests, so you know exactly what to prepare for. I can't recommend him enough!

Professor Kleinman is one of the best I've had. His lectures weren't mandatory, but trust me you'd want to go because he's so passionate about what he teaches. He makes everything interesting and funny, and you'll find yourself wanting to learn all about ancient history. The only downside is he's a bit of a tough grader.
Very good lecturer but tough grader. Quizzes, exams and essays were harshly graded.

Loved his class in HIST 205, was also my TA and gave amazing feedback on the quizzes and papers. The lectures were only 1h which were relatively easy to get through while watching on 2x. Wished I went to more classes because of how fun he is in class. The tests are okay and he tells you exactly what he wants to see, but the papers were a bit hard.

Amazing lecturer. The slides and the content were very interesting. Most classes felt like I was sitting down to watch and entertaining 1 hour documentary. I took this class as an elective and it was very fun and also easy if you're willing to put in a normal amount of effort. There were two very small quizzes, 2 ~4 pages essays and a final.

Kleinman is engaging, knowledgeable, and funny. You have to work for a good grade on essays and quizzes but its feasible to do well in the course and have fun with it. Ancient history is not my favourite but this class is well worth it-- the primary sources are interesting, essay feedback is thoughtful, and lectures are engaging.

He's the GOAT!!! One of the best profs at McGill, period! Every lecture feels like sitting through a mini movie. Would 100% recommend anybody taking it. I took it as an elective and have abosutley no regrets.
absolute legend. took this class as an elective and its still one of the best decisions ive ever made at mcgill. lowkey made me wanna switch majors just to get into more of whatever he's teaching.

This will be the best class you can take at McGill. TAKE HIS CLASSES. the best prof ever, I look forward to his lectures, some reading but very light and interesting. This class had 2 small quizzes, very easy if you go to lectures. He's very helpful, its very easy to talk to him outside of class, really great TAs too!

Great guy, bad teacher. Textbook and lectures both confusing, verbose and repetitive, and unclear. When I started copy pasting the textbook into AI and asking it to simplify, my understanding of the course and my grades much improved. Has no skill for teaching, can't explain a concept understandably to save his life. Harsh grading.

Prof. Gillon clearly cares about logic, which, unfortunately, is not what most people would agree covers the interesting portion of semantics. If you love logic and want a logic class with brief mentions of Linguistics, this is your class, but IMO if not a req, I would sit this one out.
This class confused me so much.

This course doesn't have as much "math" as people say. There's some predicate logic, but the hard part, IMO, is using the nomenclature and definitions he wants. He also seems to look down on students. He simultaneously thinks arts students are clueless about math and expects them to grasp proofs right away. Also the textbook is very poor quality.

He does not accommodate students because the mandatory textbook is not free online and he does not upload his PPT. You can either transcribe his PPT or listen to his boring lecture but not both -- that's impossible. You have to use exactly the same words as his answer in the exam otherwise you lose a lot of marks. Dispute your grade is impossible.

Loved logic, hated semantics bc of this dude. You get -2 for using different synonymous WORDS on exams. You need to transcribe EXACTLY his words from class. He does not care that you get it, he cares that you copy paste HIS opinions and views directly from his brain. Hates u if you dont get good grades but loves if youre in compsci.

he sells his own overpriced bland copy-pasted half-baked textbook, crushes curiosity, grades with impunity unless you worship his greatness. Want to dispute a mark? Prepare for a three-week wild goose chase. Bottom line: he's after your cash, not your education.

I took LING 460 last year and LING 461 this year with him. Both courses are interesting and easy A (a least for me). Professor Gillon is caring and easy to reach after class. He gives me lots of support and encouragement, making me fascinated by formal linguistics. Excellent course and professor, recommended to everyone!

Semantics was rough. Very math-heavy, very difficult exams, and very nit-picky grading. But, the semester after I failed his course, Professor Gillon met with me several times and walked me through the topics I was having trouble with. He took the time to make sure I passed the supplemental exam, and I did! With an A-. Truly an amazing professor.
He's very caring and very approachable outside class. He's great!

Excellent professor! Sincerely cares about students and wants to see them succeed. I had a tough time in the class due to the mixed levels of the students and had a hard time integrating, but I'm glad to have met Brendan and really lucky to have had him as a teacher.

I loved Brendan's  Internal communications class. This is one of the most valuable courses I have ever taken! I work as a Marketing Manager, and was able to apply the Communication templates he provided  into my company. Amazing teacher with real life experience. I felt like I was getting free consulting to improve my company and my career!
I learned stuff I can actually apply in real life. It's not a difficult class. He's an effective and approachable instructor.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! Automatically he takes off 5% for participation from everyone because apparently only 3 people can get an A (even if majority of the class is more than capable). Doesn't know how to teach or grade. Avoid if you can!
great class. teacher was informative and fair. very helpful. would take a class with him again.
WORST CLASS EVER. STAY AWAY AND SAVE YOUR SANITY! He is so obsessed with the Bell Curve and gets mad if we leave class. Some of us have a JOB and KIDS you know! Get over it, Brendan.
Great class, great professor.

Horrible class. Your grades do not at all depend on how well you do, but how others do. He's obsessed with the bell curve and even admitted what he spent 25 hours trying to play around with our grades. The class does not require any effort but if you don't write in french, your chances of getting an A is quite low. Do not take this class!

Chee 200 is a brutal class so it will never be easy. He is super accessible and caring so if you put in the work, go to office hours and send emails with questions, he will be great. At the end it was a bit messy with formula sheet and mistakes but it was his first time teaching and overall he crushed it. Reach out for help!!!
Very caring, very compassionate and overall very good person. Teaches the concepts really well especially since its his first time teaching. The course was tough but it wasn't his fault.

He's a very passionate and good lecturer. I think he struggles to write good exams, which is his only fault. (For example, not giving students enough space to write and not allowing extra pages seems to be a common thing he does). I liked him personally and learned a lot from him. His handwritten lecture notes for this course were very good.

Prof Pym is one of the best profs out there. He is so caring towards his students and his explanations make sense. He ensures fairness, is very accommodating and really wants the best for his students.

We had a midterm that was way too long for the time allotted but he was receptive to feedback and gave us a pretty tame final. He thankfully goes slowly through the material and explains things quite nicely. I need him to stop apologizing for his "messy" diagrams because I have never seen hand-drawn surfaces and graphs so beautiful.
This guy is so smart and clearly loves what he's teaching. I have a history of falling asleep in class and I never once dozed off during his lectures. Luv him

Prof Pym is so caring and helpful. Lectures are organized. Doing homework really helps to understand the material. Exams are fair. Material is a bit hard in the end but overall doable. Very lucky to have taken 316 with him. Definitely would recommend.

A humble mathematician who is also good at teaching. The course is well-organized: clear lectures and instructions, accessible course materials, fair assessments. The learning environment is safe and welcoming. He listens and communicates really well, respects students, and validates their questions. He is supportive and we are in good hands.

Very smooth style. He knows his stuff back to front and presents it all in a clear and accessible style. Superb office hours. Personable, and and answers questions in class in a helpful manner, even when I asked loads of them. Good sense of humour. His tests are a challenge. A bit of an uphill slog but if you know your stuff, the path up is clear.
Really caring teacher! Accessible during office hours and by email! Overall it is a challenging class, but very doable if you go to class, do your homework and practice problems from the book!
Super clear, passionate lectures, and relatively easy homework and exams. 10/10

He explains the material very well and makes it interesting. Great slides too. The exams are fair and he is very upfront about what you can expect to be in them. Final and midterm are "hard" because the material is, but IMO out of all the questions he could possibly ask within the bounds of the class he mainly asks the easy and obvious questions.
Prof.Meyer is the coolest prof at McGill!
heavy work load, hard exam!!!!!!!!!
One of the best profs I have had at McGill so far. Really helpful. If only he is teaching 444 next year...
All the reviews say he's amazing and he is but he is also a tough grader with difficult assignments. Great personality but some more support on the assignments would be great

Hands down, the best professor I've had at McGill. I've had my fair share of really amazing professors but Brett was the most understanding and caring professor ever. 324 is an assignment-heavy course, you have tough labs and reports due every two weeks but he makes sure the midterm and final are fair (PS- he loves memes!)

Brett Meyer is for real one of the best profs I've had so far, a true G. 

Exams were really tough, but he curved the entire class at the end more than fairly. You'll be fine if you've properly digested the material and you know how to apply it extensively.

That said, the labs were (a bit too) long.

Very good professor, definitely appreciate how he adapted to teaching "post" COVID a flexible lecture, tutorial and grading scheme. He is also knowledgeable and the course is well structured, you will come out of it with a solid understanding of how computers work! Labs were long and the exams were tricky, but you can get a good grade if you study.
Amazing, the only word that deserve this man.

Great professor, one of the best professors I've ever had, he really cares about the students. The course was mainly based on reading many papers and discussing them in class. The assignments were challenging a little bit, but you would learn a lot from them. Take the course and enjoy your time at prof Meyer's class, you will surely learn a lot!
This course was well structured and delivered, making complex concepts accessible and engaging with a strong emphasis on "practical" application.
Very disorganized and doesn't practice what he preaches with regards to pedagogy. I feel like I wasted both my time and money on this course because of his poor leadership skills.
Great prof overall, took the time to get to know me

Super nice and obviously loves his job. Gave us chocolates multiple times throughout the semester for no real reason. Fun and easy assignments and even more fun to be had in his classes. Probably my favorite prof I've had so far at Bishops.

He's a great prof. He posts short videos (only 15 mins) at the start of his section and all the content you need to know is in them, and he encourages you to watch them before class. In class, his explanations aren't perfect, but it doesn't matter because you have the videos. Most of class becomes an interesting discussion. Had very fair tests.

Cherney is a decent prof. Though generally nice & understanding, he is somewhat prone to cranky-old-man rants and outbursts. His feedback in MUCO245/246 was not helpful & mostly amounted to stylistic suggestions on notation. However his guided analysis of works in class is thorough & insightful. Pass/Fail, doesn't have the energy to grade properly.
Dry and boring in a classroom setting. Maybe he's different one-on-one.
I study music composition with him and I just have good words for him. Very good person and teacher!

Brilliant and caring professor, highly understanding and inspiring, with a hidden sense of humour, and very generous with his time. His wide experience was evident in the most compellingly thorough and eye-opening theoretical analyses I ever heard or read. I agree with the previous doctoral student reviewer completely.

Loves his students - makes sure they are well personally also, not just professionally. Winner of the Faculty Teaching Award. He shows his really fun sense of humour if you get to know him as a private composition student. I am doing my Doctorate with him, and I know...:-D

great prof and interesting to listen to!! i never thought I would enjoy 16th/17th C history but here i am! that said, he's a really harsh grader for the essay. the final was fair (hasnt been graded yet) but def had to study a decent amount

Prof. Cowan is a lovely man. He delivers great lectures and is interesting to chat with in office hours. But he has the occasional tendency to be either opaque or arbitrary about how he marks your work. Grading was based on three two-page papers.That isn't enough space to develop (even the most succinct) complex historical thought.

I absolutely loved this class! Professor Cowan's lectures were extremely interesting and genuinely felt like listening to a good story. The subject matter was fascinating. The readings were a great mix of interesting primary sources accompanied by clearly written secondary sources. The workload was light so it made it a great elective course.

Friendly, pleasant teacher. Lectures are repetitive and sometimes hard to follow. Still, I felt I learned a lot from how he does social and political history. Workload is light, reading list is sometimes heavy. Grading focuses on primary source analysis, which I enjoyed.

Very passionate about the material and a kind person. He wants to answer your questions and have discussion in class. The assignment descriptions and criteria were too vague though, which made them much more difficult (imo).

Professor Cowan is such a kind soul and truly cares about his students while displaying a vehement passion for his lecture content. That said, even as a history buff, most of his lectures put me to sleep. Sometimes the criteria for his papers aren't the clearest but he's super accessible outside of class so you can ask tons of questions.

Honestly I've heard people say Prof Cowan's lectures are tough or boring, but I genuinely don't see what they're on about. Cowan clearly cares so much about the subjects he teaches and is such a wholesome person who grades clearly, teaches with enthusiasm and is always accessible and willing to talk to students for whatever reason. Good man.
Really nice guy, but very dry lectures and the PowerPoints aren't always helpful. His assignments are really straightforward, and most of the TA's are easy graders.

I'v had him before in 200 level courses and he wasn't a great prof, but for a higher level course I would recommend. He is always available for consultation and gives good feed back but I've never read so much in my life! Sometimes 300 pages a week on top of personal research for the term paper. Good if you love history and the topic!

Professor Cowans lectures were not organized and they were so boring. The slides on the PowerPoint were useless and he reads his notes super quickly which makes you spend an hour and a half on a 30 minute video. I was so disappointed with this class, we had more than 200 pages per lecture and its only a 200 level class. Do not recommend.
very nice prof and explains stuff very well. exams are not easy but graded very easily. require minimal effort to do well compared to average biology classes. need to memorize lots of stuff tho.
He's kind of boring, but really nice.
Boy does he like his models

He is really funny, but his lectures weren't my favorite. He often talks about models, which was connected to the course, but not really the point of the course. He wasn't my favorite of the 3 profs teaching this class, but he is by no means a bad prof.

Boy does he love his models, which I'm not totally sure why he includes. Like yes they are related to the class but that's not really the point of the class. His lectures are pretty dry. Overall he's smart, a really nice and chill guy but not an ideal prof.

I really liked Prof Leung. He's really passionate about his statistical analyses, which he makes for fun and that don't have to be memorised or really understood to a great extent. He's quite funny, asks a lot of questions to get participation going, and is pretty clear about the content.

of the 3 professors i've had for this course brian is def one of my favourites. i love how he explains things, i really enjoy his lecture style (though i feel envr 202 never gets THAT interesting, so dont expect much regardless)
Of the three 202 profs, Brian was my least favourite. I find he didn't make topics simple enough considering this is an intro level class and non-science students are expected to take it.

I was scared of taking a course with him before the semester. However, other comments I read were dated and no longer accurate. Although there were quizzes they were very fair (even straightforward) and we could discuss in class. Assignments were intellectually stimulating. Good lecturer, seems like a nice person. Would recommend this course.

Brian goes through material very quickly and I don't find his explanations clear at all. If you're not good at statistics you'll definitely need to outsource some learning materials because after Brian's lectures I was very confused and frustrated. You can tell that he cares and that he's a nice guy but his teaching leaves something to be desired.
There is no lecture material whatsoever, no exams, only at home assignments, which can get annoying, but prof Robinson is a very easy grader. Be ready to do a lot of Excel!
Loved this class it was such a practice type of learning and the professor was accessible for questions in and outside of the class.
Great prof who is very accessible for questions, in and outside of class.
Just a chill, smart, and caring prof. The class was well-designed and interesting. The group projects actually facilitated learning.
Maybe it's because it was online, but the format this course was taught in was beyond boring. Knowledgeable prof, but not interesting or particularly accommodating

The two professors of this course are very nice. Lectures are clear and easy to understand. Online quizzes focus on random nuances on readings, you can do them in group. Assignment instructions are not clear, you need to ask TA to clarify a lot of things. For the midterm, memorize everything on slides, including trends but excluding specific data.
Very interesting prof, definitely would recommend taking his class.
His lectures are clear and organized. He is very kind and willing to answer your questions. The midterm is fair, but online quizzes are unreasonably hard. They focus on random nuances in reading.
Mediocre at best He cares more about himself (where his own research could lead him) than teaching
I won't say it's an easy A, but definitely an easy A-. For Robinson's midterm, do the reading.

He breaks the weekly lectures into three which helps you better digest the very full topics. He'll also go on odd rants about random things which actually helps you stay awake when the course content gets a bit dull. He's a funny guy and does care about his students, so if you need help, just ask him. He's an approachable and knowledgeable prof.

One of the nicest, most understanding, and thorough professors at McGill. One of the fairest testers, the exams will be a direct application of what you learned. During my rough times, he was always supportive and understanding, which I really appreciated. This is cheesy, but although he is your prof, he feels like a friend. Kind and teaches well.

Clear about test material. Tries to be caring by remembering your name, but if he remembers the wrong thing, it will get under your skin. no textbook, go to class to get all the material. Small talk about unrelatable entertainment but occasionally funny

He was a straight-forward lecturer who told you what was important. Considering how busy he is, he was able to mark things in a reasonable timeframe. Exams aren't easy you need to use a lot of detail from what we learned in class but if you study hard and recognize the 'main stories' from the lecture material you should get a decent mark.
I was amazed by the lectures! Very interesting topic!

Easy going prof who is passionate about microbes. Really interesting course which I had limited prior knowledge in. Exams are fair, not super easy, but they are predictable and serve to get a point across.
Funny Prof! Provides lecture notes to study as well, all you need to do is to memorize the notes he gives out.

Brian Driscoll was my favourite prof as an undergrad. Funny, quirky, quotable, insightful and intelligent. I liked his microbial ecology course so much that I went on to do graduate work in microbial ecology and am now a new professor, teaching students using some of the same demos and approaches I picked up from him. Thanks for the inspiration!
No Comments
Really interesting class, amusing guy

Everyone I know hated tax. Brian's teaching style made the class 10x harder than it should have been. Go to class to work out the examples (bc not all solutions are posted) but be prepared to teach yourself everything. The textbook is dry and confusing, but it's the only help you're gonna get. You're lucky Brian's on sabbatical W25

You have to read pages of the textbook before every class. The textbook is so unclear and the material is very challenging, yet Brian still expects you to come to every class having already understood the material.
He's not accessible outside class and clearly does not care about his students. He does not answer questions because the answer "should be obvious" and the exams are not like what you see in class.
Avoid him at all costs if you care about your GPA!!!!!!!!

It's a tough class, and even harder when you have to teach yourself everything from the (poorly written) textbook. He assumes everyone has already learned the material before class and just goes over examples, skipping over some important explanations. Most of the solutions to his in-class examples aren't posted either. He is charismatic tho.

Really good grading scheme (2 midterms, weekly quizzes, assignment and final) and very charismatic/funny prof. However, the textbook is extremely dense and he doesn't really explain anything in class but more just throws examples on the board. When you ask clarifying questions he often just refuses to answer them. Not a great learning environment.

He is an energetic, charismatic professor. However, his pedagogy, his approach to teaching this course is absolutely awful. The structure that professors bring to every single other classes I've had at McGill is something that is non-existent in this course. He does not help you understand concepts at all, but rather overwhelms you with readings.

My class this fall was online. Not a lot of people attended zoom classes, which made it awkward since sometimes nobody answers when Brian talks ;( Other than that, Prof Wenzel is extremely precise when he teaches and you really learn a lot! plus the tax return is really fun to do. You have to get used to his lectures since they are different.

lectures help since the book is complicated. Brian is a very nice and caring person, but at the beginning when I got bad grades because of his vague quizzes, I did not think of him like that. He is one of the profs where he is very considerate of students during the pandemic (s/o to Desmond too): no midterm, 1 assignment and 3-4 quizzes. take him!

Prof. Wenzel was always well-prepared for lectures and got grades back to us very quickly. He provides tons of practice problems (more than you need) and the exams are usually similar in difficulty to the easier textbook problems.
She's great at explaining things and knows a lot about what she teaches. One of my favourite CS profs at mcgill.

She's quite strict and not very understanding. Even though attendance isn't graded, missing class still affects your marks. Her lectures were dry and hard to follow. For our final project, she kept questioning our topic and pushing us to adjust it, leaving little time to study her materials, then criticized us for not going deep enough.

Insane time-consuming homework: our last hw assignment (2%, individual) was to make a functional prog. compiler in OCaml, which was the ~15% FINAL GROUP PROJECT from 2 semesters ago, almost word for word exact (per my friend whose final it was). Reasonable exams though (was about failing, saved it w the final). Hardass, respect her but never again.

302 is a difficult course with new concepts, and you have to be on top and ensure you understand. 302 is simply not a class that you can just "grind out" you need to understand the concepts. I felt whatever I didn't learn from the lectures I was taught in the homework. Prof Pientka's exams were always fair, as was the grading

If this class is optional, consider switching, if this is a mandatory class ... well good luck, you will actually need it. She is a tough grader, hard assignments. The lectures were not recorded, and the in-class slides were almost never posted afterwards. And when the slides were posted, they were blank since she would rather write on the board.
There isn't much to add from the other reviews about her. Very hard grader and a rude teacher to students who have trouble understanding concepts. Would avoid her at all cost.

The grading scheme for this course is a bit messed up, its incredibly discouraging knowing that you are spending hours on assignments that are pass/fail and worth 1% of your grade. The requirement to pass the final exam to pass the class had to be removed and the final was curved!

this class burned me out bad! I worked more on this class than all of my other 4 classes combined. She never posted the answers for parctice midterms or finals, the solutions to the last 3 assignments were posted THE NIGHT before the final. She's very knowledgable, but man this class drained me. Also, very weird grading scheme. AVOID!

This class used to be online, and she has all the lecture videos from previous years. For some reason, she decided to GATEKEEP the class instead and didn't allow lecture recordings and didn't post the videos that she ALREADY had. But when the classes were online, she was so quick to cancel the class and upload the videos from previous years. Avoid.

Avoid at all costs. Wish I could elaborate more to make it more clear why for those reading this, but I can't even articulate the degree to which she ruined my semester. She is extremely rude in the way she answers (or refuses to answer) questions. I know 302 is mandatory for CompSci and SoftEng students so just pray it switches back to ProfJake.

Brigitte is an amazing lecturer and so entertaining—she manages to make boring algebra and derivations actually fun. She's very clear at explaining abstract topics, and you genuinely can't get bored in her class. Amazing grading scheme and a very fair final. Would take her class again any day.

Brigitte Vachon changed my life. I was never inspired and enlightened in class but when I first came into her class, it was a life changing moment and truly a wakening for my academic performance. She is the best teacher I have ever had in my 4 Phd. Truly recommend her and hope the future students have her class. Thanks for turning my life around.

She doesn't seem to care a lot about our grades, mainly that we learn the skills she's trying to teach. I found her pace a bit too fast in lectures to take notes, especially since she used a slideshow rather than writing on the board. Labs were fine but I had some trouble with my lab partner and didn't feel like she would help.

Prof. Vachon is a really great and entertaining teacher, during the labs she really answers you well. Lectures are a bit boring since its only stats. The course itself is very heavy so expect to spend a lot of hours outside the lab to finish the reports. Try to talk to the TAs as soon as youre confused. Final was like the practice given.

Brigitte is super passionate about quantum and she makes the class very interesting even though it's just a bunch of linear algebra. Tough lectures sometimes but you can get tons of easy marks from quizzes and homeworks.

AMAZING!!! Cares about her students, knows the material well. Even though PHYS257 is a pretty random class that feels completely useless, this prof's final exam is almost a direct copy of her practice. Her lectures are engaging even though the content can be quite boring.

A clear, passionate, motivated and inspirational lecturer. I dreaded this class after PHYS240 but now that I'm done I'm proud of what I learned. Best prof I've taken at McGill yet. Tough learning curve at beginning (first few labs are a bit hard) but midterm and finals were fair. Shortish assignments, but 10 labs. Final project was really fun.

We covered all the textbook (Griffiths), but we only skimmed each part. We were still expected to solve complicated problems in the exams. It was the first time she taught the course. Hopefully, the tests will be more representative the next time she teaches it. On the upside, she was very insightful and intertaining.

I scraped by in signal processing (phys 241) and was dreading this class... Now I understand everything! What a lifesaver. Explains everything clearly, starting by component, then delving into different circuits with said component. Good notes. Brutal amount of work though; 6 assignments, 10 labs, 1 midterm, 1 final project and 1 final exam!
Clear, enthusiastic and extremely helpful. Assignments and exams were fair.

Very sweet prof! She's a little disorganized and all over the place... She ended class 1 hour early for the first two weeks because she forgot it was a 3hr class. Lots of book talks and reading, but all of these are done in groups. If you are unsure about what to do on an assignment, make sure to ask because her instructions are not always clear!

I'm very surprised by the amount of negative reviews that Bronwen has. She has been a very patient and understanding teacher and she encourages discussions and exploring other peoples' opinions. There is a lot of group work and reading (6 books total, one book to read a week for 6 weeks), but overall a pretty easy and enjoyable class!
Avoid this teacher. She is unclear when it comes to her assignment expectations and will find a way to put you down.

Bronwen is phenomenal and inspired my love for reading again. I don't want to invalidate the experience of the previous review, it just doesn't sound like her. She integrated conversations of social justice into the YA literature course because of its importance. She also went out of her way to seek information on micro-aggression workshops for us.

she is an okay teacher. this was an online class, so you may show up if you want or not. Her instructions were vague and sometimes she changes the rubric a few days before an assignment is due... very fustrating. Her classes are kind of useless, for the assignments you don't really need the classes at all, just the readings which she provides.

I loved her class! I have no idea why people here dislike her. She super friendly, assignments are easy if you do the readings and the books chosen are great novels that I now love. she even brings in a panel of teens at the end of the year so that you can engage with teens about the novels you read. shes funny and approachable. overall good prof.

Terrible teacher! Seems nice and good at first but once she starts grading you you start to understand how terrible she is... Her instructions are very vague so you never know what to do and then she grades really really harshly which is uncalled for. If you take this class you need to ask her exactly what she what and do that no execption.

Avoid at all costs. Get through her YAL class if you have to take it but try not to counter her arguments because she won't like it. The class overall is a joke as long as you put a little effort in. On your presentations or assignments talk about racial/class issues because she eats it up and you'll get a good grade as long as you back it up.

Bronwen Low is a very ungifted professor. That is her major problem, which leads to jealous and begrudging attitude towards students. Be careful!! She can easily steal ideas from others and appropriate for her own research.

this woman has mental health issues. She lived on a dream world where white people are to blame for everything. She does not like to be challenged in class, especially from someone whom she thinks is beneath her. She crated a hostile environment in which to learn.

What an awesome professor. I used to hate organic but he made me love it. Very clear in his lectures, helpful in answering questions, goes at a good pace, and exams are very fair. He'd rather test you on everything with fair (and sometimes easy) question than focus on 2 chapters and ask the toughest questions. Definitely take him if you can!
His lectures are extremely clear and he goes at a good pace. His classes weren't boring at all. Exams were fair.

Best prof's I have ever had at mcgil. Super super helpful, always nice in office hours, replied to your email the same day. material very clear, a lot of practice which is great. Got above 85 on both midterms and found final very nice ans straight forward got an A in the course.I have never met someone so willing to help you outside class!

Great prof, one of my favourites. Really good at explaining the material and asnwering questions, but you need to go to class to do well. Know the material he taught in class and you'll do well on the exams. Didn't really use the textbook at all. Listens to student input on exams and adjusted the marks based and what was said about the difficulty.

Great prof, worth getting up for at 830.  Always available in his office and didn't mind spending time to basically tutor you.  Very fair marker, course was minimal work.  Know the trends and how to justify your answer and your going to get almost full points no matter the answer you put.  Good prof, good sense of humor

Very clear and concise. Speaks at a relatively fast pace, so you should be on the ball during his lectures. Midterms were fair. The final was quite difficult, but I am certain he curved. Overall, an excellent course.
Best professor I've had in a long time.  Knows his material, is passionate about it, and presents it in a manner most appealing.
He was an adequate teacher. Lectures were clear and the section was not too difficult.
Terrible prof

Arndstern's a good prof (just as good as Wiseman and Fenster). Everyone is just tired of chemistry by the time his section comes. His lectures are clear and comprehensible, and his section really isn't hard, if you watch the lectures and read the notes.

Difficult to follow in class- leads a seminar but frequently lectures, inconsistent directions for assignments and no constructive comments. Fairly glib in giving feedback with few comments on how to improve.

Apparently this prof is quite interesting at the grduate level. Her U1 undergrad development course, co-taught with her husband, is a chore to get through. Read the textbook and be creative on the assignments.
No Comments
No Comments
Might be knowledgable if she could get her act together.
Disorganized but makes up for it by being constantly available for help

bruno is pretty arrogant and also gives awful lectures. interrupted lectures given by other profs with irrelevant questions. he was insulting to people in the class asking for extra help with a calc/physics equation (as many havent taken those classes) and told us it was basic gr 9 math. but, the class was ok easy if u have basic knowledge of AtSci
Extremely intelligent and passionate

She's not a harsh grader, and really listens to what students have to say in the course (aka participation). She gives a lot of freedom in assignments and her lectures are interesting and easy to follow. She's also readily available outside of class. Totally recommend this course.
Prof Owens is absolutely phenomenal - I highly recommend taking a class with her! Her class was a highlight of my time at McGill!

Such a thought-provoking and lovely class. As long as you read the novels you will do well. Prof Owens' lectures are very straightforward, and she records them. Participation in conferences and discussion post completion are heavily weighted so papers and exams are less pressure. You can tell she's passionate about what she teaches.

This class killed my 4.0. No structure for essays or grading rubric. TA was cool but not helpful. That being said, Camille is the epitome of an Ivy-educated professor. Passionate, entertaining, engaging, eloquent. I would recommend taking this class pass/fail, soak it in without having to worry about "arbitrary grading". Eye opening experience.

Super sweet professor with interesting lectures. There is a decent amount of reading, but there are no firm deadlines or homework checks besides weekly discussion posts, so you can read at your own pace. I found some of the grading to be a bit arbitrary, with significant amounts of marks docked for minuscule criticisms, but overall a great class.

Such a brilliant, kind, and inspiring prof! Taking classes with Professor Owens was truly the highlight of my time at McGill. Do not be daunted by the amount of reading - her passion for the class material is infectious and makes the whole semester so enjoyable.

Prof. Owens is a genuine English professor who inspires her students with every novel she presents. She shows a tremendous amount of passion for the novels and the authors and is thorough in her explanations of its themes and other concepts. She also managed to include student participation within an auditorium classroom; very impressed! Recommend!

Amazing prof! Her lectures are very interesting and easy to understand. She manages to get the class to participate even though it's a big class. The amount of reading is daunting at first but the books she chose were some of the best books I've ever read! If you have the opportunity to take a class with her, you definitely should.
She is the BEST!
Quite possibly the worst courses I have ever taken in my entire university career. Made me dislike science education as a whole and question whether I am interested in pursuing further education.
So incredibly dull, jesus christ

He gives a few lectures every first week of the block for the med students and he's just so amazing!!!! He makes the material super clear and his slides are simply the best. He's also super helpful during labs and I feel well prepared for the lab exam!

Dr. Rolian is amazing. Although anatomy is hard and a lot of memorizing, his explanations are crystal clear and he avoids over complicating things on exams which was very appreciated. Would for sure take him again if I could!

He did not seem to have a good grasp of the lecture material. Most questions from students were answered with "I don't know". Much of the lecture consisted of filler, where the words all sound good, but were kind of just spewed out into sentences that made no sense because the prof did not know what he was talking about but needed to keep talking.
This class was pretty interesting, sometimes long and dry, but you do learn a lot. Can be a lot of work at times. Carl's great though.

Prof. Falk's grading standards are fair, as are his exams, but lectures are incredibly dry. Maybe that is more a reflection on the content of psyc305 than Prof. Falk, though. In any case he's a nice enough guy despite his class being extremely boring.
This guy is awesome! Super passionate about stats and always spends time answering qs! Great stats prof.

His lectures and exams were pretty normal. Everything was graded fairly, and content was relatively friendly to people who aren't familiar with statistics. The only problem is he is a bit disorganized, sometimes rewording things because he also confused himself. You can find everything on his slides, so attendance isn't mandatory.

Just finished the exam for this class and it was easier than expected. I didn't know anything about stats before this class and now I feel knowledgeable on the subject. Carl is a good, straight to the point lecturer and although I would prefer more examples and computations being done during lecture, he overall helped me understand the material.

Unfortunately although he seems very educated on the matter, its clear he may not be equipped for teaching. The material is not that bad but he is not very good at presenting it, he complicates its far too much. We also had some unforeseen circumstance that led to a fill in prof and it was a bad transition, our grades were not compensated for this.
nice dude but i really don't believe in teaching statistics in a world with computers

He's nice, but he's very dry and, while the class difficulty is not really his fault, I struggled with relying on his explanation of the concepts and found myself watching the lecture recordings and restarting them a million times. His replacement after midterm 1 (Mohammed Derainy) wasn't the best.

Dr. Falk seems sweet. The difficulty in this class is probably not his fault. I'm halfway through my Fall 2024. He was replaced after the first midterm for medical reasons. His replacement, Mohammed Derainy, is terrible. Carl was dry and always confusing himself which created a bad base, now teacher does not follow same formulas.

As a PhD student majoring in Applied Linguistics from Concordia, I am grateful that Dr. Falk allowed me to take his advanced statistics class. He gave a lot of assignments, but the assignments are helpful for me to understand the stats concepts. His lecture and lecture slides are also clear. Midterm exam and final paper are not very hard.

Lectures were super dry. Assignments are easy, midterm is okay but the final was the hardest final I had to take! AND THE FINAL WAS ONLINE SO I HAS ACCESS TO MY NOTES. I would not take him again but if you have to, good luck!

Prof. Fraenkel is well-organized and highly engaging. The TAs are generally fair and clear with their feedback and provide lots of it! Overall, I thoroughly enjoyed this course and found it to be a great introduction to philosophical studies.

Carlos is very smart and kind. He's the kind of prof who assigns interesting readings that are worthwhile on there own but who adds a lot to your understanding and appreciation of the work in class. Very accessible, fascinating guy. He's got to be a genius; he speaks like a million languages.

Prof. Fraenkel is great! In PHIL202, not only do you learn philosophy basics, but also how to read, write, and think for yourself. He lectures at an easily understandable speed, provides great examples, and although lectures are mandatory, they never feel like a snooze, and you leave feeling way more confident about the stuff you're reading about!

Great philosophy course that stands out from the rest at McGill. Professor Fraenkel is extremely available at his office hours and after his lectures and will often offer more than enough of his time to anyone interested. The textbook is very accessible, and studying for class is straightforward.
Great course and professor

Professor Fraenkel is the best prof ever! The lectures are really interesting. He covers a lot of philosophers while still providing a clear understanding of each. He's office hours are also amazing. Highly recommend.

professor fraenkel is amaaaaazing, he has clear thoughtful lectures with helpful slides, and gives clear criteria for grading on essays and other assignments. He made the class super interesting, and if you pay attention and write well, it's not hard to get an A. He's also super approachable outside of class.

He is the absolute best guy ever!! His lectures were very interesting, and you truly leave the class a whole new person. Not to mention, he is also a super funny guy! 
The course load is very manageable, and if you follow the essay guidelines well, you will do just fine. 
Totally recommend this class!!

You will learn so much in this class - Professor Fraenkel covers so many philosophers while still providing a clear understanding of each and not rushing over them. I feel like came out of the class understanding the basis of ancient philosophy. He is very passionate and his lectures are helpful and enlightening.

Dude is the absolute goat. Large majority of your grade for the whole year is based on 3 900 word essays. TA's are chill but somewhat harsh graders. Lectures are entertaining and cover interesting material and you don't have to do the readings if you simply go to class. Attendance is unfortunately mandatory which can be annoying to some.
Dr. Morales is good at explaining difficult concepts, and he is credibly sweet and funny. Histology is hard but he makes it better

Such a sweet a funny teacher. His section is pretty tough, but he explains it very well. He will sometimes pass quickly over stuff that's hard, so it can be a bit more difficult. His accent takes 10 minutes to get used to, after that there's no problem. Overall very good prof

Dr. Morales is better in terms of explanation & lecture planning but for his sections he also gives tons more details to memorize. For the exam, he gave nice practice slides. Try to draw out these slides he provided in class to have a better understanding and memories. His lectures usually get hard to follow due to his accent but he repeats himself
Good guy. Cares for his students. I found what we learnt interesting and he just makes it better. Super funny.
Dr. Morales's lectures are very organized, though the content is sometimes very dense. His questions on the exam were very specific.

Morales is extremely amusing, despite the sometimes dry material. He is a generous teacher and cares about your success. I would definitely take him again if I get the chance, and I also highly recommend him to you.
sort of unclear sometimes because of a strong accent, but AMAZING lecture notes posted BEFORE the lectures, with the slides!!! He clearely knows what he's doing, great :)

Morales has a strong accent that makes it necessary to google similar-sounding words until you find the one that makes sense. he gives TONS of info to memorize. good in the sense that he gives you exactly what you need to study. but in the sense that he gives you too much and it's impossible to know what to focus on.
AMAZING prof that's crystal clear and so funny. Would take any other class that he taught.
Excellent prof, passionate about the topic and very helpful. He pretty much tells you what's on the final if you listen carefully during class, and his questions are very fair.

Super sweet and approachable professor. Professor Mathes has high but fair expectations, and her lectures are engaging. The class itself was very technical and mandated an essay style I personally did not love, but I understand this was part of the general required syllabus for English literature. Workload was relatively light though!

Professor Mathes is an engaging lecturer, and ties in her own stories and other resources that benefit the class discussion. She is a tough, but fair grader, and she's more than happy to talk through her criticism and recommendations. Some of the readings were quite long, but they were worth it. The content of the class was generally interesting.

She is a hard marker and expects a lot, but this makes her a great prof if you want to become an excellent student/writer. She is kind but gives detailed critical feedback and is always available for office hours.
I am not very passionate about academia so this was the most stressful course I've ever taken. But if you want to learn she is amazing!
An absolute queen. Like others have mentioned, she is a tough grader, but you will learn a lot from her, and her class was absolutely delightful. One of the best profs I've ever had
Great professor who is very passionate about the subject matter. Can be a hard grader but always willing to give help and feedback.

Easily one of my favourite profs in the department. She's an amazing lecturer and clearly cares so much about her students. Super easy to reach outside of class and while she can definitely be a tough grader, she gives really detailed and helpful feedback. I HIGHLY recommend this course.

Carmen is an amazing new(er) prof at McGill. She's a tough grader, but gives great feedback and wants you to do well. Her reading list is pretty good and lectures are interesting and historical. She's very accessible outside of class if you ever need feedback or advice for assignments. My close reading, research, and writing skills all improved!

Genuinely one of the most caring professors I've had in my past 2 years at McGill. She wants you to succeed and will definitely support you as you work for it, but it's up to you to make the effort. Definitely go to office hours for help with papers, etc. My writing and analysis has improved so much because of her class. Much appreciation.

carmen is so nice and very passionate about her subject. though she's a tough grader, her feedback is extremely useful and if you ever had questions about it, she's very accessible and flexible to meet up outside of class. super girl boss.

She prioritizes having her students actually grasp the concepts and material rather than just their ability to perform on a test for grades. 

One of the best teachers I've had at McGill. 

Participation is pretty important but it's set up so that you feel comfortable participating and asking questions.

Caroline Begg is an amazing professor and I really enjoyed ENVB 210. She has a lot of patience and makes sure to answer everyone's questions before moving on. Sometimes discussions we have in class seem to serve as inspiration for midterm and final questions, so attending class is helpful.

She is very knowledgeable and teaches very methodically, lays out background and basic information before going into harder content. Always answers students patiently and makes sure everyone is on the same page before moving on. Hosts group discussions one class per week, graded, mandatory, and will keep you on top of lecture content.

At beginning, material jumped around a bit, but become more logical later on. She is good at answering questions and makes things fairly simple to understand. Lecture was 2x a week and 1x a week was in class graded group discussion questions, which encouraged staying on top of material and understanding the big picture. Grading was fair.
Absolutely loved her lectures! Finally found I was learning something applicable to real life situations. Has such a large general knowledge making her extremely interesting!
Will go way out of her way to help you with anything and supports many of the on campus student groups related to her field (student farm, farm-to-school program, more).
No Comments
A lovely professor that never lets you down. Caroline recognizes students' efforts and always wants to help them make progress.

Personally, I am not good at learning languages and I'm somewhat afraid of communications. But I have never find this course challenging during classes given by her (In sharp contrast to lectures given by kwan-lock who gave us lectures for the first 3 weeks)
The professor is extremely enthusiastic and always eager to help. Would recommend.

I enjoyed this course  a solid foundation in French. She is very knowledgable, approachable, and caring. She cultivated a warm classroom environment. It felt like a high school language class because of the small size and types of coursework.

Really kind and caring. She made herself very approachable and was patient when someone didn't understand something. The class itself felt poorly structured and very difficult to follow as we skipped around a lot, but that is decided by the department and beyond the professor's control.

Absolutely hilarious. Passionate about nursing (especially her student club). Loves her job and her students. Don't expect sugar coating or hand holding though. Would absolutely take her again. Keeps you engaged in what she is teaching.

Worst experience. Although her discourse seems to suggest that there is a wealth of knowledge, there is none. She has had no actual experience as a nurse for any meaningful period of time, but she babbles as if she is a clinicial specialists, but it's all BS. She is also hyper and rambles on, unable to focus and jittery and temperamental

Caroline is my go-to prof for everything. She's so supportive, gives amazing feedback, and lets us know exactly what she expects out of our assignments. Her classes are very structured and she takes in suggestions from students. Don't expect any spoon-feeding though. Overall an amazing prof!!
CAROLINE IS AMAZING! She makes learning fun and her cat memes are dope. Best prof
Caroline is such a nice quirky gal. She is very knowledgeable and passionate about what she does and cares a lot about her students. Plus, she's hilarious!
Best person! she should be the Nursing program director! listen to students. Cares.

In this class we went a chapter per lecture so reviewing each chapter after the lecture is very important if you don't want to cram right before the midterm/final. She's very funny and her lectures are pretty interesting, though she's a fast talker. There are only a few things that she's counting toward grade, so put your best into each assignments

Very funny teacher, she uses lots of cat memes in her slides. The material she taught was pretty straightforward: read the slides and the book and you'll be fine. Her classes were on the boring side though. She didnt mark attendance but made us sign in anyway so she could monitor who was showing up to her lectures (which arent recorded btw).

EDKP 447: she is at McGill for her own research and is forced to teach, no final exam, 2 midterms and a group project, journal readings are tested on without giving answers to questions to give opportunity to learn on own, she goes through lectures very quickly and there are long lines to ask questions after

She's definitely a knowledgeable prof but she has no teaching experience. No need to go to classes, just labs. Learn the stuff on your own BUT if you don't understand something she's more than willing to help out in private. She's better one-on-one.

She is absolutely awful at teaching and her slides are also beyond awful. My advice: read the textbook in its entirety and focus on her slides, but read the book because she does put many questions from the book onto her exams.

This is one hell of a class. She has no clue about the ways to test here students so she took the decision to make us do ALL THE TYPE OF TESTING POSSIBLE. Orals, lab exams, mid term exams, Final exams and homework's. She take sentences from the book and put them on her slides. She READ the WHOLE book in class. In 2 word: Memorize the slides!

She's not hard but she's boring as hell. The course is a 3-credit 200-level course and we had 2 midterms, 1 final, 4 lab reports, 1 lab exam and 1 oral presentation. She's also a passive aggressive and stressed out all the time. If it's your required course, my condolences for you.

Wagner is the best professor in the bioengineering department. She is passionate, intelligent, and very clear with her teaching. She really cares about her student's learning. The course is tough but fair.
Best teacher in the Bioengineering department! She makes you want to know more about fluid dynamics!

Prof. Wagner is an amazing teacher. She really cares about her students and their wellbeing, especially during the pandemic. She is a fair grader and honestly wants her students to do well in her class. As a student, if you focus on using the notes to write the assignments and exams, you will be just fine!
An amazing and very caring prof, brilliant and clear lectures; she always has a kind message to send to the students!

Dr. Baglole's section in this course was extremely enjoyable. Her slides were very well organized, complete and so easy to follow that I did not need to write any notes for her section. Her exam questions were very fair but you have to pay attention to the small details that she might test you on. Other than that, she is very approachable.
Watch out. Old second wave ideologue who is stuck in the 80s. She plays favourites. Best to keep your head down, do the work, then get out.
Very helpful.

An excellent professor who treats students fairly and is extremely accomodating.  I'm confused by the previous reviewers, she is the opposite of ideological and while she teaches on feminist theory she is not dogmatic about it at all. The class is interdisciplinary, but she succeeds in making things relatable across fields. also friendly & genuine.
I agree with the first student. I found her to be completely biased and ideological. This "foundation" course left me completely unprepared later on. How she got tenure I have no idea.

The best professor I had.  The class is a little simplistic for graduate students, but it is definitely worth taking for the prof.  She is an excellent professor, clearly explaining things as they are (shades of grey, no right or wrong) and she seriously invests herself in her students.  A model.
Aweful professor. Killed the subject for me and for all of my classmates. Left me totally unprepared for future grad studies in biomedical ethics. Worst part is that this course is mandatory.
my goat carrie i love you so much my queen mother.

The course is fine, but the readings are full of concepts, making them boring to read. The quizzes are accessible, but the professor grades the paper strictly. The professor is passionate herself, but I am not used to her teaching style. Should take another class instead of this one.

Loved this class! Quizzes throughout the term are straightforward, and there are two short papers and two long ones (you get to choose the topics, which is a nice freedom to have!) Loved the lectures: really interesting and lively, with a lot of participation (that is encouraged without putting anyone on the spot). Rentschler is also so kind!

She's super organized and makes the materials in a way that's easy to find/understand, plus readings were interesting as well. Only 1 hour of lecture per week and everything was super chill, the downside being content usually being quite surface level

Prof Rentschler is funny, relatable and extremely accessible. You have to go to class because of the reading responses, but her lectures are awesome if not a bit disorganized. Don't always get a chance to get through the material because of class discussion but the assignments are easy and laid back.

Carrie is really passionate about feminist media which is awesome. However, her lectures are often unorganized and all over the place. She gives pop quizzes during any given lecture so you have to come to every class or risk missing one. However, grading is not that harsh and there are no exams, just a few small papers. Easy class overall.

Professor Rentschler is a superb teacher. She is on the cutting edge of her subject and is most generous and helpful. The material is relevant to contemporary issues, grounded in accessible theory and broad in its scope.

Prof Rentschler is clearly very passionate about this topic and it showed in her classes. She is intelligent and approachable. There were random in-class assignments so attendance is necessary. No tests, so you don't really need to do the readings.

Amazing class. Very easy to get an A or A-. Assignments might look like a lot but they're very straight forward and not hard to do. You have to go to every class though because of pop quizzes but it's a fun class to go to as it's discussion based (you don't even need to participate).

Great class even if you don't know anything about feminism! Carrie is a great lecturer and she cares about her students. Don't skip class though - there are pop quizzes. Assignments were fair ! Take if you enjoy reading and writing papers  :)

Prof Bradley is incredibly knowledgeable and caring. I especially appreciated how she organized the group projects in a way that allowed for each person to receive an individual grade. The final project is also very open ended so you are able to be creative and do something related to your personal interests. Best theatre history class for sure!
Great professor and very interesting course if you are interested in fashion and/or theater. The assignments are heavy and take up a lot of time, but they are very interesting and fun to work on!

Took her "Fashion history" class last semester and it was the best! Among the online courses, her class had the most creative elements such as fashion sketches, presentations and free creative final project. Despite Zoom, she is super engaging and understanding. If you communicate with her well, she is willing to be flexible with you! Recommend!

This class did not feel like a safe space. Much preferred my feminist art history profs. I absolutely love fashion design and have since gotten into Parsons, but I can't say this prof helped along the way :( That being said, if you're really into theatre and costuming and want a break from lectures it could be fun to take with friends :)

Catherine is one of the best profs i've had at McGill! She's super knowledable, fun, and kind. Costuming took a lot of time, I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's taking a full five classes, but I would recommend it to anyone else. Having a good attitude is essential in this class, as is being respectful.

Easy A, but unfortunately we all agreed she didn't teach us anything. Such a shame since McGill has few design/fine arts courses. I'd recommend looking at some arts education classes like EDEA 204, or architectural history (ARCH 250) where we got to do some great hands-on projects.
Incredible woman. Super engaging, fascinating class if you are interested in fashion at all.

You can realistically get an A. But you are required to work an addition of 12 hrs or more/week on top of class to work on making your costume and working on a duty regarding some aspect of the play and costuming.
No Comments
Great Professor, very kind, very knowledgeable, and very humble. Knows everything about the subject and is always willing to help outside of class.
She is genuinely one of the smartest and most respected professors I have ever had. She clearly is an expert in her field. The class can be a bit difficult at times but, she's always there to help.

So torn how I feel because I genuinely think she is an INCREDIBLE women, scholar, and professor. However, the course load was super heavy and condescend to the end, creating a very stressful finals. I did not feel I learned a lot during lectures, but maybe I just could not follow her super easily. Either way probably the smartest person I have met.

Pros: is incredibly knowledgeable about her field. Seems intimidating but actually cares a lot about her students. The assignements and content were incredibly interesting. 

Cons: lots of reading, unconventional assignements, sometimes unclear guidelines, little room for actual participation both in lectures and conferences. High expectations

Highly recommended that you take 399 if you're looking to take one of her courses... graded on material not covered in class.

Doesn't communicate grading standards to her TAs clearly... will recommend a source in French and tell you to consult an English book review... then your TA will dock marks for not using the original French source.

Takes little to no questions during lecture, ends class late, and provides a long list of questions for essays and then proceeds to mark them without them. Told to use "IBID," which isn't in the latest edition of the Chicago manual of style. Takes four weeks to give feedback for presentations.

A passionate professor who demonstrates their expertise in clear and thorough lectures. Consider: usually goes over time (don't have another class right after). Readings and paper expectations average for the department and course level; feedback is thorough. Vague participation criteria and few opportunities to participate in conference.
Tough class, but great prof that knows her stuff.

Professor Desbarats is SOOOO knowledgeable and supportive. Do not hesitate to take one of her classes, and take advantage of her wisdom in office hours. 

HIST 333 is a lot of work (endless readings, 2 papers, and a final), but I learned so much and would happily take the class over again to focus on something new.

Incredibly knowledgeable in her field. Lectures are interesting if you like history (If you don't, why are you in the class?) Marks fairly and gives constructive criticism. Heavy courseload though with lots of reading. A 1 page reading response is expected almost every week, along with 2 papers and a couple of other small assignments.
She is sweet, the lectures r long and heavy 11
poor use of slides, bad choice of readings relevant for course material, extremely dull lectures
