She is the sweetest, most approachable human being you will ever meet. She has so much experience and knowledge and is very good at answering questions. She understands the realities of bedside nursing and is very understanding of the pressure placed on students. She will not fail you even if you mess up really badly so long as you show you care

Catherine teaches almost every nursing lab and she really has a good grasp on the material and makes efforts to be as clear as possible for us to understand. She will make sure you have time to ask your questions. OSCEs are hard (but she didn't invent them), but she helps prepare you! She's also just a very nice person who is easy to talk to. 11/10

Underrated gem, super funny and interesting lectures. Only graded on 2 midterms/a final/conferences but grading is fair. Doesn't post anything online so attending lectures is vital, also doesn't allow technology so everything is hand written. A great intro poli course and good overview into political theory. TAs are also awesome.

Super interesting class! Attendance is absolutely mandatory. She does not post lecture slides, notes, or recordings and does not allow any technology in the classroom. So get ready to just write everything she says down.

My only complaint is that she gave me a hard time about my penmanship. Otherwise, she is an insightful professor with enlightening perspectives on justice, freedom, and rights. Her lectures are captivating and the hour and a half go by relatively quickly. She's also incredibly witty and humorous (when the time is right).

This class, especially the Hobbes, the Social Contract, and the Locke readings, taught me a great perspective. Most importantly, through the content, Professor Lu made me realize the responsibility I have to keep my word as a way to build a respectful, dynamic, and authentic political community. It was quite a valuable experience.
Excellent professor.

The material was extremely interesting but Professor Lu failed to make it interesting in most lectures. Coming to class felt like a chore rather than an exciting opportunity to learn. Definitely very good readings though, but the class delivery lacked enthusiasm for the subjects.

Very unclear guidelines for how to get a "good" grade in the class. Lectures overall very mundane and uninteresting; it was hard to stay attentive and keep listening. 
Considering the level of writers analyzed and their contribution to the history of political thought, a far more interesting class could have been made. It felt like she didn't care.

Lu is perhaps one of the most underrated professors in the political science department. Smart as a whip in both theory and IR, generous and responsive over email, and compelling enough to make her 8:30s worth it. If you have any interest in justice, human rights, international politics, theory, or war, definitely take one of her classes!

This professor does not allow laptops in class and only handwritten notes, gives wayyyy too many readings (up to a full book and another 50 pages a week). Lectures are extremely boring, monotone with little information on the slides. On top of all of this, she removed all the slides and lectures one week before the final. Would not recommend.

I was okay with her teaching the whole semester but she literally deleted all lecture recordings and slides from MyCourses right before the final. I do not see the logic behind this and find it purely evil and absolutely sick ! Like who does that ?? Do not recommend at ALL, don't set yourself up for failure
Not the hero we deserve, but the hero we need.

I understood the course material better before she opened her mouth. Incapable of conveying anything in a remotely coherent manner. Drier than dried sawdust. Points for the nicotine flavoured voice, though.

Bright, lucid, well prepared. Knows her stuff and teaches it well. Exam was too easy. Pity that most of the students didn't care about the course. One criticism: those obnoxious stockings have got to go.
Boring. No organization to the course. Hostile to questions.
Harsh on the outside, entertaining on the... outside. V. interesting course, fair exam, good prof. Recommended.
Expected a lot of work but seriously learned SO much!
Dr Hilsdale manages to make the material very interesting. I wish I had taken more art history courses in the department during my undergrad.
Challenging but rewarding. Always do the readings!
Professor Hilsdale is really knowledgable and a great lecturer. Attendance, participation, and doing all of the readings are necessary.

Prof. Hilsdale is an absolute gem!! I enjoyed every minute of her lecture and I really hope that she would teach more upper level art history classes. The midterm is a lot of memorization but it is totally doable when everything is so interesting. Readings are not that mandatory as long as you go to classes and take down everything she says.

Prof. Hilsdale is extremely passionate about her subject and it shows. Her lectures are dynamic, she answers students questions with ease and is easy to interact with. Her passion is contagious and I would absolutely take another of her classes.

Professor Hilsdale is probably one of my favourite profs at mcgill so far. You MUST go to class or you'll fail but she makes her lectures very interesting and is genuinely a great prof. She is also a very fair and relatively easy grader. She genuinely wants you to succeed. If you have the opportunity, TAKE HER CLASS, you won't regret it.

She is very intelligent and is passionate about what she teaches. She has high expectations so it's hard to get an A. There are three tests, two are in class and you have to memorize a lot for them but the last one is a take-home test, for all three you use the textbook and your notes. There was one assignment at the beginning and end.

Professor Hilsdale is one if the best professor at McGill. Her course is interesting and her lectures are well-thoughout. She makes the material interesting even for students who are not necessarily into art history.

Dr. Hilsdale is an accomplished professor and a great lecturer. She is passionate about her subject and expects her students to engage with her material beyond the superficial. She asks a lot, but she also gives a lot. Her class pushed me academically and my interactions with her were both helpful and inspirational. Highly recommend!
xdhwgsvcve

He is a very nice and good professor. However, for his MECH500 class, you don't learn much and the material is quite boring. There is no actual 3D printing in this class, it is just theoretical. It is easy, but if you want to learn and have a fun class take another tech comp or take MECH 360 with him, I really recommend it.

Had him for MECH 360 in Winter 2021 and honestly think he's an excellent professor. His lectures are super interesting and his passion for manufacturing (especially additive) really shows. His exams are fair and the grading criteria allows you to do well in this course. Would 100% recommend him for MECH 360

Kenji is a great professor, and I really loved this course on Asian Modernities. The lectures sometimes dragged a bit, and he could be more engaging (perhaps the class just sucked at participation). Otherwise, I learned a lot from this class and thought the assignments and readings were fair.

I've taken 3 different classes with professor Kenji now and would definitely take more!! His lectures are a little content heavy and you do need to take detailed notes, but the essay criteria is always straightforward and the grading is very fair. Wonderful lectures!!!

Prof is really sweet and always open to hear everyone's opinions. there was a lot of class engagement and he made it really easy to talk in a class setting. course was quite easy tbh, passed without doing any of the readings. there are these really annoying weekly art analysis posts but they carry little weightage. content was partially interesting

Class is 3 hours long and way too boring. Teacher makes asking question mandatory which is annoying...makes class so much longer and irritates teachers/presenters and me. Do not take this class if you don't enjoy public speaking. Quizzes are alright. Papers are a waste of time and uninteresting. Not an easy A. Must read lengthy scientific papers.

I have no idea what course those posters took, but this course is not an easy A by any stretch of the imagination. The marking scheme is very difficult, and inconsistent depending on what section you present in. Horrible course I wish I had never taken. The in class quizzes were easy though.

Excellent professor! Best course I took in my four years at McGill! There is a weekly open-book quiz based on a scientific paper (all you have to do is read it and understand it). There are two 5-page papers (research proposals) and an in-class presentation. A very easy "A" and class is only once a week!
Amazing. She is so helpful.

Ms. Haddad really knows the subject and is good at explaining philosophical issues and perspectives. Topics and readings were super interesting and really fit together. Reasonable workload with clear instructions for assignments. Available and helpful outside of class. Very sympathetic to students concerns.
Inconsistently applied grading policy with little transparency - she wouldn't round a xx.7% to the next number. Despite that she is an entertaining and energetic professor who cares about her subject

She is genuinely a nice person, but a bad professor. Lectures are extremely disorganized. The exams are all MCQs with the vaguest questions possible, leaving answers up to interpretation. Assignments have unclear instructions. There were always inconsistencies between the expectations of the TA and the prof. The most unreasonable grading ever.
She's nice, class can be interesting, and it isn't distinctively hard. But if you're in engineering trying to take an easy elective don't take this one. It will not be good for your GPA.

Prof Westgate is probbaly the most accessible prof outside of class at McGill. However, she is very vague during her lectures, sometimes getting confused by her own content. She is also very vague about what she wants from her students, as she will say something but then turn on you when the grade comes back. The class is very interesting though!

Despite clear instructions, doesn't have an idea of what she wants from students work. Go to office hours and show interest in her course to maybe be on her good side but she predetermines the grade she wants to give you. Content is super interesting, exams are not reflective of content though. Get on her good side from the start to do well.

If I never have to take this prof again, it would still be too soon. Heavily favourites boys in the class. Tells you your work is good in office hours and proceeds to give failing grades for sections on reports she 'approved'. 
While she teaches informative material, exams ask precise questions. Just get on her good side from the start to do well.
fun class! but her quizzes are a bit odd and the professor definitely chooses favourites and grades based on that.

Her grading is just extremely vague, you NEVER know what to expect with her even if you get a rubric. Yes she is very accessible outside class and nice, but the grading just does not make sense to me. I think also she chooses favourites and is biased towards giving them good grades. Interesting content and teaches well, but EXTREMELY unfair grading

This professor can be passionate and make class fun to attend, but not worth her attitude and the way she grades. Claims that she cares about her students, but really does not care at all! It's all an act. I've had multiple other people say the same about how uncaring she is about simple things. Never again

Ms Westgate is very caring, but her quizzes are very deceiving: multiple choice, but the choices are all very similar, which makes it easy to select the wrong answer. The main end of semester project (bargaining simulation), where she gives most the important information very close to the project. Would NOT recommend as an Eng humanities elective.
Daddy Gale is the GOAT! Like, if u can take him, do so. Just an amazing physics prof that cares for his students to understand material. However the assignment can be long.

Prof Gale's lectures were pretty solid and he's a nice guy, skips through a lot of derivations which are left as exercises to us. Classical Mechanics is a pretty brutal course in general so I do not hold too much of that difficulty against him. Midterm was fair and while the final was pretty hard, nothing out of this world. Work in groups to study!

Mostly same as what others had said.Caring prof, gives extra time for assignments when schedules are busy, Very nice grader (gave me half the marks for a question when i wrote 1 equation). Someone else said this—and i cant stress it enough—Focus on lecture notes and CLASS EXAMPLES. Midterm had 2/3 and final 2/5questions identical to class examples.

Good lectures although he sometimes references mathematics we haven't learned yet. Assignments are tough but doable in groups. Exams have few questions so getting one wrong can have significant consequences.
Great course! Very rewarding if one puts the time and effort. Give lecture notes and assignment problems a priority

I got a 55 on the midterm because I wasn't working smart. This class is tough but if you figure out how to be time efficient and you really pick apart all the class examples you can totally do well. I ended with an A in the class because I started being time efficient and smart about studying.

The course is quite a hard one tbh, which might be a factor here. HW was very tough. Although the exams were not as difficult as HW, still pretty tricky. But the professor is a good person. He cares about his students, and when students' schedules were too intense, HW deadlines were extended. However, the teaching pace was a bit fast.
he skips steps in calculating answers and deriving formulas to save time but it can sometimes be unclear how he got said answers and formulas

Great Prof, really enjoyed his teaching style. Approaches problems in a way that allows you to see his thought process which is very valuable in physics. Some considered him unavailable but i think he just wants us to find our own answers. Difficult yet rewarding.
Awesome course if you're interested in music. If you have any sort of background in physics of waves, this course is going to be easy.

If you go to class and take notes, you'll do great. He is such a fun lecturer and very passionate about the material. The final was multiple choice, and everything was fairly easy. if you skip class, though, you won't do well, so do the bare minimum (easy because he makes it so worth it!!)

Prof. Silver is an engaging and passionate lecturer, and his passion is infectious among the students. I highly recommend taking this course and any other courses he teaches because he has organized his course with so much genius. I learned more from this course than I ever have, and I actually wanted to  do the work to get there.

class might seem nerve wracking because of the readings but it's really not stressful. outgoing guy, and very straightforward. he wants to get you to interact with the course content beyond the lectures, which demonstrates his passion for the subject. he makes an effort to get to know all of his students individually. overall a very decent person.

Silver is a great lecturer, his slides are clear and helpful, and the MyCourses page is actually useful and easy to navigate. I missed a lot of his class for health reasons and I needed an extension on the final paper and he was very understanding about it. I think he's a great prof and would encourage anyone to take him

Super interesting course, taught very well. He is very clear in what he expects of students for assignments and is available for office hours if you schedule an appointment early enough to discuss concepts or clarifications on assignment instructions and expectations. Reading load is not too heavy although it varies from week to week.

The best professor I've had in my first year at McGill. He is extremely helpful, kind and has a deep connection with his topic. The topics of the course stayed in my mind even after I completed it, which means he did a great job transmitting his passion for Jewish-Muslim history. Lectures and papers were my favorite.

I really enjoyed this class! I came in with no prior knowledge and was able to keep up. The midterm and final are essays, with lots of time to finish. He was kind, and really seemed to care about his students. Would highly recommend to anyone! Only thing to watch out for is that his classes feel very long and you will probably be a little bored.

Christopher Thibodeaux will knock your socks off with his charm. Get ready to fall in love with chromatography, and don't forget about proteomics. His ionization techniques are electrifying, and his quadrupoles will have you salivating.

C. Von Roretz is the best biochem. professor I had. His slides are amazing, the material is crystal clear (even though some concept are pretty tough). You can tell he loves teaching and he spends time preparing for his lecture, he motivates you and entertain you though the class. And the material is super interesting I had the best time.

CvR is the BEST lecturer I've had for a biochemistry class! He drives home key concepts that are definitely on the exam, and his sense of humor keeps everyone awake and interested. His exam questions were fair, because he wants you to understand the concepts and apply them as opposed to memorizing stuff like 99% of other biochemistry classes.

Awesome prof! He really makes an effort to keep you interested and entertained. He's clear, concise, and his exam questions are fair. He tells you exactly what you need to know to excel. Overall, he's very helpful, and I wish he taught the other biochem classes. Plus he's easy on the eyes, so that helps.

Impossibly hard final. This coming from a student who go an A on the midterm and studied hard for the final. I could have had my notes in front of me and it would still have been extremely difficult. His questions were not at all reflective of material taught. He definitely was interesting as a lecturer but very difficult exam questions be warned!

Wow what an amazing lecturer! Crystal clear, goes at a good pace, and fills his lectures with jokes and analogies to keep you awake and interested. He's a pretty young lecturer so he knows what it's like from a student's perspective and works to make everything easy for you. The only class where students are 100% motivated to pay attention.
The content is complex but if you pay attention it makes sense, but the type II MCQs are absolutely terrible

Dr Piccirillo is one of those professors that you feel personally care about you. He lectures and talks to us like we're his equals, and he's so approachable that he makes everyone feel at ease. During our final, when people had questions, he would pat their backs, ask how we're doing and encourage us after answering the question. A real gem!

Very warm, really cares about students, congrat and say good job to every single student when finish exam and ask your feedback on the exam. He was always there for answering any questions. Lectures seemed dis-organized (but that's immunology), need you to review and summarize. Need to get the bigger picture if you want to Ace the exam.
Cool guy, great public speaker, but his lectures aren't really organized and his questions are not representative of the amount of classestime spent on each topic. RIP GPA.

On the issues of organization, first of all it was the first time he was coordinating mimm 314, and second of all the second midterm fiasco was the result of one very bright student posting previous exams on webct the night before the exam.  Study and you'll get an A. Brilliant guy, gets even better in mimm 414.

I highly recommend this course. It's a great overview of immunology and really interesting. Most Profs are ok and some are rather mediocre. Dr. Picirillo is probably the tops in my view. Clear, helpful, witty, and really smart. He actually cares for students!  His exams are not easy though. He is a major reason why I am pursuing this in the future.

I think one of the major highlights of this course are the lectures of Professor Piccirillo. He is so clear and very logical in his presentations. He comes up with tons of examples and constantly engages students to test their understanding. In my book, he is tops. He should not be judged for the administrative issues he suffered from. The best!!!

Dr. Piccirillo is an amazing Professor. Incredible researcher and lectures with such ease. He is really clear in his message and he really wants you to understand and learn. My top prof during my undergraduate degree.
Many of his final questions were completely ambiguous. There were a lot of mistakes in his questions.
Might be a good lecturer but absolutely a horrible course-coordinator. btw, a follow-up on the last comment: he was a no-show for the class following the "trainwreck" midterm.

Claire is very clearly a researcher before professor. Her lecture is just her reading off of extremely cluttered slides. She doesn't often understand questions when asked, and her answers create more questions than they answer. I'm just happy she isn't teaching classes after U3/QY

The class ain't that hard. Just show up Exams are done alone and then again in groups, class averages for exams easily have to be like A- No theory final exam, only practical final Prof is smart with a lot of experience but sometimes doesn't understand your question
To the point. Great lab instructor, sometimes a little bit abrupt, but that's part of why she's a good prof.

Professor Perez's mind is that of a clinician, not of a professor. She reads off the slides with very little explanation and she confuses herself when clarifying concepts. If you ask her questions after class, she gives you an ambiguous answer... Her tests ask for the most specific things. Her pop quizzes are difficult and ambiguous. Lecture heavy.
Very clear expectations.

Professor Zhao's lectures are really clear. Although the content is quite heavy, her slides are well organized and easy to understand. Her grading for the group project is very fair, and she gives helpful feedback.

Professor Clarice had such amazing lectures. Although they were often content-heavy, she found ways to make them more engaging and interesting. There is no midterm (only a final), but many group projects and presentations. She is very helpful throughout all the steps of the projects and give timely and clear feedback. Very caring teacher!

Lectures can be boring but her slides are detailed and well-structured. She equips her students very well for the final if you just study her posted slides. Her grading on the group projects is definitely fair, especially compared to the other options for MGCR352. Pick your group wisely as group projects are worth 55% and all with the same group.

Professor Zhao is the best choice for marketing in the fall. The lectures, especially as an 8:30 am class, tended to be boring, but her slides were comprehensive enough to succeed on the final exam without purchasing the textbook. Attendance is mandatory during presentations (a sheet gets passed around) and be smart with the group you choose.
Very kind, The course covers a lot of topics though.
Best Prof! Super nice and approachable and fair grader, gives good feedback. Take her for marketing

Course has lots of material and can feel overwhelming during lecture, but everything is explained clearly on slides. Clear expectations for group projects with specific feedback provided afterwards. She's very nice and approachable, and responds to emails quickly.

She is super nice and wants her students to do the best they can. She explains concepts well, just a little bit fast paced at times. She grades well on the group projects and allows you to select your own groups. It is just a content heavy class with lots of different terms, however she does give you a lot of resources to practice for the final.

Super nice and sweet. Seemed to care a lot about improving her teaching. Lectures are dense but the material isn't difficult and is well explained. All group projects were done with the same group so choose wisely.
Provides no written material that actually supports the lectures directly, and the lectures themselves aren't great. Shame because it's an interesting course.
Heartless and self-serving. Avoid.

Pass/Fail final exam for Fall 2025 was brutal, average grade was below a pass without the curve, many students failed. Sadly this had considerable consequences on my life, I lost my graduation, dropped my GPA by 0.3 points, and lost a scholarship putting me in financial hardship... Clarke didn't care, I would really recommend avoiding this class.
Clark has been tenured since 2007, he clearly doesn't care about students, taunts students in class, makes ridiculous exams, "explains" everything in an unclear, colloquial way. Avoid at all costs.

Verbrugge's teaching in COMP 521 is frustrating. Material is interesting, but evaluations are totally disorganized and opaque, leaving students confused and underprepared. No practice material is provided, yet exams demand high performance in short time spans, truly an anxiety inducing recipe for disaster.  Pass/fail exam for a D or above, avoid!

Meh. Great explanations. But, he didn't motivate many theoretical concepts well, I didn't rly care for half the content (and I love theoretical cs). Asgns/exams/lectures were pretty separated (asgns were simple & boring, final def was not). Took it S/U and it was a great choice, not worth a big time commitment, but did learn some useful things.
Lecture notes are UNRECOGNIZABLE, the syllabus is ancient (it's basically the 2008 version), and exams are unfair—testing content that was barely covered.

Lecture notes are utterly illegible, no useful materials are ever posted, the syllabus is ancient (it's basically the 2008 version), and exams are outrageously unfair—testing content that was scarcely, if at all, covered.

Knowledgeable and well versed with the material he is teaching. His handwriting is abysmal and should hardly be considered lecture notes; be ready to take your own. There are no slides/images/code with his lectures. The assignments are incredibly tedious and are unrelated to the exams. Exam questions are unpredictable, good luck with practice.

Nice and helpful professor in general, with illegible handwriting though. It's about traditional/classical algorithms in computer games. Need huge amount time(>20h each) and solid skills in Unity/C# to finish homework. Recommend to someone who really wants to learn about games, otherwise this will definitely drive you crazy.

An amazing professor! Would take again! She is very caring toward her students! The workload was not overbearing and lectures were entertaining. Professor Mitchell was also very accessible. There were 5 book talks covering 5 novels read in class. There was also a 2000 word final essay. Ignore all past negative reviews.

Amazing professor, would take again 100%. super sweet and caring, also often available for questions or help. This class inlcuded a majority of group work and one final essay of 2000 words. There were five book talks, so be prepared to read 5 novels of around 200 words each. Not hard class at all, other than these assignments class is light work.

Old reviews describe her as a dictator, but for me she was just so nice and caring. Little old lady who loves in class group discussions and readings. One warning to look out for: the "textbook" is 5 separate YA novels each is 200-ish pages and you are gonna have to read one a week. So if that seems difficult I would be weary.
she is honestly the sweetest human!!! don't listen to past reviews at allllll
She is the sweetest prof ever. Loved coming to class and engaging with her. She's a ray of sunshine.
AMAZING WOULD TAKE AGAIN!
Dr. Mitchell really cares about her students. She is so knowledgable in her field and is extremely supportive. One of the best professors I have had.
Love Claudia. I take her any chance I get!

If Claudia was an ethical person, she would have already retired instead of playing a toxic mafia game in DISE. I cant see to what extent she could be inspirational but she doesnt possess the values that she preaches. Some students just dont want to be part of her unethical game in academia. Shouldnt be in education but can make a great actress
It is very unfortunate that she is a villain, who wears a mask that plays in a role of humanistic academic in Canada and internationally. But in reality she pursues unhealthy ambitions.

If you have ~ AP/IB French level knowledge, you'll be fine. There is an excessive amount of homework (4 different assignments, sometimes including 20 pages of grammar sheets). Practice a lot for assessments and know the vocab and you'll do fine, Prof Mathieu is super nice and tries to help you do well and understand French!

Cleo is a really kind person and always demonstrates care for her students. Since it was a beginners french course, she spoke in both english and french, which made learning a lot easier. Not very difficult as long as you do the homework and show up to class.

Very kind and approachable professor, also very understanding with my accommodations, and the workload wasn't too bad. I did feel though like sometimes she repeated herself a lot in class and would often run out of time, so it felt like we were working on the same things for a long time.

I really enjoyed FRSL 449 with Prof. Mathieu! Her lectures were super organized and had a good variety of content. She was very approachable and it was evident that she cares a lot about her students. There were definitely a lot of group projects, but in a semester that was mostly online, I was happy for the opportunity to get to work with others.

Too much to learn...she rarely ever gets through all of the content in class. Her grading is non-sensical: participation weighs 10% and is comprised of: 5 hours of conversation workshops, 14 texts to read and answer questions on, and in-class participation. We have hours of worksheets to complete each week, and it's way too much work. Ineffective.

Cleo gives way too much homework and crams a lot of material within a short amount of time, it's really difficult to learn and take everything in. She's very nice and tries hard, but has no idea how much work she assigns and how much she overwhelms her students. It's information overload for an L2 learner and is unrealistic to expect them to learn
Prof Mathieu is super sweet and a great, understanding prof. This class is so incredibly boring, but luckily it isn't very hard. There are lots of tests so nothing is weighted too highly.

I absolutely love Cléo! Honestly one of the best profs Ive had! Shes also a new prof so its insane how good she is at teaching already. I will 100% be taking another class with her. Overall she is a very fair grader, not too harsh and not too easy. Had so much fun with her as a prof, its clear that she genuinely cares so much about her students

the content itself is really dry although he does try to engage us w/ participation and interesting examples. super friendly and approachable. always made a lot of time and availability for us, and kept office hours going even after the time was up. gave great feedback for our projects and assignments as well!

This professor is pretty nice but the workload of the course and the content are extremely hard for those students are not familiar with statisics. Very strict in rating, especially the assignments. The lectures about statisics are not clear enough. Dont take the course unless you have a math bases.

I really enjoyed Professor Scott's class, and while it was a decent amount of work, it was manageable, but there was a steep learning curve with coding. Scott was a pretty generous grader and seemed to care for his students, but office hours were always packed so he often came off as dismissive and rushed.

Very engaging teacher even if the content he teaches is very dry. He is very accessible outside of class and will always answer emails with detailed answers. The material to learn how to R-Code could have been clearer though. His quizzes are fair but pay attention to details in the questions. The most caring teacher I've had at McGill so far
The professor is very accessible and frequently engages with his students during the lectures. The lectures are well structured, and grading criteria are clear.

Professor Scott is an amazing new professor at McGill. Took him this summer and you can tell that he seriously cares about his students. Difficulty and reading level was as I expected for an intensive summer class, although tests were slightly more difficult. Definitely suggest taking him, good lectures, very accessible outside of class and clear.

Awesome prof! Some professors only enjoy their research but this prof cares as much about his research as teaching. Behind his stoic stature, he really cares about his students and is very accessible outside class (replies to emails fast). His lectures can be very heavy: if you zone out for 1 minute you may not know what is going on anymore.
Rogers is an amazing professor! The best at McGill!!

Civil eng profs at McGill aren't the best. But then there's Rogers. His notes are amaaaazing. Lectures can be boring but he is very clear about everything. Exams are fair - do practice questions by yourself and you will do well.

His notes are amazing! Very thorough. Fair marker. Tests/Exams can be tricky but if you attend all the classes and do all the practice material yourself, it's very doable. One of my favourite classes so far but, not everyone agrees.

My favorite professor of all time.  While his classes aren't easy, you learn A LOT, and he is very fair and student-friendly.  My friend has gone onto MIT and prefers his notes to those from her new professors!

everybody loves the guy, but he is too reserved, rude and not very friendly! You must be 100% mentally present to his class because he goes fast with his notes and they are not always easy to understand. Exams are long, hard and tricky, doesn't test you on your knowledge, but your speed! I don't think he deserve the mention of the best professor!
If you keep up with the class, it really isn't very painful. He comes across as very earnest. Most people like him.
CIVE318 & CIVE462: Specialized in Steel Structure. He knows what he is talking about!!! Excellent note and speaking.
voted best prof. and he deserves it! just attend his classes and you'll be ok. oh yea, he LOVES trusses... hint!
Needs more experience

Actually the most precious prof... super accessible and accommodating (her classes are hybrid). Sometimes her lectures may be a bit dull, but she provides you with her notes (e.g. her key takeaways from cases), so technically, as others said, you don't need to read. She is also a really fair grader. RECOMMEND (esp since she worked on the charter).

Super nice and sweet professor who actually cares for her students. Lectures can be kind of all over the place but she gives lecture notes with everything you know (you could get a good grade from just studying the material she gives you and by showing up to class even if you didn't do any readings for the year). Very responsive in office hours.

Prof. Sheppard is a really kind-hearted prof. She cares about students. She often doesn't complete her course lecture/discussions on time. She sometimes interrupts herself when she talks, making it hard to take notes. Given the really low pedagogical standards in general at McGill law, she's one of the better ones because she gives good feedback.

It was clear that she hadn't taught the course in a while, and she dumbed the material down more than I think most of the students would have liked.  However, she is an enthusiastic and very sweet teacher, very approachable and helpful.  It was an utterly painless class, and in law, that's something!
She lectures on the fly, which I didn't find helpful. Exams were fair. Be sure to look at her old exams.
She's brilliant, and unpretentious, one of McGill's Finest, she also wrote the Oakes test so she's not a bad constitutional law prof!

She is sooooooo confusing and unclear. Uses very hard to understand legal and political jargon. If your undergrad is poli-sci you'll be fine. Otherwise avoid at all cost!!!!!! Mumbles, never finishes a sentence. My biggest mistake at law school so far.

She is great in some ways, super nice and helpful.  Not great at structure or at leading a good discussion :(  I was totally into the topic but disappointed by the quality of discussion in the seminar.
Outstanding
I agree with the previous post.  Very good prof indeed!
She really wants to help students learn and encourages creative expressions. Pretty much only group projects though

she's so sweet, caring and understanding. if you want to talk to her about your grade, she will not only help you but also appreciate you seeing her so will possibly boost your grade. overall , she's very kind and makes you want to learn more. had her for communication in education.

Class was EDEC 405. I was nervous at first, having seen some of these reviews, but professor Buki is a kind and knowledgable professor. I learned a great deal in her class, and felt supported and cared for. She can be specific about what she is looking for in assignments, but her rubrics are clear, and she is always available if you have questions.

Constance is amazing!!! She makes her classes fun and engaging! She once gave me a mark that I was confused by and when we met to speak about it, she was incredibly receptive and very excited that I had taken the time our of my day to ask her about it. She is such a sweetheart who is eager to help her students understand and do well!:)

She definitely is an acquired taste as she's very specific with what she expects and sometimes has high expectations. However, she will put in the work to help and guide you to achieve those expectations. She can be very friendly and helpful as long as you remain professional and don't take criticism too hard.

I did not learn a single thing in this class. I could not concentrate on anything she said. She's incredibly monotonous and repetitive. She's also incredibly unclear when explaining the work and grading criteria - ironic for a class on evaluation. At least she's an easy graded. It might be time for Constance to retire...

Professor Hoesli's course has an insane workload. She'll oftentimes give out assignments on a whim without warning, and with less than a week to do it. They also feel very loosely related to the course. All that being said, she gives more than enough resources to pass, and is a VERY easy grader. Overall a fine, albeit lukewarm, professor.

for biochem this year she used us as guinea pigs. She pretends to care about our feedback but really she has done nothing with what we have told her. She keeps saying that she cannot change the course since she cant change the syllabus, yet she changes the weight/lectures (in/out of class) as she pleases without consulting us. just the worst

Although not the best lecturer, she goes above and beyond to help you if you need the help. She creates a full course manual (the equivalent of a textbook) with practice problems that she gives students for FREE. Easy exam grader compared to other CHEE profs (like PLGL).

Prof. Hoesli cares DEEPLY that you learn. She made Q&A sessions just for people who's struggling with biotech, so please, please go talk to her if you feel you're behind. She's one of a kind, and I'd love to take future courses with her. Do your end of module problems, and focus heavily on excercises. Know your biology, but DON'T memorize.

Professor Hoesli goes above and beyond to make sure her students have all the necessary tools to pass her course. Aside from writing the entire course manual herself, she is open to more help via e-mail and in person. The only thing she lacks is proper lecturing skills. Her voice is low and soft, and she hasn't found out how to combat that.

Super boring lectures, makes biology such a burden; and this is coming from someone who enjoys biology. She's almost always late to class, and lectures feel unplanned and unprepared for. Easy grader though.
She mumbles a lot, stares at her laptop. The manual she created is literally your Bible for this class, use it well. Her voice doesn't project very far, so sit close.

Lectures are rough to sit through. Don't have to go to class because she makes beautiful course-packs. As long as you know what's going on in there, you'll be fine on the midterm. Lastly, for midterms, know the derivations, as she has tested that two years running (enzyme kinetics).
Great prof:) very busy, but is very knowledgable in her field
She speaks really clearly, and it's really easy to follow her lectures. Since the teaching is easy to follow, the learning is much better, and that's what's important.

Corrie is a gem, I love her class. She`s friendly, extremely knowledgeable and caring. She is passionate about the work she does and it shows. Her approach to social work is a beautiful one, definitely a mentor-worthy prof. Im really glad I got the opportunity to take her course. Thanks Corrie!

Corrie's class was interesting but her lectures mostly consist of a lot of examples and stories about her clients. Sometimes unprepared at answering valid questions about the topic or about assignments. Midterm exam was long but not too challenging since her study guide was helpful. Papers are long and poorly explained. I wouldn't take her again.

Although she is very competent in her field, Corrie is not a good professor at all. She is unavailable for feedback or questions, and her lectures have little to do with assignments. Avoid at all costs.

I found Corrie overall a good professor who is understanding and reasonable at times. However, I did feel mixed emotions with this prof. At first, I thought she was organized and professional but then I realized she wasn't really all that great despite her reputable and respected name...

Corrie is a truly knowledgable teacher that has a lot of experience. She is a fair marker (easy even) and understanding. Corrie gives so many life examples that have you feeling a little more ready for your stage next year! I highly recommend taking Corrie's class if given the choice!
BEST TEACHER. Approachable, makes topic interesting and great poise. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!
Very nice and approachable.

Really funny and gives great entertaining lectures, slides are short and not too content heavy and he makes it clear what is tested. He also sometimes gives breaks during the lecture or ends early. Overall easy class as long as you prepare well for labs.

Best professor and best class ever. Does not overcomplicate things, very easy labs and final (mostly based on lab material), even if you do minimal to no studying throughout the semester. Just go to class and prepare for the labs. Expectations are very clear and as long as you show the slightest interest in the class, you basically guaranteed an A.

The best professor I have ever encountered. Super enthusiastic. He now posts his lectures before class thanks to his wonderful daughter. He speaks very clearly and makes obvious what will be tested. He is super funny and makes it really easy to stay attentive during class. The GOAT!!
Talks very fast but at least is understandable if you watch the recording.
Talks very fast with little info on the slides. But at least is understandable when looking at the lecture recording

Great Professor, but speaks fast. Since he does not share slides before the class it can be hard to keep up during the lecture. He's cool, but goes fast over contente giving you the impression it is not important and BAM it's on the exam

I love mandato. Engaging classes while being concise. Loves to end early. DO NOT listen to comments about him not liking questions, he loves dialogue and always asks if people have questions. He doesn't like irrelevant questions that are smth u can google. No slides before class makes you focus and he posts them after with recordings. Easy exam too

I love mandato. One of the most engaging profs I've had, makes info easy to understand and is concise. DO NOT listen to the comments about not asking questions, he likes dialogue and answering questions. The questions that he doesn't like are the ones that are irrelevant to the class and are more for a student just asking something. Easy exam too.

The only "bad" thing about Dr. Mandato was that he didn't post his PowerPoint before the class, but honestly I didn't care. If you rewatch his lecture recordings, you'll see that he's very concise and clear in his lectures. Sarcastically very humourous too, which is a bonus.
def intimidating at first, but is a good lecturer. he doesnt give his slides ahead of time which sucks at first but you get used to it, and it works out in the end.

Overall, good class, but she is the strictest out of all the Italian profs. She isn't the most organized, does not respond to emails, grades very severely (no access to the grading rubric), and can be unkind in the way she says things. She is funny, and if you do all the extra problem sets, you will do well, but it's a lot of work. Can't skip.

Everyone in this class is unhappy with her. Grades subjectively, inaccessible outside of class, blames students for her low averages (~50% averages), disorganized, doesn't tell us the material on tests until 2 days before the assessment, didn't tell us about EC opportunities until November and basically said "too bad" when this issue was brought up

I found her lectures interesting, and she makes sure her students understand. However, I found that she was disorganized, not always posting the PowerPoints on MyCourse and giving the guidelines for assignments at the last minute. If you are good with languages and ready to put in the effort, you can succeed in this class.

The class was tough for me-- I felt behind everyone else but Cristiana encouraged me to speak up more in class. She was open to meeting with me to discuss grades and topics we didn't understand. I went from fearing her to realizing that she really has her students' best interests in mind. I'm very grateful to have had her as a teacher.

Not a difficult class, but a lot of work. You'll need to be actively involved and put in the work to succeed or even to pass, as attendance is mandatory. As for the prof, even the techniques she uses to teach indicate how exceptionally intelligent she is. Amazing both as a professor and as a human.
She's an incredibly entertaining and kind lecturer. Genuinely wants her class to succeed
loved it, class was interesting and prof super nice
Class is easy but she's really rude, condescending and really boring. Almost always skipped class.

Class is easy, just show up to learn the material. you don't need to take notes as long as you listen. Readings are easy but mostly just supplemental to the lectures, you can get by without doing them.  Also she's pretty hot.

Prof Baker is bad at teaching, because he's unclear about what he wants and because he doesn't teach you what you need to know. Otherwise, a kind person. Also, PHGY425 is overall a great course nonetheless, so take it.
The teacher was good but a hard grader. Beware of randomness in that class and irrelevant classes but it will be okay!

Dale is a really nice man. The course has many assignments, but he explains them all very well. They are also not that hard to do. His feedback is super helpful, especially when doing the other assignments. He grades fairly (80-90%)

He manages to make an otherwise very boring class engaging. It's online this year which is challenging, especially since it is a long lecture, but he gives breaks and time for discussion. He is super easy to get in contact with and is very helpful and accommodating. He is so genuinely caring. Definitely recommend taking his class.

The most caring teacher I have ever come across. He truly cares about his students and is willing to explain things 100 times in necessary. His grading can be kind of harsh because stupid and small mistakes will bring your grade down. Make sure to follow the rubrics and pay attention in class. AMAZING teacher. Definitely recommend.

Wonderful teacher! A great person overall and an awesome course. He really wants you to pass the course so you'll end up with an A as long as you put in some effort. I would 100% take this prof again!
So much love for this teacher. Best i've ever had.. Such a sweetheart and honestly.. Such an interesting class. I hope to god that I get him again, so worth it..����
BEST TEACHER EVER. TAKE HIM!! so nice and very caring towards his students.

Dale is one of the nicest people at McGill! He brings in his guitar and jams with students in an educational way. He is always creative and helps students after class (or during). He is honestly such a good prof.

Lectures were boring and the midterms were so long and tough. He had to curve everyone up for both midterms. Don't leave the project for the last week because it is very long.  Do well on assignments and tutorials to have a chance of having a good grade.

His notes aren't very clear but all are published online, and you can take your own if you go to class. Tests are heavy and long, so study the slides making emphasis on his class notes. If contacted by email for any question, he will answer quickly and is very helpful as he dominates the subject.

Horrible handwriting, you wouldn't know what he is writing in class. Crazy long two midterms, if he didn't curve, avg would be like 40%. Marking very tough on exams and projects. Avoid him at all cost, terrible!
Overall a great class. Exams are based on notes provided during lectures. Suggest to attend all lectures.

Good at teaching gives great examples in class from subjects covered in pre-class and goes into detail. but has difficulty explaining material in other ways if you don't understand something. Exam is brutal

Overall very fair class. You have to attend to take down all the lecture notes because the exams are directly based on that. Must know the theory extremely well since half of each exam focuses on very detailed questions about the theory presented in class. Group project (literature review) about a material of your choice

Well structured course - Interesting discussions and in-class activity - Approachable Had Professor Pasini and didn't know what to expect. The lectures and course in general were well prepared. His explanations are clear and answers questions well. Learned a lot as he kept us involved through regular readings and discussions. Fair grader.

Absolute angel of a prof. He genuinely cares about the quality of his course and about his students. He put a lot of time and effort into making sure he was prepared and had a gameplan for the online semester (unlike many profs), and it showed. Lectures are really useful and reflect the assessments.
Very systematic teaching and perfect notes. Clears all your doubts and is very passionate. Although, his exams are very lengthy. Time management is a must.
The best Prof I have ever had. Seems strict at first, but is very helpful once you approach him.
Not the most enthusiastic lecturer but he makes up for it with his overly complex exams

Prof. Barczyk is amazing at making complicated concepts easy to understand. The material can be a bit dry though and you need to be comfortable with math. My only complaint is that I wish that I had him in person!

Lectures are dull and focused almost exclusively on the math of models. Tests were very hard and asked vague questions, though he did curve generously (class average on first midterm in 50's curved to 70's). Didn't make same time adjustments to exams many other courses did (for covid). I hope he's better in person.

In the first few lectures, I found him a bit monotone and awkward; but once you got used to it, wow what a lecturer! He made everything so so so clear! Took him for ECON 330D2 and he really breathes life into the Macroeconomic Models. In terms of presenting the concepts, he has to be the best prof I have taken in Econ! Take him for 330!!!!

I never used the book for this class as Professor Barzcys lectures are very well written, organized and detailed. He also provides his students with past exams. However, the midterms were harder than the ones provided for practice.
Very engaging lecturer. Everything in the exams is from the, albeit quite dense, lecture notes. Very fair and interesting course.
Difficult but rewarding class. Require lot of studying and analysis- Prof very helpful, challenging and stimulating

This guy's actually hilarious if you're into his dry sense of humor, and probably one of the best profs in the entire university. Doesn't trick you, posts tons of exercises and past midterms so you can do well. Shame he's wasted in a class as boring as 330.

Barczyk is great. This class however is not. Truly one of the most boring and mind-numbing classes at McGill. To do well you have to show up to every class and write down what he puts on the board. He posts tons of practice midterms which are very similar. Great guy but this class is an absolute chore and I feel like he doesn't get to shine in it.
One of the best Econ prof in McGill. Just go to his lectures take notes and you are good for the exams.

AMAZING! He is knowledgable, well spoken and clear. His lectures are well structured so it is easy to follow and build a full picture of the system. He understands that students watch lectures at home and made an effort to repeat all questions so at home listeners could follow along. One of the best profs I have ever had!

Good lecture format. Lots of work in the class but honestly the worst parts are when hes not the lecturer.  He is very funny sometimes but also he is scary sometimes because he is not afraid to critisize. 9.5/10

Dr. Bernard is crystal clear in his explanations and very eloquently spoken despite the content being complex at times. He is super passionate about his research and this is reflected in his lectures.

Arrogant, strict, pompous. Also made fun of John White's teaching in PHGY 210, which I didn't appreciate since  Dr. White is teaching a small section of a 200-level course rather than an entire 300-level endocrinology-focused course.

I think Prof Bernard is one of my favourite McGill profs! He is a really good zoom-lecturer, is super interesting, has clear slides, and goes above and beyond to offer tutorials for students to succeed in the class. His questions are not super easy but I think they are fair for an upper level PHAR class. Strongly recommend taking a class with him!!

Made some really funny jokes. I read his slides for his sections focusing on the headings and not so much on the details, and I did quite well. Theres a lot of material on the course but I somehow managed it. He was 1 of the better teachers . the teacher that taught sleep and REM was the worst with the worst questions. Most ppl failed that section

Awesome prof! His lectures were really enjoyable and funny, and his exam questions weren't too hard. He also responds to questions really quickly. Anat 322 overall is a very interesting and diverse course with a lot of profs. The midterm is pretty detailed, but the final is non cumulative.  Overall 322 is a very good 300 level course to take.

Though he likes to give papers to read, they are always a reasonable length, and he's right, you should be reading papers in your final year.  He is super clear in lecture and writes very fair exams. Plus he's got the sweetest smile, what a cutie!

He also teaches anat 322 - awesome prof - so helpful, so clear, sets very fair exams in terms of both questions asked and material covered. is empathetic to student needs, and is approachable if you have questions. Great guy, one of my favourite profs at McGill. Slides are crystal clear and he is an awesome lecturer.has a great sense of humour too!

Everyone loves him, so im sure you can go ahead, but I didn't particularly get the hype... I barely attended class cause I found it boring, but honestly it might be my fault, idk ! he was understanding with me when i asked for an extension (he only gave me 24 hours tho),i think i just don't like canadian politics (ended up switching my major after)

Daniel Beland is very nice and funny. Lectures are dynamic. The Midterm was easy, the final was harder and more tricky with dates and asked a few questions on lecture's guests. Very interesting content and conferences are very helpful to remember the main arguments in the readings. I recommend !

Prof Beland is SO passionate about what he teaches, and ;ectures are very engaging.The midterm was very easy, final was more difficult are reading-based. Conferences are only attendance-based. Highly recommend this course!

Literally the sweetest human on earth. Made taking a 4pm class just fine with his vibrant and energetic personality. He's also so funny. The final was harder than the midterm for sure but really made the class interesting and relevant.

midterm was very easy and then BAM final was the worst thing i've ever looked at. still great class and amazing prof but man i am worried for my final grade. would recommend going through the readings very thoroughly if you want to do well in his future finals. like VERY thoroughly.

The prof is amazing. The midterm was really easy but the final was not. I would say keep that in mind as it covered a lot on the first half of the class and not the second half which I feel was kind of unfair. But the professor is incredible and I 100% recommend taking a course with him!

Professor Beland is one of the best profs ever in the political science department. He made a 4pm class fun to go to twice a week. He balances current news with the content of the lectures which made everything feel relevant and interesting. Not to mention he is so funny and entertaining. His exams are super fair. TAKE A CLASS WITH PROF BELAND!!!

TA plays a major role in your grade. The TA we had for Winter 2024 was a bit harsh in her grading (thankfully there was the TA strike so that balanced the grading a little bit more). Also, for the exam you need to memorize a lot of things since we do not get the questions in advance.

The course was great overall as we touched on Canadian Social Policy (his area of research). However, we are graded by few things: midterm (30%), research paper (30%), and final (40%). Although the course was not hard, you do need to memorize the readings and key arguments for the exam, which are essay format (3 to four essay questions).

The class seems pretty easy but then, depending on your ta, the grading can be really tough. Knowing the slides is not enough and you also have to learn some information about the readings even though the ta tells you it's not important

Prof. Douek is charismatic, passionate, and helpful. His lectures follow a clear layout, and he is clear with what he searches for. Keep up with the readings, lectures, and conferences and you'll be fine. If you can summarize each of the readings in 150 words or less, you'll be rewarded on the midterm and final.

For an introductory course covering politics in the Middle East, some of the content was concerning to me. Many of the assigned readings fell into repetitive narratives that viewed the Middle East through securitization only. Some content lacked adequate historical background and no serious engagement with colonial legacies which is crucial...

His voice is so pleasant that it makes you want to listen to the lectures. As long as you do the readings and pay attention in class, it's really hard to get a low grade. The exams are not about memorization; they focus on understanding the material and are often essay questions. If you have the chance, take as many courses with Douek as you can

A true gem in the poli sci department. Lectures are engaging, and he's pretty funny. Readings are mandatory, but you only use them on the final so no need to follow the schedule. Midterm is a paper, final exam is only worth 35%. Incredibly accessible outside of class. Will stay at office hours long until every question is answered.

There are only 4 grades, but he is super amazing and intelligent. Lectures are super clear and concise, and relatable to the exams. Heavy in essays, assignments and exams, but he gives you enough time to complete them. Readings are heavy but conferences cover the key points. Would DEFINITELY recommend this class and him as a teacher.

Amazing guy! He's so funny. Really interesting lectures. Don't think the grading is too difficult — papers and then there is a final. He highkey sounds like a frat guy but is very knowledgeable  and sweet.
He is an amazing lecturer who is very passionate about his subject. Be prepared for the readings and the essay preparations.
Fascinating topics and entertaining lectures.
Super interesting and engaging lectures, best professor Ive ever had.

Professor Douek is genuinely an excellent professor. Not only is he super funny, but his lectures are extremely interesting! He is very good at explaining concepts and he really takes a lot of his points from the readings he assigns. If you do the reading, you will find it easy to follow during class. Though I did find the exams tough.

Dufort is a great guy. Really nice. I had him for 303 too and he is much better in this class since it is a seminar setting. I would definitely recommend taking this class. You have to read a decent amount of papers but the assignments and presentations are chill and he gives high grades.

He's a nice guy. But he is terrible at explaining things. To understand what he is saying, you need to really tune in to pick up that one stray sentence where he gives you the preliminary information needed to understand the point he is trying to get to.

Seems like a nice guy but sat through all of his lectures confused about what he was trying to explain. It takes twice as long to understand his lectures than any of the other profs. Needed to use the textbook as his explanations were confusing.

Good luck with his section of the course. It's impossible to turn his lectures into coherent information. Be prepared to memorize a ton without having the slightest idea to the theory behind anything.
"Incomprehensible" is the word. Just wait until you try to read your notes back.

Was one of the best classes I took in undergrad. Dr Dufort was really helpful and always available when needed to prepare for presentations. Fair marker and always tries to stimulate discussion. He is much much better in 416 than in Biol 303 which was quite boring.
No Comments

Great professor who is very approachable and incredibly passionate about his work. I have never been so engaged in a course, his lectures are interesting and he brought in great guest speakers. Assignments are graded fairly, and although the midterm was difficult, he adjusted the grades accordingly and made the final much easier.

Professor Schoen was average in all respects. His lectures were generally boring, though that could just be reflective of my disinterest in population genetics, but he did explain clearly! Some of his midterm questions did not correspond to in class examples; you had to have done specific textbook questions.

His section is the easiest and he explains it very well. Some of his questions are copy paste from questions that he went over in class or those in the textbook, so make sure to go over all of them. His section is very probability and statistics based but it makes sense once you do a few of the exercises as they are very repetitive.
Prof. Schoen's lectures are interesting.  The problems he gives to work on in the class really helped my learning. I liked that he let us work in groups

Prof Schoen doesn't have many lectures in biol202 so you must read the textbook. I made the mistake of not reading and paid the price since the exam tested material that wasn't explicitly covered in lecture. He does lots of practice questions in class though which is good. Lectures were a little boring and a little confusing.

READ THE TEXTBOOK!!! Prof. Schoen only teaches a few lectures in biol202 and doesn't get around to teaching all the testable material and you must read the textbook to get all the important information because it WILL be tested. Otherwise, prof schoen's lectures are a little dry and a little hard to follow.
Great teacher. Cares about learning.
Pretty average professor. His content was neither interesting nor boring, neither hard nor easy. Seemed sweet enough and when I asked him a question during a quiz he was nice and helped me out.
His lectures are clear and interesting.
Honestly, not the most exciting nor interesting professor, but thankfully the section of the material he was teaching was interesting. Fair exam questions.

I just loved his lectures! one of the best profs. I didn't have a biology class back in high school, but this guy totally changed my idea about biology!  You should take his class to understand what I mean! I should also say that English is not my first language, but I could totally understand his lectures cuz they were super clear.

Awesome professor, very clear lectures and class notes. Seems a bit unenthusiastic, but I think that's just how he talks. Willing to stay after class and answer questions. If you ask politely, he'll show you pictures of his cats.
Good prof, cares a lot about the subject. Final was tough and does not let you choose to omit midterm. Overall, good course.
Very helpful and I like how he didn't rush everything.

Prof is really nice and very helpful. He goes at a good pace and slows down to help you understand and speeds up over the easy stuff. This class is a really good elective for science students as the material is mostly covered prior. Classes are really well structured and I love the weather discussions he uses!! overall Highly recommended :D

Least interesting series in RELG204. Nice, but boring. Do the readings and come to class if you want to do well on the midterm. Prompts for the midterm were less predictable than those in other units; I wish I had paid more attention.
disorganized, problematic lectures. drones on and on about unimportant things to the topic. grading was easy but wasn't rewarding because he managed to make interesting topics so boring!!

Professor Cere is a very sweet lecturer, and the content is sometimes interesting. However, the lectures were mostly boring, and the grading system was very random; not exactly an easy A, but depending on your luck, you'll get a good grade. Quizzes are super easy. This class needs an update as it shows that it has been taught for a LONG time.

Boring lectures, assignments not graded fairly, hard to get help outside of class. The contents/topics were somewhat interesting but I do not recommend his classes. If you see any ratings that say his classes are easy A, don't buy into that, not worth.
His part of RELG204 was the best part tbh. It can get a bit boring but I guess it happens with everyone. He's very nice and can be funny sometimes. The TA was also very helpful for the midterm.

Professor Cere is very nice, lectures can be a bit boring but he covers the material well. Readings are interesting, especially if you're interested in the intersection of religion and human rights. Papers make you think, and quizzes are based off readings and power points. I'd recommend as an elective.

people who stopped showing for this class are just people who didn't care about the content in general, if you like religious studies this class is amazing, you learn a great deal and prof. Cere is such nice, helpful person and is an expert in his field, he's extremely approchable in office hours and in class, I loved this professor

The prof loves what he does and he is very passionate about it. The class however is quite boring ... After 2 weeks half of the class didn't show up anymore and no one was taking notes. The topics he touches on are quite interesting but unless it's for your major or minor or you're really into that stuff, don't take it. It's boring.

Cere is a sweet man, perhaps an unorganized lecturer at times. However, concepts he's trying to convey are not hard to grasp, just pick the important parts out from his tangents. Talks a lot about other scholars, but not necessarily a bad thing, as it's easy to just reference/incorporate their arguments for the quizzes and papers.

I really enjoyed this class a lot. Interesting, straightforward, and really makes you think a lot. I actually enjoyed doing the assignments. If you want an enjoyable class where you can certainly get an A/A-, take this one.

Writes out his notes live during lecture, which are very clean, rather than rely on power points. Unfortunately, he doesn't post these notes which mean you have to write everything down since the topic summaries he does post are a bit vague. He talks slowly, so not every topic was covered in time.

Understood my questions when I asked, even when I wasn't quite sure what my own questions was. He does speak quite slowly which some people don't like, especially in the 3 hour lectures but I appreciated the way he took his time to go over everything in detail. He doesn't post his notes after class, but you'll need them. Go to class.

Boring lectures, the class was online and he erased the notes after the class. Why would someone do that? Waste time on details and miss the big picture. We received at the beginning of the semester a 35-page pdf and that was it.

He was a bit unclear at times and his lectures could be a bit on the boring side, but overall I enjoyed the class. I can understand why people find the class difficult, but really if you're able to pay attention in class and not fall asleep I think you should do just fine. The material isn't particularly hard once you get the hang of it.
nice!

He is a really lazy and unclear prof.  He missed a bunch of classes in the middle of the semester, but once the TA's filled in, we actually learned.  His notes are o.k. but you can't understand what he says.  In order to get a good grade you need to understand the theory behind the problems so you can be ready for tricks.  Find past exams on MUSE.
EASY course, open book; not always clear, but he tries hard to help in class; easy midterms, a bit tricky final, go to tutorials - very helpful

can't speak english. easy marker but doesn't mean he'll prepare you for the real world. his notes are the only thing that will save your ass. everyone does well in his class so you'll definetly get your grade curved down.
easy course, easy marker, easy exam (open book with all the questions taken from tutorial or assigment problems)
not a bad prof, but needs to communicate the goals of the course better.

Great course! I really enjoyed reading Russian classics, and Professor Pratt does an excellent job of guiding us through the readings in engaging ways. His lectures in Russian history really helped me better understand the context of the novels we read. Grading scheme was kind too.

Not a huge fan of his lecture style, but clearly cares about the material and wants students to succeed. Lectures felt very rehearsed, just write down what he says and use it for the essays. Deadlines are very laid-back. Gives good feedback if you go to his office hours. 

Wasn't the biggest fan of this class but a good professor.
DWP is the man.

Super passionate about his work, grading is super clear, however lectures are mandatory. Two papers and one mini writing assignment, so overall pretty light for a literature course. No midterm, but a pretty short multiple choice final and final paper.

Lectures were absolutely incredible. Even when I was sleep deprived I was completely focused and paying attention. The course is making me consider taking up a minor in Russian, and if you are able to I highly recommend taking any of his classes. (He also is incredible at communicating outside of class and will respond to emails promptly).
a very smart, kind and funny man. it's rare to find a professor with as much passion and knowledge for a course like this. incredible lecturer who got me hyped up to read/talk about the novels.

You don't understand my love for DWP. Passionate, knowledgeable, caring, accessible outside of class--just a great human in addition to being a great prof. When he talks, he gets animated by the spirit of literature, and it's just so heartwarming (and interesting). I didn't want this class to end. Take a class with DWP and you'll die happier.
Professor Pratt is a fantastic lecturer. His assessments are very fair, and he wants to ensure his students succeed. It is a good amount of reading, but it is worth it. Pratt is king.

Super engaging and passionate professor - he made even the most mundane of topics interesting! The workload was reasonable for a literature class, and the grading was fair. Professor Pratt is also very approachable outside of class. Even if you don't love Russian literature, I'm sure you will like this class!

Professor DWP seems to be one of the most well-liked professor at McGill. He makes some of the most mundane topics interesting, and people who've had him always seize the opportunity to sing his praises! If you have the opportunity to take one of his classes you definitely should!

Part of me really wanted to like him, but ultimately, he is not a good prof. You will see a lot of reviews claim that he's a sweetheart and all. He is if you do things exactly his way and do not question anything with regards to the material. You did? You now have a big bullseye on your back. Anything can and will be used against you if he wants to

Took RUSS397 w him. There was a lot of reading involved, and we were expected to watch the films at home, which is fair. He was very funny and the lectures were super engaging. The classes were heavy on discussion, & he was one of those profs that pries what they want to hear out of the class, but he still considered other perspectives. Recommend!

Prof Schwartz gives substantial lecture for a 1.5 hours lecture. If you want to learn more about German and Russian cinema he is the go-to guy. I do, however, find his pedagogy to be kind of monotonous. He comes in and gives an amazing lecture, but that's it. I think he could sometimes go off the book and just have open intuitive discussions.

took 279 as an elective with both him and Ara Osterweil, and I loved it! Favorite class this past semester. I liked the way he interacted with the class during our discussions, he really listened to the students' comments and had a lot of knowledge to share. funny guy too!

Interesting material, very knowledgeable, nice and didn't overload w info. The other prof for this class (Ara Osterweil) wasn't great but I would take him again without her. Don't take this as an elective unless you really care about old movies you've never heard of. If you do care about that though (which I do) it was very cool and I'd recommend.

Cool guy. The class is a mix of little quizzes and take home midterms. Both are pretty easy if you generally know what's happening in class. He seems a little scared of Ara (the other prof in the class) so does things her way, which isn't always the best, like they won't share their powerpoints.

Knowledgeable, interesting, and understanding prof. Couldn't dedicate time the way I wanted to due to outside circumstances. Prof Schwartz noticed and reached out. Made such a difference. Material is really engaging and exciting-- draws from a number of disciplines. Felt I learned A LOT and had fun. Do yourself a favor-- take this class!!

A hidden gem at McGill! It wasn't too heavy but I learned so much, his lectures are ambiguous and he takes the time to make sure he and/or other students are understood. Clearly illustrates his knowledge and passion for film and history but in such a humble way. 10/10 would take his course again.
Very inspirational. His lectures were very helpful in terms of understanding the readings and the film.
Prof Schwartz is a sweetheart with an unpretentious love of cinema. Great guy all around; a must for any cinema minors

Daniel is a remarkable teacher! He always makes sure to let the class participate and give their input on the thought experiments, which is rare nowadays. The questions on the tests are tied into what he puts emphasis on in class (no surprises). Every lecture is delivered in a natural manner and his passion for the field is contagious :)
Really an excellent lecturer! Every lecture was very engaging, class discussions were encouraged, and he always took time to answer questions.
Epitome of classic philosophy lectures. Chalk in hand. A gift for contextual explanations (not just spouting off summaries). An exceptionally wise professor. Side note: fantastic vocabulary

This is an intro philosophy class, you get thrown into the deep end with confusing readings, and are expected to comprehend at a graduate level. Lectures are said to be mandatory but are hard to follow and lack structure, as Weinstock often consistently falls off track. He is a nice guy, makes some bad jokes, don't take for credits or as a BIRD.
Doesn't even bother to grade your work.
Every in-office session I had with this professor as my main supervisor, he showed late/cancelled, & never apologized.

I had Professor Weinstock for both Foundations and Legal Ethics. This is a great course if you are a law student with a background in political science, philosophy, economics or sociology since he teaches with similar vibes to that. DO NOT take this class if you want any practical information on the ethical duties of lawyers or want to pass bar LOL
Not sure why McGill continues to hire him for classes. Waste of students time and tuition. Unfortunately did not learn much and barely took the time to grade.

Interesting philosopher and very liberal. However, he is routinely late or a no show for all scheduled meetings even for his top supervised students. No respect for other peoples time and doesnt even apologize or acknowledge his lack of punctuality.

Dr. Weinstock is a nice person. His lectures are funny but can sometimes be a bit messy. He is very approachable and open to different questions. He also gives good feedback on your papers to help you improve. Readings are intensive and quite difficult. Not an easy course.

Prof Vlaho is great, her videos that she posts on youtube show you exactly how to do the lab, which really helps especially if you have not seen certian techniques. She also really tries to help make sure you feel confortable during the lab, and tries to accomidate for things you may need. Went from being scared of the lab to loving it.
She is so kind and funny. Very helpful when questions asked. Lab professor. She has the best lab fits. Funny and understanding. Great TA's in lab.

Kind, authentic, and caring. She is also super responsive via email/discussion boards, etc. Labs are harshly graded, but you learn a LOT; I'm a better scientist because of the course. The labs are too much work for just 20% of a 4 credit course. Also makes you hand write pre labs which is a waste of time. Her pre-recorded concept videos are a gem
honestly, the assignments are long,unclear and honestly messy. She barely gives any help, avoid!
