People suffer from grading lab reports only because they don't know how to write them. If you follow instructions and ask her through emails or even drop in during office hours, she is really willing to help you sort it out. Also, it's TAs who mostly do the grading not her, and everything is random about who grades which part. She is the kindest

She's very sweet, her lectures (pre-recorded videos) were very clear and organized. Midterm questions were very fair. Do the textbook exercices, it will help lots. For the lab part, she's very helpful and comprehensive. She's passionate about what she's teaching. I really liked her.

I had for the spectroscopy section in CHEM222 + the labs. Shes nice but super harsh grader for the lab reports when those are supposed to be an easy boost in the class. Her midterm was waaaaay too long, difficult and completely different from the previous midterms. I wouldnt recommend.

Dr. Vlaho is an org chem sweetheart. She's very enthusiastic, which makes her instruction more engaging. She contributes to a comfortable and amicable atmosphere in the lab. She wants students to succeed and she doesn't hesitate to help when unexpected difficulties happen during labs. She's a tough grader for reports yet her feedback is authentic.

Her exams are way too difficult, it was nothing like the practice problems . The final exam average for CHEM 212 is 67%, and the midterm 1 average for CHEM 222 is 70%, Note that there is NO CURVE for her classes, the only way to boost up your marks is to do well for the lab portion. It almost feels like you are walking through a minefield!

The lab was partially online for this class. The in person labs were great but the online assignments were a lot of busy work and honestly useless. The information needed to complete the assignments was hard to find and knowledge of ACS citation is needed. She is not a great online prof.

Overall would avoid this class. Nice person, not so good teacher. Class won't teach you how to start a business, but will focus on theory. Unorganized. Good feedback. Weird grading. Not an easy A course. Beware of the TA (Hollie) - extremely harsh grader and not a nice person - You have been warned!!!!

The prof was overall fine. The class is poorly structured and incredibly reliant on a textbook. Which is interesting, because the lectures themselves didn't focus enough on the textbook, making it seem like a completely self-studied course. Demetry's feedback was fine, but also once again, difficult to keep up with as nothing was properly taught.

Prof Demetry is one of the most caring teacher that I've ever had at McGill. She strives to make classes engaging and fun. She is very knowledgeable and truly passionate about what she teaches, and is always available to students both in and outside of class. She wants you to succeed.
Fantastic professor!

She is very clear about what to do and what to expect out of the class. Her classes are always well-structured and organized. If you do what she says, go to class and do the readings, you can easily get an A. My only criticism is that the class is not very inspirational and won't teach you revolutionary things on entrepreneurship.

I adore Dr. Demetry! She's an extremely engaging lecturer who makes class participation actually meaningful, not just a way to get points. She has high standards but they're clear & attainable with hard work. Everything we did in this class actually helped me learn, which is so rare in management. Overall an intelligent, funny, amazing woman.

Prof. Demetry was the best professor I have had at McGill so far - her classes are great, readings well chosen and inspirational, she is accessible and helpful, while the class is hard enough to actually learn something, it is not impossible to get a good grade, when you work for it.

Hilarious lecturer and made 8:30 class fun. She was extremely understanding when I had health issues during the semester that prevented me from attending class a few times. Exams are super fair - clear expectations and always gives you options (ie answer 4 of 5). She also has a very fair policy for contesting grades.
Brilliant Course, Professor
Go to the lectures, and hear how much she cares about what she is teaching, amazing professor

Professor Totten is so passionate about her subject. While I'm not super interested in archeology, her lectures were engaging and I learned tons. Bi-monthly written assignments are easy as long as you do the proper reading for them, and her feedback is always super helpful. Study guides for the midterm and final were extremely detailed and helpful.

Dr. Totten is nice and funny and gets to know students by name. Her tests are very fair, although the TA grading on papers was pretty arbitrary... The readings are long and dense, but she goes over them in lecture, so as long as you review the important parts before the final you will do fine. Interesting course content as well!

Bro there's too many readings for an intro class. She knows there aren't many people who know about classics and she bombards us with a ton of info. She's very knowledgeable but that is a disadvantage because she doesn't discern what's important and just assigns everything instead. She doesn't know how to give lectures.

love! she's so funny and has really interesting lectures even though classics may not be your thing. TAs are bit tough with grading. Her lectures are recorded and she's very generous when it comes to midterms and finals. Such a sweet woman would take again in a heart beat.
Great professor and reasonable amount of work, its easy to do well in this class

Very knowledgeable professor, but an incredibly dense workload. Readings were long and not super interesting (in my opinion), grading was harsh, and no study guide was provided for the exams. A lot of the course is very technical about archaeology, which I personally did not enjoy, but the historical information is interesting.

She is passionate about the subject and makes it obvious to see that within her lectures. However, I would say she gets into a lot of minor details on every subject and doesn't ever specify what information is important to know for exams, etc. and doesn't provide a study guide; she just says that anything can be tested and never answered my emails.

Overall a great prof who cares about her students and is very passionate about what she teaches! However, there were (short) papers every two weeks and lecture slides were posted but hard to follow, so it's super important to go to class if you want to do well!

Genuinely the best teacher I've ever had! She's thoughtful and a great lecturer. She makes an effort to get to know you and is great to just talk to. She's not pedantic about deadlines and gives fantastic feedback on essays. You can usually get away with skimming readings that aren't on the quizzes but they're so interesting that you won't want to!

Darin was great. However, he is one of the slowest Prof's I've ever encountered over email. Which makes extensions, essay feedback, or any kind of clarity basically a no go. If you can live with this? He's a solid choice with some good readings and relatively lax expectations.

The lectures outline everything you need to know for the in-class tests. While the multiple choice can be a little confusing, Professor Barney goes over all the key points in the class. Was all very interesting. The permitted exam booklet with notes for the final was really helpful. TA and Prof both accessible outside of class to answer questions.

I actually do not want to hear any slander on Barney, he is the most caring professor in this whole university he knows what he's talking about!!! The TA was lovely as well. The lectures were definitely a bit challenging as it was an extension on the readings. If you ever need help, they will dumb it down. Literally just do the readings n ur golden

When going over the syllabus, it seems like the class will be easy, but that's not the case at all! There's a lot of readings to do, and while they were really great, it took me several hours every weekend to annotate everything. Also, his grading criteria aren't the clearest, and he wasn't as available as many other profs I've had.

Some of the content in this class is needlessly overcomplicated. The content of this course is pretty interesting at times. However, some of the material is presented in either prohibitively difficult-to-grasp ways without further interrogation or is presented in a blatantly outrageous way at face value making reasonable premises sound ridiculous.

I had the pleasure to have Mr Barney as my professor for 2 coms classes, COMS 301 and 361 and I must say he is probably one of the sweetest and most caring professors I've had at Mcgill. I strongly recommed

One of the best profs at mcgill. His lectures are amazing and a huge help to understand critical works. Will def take another one of his courses again. He cares more about students learning how to interpret texts than pointless testing/memorizing so assignments are constructive and not too challenging.

I LOVE PROF BARNEY! You can tell that he is passionate about teaching and cares about his students. The readings were definitely difficult to understand at first, but his lectures make everything so clear. I honestly feel like I learned so many important things from this class. I immediately registered for another class of his after this one!

Favorite professor! Reading material (all posted on mycourses) can be difficult, but in lecture Barney highlights the most important parts and explains everything super clearly. AMAZING lectures. The grading can be tough but as long as you take notes you'll do quite well. We had 6 quizzes and one final paper, so it was manageable as well.
Great prof and great class! Really thoughtful and engaging lectures, even in an online format. 100% recommend
goes extremely fast

Prof Haggard should not be teaching this course. She does not know the material herself, but rather copies the textbook onto the chalkboard (ofter verbatim). She makes mistakes often, and cannot answer questions about what she is writing. Class attendance has dropped steadily over time since students are better off with the mistake-free textbook.
You literally cannot improve in this class because all your grades are in MCQs and you can't inspect the MCQ

I feel like compared to comp250 this class genuinely graded memorization rather than understanding and problem solving with how much this prof focuses on MCQs and little to no coding questions and this is coming from someone who got an A in comp250 with the new grading scheme. If you prefer problem solving and dislike MCQs, avoid!
Hard exams and doesn't provide any relevant practice problems to solve.
funny guy but never again

He's the best prof I ever met until now; I've already taken 17 courses at McGill since 2024 Fall, and there was not any prof who is such passionate, teaches concepts in a way that is easy to understand, and gives just enough exercises and assignments! Let's take David's course!

really sweet CS teacher, very funny and super enthusiastic. Always says hello and tries his best to make the material fun. I was not a CS student and this was one of my fav classes. Hard exams tho if you unexperienced at programming, it is super diffuclt and i heard 251 is an easier equivalent in terms of content...Loved David tho:)

he is probably the best CS prof i had at mcgill. he gives so much enthusiasm and effort into his lectures and hws that it is enjoyable to do the hw´s. The exams are not easy but fair (do his past exams and he lowkey reuses the questions so that might give u an extra point or two). Anyways, take 251 WITH HIM!!!!! TRUST ME BRO
Lectures are fun to attend, but he doesn't provide practice problems

He is very funny and brings energy to the class. However, it is hard to learn the material well since he does not provide any practice materials and the slides are IMPOSSIBLE to self study. Midterms and finals are very fair, in the sense that it is hard to fail but at the same time, don't know score high grades because of the lack of practice.

a very engaging lecturer, but a bit MIA on the discussion board. assignments and exams are quite fair considering how tough the material can seem at times. leetcode helps with the programming paradigms part. he played latin music before every lecture and made many self deprecatory jokes. hope he's alright.

I was nervous about taking a music history class I wasn't familiar with, especially in a setting where class participation was a must, next to a lot of outspoken students. Thankfully, David was kind and lenient, even letting me submit a paper two days late when I messed up the due date. There are a lot of readings. But he's a very nice, nice, guy.

The lectures just tend to repeat what was in the reading and are quite dull. The reading quality isn't good and while sometimes interesting often lacks nuance. Papers are a lot of work, especially if music history is not your major, and tend to be vague and have you repeat what was said in class. Overall: easy but painful and didn't learn much

He is a rigid and unaccommodating teacher who delivers uninspired lectures on a niche subject

You can do all the readings and assignments, but the moment you're late or sick, you're screwed. What little enjoyment I got from the readings was ruined by the sheer dryness of this guy

I don't think I'll ever want to take another musicology class again

Professor Brackett is an amazing professor. His lectures are always entertaining and he has a great sense of humour. His grading criteria is clear and extremely fair. He's definitely one of the better history professors that McGill has to offer.

I was pretty skeptical of this class at first, fearing that it was a slacker course.. but I feel like I actually learned something, and it was enjoyable as well. The text was great and provided a new, critical approach to pop culture we thought we knew.. great elective class to take, and entertaining prof.. certainly recommended!!
By far the best class I've ever taken.  Not only is the material interesting, but it is extremely easy.  Definitely a must take (especially during a difficult term)
Brackett seems like a great Prof. Fun first class drummin with our hands and desks. Hope its a easy as the other ratings
I heart David Brackett!
BRACKETT IS AWESOME AND POP MUSIC RULES BABY!
music rules baby!

a controversial figure in the English department but hes great. Genuinely wants his students to succeed and loves to meet with you to discuss anything. His lectures are a bit slow but he is knowledgeable and hilarious when you pay attention. He warns you that theres a lot of reading but its not impossible... we also are english majors so face it

Kind attitude but very long and rambling lectures. Hard to follow. Don't recommend taking this course at all if you're an undergrad, and don't recommend it for anyone just trying to fill their credits like I was. Absolutely gruelling reading schedule. The only positive was that he made sure we all met with him before turning in the final paper.

Professor Hensley is one of the best professors I've had at McGill. He genuinely cares so much about his students and is always eager to discuss ideas with you. I have loved working with him and feel like I have become a better writer because of him.

Very kind and understanding professor. Unfortunately, the lectures were ineffective and grading did not match what we were taught. Lectures were just him rambling on (same as our meetings) and they were hard to absorb. Papers were only given back once and graded heavily on grammar which was not talked about. Prof was always at least 5 mins late.

nicest man ever, so sweet. but he needs to retire already. too many dense readings, lectures were rambly and unclear, took forever to grade essays, graded us on grammar even though he never taught the fine points of it, really do not taking a class w this prof if you can help it. he really is such a nice guy, but a terrible prof

Out of all professors in the department, Prof. Hensley's likely the most generous with his time. He meets with students for hours and tries to answer questions thoroughly. Yes, he takes a long time to grade papers, but he gives very detailed feedback. Unfortunately, though, he's not a good lecturer: his lectures are rambly and unclear.

He really is the sweetest guy! Just wanted to make sure we knew he was aware of our other course loads, but still very responsive with feedback and help for final paper. Also granted so many extensions to the whole class. I also went to him for my advising app and he said it would take 15 mins, but he talked with me for 1 1/2 hrs. Just a fun guy.

I can't say enough good things about Professor Hensley. I'm now 2 years graduated from McGill and it's been almost 5 years since I took his class but I still clearly remember the mentorship and compassion he showed me. Having him for a professor was one of the best things to have come from my uni experience.

The most personable and engaging professor I've met at mcgill. Haven't taken a theory course with him but having had him in a seminar setting I know that he sincerely cares about his students, is incredibly intelligent, and an honourable and respectful professor. Can be text-heavy but totally worth it. He is never not willing to help his students.

Hensley is an excellent professor and an honourable person. His lectures are information heavy but you learn a lot. I thought he was a very fair marker and he gave me plenty of feedback throughout the semester. I would recommend any serious english student to take one of his classes. my grammar has improved exponentially.

Professor Cooke cares a lot about making sure you understand your experiment. When you ask him questions, he usually gives helpful responses -- he saved our final project. I didn't always feel prepared for labs (esp. troubleshooting) and think the lab manuals could be improved, but this is not only an issue with Cooke. Just an issue with most labs.
Very arrogant. Very unclear expectations. Not very helpful when you have problems in the lab.

The only work is lab work and make sure you pick good lab partners, or you will suffer badly. All the grade is dependent of the lab reports, so learn from the first lab report and make sure to write them very well. Make the pictures large.
Good prof, you can see that he put a lot of effort into class; more then can be said about most other physics profs at McGill.
Very responsiple prof. Understands the School and architure, structure. Helpful. Quiet, maybe a bit shy, but very smart (if you are smart enough he will be very entertaining).
Best professor I've ever had. I can't help but be captivated by every word he says. And he's hilarious.

Misunderstands the very essence of teaching. Is profoundly insecure (due to his incompetence). Reflects and transmits this to students and those who won't buy it get shot down. Classic case of propagating abuse. Promoted to his level of incompetence. Sad case of tenure. I regret every moment spent listening to his drivel.
Generally not well prepared. Lack of rigour, lack of perspective and overtly political. Will not stand for principles. A career academician. A committee man. Pass if you can.

I graduated in 1985. David Covo was wonderful to have as a professor. His discussions were insightful, and very helpful, but sometimes, you had to start off with a basic amount of insight yourself to really understand the most important underlying subtleties. David helped keep things light and real in a class where things could get nutty!

i'm not a fan.  i tried and tried again to see the good in him, but i had my fill of talking about everything but the subject at hand.  I was told he was good at teaching sketching skills, but in my opinion, he's in love with watching himself sketch... i'm not a fan

I agree that people should respect him as a director at least. He's the most patient person I think I've ever met and he'll go out of his way and then some to help students with anything - especially with sketching.

He is the director of an understaffed architecture school and still has time to help you with any issues you may have... what more could you ask of the head of your department. I agree, everyone should show some respect.

Hi. DC taught me in my first studio course in NINETEEN SEVENTY EIGHT. He is quirky, sometimes funny, but overal a teacher who will help you to go in your direction in architecture. I don;t understand the bitterness against him. It's hard to teach architecture in fact YOU have to LEARN it.

I'd rather have a warm and diplomatic generalist like covo as a director for a school than an ivory tower academic with a single vision for architecture. his tenure is marked with evidence of his hard work. sometimes though, like mary, he is too busy.

There are only two things that determine your grade: a midterm and a final with barely any flexibility to the grading scheme. Within those two things, you are obligated to know every single pathway and every single other small thing that was briefly spoken about in class without a cheat sheet obviously . I promise you, do not take this course

I put that he was great in the sense that he's knowledgeable about his topics and it's easy to follow him when he talks, but lectures are a little disorganized. I found it was more a biology class than a cancer class, so a lot of pathways. In the final, there were type 1 and type 2 MCQs, as well as long answer questions (design experiments).

A little scrabbled and nervous online but probably much better in person. Taught the material well and responded really well to question on the Mycourses discussion board. Often went overtime during online lectures and sped through some important lecture material but only tested on topics covered. A very solid choice in my opinion.

Very nervous while lecturing virtually but if you watch his live in-person recordings they're much better. Tends to run long in his lectures and they can be a bit confusing at times. Very good at answering questions outside of class.

Took this because I liked him for genetics, but was the hardest bio course I've had. I love the way he talks(keeps my attention), funny & mindful of students opinions but I personally found the lectures unorganized, SO hard to make sense & hard to find continuity. I think I could've done better if this was in person & exams weren't hard on purpose
Online made this class harder. Many pathways which require you to understand more, which is good but the way how he teaches made it hard to understand.
He is AMAZINGGGG. Always stays after class to explain to you and make sure you understand. Humourous and clear lecturer. Fair midterm. Hard but very enjoyable class.

He can be facetious. I did alright but studied a lot. I would have done better if I went to the TA review sessions. Not a bad idea to take it during the summer but you have to work very hard every day. His quizzes are pretty bad but sometimes can be done in groups. I found that his tests were way too long. Not an easy A.

I have so much respect for this man. Honestly, he has made me want to become a prof even more just because he makes teaching an art, you want to listen to him and his knowledge is impressive. I'm technically not in Bio, hadnt taken the prereq but 202 was still followable and I finished with a C+ because his grading curve is pretty bae. Thanks dd 3
Very captivating professor, but he expects you to think (and not just bluntly memorize all the content).

Professor Davies is an amazing teacher - he's insanely knowledgeable, but makes sure to explain difficult concepts slowly, and in detail. He's also just a really lovely guy, and will take the time to provide extra help after class/in office hours. If you're into philosophy, definitely take his class. If not, you might find his lectures a bit dry.

I LOVED Aesthetics I, but Aesthetics II was not my favorite. Davies and his lectures are great (though dense). Much of the material carried over from Aesthetics I, and the theme of this course was Davies' own theory of Aesthetic Appreciation. I think that's why I didn't love it; it was just laying out one theory and "testing it". Davies still rocks

Prof. Davies is funny, kind, and caring. The course content is very dense, but he does his best to explain it in an accessible manner. Take the time to do the readings and comprehend the slideshow content outside of lectures and you should be okay. He is always available for help and genuinely tries to aid in comprehension through office hours.
Dr. Davies is a fantastic lecturer. Moreover, he is as nice and considerate as they come. I'd recommend taking his class to anyone comfortable with difficult philosophical texts.

Davies is a wonderful lecturer and speaker. He makes philosophy content quite accessible through repetitious explanations and examples. Unfortunately, grading criteria (particularly for the final paper) were nearly non-existent, making expectations unclear. His slides have all the info you need, but lectures provide a more engaging look at content.

After reading the reviews, this would be my easiest class this semester. However, it became the hardest class I've ever taken at McGill. I went to every single lecture but could not comprehend anything he was saying. I just found that the material became so convoluted and was hard to understand. The essays and exams had no clear instructions.

Pr Davies is so kind and approchable, and also very funny !  However I struggled quite a lot with this class as I had no background in philo, the content is heavy and not easy to digest. But Davies is the sweetest.
Love him! such a good teacher, really lovely person and is one of the best philosophy professors I have every had: explaining difficult topics really really clearly.

Prof. Davies is an extremely passionate lecturer and is always available to chat with his students and help them develop their ideas. He is engaged and truly seems to care. I found him incredibly helpful and was lucky to have his guidance in this course.
He is super approachable, passionate about what he teaches and he spares his time to answer your questions. I highly recommend taking Professor Davies class!

He's a really caring professor and he made his section as understandable as possible. His section goes more into detail about some BIOL 200 concepts and some general biology courses, so make sure to understand the basics. Overall, his section is ok as long as you do all the exercises and fully understand them especially for the drosophila section.

Not the most tech savvy guy, a lot of time was wasted trying to figure out in class polling during online lectures, but the lectures themselves were fine, a bit confusing at times but the exam questions were very fair, much easier than the midterms. Still should do the practice questions because they always help.
Not a bad choice, his lectures aren't always the clearest but his exam questions were fair and pretty easy.

I took Biol 202 this summer with Prof Hipfner! He is very clear in his lectures and all of the exams questions came straight from examples he talked about in class! Seems like a genuinely nice guy and wants people to succeed. His midterm questions were fairly easy and had a bonus question on the final exam! Really enjoyed this class!
He's a gem. Really easy to ask questions to and it super clear
Had Hipfner for the summer course. Good prof, but can sometimes be a little confusing. But his material and exam questions are pretty straightforward and definitely doable.

Dr. Hipfner is one of the best professors I've had at McGill. I was lucky enough to have him for Bio 202 and I really feel like I've learned so much!  I had had a class on similar subject matter before taking his class, but he actually made me interested in learning it. I would highly recommend taking a class with him if you get the chance!

Definitely the best professor of the three. Some of his exam questions might have been a bit wordy, but a lot of them were straightforward and sometimes even just straight up memorization. If you listen in class and study your notes in advance, you should do very well on his part. No promises for the other two, though...

He was very clear in class and it was easy to follow along with his slides. However, make sure you don't spend all your time memorizing all the little details as the final exam is mostly all application questions where you would have to apply the concepts. Do past final questions and attend conferences!

His slides are very clear and well organized, and he's very clear when he speaks in class. His MC exam questions are TOUGH. They are all half a page long and really require you to think. How to do well: 1. Do not cram, 2. Go to Vikrants tutorials 3. Do tutorial and past exam questions 4. DO NOT OVERTHINK. The questions are actually straightforward
nice guy but really disorganized slides. hard to follow. avoid it.

Worst psych class I've taken. He teaches with the most disorganized slides and the exams test on tiny details of blurry charts from 50 years ago. I did well in the class, but I had to memorize every detail he discussed and put twice as much time into this course as any of my other ones. Avoid this prof. He seems friendly, but is a horrible teacher.
His class is very interesting. He is very knowledgable and passionate about what he teaches.

Such a great professor. He is passionate about what he does which is the most important thing. He made a subject I didn't find particularly interesting in neuroscience (sensorimotor system) really interesting, and he's so cute! Very knowledgable, and sweet.

He has good slides and does a thorough job at going through them in lectures but does nothing more than that. However this course is fairly easy and if you do all the relevant problems in the textbook you're fine.

Easiest class at McGill. Gives Art of Listening a run for its money! The final is much harder than the midterm but still really easy. Ostry often cancels class due to mysterious trips to the US of A. Seriously take this course.

Good teacher, he explains everything very well. Some questions are unclear in the Ferguson book tho, and you might have to read on your own for certain details. Other then that, he knows how boring his class is, and he's trying to make it fun. Repeats everything lots of times.The midterm = super easy, the final = long/weird questions but doable
confusing questions, unclear expectations and unavailable. awful professor stay away from any classes he teaches

One of my favourite profs! He explains everything super well, and repeats important information over and over again. He is very helpful when asked questions, and really encourages questions during class. The exam questions are completely predictable, but the marking may be a little unfair at times.
Such a funny guy. Really enjoy attending his lectures.

I took THIS class and yet was being graded as if it was a 400 level course. She creates a hostile/uncomfortable learning environment. In my opinion, she thinks she is doing a tough love, teasing approach but in reality it's toxic and un-motivating. She grades pronunciation and accent inappropriately hard for this level, ignorant of native languages
Lectures and slides were unclear. The professor didn't explain topics well and was disorganized. Very tough grader, particularly on tests.

genuinely the worst, least caring teacher i have ever had in my life. she finds unessecary marks to take off on tests and assignments, she litterally wants everyone to fail and the stuff we do in class doesn't even relate to the textbook, and the textbook is all in french now (for a literal beginners french class) make it make sense.

Idk what happened to her like 10 years ago but her ratings have def changed. I find the recent ones to be accurate. She's a little unorganized/unprepared for each class and she is definitely unnecessarily rude/passive aggressive towards students who struggle with French. It makes class awkward and not the best learning environment. Don't recommend.

Marie gets a lot of undeserved hate in my opinion, she is a very tough grader and you will have to work and study for her tests but she is by no means a horrible teacher. People told me I wouldn't actually learn french in this class but because of Marie I feel like I walked away with an amazing base for my french studies in the future.

Marie-C was most definitely not the greatest teacher. She grew on me by the end of the semester but often was passive aggressive towards certain students during class. I would try to get a French class with a different teacher. The other reviews I believe are a little too harsh. You won't die if you have her.
I would say, she is the WORST teacher I have ever meet.

DEFINITELT EXTREMLT HARSH GRADER
DO NOT TAKE CLASS WITH HER!!!

Harsh grader.
0 accessibilty.
0 caring.
DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HER!

She is also procrastinating. I didn't get most of my grades even if it was nearly the end of the term.
She almost does not respond to emails. 0 caring.
She always forgets to post the answer key even if it is the day before the test.
Her classes are always irrelevant to what we have in the book, we have to study by ourselves for the tests.
if you dont know music or dont like jazz do not take this course. i was tricked by the bird course fallacy and oh my god am i sorry - prof is adorable but studying is so miserable rip

One of the coolest and nicest teachers at Mcgill. Super easy quizzes but a bit challenging tests as they require a lot of memorization. However if you put in a little effort you can easily ace the course. Jazz with Dave was so much fun, it's a great class to learn some basic Jazz.

Jazz with David Laing is unarguably a fun and easy time. You have no textbook because the assigned songs you must listen to essentially make up your textbook and the entire material of the course. Imagine each song is like a chapter of a textbook. That is literally all you have to master for this easy A course. Therefore attendance is pointless.

Great GPA boosting elective. The tests are MCQ and centered around listening identification and the questions themselves are very straightforward. I recommend listening through the assigned playlist for each test at least three times per week to really master it and then your test will be a breeze. The concert reports are also graded generously.

This is Art of Listening on steroids. David Laing takes over the second half and the test is based on pure listening and memorization skills. Second test: 40 songs, remember the bolded artists, what instrument they play, and title of song. Third midterm: same format but only 21 songs (because they last longer). Classic memorization-MCQ easy electiv

MUAR 393 is not a bird course. The teacher makes it hard on students to identify what song is which, as they all sound similar (most do not include lyrics and have similar instruments). However, if you are ready to devote dozens of hours to listening to the tracks, you could end up with an A. I would not recommend to take it in the summer.

not a bird course and probably hardest class i've taken at mcgill. super hard to differentiate songs (almost no lyrics and all have similar instruments). take art of listening instead. 3 exams, 2 music reports + 1 liner notes. i have an elaborate background on jazz and thought this was extremely difficult and almost dropped it because of low avrg!

Avoid at all costs. The class is quite easy because there is nothing too difficult to comprehend or any tricky questions. However, this will consume your life- you will need to memorize more than 30 songs for tests (some of which are 16 minutes long) and you'll need to know all the different instruments, players and titles. Prof is adorable though.

Though very kind and talented when it comes to his knowledge of Jazz, Professor Laing could make this class more difficult than required on the basis of simply lowering the class average. Be warned, it is difficult to distinguish songs from one another and he doesn't care. He went out of his way to increase difficulty due to the high average.

The guy is a jazz genius. Not only is he a master of his craft, but he transmits that passion to his students. His lectures are very informative, yet also entertaining, and his exams are incredibly easy. If he taught any other classes, I'd take them in a heartbeat!

do NOT take biol465. he clearly does not care about the course, has no interest in giving feedback and is unclear in what he expects from you. i took this course of out genuine interest for the topic and i regret it majorly. course as a whole is unorganized, TAs unhelpful, and Green unwilling to do anything about it.
He gives vague or no feedback and admitting his grading of presentations was subjective and pretty random. His lectures were boring and mumbly. Would not recommend taking conservation biology.
Prof. Green is an awesome guy, with a clear passion for herpetology. Fun field trip, interesting lectures, and many different modes of testing - the lab exam is the hardest!

No complaints for Green, he definitely is very knowledgeable. However, the course and grading of the course (along with one of the awful TAs) made me regret taking Conservation Biology. I've heard the equivalent at mac is a lot better.

AMAZING class, AMAZING teaching... made me change my major from neuro to bio.  If I end up back at McGill for grad school, I wouldn't be sad to work in Green's lab.  Just be prepared for lots of work.
This class is awesome, and Green knows his stuff.  Lab exam is a killer though.
Good prof--funny, enthusiastic, approachable.
Often delayed or cancelled classes. Unorganized and empty promises about robotic usages. Poor communication.

I think the course by itself requires you a fair amount of knowledge beforehand. If you are comfortable with search algorithms and some stats knowledge such as conditional probability, then this class is helpful to you in going deeper into the field. The Prof. is very nice and helpful during office hours and after classes, yet disorganized.
Everything was sucks. The materials were unorganized. No solution for the question.

The most disorganized prof I've ever had. December was filled with 3 assignments while for two months of the semester, he put nothing out because "he's working on it". Took forever to release the project even though it's pretty much the same as last sem. 

This class could be better if taught by a prof who is passionate and on top of their stuff.

We didn't get the grades for the first two assignments a week before the final exam.  For the entire first 2 months,only 2 assignments then the last 3weeks, one project one assignment 2 study report due the same week. Super disorganized, awful experience. Seems he doesn't pay attention for this course at all. Content is great, but he made it worst
Do not take him ! Final so difficult a lot of assignments projects at the end of the semester. Do not take him if you can avoid.
Just No. Do not take this class witht his prof. Spare yourself.
Uninspiring lectures and very disorganized. This class would definitely be easier if it was taught by someone with more enthusiasm. The other review on December 10 sums it up pretty well.

He only gave us 2 assignments to do for two whole months. Then in the final month where we have to study for finals, he posted group assignments, group project, assignmnent all at once, which I found pretty heavy. Even though it's the end of the semester, we still haven't gotten graded assignments. Lectures are pretty heavy.
ChatGPT can teach this course better than this guy. Probably grades faster too.

He mentioned not much math in this course, however all of the homework was math based. I repeatedly emailed for help and help was given but still not understood. Lectures are too fast with too much info to digest. No time to ask for elaboration. Not very approachable. Laughed at students' responses (discouraging others)

If you don't like math, you won't like his teaching style. Uses calculus equations instead of words so everything is extremely unclear. Exam questions always use this math but never in a way covered in class, so you're expected to understand it fully so as to go beyond class material. Not a fun course but he's a nice guy, and knows his stuff.

Disorganized, unclear, rambling.  This guy likes to walk around with a stunned look on his face and scribble on the board.  Absolutely the worst prof I have ever had.  He might be better for lower-level classes but the obvious disinterest he has for teaching is appalling.
Easy class. He truly is goofy but is a really nice guy.
He's a good prof. The class was fairly interesting.
Damn good prof. He managed to teach a course full of Calc 3 level math to a bunch of students who didn't have experience past calc 2. I highly reccomend.
Best Teacher / Class I've Had So Far!

I heard a student say Straub told him the only classes he really cared about were the upper levels, and you could tell in class.  Even so, the course material was interesting, if you're into that sorta stuff. Funny guy.
Great guy - truly wants his students to do well - great sense of humor
He's so goofy!

David is amazing. He does sometimes lose his train of thoughts in the middle of an explanation, but his lectures are fun and engaging. I learned more from him and his funny rants than I did in Circuits 1&2. If you go to lectures/ talk to him about things you don't understand, he'll be super accessible and caring. The midterm averages turn around 40-50%, but he is aware of this so he makes the final so much easier.

He's an awesome prof who cares for his students. His lectures aren't too great since he sometimes gets lost in his sauce but it's worth attending as he'll only cover materials featured in class for the exams.

He's not a good lecturer, hell he doesn't even understand the material he teaches, but he is a nice person, makes the lecture a bit more lively and will own up to his mistakes. His exams are also not impossibly hard. Be ready to work on everything yourself.

He was a nice guy, but his lectures were not well organized and did not help much for the course (maybe he was just tired as it was an 8am course). Unclear prof with low quality and incomplete notes and slides.

holy yap. every lecture was crammed w info and not much opportunity to engage, so somewhat mind numbing. he is nice and very passionate ab china

I recommend if you actually want to learn about China. Definitely attend all lectures and be ready to type notes quickly as he covers A LOT. Writing reviews of this guy as the semester goes on. Thoroughly unimpressed so far. Has no control of the lecture (kids talk over him the whole time). took it for Age of Samurai, wow. awesome class. for a 400 level, its normal to have 150 pages/ week of reading, but it was super interesting so it wasn't too bad. had this class in fall '23, the lectures are pictures that he talks over, so better pay attention and attend class. Lots of work and lectures are hard to understand if you weren't in class.

He would carefully read your paper and provide extensive feedback. You can tell he is a thoughtful person who takes both academic work and teaching very seriously. Talks quite fast and puts little information on the slides. It's really difficult to know what you're gonna be tested on considering the midterm criteria feels quite vague and broad and so much material is covered. But he's passionate and gives thorough feedback. I'd suggest using the s/u option for his classes as they are interesting.

grading was brutalll on the papers but he gives good feedback. intimidating/not very approachable and his lectures are VERY hard to follow. he goes off on a lot of lengthy tangents but the slides have like 10 words on them, and there's so much content it's impossible to figure out what you actually need to study (which he doesn't really help with)
Simply put, the best lecturer I have ever had. Super fascinating guy that fosters a thought-provoking and comfortable environment.

His lectures are really engaging. Mandatory isn't necessary but would recommend going to class to get a full understanding of the content. The class is not hard but depending on how interested you are in neuro can be a lot of information.
Genuinely good at explaining slides. Clear presentation and answers questions well.
The best professor
Really good teacher who is passionate. Very open to questions.
He is one of the nicest professors and makes sure to explain everything clearly. He really wants you to do well and understand the material. Would definitely recommend!

Great guy, doesn't expect too much from students, tests are fair. I enjoyed the readings (all of them are written by him and they aren't boring like most classes). Cares about students and teaches very clearly. Tests are very fair and all multiple choice.

Ragsdale is the most energetic and caring teacher I had in U1, straight to the point with many explanations and examples to make the picture very clear. Professor Ragsdale makes even the driest anatomy topics engaging. Lectures are clear and thorough, with fair exams. Attending class and using tools like unstuckstudy make for an easy A if you're willing to put in the work.

He was the best professor I had in my first semester. His explanations and slides were beyond clear. He wanted the content to came off as common sense and he achieved that. His questions are very applied and not just based on memorization, so make sure to understand his parts.
One of the best classes I've taken at McGil - Prof Schumacher teaches in a very engaging way and I would reccommend him.

Listen to everyone who says this class is the HARDEST you will ever take. However, Prof Schumacher was great - always accessible via office hours/email, and provided very detailed feedback. The final is worth 50% + really long, but actually not difficult if you review the material thoroughly. Didn't enjoy the course but appreciated the prof.

He is one of the best profs at Desautels. His class is one of the hardest, but you will learn more from this class than any other. You'll spend twice as much time on this class but it'll be worth it. He's a very smart, humble and caring prof. Highly Recommend if you're up for it.

This course is probably the hardest of ALL Desautels. Be ready to put in a lot of time and effort. However, it will be very rewarding. You will learn a lot of things from a great prof (unlike some major courses). Best finance class I have ever taken, best professor I have ever had; so glad I took this class! Anyone genuinely interested in finance who doesn't take M&A with Schumacher is making a huuge mistake

Schumacher is a great professor. Really interesting and knowledgeable. Very accessible outside of class. For M&A, it is a lot of case work group projects. Fantastic lectures, but brutal Exam. Definitely a professor I recommend, but be ready to really put the work in. His class is no joke. You will genuinely need to put in twice as much time as you would for a regular class.

Fantastic Professor, but high expectations for the class as well as your pre-requisite knowledge. The pre-requisites listed for FINE 490 are nowhere near enough. Super interesting material. David is really nice and knowledgeable. He gives detailed feedback on each (of the very numerous) submission. Solid prof, he teaches what I consider to be the most content heavy part of NSCI 200 and teaches it pretty well. No complaints. Would recommend.

Clear and interesting lectures, although not necessary to attend them since the slides are very detailed). Fair evaluations and the midterm/final were similar to assignments/examples in class. Very active on the discussion page and would always give clear and detailed answers/explanations.

Lectures are definitely not necessary to attend, everything he goes over in class is in his slides already. Very clear instructor, provides a ton of practice materials and exams are simple.

Traditional blackboard teaching,

worst experience in mcgill so far.

He is definitely one of the most caring professor I've ever met, respond emails really quick, really trying his best to help you to learn and if you have any problems with the course, tell him and he will definitely help you! If you see him teaching the course, choose him! Midterm and finals are fair, really nice prof!

An angel descended from the heavens that somehow landed at McGill University. His assignments, midterm, and final are all super fair. Unlike all my other profs, he scanned all our finals so we could see mistakes. A bit monotone, but cares so much about his students.

I took Math323 in Fall2018. He is the kind of prof. that even after leaving the course for quite a period of time, I still want to say Thank You and appreciate that I had him for this class. great! pretty cool

Don is passionated, funny and willing to help. However, you need to be very confortable with matlab to be able to complete the assignments and the geochemistry material is challenging. The lectures are fast paced and you are often expected to figure out new stuff by yourself in the assignments. Even the TA's don't know the answer sometimes.

Don is a phenomenal prof. He takes the time to clearly explain concepts to be sure that you understand the material. He will take the time to go over tests with you so you can understand your mistakes and avoid making the same ones in other evaluations. The assignments are difficult but really help with your understanding of the topics covered.

Don is really good at explaining concepts and he's a fun prof. Tests aren't too difficult, but the assignments are literally death. Labs are not mandatory or graded but good luck understanding anything if you skip them.
Makes the assignments and midterms tough to force you to think through the material. But grades very easily. If you put in the work, he'll reward you. Super approachable, nice guy.
Assignments are challenging, really encourages students to think. Great professor, not an easy course though.
Great Teacher!And really not bad looking...very nice guy.

This course will suck up your free time. Assignmets are never-ending, and tests are difficult. Get in with the EPS crowd, 'cause they're huge helps! Don is helpful, and go and see him, or else the assignments will remain impossible. He is a bit pervy though, and I hear he married his grad student...
Don is a rude man, plain and simple. His thinly-veiled annoyance and consistent belittling never cease to amaze me.
a little flamboyant, but friendly none the less. Could HE be the reason there are so many hot ladies in the EPSc undergrad program?????
A great proffesor who is sincerely interested in the progress of his students.  The best geology prof. at McGill.

great prof. not a huge fan of the topic, but he still made it engaging. very chill, enjoyable class. i thought grading was also very generous (compared to polisci grading, notably), and he was always available to help. truly a great professor

Nerbas is frankly one of the greatest professors at McGill. He is a wizard of Canadian history and is very engaged in his work. His lectures are slow-paced, but exciting moments make up for it. His assignments are fair; the study direction is clear. So long as you put in fair effort, you will get a fair grade. I could write more, but a wordcap here
incredibly knowledgeable, passionate, and kind. very highly recommend taking one of his classes, you won't regret it !

Professor Nerbas' lectures on Canadian history will be among the greatest you'll ever sit through. Every assignment has the most inspirational, detailed, helpful feedback you could ever ask for. He is an encyclopedia and will undoubtedly go down as one of the great scholars of Canadian history. Do not pass up a chance to take one of his classes.

Among the best history profs at McGill. Super kind and accessible during office hours, a fair grader with good feedback. He made what could potentially be dry lecture material very interesting and interactive. Grading consisted of one short essay, one research paper, a final exam and participation. Highly recommend taking any of his courses
Amazing professor! He engages with students and tries to bring some humour to canadian history. Hist 202 is not demanding and is fairly easy considering the topic.

Prof Nerbas is a fantastic lecturer and is engaging although only so much can be done considering the (no offense) boring topic. There is a fair amount of reading and the grading on the papers can be a little tough. Lectures are mostly from him speaking rather than slides so paying attention is critical but besides that, great prof.

Makes pre-confederation Canadian history so much more interesting than I could ever have imagined. If you are in first year and have the opportunity to take Hist 202 with prof. Nerbas DO IT!!! Not only is he a really strong lecturer, and the TA was a really fair grader, but the assignments were interesting (historical newspaper analysis).

great professor who made the course (which could have ended up extremely tedious) interesting and engaging. the criteria for assignments was very clear and the question response marking was fair. i did find that the TA marking for the essays was slightly harder.

While the lectures could sometimes feel long and slightly boring (let's be real - it's Canadian history), prof. Nerbas' passion for his craft absolutely makes up for it! He genuinely seems super interested in what he teaches, which makes duller lectures more engaging. He's also super nice - went to his office once and he was extremely helpful!

Amazing professor. MGCR382 lectures can feel repetitive since he spends 30mins recapping the previous class, but they're worth attending. He clearly explains the logic behind diagrams and calculations in a way slides alone don't. He's accessible outside class and brings great energy. Highly recommend.

his lectures were fun to attend, he always goes over the material from last class so even when i missed a class i never felt behind. takes a lot of time to explain complicated concepts he's just a good vibe
Prof gives lots of practice for the quiz and exam, but the exam was much harder than expected. Lectures are generally helpful, but diagrams and explanations are confusing sometimes.

Professor Don is a great prof who knows how to explain concepts really well. His class pace is quite slow which gives you a lot of time to review content and understand. He grades fairly and doesn't have hard assignments.
Good professor, explains well. Do exercises and listen in class and you can definitely get an A

Professor Melville appears to be a "chill" professor, however, I would argue he's just disorganized. Very little explanation of expectations/guidelines for assignments, and repeats the same content over multiple lectures. Wouldn't recommend a class with him if you even slightly like to know what is expected of you.

Very engaging prof who made IB more enjoyable! I found the lectures interesting and I love that the prof gave a recap of the previous class to make concepts extra clear. Exams are fair and the quiz is easier than midterm—just make sure you know the content well.

Don is a great professor! His lectures are clear, entertaining, and useful (they're always packed). The course content is not easy, but he simplifies it and gives lots of practice questions. Stay caught up with him and do all the assignments he tells you to do, and the midterm will be super easy.

Very nice simple professor. Explains concepts very well making them simple to understand. Will go over things many times if he thinks people haven't understood. Just a great guy. However, the second half of this course sucks.

I learned more in this core class than in Fine482 with Sujata. Shows to what extent a professor can make a class more or less interesting. Don is a great professor, and the content was hard and challenging but feasible.

Dr. van Meyel is a great prof. He does an amazing job organizing 532 and lets the students run the seminars. The seminars are both engaging and insightful. I highly recommend taking this course regardless of major.

This upper level seminar class was fantastic. Tons of readings and work, but overall an incredible learning experience. Well worth taking if you can manage to handle the weekly workload and are genuinely interested in neurodevelopmental research. One of the best professors I have ever had at McGill - super clear, helpful and kind.
A beautiful soul. Truly a godsend of a Professor.

Often the students who have negative remarks are those who don't put in the work for this class. Honestly, it is a heavy class that requires constant review. Dr. Ventura does an AMAZING job at teaching the material, is available when needed for questions and is fair. Don't learn by memorizing..understand the material and you will do great!

I had Dr. Ventura in Fall 2020, an online semester. She is very kind, but the way she planned it made it harder. We had 4 hrs/week live sessions, and 2 hours pre-recorded lectures that took 4hrs. The course was also very heavy, so it seemed like we only studied anat. Her exams were tricky and very long, but you get used to her questions. Not easy!

She's so far the best professor I've ever had. Lectures are GREAT and labs are so chill. Go to that class with the mindset of learning not getting an A, and you'll get an A. She is the type of professor that put effort to help her students so appreciate that. Got F on the midterm bcs i MEMORIZED, ended up with A on the final bcs i VISUALIZED!

Dr. Ventura is one of the best teachers I have ever had. She explains the material clearly and accessibly. She is also not afraid to make her lecures fun. Her exams can be difficult - definitely not an easy A class, but her questions are reasonable and not excessively tricky. She is a professor that truly wants her student to suceed.

Dr. Ventura is one of the best profs in McGill. She really cares about her students doing well and actually learning the material, not just memorizing and regurgitating it (aLthough memorizing everything is a must to actually answer her questions). Her exams are kinda tough, but they're not impossible. If you put in the work, an A is VERY doable

Dr. Ventura is simply amazing. She brought back the cadaveric dissection labs at McGill to help improve our education, and is extremely knowledgable and well respected in her field. She teaches relatively fast and although classes and labs aren't mandatory, I highly encourage future students to attend them.
Very accessible. Had her for 315 & 316. Study hard and go beyond just memorizing the facts and you will get an A.

I took her for ANAT 315&316. Admittedly, her notes and lecture/lab outlines are great; however her tests go way beyond what she teaches in class. She is a med/dent professor as well so her exams have way too many clinical case study questions which are not easy at all and often irrelevant to a PT/OT/Kin student. She makes mistakes in lectures too.

I wont lie, Dr. Ventura's class is hard, but its more due to the nature of the content rather than her teaching style. Her slides and lecture outlines are super useful, and she's super accessible and understanding through email, lab time, and office hours. She also keeps you on your toes by giving midterms that make you think, overall a great prof!

Great prof! Had her for both ANAT 315 & 316. Really enjoyed her class. She's super clear with explanations, provides goods demos and lecture outlines, is approachable to answer questions and has great slides! Her exam questions vary in difficulty, from pure memorisation to clinical questions. Tip for studying: Understand the material!

A fair bit of reading (very niche & well-chosen books), if you tooknotes during the lectures, it is not hard to do well on the tests. Farrow seems eccentric, he has an unconventional or slightly odd behaviour that hints to extremely deep insight. This class changed my perception of religion & opened my eyes to incredibly moving & profound concepts.

My first sign that something was wrong should have been when the class of around 25 people shrunk to 8 by midway through the semester. I guess I didn't see the writing on the wall. I had a university excused absence that he refused to acknowledge, and that took points off my attendance grade.

Great Prof. Definitely a though grader, but he makes you a better writer so it's worth it. Clearly has strong opinions, but will allow argument if you have a good point and if you operate in good faith. Highly recommend, one of the best profs at McGill.

Farrow goes up twice a week and performs more of a catholic mass rather than a lecture. there is ZERO critique of religious texts or beliefs. he just spews his own religious propaganda and deems it as fact for the course. the content is extremely challenging NOT suited for the 200 level. the absolute worst professor I've had at McGill.

Very, VERY Catholic. Dismissed some aspects of Protestant theology as 'not worth focusing on,' which is hilarious. Has some Interesting Opinions on patient-led euthanasia, vaccines, and LGBT rights. Possibly pro-life, but won't come out and say it. Deeply condescending. Fascinating the same way a car accident is.

Farrow does have some 'polarizing' personal opinions that he makes known, he accepts differing opinions AS LONG as you are well informed and can back them. He clearly is very well educated and I enjoyed the reading material. He's up for debate but people are scared to challenge him.

While I disagree with him on many things, Prof. Farrow is an exceptionally intelligent man and well-respected for good reason.  That being said, I would NOT recommend him as a professor for lower level religion courses as his delivery of info can be complex & not undergrad friendly.  But if you put in the work and show you care, he will see that.

Expects students to be already well-versed in Christian theology + have previous knowledge of the Bible. 
Unfriendly, polarizing attitude. Lectures included a lot of unnecessary personal opinions that did not improve the lessons.

Farrow has very little respect for his students and their intelligence while also expecting that everyone have a thorough knowledge of the Bible. Class was insanely difficult for a 200 level course and Farrow lectures more on his opinions than well-rounded analysis.
Worst class at McGill. Farrow is unhelpful when you have questions and has no respect for his students

Dylan's content is well organized, clear and well communicated, however his testing style is very harsh, exams are not easy. It's nice to have a mech prof who can use technology efficiently and appropriately but beware on how difficult his exams are, will test you on something he spends 30s mentioning.

Took both thermo 1 and 2 with Prof Caverly. Easily the most well-organized MECH courses I have taken at McGill. His expectations and deadlines are reasonable, lectures are clear, and exams are fair. He is also very available for office hours and responds to emails and discussion board posts.
Very good lectures, notes, and PPTs. Exams are fine if you study properly, which you can do by following his notes. Nothing too unexpected either, although they are sometimes long.
Very easy to understand his lectures, tests were fair and alternate grading schemes were very helpful!
Engaging and kind professor. Open to feedback as a new professor. Would take again anyday!

He speaks clearly, records lectures, and posts all his content for students to access. Exams are fairly written and graded. The group project was a little too intensive to only be worth 10% of the grade, but not the end of the world. Overall a very smooth learning experience.

Lectures are never too fast-paced and he always explains the basic understanding of each concept, no matter how far into the course. Very approachable and easy to talk to and will email you back quickly. Group project is way too much effort for the weight though
Nice guy. He introduces students to neurophysiology very clearly and writes straightforward exam questions.

Ruthazer is a great prof; he knows what he is talking about and is clearly interested in the work and material. However, he is a busy person so he takes ages to get grades back. We received our midterm 1 grade back a day before our midterm 2, which can suck for people who like to know how to change their study methods based on previous exams.

Ruthazer is solid by McGill standards. In typical McGill prof fashion, he's a bit full of himself, but he's a nice enough guy. He zooms through content, so definitely go to tutorials and rewatch lectures. Aside from that tho, his exams are fair and he delivers boring content pretty well. Did catch myself falling asleep occasionally in his class...

This professor is probably one of the best I've ever had at McGill. Not only does he explain the course material well and in an engaging way, he is a very kind person. Also answers emails extremely quickly! The course itself is not easy; you have to study, but he readily answers students' questions and seems to care about students' success.
He's a solid prof - I have nothing good or bad to say about him. NSCI 200 is difficult and he gets the material across pretty well. Would recommend.

This prof is really smart. He is a very fast lecturer, so you'll probably have to use Lecture recordings in order to write down everything he says. His part of the course is the easiest, and he explains it really well, with a great deal of details. Make sure you understand everything for this course. It's the key to succeed.

Fantastic prof that will take the time to ensure that you understand the concepts even outside of class hours.  Very helpful and very clear, although he does speak rapidly.  His exam questions are fair, and based aprox. 50% memorization and 50% concept - all from his slides.  Material was very interesting.
Excellent professor and incredibly clear explanations but he tends to run through the material at a blindingly fast speed (luckily the class is recorded)
GREAT prof! Very clear, very organized, and very helpful. His  classes are fascinating, and he really knows his stuff :)
Great prof! Very helpful whenever you have questions concerning the material. Approachable, clear, gives fair(not necessarily easy, but fair) exams. I'd definitely take a class with him again.
Her lecture are interesting to listen to
if youre not religious, pick a religion and pray.

ridiculous lectures and final and grading scheme. don't even give a free homework/quiz mark. all your grades = 2 midterms and extremely difficult final exam. she grabs all tiny tiny details which only occupies 1/10 slides and puts them into your exam. every ppt is more than 100 slides and with bunch unrelated old pictures but no words. don't take.

Very nice person, should not teach this class. Slides are decades old, no words, just terribly pixelated images. Gives outdated information contradicted by textbook. Get ready to be tested on a name that's on a single slide no context and a picture of a plant. More concerned about herbal remedies and environmental toxicology than drug mechanisms.

If so many people complained about her slides for the past few years yet she didnt take any feedbacks, i think it says alot about the professor. 
Her lectures are boring, tedious, monotone.

i hope she retires. 
her slides are TERRIBLE. its like she took a screenshot of a screenshot of a screenshot of a screenshot to a point where the pixels are too blurry. the slides have no words just bunch of pictures and graphs.

Dr. Zorychta is nice. Honestly the class she teaches just has a ton of content, but its clear she puts a lot of time in her lecture slides and all the images are very helpful, without them this class would be impossible as my brain would melt from how boring it is. usually only puts content she discusses on exams, so no suprises.

Her lecture slides are pretty bare and difficult to follow, and lectures are low energy- i highly recommend buying the NTCs for this class if you want to succeed. That being said, she is a very sweet prof who I think truly cares about her students learning and doing well.
Avoid this woman at all costs!!!!!! I believe her courses need a more modern teaching style. ALSO, POST REAL SLIDES!!

As a graduate pathology student, it's a little unnerving knowing that undergrads' GPAs are in the hands of this woman. I have never encountered a professor as out-of-touch and unaware of her inability to teach in my entire academic career. My deepest sympathies to folks who are required to take PATH 300.

If you want bird courses, you've come to the right place. If you want to learn anything, LEAVE! The only thing you will learn is everything this man has ever done in his life. Every lecture is him talking about himself and then panicking that there's a reading we have to review. Self-centered, uninsightful, boring. Avoid unless you wanna waste time

He's an approachable and passionate guy, but his lectures are all over the place and disorganizes, and his assignments are vague and toughly graded. The class is very abstract and its unclear what is important or not. I would not take this class unless you are an anthropology student.

clearly passionate and approachable, but all over the place making it incredibly difficult to grasp what you're supposed to be learning. Assignment instructions are so unnecessarily wordy, making it difficult to get a clear idea of how to do the assignments. every student was given 100% on the first assignment worth 15%, with a final worth 50%.

pretty interesting guy, but in my opinion, some people just aren't meant to be profs. very unorganized during the lectures to the point you're never really sure what to be taking notes on (spends a lot of the lectures talking about his dreams?). overall the class isn't that hard, just very confused what i learned.

Great professor and easy introductory class. Very knowledgeable and likes to go off on tangents during class, but these are often funny. Don't really need to do readings or even come to class. Final was take-home and online. Would highly recommend as a bird course.

Super funny, laid-back, and knowledgeable, but his lectures are hard to follow. They are not recorded and slides are not posted, and he often goes off on random tangents. That being said, the grading is  generous and the assignments were interesting. A lot of the topics are very niche, and are fascinating if you can figure out what he's saying.

No slides/lecture recordings. There's only 2 assignments & 1 final worth 50% so no way of knowing what his exams look like, note taking wise. A bit disorganized, someone reminded him that he skipped over a unit and he just pulled out a folded piece of paper and gave a 10 minute summary of it. Not a bad person, just maybe not the best teacher

Just take notes of what he says. He talks about every reading and what's important. Topic wise, follow the sequence like a narrative. I'll confess that I am already familiar with quite a large portion of the topics but they are so simple to understand using what you already know. All assignments were take-home and was so engaging and fun. Do it!
Very knowledgeable and caring professor. He does go off tangent, but his lectures are still really interesting. Easy and engaging class that I would recommend

Honestly one of my favourite profs so far. People say that his lectures are boring, unrelated to the course content, although if you pay attention he has a lot of interesting stories and experience to relay to his students. Its obvious he is an accomplished anthropologist, and for many who are studying anthropology, he is very accessible.
He doesn't know what he's doing unfortunately. He's not a bad guy and I can tell he's really smart, but he just doesn't know how to teach.
nice prof! nice teaching method, but i always feel lost in his lectures, but still can understand the material.

Best teacher ever! He treat class as entertainment. I don't understand why you guys treat him so bad :(    I love his passion and confident so I'll definitely give Lima 5star and divide these stars into 5 times. He just play on one board and go to another one, class finished! don't look slides, you just look at him--the shiniest star in Armstrong!

I have never studied harder for a class in my life and felt like i was getting so little output. The midterm and exam are nearly impossible and no matter how many times you do all the practice problems they will not be similar to the exam. Best tip is to live by practice exams and prepare for the worst

He is not a great lecturer, although his slides are very clear. He is also a nice person that is willing to help. Assignments and midterm were straightforward if you practiced enough but the final was much tougher

Overall a careful and nice teacher. He used flip classroom, which means you do need to watch the recordings and understand the lecture of the recording. If you focus enough while watching his recordings, you will know the materials better and realize he explained clearly and organized. Do enough practice is helpful as well.

all the needed material is on the slides, which he communicates clearly in his online lectures. Very responsive to questions and always available to help. Provides lots of information on how to do his assignements
Very bad teacher even though he is a nice person. He can't teach nor answer questions and exams are very tough. Don't take this class if it is your teacher
This semester was a weird one with it being half virtual and half in person, but I felt that he did a great job making sure students understood the material.

Lima is not the best lecturer in the faculty but doesn't deserve a 1.x rating. He reads slides in class but his slides are really good for a stats class. Assignment and exams are marked fairly and he's quite nice. can't complain
Amazing professor, wants to see her students do well, very accessible outside of class

SOCI247 was my fav lecture this semester. There was a lot of reading but most were very interesting. highly recommend this class for anyone interested in the social sciences, and especially for soci students. Note - no lecture recordings and handwritten notes only so attendance is mandatory to do well and be up to date on testable material
This class is really eye-opening and I loved the teaching style of the prof. Readings are very important. It was one of the best classes I've taken at McGill.

I genuinely love this professor. They're so good at teaching and so knowledgeable. Very accessible for office hours. I think I learned more from this course in 1 semester than my entire time at McGill.

I liked her lectures, I thought they were entertaining and interesting and her lecture style worked for me. The no technology in class is annoying, especially because lectures aren't recorded and her slides are basically just a few bullet points, get ready to write in class. Although I found her grading scheme fair. She comes off tough but isn't.

Although very knowledgeable during her lectures the way the course was set up was personally not for me. No technology allowed when taking notes in the class, no lectures are recorded and gives only bullet points on her slides, there are lots of readings to do and specific details that will be tested on. I saw these as barriers to my performance.

The pace of lectures is a bit slow. I found Prof Weiner entertaining, but I think the syllabus could be much more engaging and progressive than it is. Attendance is not mandatory but very helpful when translating content to papers. Prof Weiner is blunt but reasonable, grading can be unclear.

- Prof Weiner is very knowledgeable and accessible outside of class 
- The course is very reading-heavy, but the readings are very interesting
- Lectures can feel disorganized, difficult to pinpoint what information is important
- Lectures are not recorded, and slides that are posted lack a lot of the details talked about during class

Her lectures were boring and unorganized but clearly interested in what she taught. Feedback was minimal and assessments were reading focused. She came across as rude and condescending the majority of the time, especially when answering questions.

Very passionate about her topic, has interactive and interesting lectures, and encourages discussing and sharing opinions in class. Accessible during office hours, gives good advice about assigments. Very tough grader though, if you're looking for an easy A this is not it

I don't have a science background and I found that some of her examples and stuff I didn't understand. She made videos to watch before class and they aren't too long. The assignments have tough questions but the teachers are always available to help.

She is clearly an expert in her domain; her lectures are crystal-clear. Does a fantastic job of exploring all the nuances and complicity of environmental issues. A very passionate professor and extremely nice human!
Methodical, passionate, kind, fair and well respected prof.  Takes the time to take questions.
absolutely loved Prof Cristescu, she is very passionate about invertebrates and it shows. she has a dry sense of humour which is funny. I would take another course with her if she offered one.

Great Lectures. The labs (biol 311) were very interesting dealing with modern concepts in organismal biology. I had a great hands on experience. I particularly enjoyed the poster presentations and the friendly atmosphere at the end of the class.
Sometimes difficult to understand but delivered content straight forwardly

She is well organized and makes smooth transitions between evolutionary concepts and specific details about various groups of invertebrates. I also liked how she repeats the key concepts (take home messages).  The words of the day are also useful and exam questions are fair.

She makes sure to answer questions when needed. Her slides and the content in this section are super clear and quite easy to learn. Questions in the finals were also exactly what we would expect after taking this section. I do think that the lectures are heavy but it's super easy to review them afterwards.

She was super sweet and answers questions very well, however her lectures can be sometimes boring and monotone. I usually just watched the recordings on 2x speed because they were pretty slow. She was good at answering questions during the final and her questions were very fair and straight from the lectures. She also explains the material well.

Answers questions really well when people ask. She makes little jokes in lectures and doesn't change her tone sometimes when she does which makes them even funnier. Her exam questions were pretty fair and she's actually one of the only professors that answers questions at the exam in a helpful way!

Not sure where to begin. She seems frozen when she lectures and yet is all over the place in her thoughts and details. Once I could have sworn that I some kind of yellow fluids in the corner of her eye.

Content was very boring to me, and the prof was very difficult to understand. Lowkey would recommend not going to the lectures and just watching them online, or even go though the slides because she just reads off them and does not explain.  However the questions she made for the final were very generous and fair.
