Pretty shocked by her ratings, she really is a great prof with very interesting lectures. You just have to participate and come to class, and you will do great in the tests. Retook another class with her and got an A- with moderate effort.

honestly, she rocks. i went into the class super scared cause of the reviews, but she turned out to be super fun, super open, and a lot less scary than i first believed. she's not a prof that's gonna coddle you but she does very much want you to succeed as much as you want you to succeed. she's unironically one of the coolest ppl out there.

Honestly, many people really hate this teacher, but I did absolutely like her. If you attend every class, her material is interesting, and her way of teaching is also critical; it pushes you to reflect. Trust me, I have attended many stupid and useless classes, but this one is good. Yeah she is strict, but it does not mean she doesn't teach badly.

This was one of the most frustrating classes I've taken at McGill. The professor was disorganized and didn't seem to have much real-world experience related to the course. She wasn't open to discussing grades or feedback Even tho I passed, I didn't feel like I learned much from her teaching. Would not recommend this class if you have other options.

She doesn't teach she diminishes. There's no grading scheme, no transparency, just arbitrary marks handed down with zero explanation. She shuts down questions, discourages curiosity, and makes you feel like effort is pointless. It's not just incompetence it's a complete lack of care. Cold, distant, and unfit to mentor anyone. Avoid!!!!!

Avoid this professor at McGill. Her course materials are severely outdated, lectures are disorganized, and grading is inconsistent. She demonstrates a profound lack of expertise and closed-mindedness. Even MBA students find her lost. You'll learn nothing despite an easy grade. I got an A but learned nothing hope she gets hit by a bus worst human.

She does have a particular lecturing style, but tries to make the class engaging. There are frequent readings to be done and discussion posts. Graded by group project with presentation, midterm and final. I found the final more challenging and a bit tricky, but overall solid class and I'd take it again.

In general, the prof is nice, the midterms are not easy, and the grading is bad. We don't receive any feedback on our grades or responses to our emails. Even if you are a good student, be ready to have an unexpected grade in that class. Very disappointed. Worked hard to finish with a grade that did not reflect the work or effort put into the class.
One of the best classes ive took, lectures were always interesting and she made class very engaging! I would definitely take her again.

Prof Obukhova is one of the most caring teacher I've had. She strives to to engage her students with the content even during in online classes. She is knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches and very flexible. Read the cases, understand the main concepts, participate, and ask about her expectations. Great professor!

The goat. Kind inside and outside of class. Pleasant to speak with. Easy to bounce essay ideas with. Teaching was mainly student discussions. How fun a class depends on how much the students participate and engage with the material. Nothing out of the ordinary aside from his extraordinary kindness

If you're going to take poetics, take it with professor MacLaren! He's an incredibly knowledgeable and understanding prof. Great lectures, although no online resources so if you want to do well you absolutely must go to lectures. The homework is very reasonable and he's super helpful in office hours. I wish he taught more undergrad classes!

i found prof maclaren very kind at first but kind of sneaky--i managed to do well in his class but his paper grading was sometimes really unexpectedly harsh, in a way that no other (even strict) mcgill english teachers have been. overall grade is a mix of papers, exams, participation/attendance, and smaller assignments, so easy to do well.

Prof. MacLaren is passionate and strives to pass on his love of literature to his students. Kind and clear, he wants his students to do well. Classes were interesting and pleasant. One of McGill's best professors. Highly recommend.

Took his course on Alice Munro, and later asked him to supervise my undergrad thesis. Great guy. Some fairly stringent requirements for papers, but there are only 2 (plus one oral presentation) during the entire semester, so it isn't that hard to manage. He gives lots of good feedback. Only thing that may be difficult is keeping up with readings.
Super caring and sweet- was always willing to provide extra feedback / resources / help if you asked for it

maclaren is probably my #1 prof. his class is done discussion-style, and participation matters. personally, i really enjoyed this and it worked for me. maclaren is always available for an office hours chat and gives rlly helpful feedback, but has high/tough standards. rlly improved my writing. would love to take another class with him !!

Harsh grader without a lot of useful feedback. 311 lectures are dysfunctional open discussions. The content is interesting, but I don't think it's taught effectively. There are a LOT of papers, quizzes, exercises, and a midterm and a final on top of that. Way too much time required. I really wanted to like this class.

Loved taking this class, I'd absolutely recommend it! MacLaren is very caring and always available during office hours for feedback. There wasn't a lot of reading and only 2 essays for which you have quite some time. He takes attendance and participation so you have to come to class. Very interesting content.
Dr. Georges is a laid-back guy who is nice. His lectures are straightforward, and he included interesting fun facts in his slideshows. His portion of the exam was straightforward.

Elio is by far the best Math140 lecturer. He explains things very clearly and always answers questions during class. Uses some class time for textbook problems, which are also the exam problems-so that is very useful.
Great professor, explained the concepts like one would to a beginner, provided notes, and made classes fun to go to.

For someone who is not a fan of math, I loved taking MATH141 with Elio. He explains rather difficult topics in a straightforward way backed up by his strong reasoning & logic. He is a very accommodating prof who cares about his students. While both midterms were reasonable, I think the final was quite difficult. Nonetheless, I'd recommend his class
Nice guy, explains things thoroughly, and is easily available, I found the midterms to be reasonable but the final to be quite difficult!
very strong resoning, explain everything in a logic way, very kind

The best math teacher I've ever met.Calculus 2 was supposed to be a difficult subject, but Elio's strong logic and presentation skills did a great job of helping me understand the difficulties of the subject. He gives his students bonuses, which relieves some of the pressure on them.
She is definitely knowledgeable for the subjects she taught but the course materials and evaluation are very demanding and little help is provided.

My Berwick 618 advice to poli scis: Do the summer R Bootcamp no matter what (spreads out steep learning curve for non-quant people). Her peeves: perceived arrogance and using office hours to ask questions beyond the scope of the class. She's conflict-avoidant, sugarcoats feedback, and very competitive. Be careful how you assert yourself, she bites.

She's an amazing with the math, but I really found her difficult to communicate with and even more difficult to read (which is an observation also spontaneously made by friends). I usually don't give prof's 1/5's, but she didn't really help/address arising problems. She's not very flexible, and she's uninterested in mentorship. These matter.

Professor Berwick is an absolute gem. She is extremely knowledgeable, but remains very approachable and never flaunts her expertise to the class. She teaches content that is super relevant and necessary for those who want to pursue graduate studies or serious research. The content is tough, but she makes it accessible and easier to digest. 10/10!

Really nice professor. He cares for his students and doesnt just bulldozes with hard exams like other engineering profs. Lab reports werent marked too strictly. If I had an option to take all my Bioeng classes with him, I'd love to

He didn't lecture this year so it's not that he's a bad professor in any way (and the lecturer was honestly pretty great). Problem is the lab manuals are insanely unclear, loads of typos and unnecessary information. unclear grading, MATLAB just throws you under the bus, procedural errors in basically every experiment we've done so far.

This class was kind of a mess. Most labs didn't turn out like they should (procedural errors). The MATLAB section was on steroids. Lab reports were extremely long (+20 pages). A lot of work for a 200 level. Lastly, the statistics section was a total mess. But that was taught by a TA. Take home final (25%). Lab section (70%).

Great prof, very easy going. Class grade scheme was discussed as a class before made final. Gave us the option of exam or no exam and having papers weigh more.  Really knows the subject well, and is a chill prof as well. Take a class with him!

Very caring and warm professor who seems to go beyond to ensure accessibility and support. Prof Elbourne created an excellent environment to address a plethora of different historical issues and I enjoyed the class a lot. The emphasis on her assigned primary sources is important, and conferences are required. Her conference was also excellent.
Heavy on the weekly readings. She's a genuinely good person, gives good feedback, is very enthusiastic about what she teaches. Recordings are provided when needed and slides are posted.

She is such a caring and enthusiastic prof. She genuinely loves what she does and she is always willing to answer questions. If she doesn't know the answer to you question, she will find the answer and let you know the following class. Textbook chapters are long but they give additional information to back up her lectures. Would totally recommend

Warm, energetic, engaging and caring - she clearly loves what she does. Accessible and helpful. Her slides are perhaps not always the most well-structured but I enjoyed her lectures. I would gladly take more courses taught by her.

Take any course Dr. Elbourne offers. Not only is she incredibly knowledgeable about every topic she teaches, but she is easily one of the most approachable and helpful professors at McGill. Although there is a fair bit of writing in each of her courses, it is always marked fairly, with room for extension if needed. The praise is honestly endless.

It was a big class yet she still came off as very sweet, genuine, and approachable. Super knowledgeable without being pretentious. Great lecturer, but admittedly slides could be organized a bit better (not great for referencing after class). Watch out -- TAs could be hard graders, & conferences are awkward if you don't do the work. Go to class.

Prof. Elbourne is so lovely. She is so kind and looks to the class for feedback on assessments and lecture format. Though she sometimes seems a little frazzled and has a tendency to spend a little too much time on certain things (and not enough time on others), I really enjoyed this class. I'll take a research paper over a midterm exam any day!

Professor Elbourne is a model professor. She is not only incredibly impressive and accomplished as a scholar, but also extremely humble and goes above and beyond for all of her students. I could gush for a while and it would sound kind of weird, but she deserves it all.

I was so nervous taking this course again, but Elizabeth made it incredible! Everything was easier to understand and I am truly going to miss the class. Definitely plan on taking other classes she teaches.

Ms. Elbourne is everything you could want in a professor. Her lectures are really engaging, and most importantly, she goes out of her way to make everyone in the class as comfortable as possible. She is always available, and she is truly a kind person. Thank you for a great semester, I will certainly be taking a class of yours again.

prof knows material inside out, super articulate, very organized, and great at explaining difficult material.  attendance is a must as slides are skeletal; take notes! assignments (2 of em) can be tough, but help is super accessible via office hrs. somewhat difficult material made clear due to prof's excellence - what every course should be like!

Really great teacher.  Attendance is necessary to understand the lecture material, but his explanations clarify everything.  Interesting material and the occasional interesting tangent.  Overall a great class.  It's not easy at all and some of the material is difficult, but he explains it well.

A pretty hard class, attendance is highly recommended because the slides alone don't tell you much. BUT: If you attend, Tobin will make everything so much more worthwhile. So much knowledge, interest and fun bundled in one person is just unbelievable. Go to the office hours as soon as something's unclear, he will explain until you get it all.

This is an excellent teacher. He's super interesting and knows what he is talking about. He gives EXTREMELY useful examples, he is super helpful and is disgustingly organized. I would recommend showing up to all the lectures, the second teacher for intro to lingusitics is a bummer though and it gets MUCH tougher in the second half.
He's really interesting, talks fast, doesn't get behind in lectures. Everything is really easy to understand, but you have to keep up.
No Comments
took her summer class. just a midterm and final, plus 10% free with reflections during class. she's goated. midterm went great. awesome prof.

WOW. Prof Solomonova is incredible. She is a great lecturer, and her exams are perfect in terms of difficulty. She also readily accommodated during the STM strike, which few professors did. What a treat to be part of her class. I will truly miss PSYC 444 and her lectures.

Professor Solomonova is knowledgeable and there is not one dull moment throughout her lectures. She is  and respectful and charismatic. Final exam was take home, the questions were explained ahead in class.Concordia would benefit from having more teachers like professor Solomonova. I hope to be able to take one more class one day with her .

Not my favorite class. The project that made up 30% the course grade had unclear instructions and a vague rubric, with points removed for components that weren't mentioned in the rubric. Grades took a long time to be returned, and exam questions were confusing.

She is funny but sometimes very unhelpful. There's 2 midterms, 1 non-cumulative test, and video project. I had a meeting to talk about ideas and all she said was "it's good." No extra credits, no clear instructions, said this was a "400 level course." (aka I'm not helping you) Recordings released a week before any exams making attendance mandatory.

Despite the course being at 8:30 in the morning, her lectures were so engaging. The subject is super interesting and I love how many personal anecdotes he incorporates. The project and paper definitely weren't the most enjoyable for me but if you do well on the exams you will be fine. She is a wonderful person and interesting professor.

Great professor who truly seems genuine and caring. Her lectures are fun, she is very open and she's definitely not out to get you. That being said, the grading for the group project was pretty tough and having three exams + 2 assignments calls for a lot of work.

PSYC444 with Solomonova is one of my favourite classes I have taken at McGill. Her lectures are so engaging and and you can tell how much she loves sleep science. She also just seems super cool. The class structure got shifted a bunch this semester, but everything was still very fair and maintainable as long as you put in effort.

Incredibly engaging lecturer, interacts with students and funny personal anecdotes. She's a genius and obviously super passionate about what she teaches. Such a fun class. Challenging but in a great way.

Prof Solomonova is the best. Super knowledgable and funny, and awesome to talk to in office hours. Tests were super fair but I thought the group project and paper were overkill - previous years didnt even have this. Still, I learned a lot and wish she was teaching more classes.
Not easy to talk about problems, strict with rules, not a good lecturer. The handwritten notes he provided is not what being taught at class.

Good lectures but the grading scheme is a bit annoying. Everything counts for quite a lot (20% assignments, 40% across two midterms, 30% final) and none of the homeworks can be dropped. I did quite well on everything except for one midterm which meant that I couldnt get an A. Doing well is more about consistency than talent.

Good professor, with interesting material to teach. He seems willing to make sure you benefit from his course, but keen on not wasting more of time than he wants to. He has a stubborn sense of what's fair and what's not fair for his students.

Had to take MATH222 twice and Paquette made the material MUCH easier for me. Tho I really wish he had ppt slides or at least recorded the chalkboard. He's a bit dry in class but he makes calculus bearable. Midterm was surprisingly easy. Final was hard but not unfair. Textbook pdf was posted! He gives suggestions on which hard exercises to focus on

Overall correct. He should probably give more example in class. The quizzes and exams were much more difficult than what he presented in class, but as long as you do the tutorial you should get a excellent grade

Assuming you enjoy calculus, 222 is an excellent extension of concepts developed in previous calculus classes. Paquette is quite a good lecturer, my only complaint being the occasional lack of examples (in-lecture) and semi-frequent errors on his part when writing out formulas. As long as you refer back to the textbook, one can reasonably get by.
Great professor, would take again. Negative reviews are from probably from people intimidated by his 6'+ stature. Hopefully he gets his tenure

It's more like a measure theory class than an INTRO prob class. 

He uses Jacod Protter as our textbook and most assignment questions are from the textbook exercise. Assignments are long and really hard. Exams are harder. Lecture notes were pre-written, so it's really hard to follow in class.

great prof!! here to defend eliott's honor. "A practice assignment was given before final with problems that were almost impossible for many to solve, but no solution was provided." okay but problems from the practice asg were put on the final of course solutions could not be provided. he had 3 out-of-class review sessions to go over them.

Elliot has been one of my favourite profs at McGill and he puts a lot of effort into his class. For some reason other students in the class planned a coup-d'etat. The content was measure theoretic, but it was definitely possible to succeed with the prereqs. I loved 356 and decided to take 447 as an elective because he was teaching it. He is great.

Kind & patient prof and explains stuff pretty clearly. His questions were not as complex as people say at all. They require a mild amount of problem solving & critical thinking --- in most stem fields this is the norm and in fact it is way more intense than this. Some people just aren't used to thinking that way and then blame the prof.

For people taking this class in the future, try to get 100% on all assignments/class tests except class test 1 because final will be hard, and don't expect you will be able to solve stuff on final using similar methods you see in class. This class hurts me so much I would rather take biol200 again honestly :(

Some of the things on the slides are strangely organized. Expect test questions to be harder than the in-person material. Also, be careful! His section is first in the class, but features heavily on the final as well. Lenient grading for questions (show your work). Cooper is also just a nice guy, and very responsive to student inquiries.

Dr. Cooper's teaching abilities are passable but he provides very few practice problems, making it difficult to learn and study for his section of PHGY 311. In addition, the few practice problems he does provide not only lack an answer key but are also vastly simpler than his questions on exams, which are complicated and convoluted.

Coop is a great prof and presents material clearly. The only drawback is that he likes to make really hard test questions which require you to think out of the box and find a solution in a way he likely has not shown, which is difficult to do on a timed test. The flipside of this is that he is generous with part marks so long as you show your work.

PHGY 451 is very much different from PHGY 311. Dr Cooper's section consists of seminars instead of traditional lectures. He's very patient and will make sure everyone understands difficult concepts before moving on.
Tests are pretty hard, but the trick is to practice and not to overthink during them. He "just wanted to keep things simple"
No office hours, doesn't answer discussion board questions, and exam questions are always unclear. He seems like a nice person, but his lectures are so disorganized.

Absolutely horrible gives no partial credit on 2 question exams, luckily he only has a 4 week section in phgy 311, but he damages your entire semester grade during those 4 weeks, unneccesarily. Power trips on making questions hard and feeling smart.
Horrible prof, seems to take pleasure in making questions unreasonably hard, and gives no partial credit for 2 questions exams

Heaman is an amazing prof and historian. A bit disorganised, but on the whole she is an incredible historian who will help however she can. She will gladly share her knowledge with her students if they engage with the course material, and she is always happy to engage in debate or clarify her viewpoints to help you better understand the content.

She's a good person, a warm-hearted person. You can tell she has a lot of passion, but the problem is her course content is disorganized. Compared to other history professors, her lectures are chaotic that it's a little bit hard to understand what she's talking about.
Super smart and interesting, sometimes a tough grader but ultimately she wants students to improve and succeed. Taking courses with Heaman will definitely force you to become a better historian.

Fantastic lectures, though quite rapidly paced. I personally greatly enjoyed the small tangents that she sometimes goes on, as they always contribute interesting or entertaining details. While I do believe the grading was more than fair, Heaman's standards are probably not suited to beginners. Recommend anyone be in second-year HIST or above.

Lovely person! Prof. Heaman is a very passionate lecturer, sometimes will go on tangents but these tangents are often super interesting and at times funny. Amazing person outside of class, very supportive of students and a caring person. Will always answer questions, whether in class, after class, email or office hours, very accessible prof.

I see a lot of reviews saying she is a bad lecturer, this is not the case. Her lectures are based on the readings, while her thoughts may seem scattered, she connects her lecture with outside sources and to the required reading of the week. 

Super accessible out of class, not a harsh grader at all, she just looks for specificity in your answers.

Heaman is an absolutely wonderful person outside of the class, but this class is tough. Don't expect good marks, and expect to sit through some confusing lectures. It's an interesting class, but you will have to put in loads of time to understand the material and to pass the class. Prepare to read and write- it's a lot for a survey!!

Heaman is very scattered and harried + her powerpoints are jarring to look at (blocks of text). She'd start a sentence and not finish it. This course is taught by Nerbas as well, and I'd recommend him over her for it. Overall, the workload and expectation of knowledge was HELL and not suited to a 200, survey/entry level course.

Heaman is passionate about her work, which translates to fascinating lectures. Lectures are chaotic but manageable. She is a fair but tough grader who offers excellent feedback for you to improve. The class isn't excessively demanding, but definitely more work than average for an A. Do not let bad reviews discourage you from taking her class.

Professor Heaman is one of my favourite profs at McGill. Yes, her lectures can be a bit scattered but that is only because she is so smart and has so much to say about each topic. She is a difficult grader but I liked having to work for a good grade. She is also incredibly helpful during office hours and seems to be a lovely person in general.

She's VERY disorganized. We were literally weeks behind schedule, but she neither made any official changes to the reading schedule, nor did she inform us of where we were in the texts, it was just a new surprise every lecture. Also, you must follow her interpretations verbatim, or else you'll be met with comments like “I don't get what you mean”.

Seems like a caring enough person but don't be fooled. Highly confused lectures make interesting subject matter soporific. Needs constant reminders to do basic things like uploading slide sets (too bad the slides don't help anyway). Seems like the only way to get past a B is to parrot what she says word for word. She won't understand anything else.
She is a very knowledgeable professor, but her teaching is utterly unacceptable: she reads her lecture notes sentence by sentence, making it incredibly boring and easy to zone out.

I take phil 480 with her and I know the lack of TA did not help but she is awful.

As of november we are a month behind schedule, her lectures are extremely disorganized and confusing, and she is barely available for office hours
We are mostly just left in broad confusion with instructions as clear as "write in perusall about the text"

Very, very nice professor who is more than willing (in fact extremely happy) to take questions. She is encouraging and helpful. She will not hold your hand, but she is fair. Content can be a little tricky at times, especially if there are some words you do not understand.

The course itself is pretty chill and she is ok in terms of delivering lectures and making relevant clarifications. The problem is her TAs are highly unprofessional, giving random grades and unsophisticated feedback to the paper. Be aware!!!

She obviously really cares about her subject, so lectures tend to be pretty interesting and really help clear up anything you don't understand in the weekly readings. Because of class size though, she doesn't grade any of the papers, so it's really a toss-up depending on what TA you get...

While readings can be tedious, Professor Carson's lectures are interesting and she is kind and accessible. She doesn't grade her own papers so grading becomes highly subjective. Just hope for a nice TA - this course is honestly just a TA Russian Roulette. Got hardly any feedback on the exam nor on any of my papers, which can be really annoying.

I LOVE prof. Carson And hands down Phil 200 is the best class I've taken for my first semester online lol Her lectures are clear and she leaves time for students to ask questions. I feel like I have learnt a lot about philosophy. If you are looking for a philosophy elective, take Phil 200 with Carson! I will definitely take more classes with her!

I didn't really like this class very much, but I felt I learned a lot about philosophy. There's a reading every week, and they are often very confusing but Prof. Carson helps clear them up in lectures. Fair warning: there is no clear grading system, and the TAs will give you very different grades and/or a lower grade than you deserve.

Dr. Kopley is a gem! Her lectures are amazing and her passion for the material is palpable. Lots of reading (a bit less than a book a week) but very rewarding. Very kind, and gives great guidance if you're struggling with an assignment.
An incredible lecturer. Did not care for all the material but found the classes fascinating nonetheless. Learned a lot. Has high standards for writing but very supportive and understanding

Love Doctor Kopley!! She was an amazing lecturer and she engaged the class really well. She is always available for a meeting (I highly recommend going to her office hours), and she really takes the time to give great personalized feedback. I would take all her courses if I could!

Dr. K is an amazing teacher
Not an easy grader, but she will give you feedback that helps in all of your future writing
Discussion heavy, but relaxed
So clearly caring about her students and very smart
Small classes and quick to help you always!!

Dr. Kopley is a really terrific teacher. Cares a lot about the material and is very knowledgeable. There was a lot of reading in this course - I made the mistake of taking two literature course in the same semester and that was a little much for me - but it's definitely doable. Was very quick to respond to any questions I had. I enjoyed class.

Definitely one of my favourite profs! She really cares about students and their wellbeing. Her readings are super interesting and classes are heavy on discussion. Professor Kopley knows a lot, but it's clear that she's always trying to learn more, which really encourages students to engage in the topics, do extra research, and share what they know!

Caring, smart. Get ready to read A LOT, but also to have interesting discussions that are open, fair, and thought provoking. A wonderful balance between lecture and discussion. She is tough, but expectations are set out clearly. I definitely recommend learning from Dr. K! She is the definition of the education one would expect to receive at McGill.

Kopley's keen on teaching Romantic Lit even though it's not her area of expertise. She brings in all sorts of other theoretical approaches like art criticism and focuses heavily on biographical understand (though she urges against using biographical readings). All in all, it was a very enjoyable class and McGill would be stupid to not keep her.

Kopley was an excellent prof. Extremely accommodating, smart as a whip, and is passionate about imparting deep knowledge on the subjects she teaches. You will need to do your readings, but you will leave the class feeling you've gained real, lasting knowledge. One of McGill's keepers.
Amazing teacher. If he was not a teacher he would be an amazing motivational speaker. Would take again in a heartbeat.

You will learn so much about life with him. Insanely approachable, hilarious, and knowledgable. Connects theory to example outstandingly. Sets the example of being vulnerable with his students, makes his class a safe space while trying to teach us to be the same. Leading by example first, this guy is the goat! Do not take 248 if you don't take him
He's really understanding and accommodating with the students.

Dr. Tabi is extremely knowledgeable & approachable. His lectures are inspiring and his assignments are creative. All throughout the semester, he invited guest speakers or told stories about his experiences. I really recommend him because he has so much worldly experience!
No textbook required. He uploads all the readings!
Overall so sweet and caring!

Dr. Tabi is one of few profs who genuinely loves what he does, and wants to share his knowledge with us. He is so kind, and he just wants us to succeed and learn how to help those around us. The readings are super interesting and applicable as well. His course is interesting and there is work involved, but if you try your hardest you'll do well!

I was initially skeptical, but after completing the semester I realized it wasn't necessary. She is an engaging, approachable professor and a fair grader. The course is well-structured, and the grading criteria are clearly outlined, making expectations easy to understand. Overall, I had a positive experience and would take her class again.
She is the pretty bad.

She just has no talent for teaching or researching. Did she even hire someone to help with her own papers? How did she obtain tenure and become a professor? It is so doubtful and literally discredits McGill University. Well, the fact that she never found any job in France tells everything about her competency.
She is the worst professor at McGill, incompetent and ignorant. Not sure how she even got the position.

She's nice and her lectures are interesting. But her grading makes no sense. You can do the best you ever did on a project and she will just give you an arbitrary grade with no explanation as to why you got that grade. Grading criteria is not followed at all.
No feedback lot of grade comes from group project which sucks final paper is super long and unclear lovely prof, super nice and upbeat. nice teacher but content is dry

She is very organized, clear and available. She focuses a lot on participation. She has a lot of criterias to grade presentations (around ten including enthusiasm and  engaging the crowd) and she did not necessarily communicated them at first so that came as a surprise for me. Very interesting class and great prof overall. Not a hard class.

Gives no feedback. Has criteria, but does not follow them. No help at all with the term project. Most of the class is group discussion (in smaller groups, not the whole class), so she doesn't really contribute.

Very disinterested in the students. As long as she’s getting her paychecks, she’s happy. She knows nothing about IT or IS, hence the TAs need to show her how to use excel. Be prepared for an intensive negative curve at the end. She will not bump you, even if you’re close. One of the worst teachers I’ve had at McGill so far! Avoid at all costs.
She is extremely nice and joyful! IS is a relatively easy class, the excel assignment was brutal though... I recommend her for this core course.

Prof. Shor is an amazing lecturer, extremely engaging and kept my attention every single class. He clearly has fun with the class, so expect some out of the box thoughts from him. The class discussions were great and his exams are straightforward, as long as you come to class and do the readings.
Great teacher, but his exams are super hard. I studied 2 weeks in advance each time, and I was close to failing each one.

An incredibly engaging lecturer, getting to take Prof. Shor's class is truly what reminded me of why I chose McGill. Every lecture feels like a professional TedTalk, all the while he'll still manage to learn your name in a class of 200 people, great stuff.

Shor will always be one of my favourite professors from both his classes. This class has a lot of reading that is necessary to do bc the entire 2 hr seminar is just discussion that is led by him or students. However, the readings and the topics are SO INTERESTING! The assignments aren't easy, but there is a lot of time between them.

LOVED Dr. Shor. Best prof by far at mcgill and i am not even a soci major. His class on deviance are engaging, entertaining and fun. His exams are fair and straight to the point (also very easy if you studied a minimum). Listen in class, remember the theories and you will do just fine! His class is worth taking.

Take this class if you are an arts student looking for an interesting subject with low commitment. (while I will specify you have to attend class because lectures are not recorded and slides don't cover everything) If you are like me however, and like few tests, take this class. 1 40% midterm and 60% final that are very passable if you go to class

An incredibly compelling lecturer. I appreciated how much he welcomed class discussion. There are a lot of readings but I found most of them to be very interesting and eye-opening. I will say that you really do have to review every single reading because he tests on all of them. Overall, it's not impossible to do well but don't expect an easy A

Prof shor was amazing! Super engaging and the class material was super interesting. However- not an easy A. NEED to go to every class as his slides do not reflect the class material. Also, Only graded on midterm and final (multiple choice) but the questions made you second guess yourself and were not at all straight forward IMO. Take as S/U

Professor Shor is THE BEST!! He made this class incredibly interesting. The subject matter alone is really stimulating, but his lectures really brought it to a whole other level. I highly suggest taking this class even if you're not a soci or psych student. The course was just two multiple choice exams based off lectures and readings.

I'm a 3rd yr bio major and this class had me constantly questioning whether I've been on the wrong path this whole time and soci is my true calling. The readings are genuinely interesting and thought-provoking. Professor Shor creates an open-minded atmosphere and presents perspectives that sometimes leave you questioning life as you know it. Best.

I didn't love the course content because it wasn't really my field of interest, but I really enjoyed his lectures! He got me interested in the content, and the readings were interesting! Essay portion of the final is a little evil, but fair! Three 3-4 page papers throughout, overall not bad!
Eran Tan gives great lectures and was very helpful in office hours. Grading was tough, but I imagine it depends on the TA.

Prof Tal is great and truly cares about what he teaches. Readings are tough, so I wouldn't recommend this course as an easy elective especially if you aren't particularly knowledgeable about science. Being able to pull examples is important for the papers and exams. Grading relies heavily on the TA, but the assignments themselves are doable.

Prof Tal is very good at summarising the readings, which is super important for an introductory phil class with extremely dense material. I truly hate writing, but had to take a phil class for my program. The essays were tough to write but we got good feedback and I feel like my writing has seriously improved bc of this class.

this class was fun, but i found it lacked philosophical background. as in like i found mos of the texts we read were really dense and a little irrelevant. but if you love science and are looking for an elective, i think this is really fun! i personally took it for my phil major, which is maybe why i wasn't as interested.

Professor Tal is a great lecturer, and it is obvious he genuinely cares about his subject. The readings for this class could be difficult, but he never failed to summarize and point out key ideas during lecture. As a first year arts student taking a more science-heavy course, I would highly recommend PHIL221. You will learn a lot.
essays were difficult to write and coursework was boring. The professor seemed like he cared.

Super nice and understands that this is many's first PHIL class, yet not condescending and respects his students intelligence, good lectures and fun discussions every class and conference, grading on papers is FAIR, you wont get an amazing score, but you can a good one if you pay attention, he also gives lots of extra credit from conferences
Professor is very good at giving lecture. He makes all the contents simple and interesting. However, the essays' grading is harsh. Not easy to get A or A-.

Very smart guy that makes some dense philosophy readings enjoyable and comprehensible. The essay feedback is awesome too, would definitely take another course with Tal even if it was a lot of writing!
Informative, can be boring, but also interesting. Fair and predictable midterm prompts.
He seems like a nice guy, though he doesn't mark anything throughout the semester and the very few times he does, he gives feedback with very minimal to no explanation at all.

I love him. Very sweet man. His lectures can be hard to stay focused on, but they're extremely well-structured. Would definitely take again <3 He was very considerate of his students during COVID and clearly cares. He gave extensions and was forgiving.

Eric is 100% a nice guy, but his lectures ramble on until you can hardly stay awake and are completely unstructured. Unclear grading schemes, impossible to take notes in class. I took "Teaching the Holocaust" because it was a topic that seemed genuinely interesting to me. By the end of this course, I was completely turned off of the subject.

I took his course titled "Teaching the Holocaust." I learned so much from this class! Just keep in mind that the class will not go in depth with the actual genocide; however, will discuss the main events as well as different methods for teaching the Holocaust. He is not a hard grader but not a super easy one as well. Also, participation matters!!

Everything falls on your papers and reading responses. Just listen to the lectures, try not to fall asleep. He rants a lot so you never really know what points to write down. Just focus on the readings and google things for generalized descriptions.
Fave prof

Pretty straight forward class. If you read the textbook, and attend lectures (catch everything he says) you will do well. His voice is a tad boring, but it is easily overcome. Make sure you write dates and the names he says in class, those are important. Don't listen to anyone who says he is a hard-marker, it's false - he's average.

Took an intro class to Judaism, Christianity and Islam and he was the prof for Judaism. Did not introduce the religion and just started using terms and timelines that were unfamiliar. Did not use a powerpoint, making the class unstructured and very hard to follow. Did not treat it as an introductory course. Needed baseline knowledge to do well.

The class I took with this professor is Teaching the Holocaust. Great teacher and great class!  There are many assignments, readings and work but they are very helpful in learning how to teach. I am glad I took it and I recommend it! :)

did not attend many lectures, except for fun, because he does know how to work a crowd :) memorize from the textbook - this includes all the terms, theories (with all the details), and key results (for example, which age group is most susceptible to X). quizzes represent the easiest questions so don't be misled.

Hilarious and entertaining. Each lecture had me engaged from start to end. Sadly, that didn't translate to knowing the test material. Almost everything you need to know is in the uber dense textbook. His questions aren't easy either, as they're hyper specific and designed to trip you up at times.

Good lecturer but exhausting to know what to study. Tough tests without flexible gradings. Too many details you have to learn on your own. The prof was nice but I mean a lot of concepts could be discussed in the on class but he didn't. Textbook matters more than you think. Just be prepared to memorize the entire textbook if you're heading an A.

Loved his lectures! People are right when they say it's all about the textbook but I found the way he taught so entertaining I always went to class. Lots of content on exams and questions ask you to apply the phenomena we've learned to examples instead of just memorizing definitions, but I think that's beneficial. Very kind when I approached him.
Great lectures, textbook is important

Prof Hehman was very interesting and i loved attending his lectures, they felt like podcasts and I would recommend for you to attend all of them, and just sit and listen, notes can be taken after. He was funny and liked to engage with his students. However, I would say it was tricky to know what to study for his exams.

GENUINELY THE BEST PROF I'VE EVER HAD!!!!!! Technically you're fine if you just read the textbook and memorize that, but his lectures are so engaging and fun to listen to you're probably gonna go to them anyway!!
Good teacher but just study the textbook
he was such a king but his tests were difficult. however, social psyc in general is a lot of memorization so you can't really avoid that. his quizzes were super easy though.

Funny lecturer, but I do agree that the exams were not always 100% reflective of all the content covered. Had very intricate questions, like you had to remember a specific sentence from a specific paragraph of the textbook. I recommend staying on top of textbook readings & podcasts as often as possible. Quizzes/extra cred help boost marks too!

Prof. Lewis was amazing! Abstract content was made accessible and engaging, and he's genuinely funny. Expectations and grading are fair, and he consistently checked in with us to ensure we felt prepared. The slides are posted, but lectures are worth attending. I'd happily take another course with him! One of the best profs at McGill hands down.

Lectures are super boring but you don't have to go, despite them not being recorded. Super easy online quizzes make up 50% of the grade. the rest is 2 papers. Very chill guy but will put you to sleep, very quiet lecturer but knows his stuff and is quite funny if ur actually listening.
easy quizzes and interesting lectures.

Prof. Lewis' presocratics class is the coolest I've ever taken, he's an amazing prof and so funny. YOU NEED TO TAKE THIS CLASS, i would recommend to anyone. Background in philosophy is not really needed.
One of McGills best profs

Prof. Lewis is so down to earth and his lectures are HILARIOUS-- I looked forward to them wondering what would go down. He did such an incredible job of teaching on philosophers whom we legit have NO TEXTS FROM! I'm convinced that he's a genius . . . he drops pieces of his life story here and there and everyone is left wanting to know more.

hilarious!!!! the content of this class is tough, but he tries to make it as accessible as possible. such a great lecturer and i swear i laugh my ass off every class. he's so down to earth, but is definitely a secret genius. 
take his class!

Such a wonderful professor and person. Cares deeply about his subject and his students' well-being. Really dynamic and funny, too. But the lectures get very abstract (expectedly), so if that's not your cup of tea, you probably will find yourself zoning out.

353 is a super exciting class, which Lewis teaches excellently. Lewis uses funny but relevant examples to help grasp concepts and successfully makes abstract/theoretical pre-Socratic theories more digestible. He makes himself accessible outside of lectures to discuss assignments and answer questions. He also has unique stories.

Really loved professor Lewis. He is such a sweet and caring person! Very easy grader. Studying for the quizzes to get a full mark is effortless. My favourite class this semester. The only problem is that he assigns a lot of readings, and the instructions on when/what readings should be done is unclear.
I enjoy his class

McCalla is great at teaching, he really cares about the students, and you get lots of demos which makes an otherwise pretty bland class fun! Preparing for tests is a bit difficult - the only practice you get is some textbook questions (no practice tests) and the tests are out of 20. He's really sweet and receptive to feedback from students :)

great prof, very fair exam, make sure to look into and review the note thoroughly for the exams, and the lab part includes python but the TAs and the prof respond to questions through email

especially the prof, he responds to emails fast and has great amount of details.
Entertaining lectures, quite a funny guy! Definatly knows his stuff
He's an excellent lecturer who easily engages the class and makes his lectures, which are fairly memorization heavy by necessity of the topic, actually interesting. Plus he's hilarious

He is not very structured in the way he explains things in the lectures and the exam questions for his section were very specific so make sure you remember every little detail. In general he is a good teacher, explains well and you can always ask him to reexplain which is nice.

I don't understand why his reviews are very mixed. To me, Erik Cook came off as this very funny and enthusiastic neuroscientist. His lectures were not dull and he made sure to try to keep people entertained as his material was mostly anatomy, pathways, and memorization. If a question's answer is between his answer or the textbook's, trust his.

He's a good teacher, but sometimes his lectures are a bit all around the place. He doesn't like being asked questions that differ slightly from what he's teaching in this course. He will sometimes go quickly over stuff that's very important because he's running out of time, which can be a problem. Overall he's okay.

He comes off as pretentious and seems to lowkey have a vendetta against "pre-med" students. I understand his pain, but not everyone in PHGY 209 are planning to go to medical school. Most are taking 209 and 210 just because they are part of the major requirements... I certainly wouldn't take these courses for fun!
Really bad at explaining concepts, really pretentious. Thinks hes funny. His slides are really unclear and his exam questions were stupid and hard.
Great lectures. Really interesting material as well

Honestly, he's not THAT bad. Just rewatch his lectures and make additional notes to what you've already while in class. You SHOULD do well. The department gave him too much material to cover in too short of a time so don't blame him. He still did a decent job.

Super nice and fun professor, however there is a lot of material with his part of the class and the exam questions on them are quite precise as well. So he may not be the easiest, but I definitely enjoyed having him as a professor.

Professor is kind and knowledgeable, but the course is skewed. No slides, no recordings, and heavy weekly readings. TA Thu is, without exaggeration, one of the harshest and most unpleasant TAs I have encountered at McGill. The midterm was long, worth 40 percent, and the promised weekly ID terms were only given a week before, which felt unfair
The professor is good and lectures are very interesting, but the singular midterm is impossible to finish on time, even if you're prepared.

The material is really interesting, but he uses convoluted language and refuses to record a lecture and never replies to emails. I had to miss class because of something out of my control and he never bothered answering my email asking for a recording. If you miss class, you have no chance to make up for it.

I loved his class. I did horribly on the midterm, class average B-, but the final was manageable, and you were able to prepare effectively. He gets too much hate, but if you show up to class, write everything he says (easier said than done), and go to the conferences, you'll be fine. Loved the debates in conferences. Made me love my major again.

Clearly he is passionate and very knowledgeable but that is the only positive thing about this class. He does not set up his students for success and tests are reliant on the memorization of an unreasonably high number of terms. The grading criteria for this class was extremely unclear, harsh, and TAs were unhelpful. Would not recommend.
He is the most unhelpful professor at McGill. He never replies to emails and never accommodates students' needs. Also watch out for SAs!

You can tell he cares deeply about his research but that's about it. Lectures are dry, grading is extremely harsh (midterm avg was 60s) and criteria unclear, TAs of little assistance, midterm/test based on memorization and recitation, you will buy three books (one is his) yet barely have the need to utilize them. Best of all? No tech in class.

Professor Kuhonta is a good lecturer but that is the only positive aspect of his courses. Exams were designed to be difficult with extremely harsh grading criteria. They seemed to be aimed at testing students' ability to memorise exact terms by heart rather than their understanding of the material and wording of questions was purposely ambiguous.

RUN! TAs are not given grading rubrics until after the test, prof vague about what you will be tested on, and you are not graded on your understanding of the textes but on linguistique nuances. This prof does not give you the tools to succeed and/of to work for that effect. Don't be fooled by the good reviews -he's in charge of the internships dpt.
Very interesting class, Prof always up for questions, and format/content for exams very well clarified. Would definitely recommend this class.

A truly phenomenal professor who cares deeply about her work and students' success. She is easy to reach, and even encourages students to stop by her office to chat about theatre. Her lectures are passionate and insightful, but might be more challenging for someone with little to no theatre background, though she provides entry points.

Prof Hurley is really caring, by far the most approachable professor I've had. She's really passionate about the material, and her assignments are fair. Definitely take a class with her if you can, but maybe not ENGL313 - the readings weren't very engaging, and the content was so niche it didn't seem applicable to anything outside the classroom.
Very nice professor. The midterm was really hard though.

Professor Hurley is a very interesting and cool woman and the structure of the class made it very manageable to perform well without much preparation or reading. Overall a good course to take if you don't want a heavy course load and are interested in the topic, but I would steer clear if you aren't at least somewhat interested in plays or theatre.

Professor Hurley is a great professor - accessible outside class, cares about her students and passionate about the material. Lectures are really slow-paced, so you can easily skip and catch up from lecture slides. Not much reading at all and the assignments are fair. Would definitely recommend taking a class with her!

Erin is super sweet and her lectures are interesting, and she does truly care about her students. With that said, the grading is very inconsistent with little feedback. Also, the textbook is super expensive and it was only used about 4 times throughout the semester... But, if you enjoy theatre, I highly recommend as it is an interesting course.

The class was disorganized and took up to or more than a month to receive grades for assignments and midterms. Professor Hurley graded harder than a 200-level theatre class with unclear expectations. As someone who has no experience in theatre, this class has discouraged me from taking another. I do not recommend this class or professor.

The class felt so disorganized. Going into assignments, I feel like the expectations are really unclear for the particular nature of her grading. I agree with her other reviews, she needs to make her exams shorter for the time allotted. As well, there really isn't a lot of room to redeem yourself if you do poorly on an assignment.
She doesn't know how to make an assignment structure and her exams are way too long.
Super nice and caring.

A very harsh grader unlike other econ courses at mcgill but she is so willing to help out outside of class. If you're looking for some advice and just to chat she is always willing to help you out which is very different than most econ profs at mcgill!
Absolutely brilliant!
Avoid. Not good. Excessive work. No teaching during class. Unfair grading.

Avoid at ALL costs. She thinks really highly of herself and comes off as condescending. Someone needs to tell her that being a tough grader doesn't make her a good professor. Did not learn anything of substance from her.
She is a great prof! You can learn a lot from her. Okay, there are a lot of readings but she highlights important parts in class. She is very professional and at the same time cute.

Great if genuinely interested in topic and your GPA can take a hit. Doing the work will get you a B, but to get A/A- you must LEARN it - she expects more than regurgitation. 5+ students dropped the course  due to tough grading and not knowing how to improve. Be wary if not an econ major.  Go to office hours for papers. Education-wise  fantastic.

Terrible course. Far too much work (8000 word journal, 3 essays, midterm, final, more than  reading I have ever seen in an Econ class). Strumpf doesn't seem able to answer any questions that diverge even slightly beyond the course material, and often struggles with the material itself.

COMPLETELY disagree with the previous comment. This was by far my favorite econ class at McGill and Professor Strumpf was one of my favorite profs. The assignments were short and not too demanding. There was a lot of reading but she highlights the important details in class.

She is dreadful. Avoid at all costs. Thinks very highly of herself, but really comes off as not very intelligent. Unwilling to accept diverging views. Marks unreasonably stringently. Way too much work (2 midterms, 5 papers, final exam, most reading I've ever had in an econ course by far).

Very approachable, very kind teacher. The slides are a great summary of what she says in class. Make sure to focus on policy issues because her exams are all about that and they aren't easy. If you want to learn about insurance and health care, this class is very useful, but you will need to work hard

Professor Haruvy is very caring and always available to answer your questions. He explains the material clearly and makes sure we truly understand how to apply the concepts before quizzes. Although the course involves a lot of teamwork, we are always given enough time to complete the tasks, so it never feels overwhelming. I would take it again!

Professor Haruvy is very accessible outside of class, willing to give insightful career advice, and cares about his students. There are ways to succeed in the learning outcomes even if your group wasn't the highest placing in the simulation. The learning guides for quizzes are very clearly laid out. Overall, I enjoyed the class and its structure!

good teacher, lectures are interesting but sometimes he goes a bit too far in his explanation and diverge from the actual subject. the material is not that hard you just need to be regular and learn it efficiently, if you participate in class and are present in class he will do his best to curve your grade. gives good feedback.

The quizzes are very straightforward, so if you study and put the work you're guaranteed good grades on those. He is a tough grader on assignments but you can ask him for help and he ll guide you. He is very understanding and very available outside of class. He's also quite funny sometimes. You can tell he wants every student to succeed

Gives insanely detailed feedback and treats projects like real businesses. 


students hate him cuz

1. grades are tough - kids expect 100% for effort, but B+/A- is fair for people with no business knowledge. You are able to improve to an A with feedback
2. doesnt teach off slides - slides are a bunch of boring definitions. read through it yourself
His class may be difficult but does prepare you for the real world. If you need help not only is he willing to meet with you but encourages you to meet with him.

He brings strong industry experience to the lectures, which makes the class very engaging. I found his feedback on our final project to be detailed and genuinely useful. A great choice if you want to learn practical marketing skills.

There's definitely a fair amount of memorization in this class which can be hard, but Mr. Haruvy made the lectures engaging and was always available to help students. For the project, we could pick our teams and product, which made the work more motivating.The slides are also clear but you must be prepared to put in the work in order to succeed.

This guy's class was nothing more than a nightmare. The amount of work required to even get a ChatGPT, randomly generated 75 will make you sad. Mr. Ernan seemed like kinda of a nice guy but he's sometimes... unhinged. Overall, I wouldn't recommend this class/professor. You will work and you will get depressed. The final exam was insane too.
Very nice person - but a very bad lecturer! He didn't make it through the slides most classes, and the way he graded was super inconsistent and confusing.
Very nice guy !
Nice teacher, good lectures

Professor Bolongaro is extremely passionate about Italian Cinema, which definitely comes across in his lectures. It's mandatory to watch the films each week (and there are a lot of them) so it can be time-consuming, but the readings are pretty much optional (we never talked about them in class). He's a generous grader, too. I'd recommend!

The class was interesting, and he is definitely very knowledgeable, which helped a lot. There's a lot of preparation that goes into the course, like readings and viewing films, but imo it was manageable. If you show up to class and listen to his lectures, the assignments are not bad; he practically gives you a guide to answer them in class.
Bit of a tough grader but cool class

Generally pleasant, approachable man and decent lecturer. That being said, very demanding on the readings/viewings, only to be resolutely convinced of a singular (his own) interpretation, which can come across demeaning. Not an easy grader, but does give fair feedback to justify this. Class is well organized and insightful overall.
Very interesting and engaging lecturer, just has a way of speaking that grabs your attention and makes you want to listen. I did not find he was condescending like some other replies have said

I had a lecture with him and it felt like a seminar because of how much space he was leaving for questions and participation - which was amazing. Interesting film selection, easy grader and genuinely open and curious person. The quizzes on the film are super easy (yet tricky at times) and you have options for assignments. I loved that class!

Prof. Bolongaro is very tough but fair, and he gives really good lectures. HOWEVER, do not take this class as an elective. This is way too in depth for someone who is not very passionate about cinema and isn't particularly interested in Italy (it's a fine country, but I'm not particularly interested in it). DO NOT TAKE IF YOU DONT LOVE CINEMA

Professor Bolongaro was nowhere near as demanding as I expected. He lectured in class very clearly about the material that he will ask for evaluation, so clearly in fact that I did none of the readings and saw none of the films yet I got an A. If you show up in class and take good notes, you're golden. Great lecturer as well!

Very passionate lecturer. We once spent an entire class analyzing the first two paragraphs of a 250 page book. That being said, he is a tough grader and unnecessarily harsh with criticism. Do the readings, watch the movies, and go to class ready to discuss.

Never had a professor with as much passion as him. If you're not going to work, you shouldn't take the class. He expects you to read your novels or watch movies, which is normal for a class like this. People who are hating went through the semester without doing one or the other. He is a hard grader though, but reasonable.

What a pleasure to attend this class!  The material was explained fabulously in class, the discussions were challenging and interesting, and there was always a chuckle to be had.  Nothing better than a prof who knows his area inside and out, is sensitive to the seriousness of the issues at play, and can still have a dry laugh in the face of it all.
Fantastic teacher. One of those people you wish were your neighbour so you could learn from them everyday beyond university. Clear + passionate. One of my favourite classes!

Very nice person. Very student-friendly. Summary is great for that class. Essay is theoretical but he gives a lot of time to prepare. Classes are a bit dull but he has a great sense of humour! Where is he situated on the political spectrum? REAL DEVIL'S ADVOCATE... but I still think he is an anarchist!
Accessible, willing to help, good sense of humor and left sided thought. Fair grader.
Classes were alright, but final exam was a killer.
A slice of alright.
Frighteningly articulate.
An excellent prof.  Clear lectures, very organized.  Nice person.

Really great professor with clear grading criteria. She doesn't try to trick you and gives you everything you need to succeed. Only slight pitfall is her unpredictable reactions when you answer a question (she'll either respond normally or kind of cut you off to tell you that you are wrong). Other than that I loved her class!
only got a bad grade because of the TA, also studied last minute, but love Dr. M!!

By far my favourite teacher and class so far. She was so passionate and knowledgable, I was SO excited to go to her lectures every week, the material is insanely interesting and the teacher is so funny and good at teaching, it was actually impressive! I have another class with her next semester and I can't wait, she truly is the best!
Great teacher and class overall — definitely recommended! Show up to class!!!!
Amazing prof. w/ clear, engaging lectures. Clear assignments. You must attend!!!! BUT YOU WILL NOT BE BORED. Really recommend.

Definitely my favorite prof in McGill, I would listen to her talk about anything. Her lectures are super clear, super interesting, and the grading scale is really fair (pretty easy exams if you listen in class and study, and participation points are easy to get). Absolutely love her and would strongly recommend to take (at least) a class with her.

DR. EM is 100% my favourite professor. I had ARTH360 with her last semester and am now taking her ARTH353 (Totalitarian Art) class and I've loved both of them! She is so engaging and her classes are the only ones that I feel go by too quickly. She is kind, funny, and super approachable. There are also fun extra credit opportunities and field trips!

Amazing professor. Super fun, kind, professional, and knowledgeable. We had fun and practical assignments, lots to write but it is a good way to improve your art history skills. Although the grading rubric is not clear. Overall, as long as you put effort, you will get a good grade.

Took this class after taking ARTH 339 with her last year. She has the best TAs and is very approachable. I barely went to class but managed to fulfil the participation criteria during office hours and by participating whenever I was in class. Her classes make the overall experience of studying art history interesting and enjoyable.

Dr. EM is a great educator, highly passionate and knowledgeable about architecture. You don't have to go to class or attend the lectures to do well if you know how to write a good art history paper as the assignments don't have much to do with the course content. Some lectures can be a bit boring and could use more engaging course content.

This course is the hardest course I have ever seen in my life. Even Grad students don't take it. As an undergrad I highly advise you to avoid it. The material is insanely hard and the homeworks are 9 LONG problems long. Take any other Tech Comp, I regret taking this course thinking it was an easy A (I might fail).

Really great prof to take Fluids 2 with. He posts a TON of past exams, while also giving weekly homework, both of which give a VERY good idea of what exams will look like. Lectures are a bit dull, but given the shear magnitude of other resources provided, this really isn't a problem. Highly recommend.

He teaches well, gives his lecture notes out which covers everything you need to know about the course so you don't have to copy them during lecture. The homework can be complicated but very much reflect the complexity of the exams. If you need extra practice before the midterms and finals he also gives out past papers.

His lectures are useless as they only cover the mere basics and the homework difficulty is nothing compared to the midterms. His final exam was brutal compared to old ones. He somehow believes that doing an exam online and having more resources is an advantage and hence gives us impossible exams. Completely inconsiderate, avoid him.

I am aware it is his first time to teach this class online, and it is apparent, the quality of his lectures has suffered. Another point, I would assume, Professor Timofeev does not trust his students and therefore he made his midterms difficult such that if the students worked together, they would not have time to compare results, exams are HARD

One of the best profs i had in mech eng, I really recommend taking MECH 430 with him! He posts his own notes and all past exams. His exams are fair and never too challenging. The resources for this class are amazing. Overall, this is not an intense class, very doable and if you put the necessary effort you will get at least 80% in the midterms.

Evgeny is one the best professors I've ever had in my life. He is very clear, and posts all of his notes online, along with all past midterms, finals, and respective solutions. He provides detailed updates and tips with his Fluids Newsletters, and tries to maximize your grade with bonuses through the semester. I'd definitely take him again.

Good class, his lectures are right from the textbook so you could just read that. The outline says exactly what chapters are covered. Very detailed feedback after midterms. Really cares about his students and fair exams.
Solid professor, assignments are where you do most of the learning (you're given ample time to do them). Only thing is his lectures can be pretty dry.

Do well in the midterms as the finals are usually incredibly hard (he always has to omit a question in marking or curve). He is  among the most caring professors at the Mech Eng department. I failed two out of three midterms. He really helped in my understanding of the course and ensured that my effort is rewarded. Pro tip: DO ALL PAST EXAMS!

One of my favorite professors. The class content is extremely interesting and is a good mix between theory and empirical work. Yes the class is more difficult than many other ECON classes since it requires more math but the problem sets are very similar to the exams and to be fair it is a 400 level class. I would love to have again as a prof.
Professor Lange knows his material, but the grading is extremely strict and often unpredictable. It's very common to feel confident after an exam and still receive a much lower grade than expected.

*He only replaced my other prof, who was on maternity leave - he couldn't grade us on anything* He likes to cold call, but it's apparent that he's very into what he's teaching. Seems knowledgeable, and he takes the time to explain difficult concepts. During my final, I got a question right because I remembered him explaining it super well in class.
Very good lectures, passionate and engaging.

He lives to destroy GPAs. There's no cohesion in his lectures. Introduces Cal III concepts when the course requirement is Cal I. I loved economics until taking his course. It made me question my career path. I devoted easily 2.5x more study hours to his course, and it was by far the worst grade I received in my undergrad.

I took fabian's class last year and i absolutely hated it. looking back now his class was one of the best things I could have taken in my first year. prepares you very well and he is  fair with grading and exams. you just have to put in the work and it may be a bit difficult for an intro class but it will set you up so well for other econ classes

Really, really enjoyed my 230 D1/D2 with Prof. Lange last year. He likes to cold call, but encourages volunteers and participant; if you accidentally say something wrong, he is more than willing to help guide you to the right answer. Tests were hard but if you studied properly, you will do well (he also always curves). Can't recommend him enough.

Passionate teacher. Highly suggest to have taken a calc class (at least have minimal knowledge about differentiation). 1st semester harder than 2nd semester. Asks questions if you have any / come to office hours! Exams can be hard, expect big curves (2nd semester final curved by roughly 30%). Econ230 ESA on YouTube for additional resources.

Fabian's reviews are totally unfair. The class itself is hard but he is a great professor. He keeps the class engaged and explains concepts very clearly. The homework is pretty hard but his exams are super fair if you take notes and pay attention in class. If you have him you're in luck and this is coming from someone who got a D in 208.

Great person and lecturer. He really likes anyone who asks questions, and his OH portray this. Is very happy to help. The grading scheme is pretty solid and doesn't change but the exams are constantly curved probably in relation with class performance - including a historical curve on the final as the format had to change because of the TA strike.

Gelinas' contract class was just based on vibes - he would meander sometimes and then pop off about consideration at others. Loves class participation and asking thought provoking questions. Exam was extremely fair but he is a vague grader - would recommend seeing him for feedback afterwards. If in doubt, go to the  McCamus textbook for clarity.

Fair with the assignments he gives. Tends to be lecture heavy with a lot of readings. He can also go on a tangent and ask confusing rhetorical questions. His frequent back and forth also confuses many about the main differences between Common and Civil! Caring and approachable prof overall, but confusing when contract law is already confusing.

Apparently his reason for not recording the lectures was because he didn't have that advantage, which was mean boomer energy. Many of the other reviews are spot on - super boring lecturer who uses all the time given every class. I taught myself what little I did learn. Always unclear where you should be in the reading list because he's disorganized

Professor Gélinas' class was the highlight of my 1L year. I looked forward to his classes. He bends over backward to help students learn and he genuinely wants us to be good lawyers. If every professor were like him, McGill Law would be a much better place. Don't miss an opportunity to take his class. You'll be glad you did.

Gelinas is clearly smart but I found him very disorganized - we were constantly behind and it was never clear what readings we were going to cover in class. Also he speaks in a monotone voice so it's never clear what is important and it's very boring. Taught myself the class (which luckily was possible to do).
Favourite prof in 1L even in an otherwise boring class

Had the good ol' G-Man for K1. Overall he's a good lecturer who was a powerpoint for every topic and can discuss singular topics at length even without his visual support. My suggestion, however, is to take your own notes instead of copypasting his PPs and refer yourselves to Halsbury's for more concise teachings. Pro: very sharp dresser!

He is an expert at what he teaches, but not an expert at teaching. He doesn't simplify notions or link them together. Every topic is taught in a silo, making it hard to grasp the bigger picture. I didn't want to rely on past years' summaries, but I kind of had to at some point. I think people who did this from the start followed better.
A valuable asset to the faculty. He's just perfect on so many levels. Highly recommend.

Even though there were way too many readings (pretty much impossible to actually get them done) he synthesized them pretty well and was by far the most approachable and helpful prof in 1L. He can ramble at times and repeat himself, but his lectures were always stimulating. Also, he's really attractive.
avoid if possible !! rude for no reason. if you care about your grades/GPA do not take her. Her feedback makes no sense

Her grading is subjective, she takes out points for irrelevant things. She makes rude and shocked faces during the presentations? We took her corrections into account and still didn't get a grade above 65. Avoid this professor for the sake of your GPA.

Very condescending especially during presentations, would make faces during presentations (evil faces). You never know exactly what she wants and she is super nit-picky over unimportant aspects of the presentation. I do not recommend. Most of the grade is based on subjective stuff that u cant really prepare for.

Poor prof.. scribbled random notes on written reports and presentations and assigned a random grade between 70-78 regardless of how well you hit the criteria. Only thing that saved my grade was the final as it wasn't marked by her alone.
Avoid at all costs. Doesn't give any grades during the whole semester and doesn't explain to you exactly what mistakes you did so you can improve.
Took one class with her and instantly dropped. Very rude.
worst prof i've had at mgcgill

Never grade anything from the start until the finish of the semester. Often come to class late and cancel the class. She didn't give a clear instruction for the assignment, like I don't know what she wants.
The worst professor I ever met. Please don't take her class.

teaches a communication class but sucks at communicating. Whole class has received ZERO grades since the beginning of the semester with her. No grades, nothing. silence.
