He mumbled to himself at times and spoke in a somewhat disorganized way. I studied hard for the final because I did poorly on the midterm and still only received a c+ and I studied very hard for his final.

Great prof. Chill guy--very helpful and accessible. Takes the time to explain things; possibly a longer time sometimes, but I didn't particularly have trouble following along. Really enjoyed the course.
Sometimes his explanations are a little convoluted, probably because engilsh is not his first language. However he is a great guy and the course was extremely interesting.

Relatively interesting class with this professor and Fussman. Guichard's part was interesting, but he made it very difficult to follow simple concepts and didn't seem to have an organized lesson plan. Very accessible and ready to help whenever you have a question though! (Similar for BIOL 434)

Very good lectures, extremely knowledgeable in both theoretical and practical aspects of international law, especially human rights and international criminal law. Rewards essays with a central argument flowing through it. Not a harsh marker as long as you do your research
Awesome!
This was my favourite class in first year hands down, extremely interactive, come prepared!

This was a super interesting course, but quite challenging. The fact that it was the first year the prof taught it didn't help, I think it will improve. Yes, there was lots of materials but a lot of it was super interesting. The assignments were ok and there was pretty extensive feedback after the first one. Not just black letter law, for sure.

worst professor I have had; incoherent, doesn't prepare; lots to read but material is mostly blogs and newspapers rather than jurisprudence or doctrine (umm?). he gives no direction for assignments and his feedback does not match the grades he gives at all. Big wild card, so avoid his classes.
Professor Megret was a terrific instructor.  He's enthusiastic and incredibly knowledgeable.  Definitely recommend his courses.

Interesting subject matter. Knowledgeable prof on the subject. Comprehensive but reasonable readings. Good exercises and evaluations were not too taxing, although he's not as easy a marker as I had heard!
Took ICL in 2009, great seminar ,really gives you an overview of the topic. Almost too much covered.
I really like this class. Great use of technology, good mix of the practical and the theoretical.
Very interesting course. There is a lot of jurisprudence to read. A tip for the exam : Make sure your answer is cleary structured.
The amount of memorization in this class is simply unrealistic. The slides are poorly organized and the directions for evaluatuions are misleading.
Frieda's class will be demanding but at the end you will be grateful for all the knowledge you'll gain, more than what you get from most classes.

Frieda will make you discover plants like never before. The slides are packed images and names to remember. It is a memorization heavy class without a doubt, but out of all the memorization, the family specific traits or recognizing the species of all your local trees, you will surprise yourself by how much of it you will retain. Solid class.
Alot of information is presented fast. Powerpoints are dense and sometimes confusing. She's nice and very passionate about plants.
PLNT 358 was one of the most difficult classes I've taken at McGill. To say it involves a lot of memorization would be an understatement. It has changed the way I look at plants, however.

This was a challenging class, but Frieda made it interesting. She made an effort to make class fun by interspersing lots of fun facts. She was also very pleasant and willing to help you, and made resources available for studying. Her expectations were high, but were fair and were explained well. She wanted students to succeed.
Awesome prof, is really sweet and really takes time to answer questions. His explanations are very clear.

I took this class with not much of a science background and I found that he explained everything in terms that I understood. He uploads power points with audio to go through before class, which take about an hour to do. Class time normally is very similar to the pp though. Assignments have some tricky questions but he clarifies them if you ask.

I took a course with him about environment. His behaviour seems very friendly in person. However, he grades UNFAIRLY. I would avoid taking any course with him again (otherwise I would go through so much work for very little grade.)

This prof sucks bad. Seriously he is the WORST PROF I EVER HAD IN UNIVERSITY. I can't believe they let him teach. He doesn't post solutions to homework, his TA grades unfairly, he doesn't know how to give a good lecture. AVOID THIS PROF IF YOU WANT A GOOD LIFE
No Comments

I cannot stand this professor. I've had him twice. I fall asleep almost every time he teaches.

Raghavan is a nice guy but you can tell he's not interested in the students at all. His course organization is non-existent and he is unclear. Its not a difficult class, but mainly because all the answers are online and you learn by copying and figuring it out afterwards
He's SO nice, always in his office to help you out. I feel that in heat transfer, you'll probably feel like you should have learnt more in fluid mechanics though.
The Best Prof I have ever had !! more than a teacher... a father figure to me :)
Great teacher, nice, clear, with a great indian accent! Raghavan , u da man

Professor Frieden is an excellent professor who cares about his students and explains concepts in a clear manner. He is also accessible outside of class. I would highly recommend taking him for statistics. The course has recently shifted to include Python. The midterm is challenging, but the final is easier.

Gabriel Frieden is excellent at explaining the material in a very clear way, and its very clear he loves to teach. He does tend to make mistakes in lectures at times, but he corrects himself. Overall, he teaches an extremely challenging course but he makes it easier with examples, clear explanations and relatively forgiving grading

This is one of the most challenging core courses. Frieden is a clear teacher, and if you do all the practice questions multiple times and understand the course material (not memorize it), you can succeed. It's not a course for the faint-hearted.
Skip class and review the notes instead

Might seem shy, but very approachable during office hours! Slides (+ excel graphs/tables) are detailed and contain all necessary info for exams. If you have time, do ALL the practice problems on the list, not just the highly recommended. Review assignments before the exams. Exams are easy/fair if you did the practice and kept up with the material.
gabriel is a g

Professor Frieden was super kind and helpful throughout the semester. He gives clear explanations in class and is very accessible outside of class by email, office hours and class forum. His practice questions were very representative of the midterm and final exams' level. As long as you do the exercises, you'll be fine!

Professor Frieden is a solid lecturer. He explains concepts clearly, goes at a decent pace, walks through exercises step by step (showing how to approach various problems, which is very helpful for exams), and covers many key questions during review sessions. Just redo the assignments and practice exams many times and it will be an easy A.

Frieden is great! Very chill and nice guy. Imo goes a bit slow at times so lectures are sometimes boring. Double-sided A4 crib sheet on final and midterm makes the exams feel practically open-book. Not hard to do well as long as you do the assignments yourself and do the practice exams. The assessments are very similar to lectures.
Very chill prof with excellent powerpoints. He is phenominal at explaining the course material.
Probably the most inconsistent lectures I have ever seen.
Love him! If someone were to describe the perfect prof, and someone else would describe Dr. Venne, the lists would match perfectly.
Super thoughtful professor, truly loved taking anat 214 and 314 with him. He actually cares about his students and what they think.

Dr. Venne is an amazing teacher - he is super accessible, caring, and always enthusiastic. ANAT514 is a new course and I highly recommend it, it was probably the best course I took at McGill. If you have the chance to take it, do not hesitate! You will have an amazing time.

I had Dr. Venne for anat 214 and anat314. He is really passionate and clear in terms of his explanations of anatomical concepts even though the materials can be overwhelming in the first place. He has some spelling issues and be careful when it comes to lab/concept exams. Try to review everything after each week (anat314 has more stuffs to know)

The most caring professor I had at McGill. A quote from his most recent announcement for ANAT 214: "The only thing we care about is your success and mental health! So help us help you by providing us feedback to make this possible and to ensure we keep you engaged and motivated in this course.". I've never heard any other professor say this.

Venne is literally the best prof in the entire science department. He is inspired and connects very deeply with both the material and the students. His class is dense but if you attend lecture, go to labs and use the course pack to study you'll be more than fine! He's such a great prof, it never feels like work- you just end up absorbing it !
My favorite prof at McGill! Love his lectures even though they are at 8:30 up the mountain and not recorded... I think that says enough!
Best professor ever, super nice and cute, amazing prof, makes me actually want to go to 8:35am lectures and morning labs!! He's also kind of funny and quirky, very young so super relatable!

My favorite professor at McGill. Unbelievably wholesome, and very knowledgeable of the topic. He was my professor for ANAT 214 and 314. His questions are fair, and do test your knowledge of the material. Very accessible for students who need help. Furthermore, he has a good sense of humor.

The course content was interesting, and i feel like the tests were good and fair. the class is just very lecture heavy and was very early in the morning so it was hard to go to class but she took attendance

Tends to politicize asian culture in the context of her western ideologies. Several of her TAs are spectacularly unprofessional

She will defend her TA when they grade you via their personal politics, which often conflict with the subject matter/broader realities of Chinese culture. 

She's reflective that this is not the East dept it once was.
One of the most caring, genuine professors I've met at McGill. Have taken multiple classes with Professor Gvili, and all of them have been great experiences!

Professor Gvili was really caring and understanding. She wasn't a tough grader and made the grading criteria clear from the start. There were a lot of readings, which made it hard to keep up, and early class times made it tough to focus, but her lectures were genuinely interesting and worth attending.

Be ready to read and be alert during class, its a history class so its quite normal. You have one in-class test which is an easy A and two takes (one midterm and one final) home which are movie reviews. Just know that they aren't recorded so if ever you miss, ask for notes.

Prof. Gvili is a great professor and is quite accessible out of class.
However, as a Chinese I find the mythology in her class was dramatically different from the stories in my childhood and I had to memorize the new... Chinese... mythology... I guess that is something to be discussed academically...

Amazing class. I'm not a big lit fan, but the readings are interesting (no textbook). Engaging, open-minded and fun discussions. Grades super fairly and is really caring and accommodating outside of class. She keeps the class creative and material fresh. 100% recommend if you're passionate about feminism and history.

As of now my favorite professor at McGill, the material and her lectures are interesting, and she really goes easy on you with the exams, which are, somewhat strangely, pretty fun to do. The movies you have to watch are mostly really interesting and getting an A was a breeze. If you have the opportunity, take her classes and enjoy the ride.

Professor Gvili is such a strong lecturer and is so passionate about the subject that her classes are so engaging! She is accessible, but there is a lot of reading and movies during the semester's second half. I didn't do all of them and still got an A, so you can definitely skim some. Recommend this class and prof!

I found the classes to be very dense in material, but clearly organized and easy to follow. The 3 assignments were interesting and not too difficult. I was interested in class, which made it easier to attend at 8:30. She's also very helpful when she answers questions over email.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS AS AN ARTS STUDENT...The guy knows his stuff and is like a mini celebrity in the geology world, but the class covers so much stuff that you are not prepared for based off the course description. Be ready to have to learn chem, bio, history and geology. Tests cover very niche topics that were on one slide in one lesson.

Overall great professor who he cares about his student success. However, his 2 tests were very hard, very short (half multiple choice). Assignments on the other hand are very easy to get a good grade in and will boost grade. Pop quizzes are not what you think it's open book on kahoot! If interested in Geological timescale take class, if not do not.

This was a genuinely interesting class and I think my not doing that well is mainly a product of not going to all the lectures. BEWARE that you are expected to know topics in great detail including memorizing exact dates of lots of events and their significance to each other. He wasn't great at signaling what content to focus on, making it hard.

If you're a BA student or just not interested or motivated enough, DO NOT. take this class. Heavy course with so many details and the tests barely cover half of them; so annoying bc you never know what to study.

he tries to make everyone pass tho, so he gives very easy assignments and open books pop quizzes that boost your grade

This class was difficult for an intro class. He provided a textbook that he wrote, so if you didn't understand something in the lecture the textbook wouldn't help. It was difficult to get help outside of class. I found the quizzes difficult (only 4 questions) but the problems sets and paper got my grade up, and the final as it was open-book.

Professor Halverson is really well versed in geology, especially sedimentology. He has really interesting answers to the questions asked in class. The readings and lecture slides (all written by him) are engaging. Great class, unless for some reason you don't believe in evolution and the scientific method!

Very inspiring to learn from someone who is both at the head of his field among colleagues, and very passionate about teaching students. Its a hard class because youre learning on the cutting edge, but very worth it!

This class was harder than accepted and should not be an entry level course to Geology. Professor Halverson was very passionate about this subject and tended to go into a lot of detail about some things and yet didn't explain enough about other concepts. Overall, this course is pretty difficult. On the upside, he is a pretty easy grader.

Galen is highly respected in his field and it shows in his lectures. He's very passionate about EPSC and tends to go into a lot of detail. This class covers a ton of material, most of which wasn't tested on, but it was overall very interesting. I failed the midterm but aced the final... lots and lots of studying is needed.

Professor Halverson is a nice person who knows the subject matter very well but this course should not be available to freshmen or students with no background in Geology, it contains a heinous amount of material very little of which is tested, few resources to help prepare for exams which are short and difficult. Do not take will likely hurt GPA

He is obviously very knowledgeable in mathematics, but I feel as though he was bored to death teaching such a low-level course. His lectures were not very engaging, but he answered any questions people had. He also focused a lot on proofs that weren't applicable to the exams. Granted, it was a different professor who made the exam.

Forget that his students are not all math students who know every term he is using, and when we tell him he tells us that it's simple (it's not simple). Proof heavy, but only the practical are on the exam. Not exactly helpful on the forum, but stays after class to answer every question. Homework is heavy but graded nicely.
He focuses a little too much on proofs, which are not on the exam, but explains clearly.

I attempted to take MATH 317 with this prof but after leaving the first lecture it felt like I registered for the wrong course. The
material he reviewed was far more difficult and different than anything taught in any pre-requisite course. Also the recommended readings were unfairly long. I hope a new prof teaches the course this Fall.
Wonderful course!
He teaches very well and the homeworks are useful. The midterm and final are both online.

Very smart guy and generous grader. Doesn't seem to understand that his students are undergrads with other work to do. A lot of "figure it out yourself" and "just look at the textbook". No TA, tutorials, or assignment solutions. Do not recommend unless you're very passionate about the material and willing to put in a LOT of time.
Gantumur explains things very lucidly and clearly, his examples are illustrative and his diagrams are awesome.

A difficult class but very rewarding if you get through it. Tsogtgerel specializes in ODEs and you will come out of the class well prepared for higher level PDE courses. Lectures are dense but the professor is doing his best to be a good teacher. This class would have been 100x more enjoyable if it were not held at 8:30 in the morning

really nice guy but teaching in a confusing way. It assumes that you know a lot about math so if you haven't finished analysis it will be painful. assignment is not easy but midterm and final are quite fair. good luck

Beitel is unfit to be a teacher. He was unbelievably harsh when grading my beautiful work. Also, for the most part, the documentaries of his that he showed us in class were boring. One of his contributions to society is a film (Chez Schwartz) that shows people sitting in a restaurant eating dead pig. It's absolutely riveting! Lol!

Professor Beitel is extremely nice and approachable. He clearly cares a lot about his students. He's a fair grader- generous if anything. The one frustrating thing about JWST 309 is that attendance for classes where we solely viewed films (which were posted on MyCourses anyways) was mandatory and cooked my grade.

Ah Professor Beitel! You can tell when teachers are passionate about their subject. Rarely do they transmit this passion as much as this man. He makes one want to LEARN and ABSORB everything he has to say. School would be magnificent if every professor was like him! Such a beautiful soul. I will fondly remember McGill because of people like him.

Jews in Film was a breath of fresh air at McGill. It is a small class with thought-provoking conversations and assignments that make you reflect on yourself. I learned a lot in this class and I think Garry is a phenomenal person and professor and he just all around rocks.

An incredible professor and Human. Genuinely cares about his students and is interested in what they have to say, and the course is a pleasure. The assignments demand thought and engagement with the material, but if you are a good reflective writer you will do well. And if not, and you see him for help he will get you there.
If you're Jewish, and you like film, take JWST 309. He wants you to succeed, the assignments are though provoking, and most of all he's a total inspiration.
No Comments
Great guy, maybe my favourite prof at mcgill.  Take this course!!

Best prof you could ever ask for at McGill!! Sooo interesting! Docu film is a great class. Easy, but you learn so much. It's all about class discussions... Very easy going. Can't recommend him enough!
Gary Brouhard single handedly tanked all my hopes and dreams. No idea how he sleeps at night. Making jokes about his kids does not make him a good prof.

Best professor I've ever had. Lectures are incredibly engaging and entertaining. I appreciate that he shares things about himself too. Exams are not particularly tough if you have a good handle on the content. Unlike most biology classes, Gary does a great job of avoiding ambiguity in his exam questions too, which is much appreciated!

He is an excellent professor and always makes his lectures fun. Undoubtably, he is very good at teaching. But his exams are really tough. Don't be too relaxed about exams just because the course is fun. You really need to attend tutorials and SciLearn sessions to improve for the exams.
actually out to destroy GPAs. Evil.

One of the best profs I've had at McGill! He really cares a lot about his students, and although the content can be challenging and confusing he always explains it in easy to understand ways. Midterm and quizzes were also very fair, an A is definitely achievable if you put the work in!!

He is so kind and tries his best to make lectures engaging and informative. I really loved attending class! His relatability was so refreshing and he added a creative component unseen in any of my other science classes. Go to lecture and study but Gary rules!

He is very entertaining, and interesting. He makes you want to learn, which was a nice change from biol 200 despite the teachers being kind. Everyone compares the two because of their difficulty, I personally believe that because Prof Brouhard is so engaging and entertaining he makes the content easier to retain.

dont be fooled by himr. He is an amazing lecture, NOT a good teacher his lecture slides contain minimal notes, you to have to write everything he says

 worst part: You can study as much as you want, memorize every single slide, write down all his notes THEN when you show up to his exam; he will ask the most random difficult questions ever
Engaging lectures, but beware - exams require deep understanding, not just memorization. unstuckstudy was a game-changer for my study prep.

This guy is hilarious and a fantastic lecturer. Write down literally everything he says, even the smallest detail, and work to understand the material deeper than surface level memorization. His test questions require you to think in new ways about the material which is what makes them so hard, but not impossible if you understand the material well

Dr. Wild was a tad bit condescending I must say. Other than that, I would say it's a pretty chill class as long as you do the work. Highly recommend + it's online + he barely shows up to class because he's a doctor.

If you put in the work, you will get an A. It is heavy in terms of the amount of writing we need to do. However, with time management skills, you will ace it. I like the Case based discussions a lot. He makes a lot of room for communication with your group mates and working on the group project, which is also very interesting. He is caring!
He is such a nice guy! Assignments require a bit of work, but he grades them pretty fairly if you just put in the work! Group project was a little complicated but I learned a lot in this class!
A lotta writing but Dr. Wild gives you awesome feedback and as long as you put effort into the class, you'll do well..
great teacher. once a week class. a lot of work but interesting topics.
He is a great teacher. His style of teaching is unique and he's very engaging and funny.

Fun class, you learn alot without the pressure of memorising  pointless details, as there is no written exam in this class. Online work and a term paper are all you need to do. Oh, and classes are 50 minutes every two weeks!
Truly a superb teacher. Course is almost entirely online and working in teams for the research proposal was the most interesting part of the course. A must.

He is the best example of a great professor. Super smart and knows his stuff, cares about the undergrad much more than the university. A great mentor and he gives really constructive feedback. I learned a lot.
Very good prof, that knows well his area.

Extremely intelligent, interested prof. This class is really interesting, very challenging, and very rewarding. Its nice to find professors like this who treat there students like real people with real ideas.

Professor Fiasse is okay, but unfortunately, I had a really hard time understanding her lectures - her accent is heavy, almost indecipherable, and the visuals she uses are extremely vague. I typically left class feeling more confused than when I came in. Lots of group discussions, which is fun but also felt like a waste of time.

She's a good prof, really cares about her students and explains things clearly. Sometimes a bit intense, but you actually learn a lot. Philosophy feels real and interesting with her. Would definitely take her class again.

Truly one of the best professors at McGill. Passionate, deeply caring, and explains complex ideas with clarity. Her lectures make philosophy engaging and meaningful. Inspires critical thinking and respect—highly recommended!

Fiasse is honestly such a nice professor. I genuinely would take this class again if I needed to. I found it very interesting and captivating. The work load was reasonable, the class isn't too hard and I didn't find myself stressing too much. Definitely would recommend and I think most students would have a good time in her class. Super nice.

Every class is a desired part of my day, her expertise is incredibebly shoking , prof fiasse is a very empathic thatcher always ready to help you, no matter what, I never noticed any favourites and her class is a well being space. Love the subject.

Professor Gaëlle Fiasse is truly one of the most inspiring educators at McGill University. she brings every concept to life with clarity, empathy, and deep intellectual insight. What makes her exceptional is not only her vast knowledge, but her ability to connect complex philosophical ideas to real-world situations and human experiences.

She really went easy on the readings. She opted for in-depth reading and reflection over than lots-of-information absorbing. She might be a little bit missing a pre-defined structure for the lectures, but she follows the readings. Her examples, ideas and explanations are clear. She is very helpful in office-hours. Very nice person. Good professor.

the class is interesting but prof fiasse is frankly rude and didn't provide any feedback on the midterm. she wouldn't accept my accommodations through OSVRSE until i got OSD involved, which caused so much unneeded stress this semester

Prof. Fiasse takes some getting used to, but she is honestly one of most understanding profs I've had at McGill. I've taken RELG 373 & RELG 399, both times needed accommodations for mental health and she did all she can to make things manageable for me. Show that you're interested in the content and are trying your best and she'll help you succeed.

Professor Fiasse is knowledgeable but the grading criteria and instruction for her graduate courses are nonsensical. Her grading is arbitrarily difficult and unpredictable, she plays favourites with students when it comes to grading, and during the Covid-19 pandemic she showed no sympathy to suffering students.

The skills you get are useful both in other classes and in the professional life. Grading was tough as she deducts marks for details. But you can go argue and she'll give you back some of it. Group project is interesting as it is in partnership with real organization. Some mistakes in quizzes but she rectified them later by giving points. Good prof

Just took her for INSY 442, tbh, I don't know if that is the way the course was designed. The way she teaches us was like 1 put almost nothing on the ppt 2. attend lectures and do something really superficial(level 1 or 2) then for the quiz and exam(level 10 ). Tough grader and she made the group project way harder than the course requirement
Please avoid her if you can. The course content is not hard, but the grading way is so confusing. You may lose your marks for every single missing details.
Easy course but confusing grading scheme. She always got lost in her own lecture.
Always smiling, full of energy, and completely fair in her assessments. A pleasure to attend her classes!
Shes scary and a very angry person who will go after you if she doesnt like you. She does t know how to teach a course
Very appreciated her. Her class was entertaining. Very interesting class, I've learned a lot. The only bad thing was the pop quizzes
Prof. Bassellier is amazing. i've taken her for the intro IS class, and she is great. for sure her lectures are all over the place, but she will help you if you ask.

Avoid it at all costs, horrible experience, she tried to be nice and caring , but her anxiety gets in the middle of it. The whole semester was a big headache and a mistake. Take it with other profs, unless you want to add misery to your life.

Very good professor, clear, kind and always dedicated to help. Exams are fair (neither too easy nor too hard). I also had Donovan as a professor, both are great, Donovan is more into jokes, Genevieve more into teaching you the most she can in a lecture. You can take her it won't be a mistake !
Not a bad teacher. He was funny and fun. I did have to teach myself mostly everything though.

Don't understand what he is even talking about most of the time and are expected to learn what you need for the exams using the assignments. The stuff in the assignments are not once mentioned in lectures, making it all self learning.

I took MIME 512. A demanding course, but this way I learned a lot about the subject (corrosion and degradation of materials). Although not strictly mandatory, he really wants us to participate in the class, which I think is good. The exercises in the quizzes were similar to the ones taught in the tutorials. Tough but fair.

absolutely horrible. he only teaches theory in class, and then the whole final and midterm are applications that we mever learned how to do. he barely every mentionned these formulas. nice guy, horrible teacher
avoid if you can but mime352 is compulsory so good luck

Mistreats students, hasn't updated his lectures since early 2000s, if he can't answer questions in class he will get annoyed, apparently has no industrial experience? I saw him yell at his TAs as well... On the plus side he never updates his material and reuses quizzes from last years.
Unhelpful, can't teach and boring classes.
One of the best Professors in signal processing and system identification

Professor Mitsis is a real gem. Though he teaches one of the hardest bioeng classes at Mcgill, he tries his best to make the material understandable and engaging. In terms of grading, his exams and assignments are intense because he expects you to put a lot of time and effort. Study hard and you'll enjoy his class.
Phenomenal!
I love him

He is genuinely one of the sweetest, most understanding instructors I've ever had at McGill. His compassion shows in every part of his teaching.

He is an exceptionally fair grader. You always know what he expects. Most importantly, he creates an environment where you feel comfortable asking questions, making mistakes, and actually learning.
Super nice man! Very easy grader but has a very annoying 10-12 page research paper as a final. Also very helpful with advice if you ask him anything. He has a thick Dutch accent.

The most caring and inspiring professor I have had at McGill. He inspired me to continue with my studies. His lectures are accessible and he makes the material seem simple but he is actually a world expert and is just good at making complex things enjoyable. A favourite.
the greatest. super chill, no need to read

This class was so easy. I have no idea what I learnt honestly, but thoroughly enjoyed it. He took attendance once (20% of your mark), had a take home midterm (answers were easily found in the coursepack), had either a 10 minute presentation to reduce amount of pages in the final paper, which was about any bible related topic you wanted. I loved it.

What can I say, super laid back, he doesn't care about grading, want to boost your GPA take him, 50% final paper, 30% participation 20% oral, I took him for both Relg 307 and 300. NO EXAMS. Attendance isn't mandatory. Show a bit of passion and your getting an A
Great prof, doesn't stress you too much and gives you a lot of flexibility, tho he doesn't give much feedback on the assignments. Beware that he takes attendance occasionally.
Great professor. He's the reason I returned to McGill for grad studies after a horrible experience with an egotistical legend-in-his-own-mind professor at Université Laval.
Prof Zavosh is the goat.
Professor Zavosh is the goat.
he was a nice teacher but his lectures were hard to sit through because he goes on many tangents…

Lectures were hard to follow as prof would often go on tangents, slides had very little info. Feedback on assignments was very vague, grading was arbitrary. The final was based on the textbook and readings, and entirely self-study. You wouldn't know the answer to many MCQs on the final unless you read the textbook, which he only mentions once.

Prof. Zavosh is one of the best! He's accessible outside of class, explains the material thoroughly, and genuinely wants his students to succeed. Although attendance isn't mandatory, his lectures are insightful and offer much more than the slides.

Professor Zavosh is one of the kindest and most passionate professors I've ever had. He's incredibly responsive to emails and brings a contagious positivity to every class. He genuinely wants his students to succeed and is very mindful not to overload them with unnecessary work. Highly recommend.

Professor Ghahhar was super sweet and caring, he really wants his students to do well. He taught the second portion of MGCR 382 which was more logic and case studies. He makes class engaging and easy to follow. Easy grading too for group projects. Very easy to do well in this class if you go to class and listen, not much studying outside required.

I preferred Melville's part by far. With Zavosh, the lectures felt all over the place. He seems like a smart guy, but his teaching style was hard to follow. The final exam was really short and didn't require much studying. Some questions weren't covered directly in class and relied more on common sense.

Ghahhar cares a lot about his students and wants you to get a good grade. So, his final is ridiculously easy (just review the PowerPoint slides), but his lectures are all over the place and very difficult to understand. I honestly wish this class were approached differently since the content seems genuinely interesting, but it's all surface-level.

What are these reviews? I haven't taken MGCR 423, but for MGCR 382 he is absolutely terrible. Horrible lectures with random grading and useless feedback. He seems like a fun guy, but he has no idea how to teach nor grade.

Professor Arcuri cares about his students. He takes the time to ensure that his students understand the material and also makes it enjoyable. He gave good examples of his work in the public healthcare system.

It's a hard course, and she is not a bad teacher. I think the grading scheme is ridiculous, it just pushes a lot more students into the B and C range. She's an ok teacher to take content-wise for 250, however she is the one who introduced the grading scheme and it really should be changed.
The grading scheme is really stressful and doesn't feel helpful. She said it would help us learn better, but it honestly just makes us stressing about the exams instead of actually learning.
Please don't do this to yourself, she is a pain to both your Java/Programming learning path and your grades
One of the toughest graders I've ever experienced, made all the studying worthless be aware about this prof.

I think Giulia does care for her students, but she is doing too much with the grading. I have never failed a exam as badly as I did in this class. I ended studying for the exams instead of optimizing my knowledge.
Avoid at all costs

One of the worst prof I encountered in my degree. She is just an ordinary lecturer but she expects smth very supernatural from the students. You can tell she doesn't put much effort into lectures and she randomly cancels class without prior notice. Easy but I didn't learn much.

I was really excited to take this class and unfortunately, the lectures were really not effective. Lots of field trips to art museums which is really cool, but make sure you don't have class before or after to account for transportation. Grading is just 2 pass/fail reflections, a midterm paper and final paper.

Lectures are dense, and he tends to go on many monotone tangents about his research. Also, kind of ironic how he likes to emphasize how to be a "good coach" or "teacher", but lacks those characteristics himself. His exams are 50/50 and memory-based (remember random facts he mentions in class because they'll be on the exam).

I don't understand the negative comments about this professor. In my experience he is a really genuine and caring person. I had a medical problem and he was so comprehensive and suggested many solutions that worked best for me. He is not condescending he is simply proud of the research he has done and rightly so. His lectures are very interesting!

Monotone boring lectures. Has a tendency to be egotistical. Large portion of his tests is useless trivial information on quotes and his and his colleagues accomplishments. Make sure to memorize every date, quote, study (in detail), even the random stuff he says in class. Heavily recommend going to the lectures. Only take the course if you have to.

Boring lecture, his voice makes you fall asleep. He only talks about his research all the time, nothing else besides his "amazing" research during the past 20 years. Be ready to welcome the most famous guy in the field.

Awesome guy!!! Could talk about sports with him forever. He's an absolute genius BTW. He is very kind, patient, caring, helpful and truly cares a lot about his students! Would recommend taking him again.
Very nice guy! Cares a lot about his students. He's extremely intelligent and knowledgable, would recommend taking him.

Honestly, this teacher is the embodiment of what a teacher should not be. As the head of the department for Kinesiology and Physical Education, he is an uncaring, and quite selfish individual. Seriously just an overall rude professor. No one wants to learn from someone so condescending to his students, almost makes one feel unwelcome to email him and ask questions. Tests are FINE but asks ridiculous unnecessary irrelevant questions to the course.

I do not understand all the negative reviews this Prof has received. He is by far one of my favorite professors at McGill. Prof is alright and the material is interesting. The exam, just like his sports psychology class, is completely bs.  Test you on the most trivial things ever...

Professor Hickey is awesome. He is knowledgeable in so many fields and his research is really cool! He is very mindful of students and is very approachable. He seems nervous and bland at first but you'll grow to like him very quickly.
Great Prof!

He is an easy-going professor who did a good job at being minimally opinionated (important since environmental assessment can be subjective). He may seem a bit bland at first but after a while you realize he has a good sense of humor and is thoughtful about the material he teaches.

Prof. Hickey is a great prof because his lecture slides are clear and he is great at explaining everything. Not only is he very knowledgeable, the class is graded very fairly. There's no final and test material is based on slides. You must attend class since it's worth 10% of your grade.

A super easy but interesting course. Only one midterm in the 5th week. Make sure your presentation and website looks nice and informative though. The outlook of your project is as important as the content.

I think the course number has changed since I've taken it, but the content is the same. Very boring material, but there was only 1 in-class test (in the first 5 weeks!), no final, no textbook,and the project was interesting enough. Takes attendance for participation though. Recommended if you're considering pursuing impact assessments
I am a grad student, so dont know about his classes.

Roberts is the worst teacher I have had in my entire academic career. He has no respect for students and does not care if you understand the material or not. There are no class notes provided. When you do not understand, his answer is to read entire chapters of the textbook, the same that he suggests is wildly inaccurate. DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS

Quizzes made and marked by TA's, usually more difficult than Midterm & Final. His lectures are more focused on qualitative analysis but does not grade this way. Marks all 100+ exams in one day, hardly any part marks because of this. Very busy prof with grad students and a consulting company
Very good Prof! Passionate about electronics. Quizzes were hard but the midterm and final were easy if you studied.

God of electronics. Truly good in electronics and most of all, best lectures ever. They were so good that I had to come back next semester and do them all again with my craving for understanding. Again, take him, take him and don't even think a second time. Best of the best, you go Prof. Gordon!

He is a condescending so and so who thinks he invented electronics itself. In his eyes students are nothing more than lowlifes and treats them with little respect and consideration. His lectures have little coherence although his slides are good. But if he is what McGill prides itself in, then it reflects on the flawed philosophy of it all.
This class really isn't as bad as people say it is. You don't really need to go to class, just read the textbook and do the assignment questions and you'll be fine.
Good explanations and use of animations and analogies. Quizzes are just questions from assignments. Sometime rambles on offtopic things. Often misunderstands student questions.

Makes you buy HIS book and use HIS program. Too bad the program does not work AT ALL. Avoid this dude like the plague. Seriously injured myself halfway through the course and he was not accomodating whatsoever.
NO NO NO, do not take his class.  IF you do remeber this:  YOU WILL BE ALONE FOR THE LABS and you cant do them.  DONT TAKE THIS unless u like learning nothing and doind a lot of work
Not recommend
Not recommended at all

An incredible researcher and such a caring person. Avoid this professor at all cost my friend

Terrible professor. Lectures are incomplete and force you to type nonstop instead of actually learning. She never uploads complete PowerPoint presentations, the content is abstract, and she doesn't provide any explanations. For assignments, even a minor mistake results in only 50% of the possible points. The exams are very difficult, and the grading is extremely harsh.

Reviews here about toughness and difficulty are right. However, she has been one of the most caring profs that I've ever had. She is going to fail you . Do not take this course at all . She love to fail students

This prof is the worst prof you could ever take. I am even surprised how she still has a job because she clearly does not genuinely care about her students. To be realistic, it was a tough course but there were many interesting topics and creative teaching method. I really liked the class with Prof Brilmyer.
Prof Brilmyer is amazing! I really love our class discussions. (the assignment feedback is also super helpful :)))
They are the most interesting and compassionate professor I had during my time at McGill
Really great professor, will be taking them again
A very nice and inspiring prof, passionate on the studies. I took his GEOG203 second segment but that was great!

Graham was kind and really accessible to students outside of class and he gives really great insights. He really cares about the students' interests and is really flexible and open to feedback on the class.
Amazing professor and really knowledgeable! Was really helpful and gave amazing feedback on the assignments. He is accessible and honest, and was also really accommodating.

*General review, not a specific class* I have now had two classes with Graham and loved them both. You can really see the effort he puts into making sure everyone understands course content and doesn't mind slowing things down and reviewing. He is one of the most dedicated professors I've experienced and I'm happy I got to have him teach me twice.

Graham is one of the kindest professors I have ever encountered. His material is interesting, and he is clearly very passionate and knowledgeable about it. He will give great feedback and follow up later to make sure you've understood and are on the right track.
Very entertaining, a genuinely cool personality. But very racist

I've had Grant Clark many time as my teacher and also as my advisor during undergrad. All I can tell is I think this professor is an incompetent. Grant is a great prof, this class really expands on what you learn in 201 and the way he structured coursework was really pleasant. Only thing to really watch for was the midterm which I found kinda unintuitive.
Really fun class. Learned a lot about GIS and programming. He really made the material interesting and was accessible during office hours. Would highly recommend

Grant is brilliant, presents material effectively. Accessibility was an issue, as he tends to overcommit, lacking collaborative coordination. Rlly love! Grant's great. Definitely a useful class if you want to get better at GIS.
Hes great in MIMM 211 and MIMM 413! Very calm, lectures at a good pace, clear slides, fair exam questions, approachable prof
Presents really interesting stuff. He's very clear & has clean slides.

So pretentious, inspirational and amazing 3 3 3 He made me fall in love with parasitology. His lectures were super engaging, and although the questions on the final are specific, they aren't terrible. MATLASHEWSKI FAN CLUB
The contents of the lectures are so interesting and they way he teach is very clear! Best prof I met!

Best teacher, he really takes his time presenting the material so that it is clear. His exam questions were pretty easy (not so for the other professors teaching the course). very good teacher. clear and insightful. he ties in enough anecdotes that pertain to daily life which makes the material so much more relevant and interesting.
Yup, this guy was my favorite out of the four lecturers we had for this course. He was not at all boring and his exam questions were rather easy.
He makes his subject very interesting! AWESOME TEACHER! and He's kinda cute too.

a very interesting prof. his passion is evident in the way he teaches and gets the class interested too. oh yeah and he's also cute!

Extremely massive, disorganized lecture, there are always problems with lecture recordings (image cropped of, no sound etc) and he never fixed it, exam heavy (midterm+final take up about 70% )

Literally zero organization this semester, grading scheme was not followed and was revised multiple times, assignment base code was broken for each assignment, lecture recordings were either corrupted, had no or bad audio, and content we were promised we'd have access to (slides) were either not posted or posted too late.

Worst organization of a course I've seen yet. Programming assignments took AT LEAST an hour to even get working (setup), then the questions themselves were incredibly unclear and confusing. This class is a mess. It gave me so much anxiety because of how disorganized the class is.
Worst prof and class ever. Very disorganize and extremely unclear in his assignments. His teaching is fine but the assignments are just disastrous.

He is one my favorite prof! Super super busy and this affected the course's tempo and he didn't response to people's emails, but his lectures were really valuable and his knowledge and practice skills - excellent. Maybe I'm biased because I didn't enjoy the course material that much, but it just didn't seem like he was very interested in teaching this course. he is one of the BEST teachers EVER. makes boring material interesting, wont let you fall asleep, help his students as much as he can.CARES about you.You are always welcome to his office even if he is busy.goes thorugh everything even not related to the course with you to make you feel good. give the BEST advices.knows his stuff.AN ASSET for mcgill
The best teacher ever
Teaches post-midterm, great guy

Slide deck can seem super long, as instead of slide transitions, it's multiple duplicates with added pictures/diagrams, but content is easily digestible. Super sweet prof, comfortable to ask questions.

Midterm and Final were really hard with both needing to be curved. I found the questions to be pretty vague, with many not being like the practice. He gives very little practice questions. He is however very nice and the lectures are pretty engaging
Professor Weitzner is an okay professor. The assignments are long, and the exams, especially the midterm, are very challenging. Office hours are not very helpful.

Very hard exams and gives few practice problems. Tough grader ex: will sometimes not give any partial marks on an exam question, even if you are mostly correct. Also, sometimes asks an undetailed and subjective question that can be answered in multiple different ways but only wants to hear what he believes and takes off marks. would not recommend.
Gregory is a one of a kind! He is super nice, hilarious, encourages participation and questions. He gives hard exams but they're doable if you focus. I would take him in a heartbeat!

Great Professor. Super interesting and wants to help you if you have questions. Midterm and finals are tricky, because you only have 1-2 mathematical questions, with the rest being qualitative. But if you are able to understand the material conceptually, then you can do well
Not a good prof, few practice problems, brutal exams.
Great prof, I loved his class
Honestly not a good professor, midterm and final have nothing to do with practice he gives. Lectures can be interesting at times but not reachable, I do not recommend.
Great prof, super chill guy, super interesting lectures
great prof

No midterm or Final so thats good news. Only thing is the reading for conferences can be a lot for someone not in history, as long as you do them not all the night before you'll be fine and get a really good grade, participation matters in conferences too. Only thing it can become boring but her classes are still good

The class was nice, quite easy to follow. Tests and assignments aren't difficult if you pay attention to lectures and do the readings (which happened to be pretty heavy for some conferences). The prof is really nice. I would recommend her

She is a very nice and knowledgeable teacher; however, she is very monotone, which can make the lectures quite boring. The readings and assignments are very fair, with no exams. You will learn a lot about the history of East Asia and finish with an A pretty easily.

She is a nice teacher who is very knowledgeable. However, you will not receive 100% on any paper you write. She told me herself that giving out an 100 is remarkably rare and basically said she won't do it. Her lectures were boring and our attendance was marked. The quizzes were... okay?? Must have read all of the required readings to do well.

She is nice as a person and knowledgeable as a professor. The workload is very agreeable for a seminar and it has a good portion of primary and secondary sources. She can be monotone but her lectures are effective and fruitful. I ended up learning a lot from her. You can really tell that she cares a lot about her students and the course material.

While her lectures can be a bit disorganized, especially towards the beginning of the semester, HIST 208 is the most free A you'll find at McGill. The assignments are not too hard, the quizzes a mere formality and most of all, no final. The material is interesting and requires very minimal effort for a good grade. If you can take this class, do it.

I like her a lot- the lectures were interesting but the feedback on essays was always too late to do anything. However, there was no final which was super great! She's very kind and will listen to any questions you have.

She managed to turn a fascinating subject into a boring one in her dry lectures... Her quizzes were extremely specific and it was nearly impossible to get a great grade even after having attended all her lectures and participated in conferences. She gives absolutely no feedback. Nice lady but bad teacher.
She is sweet and accommodating. Reading a bit heavy and lecture a bit dry. Yet she is very clear with her expectations on each assessment. Fair grading. Recommended!
Gave me a passing grade on the final and was easy to contact to get marks back on my midterms. Clearly cares and wants his students to pass. Grading criteria is very vague and the class is hard.

Tests are graded extremely harshly but he will often give back marks if you argue or through his peer-review method which is a big boost to your grade. Terrible prof. Avoid. At. All. Costs.

The WORST teacher I've ever had in my entire life. This teacher needs to give up and retire NOW. His Finals are impossible, and he fails students over technicalities—like needing a minimum grade on the Final. He will fail you.

Terrible teacher, hated being in his class. AVOID!!!!! Register with Meyer Nahon, he's way better!

This guy doesn't care at all about his students success. Made one question on our midterm impossible to solve and just said sorry. Tiny mistakes can cost you your whole grade. I'd rather tack on an extra year than take this guy again. If you have to take him you're cooked, good luck.

Teacher doesn't care about the course. Multiple mistakes in the powerpoints, in the exam, in the quizzes. Get ready to learn everything by yourself and complain when you see the grading for your midterm.

Useless lectures. So many mistakes in slides (especially in the 3-D part). Very bad at teaching the material. However the class is slightly easier than with the old prof. Would NOT retake this prof in any other class.
He was chill. Grade averages are higher with him than past professors.
Cool prof but does not explain well grammar and vocab. Lots of grammar and structures to study alone. The tests are very difficult specially because he did not prepare us.

M. Gachet is such a nice guy. Really cares about his students' well being. He assigns a lot of homework between each class and expects participation by everyone seeing as it is a language course. Can be a harsh grader, but he gives extensive feedback on compositions and is always very accessible for questions and happy to help.

Super friendly prof and a small class, so the lectures are mostly discussion-based. There are two group projects and a few assignments (one paper, one video, and 3 vocabulary assignments). If you show up to class and participate it's definitely an easy A. I recommend taking this class just for the prof or if you want to practice your oral french!

He's fine. Homeworks are good, course material makes sense, he's a pretty fun guy. My main criticism is that the lectures just aren't dense enough. He shows up for an 80 minute lecture with only 60 minutes of material worth teaching, so 20 minutes of each class is just doing absolutely nothing, mostly just sitting through very hit or miss jokes.

OMG he became my favourite physics teacher EVER! His lectures are so interesting, and he truly IS passionate. His homework are hard, BUT final and midterm are VERY fair. He rambles and makes "edgy" jokes that just aren't funny. He made a joke this year about bringing a gun to class to fend off the pro Palestine protesters... Kind of crazy how some profs use their platform.

One word - The G.O.A.T. Was blessed to have two classes with this man in one semester. Prof. Guillaume's passion for physics is truly contagious, and I mean it in the most positive way. His approach is different than most physics professors. I would say it is more oriented on how a certain formula was obtained rather than applying it. Funny and approachable person with a clear passion for the subject. Very manageable course if you do your due diligence.
So unclear and unhelpful

He's a great lecturer, very passionate about teaching. Can sometimes go off on a tangent about other areas of physics but does so to help you see the big picture. Course was such a joke. Couldn't teach so he made the exam super easy. If the exam was remotely fair the entire class would've failed. He could have been more clear and could have included more examples. The final was pretty difficult.

He has poor teaching ability and often rambles about his lab. His lectures will make you even more confused then before. However, Gervais's exams are very easy. Fantastic professor who is really knowledgeable. Took for winter exchange and I really learned a lot! Guillaume is a great guy, you learn more about fixed income than any other teachers could teach you. Would swear at his TA in class.

Very difficult course for the wrong reasons. Lectures often feel condescending and unclear. Grading is slow and feedback is limited. Materials, including sample exams, contain errors that are not corrected promptly. Overall, a frustrating experience and I would recommend avoiding it.

Probably the hardest class you could possibly take in Finance at McGill. Extremely long project, a LOT of material (and most of it is extremely difficult). If you value having a good grade, your time, your sanity then take this with another professor. He is super knowledgeable and willing to help but just makes the class way harder than needed.

class discussions through perusall before every class--he is a literature prof so make sure you are reading everything! as long as you read and absorb the texts you will be fine. very lenient marker with final projects and very flexible with the form those projects take. you were able to do anything from fanfiction to creating a website. great guy!

I absolutely loved this class. The lectures were absolutely great and definitely mandatory - don't think you can skip because there was 0 material online, everything depends on notes taken in class. Personally something I really enjoy, but know many won't be into. Just be aware ! Made me enjoy history. Easy to do well, hard work to do excellent.

Overall Professor Campbell was an excellent teacher. The grading system is 10% participation, 10% conference participation, 60% final exam and 20% midterm. As long as you showed up to the lectures especially the conferences where he basically gives out a summary of all the content needed for assessments, you should do well.

Engaging lectures; I enjoyed attending every one of them even though they were scheduled at 8:35. Revising was a bit stressful but manageable if your workload isn't crazy

prof Campbell was one of the best profs I have had so far (second year). His lectures were amazing, making studying for the midterm very easy. Attendance 10%, conference 10%(3), midterm (20%), final exam (60%). slides not posted so attendance is mandatory and readings are not required

The course is structure like this: Course Participation: 10% Class Presentation: 15 % Mid Term Examination: 15% Final Examination: 60% - Although Prof. Campbell is very unclear, off-topic, disorganised, it is not to hard too get an A. - Powerpoint slides not posted on mycourses - there is no textbook and you don't need to do the readings

Very interesting prof who brings a new perspective to history. If you want a non-european centered view of history, take any of his courses. You need to understand the themes, make connections and remember some details to do well in this class.

Terrible. Just terrible. Unorganized teaching, 100% exam final, vacuous class, inexplicable grading...

In-Ho teaches a very conceptually challenging subject. But he is really funny, and he takes an interest in every person who goes to his class. HIGHLY recommended prof, and i HIGHLY recommended you go to his lectures because thermo cannot be fully learned from a textbook. Assignments=difficult, but VERY helpful and relevant for exams.

Best Prof! Very funny. Assignments are tough but helpful for the exam.
One of the best profs I've ever had. Very good at teaching, clarifying concepts, and a good sense of humor to boot. Exams are tough, but not mean.

Hala is absolutely incredible. Introductory Arabic would be impossible without her.
