She is one of the main reasons I have stayed with the Arabic program (and continued to take it from an elective course to making it my minor) for all of my years at McGill!

Hala is honestly the most caring and understanding teacher I have ever met. She is incredibly hilarious and will always create a nice atmosphere in class. She does her best to explain the material in a way that will make everything easy. However the class is given 5 times a week and there are homework everyday so it can get heavy and annoying.

Hala is one of the most amazing teachers I have ever had. She is unbelievably knowledgeable, caring, funny, and enthusiastic every single day. She truly made the class feel like a family and a safe and fun place to learn. Thank you Hala, we love you!!

Hala is so knowledgeable about language and can make even the hardest Arabic grammar problems seem doable. She always welcomes you into her office for help or just to talk. She's also just a very sweet, caring, and funny person! One of my favourite profs by far.

Professor Hala is easily one of the best teachers I've had period (both across University and school). UBER charismatic, nice, and effective in her teaching style! You cant help but enjoy her class! She truly lives up to and exceeds her 5 star rating!! Highly recommended!
Hala is super nice and though arabic definitely is a lot of work it's also really fun

by far the SWEETEST, most DOWN TO EARTH and helpful prof ive ever had! Arabic is a tough language to learn and she really makes it alot easier. So helpful her in explanations and she's just so cute. its really hard not to like her and shes a great teacher ! Wish I had her for all 3 years I took arabic at mcgill

All the professors teaching Arabic are great, but Hala is the sweetest you'll ever meet. It's a small class at 8:30 Mon-Fri, so you get to know everybody (including the professor) really well. Coming from Lebanon, she shares a lot of Arabic culture tidbits/personal anecdotes. She is always available for consultation outside class, even just to chat
Arabic was hard, but in teaching it she was very good at teaching. She's also is very nice and helpful if one needs help. Do your homework

This class is 100% doable. Just do the homeworks (and redo them before the final), rewatch lectures and understand the proofs he does in them, and do the practice finals that he posts. Incredibly straightforward. There were no surprises on the final. I also felt that lectures were clear, occasionally supplemented with the notes or office hours.

Very harsh grader, gave me 0 for a 15 points question, even though the proof was half right, I'm not saying it was completely right, but I think I deserved partial grades. Took this course in my last semester and I didn't graduate because of it. Avoid the class and the professor!!!
This is the worst class I've taken so far. Final toooo heavy and tooo hard to pass.

Good at teaching but wild grading scheme (70% final, assignments 3% each). Exams were p reasonable, just graded very harshly (few/no part marks). Assignments were killer, start early. MUST stay on top of content: do practice problems to prep for the assignments to prep for the exams (I didn't, see grade). I think 360's just a hard course :/

This professor is a disaster. Incomprehensible lectures, zero resources, and impossibly difficult assessments graded with sadistic harshness. Final worth 70% with no mercy for even minor errors. Coldly refused students begging to pass/graduate. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

His final is worth 70% so if u mess up the final, u basically is done.....
Does not show sympathy at all, there were at least 7 ppl begging for curve at the office hour since they need a few marks to pass or graduate, he refused them all
Avoid at allill cost!
god aweful exams (15% midterm non-shiftable (60% average) and 70% final (worse average)). Typical prof that's retained for his tenure. decent lectures but tanks your GPA
No curve, 70% for final, I'm glad that I didn't take this course in my last term

An absolute legend. Hard exams, but great payoff - you actually need to understand the material to do well and can't fake it. 

Incredibly kind and understanding, 100% recommend. Loved my time in his class so much.

The slideshows are based off the textbook and read through during lectures. Little guidance on the assignments which was frustrating as we weren't given a rubric, only a brief paragraph description on the syllabus with very harsh grading. There was also material on the final exam that wasn't taught in class or in textbook

Bomboclat he's the most lost, unorganized, unhelpful, boring and unfair prof. He has hearing trouble, a heavy accent, doesn't give over 77%, the least useful notes and rants about random objects he finds around the house

The teacher did not provide any instructions for the required assignment, which confused many students . Attendance was also graded, even through it was not mandatory . He reads outdated slides, which misleads students for the final exam . He also lacks communication/organizational skills as well as question handling . On this note, good luck !

Gives no outline or rubric for assignments and takes marks off when you don't meet his expectations that were never clear to us. Super hard grading. Terrible slideshows and had a very messy final review slideshow. Super nice guy but is very old fashioned with his practices in teaching.
He is a very nice person but his teaching skills are completely outdated. He forgets things, loses papers and he is also a pretty tough grader.

Professor Hamid is a nice man, but unfortunately his teaching abilities were not the best, he read right off the slide (which are very lengthy and all over the place), and always had technical problems. This course is very content heavy so be ready to memorize many concepts for the exam. However, he is accessible outside of the classroom.

He is not clear at all in lectures. Slides are really unhelpful. Tough grader. Doesnt respond to emails. Doesnt really know whats going on. He is kind though, and will make himself accessible and really help you if you go to office hours.

Probably the most unorganized person I've ever met. His slides are all over the place, and half the time even he doesn't know what he's talking about. Super kind and smart guy, but his background is in engineering and he's super out of touch with the modern world, so definitely not the person you want teaching your marketing class. Stay away.

Probably the most unorganized person I have ever met period. This guy is a mess - his slides are all over the place and half the time even he doesn't know what he's talking about. Super smart guy, but his background is in engineering, so I have no idea why he's teaching a marketing class. Super out of touch as well, which is not good for marketing.
He is very nice and helpful but the course is unorganized and outdated.

Prof Stainton is really nice and caring. I took RELG 252 and RELG 254, and in both, I thought the lectures were really interesting. In RELG 254, since it is a smaller class, he made sure to know everybody's names and always encouraged class participation. If you're interested in Hinduism at all, take his classes. You won't regret it!

Prof. Stainton is highly knowledgeable. The Hinduism section of RELG 252 is slightly more rigorous, but the course is genuinely approachable and a great introduction to East Asian religions. His tests are more technical, and he expects you to reference readings and identify images, but if you have good notes, you should be just fine.

engaging, clear lectures
note down what he says, often just talks but clearly passionate
tests sometimes have random questions: you will be fine if you listen in class and look at the photos
he emphasizes the readings that you will be tested on (non-textbook readings); just skim them
sometimes gets off topic but really great guy

He is clearly a knowledgeable guy, however I don't think I learned as much in this half of the course. He seemed to overestimate the digestibility of the course which definitely shown through on test days. Ultimately, he was still a good teacher and the class was interesting.

Prof Stainton gives a lot of reading as supplements to the lectures where you talk about the main material. He's a bit of a fast talker but he posts the slides. Tries to bring in alternative viewpoints on Hinduism (eg. music, poetry), and his lectures are very engaging and thoughtful. Keep up with the content and you'll be fine. Great prof :)

Hes not bad but its very difficult if you're not 100% interested in the material he's presenting. He talks in big words and often uses complicated explanations. Also, talks pretty fast so you really have to keep up. But he does take breaks 2-3 times in class for questions! Its a memorization heavy class so as long as u know ur stuff, u will be fine

He is very passionate and clearly knowledgeable on Hinduism. His lectures were interesting but overwhelming; definitely not Introduction level! I found myself studying for days on end to memorize the endless terms and traditions required to graze past his midterm. On the midterm day, everyone seemed dumbfounded by the specificity of his questions.

prof was very knowledgeable and eager to assist student's interests and questions. i liked how he connected hinduism in the past and contemporary hinduism. course was pretty reading heavy but prof stainton made the content more manageable and clear. great prof, interesting course

I absolutely loved the Prof.Stainton. So passionate about his subject, but also his students. went out of his way to learn names and answer every question. really enjoyed the way he presented the subject. You can get by without doing all the readings, but at least skim them.
This was by far my hardest class this semester. Would not recommend unless Hindu Goddesses is your passion in life.
amazing lecturer. always there to answer questions during tutorials and exams are very fair.
Presents the material in a clear manner so that the textbook is not needed. Funny prof!
like an angel fair/easy test elegant  caring best prof

Great lecturer and exam was super fair. She didn't really have any questions on the final, but her midterm was not hard if you do all the practice questions available. If you go to office hours, she is super nice and helpful and smart.
She is a very sweet person, and she explains ok, but her lecture slides are horrendous. 125 slides with 10 identical slides with barely any notes on them.  Forgot to mention some critical details.
I originally thought she wasn't very good, but after writing the 2nd midterm I realized she did a very thorough job preparing us, and made the midterm really fair.

She seems really nice and is easy to listen to, but the way she lays out/presents the course material is not the best. Khan Academy teaches it in a more logical fashion than she does. You can tell she's brilliant and very passionate about organic chem, just not very easy to follow sometimes. Would take her class again if it were smaller.

Really knows how to teach. Explains things very clearly, never expects you to know a huge amount which is great for building confidence in you. Very enthusiastic, genuinely loves what she's teaching and teaching itself.
She's so into her class and is so engaging with her students 3 also, she's great at explaining the specifics in her office hours. Brilliant woman.

If you understand the basics of chemistry, you can look up whatever you need in order to succeed in the class in conjunction with her lecture recordings. Her lecture recordings are more than enough to get an A in the class, although the last parts of material take a day on its own to internalize, memorize, and understand (DNA chemistry)
Professor Mitri's lecture notes are amazing! He comes well-prepared to every class.  His pace is a bit fast so you gotta be very careful. The final is really long so you gotta be really fast
Really great and very human.
Useless

Hans only gives 4 lectures in biol206 but they were the best 4 lectures of the class. The material is different and engaging and refreshing after many weeks of statistics. He explains concepts in comparative anatomy well and the labs that go with his material are very easy compared to the other labs in the course. I would definitely recommend him.

Hans is great, probably one of the smartest profs at McGill. BIOL 352 was awesome when I took it, got to dissect crocodilians in the lab portion of the course. If you're into it, highly recommend BIOL 573 field course with him too. Couple weeks digging up dinosaurs in the badlands for the same amount of credit as any other BIOL course.

good prof. Sometimes it was hard to understand how he explained macroevolution concepts (esp bc im not so interested in the topic) but most of the stuff made sense. If he can speak more clearly (mumbles sometimes) it would be even better!

Really passionate, interesting lectures and fair questions on the exam. Plus there's not a lot of extra reading. His concepts were sometimes presented in a bit of a scattered way...overall though, really good and really helpful - his passion for his area of study spreads easily to his students. plus he's a total fox.

He's a super sweet prof and he's super helpful during and after class... much better then his conceited teaching partner. He's very organized... overall, I really enojoyed going to class... final questions from his section were very fair!
Sometimes a little sketchy with explaining concepts, but he seems so nice and his exam questions are fair so he's cool.
No Comments

Larsi Marsi is not so bad, except that he needs to work on his tone and pitch while presenting. He frequently assumes that we all understand him the first time around! we dont and so he needs to go make sincere attempts to make us understand ,like present us with new slides with more info etc.Its funny; i have caught him staring at me some times!
has a hard time explaining some difficult concept, TA seems a though understand the material better. larsson is a funny man, passionate about macroevolution.

Loved his enthusiasm, obviously very dedicated to macroevolution and vertebrate evolution. Liked how he laughed quietly about paikia (etc.) to himself. Will be great prof, needs a bit more confidence.

There is a difference between constructive criticism and inapropriate, hostile comments that do nothing but discourage. This course has no prerequisites, and many students like me have never taken philosophy before. Thanks to the TA's rather nasty comments, I am sure many, including myself, won't take it again.

This class only works for someone who thinks exactly like her. The Professor is a really tough grader, and my TA did not know what was going on for half of the time. I have NEVER experienced such borderline malicious feedback that is not helpful AT ALL. Even if you do all the readings and try hard, be ready to have your sense of self destroyed.

tough grader, not because she is philosophically more demanding to her students, but only because you really have to write what she thinks is right. She does not accept any other interpretations or viewpoints. Among sooo many philosophy classes I have taken, is she really objective, as she should be, in her grading?

Professor Sharp is great - really knowledgeable and passionate about philosophy. Her lectures aren't the most engaging, sometimes too long spent on class discussion, so I would definitely recommend doing the readings properly for her classes. If you take a class with her, I'd say take a 300 or 400-level one- she's much better with a smaller group.
Absolutely terrible. Made me think of quitting philosophy. Disorganized and insightless classes. Her classes are highly partial, and unless you agree with her, forget about getting a good grade.
Made me reconsider taking philosophy classes. Unclear and hard-to-follow lectures. Ambiguous and unreasonable grading makes students suffer. Take a different philosophy class instead of her classes.

Really kind and accessible in office hours, but unfortunately not the best lecturer, constantly seeming overwhelmed and rushed. Encourages participation too much, meaning we never got through the lecture material and had to finish reading lecture slides outside of class almost every week. Readings were very dry - maybe avoid this course!

Prof. Sharp is an excellent philosopher and equally excellent lecturer (I'm quite confused by the other reviews) who clearly disseminates the relevant material. She is neither overly harsh, as many say here, nor overly easy (as should be the case). She is both incredibly accessible and incomparably kind and considerate. Her assignments are fair.
excellent philosopher, but avoid her class
Hasana Sharp is a very tough professor with very boring lectures. Even though she provides class PowerPoints and detailed feedback on assignments they are absolutely useless.
Very boring and unengaging. taught the entire course through example problems. Very boring class for such an interesting topic. Very unorganized.

He seems nice but is ineffective at explaining even basic concepts. I attended every class and learned nothing. He relies on group work rather than teaching, and we're left to figure everything out on our own. He rarely shows solutions and even struggles himself. He is also completely unresponsive to emails. Midterms have only 3 unseen questions.
nice guy who tries to get to know his students but gives tough exams. The material gets real after the 2nd midterm, be prepared for linear algebra, differential systems, dynamic programming
(D1) - Very unengaging professor, the 3h lecture also didn't help. Material is however very interesting, midterms were easy and the final was ok. Do the problem sets and you'll be ok.

Course contents are as difficult as they are interesting. Midterms can appear deceptively simple; do expect surprises in the final exam. The second half of the course is when 452 really begins. Do not let the first half fool you.
He is just bad. Reading the pre-made pdf should not be considered teaching at all. I learned more from the TA than him.

That review mentioning he was talking about his wife and kids, that straight up never happened. His lectures are hard because they are very abstract but once you do the examples everything is chill. Just make sure you can do all the problems given in class and specifically the conferences and you'll be fine.

Professor Benchekroun is a great professor who is an expert in his field and clearly knows what he is talking about. He is also very caring of his students, and he is not opposed to staying in touch with them after the course is finished. He does have high standards when it comes to the material, which is not easy.
The most boring professor I ever had. The class is poorly paced: the first weeks are way too slow and easy, the last few weeks are difficult. He is difficult to reach over email.

Hes so nice! exams were super fair and he explains really well. His classes are a bit boring and he doesn't like when people talk but he's a great teacher. His exams were copy paste the exercises he gave us

Dr. Heather Goad is one of the most organized, prepared, knowledgeable and down-to-earth professors I have ever had (and I'm an older student doing a second degree in linguistics). Her assignments complement her amazing lectures and make the material crystal clear. If you are serious about linguistics, be sure to take at least one course with her.

SHE IS AN EXCELLENT LECTURER. Heather is the most accessible professor that I have ever had at Mcgill. She is always willing to help and explain. You can have a decent grade as long as you understand all course materials and conference materials. Assignments are challenging but the exam is not unexpectedly difficult.

Prof Goad is super passionate about what she teaches and very caring. She is not out to trick you, but sometimes her questions are a bit ambiguous. She is very accessible and always ready to help. Can get a bit side tracked, but she will adjust what she tests/deadlines accordingly. Her exams are not hard if you know the material. A total sweetheart
The lectures were interesting but the exams required "keywords" or you'll be losing points. The grading is fair.

Professor Goad is really kind, caring, and genuinely loves teaching. The material can be difficult to grasp, but never hesitate to reach out to her. I had her in the same semester for 331 and 355 and still attended every lecture!
Wonderful and super accessible! Her classes are hard, but Heather is always there to help. She works too hard, and deserves a break.
She is a great lecturer and has made the class really fun!!

She's really passionate about what she teaches and super friendly. However, some of her assignments are extremely hard, especially if you've only taken LING 201 (it felt like she was asking for way beyond our skill level). Her exams on the other hand were pretty fair though so if you do good on them you can still end up with an ok grade.

Interesting but tough course, definitely recommend taking it with a friend or two to study together! The assignments require a lot of time and effort (like 6+ hours on one really hard question), while the quizzes and exams are tricky but manageable. I had no clue about how I did on the midterm or final until the marks were released.
good lecturer but tough grader. the exam is quite difficult and she hardly curves. don't skip classes.

I had two classes with Mrs Hart and she is a kind and passionate teacher. She does have an unusual approach to the classic university curriculum, which might not suit everyone. She encourages students to self-reflect and participate in thoughtful discussions rather than just giving theory. If you are a curious and avid learner, it should be fine :)

I took a few courses with Prof. Hart over the years. I always found her teaching style to be extremely empathetic, with plenty of practical experiences to share from her years as a palliative care clinician. My peers also trusted that we could go to her for support with sensitive issues, such as inter-professional challenges. Recommend.
Disrespectful, unprofessional, patronizing, and incredibly racist. Her treatment of my cohort soured my experience as a graduate student at McGill. Stay away if you can.
Heather is an incredible prof. Very passionate about her content and provided clear expectations for exams with some in-class examples. She also just seems like a chill person.
Very monotonous, slides could be more structured

Prof McBride really cares about her student's success. Her class really aims at preparing us for what research will be like later. She uses a lot of examples from recent papers and address current controversies in the field during her lectures. Her exams can be harsh, but they are fair and she is clear about what she expects.

Prof McBride is very respected in her field and her lectures are super interesting if you enjoy cellular trafficking. She grades fairly for the paper and is explicit about what she tests on. Although the lecture content is sometimes on the heavy side, you can do well in this course by keeping up with reviewing the lecture slides.

His lectures are boring and he is extremely difficult to understand as he mumbles. His instructions for assignments/the midterm are very unclear. It's not a hard class to pass, but if you can take another prof I highly recommend!

you have to teach the class with ur group because besides putting slides up and then putting you in groups to discuss, he won't talk. you have a presentation where you need to teach the class again on a specific reading. it's boring and i found myself leaving class early everytime. he won't notice either btw bc he falls asleep during presentations.

He is so hard to understand and often mumbles what he says. His class is not interesting and the way he teaches is so uninspiring. If you can switch out and take the class with another prof 100% do that.

His class is really confusing, his explanations are mediocre at best (since the students present the readings RIGHT AFTER HIM, you'll either fall asleep or understand but only thanks to the students). If this class is not mandatory for you, please do not take it! A waste of your time!
so hard to understand what he wants from us

This prof will only teach half of each class and relies on student seminars for the other half. He reads off slides and barely engages with material. In student discussions, he either asks 'what' follow-up questions or nods along. If attendance wasn't mandatory, you could pass this class without showing up (except for your presentation).

He was extremely confusing and boring. I did not enjoy this class. He never explained assignments and just expected you to do it and understand it from what is written in the syllabus. I would NOT take him again.

Unclear lectures as well as his answers. Often changed our syllabus after we started. Students my class were treated unfairly; could have been avoided if he listened to students. When we presented he didnt paying attention because his feedback said things were missing in our presentation but were already included. As a future teacher I'm let down

students are basically teaching the class through their presentations. instructions are never clear. course outline wasn't clear until one of my classmates went to see the department chair. 
this class is passable but might be a headache

A mandatory course that is quite hard to follow. Each class, the professor has to address a new problem that has arisen from his lack of preparation for the course. We deal with philosophers and he has students teach the class seminar style with little to no instruction. Unorganized and Unclear are the two words that come to mind.

Really enjoyed the classes. He's very passionate about what he teaches. The lectures are clear and coherent to understand. Go to his classes (& pay attention) and you'll most likely do well in the course. Funny and very approachable character. Made me learn so much (w/ ease) about Canada's FP even though this was my 1st class in Canada's politics.
Excellent, clear professor with very reasonable expectations. Didn't love his multiple choice assessments, but fact pattern final was very fair and his classes were engaging and comprehensible.
Hilarious, kind and caring, really focuses on cases and the law not very theoretical

Pretty open to student feedback and has clear and reasonable expectations. Would not recommend attending online if he's lecturing in person because it can get confusing. Otherwise, great lecturer. Would prefer him to any of the other contract profs any day.
Dedek is good. :)

This man was simply the best teacher I have had at law school. He uses the Socratic method just enough to keep the class stimulated, and his questions are precise enough that they rarely lead to long or irrelevant answers. And, when hes speaking, his lectures are perfect, shining models of efficiency and economy. I give him all the stars.

Excellent professor, perfect for 1L. Very manageable workload, fair grades. Clear explanations and powerpoints, he cares for students' success and wellbeing. He values participation (it can boost your grade), so show up to class - you won't regret it, Dedek is a gem who actually makes you look forward to 8:30AM lectures. 10/10 would recommend.

A truly excellent professor. The man is brilliant and knows the material like the back of his hand. Dedek is a genuinely nice guy who is approachable and makes the class interesting and fun. He assigns a very manageable reading load and grades fairly. Highly recommended.

Great prof, very smart, very relaxed and good-humoured. He fell behind with the syllabus, but in a good way -spent more time at the beginning, when the concepts were new, and caught up afterwards. Also, he gave us a brilliant synopsis for breach of contract - I followed that model for summaries in all my other courses. And yeah, very elegant.

Lectures become monotonous and offer little room for discussion. Nice guy and approachable outside of class but somewhat shy. It appears it's either a love or hate sort of relationship. Nothing terrible, but nothing will blow you away.
Pretty good class. Actual case analysis, clear descriptions on what we will be reading, helpful class exercise before the test. Stylish, young, and attractive with a cute accent. Yup, good class.

I took 245 and 249 w Darmon -- my favorite lecturer in the Math Dept. He is wildly entertaining. His lectures are terribly disorganised. At the same time, he presents material in a very concise way. Never found his off hr helpful, but he's a joy to talk to. Memorise and understand everything he ever writes in lecture to prep for exams.

Took him for MATH 249. Decent lecturer but sometimes panders to those with knowledge outside of the prerequisites of the course. Assignments were pretty difficult, start them soon. Midterm was insanely easy, very computational. Final was much harder (more on par with expected difficulty) so make sure you can understand and prove key theorems.
Fascinating and clear lectures. Biweekly assignments were long and tough but interesting and doable with effort and working with others.

He absolutely knows algebra. The teaching style, despite one other saying how ridiculous the workload is, is engaging, prompting you to think and participate in class. The only way you get better in math is practice. the final was indeed a bit out of the blue, but still manageable and requires you to think a bit under the pressure in studio2.

Took 4 credit courses with way less work. Spent 7 days straight working solely on the last assignment (topics not covered in lecture) & didnt even finish it by the end. Had only taken 4 courses this sem and the ridiculous time needed for the last assignment completely messed up how I planned on studying for all my finals. Would not take again.

Darmon is super caring and comprehensive in his lectures, answering all questions in detail. He has a deep understanding of the content; class is very proof-based but expected in an Honours course. Take a class with him if you get the chance!

Lectures were very proof heavy and I barely got anything out of them. Assignments were interesting, very proof based for the most part but definitely interesting. Final was relatively easy, at least compared to what I was expecting. Wouldn't take again though just because I hated his lectures.
Great Prof, very clear and understanding. Makes hard topics seem very easy. Would answer your doubts 100 times.

You can tell he's really sincerely invested in the material, and cares about actually teaching it over just regurgitating proofs. Interesting stuff, too. 

The class can get super abstract, and his notes are a bit meandering, but overall this is one of the best math courses I've taken. Highly recommend.

Pretty disorganized lectures that don't help all that much with the assignments. Very harsh grader, generally doesn't give partial marks unless your answer is just barely off the correct answer. Doesn't explain why you have marks removed on a question, will tell you to review the material if you ask him for clarification.

Wonderful prof. Very funny and respected guy, and i love his lectures. attendance is not mandatory and you can do fine just reading the slides he posts, but i think the lectures are the best part of his course. highly recommend if you want an understanding prof and an easy A.
He's fabulous

Horner's class was the easiest ive ever taken at McGill. You get free points for basically being a warm body in class! He's a very easy grader, hilarious and connects with students super well. Gives great advice and takes entire classes to give advice on grad school and future employment. I would take him in a heartbeat
Huge help to speak to about grad school applications and the GMAT! That's the only reason I went to his office. His course was easy to follow / clear.
It is fine, but cannot say that the lectures are very interesting.

Super great prof and nice guy. He likes telling stories and giving random and unrelated lectures most of the time. The prof teaches one day a week and groups present the readings the other day of the week, essentially teaching the class.

My favourite course at McGill even though I'm not an econ major. The first few weeks of current economic problems were basically a crash course to get everyone up to speed. Very welcoming and peaceful vibes.
Boring lectures, prof was ok but weird jokes. Too many readings and assignments.

Professor Horner was an exceptional professor; very inspiring and funny. Participation matters but you are still able to get points by answering online discussion posts, which was a great way to accommodate students who didn't want to speak in front of everyone. Lot of readings but evaluations are not hard. 100% would recommend him!
Nice chill guy. Basically just gives everyone an A- or B+. Very dry lectures. Nothing to study.

Mr. Tan is an awesome professor. I took ACCT451 with him. The class content is extremely interesting and pushes you to work on frontier subjects. The class is fast paced and content heavy, but Mr. Tan is caring and will make sure that everybody is on the same page. I had a wonderful experience working under his guidance and will never forget it!
Extremely disorganized professor

Took him for ACCT401 (not 434), very caring. No textbook, and while the lectures can be be very content-heavy, he makes them engaging and mostly discusses real-world situations, meaning for the midterm, apart from the actual concepts, you won't have to memorize everything he's discussed. Even without an accounting background I recommend the course.

Prof Tan is a really sweet and amazing person. the only problem would be his style of teaching might weird for most people and slides a bit confusing, and he really likes to talk about fraud. but you can always trust him to go above and beyond for his students. he is super intelligent as well. I am shocked he has so low rating.

The worst course that I have ever taken at McGill. The professor wanted to put so many contents in one course but he had no idea how to construct it. It is a coding-based course but asked you to read tons of long papers and submitted a summary every week. He is also bad at teaching coding, but his coding assignments were super hard by using SAS.

I got Hongpin in Fall 2019, he is a nice professor. However when we ask questions the answers he gives can be really confusing. Just read the textbook and you'll be okay. (heavy work) There are many tests, (if I remember 1 quizz a week) which are really time consuming for this class. If you can take another acct prof take it but if not he is fine
I would definitely take him again!
I have learned a lot with him. Learning Intro to Accounting with him will help you to gain concrete fundamental knowledge about accounting. I would definitely want to take him again.
Best professor I've ever had at McGill. Professor Tan cares about students a lot and explain things clearly. I have learned a lot from him. I recommend taking Intro to Accounting with Prof. Tan.
A great and caring prof to start your Core classes at Desautels. Intro to accounting by itself isn't really fine, but the prof tried to make it interesting
Really boring class, and class will never ended on time. He just try to squeeze everything into your mind. Bad experience.

Class is dull and boring, but you can easily get A if you understand the basic concepts & calculations. He is very knowledgeable, and willing to answer questions. The course load is not high compared to other courses I had. Recommended if you wanna boost your GPA without spending too much time on memorizing/studying. Easy A.
Just a poor fellor trying to survive
highly knowledgable
Reads off slides, uses an autograder that does not work, do not take this course

Over 30% of the grade came from projects, for which we had designated weekly time with a TA. Her final and midterm were entirely MCQ, and as long as you had basic syntax knowledge and either read the slides or went to class, they were fine. Questions were 60% easy, 30% med, and 10% hard (her words). She also holds reviews leading up to the tests.
Her tutorials are basically impossible and her final was long... She tests you on small details...
I really enjoyed the course, and liked the professor!

very politically conscious with a humanitarian focus (uncommon at McGill). Content is interesting but he is actually the worst prof I've ever had. Not nearly as bad as other reviews say. Explained concepts really well and made pretty funny jokes to break up the potentially boring topic of ethics. Juan is a great professor, he is intelligent, kind, and inspiring. No matter you want to do analytics or not as your career, his class is a must-take! He makes it fun, easy, and he puts a lot of efforts into that. He is definitely a gem and the most impressive professor I can remember.
His lectures were probably the most engaging online lectures I've ever had. Very well-done, funny but covered the data science content effectively.
He is super awesome! You can tell he loves teaching as soon as you take his course.
Favorite prof so far. Juan knows how to make the most tedious subject arresting

Juan is honestly one of the best profs I've had at McGill. He is extremely caring, his lectures are hilarious, and he manages to make really heavy content seem interesting and manageable. Highly recommended.
One of the most inspiring human beings you will meet. Cute curls is the icing on the cake.
Excellent

Juan does everything possible to make the learning experience as engaging and insightful as possible. Great teacher! I love his slides. :D "This is an art, not a science!"

The best prof I have had at McGill. He teaches the subject in a fun way and ensures to keep everyone engaged. His presentations all go beyond what i have seen from other professors and he is very well versed in the subjects he teaches.
Assignments worth 5% each, tedious, useless, multi-hour repetitive work each question, mindless you dont learn a thing from doing assignments. Lectures are just spent reading the powerpoint.

I actually had a great time in 550 with Jackie. I found that his lectures were interesting and he had a sense of humor, and I rarely found myself feeling bored by the material. Pretty good Prof. Course was well structured. Assignments weren't overly difficult and exams weren't too bad either as they were take homes. Lectures were decent.
Pretty generous Prof. No exams and plenty of places to get free points. Interesting course material too.
The requirements of the assignments are very unclear. The TAs are incompetent and do not have a proper understanding of the course material. Avoid taking this course with Jackie.

class in general is super easy. People who had sufficient math background should breeze through, especially those who took classes in the math department. everytime a student has a question notice how he says yaaah, was worth going to class just to class to hear him say that, good prof all around

Jackie's an awesome dude and amazing professor. Basically just reads the slides made by another professor. Assignments are long and unclear. Too much material squeezed at the end of the semester. Final was fair.

This is his second year teaching this course but he just read other prof's slides in the most boring tone ever ( If you think Vybihal is the most boring prof in comp sci then you should definitely check on this one ). Assignment gradings are confusing, material's heavy. GitHub is your friend.

This is one of the worst teachers ever. You can barely understand what he says. He is very disorganized and fails to upload the slides until just a few days before the in-class exam. He is a great lecturer and is great in class. The textbook is not too great but the in person lecturws make up for it

I've taken three courses with Jake and enjoyed every one, but this was probably my favourite. He is  a brilliant man, but prefers a didactic approach to teaching. Very difficult to hear. Mark based on 2 tests and 1 group presentation.

Great lectures and good slides, very knowledgeable. It's clear that he thinks deeply about why he's assigning work and how it's assigned. I've taken three of his classes and find that I learn more from Blanc classes than most, if not all other classes I've taken at McGill.

Professor Blanc is one of my favorite professors so far at McGill. The lectures are engaging, and he and the TAs gave helpful feedback on assignments. This class was the best one I've taken so far at McGill. Dr. Blanc was respectful, joyful and happy to teach us about Latin American history. The map quizzes were straightforward and easy to get 100%. The quizzes were more challenging, but they were a practice for the final paper, for which I got an A. NO FINAL EXAM! The class was very enjoyable.

I would love to talk about how amazing this prof is. Blanc always showed up to class with a smile on his face and completely prepared. The TAs showed up to every class, and always answered questions. Assignments had clear criteria. Feedback on quizzes and classwork was constructive. Would absolutely take again.
What an amazing teacher, he's always there for his students. The guidelines for evaluations and papers were clearly explained and he is so sweeettt !!

Prof Blanc is an amazing person, he truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Him and his TAs provide great feedback on all assignments which if you use to improve, will help you immensely. The class itself is very engaging content wise, but does involve a lot of reading and writing many papers and quizzes.
Really interesting class
Sweetest teacher ever. The class was interesting, so many topics covered with a lot of content. You need to be ready to write and read. Him and his TAs gave really good feedback for you to improve.
second midterm was very hard. lectures are very fast pace did not understand anything. overall aweful

Honestly the best lecturer I've ever had: inspirational, very organized, and easy to understand. I don't understand the bad reviews, he gives amazing feedback, the grading isn't more strict than other profs, and there's not more reading than other poli classes.
My favorite class I have taken so far! The course was extremely well structured (very satisfying, imo), constantly having me see each side of an argument clearly.

This was the best course I have taken so far. Professor Levi was great, and the lectures were so interesting. Excellent person to go to if you need something to get done in the department. Rather baffling as to how she ended up teaching/coaching most of the things that she does
Really nice, smart guy. Jacques is really caring about his students, and is very clear on what is expected for the exam. I would take this guy again in a heart beat.

Dr Debruille is always ready to answer any questions, he is very helpful.

I had Dr Debruille as a teacher and PhD supervisor. In addition to offering daily support and guidance to my work for 5 years, he provided a stimulating and friendly environment in the lab. His teaching in the course "Current topics in Neuroscience" was excellent and this course was really great.

Prof Adamski is a funny, clear, and interesting lecturer that manages to make a very dry field of law (Business Associations) fun. (Yes this is a McGill law course and it will be curved...)
Fantastic prof, fantastic guy.  Definitely worth his office hours for the extra essay help.  He provides ALL possible midterm questions WAY in advance, so no surprises.

I love him. He's adorable and extremely helpful and witty. Although lectures can be potentially dull, they move quickly and his enthusiasm is contagious. He has a passion for the English language that inspires students to dedicate time and effort to learning. Really fantastic.
Basically copies Jessica Riddell's style. Unreasonable marker. His lectures can get a bit dry, but he tries. Good selection of material, though.

Extremely helpful & friendly and very clear lecturer. I enjoyed this class and found it really useful. See him during office hours to get advice on your essays. An A is not impossible but you definitely need to be a very strong writer. Proofread your work thoroughly.

Great prof! don't waste a chance to take a class with him! he's funny and a great lecturer. He is the coolest guy ever and has a great sense of humor. He loves it when students ask him for help, and is extremely helpful. Brilliant, funny, keeps it real. Much more self-aware than other professors in the department. Knows pop culture better than most of his students. Best prof I've had at McGill.
Funny and knows films!

One of the best lecturers I've had in 3 years: passionate abt content & knows how to teach it. Very opinionated.

Prof. Crippen showed daily that he is super excited and committed to the material and the study of Indigenous languages in general. AVOID! Prof CANNOT explain complex concepts.Doesn't reply to emails. Un-understandable handwriting and notes. Interrupts himself, students have to correct him. Yes he can be disorganised. BUT i enjoyed 408 once I got over the whole blackboard no slides thing. Incredible, super kind and fun professor. The content is challenging but manageable if you attend lectures and keep up with the textbook. EW is one of the great theoretical econ profs at McG. Pay attention and attend lectures; you will do well. I am an average student and got an A-. The content of the class is very interesting, so if you are going to study outside of classes because the topic interests you, take it. He gives the impression of being a bit stiff, but is quite funny. The lectures were interesting, though dense. If you engage and ask questions, it is quite easy to do well. Lectures are content heavy and so interesting I never skipped. Textbook is optional and imo not necessary. Lots of mandatory primary source readings, found them interesting and fairly manageable. krapfl is clearly an expert in his field, but often couldn't see the forest for the trees in lectures, getting bogged down in random details and not illustrating the broader point (not helped by basically empty slides). Prof. Krapfl is truly an amazing and inspiring teacher ! I really enjoyed going to every lecture as someone interested in the topic. He and his TAs are fair graders. I HIGHLY recommend taking his classes if the topic interests you.

Great professor, expert in his field. The platonic ideal of a history professor.
Such an amazing teacher. Really interesting readings and descriptive and extensive lectures. Offers a lecture guide each class with dates, names, etc. Super kind and inspiring.

Expert in his field of Eastern European history. Interesting lectures, talks really fast and can be hard to follow if you are not already familiar with the content. Wish I could take his classes next semester but he wont be at McGill I guess.

A really great course and profesor.

Very useful class. Excellent professor.
He is a very good lecturer and organizes his classes well. I learned a lot in this course.
Amazing course and professor. He cares about what you learn, and even though he is very busy, he will find the time to help with career advice, etc.

Excellent course and professor. He is a hard grader but fair. He emphasizes being thorough and professional all the time when doing engineering work and reports which I think is very important (and not emphasized enough in courses given by other professors at McGill).

Very interesting and useful class. I learned about topics that I was not familiar with before that are important in engineering (stakeholder engagement, analyzing problems from a systems perspective, adaptive management, etc.).

I genuinely love this Prof. He's very good at explaining the materials and i honestly loved going to his class. Tough grader but ngl it lowkey pushed me to be more motivated to study.

Great professor!

Buy a textbook (you'll need it!), and don't be surprised if some of the material on the exams isn't actually covered in the textbook.
Very good class!
Boring lecturer, writes HORRIBLE exams and assignments, doesn't reply to emails. If you can avoid her, do it. If not, definitely buy the textbook. You'll need it.

Too smart to be teaching this intro level class. Appeared interested @ beginning of semester, but seemed to tire by the end. Applies concepts and techniques used to real life uses, but doesn't go into detail about how it actually works. Assessments poorly written (possibly due to language barrier). Textbook is your friend! Lab comp. taught me more.

She seemed interested and excited to teach 287 at the beginning of the course, but I think it was a mix of negative class response and the wear of the semester that made her less responsive/eager to be teaching. I'm sure she's good at what she does, but she doesn't do a fantastic job of explaining things. It was her first year, I'll give her that.

Honestly, she is super sweet and all, but one thing I would say is she takes a while to put things up on my courses; we would have to remind her. Other than that, if we would ask her to push a due date she would and was super flexible and understanding that we had other classes and things to do. I'd take her again

So caring and sweet but get ready to question your entire academic career. This class aims to prepare you for the EETC exam yet we were never taught anything that could help till the last possible second. Lots of grading issues as well. Also would chance instructions and worth of assignments at the last second or after the fact.

Dr. Metallic is sweet, but she is very disorganized. Assignment instructions were incredibly unclear and asking for clarification did not help. One classmate asked how many sources we were supposed to use in an assignment and she answered that she did not know. She changed an assignment from being worth 1% to 5% weeks after it was due.

One of the best professors I've had. His feedback is practical and directly applicable to real life. Classes are efficient, hands-on, and actually make you apply what you learn. Expectations are pretty clear, he's very logical, and easy to reach when needed. Highly recommend if you want to actually gain useful, real-world skills.

One of the best profs i had in McGill. He is very fair when it comes to grading, gives a very clear rubric specific to each assignment, give SUPER detailed feedback that help you to do better in the next assignment. He doesn't give grades just for the sake of the ave. to be B+. The lectures were super fun and interactive.

Prof Jared was great; really cares about entrepreneurship and his students. I really don't understand the poor review below—of course he's not going to assign peer-reviewed research articles for a business class. If you expect/want that kind of rigorous analysis take a poli-sci class or something. A bit of a tough grader, but a very fun class!

Professor Jared has very fun and engaging lectures that connect all class concepts to real world applications. The journey he takes you through to building a business is super interesting and guided. He is organized, and while he can sometimes have high expectations with grading, he is always open to giving very thorough feedback. Would recommend!!
Attendance is mandatory but worth it! Lectures are engaging and interactive. He keeps things real! Grading can be tough but he is very open to giving feedback.
Amazing class and amazing Prof! Super entertaining and interactive. I recommend it to anyone interested in entrepreneurship!

Jared Lee likes to teach in a "fun way," which turns out not to be very academic at all. His enthusiasm would make him a great middle school teacher, but his shallow academic understanding leads to a "busy work" class setting. If you don't like reading primary research and prefer a magazine-style "top 5 methods for xyz," this class is for you!

Jared made this class very engaging all semester. He has a good mix of lectures and interactive exercises and nurtured a nice classroom dynamic. He sometimes would make jokes out of nowhere which would take me a a while to process but were really funny, and much appreciated. Gave really clear feedback too, and would be willing to explain further.

Jared Lee is a funny professor who is clearly passionate about what he teaches. He always tries to make his classes entertaining by developing games related to the content covered. Although some assignments, specifically the group ones, can be a bit demanding, the grading criteria are particularly clear and you'll do great if you respect them!

Overall GOAT Prof. Group project is fun and challenges you to be creative. Lectures are engaging. Some of the smaller assignments were graded pretty subjectively IMO, though. Def would take this Prof again
best prof ever, goes through details very well and easy to follow even if no knowledge fo coding before
Awesome guy with awesome course.

While I'm not sure if he teaches AEPH 112 anymore, he is undoubtedly one of the most helpful teachers I have met at McGill. More than willing to reexplain concepts and give example both during and after class. Class overall was not incredibly diffcult, any struggles were more so with studying and taking notes at the college level as a freshman.

His lectures might seem slow at the beginning, but keep showing up to them and the exams will feel easy. He only teaches this class in the winter so make sure to take it then, the fall prof is considerably worse from what I've heard.
Loves to answer questions. Really interesting computing labs. Always looking for feedback from students, and adjusting the class work to our needs and interests.

Very caring, understanding and knowledgeable professor. Met with us as much as needed to make sure we understood the material. Open to feedback (constantly asked us throughout the semester how he could improve/restructure the class).
Gave lots of practice problems and made sure you knew what was going to be tested during exams. Nice prof and easy to reach outside of lectures and labs.

I had a high school physics teacher who didn't know any physics. The class consisted of students showing up, only to, ironically, teach the teacher. Compared to her, Jasmin is a fly on the wall. He somehow lowered that impressive bar. He does not try to act like he knows how to teach. His honesty about his lack of teaching ability is honourable.
Very poorly organized and makes even simple things confusing. He tries to put the bare minimum effort in to the class. the ta's are the only reason I even understand a bit of this class.

This teacher lives in his own bubble. The material isn't even that hard, but he takes it to another level of difficulty. Never-ending assignments, poorly edited and confusing slides, and 91 badly worded challenging questions on the final. Not a fun class overall. Good luck if you have him (you'll need it).

So bad students got together to send him a clear and respectful email spelling out exactly how were struggling and simple things he could change to help improve our understanding - he ignored it completely lol he does not care

Jasmin is completely incapable of teaching. He speeds through content by just reading off poorly made slides and can't answer questions. Assignments are so long it took 2 months for the first one to be graded. They also require complicated coding that he doesn't know how to do himself, so he says "just use AI." Also no crib sheets on the final.

A despicabIe experience. Even the bio dept. are mad with how horribIe he is at his job. Can't teach, gives wrong answers to questions we ask+unbelievable assignments. I would have dropped, but there's no other teacher for this class next semester either. All of us can barely comprehend 20% of the material, 80% of which is thanks to the 8:30AM TA.

He spent 40 minutes on the entirety of the COMP208 content and expects us to know how to code in Python for assignments. His lectures are jam packed with information and his assignments are long and difficult. Feedback is absent or minimal and given a month later. Words cannot describe how bad the situation is.
Zero feedback on an assignment that took all of us 15+ hours... Didn't even get the grade back until almost 2 months later.
retire dawg

No logical progression between concepts. It makes it difficult to remember how to use each test and how they relate to each other. Needs to improve provided simple examples and working up to how to effectively use data to craft an argument.

If you want to fall asleep listening to left-wing rhetoric, this is the class for you. Every lecture quickly starts to feel the same. Don't bother asking questions as this professor is unwilling to offer a succinct answer or deviate from the lesson plan

He is evidently passionate about what he teaches, and I found his lectures to be fun. I prefer being graded by few things so it was a plus that there's only a midterm and a final. He provides a very specific breakdown of the questions which is helpful, but still the questions were too detail-focused and required memorization of a lot of statistics.

If you take any review please listen to mine. It is no longer a bird class. This has only 2 test that are all based on memorizing very minute details. If u want to take an intro to soci class take 210 l, this class will not make u excited for sociology. He is a wonderful prof but as a response to McGill his class is hard now! It will not b easy A

He is very helpful and the class expectations are clear. Honestly I appreciate having no papers to write, as the only grades are the midterm/final. His lecture slides are all posted and attendance is not mandatory but I would recommend you go as he gives extra info that might be on the exams. Overall very straightforward and cool professor

Prof. Carmichael is simply put: amazing!! It was my first year at McGill, and this course really cemented that I had made the right choice in choosing Sociology as my major. Although the class is test-heavy (40% midterm, 60% final) the lectures and the textbook prepare you extremely well for the tests. HIGHLY recommend!!

Prof. Carmicheal is amazing. Your grade is divided by solely the midterm (worth 40%) and the final (worth 60%). He is truly so interesting and the class material really helps you understand current issues in society. The textbook was very easy to read and understand as well. Highly recommend as an elective or if you're a SOCI student like me!

I think that Professor Carmichael was very interesting. Def cool material in the course, just not a fan of the way he tests. One midterm, and One exam 50/50. So no room for mistakes and lots of memorization. Because of this was not very successful in his class. Still think he is a decent prof though.

The prof is a good lecturer and a very nice person. however, the workload for this class is RIDICULOUSLY high. expects you to memorize a bunch of statistics and also expects you to memorize the textbook, which is pretty heavy in content. a lot of unnecessary knowledge that is expected to be memorized

Jason Carmichael is an absolute beauty. He is the coolest and dopest homie prof that I have. 10/10 would take his Soci 250 class, you do have to remember some stats for the midterm but, easy price to pay for an absolute god of a teacher. Guy also really likes his Tree/Carrot diagram btw.

truly such an amazing prof!! This class is a favorite not only bc the material is so interesting but he really engages the students and is clearly passionate about what he's teaching and its infectious. It's test heavy, one 40% midterm one 60% final with big emphasis on memorized statistics. Thats the big con of the course but totally doable.

fully a political theory class. he doesn't have slides or recordings, just rambles while students scramble to take notes of everything. readings are tedious and class material gets repetitive/boring fast. doesn't seem to care about his students honestly. was also running super behind schedule. his exams are pretty fair game though

Great guy, took two classes with him. Don't expect anything to be offered online (recordings, slides) besides readings as he is an old-school, oral-only prof. Very funny with his same schtick of loneliness year after year. Very accomplished political theorist so regardless of what he teaches, it will be theory-based. Would recmd based on character.
Great prof!

very funny and engaging lecturer! however, midterms were only 1 hour and did not give enough time to read the prompts, write, cite, and submit an essay within the given time frame. lots of reading, but was for our own benefit looking back. was consistently behind in the syllabus, leading to very rushed and condensed lectures.

Prof. Ferrell took over our class under v. unfortunate circumstances + I really appreciate him for that. No-BS, clear grading criteria; he is not out to trick his students on exams or papers. Very kind, authentic, down-to-Earth guy. Only complaint: doesn't record lectures + has no slides (even though our former Prof. always posted thorough PPTs).

This guy loves his job and knows how to lecture, that's for sure. With the most boring material imaginable and no powerpoint whatsoever he'll keep you engaged and make you laugh every lecture. My only real complaint is that his exams are on an extremely tight schedule and require lots and lots of details. But do take his classes, he's a legend.
The material is very interesting, but the lectures are sometimes hard to follow. There is A LOT of reading!!

I didn't find this class to memorable as the lectures were just a short recording with a small written summary of them. Could have been better in my opinion... the course is interesting and has more potential. I found it disappointing but quite easy.

POLI 325 was taught remotely this year. Prof Ferrel gave written and video lectures (reading the written ones was enough though). He is engaging, funny, and loves the content of this course. If you do the readings and attend class, you should easily get an A.

Super easy, super clear material, makes Poli really easy even for students with no background in it. The dad jokes help you come to class too. Got away with doing everything for this class the night before.
Very disorganized.
The lectures were straightforward. Tough assignment problems but I thought the midterm and final were quite fair.

The professor isn't as bad as some of the reviews suggest. The lectures can feel a bit repetitive since he spends a lot of time reviewing material from previous classes, but the explanations are clear and the content is interesting. Both the midterm and final are fair, not too difficult if you're comfortable with the assignments and lab's

Ok i didn't do well in this course but I don't think he's as bad as the reviews make him out to be. The grading scheme was changed due to missed classes bc of the snow days. The assignments were a mess and i did not like the final at all, but he's still better than other physics profs i've had (i'm looking at you Hilke)

He's new. It shows. He's a nice guy, and I'm sure he'll likely improve. However, the course was poorly planned. We didn't get to some material, and seemed to randomly repeat other material in slightly different forms. Homework was mixed between trivial and irrelevant/too difficult. Poorly planned exams, large curves. He's nice and does try hard.

Slides were very messy and hard to study from. There were no "chapters" or form of organization. There were no textbooks to do practice problems from. There was no course syllabus, and the grading scheme was changed halfway through the course. The assignments were graded SUPER late. Assignments were either way too easy or graduate level questions.
"It's just vibesss" - prof Lister

This prof is a real one and is big on student empowerment. He is passionate about his views and he'll make sure you engage critically with the readings. I personally find his manner aggressive but there are few actual issues with his teaching style. He's also super accommodating with extensions as long as you give ample notice.
Made an 8:30am class interesting. Wonderful and enthusiastic prof.

Jay is a great guy. Interesting modern topics and very understanding. Attendance is recorded but is not part of the final grade. The grading is very clear for all papers and projects. Everything is straightforward.

Overall, great classes and Jay is great at pushing students in their own reflection and encouraging conversations. However, it did feel like he was imposing his opinion at times and would tend to cut students oof as they were talking. Assignments are really interesting and make use of the learnings. Easy a if willing to make a little effort :)

Loved Jay's class. The lectures proved excellent and relevant to the teaching philosophy. It gets you thinking on your aspirations and is truly motivating. Jay provides good examples and advice to use in the classroom.

Absolutely loved Jay. Had him twice, and it wasn't enough!! Incredibly caring, knowledgeable, interesting, passionate. He considers his students so much. He catered class content to our questions or topics of interest. Very understanding and respectful of individual circumstances/situations. The set up was also great. Wish i could have him again!

Each class we discuss the assigned readings as a group. 1 midterm paper and 1 final paper on the readings plus 1 presentation on the topic of personal choice. Other small assignments that are easy. His extensive education background plus his care for the future of students makes this class interesting and worthwhile. Easiest A ever you learn a ton!

Best teacher I ever had, he cared for his students and was always available at any time outside of the classroom. The course is really easy, there is no test, and a few of the texts you read are hard, and you always talk about them in class, so no worries. He grades really well. Overall it is an easy A.
Most disrespectful man I have ever met at McGill. Sad how he makes his students feel terrible about themselves. Do better.

I love his section about epigenetics since everything is clear despite a somewhat disorganized presentation. The questions are not necessarily hard but the word limit is annoying. Other than that, his section is much better than Ryan's part. I really wish some concepts have more explanations than others but he is glad to answer and inspire students

Dr. Tanny gives really clear lectures. His portion of lectures in PHAR 563 made the course more interesting and enjoyable as a whole.  Listening to his lectures and taking good notes are keys to success in his portion of lectures.
He is extremely helpful when help was asked and his questions are quite straightforward. However, he can give quite a bit information.
His section was extremely packed with useless protein names and the mechanisms were boring as hell. Remember everything, every little protein will be tested!
Excellent Professor

he didn't make genetics interesting even though they usually are. I also had some trouble understanding his accent but maybe that's just me. His slides are not very furnished, I only studied with the textbook (i recommend buying it, it's so much easier to understand than with the slides!). Got tested on material we didn't see in class.

This was 1st time teaching genetics. Explained most things verbally, with very little on slides except for diagrams he explained. On tests, there were things only in the book & never touched on in class, but even with reading the entire book I had difficulty. Amiable, but should have put more on slides and better emphasized what needed to be known.
reads off slides. Makes me want to sleep even I'm sitting in the first row. Sometimes too fast and sometimes too slow. But material is interesting.

He just reads off the slides...He needs to study his subject first, before teaching. His English is horrible..Not tough in exams though and good nature wise..His TA can do better in lecture and labs...

The material is interesting but the class itself is a bit boring because he simply reads off the slides. He is very nice though. His exams were pretty easy; all the material came from the lectures so if you memorize that you are good.

Professor Ellis doesn't use PowerPoint, refuses to answer class questions and doesn't give proper feedback on exercises. She would spend 80 minutes gliding through the superficial facts of cases without ever giving us the test or ratio. She gave us the wrong final grade thrice.

I wanted to do this class in French, so I ignored her rating; biggest regret ever. She strays away from the class plan, spends hours on a basic thing but seconds on a hard notion, is unclear when talking (she shouldn't be teaching in French) and is rude when answering questions. I'll backflip from a roof before picking a class she's teaching again.

I would recommend avoiding this prof at all costs. First, she is very confusing in class; she would omit some explanations and use dismissive tones towards classmates who ask questions. Second, she committed a gross error by releasing a feedback form without any correct grades, and then releasing incorrect grades.

Worst prof ever. Released the grades 4 days late all that to just be the wrong grades and her having to send the corrected grades days later. If you value your mental health, do not take any class with her as a prof! Also you will end up having to teach yourself the class because she explains things horribly!

She is very accessible outside of class, but is generally unhelpful. Lectures are confusing, goes off on tangents, doesn't explain concepts at all. 

I talked to her outside of class and she said that she couldn't answer any of my questions that I wanted to clarify because the answers are all in the readings.

Very confusing lectures, the reading list changes all the time, doesn't explain the concepts clearly.

Then blames the students when the class does horribly on the midterm!

If you value your mental health, take someone else. Good luck understanding her and whatever it is she's talking about. She is never clear about what she expects and often shuts students' questions down whenever they're not regarding the exact topic of the day. If you have her, pray.
elle est méchante et je détestais ce cours. J'ai essayé de aller aux heures de burreau mais elle m'a dit qu'elle ne voulait pas y parler.

Does not believe in clear instructions. Obsessed with Labelle v. Gatineau for no reason. Easier to not attend class and to learn the material on your own. Very condescending. Tells us one thing and next class she changes her mind. My best piece of advice: avoid her at ALL cost. Bring your own chair if you chose to attend (bring cushion to nap).
top 10 worst professors of all time. you never know what she wants, and she obviously picks favourites in the class. AVOID AT ALL COSTS
no notes or recordings and very disorganized lectures. good luck understanding ANYTHING. take it with someone else
take it with someone else

He is a really caring professor. You should be fine if first you are interested in the topics of the class, second you are prepared to put in quite a lot of work. You will learn a lot from him and it is great learning experience for me personally. I would recommend!

Under no circumstances you should not take MATH 376 (or the nonhonours version of it). This course is a total waste of time and money because it only scratches surface of every topic. Professor Nave will not teach you a thing. His lectures are boring. His notes are messy. His assignments are too long and purely computational. His exams are hard.

Really enjoyed his class. He makes you see things in a very fun, inspiring and almost magical way. He was using the Strogatz textbook, which was a brilliant choice. The delivery of the end of the class was a bit rushed and the were some administrative problems with TAs, but other than that, would take again in a heartbeat.

As mentioned in the most recent reviews, Prof. Nave is a very intelligent and funny guy! Problem sets and in-class graded quizzes are given every two weeks to prepare the exams. He also provided the detailed exam format which was very helpful for studying. He tends to be unclear but reading the textbook clarifies very quickly!

Don't listen to the other reviews; this professor is one of the best at McGill. His choice of topics was excellent, and he always tries to give us a motivation for the concepts seen in class. He is also very funny (although its french humour!). Tests are long but not hard. Those who complain usually have a very superficial grasp of the material

I found Prof. Nave to be an intelligent and funny man although he was extremely unclear on the board. The course load was easy and the assignments manageable. The topic of each question on the final was given in advance, which was very helpful. 8/10 would take again.

I don't understand the negative ratings. Final was very fair. He is clear about expectations, and the assignments/tutorials helped a lot. Personally I found that his teaching style is great. Often gives a big picture explanation of where we are in the course before a lecture. Funny and interesting to listen to.

JC was definitely the best math prof I've had at McGill (although that's not saying much). I thought the way he structured the course was really helpful, but it's true the averages for our midterms were both about 50%, which is not ideal :/ Still, it's curved, and the assignments are self-graded which was really helpful
unclear speech in lecture- very vague with what he wants us to know during class- is unnessarily mean. Gives questions in exams he never taught in class.
He is a good prof if your a good student. He also laughs at his own jokes which cracks me up everytime, he loves teaching this class.
You need to put 0.75x speed to watch the lecture recording to understand his English
you wont understand anything he says . this man doesn't know how to speak  proper English
I heard that he failed all of the pro-palestinian students because of their political views
terrible
he has a very thick french accent, tout out to the American student. you won't understand a word he says

Truly one of the best profs of PHAR 562. Very passionate about his work and funny! Always willing to stay after class for questions and answered emails fast. Test questions are very fair! He really loves what he teaches, making it exciting to go to class

Dr. Trempe is such an amazing prof! It is clear that he and the prof put a lot of work into this course to make it easier for students to learn the content. The course content can be tricky but the assignments give you a good idea of what the final exam would be like. Very responsive and prompt as well!

Dr. Trempe is such a gem! Every single lecture he taught, he was always so positive! It seems he cares to teach, something you don't see much of for research-oriented professors! Plus this class was probably the most relevant to my degree so far!

This is the second time I've had JM for labs, and he's amazing. With the TA strike, we had a lot more time 1-on-1 and he's extremely helpful and caring. His lab manuals need some TLC as they haven't been updated in 10+ years and ask you to do things that are impossible, but besides that, JM is the best lab coord and it's really easy to do well.
He ran a good lab. Relatively organized and was kind when I asked him for help.

Labs were difficult and demanded ridiculous accuracy, especially for a first-year course. I've taken 4 higher-level labs since this one and it is still the hardest I've had to do. TAs were a mixed bag, but mine sucked: clearly disliked students, and was critical to the point of rudeness. Rolled his eyes & heaved sighs of disgust when asked for help
He'll talk really fast to get in information that over complicates the material

Very unfair when it comes to marking. The level of accuracy demanded to get full marks are extremely difficult to achieve with the equipment provided. The labs will significantly drag down the marks of students.
Make friends with the TA. TAs are the ones who do everything in the labs. My ratings aren't for him but for my TA.
So nice and funny. A great guy.
i can't believe how this guy is unfair in his grading.. very very unfair, and that's enough to lower you grade by a great deal since labs affect your mark significantly. The TAs are much better.

This guy is weird. Sometimes he's quite helpful and nice, and other times he can be quite cold and dismissive. Overall, he seems to do his job effectively. Ultimately, it's the TA who is more significant.

Seems unapproachable at first, but if you've got a legitimate question/problem pertaining to the experiment, he is willing to help. Those pre-lab quizzes are nerve-wracking, esp. when his voice suddenly booms out from the speakers: "TWO MINUTES."
just love Dr. R. he's so so nice and so so helpful. a bit chatty but who doesn't want to talk to him?! Love the dude.
One of the most amazing professors I have ever had - very innovative and helpful

He's a good prof especially if you enjoy a fast-paced but engaging learning environment. This class was 3 hours on a monday morning, and even then I found it to be interesting because half the course is practical. He asked us how we wanted to be graded and gave us the highest possible grades, but beware that the grading scheme is unorganized.

The course is very interesting and very applied and Professor Reyt is interesting and very available. I would just review the grading system a little as a lot of the grade is out of your control in this course.
I highly recommend this class. I think every body should learn and practice negotiation. Jean-Nicolas Reyt is a great teacher and is really chill, each class was a pleasure and I really had fun.

Very good and very applied course. The group project is stressful, but it makes you apply course concepts to the real world. Prof Reyt is dynamic and really available to meet, which was helpful. I wish there were a few more graded components that would be easier to control. It is a very competitive grading against other students and teams.
Overall he made a pretty heavy class interesting and applicable. JN is also easily available outside of class. A bit too many assignments though.

Emphasizied a lot that many students fail the class was really not encouraging for an intro class. Yes it is theory heavy, but I think it could have been very nice with a prof who was not so focused on convincing us it was hard (and making not hard). I still liked the class and the content, but wish I would have taken it with someone else.

He really reminds me of some influencer and he absolutely cares a lot about whether he can get a teaching award. It was not very pleasant talking to him as he can come off as dismissive. Put your effort and you will be fine.

JN is a really great prof. He simplifies complex topics, relates them to our lives. No memorizing. Makes sure we understand/expand on concepts. Fun group project! Good assignments.
He's super understanding/flexible. I had family obligations during the semester. It allowed me to prioritize them, along with the class. 

Would 1000% take again!

The course is very theory heavy, but still quite interesting. Professor Reyt is decent, but often seems a bit frazzled and he can be hard to reach outside class, at least in my experience. The grading seems a bit capricious at times and he is not happy when you seem to question it.
