Cocky. Told me on a 1-1 session that people fail (after I did poorly on one of the tests) and then proceeded to talk about how he just failed to get a teaching award. Cool relation dude! He is a good teacher, but he thinks too highly of himself. Still managed to get a good grade in the end but takes a LOT of studying.

I absolutely LOVED her! She is an amazing, kind, caring professor who really wants everyone to do well (and she doesn't just say it, she actually makes sure that we do eg group exams to boost grades). She prepares fun in-class activities and has very clear presentation slides with boxes to show what should be learnt for the exam and what shouldn't.

I LOVEEE her. She gives very great lectures, and keep everyone engaged . I liked her two part midterms , I have never been excited or laughed during a midterm. I wish McGill had more teachers like her. TAKE HERRR.
She really cares about her students and it shows. She also puts little boxes on the slides to tell you what you need to memorize.

Although this class does have a lot of information/content, she really explains everything in detail and points out exactly what you need to know. It definitely is not an easy A but she really wants everyone to do well and if you put in a decent amount of work you will get a good grade. I found it very interesting and she is an amazing prof!
Such a great prof! Really wants you to succeed and thrive! She incorporates lots of group work and participation which keeps you active and makes the class fly by. Love her class!

Best prof!! She genuinely cares about her students doing well and is really enthusiastic about the material. She includes in-class activities that help grasp the material a lot better. Everything you need for the exam is in the slides! Understand them (don't just memorize), and the class is an easy A.

I really like her teaching style! She is the type of prof that really cares about students, and also tries to arrange the order of topics in a understandable way. Her questions requires both memorization and thinking. The thinking questions are a bit hard and requires a bit of time. But overall her questions are pretty fair!

The prof structures her course well and is very enthusiastic during lectures. Specifically for MIMM214, the course itself is heavy, but the prof tries her best to make it interesting and clear, and she does! Not an easy-A, you still need to work hard for exams & a term paper, but it doesn't feel as tedious as typical bio courses. Would take again!

Her lectures were very content heavy and the class was very difficult. I did alright, but beware, this class isn't easy and she really slams you with a lot to memorize. The exam questions were also pretty tricky, but manageable. The one good thing was that she was always available after class for any questions.

Best professor I had at McGill. She is full of energy and all of her lectures are really fun and interesting. The grading is really fair if you do your readings, study and complete the tasks. I loved that class and I would do it all over again. Once again, if you do what is recommended, you will get an A!

Whenever you didn't understand something in class Lumb would always work it out with you until you got it. Very smart man and came up with some very creative practice problems. My only complaint is that there was a huge disconnect between practice problems and exam difficulty which he straight up denied in class after the midterm.

Lumb is great! Was forgiving when I had technical difficulties submitting a midterm. Lectures are straightforward and detailed. Encourages participation. Exams are fair with some challenging questions sprinkled in there. If you have any misunderstandings, he'll help you! Try to ask creative "what if we had this...?" questions during class.

You can tell that Dr. Lumb is a smart man. However, there is a disconnect between the actual content presented in the organic chemistry course and what he explains and expects from students. His exams are insanely difficult and will include questions that you have never seen before in any practice material. Makes it extremely hard to succeed.

Prof Lumb is amazing!!! I am not into chemistry at all, did not have high expectations for this course, however he has made it so enjoyable! He is so nice and funny and also an awesome prof, he explains the material very clearly and does tons of practice examples which are very helpful. Answers questions and helps when needed.

A really knowledgable and fair professor. If you go to class, study your notes, and make an effort to understand the lecture content you will do well. He takes his time presenting the content to answer all questions and provide a solid foundation for organic chemistry.
Pay attention to the mechanisms he shows in class.

Prof Lumb has been my favourite prof so far at McGill. I'm not even a Chem major and Chem 212 was my favourite course. He is obviously very knowledgeable and wants you to genuinely understand the material. He is also a prof you feel comfortable around and will make you laugh! The exams are tough but fair if you put in the effort.

I'm honestly surprised to see prof Lumb rated so low on this site, I think everyone expects CHEM 212 to be challenging but he certainly made it less so. Explanations were crystal clear, gave a lot of examples and practice and was fair in tests and grading. He made organic extremely bearable (coming from an environment major)

Prof Lumb is clearly incredible at what he does, and he wants you to be too. He expects you to understand absolutely everything, which is fantastic if you're a chem major, but awful if not. It's a really difficult class, and he's known for making it more so. Do note that he is 100% fair in his grading, and forewarns you about tough things.

He does upload lecture notes but he adds a lot during lectures so it's important to attend or at least watch the recordings. He's a great lecturer, and my only criticism is that he doesn't provide clear guidelines for what's going to be on exams.

He was easily my favourite professor last semester. He gave amazing lectures and kept the class engaged. He doesn't post slides, so you almost need to attend, but I definitely think it's worth it. The MT and Final were both easy and were graded generously. My TA was also very knowledgeable, and I attended every tutorial, even though it was 8:30.

Pros:
- Passionate about what he teaches which makes class enjoyable.
- Gives cool real-world examples about the material (tip: take note of these there was a question on the final that asked you to give a real-world example)
- Easy midterm, final was harder
- Assignments are good
-Posts lecture notes
Cons: 
- Speaks fast (but you get used to it)

This prof is super passionate and uses cool examples to make ODE problems as interesting as they can be. He explains super well and his exams are very fair. Very organized and has helpful WebWorks. I highly suggest taking his class.

Best math prof I've had at McGill. His lectures are so clear and so captivating, and he really does teach you everything you need to know for the exams. He is also quite funny and interesting, and it is really easy to learn the important concepts in order to succeed in the class. He does like to go over derivations, which isn't important.

His lectures notes and content are so well structured and organized. Captivating teacher with incredible knowledge on how the material actually applies in real life. Tests were relatively easy since he prepares you well for them, you can always guess what the questions are gonna be. Charming quebecois accent, would take again for sure

Amazing prof! His lectures were fun and clear. He has this way of explaining concepts that make them seem simple. The midterm and final were fair given what we had seen in class. MATH263 with this prof was by far my favourite class of the semester! Do the webworks, stay up to date with the material and this class should be pretty easy.

Amazing prof! His lectures were very fun and clear, he has a way of explaining concepts that make them super easy. The midterm and final were very fair given the material we had covered in class. Do the webworks, make sure you're up to date and this class should be pretty easy!
best teacher, lectures were clear and punctual. he has nice notes that are posted in advance. midterm and final were quite easy. overall great teacher
amazing teacher - clear & straight to the point. What every math teacher should aspire to be.

He gives great lectures that are organized and pertinent, definitely go to them to understand the content. His midterm and final were hard, so don't just rely on the practice exams he gives: cover and practice all topics possible.
Most inspiring conductor, leader and professor I ever had! His leadership is exceptional, he should be dean!!
Amazing conductor and leader!!!

Dr. V is an inspiring conductor and teacher. His rehearsals are clear, expressive, and full of meaning. He brings out the best in every singer and creates performances that are both powerful and emotional. I've grown so much thanks to his leadership. It's a joy and a privilege to sing in his choir!
Most inspirational conductor I've ever had! Thank you Dr. V for sharing your passion and knowledge!!❤️
Inspirational conductor! Choral music at McGill University is a spectacular experience with Dr. V.
Best conducting faculty at the Schulich School of Music!!
Thank you Dr. Vallee for creating such a safe space for creation in your rehearsals. Inspired and inspiring music making!

Amazing conducting pedagogue! Dr. Vallee is one of the leading figures in choral conducting and knows the demands of the professional world! Extremely details oriented in his teaching, he has trained some of the best choral musiciens of our time!

Merci Dr. V!
Superb conductor! I had the greatest time singing Beethoven's 9th with him....Thank you, Dr. V

Great pedagogue and conductor! Also quite charming and good looking...just saying!! ;-)

Love love love!

-SUPER invested in the success of her students, as an advisor and as a professor. -Always makes sure to accommodate you if possible
-Answers emails quickly 365d/y, with very detailed answers.
- lectures and powerpoints not always super clear but she explains well during labs. 
-around 4h of homework each week
-good grade if you put in the work

Jeanne is patient, kind, encouraging, knowledgeable. The online labs are fun to work on with her (but I imagine they're harder in person). Labs are graded harshly sometimes but I think that's because of the TA's, not the prof. Also she's the most helpful EPS advisor I've met. I love the way she pronounces "breakout rooms" in her French accent, lol.
Jeanne will take the time to explain things to you if you approach her outside of class. She really cares about her students and is passionate about the subjects she teaches.
Lectures are a bit confusing but she is very nice and extremely helpful outside class if you need help.

She's very passionate and is obviously knowledgable about what she presents to the class. Expectations for understanding difficult science concepts are too high for a class made up of primarily non-science students. Assignments barely relate to the material that is presented in class.

Not sure how to describe dear Jeanne... such a lovely lady but impossible to understand and so hard to focus in class. She is very passionate about biology and earth science but unfortunately isnt inspiring any interest from me:/ tbh i just wish she was my grandma. <3
I am interested in the hear and now and I appreciate the need to understand the past, but I think that structure of rock is not useful and if I need it I can look up the information
I never understand why she gives the facts she does

The labs are super chill and pretty fun (you look at rocks or use a microscope), but the mineral ID tests are tough - especially the first one. The lecture material is a bit abstract and boring, and the test/exam questions are worded rather cryptically, but overall a pretty good class. She's super approachable and wants to help you.

It is extremely hard to understand what Prof Paquette is saying, her English probably isn't good enough to teach in an auditorium. Moreover, Prof Paquette wasn't helpful by not providing us with clear guidelines and averaging an incredible 6 weeks to correct short assignments.
I took a seminar with her and it was so interesting !!! I had so much fun and it was honestly one of the best classes i ever took. It was sooooo difficult though, I had to work very hard !

The two midterms were weighted very heavily and she tested on so much material we had to memorize with dates, artists, etc. Also there were so many readings that were also included in the midterms, around 20 pages per readings for every unit.

Took this class in my first semester and it was a big mistake. She doesn't not care about your understanding of the course, she wants to know that you memorized every single information. We go over 3000 years of East Asian history in a single course and she somehow expects you to memorize date, artists, title and provenance of 100+ artworks.

Avoid this course if memorization isn't your strength or you're new to art history. Exams dominate your grade: open-ended (no multiple-choice), randomized examples from hundreds of slides test pure recall of everything covered—every detail you write is graded, no room for error. I barely passed ARTH 215—proceed with caution.

I've had my favourite art history class at McGill with Prof. Hong. She creates a very safe and pleasant environment for seminar discussions. Great guidance that challenges you to develop your own interpretation of the artworks. I've learned so much from the class!

Three exams that follow very closely the lectures, structure is always the same and fairly graded. Every lecture is almost always 1h+, but they aren't a pain to go through. She cares about her students doing well and sends examples of perfect answers after tests so we know how to improve. Final essay is also guided by questions, so easier to write.

A little intimidating at first, but very kind. Be prepared to work your butt off; art history is no joke. Her readings will take you all day and her lectures, if recorded, take hours to get through because of how packed with info they are. That said, shes great at answering questions and the class will really expend your worldview.

This class is an amazing introduction to East Asian art, history, culture, and religion. The prof was knowledgeable and organized. If you have a genuine interest, it's really rewarding! That said, don't take this class as an 'easy elective'. To do well, you MUST attend every lecture and take notes. Tests are fair but require memorization of dates.
Too much readings, too much work, the teacher doesn't interact with the students. The workload is horrible and she is a very tough grader. If you want to take an introduction class AVOID THIS CLASS.

Really interesting content! The concepts are a bit hard to grasp at the beginning, but if you keep up with readings and attend lectures it all starts to make sense. Memorization is pretty important in this class. No laptop policy, which I personally liked, but I know a lot of people hate it. No text book, which is super nice.
I absolutely learned everything by myself. Thermo is already a very difficult class, doesnt do examples in class
Very bad class, doesn't teach just shows proofs and exams are not similar to class problems at all
run. did not teach anything

Honestly a passionate guy, but he will make your life harder . Lectures are hard to follow and I barely learn anything, which may be a me issue but I didn't have that issue in other classes. If you didn't spend your life into studying his class, then his exams are overly hard. But they are doable.
Very passionate about his work, though his lectures are very long and can get boring sometimes. He has a very good teaching method, and he really tries to connect with students.

Lectures are incredibly long and heavy, speaks as if he is talking to PhD level students. Makes every single concept sound way too complicated than what it actually is, and expects students to already know everything. Gives lectures as if they were PhD level seminars. Often speaks in a condescending manner. NEEDS TO BE HUMBLED

Really passionate about his research, and a great motivator. I understood the main concepts, but left fuzzy on anything other than the big points.
Tests were hard, but fair.

His exams have nothing to do with what he teaches in class. You can think you understand the material and you can do all the problems in the textbook but good luck solving the exams. His way of judging if his exams are fair for the allowed time is by having his graduate students complete them in that same time.
worst professor at mcgill, avoid at all cost. take thermo 2 with prof habashi instead
speaking in supersonic speed in lecture and don't give time to student to copy down the notes, impossible to follow in person lecture

Great & likeable guy, and great at teaching. But his ENVR201 taught w/ Garver was a total mess. Physically impossible amount of readings (they admitted to it but didn't change it?), lectures all over the place. Can't even tell you what the main topic of the course was. I liked that you could secure a lot of your grade from projects/participation.

Extremely disappointing lectures with no appropriate vocabulary. Unable to properly explain some of the simplest concepts and struggles to discuss topics related to his own research field. Uses excessive friendliness to compensate but won't move a finger to help you. He might actually make your grade worst if you ask for a review.

Dr. Cardille is a really interesting teacher--his lectures were engaging, and he knew how to start up conversations with students to really make us think. Where I had my problems was with the 3 group projects assigned. Grading for these was super harsh, and in my opinion unfair as the criteria was overall super disorganized and confusing.

Prof. Cardille made online courses so engaging and interesting. Classes revolved a lot around group work, presentations and discussion which was a great way to get to know the material as well as exchange with the class. Prof. Cardille was easy to reach, approachable during (online) classtime and invested in his students. Great course, great prof!
The class is over and I still don't know what it was about :/

Dr. Cardille is very cool and easy-going. He's good at guiding students during their thought processes. It's a fairly clear-cut course. In-class discussions can get pretty interesting, esp. after group presentations start.

Dr. Cardille gave this course together with Dr. Kosoy. They worked very well together. Each had their own different vibe which made the course enjoyable. Dr. Cardille knows his stuff, shares his personal experience as well as scientifically supported data. Easy-going.
He knows how to involve students in class. In-class assignments and activities were fun. No final exam. I never missed his class.

This guy is solid! He doesn't seem known among the students of the department quite yet but I thoroughly enjoyed this class and would also recommend it to those in CogSci who want to take a Ling class that isn't 201. Honestly, the combo of interesting info with a not-super-high-pressure environment made for a good class.
Jeff is a great prof, both approachable and knowledgeable. Definitely recommend his classes!

Jeff is awesome. Super funny and engaging. One of the best profs in the geology department. He's very approachable and open to questions.  Exams are very fair and test overall concepts as opposed to small details.
As per other reviews grading is tough, but definitely winnable. Probably my favourite class at McGill content wise so if you're up for the challenge I think it's worth it!

Honestly, I think the prof made the course slightly easier (as he clearly mentioned for this semester Winter 2026). The average of the class was 74%. Lectures are recorded and the content (even though there's stuff to memorize) is very interesting. If you want to do well in this class, you definitely don't want to be last minute. Amazing prof!

Ive never failed a class in my entire life and yet here it is, the most confusing class I've ever taken at Mcgill. Run far away from this if you are not either pre-med, neursci or psych majors, because the workload is insane considering you are to learn by heart not only very complex scientific concepts but who wrote articles about it and so on !!

I can only say that this is the best class i've take at McGill, incredibly knowledgeable professor who basically nerds out every class. This isn't an easy A, but if you love diving deep into a subject and looking at it from a interdisciplinary perspective, this class is for you.

Fascinating subject with difficult exams. Prof Mogil is engaging and enjoys adding personal anecdotes to the lectures, and the guest lectures were all very interesting. I learned a lot of useful information that was not tested upon (for example, why we should be critical of published scientific papers), and would recommend it for that reason.

I would blame myself for my C+ grade, but he didn't really make it any easier to study. He doesn't believe in practice exams or questions (how?), goes on pointless tangents during lectures, and expects you to memorize some pretty minor details rather than overarching concepts. Still an entertaining lecturer, though, so might just be a skill issue.

fascinating class, but so so so hard. but also so so so so worth it. it's really a dichotomy, but if you're ready to put in the effort, it'll feel so intellectually rewarding. he is a tough exam maker, but he is fair and curves when required. you hate to love this guy, he's really an incredible (somewhat cocky but still) dude
I like him because he kinda looks like Buddy the elf

He's organized and clearly explains topics; funny as well. This isn't an easy course by any means but it's well thought out and really teaches you about pain IF you're engaged with the material. As long as you put in the work I think you should be good. As a B strain student, def challenged me but in a good way.

Dr. Mogil is a great, entertaining lecturer and PSYC 302 is an interesting course.  The final exam was unfortunately comprised of only 40 multiple choice questions (too few!). You need to know all the little details that you wouldn't think are crucial. They are crucial if you want to do well. The lecture slides are nice and clear. Read them well.

I am so confused by these positive reviews as everyone I have spoken to about her has had bad experiences. The highest grade on exams was 85, and no one got any question 100% right. She does not seem to care about her students and makes it difficult for us to do well. She is rude and I would avoid her if possible.

Prof Elrick is incredibly knowledgeable and engaging. Always willing to do extra research for her students and talk to us after class. While the midterm grading was hard, the final was easy as long as you did the readings.

Great, engaging speaker. Pretty harsh grading for the midterm (take-home). Final was easy, as long as you do the readings and put in effort. Wants students to succeed, super knowledgable and takes criticism.

Professor Elrick is a very kind woman and accessible during lectures. The class was fair and the readings were not too excessive. My only critique is that her lectures can get repetitive, if you do all the readings you probably don't need to go to all her lectures. Overall a good class.

Knowledgeable, she really knows her stuff! Lectures were super interesting, I enjoyed going to class. However, I found that the grading was really harsh. On the midterm,1/160 students got an A (85%). If you ask specific questions, she tells you to refer to the textbook or other peers. She's pretty big on protecting her "intellectual property"...

Professor Elrick is HANDS DOWN one of the best professors at McGill. While some people may say she comes across as "dry", when you really sit down and pay attention, you realize that she is dropping so much rich information and wisdom. She really wants students to succeed and shows that she cares. She really helped me appreciate Sociology!

Professor Elrick definitely knows her stuff and is passionate about sociology. However, her lectures are very dry and dense. Her explanations of concepts are very confusing and the grading is quite harsh.

Engaging and entertaining lectures, she def knows her stuff. I would def take one of her classes again. I didnt rly do any readings except for the perusall ones but did well bc took good in-lecture notes (maybe just bc I was interested in the info & it stuck with me).

I had a few gripes with the way she handled grading, the criteria were pretty unclear overall and I wasn't too sure what she wanted on any graded assignments, and I didn't get a lot of clear feedback. However, this prof inspired me to start a double major in soci when I was already in my third year, I think she delivered the material phenomenally.

Professor Elrick is a very smart woman and clearly knows her stuff. However, I find I do not connect to her teaching style, and I believe her assessments are weighted too heavily (midterm 36%, Perusall 24%, Final 46%) that's my personal opinion. Also I'm not sure if it's the set of TA's I had but have been graded very harshly so not a huge fan.

she is a very respected, caring, and knowledgeable professor. there are lots of helpful guest lectures in this course which i found pretty interesting. this FDSC545 that i took is purely essay-based and requires excellent researching and writing ability. no midterm no final. only review articles and many essays
She is the best teacher in the faculty. HIGHLY recommend! I love her

She's very sweet and seems to care about the content she's teaching about. She also gives really helpful learning objectives, which is good for the final. However, her lectures were very disorganized and its hard to follow her train of thought sometimes. Sometimes she's not great about clearing up tough to understand ideas. Overall good though
Very nice prof and nice person. Lecture is not very in-depth though. Would rarely give answers to in-depth questions. Very generous on giving exam practice guidelines, unlike the previous two profs.

Don't really get her bad ratings, Prof. Sunday is super caring, and her lectures are really engaging. I don't think she's disorganized so idrk what people are saying. She does teach the easiest section of the course though so maybe I'm biased.

She is nice but so disorganized. We wasted so much time in lectures and were always behind because she has to take time during class to try to figure out what her slides mean. It just doesn't seem like she reviews what she's teaching for the day at all before class.

Super cool prof, her research sounds super interesting and I loved her final assignment by far more than any of the others; it was pretty cool to get a chance to study raw footage of marine populations and feel like you were doing real research. And yes, sometimes her lectures seemed a little "improv", but it's clear she knows her stuff.

Prof Sunday is very energetic and enthusiastic about what she teaches. The material she teaches is pretty easy but her test questions were pretty tricky. Assignments weren't too hard but were time consuming. Overall very nice and cares about her students and I found her online lectures the most engaging out of all the biol215 profs.

shes not THAT bad. Shes nice. She just needs more confidence, but she does care and try. She sets clear expectations and theyre not too far to reach either. Her questions are clear/easy. She doesnt know the answer to every question, but thats common for the other profs too. If she doesnt understand a slide, she doesnt expect you to know it either

She really has no clue what she is talking about and is really poor at explaining things in class. She has the potential to be a good lecturer if she just reviewed her slides before class, but honestly every day it looked like she had never seen the material until she was presenting it.

He was pretty great. I had no experience in stats before but still found it relatively easy. You will need to study and try hard, but not any more than your average mcgill class. I found it easier to watch the recordings than go to class so I could pause and play back, seeing as its pretty technical. Overall a good class. Def dont need the textbook

He is very nice and takes time to explain things well. Don't be afraid to ask questions and go to tutorials, it can be helpful. The TAs post the tutorials online as well as demonstration videos. Midterms are very representative of what we see in class and nothing is to be learned by heart.

Shortened version of a MUCH longer review I will post on the McGill subreddit:

TLDR: Traditional lectures with interactive learning checks and a very supportive prof. Homework quizzes boost your grade, but exams are algebra-heavy and denser than practice. Stay on top of concepts and numeracy and it's very passable.

Very sweet and approachable teacher who loves cats. The assignments did not reflect the format of the tests or the difficulty of the exams, which was misleading and made it harder to study effectively. Slide exercises were helpful to understand the material, but repetitive and did not prepare you for the different types of questions found in exams.

Really wonderful professor who explains concepts VERY clearly and provides lots of examples. Grading scheme was very fair, homework helpful and a very similar style to questions on midterms/final. If you pay attention to lectures, do the homework, and create additional practice problems to nail down the concepts, you will get an easy A. Recorded.

Don't be fooled, exams are no longer online. However, overall a decent class, midterms aren't worth much (15% each), and many online homework assignments which can help your grade. Slides are very clear & provides many examples. Exams are theory heavy and multiple choice which is a disadvantage personally for a math class.

Loved taking this class, the prof is super clear and honestly hilarious , I would definitely take his class again. I didn't do too well on the final by my own fault but tbh it was much harder than the midterms. If I had to give any advice don't limit yourself to the difficulty of the exercises in the lecture slides, aim higher!

Prof. Kreitewolf is very wholesome; he came up with as many statistic questions relating to the fluffiness of cats and just cats in general as he could. In my experience, you don't really need the textbook unless you need extra practice probs (there aren't enough given outside of lecture imo).

Dr Jens is a really nice prof. He explains really well and gives multiple examples in class for the topics he teaches. Its nice that he sometimes asks the class question to try to engage everyone even though the material is not the most interesting. The course is still really easy and just attending lectures can almost guarantee an A in the class.

In 204 he was very sweet and caring, clearly passionate about the material. I also had him for 305 in winter, and he was tougher on exams and sometimes seemed to not want to teach that class (less patient, sped through lectures). Unclear explanations, sometimes you have to teach yourself. Very approachable guy, but not great as a teacher.

All you need to know is he is the type of guy that is trying to catch you saying something that you don't mean in that way and is the type of Prof who won't round you if your grade is 84.999. NEVER TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM!
The participation rubric is really confusing and unfair. The lectures alone are not enough to study for the tests. Make sure to take notes in class and do the assigned readings. His tests are hard...

He is my least favourite prof in the faculty. Thinks he's above teaching an entry level class, makes it hard and extremely time consuming. He revamped the whole test structure this year (only OB prof to do so), making exams way harder than other classes, requiring 15+% curves. He was patronizing in the classroom. Unclear grader, easy avoid for OB.
He probably wrote those last reviews himself to boost his average because honestly it is a bad class and his grading made no sense.

Good prof and explains things well, always open to questions during class. The quizzes were the worst part because they had questions that were so ambiguous but I'm pretty sure he didn't make them (it was the other ob prof) so ignore the comments about that. You do need to participate a lot to get a good grade in that portion tho.

These comments are dramatic. Prof Mackey is super knowledgeable and a great professor. You should never go into a core curriculum course assuming it's a ‘bird'. The quizzes were difficult, but attainable if studied properly and thoroughly. He is very open to questions  if you seem interested in more than just the grade. Make sure to participate.

I enjoyed Prof. Mackey's class. Though the quizzes were tough to study for, the concepts themselves were not challenging. I also enjoyed his lectures, and he is clearly passionate and knowledgeable about Organizational Behaviour. If you speak once every class, you will get your participation grade.

Professor Mackey was super engaging in all lectures and made sure to include a somewhat interesting/engaging activity every class to spark some fun in the learning. You could tell he put a lot of effort into them as well as his slides and knew a lot about the course. Some of the quizzes were kind of confusing but he knocked off the worst grade.
Just not a very nice person. Tried to go to office hours to ask questions, but he was giving the impression that I was bothering him. Made me feel stupid for struggling.

Prof Mackey was a great lecturer, always open to help, and cared about students.  However, he made his course this fall far more challenging than needed. This was the first year he decided to make the course harder as it used to be a “bird”. His tests were super challenging even though the concepts are easy. He had to curve every test

Potter is the reason I joined the CANS department. He's super chill, really knowledgeable, and downright hilarious. The TAs for CANS200 are notoriously tough graders, but don't let that discourage you from taking seminars with him.

I took CANS200 in the fall and 311 in the winter. Many readings, but the lectures are very clear with the themes he is looking for when grading. I found it much easier to do well in 311 because he was marking. Overall as a first-year student I was afraid a 300 level would be too hard but it ended up being one of my favourite courses all year.
Clearly needs a job, not the type to ever make real money. The personality and the disdain for people who are better educated than him is astounding, avoid if possible
Professor Potter makes lectures very interesting to follow. That being said, the papers are extremely difficult and the TAs are very tough graders.
The most unprofessional individual at McGill

Potter is a really chill and good prof. His lectures were really interesting and he always made sure everyone understood the content. The few assignments were tough and graded hard but the final was exactly like the study guide so pretty easy. If you're not interested in history then do not take this class, but if u like it then Potter is great!

Lectures were boring with info that wasnt on the final exam, TAs were not helpful with assignments and very harsh graders with no helpful feedback. Seminars were very boring with no relevant info to the final. would not recommend taking this class.
Expects us to read 5 books in 1 semester hahaahahaha
Very nice lectures, the TAs help you get through some details. Assignment grading was harsh. A lot of readings.
Good course if you want to learn more about Canada. I didn't know anything about Canada before taking this course, and CANS200 was really useful.

I took his course in 2023 and I had no prior experience with HCI. Engaging lectures, varied guest lecturers from the industry; both a great introduction and deep dive into HCI.

As others have said, the workload was huge. Weekly readings that required online annotations. Term project. Not a course for GPA-farming. Recommended only in retrospect.
McGill should fire this guy, he always forgot his words.
Avoid at all cost and keep your mental health in a good shape. He is laterally the worst professor at McGill.

HUGE workload, long readings every week, and random grading. The lectures were engaging and very participative, with lots of heavy math. 
But I repeat, huge workload (especially on the assignments/project) for a 3 credits course

This course is quite interesting, but definetely not worth considering the amount of work expected. He asks us to read textbook chapters every week (graded). Only that requires a lot of time, but the projects you have to do on the side require way too much time, even if they are all very interesting.

Globally, I don't recommend taking this course.

This class is excellent and is really a eye opener. However the workload is just too much and you'll be graded on everything that can possibly be graded.

I highly recommend taking this course, but think about it as equivalent to 3 courses in terms of workload.
He thinks he's brutally honest. But that's not true. He's just rude. He discriminates his students and is emotional. There cannot exist a fair judgement.

The course demands a lot. Assignments can take from 20 to 60 hours, lectures are arduous, readings are very theoretical, and the peer marking is blatantly ridiculous. If you're a new masters/phd student I wouldn't recommend. The only worthwhile part of the course is AI, machine learning and stats portions are poorly delivered and confusing.

Pros: A good lecturer. Interesting guest lecturers invited, too. Cons: Irresponsible. His class uses peer grading (neither he nor the TAs grade!), and his rubric doesn't make sense. 100% for very satisfactory, 75% for satisfactory; and "if you grade radomly you won't get grades yourself", driving almost everyone grading merely 75% to each other

To shed some light on the disparity between people here who give 5s and people who gives 1s: Cooperstock's grading is RANDOM, I repeat, RANDOM. Everyone works extremely hard but is graded completely arbitrarily, hence the disparity between his ratings here. Furthermore, he's not responsive or sympathetic. You deserve to be treated better, avoid.

Good lecturer. Orgarnized, Posts everything you need online (lecture recordings, notes, solutions). Class was fun until the end where we kinda handwaved stuff a bit too much. Midterms were tough time wise but the final was very fair. Assignments are sometimes annoying.
His exams can be tough, but the lectures are easy to follow and he posts all the notes.
Good lecturer, can have tough exams but the lectures are easy to follow and he posts all the lecture notes
wasn't even in his section but I got mad beef over those exams
visions of the final keep me up at night

DO NO GO TO CLASS ITS A WASTE OF TIME. attending lectures only made me more confused. This man is very kind but sees math in other dimensions which I was too simple to understand. In my current classes whenever math 133 is mentioned everyone gasps and sheds a tear. TRAUMATIZED by those exams.

AVOIDE AT ALL COSTS. Im taking 133 again second semester with a different prof and everything makes sense. Average in the class last sem was a c+. lowest it's been since 2014. save yourself and take this class when Jeremy macdonlad is not writing the exams.

Guys, this professor is just gonna waste your time. I used to go to his lectures every time and each time i went i'd come back with zero gain. He just takes the content of the book and states it in class without explaining anything. He thinks that everybody knows what he is talking about. Khan Academy carried me a lot!

Jeremy is an amazing prof. He takes his time explaining the material and he's super chill. Midterm was easy, final was much much harder but doable. His notes aren't great but you can always read the ones from Miguel's section.

There are two exams and both are very challenging and not reflective of the webwork assignments, or lectures. There was no attendance and his lectures were not useful at all. Every time I went, I regretted going. I highly recommend though, and a quick thank you to Miguel's notes and textbook for making my days better.
Professor Tai is an engaging lecturer with good content and amazing readings. Took as an engineering elective, would recommend, very nice, give great feedback and cares about his course.

Took this class for credit for INTD major and it was my favorite of the semester. Prof is really clear on what the material the midterm/final will have on them so they were really easy to prepare for. I really enjoyed the course content/material, the readings were interesting and he was a pretty funny lecturer towards the end. Highly recommend!

Super interesting class with alot of content so naturally the classes are going to be very cramped. However, he gave us a super extensive and helpful study guide for both the midterm and non cumulative final with all the possible ID's and questions.

hist 218 seems hard at first - many readings, he talks a LOT. however, if you keep up, it's super interesting and he is always there for help. do at least summarize the readings so you can keep up in conference. exams are pretty fair but lots of memorization, as it is a history course!

This class was one of the best ones I had during the semester. The prof was kind and his lectures were very interesting, some of the projects he asked us to do were actually nice, like creating a big character poster. Loved it !

Prof Tai is really an amazing teacher. His lectures were easy to follow, and the readings I found were always interesting as I would prioritize them first for homework. The essay grading WAS tougher than anticipated, but there are ample ways to boost your grade to do well. I learnt a lot in his course.
Truly a caring and dynamic professor who motivates you to do your best with the material. I learned so much from him and the readings he assigned.

Jeremy Tai is by far one of the best history profs at McGill; His seminar was one of my favourites so far, and he set up a great discussion environment. He is super understanding, and flexible as a teacher. You can really tell he cares about his students. About 150p. of reading per week, but don't be scared by his syllabus, great and doable course!

Compact lectures, great selection of readings, effective conferences. Grading is a bit tough on essays, but 25% of the grade is essentially free marks. Also willing to make accommodations regarding workload

Such an incredible professor. He truly cares so deeply for his students and is very accommodating. You definitely read a lot, but the readings are really interesting. I will be taking as many classes with him as a I can.

Honestly, he improved my writing skill. He has his own professional way of teaching students with clear explanations. He gives lots of useful homework. I recommend everyone to take the course with him.
A solid lecturer but be warned that this class is extremely, EXTREMELY difficult.

I attended a few lectures, but not that many. Calc 3 is one of those courses I recommend doing at home, with your textbook and simply going through all the exercices given by prof. I thought his lectures were okay. Midterm is optional (yay) and assignments pretty straightforward. Final was messy. Grading for this course was very generous though.
Speaks fast, writes fast and badly, do all the assigned textbook exercises if you want to do good

He is a very caring professor, but I did not understand any of his lectures. He is very accessible in office hours if ever you have a question, and the tutorials for the class saved me. I recommend reading the textbook before doing the exercices. Midterm was tough but fair and the final was way too hard, had variants we never saw.
Confusing, and overall didn't learn any material from him

Lectures aren't recorded and his lecture notes are illegible so you definitely have to go to class. Teaches in a confusing way but if you read the textbook you'll be fine. Grading on the midterm was very generous but the average was still pretty low.

Jerome's lectures are convoluted and unmotivated.Overall I didn't like the way he presented the material in class. While his midterm was fair, the final was a DISASTER. I don't feel like I learnt much despite my interest in analysis. In fact after taking his class, picking up an analysis book feels scary which is saying something.

Very clear and easy to follow lectures, super easy nice midterm with nice bonus question, but quite a difficult final with pretty much no curve aside from turning a very small part into a bonus question mid-exam which was confusing. Overall I appreciated the lectures and found the content interesting but the final was too hard.

Had to respond to the last rating. Don't get me wrong, Vetois is a great prof, great at lecturing, and I felt like I learned a lot. But the final was definitely not fair. Only 1 part of 1 question was from the list he gave. Yes the questions were easier than homework, but the homework itself was hard (good, but hard) and not reasonable for a final.

The prof's final was fair - he gave a very reasonable list of proofs that could be asked and questions were easier or comparable in difficulty to assignment problems. If you put in the work you will get an A. I also love his accent.

Sjostrom's lectures are really content heavy and difficult to follow at times, because he introduces complex physiology concepts. The good news is that he hardly tests on most of the material he presents, the main focus of his test questions are the math concepts only. His practice problem sets are very well made and are all you need to get an A.
Hard to understand

I expected his section to go smoothly based on those reviews, but this was not the case. His problem sets are helpful for the assignments however the test was not really reflective of the assignment questions and was very tricky. He was also very tough with the grading which did not help.
Very difficult to follow in lectures

Prof Sjöström really tries to help his students by making problem sets (with video explanations) and taking questions from students for review sessions. Outside of class, he is also accessible and open to helping students out with questions. PHGY 311 is a hard class, but Prof Sjöström really tries to make the content clear to students.

Great prof and an even better person! Clearly put a lot of time and effort in preparing for the online delivery of the class. Content can be challenging but make sure to do the practice problems and you're set. Quick turnaround for grading and providing solutions/feedback. Would take again!
One of the best profs i've had. He talks super fast but doesn't test 80% of what he says. Also, his tests are identical to the practice questions which are super easy.

Amazing prof! His tests reflect his practice questions! His lectures a bit hard to understand but he's open for questions which is great! He wants to make sure you understand. A breath of fresh air after Haghighi...

Exam questions were very straightforward. Though the concepts he teaches are tough to understand and a bit intimidating. He presents a lot of frontline research, so referring to the textbook is not very helpful. VERY fast paced lecturer (talks REALLY quickly).

Compared to the other BIOL111 professors, he didn't stand out much. Sort of just read off the slides but other than that, really nothing negative I can say about him. Seems really nice and is an overall solid lecturer.
Lectures had no connecting thread between them, very unclear expectations on important versus supplementary content, went into excess detail about irrelevant points without explaining basic ideas.

I had quite a hard time during the microbe section of biol 111: nothing is written on the slides, and it's hard to keep up during lectures. Questions in exam for this section are also the hardest. The prof still made sure to answer questions.
Super nice guy- super super smart and well respected. Content was really interesting. I would be his friend.

This professor had interesting content but was confusing to listen to. Took it for granted that everyone understood what he was saying and often did not finish his sentence. He was very kind and clearly cared, but his content was more difficult to follow than the other professors. He also jumped back and forth a lot without explaining his thoughts.

Clearly passionate about his work, but his lecture content was the most disorganized out of all the instructors in this course. Rather than going in an intuitive, chronological manner, you jump from DNA replication to viruses, suddenly the tree of life and back to microbes. Great potential, but I wish he just organized better.

Really excited about what he is talking about. His slides are a little confusing and I had to do some of the most revisions and rewatching of lectures for his section but it wasn't too bad. He answers questions in a really good way if you are confused.

Super nice guy who is easy to approach and ask questions regarding his content. However, his lectures were quite difficult to follow as they were unorganized, and his exam questions were somewhat difficult to answer with the information he provides in class, so you will likely have to do extra in-depth research regarding the topics.

the ms frizzle of linguistics.


Seriously do whatever you can to get into 410 if it rotates to her again. Not only is she great at teaching (and being a nice person) but she's also a world-leading expert both on the Mayan family and on a major phenomenon in syntax (ergativity), so this isn't one to miss.

Prof. Coon is easily the coolest professor I've met at McGill. It's almost upsetting how awesome she is. Her lectures are incredibly engaging, she leaves so much room for discussion, questions, and theories, provides extremely thoughtful feedback, and is genuinely interested in hearing what everyone has to say and ensuring everyone is successful.

Prof. Coon's lectures were very engaging and made the 9:30 in Stewart Bio much more bearable! The content covered in her part of the course is definitely tricky, though she breaks it down well. I found her problem sets to be a bit abstract compared to the material covered in class, though the final exam was a bit more straightforward.

Her lectures were super interesting but I found the textbook to be a little clearer at times. The problems sets were difficult but the quizzes were super easy and short. I would say that the textbook is pretty important even though she does cover most of the material.

Jessica was a very good instructor overall and taught difficult course material fairly well in class. Her lecture slides are quite confusing, however, and I often had to re-watch lectures altogether to get a firmer grasp on certain topics. Overall she was very approachable and you can tell she is very passionate about her work.

Her lectures were engaging, but it was difficult to study lecture slides without rewatching the lectures entirely because the notes are quite confusing. She explains concepts in-class quite well, and the material itself was pretty interesting
great teacher!

Jessica was a nice prof and obviously super passionate about the course. That being said, I found concepts were really difficult to grasp as slides were super confusing (could be up to 90 slides long for a 50 min lecture). Recap slides really helped and you 100% need the textbook to survive this half of the course. Also she's great at answering Qs!

Great professor, amazing and charismatic. Explain hard concepts clearly. Her class is rich but well organized. Important concepts are listed in a recap page in her slides. The final is quite easy as long as you understand what's in recap pages.

amazing prof whos great at explaining concepts, makes you really interested in the material. her assignments are NOT easy and heavily application-based, so just "understanding the concepts" is truly the bare minimum you can do to prepare. its easy to get a good grade if you work hard, though. (she only taught the 2nd half of the course)
Great lecturer

Dr. Jessica Head is a very kind and knowledgeable professor. Everything was explained very clearly, and she takes the time to ensure that students fully understand the material before moving on. I really appreciated the content and the logical order of the presentations. The exams are very manageable.

JESSICA IS THE BEST PROF EVER!!!! She is so kind! She uses recent academic tools to teach and make sure we understand the material without the stress of tests and exams, as she understands the students' reality. She is knowledgeable and overall the best prof i have ever had.

Loved prof Head. she made lectures interesting and easy to understand. weekly "quizzes" on material but very easy and helped with understanding. easy and fair midterm. Loved the first part of this course taught by her
lectures are straitforward, but midterm was harsh seems like a good person only teaches the 1st part of this course

I enjoyed having Dr. Head because she is very knowledgeable about the material and incorporates a lot of examples from the literature and her own research to make the material more concrete. I found her better in this course than in AEBI 212 because she is more familiar with the material. Very pleasant, and I would take again!

Prof Head is a solid choice. Everything that's on her exam is included in the slides (no textbook). Her exam was probably one of the easiest exams I've written at McGill. She only taught the first part of this course so none of her info was on the final. But you are bound to receive an A on the midterm at least.

She really cares about being a good prof, but sometimes is very vague and doesn't give a definitive answer. Also, she has a lot of mistakes on her slides, which can be confusing. But in general she is a really caring prof and when she brings her own insight to the course that makes it more interesting.

Had her the 2nd time she taught this class. She seemed to not know the material thoroughly. Answered student questions with "I don't know" a lot. Clearly trying hard to be a better professor (e for effort), but still needs to improve. Tests very fair. Slides follow textbook closely. Interesting material, but class was boring, which is unfortunate.

Really nice professor, will always answer your questions and puts a lot of time into making sure everything is clear. The class got more interesting as the semester progressed and the exams are extremely fair!

First year she taught organism 2.  No required textbook, just read and memorize her slides.  There is a lot of vocabulary for this course that you have to memorize.  Labs are a joke, they are not very useful you basically just look under microscope or do dissections in groups.  Lab exam was kind of difficult you need to be adequately prepared.
Fair final if you did the practice problems and went to class. Overall good teacher but should improve on her public speaking skills.
Good lecturer and exams ranged from medium to hard. I found herself to be a bit attitudinal/pretentious though and didn't record her lectures:(

Decent teacher but very hard and long exams. It was the only class that I had that semester that was not recorded and the notes that were hard to follow in my opinion. Even though I went to every class I ended up relying on the website Paul's Online Math Notes to really understand what was going on.

Overall prof Lin is pretty good for ode with great lectures and clear handwriting. Her exams are very long and questions are worded unclearly which caused some confusion. But she has a good grading scheme which is very forgiving and eventually I ended up with a good grade.
Her exams were hard for absolutely no reason, especially the final people left laughing.

AVOID AT ALL COST. If you want to take Professor Lin's MATH475, please read Partial Differential Equations in Action: From Modelling to Theory by Sandro Salsa. Her taste on choice of text is very special and her lectures are consequently hard to understand. The midterm and final were both extremely difficult. Assignment load is very heavy as well.
Her lectures are clear, interesting and easy to follow, and she cares about her students. She has great hand-writing.

I also want to counteract the person who posted 4 consecutive bad reviews out of spite. Prof Lin is a great teacher. The notes aren't typed, but they are definitely clear. The accusation that people cheated on the mid term is baseless. It is apparent that she wants students to master the material and gives ample opportunity to do so.

Prof Lin is a great professor, and I didn't find her notes unclear. Lectures are fruitful, and homework is solid. Please remark the four consecutive 1.0 rating below are all posted on dec 8. I suspect the authors might be the same person, so readers want to be careful.
Choski is infinitely many times better than her

Jessica is honestly the best! She is energetic, fun and most importantly fair . She is amazing with feedback and is always by your side when needed. Just make sure to go to class because she is always aware of who shows up (even if you think you got away without her realizing - trust me she realized).

Pretty good teacher, was an accountant before and it's pretty clear she loves what she's doing. Maybe a little too much. Exams are fair and she tells you exactly what to expect on it. Do all the textbook questions and u should be good. If the class average for the midterm is below 75% she'll get really worried and curve the next one.
I definitely learnt a lot from this class! I highly recommend doing as many practice questions as possible!

The class is overall, not complicated. Jingjing is a very clear, concise, and engaging professor. I really enjoyed lecture and although it is not mandatory, highly suggest going! The material itself is not that complicated and Jingjing does a very good job of presenting what is relevant and not relevant from the textbook. Overall, great prof!

Her lectures are very clear, slides are useful, and she's overall quite helpful and kind. Still, you'll need to study with the textbook, lectures are not enough. Final exam was extremely difficult and theoretical - nothing like practice final. But MGCR211 profs are very consistent, it doesn't really matter which you get-exams, grading are the same.

IMO she's overrated on here. She is just okay and slides are mediocre. I went to all lectures, wasn't really useful, she goes fast and on a surface level, often leaving things ambiguous for us to "figure out at home". Get the book, read the sections taught in class to understand fully + do all the practice problems. Exams are challenging but fair.

Jingjing was by far the best prof. I had last semester. She let you know exactly what she expects of all her students at the beginning of the semester. You don't need to attend the lectures but it does help to hear her explain things in person and do the in-class exercises with her. Midterm was brutal, but they made the final easy. Got an A-

Prof. Zhang was the best professor I had last semester. Her lectures are straightforward, fun, and well-paced; you definitely need to attend them if you want to do well in MGCR 211. She was extremely helpful and accessible during office hours too. Just make sure you do more practice problems than she recommends--the midterm and final were tough.
Difficult to remain attentive, the class is very slow and her lectures are not engaging whatsoever.
Prof. Jingjing is really helpful and caring. You can ask her everything in her office hour and she is patient all the time.
Put in a lot of work and you'll see the results
She is a real stubborn prof. not at all helpful. It took me 5 days to do the assignments and she didnot accept it because she said I was five minutes late for class.

Not a fan of his teaching style whatsoever. His slides are really disorganized and hard to understand: he complicated the course so much and the only way I got through was by watching youtube videos. Exams are a little weird since he takes textbook problems and tweaks them so that they're impossible to solve under the time constraint.

Lectures can get a bit boring because he reads off slides, you can learn by yourself with the textbook if you want. Midterms and finals were pretty hard, definitely do a lot and a lot of practice problems in the textbook.

Great prof, made the exams easy and I feel like he literally gave us everything to get high grades
Do the hw and tutorials you should be good. Hopefully I can get him again in a future mech class

The ratings on this reacher can vary from person to person. Personally, he just read off slides, assigned homework questions, spoke very fast, wasnt clear, and expects you to answer questions a lot harder than the ones covered in class. IMO he is not a good teacher.

Not helpful outside of class, didn't show up his office hour right before midterm. Crazy long final exam, you wouldn't pass if you did bad on midterms. Course organization was overall pretty bad, TAs not helpful at all. Avoid!

Clear grading criteria. This course had higher weightage for project. Need not attend all the classes, but strongly recommend you to attend the lectures as it is useful for the final examination. This professor takes a lot of efforts to make the class interesting and is really passionate about the subject.

His lectures were a lot of reading off slides which were just not my cup of tea, and his worked examples weren't always the clearest. The 2 midterms were pretty fair but the final definitely required some very good understanding of the course material and combining things in ways you hadn't seen in class.
The professor did his best to convey and manage the course materials. Midterms and final I took were very reasonable. Recommended

Professor Li is very caring and you can tell he really wants the students to understand. Even for a course he claimed to be relatively "boring" for him, he still puts in a lot of effort to teach every lesson clearly and go over many examples in class. He does good review before exams and is takes feedback seriously. Great professor!

He was one of the sweetest professors I've ever had. He genuinely cares about helping you understand the course material, and doesn't make it unnecessarily hard for no reason. Not an easy A, but you can get there if you do the practice problems and show up to class.
One of the best profs I ever had. Caring, smart and really knows his stuff. Very clear and well-organised lectures. Exams are hard but fair. Class is not recorded so make sure to go!

I simply love this prof. He is so clear about his lectures and he definitely knows what he is teaching about. But his exams are hard, testing both memorization and understanding. Makes me work for it.

He's probably the best lecturer in the Department of Chemistry - speaks really well and logically. His pace is great and he answers questions very fluidly. It's obvious that he really knows his stuff. His exams are very difficult and he can be very uncompromising.
Seriously tough grader, makes you work for it - excellent lecturer
I found the lectures super interesting and Gleason really knows his stuff. The 2 midterms are quite difficult but fair.

His classes are really well delivered and thought out. His lectures, to me, are very clear and he presents with a lot of detail and uses some real life examples as well which can be interesting. You have to know the content really well to pass, if you don't you're in for a tough time. He puts up a few practice questions and a paper which is good.

Prof. Gleason was pretty impressive. He would enter class and draw mechanisms from memory. He definitely knows the course material. He can be pompous at times but overall I think he was a decent professor. No complaints here!

Loved this course thanks to the prof! Made organic 3 extremely engaging and interesting. He explains very well and spends a fair amount of time on difficult concepts.  The exams are fair provided you're well prepared for them.

Awesome prof. He explains well and in details. Apparently all the hate comes from the fact that in the previous years, the exams were extremely hard. The exams we've had were pretty challenging but very fair.

He is one of the best chemistry teachers I have ever had. He is passionate, makes the material very clear and extremely interesting. The only downside is that his powerpoints have many structures and reactions but very few words, so if you miss a single class, you are screwed. Apart from that, he is very helpful and gives up his own time to help.
Richard is an amazing teacher! His class is fair and realistic of what social workers would encounter in their practice. I would definitely take another of his classes, too bad he only teaches one!

Rick is extremely fair. He does not believe in memorization; the final exam is open book and the assignments are done in groups. He is extremely knowledgable in the field and is very useful for answering questions. Most of the class is spent going over the course pack so attendance isn't mandatory  but his comments are important.
Very useful class, the coursepack is a bible for all budding social workers. He is hilarious and is basically Larry David undercover!
Best prof I've ever had! He has a great sense of humour he's extremely helpful. Ask him any question and he'll be pleased to answer! Montreal's Woody Allen!
extraordinary prof! the trick is to participate in class. if you participate, you're guaranteed an A. he's not out to trick you - very straight-forward! his great sense of humour is a plus!

AMAZING class, AMAZING prof! He is like a walking encyclopedia! Ask any question and he knows plus he is a law graduate! It was an honor to be taught by him! Exams are easy, but make sure you put ALOT of detail!
Make sure you ask questions! What he says he wants, and how he ends up grading are 2 different things. You'll do great if you really participate.
No Comments

Kanaris is very kind and very handsome. He's truly passionate about religion and it shows in his lectures. However, he tends to speak in what I can best describe as "riddles", which makes it difficult to understand what he's actually trying to say. I had to rely on the textbook and course slides to learn and properly study for the test.

Kanaris struggles to keep his students engaged. He fails to maintain an organized syllabus and class schedule, and his slides are often riddled with spelling mistakes. He draws almost exclusively from textbook content, making the class sterile and uninspired. I expect professors to approach their work with care. It appears Kanaris does not.

Professor Kanaris is feverish about religious studies to the point that he talks in riddles. Most of the class don't understand him and even few could follow his lectures. Most of the students read the textbook and hoped for the best. The grading criteria for his tests were confusing.

Prof. Kanaris is by far the most passionate professor at my time at McGill. I personally found the content of the course quite difficult but it was definitely an interesting course that I don't regret taking (even if it did tank my gpa). If you are remotely interested in religious studies take this class as a pass/fail option.

Exams don't contain unexpected content and can be studied for with the slides and textbook (relatively low amount of reading). The prof seems to really care about his subject and knows his stuff, so if you're truly passionate about the study of religion and would like to actively participate in class, I would suggest.

Great professor. He genuinely cares for his students and answers every question, in fact he'd wish there were more questions. He loves participation and when you take time to engage with the material, what he says will make more sense. I suggest doing the readings before class because it's difficult to simplify the concepts in class.
He waffles so much

Kanaris is a passionate professor who really knows his stuff, but the class can be a struggle. Definitely read the textbook and use Unstuck study for study prep - the AI-driven practice questions were a lifesaver. Go to office hours and get to know your TA too. Overall, it's a rewarding class if you put in the effort.

Too difficult for an intro class, lots of reading and understanding of the teachers pov and not any other or self. Especially worse is the for gradding, 35% exam, 40% exam and 25 paper. Bad grading spred

You cannot understand him, you cannot reach him you can barely survive a class of his if youre not ready to read. Apart from reading you have to understand the text the way he does- this means you have to somehow pray that you understand what hes actually trying to get at amongst all the waffling. Seems like he just likes listening to his own voice

Feels poorly organized despite having a clear outline. Lectures unclear but you have to go due to attendance. Textbook feels like reading a fictional story compared to similar online materials. Graded on exams and participation. Later practice questions lack solutions. Not the hardest but definetly the worst CS course I've taken at McGill.

The semester just started and I already cant with this teacher. Never seen a teacher that makes easy concepts look complicated like she does. Whenever I listen to her she just looks like a student making an oral presentation and half understands the subject. And there are pop quizzes that counts so you must attend class.

I'm surprised so many found this course difficult, might be one of the easiest ones besides COMP370 &COMP307. Professor Guo was amazing, lectures very clear ¬ heavy. We did have 4 graded labs & pop quizzes, but they were all graded leniently&easy. The exam was easy too, cheatsheet allowed.lectures not recorded, and pop quiz(with x days window)
Class is insanely hard. Explanations are not good. Syntax matters (you have to write Java code on paper without missing a single symbol). Not recommended.

Guo is so far the best 303 prof you can have imo. I did not expect the material to be easy, but she is always happy to help you succeed. I do agree that this course is poorly designed, but it's not her fault.

Class was aight, the exams weren't particularly difficult or out to get you. Most concepts are taught solely around the Java implementation which makes it not that applicable to other languages -- the ideas around them are pretty important universal though. Jin Guo is perfectly nice and helpful, but I still think this course needs to be reworked.

Prof Guo truly cares about her students and is always patient to answer our questions during or after class. Her pace is good so you won't feel rushed or that it's too boring. Her in-class code from GitHub basically sums up what you need to learn and the midterm and final were very fair.

I thought she was great! Her lectures may not be the most fascinating, but I thought she explained concepts well and if you complement the lectures with reading the textbook, it's definitely not that hard to get a good grade in her course. I thought the grading scheme was very fair and forgiving.

Prof Guo isn't bad, shes just teaching a hard course and out of all the profs who teach 303 she's by far the best. Many of the lectures are not great but for a McGill COMP professor, they're very interactive. Also, she cared about the comments I made in OH. Yall could just tell her all the negative stuff to her face and shed probably try to fix it.

I feel that Prof Guo cares about her students but how she explains things make the concepts even more confusing. You can go to her office hours, she tries to re-explain the concepts, sometimes things click you know. Lecture+textbook+in-class code+lab should be enough to get a good grade.
Professor Cho is irresponsible, ignoring students' emails.
Professor Cho is a tough and mean professor, always chewing gums in her lectures. There is no chance to contact with her after class, please think twice when you have this class.
At First, she is a professor in University of Toronto. She is a bad professor, don't take her class.

She is not a good teacher. Her lectures are so boring and disorganized, TA can do better lecture than she does. Don't take this class, and don't take any classes of Michelle Cho, unless you wanna have class with a self-centered professor.
Can't contact with the professor...She did not reply emails. Hate her.

Took multiple courses with her (not by choice; courses were required for my program) Please avoid her. I could write an entire thesis on why this woman should never have become a professor. TLDR: boring, refuses to answer emails or give grades back, insane amount of readings, not even a particularly nice person.

Easy in the sense that theres no tricky material to learn, as long as u can write well youll be ok. Slept through everything & didnt even read anything past the 5th week because there was honestly no point, pretty much taught myself. Shes nice but completely unreliable I still have an unopened email from sept that she hasnt replied to lol

I spoke to numerous classmates because I thought it was just me having the worst time of my life in prof Cho's class but turns out it was universal. You basically have to learn the entire course on your own and I can't even defend incompetence by saying she's a nice person because she's not. I have nothing positive to say about her.

She hides behind this nice smile and fake caring persona when in reality she's the complete opposite. I'd almost rather she be horrible and mean upfront. Add that onto her incompetence and disorganization of a prof, as well as her inability to respond to any emails, and you have quite possibly one of the worst professors uoft has to offer.

Prof Cho is tactless, incompetent, and disingenuous. She comes off nice but is actually very uncaring about her students.
