It's basically her just rambling off topic for 2 hours.

Energetic and engaging in the classroom. Very caring. Covers a lot of material that's practical not just theoretical. But he also gives practice exams that reflect and prepare you for the real final and grading is fair. Feedback on homeworks is on the slow side though I heard he does all the grading himself rather than using undergrads.

He is a very caring Prof who had a tough semester due to his personal extenuating circumstances he is experiencing. When approached by meeting one on one, he will give you the time needed to understand the content and extend deadlines. 

His class was very practical for real finance jobs (m&a) in the market.
Very caring about his students, wants all the students to succeed and won't try to trick you on the finals.

Came in expecting a great class given this prof's ratings—was badly surprised. He lectures assuming we all understand; participation is 10% but there's no chance to speak. The course lacks structure, and multiple group deadlines were dropped last-minute, back-to-back. Would not recommend. No grades yet; hope he's an easy grader...
Guy yaps so much and assumes you know all the content
Best finance teacher at McGill! Make sure you take him for FINE 447!

This is a great professor. He is very inspirational, although at times he might he might come off as distant. The content taught is very interesting, although not enough focus on quantitative parts. He also gives personalised feedback which is great. I highly recommend this professor for Venture Capital.

This is a follow-up review as I found that learning materials in my taught-PG course were almost all covered by Jiro, and previous notes are always useful. Course materials are kind of challenging but if you understand all examples in class and in homeworks you will get at least A-. He is the best professor I've ever met. 100% recommended.

Professor Kondo is the best professor you could ask for at McGill. Cares about his students, he is always available after class to answer questions, and he is so knowledgeable. If you have the chance to take a class with him, do not hesitate. It will be difficult, but so rewarding.

One of the best professors I've had at Desautels!!! He is really amazing. You can learn a lot of real world things in his class because his class is practical. The final exam is hard, but doable. He curved a lot, so you don't need to worry about that.

Awesome educator, the class was super interesting and really covered what I wanted to learn about libraries and info behaviour. Not super interested in students outside of class though. Nice but not likeable. She let go of all her responsibilities towards students (advising, feedback) when she had papers to write despite faculty saying otherwise :/

Great class to get experience presenting (lots of mini presentations). Textbook was weird/dated, wouldn't recommend. The class and the teacher were great though. Definitely take to up your presentation style game.

Health Science: Great class and textbook. Prof is very passionate about the subject matter. Lectures are full of real life examples. Lots of practice assignments. One group presentation. Final project was to make an Info pamphlet for a health user group. Classes were fun and full of discussions.
a great prof

Great teacher. Awesome, quirky sense of humour. She doesn't fill you with any delusions about the profession. Fair marker. Provides you with PRACTICAL knowledge. Even if you're not interested in the library stream like me, she still teaches you valuable skills that can apply to any information profession.
If you are considering graduate work with Joann Whalen, be very careful. She and her husband/lab manager have a history of abusing students.
An absolute star. Fantastic lecturer and teacher. Extremely humble. If you attend the lectures and participate during the classes and labs you'll do fine. Actually took SOIL 315.

she is super dedicated to her students, gives very detailed feedback, always challenges students to do more and think more. Assignments are inspiring and challenging, includes a lot of presentation. If you research well, you will get good grades, she values both the quality and quantity of your effort. Very accessible outside class. Amazing prof.
Took her Soil ecology class and really liked it, which I didn't expect. She was nice and friendly.

This was probably the easiest course I have ever taken. Cool topic but the lectures were unfortunately boring. Prof Maclure is a nice dude tho. Grade is a few short papers and a final. The different TAs graded in different ways so it was hard to tell how you were doing in the beginning, but the final was ridiculously easy.

His lectures were a bit repetitive and boring. The assignments had bare minimum level of description and were sometimes based on bad quality lecture recordings. The grading was pretty lenient, but taking intro to philosophy and learning mostly about AI, which involved a lot of what seemes like technical terms, was difficult.
I took PHIL 201. The class lectures were disorganized, but the content was simple, and the assignments were straightforward.

The class I took was PHIL 201. His lectures are incredibly boring and repetitive but whatever. The issue comes in with the assignment. They have no guideline and are based off of lecture recordings with TERRIBLE quality making it incredibly difficult to dissect the relatively dense content provided. Miserable work.

The grading is lenient but the lectures were surprisingly boring and the prof had a tendency to ramble about topics that weren't on the syllabus or in the readings. Also disorganized - didn't post assignment instructions or presentations to MyCourses. Overall he's ok, not the best or the worst.

CANS 200 gives a strong overview of Canada from both historical and contemporary perspectives. Some people complained about the difficulty, but in my view the class wasn't very challenging as long as you attended regularly and did the readings. I found that Professor Nurse really wanted people to succeed + was very supportive if you put in effort!

Dr. Nurse is extremely clear with her expectations and perhaps the most organized professor I've encountered at McGill. Exam was more than fair/reasonable. Readings are interesting and simple. Overall, the class is an easy A if you know how to follow specific requirements and instructions. Would take again!

One of the best professors at McGill! I've taken her twice, once in the large CANS 200 lecture-based course and once in the smaller CANS 301 course. She was excellent in both, but she really shines in smaller, seminar-style courses!

She is very kind; however, the TAs and their grading seemed to be a bit inconsistent. Lectures were quite monotone and personally made me a bit sleepy, but the content is interesting! Both the TAs and Dr. Nurse were very accessible via email, which was helpful. The exam questions were very generous as well.

Overall good teacher! loved this class and its content, however the lectures were very monotone and its felt like she was just reading for the slides, which makes it really difficult to lock in. However, she does post lecture recordings, as well as explain whats on the final, which overall makes the class a lot easier.

Dr Nurse is one of the sweetest profs at McGill.She posts all her slides and recordings, which are very easy to follow. One thing to note is that sometimes during lectures, it feels like she's just reading from her slides, which leads to the class falling asleep and the lecture room becoming emptier each week.

Jodey is truly a hidden gem at McGill. I have taken two of her classes and am planning on taking two more of hers. She is great in big lectures and small ones. I love her because I always know what she expects of me (extensive rubrics) and is lenient if necessary. You can tell that she loves what she does. Take a class with her if you can.

Prof. Nurse is amazing! I took her for 301 and 312, and in both courses, she fostered engaging and insightful dialogue about the material, which encouraged comprehension rather than memorization. Her written assignments were well-designed, and her feedback allowed me to substantially improve my writing. She's also a very fair grader. Take her!

Dr. Nurse is the nicest professor. Her assigned readings are very reasonable as well as her assignments. She's always available for help and genuinely cares about her students. I highly recommend taking her classes if you can!
CANS 420 is a great class. It's mostly guest lecture based with amazing guests (Canadian Senators and policymakers for example). Professor Nurse is also amazing

She is the best professor I've had at Mcgill by a mile, and probably the best teacher I've had in my life. I have been struggling with my other classes and grades and my advisor told me NOT to take this course because of the workload. DO NOT listen to them. There is homework everyday, but only for completion marks. 
You will enjoy the elective.
hands down the best instructor at mcgill— nay, in the world
It's a good class, professor is very nice and grades pretty generously.

Jodie Beck is a great prof who cares about her students. She gives out a lot of homework but this is standard for any language course at McGill. She is very willing to make time for you if you need assistance on anything.

Professor Beck is amazing. She clearly values students' success and makes Japanese very approachable. She corrects work extremely quickly, answers questions in great detail, and is overall a cool person. There's a lot of homework and studying, but that's why it's 4.5 credits per semester! If you keep up and work hard, you'll definitely do well.

Beck sensei is an amazing prof and person! She really cares a lot about her students. Her lectures are well structured and interesting, however, be prepared to work hard as language courses can be overwhelming. I honestly had such a great time and even enjoyed going to class every day. I definitely recommend taking this course if it's with her!!

so wonderful, always puts in the work to answer student questions. Marks homework very quickly, tests and quizzes graded and returned within 2 days! sometimes she emails everyone individually on weekends to give feedback before a test. Very fun small class environment. 10/10 recommend if you're serious about learning Japanese

She gives out tons of homeworks but it indeed helps us to get good grades on quizzes and tests. She is very helpful too! she would reply you thru email within a few hours if u have any questions with regards to any materials from the lecture. + very organized too. overall, an excellent lecturer but bit heavy on homework.

Prof Neslehova cares about her students. However, she seems unaware of the fact that students have other courses. This is one of the heaviest assignment courses I have taken after 3 years of math! She's accessible, and answers questions clearly, but I didn't find her lectures as clean as other people did. Would avoid unless you adore statistics.

Johanna is the best stats prof that I've had at McGill. Her lectures are extremely clear and she is very kind and helpful during office hours. GLM is a great class, and the material is truly interesting. I'm an engineering student but I was able to get A just by attending lectures and reading the Agresti book thoroughly.

Overall, it was a very challenging class. Johanna gives practice exams before the midterm and final, which are REALLY helpful in my opinion because the material is very hard and there's a lot of it! The book was useful but not necessary! Only take this class if you're willing to put in the hard word
Johanna is a great prof. She goes fast, but she will post useful material and usually is very helpful in office hours.

She is good compared to other statistics professors, but she teaches very fast. However, her notes are clear and she is helpful during office hours. I took math 523 with her and she started rushing through the course material after the midterm - it was crazy. Finally, her assignments are helpful for learning the material, but they are very long.

GLM itself is a hard course. Professor Neslehova's not the best one, but certainly not the worst. You need to read the textbook before lectures or you will be lost forever because she goes over material real fast. The exam and assignments are tough but the grading is not that harsh.

I had Johanna for QEP intro & Evaluations. She regurgitates the QEP but also actively contradicts herself when explaining how we are allowed to evaluate as per the QEP. Have never ever used what I learned in her class. Also, not understanding, forced me to come to class with a raging fever or else I would fail. Would avoid, but that's impossible.

Toth is a pretty chill dude and a prof that wants to and does everything to see his students succeed. He's clear about whats being tested and gives a clear outline so that students study whats actually being tested. Lot of profs could take a lesson from him.. jmac😔

I took the class in 2025 Fall. The lectures were given in a very structured way, with no redundancy. The notes are helpful. However, typos usually appear in his blackboard writing and notes, which could make the materials really confusing.

This course was taught straight out of Folland's textbook, with some extra time devoted to certain proofs and examples. While the content is interesting, Toth's presentation of it is neither inspiring nor horrible. Although, he consistently extended assignment deadlines close to their due date. On the other hand, he graded quite leniently.

There is an isometric isomorphism between his lectures and Folland's textbook "Real Analysis: Modern Techniques and Their Applications." Since this is the first year students are allowed to skip analysis 3 and 4 to take 564, he is especially lenient.

Toth is hilarious, sometimes intentionally, sometimes not. His superpower is explaining the concepts in the way that you might not understand every epsilon of the proof, but you get the overall idea. Exam questions were very application based, but the exams were a fair bit harder than the given practices. Assignments graded generously.

Toth's course was exceedingly difficult. He is a lax grader for homeworks, mostly because he doesn't care what amount of detail you go into. The exams are tough, and he grades based on arbitrary criteria. I got marks off for an answer other people gave and got full credit, which kept me from getting a perfect score. Go to office hours for this one.

Engaging lectures, especially given how passionate he is on topics related to his research. Always willing to answer questions and provide additional resources to help learn the material. Would take him again
He is a good dude. Lectures are clear and his proofs are very detailed. He is understanding and asks for feedback to make sure pacing is good. Exams are reasonable but grades are 90% based on exams

It's tough to do well in this class as the evaluations mostly consist of multiple-choice questions, making it hard to earn any partial class. His examples did not reflect the difficulty of his evaluations.
Exams were all multiple choice which sucks cause I couldn't get partial marks and you could lose marks for dumb arithmetic mistakes. I hated this class. Ruined my GPA.
Drained my excitement for my Econ major this guy is bored too bored to help u prepare for his 70 percentttttt final

RUN never suffered so much in my life, slides don't help at all, exams are on topics and problems that were never covered, can't understand shyt even if you attend every single lecture, so stingy with past exams and practice problems, just RUN, had to change my econ major to smt else bc i cannot bear taking him again
ok upon that midterm im sorry galbraith ur might just be a decent guy
Good teacher, not as bad as people claim.

He is nice and extremely knowledgeable in economics but he should not be teaching an intro undergraduate class. it's impossible to tell from his lectures what is actually relevant to the course versus what he's just rambling about. Everything is vague and theoretical and he doesn't give practice problems to actually learn the math. Nice guy tho

Really nice person and obviously really smart. However lectures are pretty boring and he wrote the textbooks so you can just use that and lectures slides to study. Exams are really fair and he curves the final grade. You can also try to negotiate your grade, he is really understanding.

He's very kind and clever, unfortunately a very boring lecturer. Barely showed up to class and just read the notes, went ok. Midterm was not too bad but each MCQ was worth 10 pts (?), final was very easy. Involves fairly easy math, and a lot of theory to remember

Please drop unless required for major. Doable but not worth it, weighing of the assignments is completely ridiculous (midterm 25%, final 70%,  practice sheets worth 5%).  Clearly very smart and sweet but not everyone is meant to be a teacher; the lectures are not engaging. Skip lecs and use the slides to teach yourself. Focus on the THEORY.

Currently taking this class.I haven't missed a lecture,I read our given notes/textbook, nothing is correlated incredibly unorganized. Always goes on unrelated tangents. This professor didn't post the midterm date, and on the day that all the econ major's had a different midterm he disclosed the midterm would be in a week.class is interesting but...

IMPOSSIBLE. How are you supposed to pass this course with empty 15-pages slides while the tests include excruciatingly long formulas, concepts not mentionned in lectures and no justification required for finals ????

Paper was the most intimidating part of the course (12-15 pages). Difficult to manage with other courses and full time jobs, but anything is possible with time management and a little effort. Easy to say "I'll take it next semester" but just get it done!!! Really not bad overall. Exams are mostly opinion based questions and a case study
A good professor. Long lectures but he puts his lectures online, which is great. exams were easy but long.
Very entertaining with real-life examples of lecture material. Communicates well, loads of experience to share. Pay attention in his class, tough marker.

Dr. White did the endocrinology section. His slides have a lottt of information, and he does occasionally say something in the lecture that is not mentioned on the slides. He explains for the most part very clearly, but can be quite confusing at times. That being said, his final questions were extremely fair, and the content was interesting!

His slides are full of text and he mostly reads them and then goes on tangents. He explains pretty ok but you can mostly just read his lectures and you're good. His questions focus mostly on vitamin D
He can't teach, he only reads off the slides and doesn't explain anything lol
All im going to say is dont go to the lecture if you didnt look at the notes ahead of time, because he goes pretty fast and i found it hard to follow.

Not the best but not the worst. His section (endocrinology) is not at all hard to understand, it just requires a lot of memorization. His lecture slides are way too busy and he basically just reads off of them so going to class isn't super necessary, though some slides he says don't learn the details. Questions are ok, just memorize the stuff.

Easy exam questions. Does not test little details. I bought the NTCs, read them and went to the exam finding his section a breeze. Endocrinology was overall interesting. Would recommend. I'm happy they offer it in PHGY 210.
Awesome prof, makes endocrinology a piece of cake! Everything you need to know is in his lecture slides, and his exam questions are by far the easiest in the course.
he is a bad prof, reads of his slides and doesn't explain anything. he is unorganized and lectures in a condescending manner, and everything he says is jumbled together with no real structure.
His slides contains everything you need to know, he basically reads off of them. Exam questions are representative of the basic concepts covered, doesn't press you for too many details
Great prof, made endocrinology, a topic that i found quite tedious and boring in the past, very interesting! Fair exam questions too!

Very nice prof, the lectures are really interesting! Even if there is a LOT to read for exams (prioritize textbook), he makes exam reviews and reuses a lot of questions which makes it easier to succeed. There are no trick questions! He also calculates your grade in whichever way is better for you in the end.

the midterm wasn't easy and doesn't give study guides. However, you can tell he wants his students to do well by adding bonus points to exams and gives students best possible marks. He'll do review sessions and adds those question on the exams which is helpful if u memorize them. he also adds bonus points from conferences (up to %10 per exam)

Prof. Lydon is very sweet and has good lectures. However, there is very low overlap with the textbook which means you have to read and know it very well since 60% of the exams are on the textbook. Make sure to focus on all the definitions, how to apply them, research cases and their findings in both lectures and the book to do well in this class.

Interesting class but very heavy readings and lectures. Exam questions are based on lectures and textbook but super detailed so not a class you can cram for. Slides are lacking info so I suggest skipping the lecture and watching the recordings for most effective notes. Final was cumulative which was torture.

These reviews made me fear Lydon before taking the class but he ended up being my favorite professor of my semester. You can easily get 3+ points of extra credit on each exam (very generous). Most of the exams are based on the textbook chapters (60 ish pages per chapter) so pretty heavy but very doable (i'm usually not an A student so believe me).

The absolute goat, I loved his class so much. Very funny and engaging, lots of extra credit available. The course is very reading heavy, it is NOT a class where you can cram. Many people complain about the poorly made powerpoint presentations, however if you listen to the lecture recordings you can easily get all the info you need.
Absolutely loved his class. He's funny, makes lectures engaging, and the textbook is easy to read + annotate. TAs were also super helpful. 10/10 would recommend :)

Lydon is one of the best profs I've had at McGill so far. He's so passionate and makes class fun and engaging. Social Psych is a very interesting course, and it's not difficult to do well as long as you really commit yourself to the readings (exams are 60% reading based). Definitely would take again, and you learn very valuable information

Professor Lydon is engaging, but the course is demanding. The exams cover ~ten lectures with horrifically disorganized slides, as well as 40 paged textbook chapters that don't align with lectures at all and carry an insane amount of information. The workload is so overwhelming alongside a full class schedule.

Definitely read the textbook. Lectures can be a bit disorganized but as long as you know the studies he presents and read the textbook you should be fine. He's really nice and super engaging. Lectures are definitely not boring

Prof. Presley is a solid prof with some really good traits, and some pretty bad ones as well. He makes it very clear what's tested, has good slideshows, and generally finishes class early as well which is nice. But he is very monotonous (class is so boring), the exams are pretty tough (u gotta know ur stuff) and he goes on a lot of tangents

Seems like a nice guy but cannot string two sentences together in a coherent manner. It's shocking how bad he is at explaining simple ideas. Avoid at all costs as he will destroy ur will to learn. So confusing, so boring.
His slides include everything that will be on the exam.
Super nice guy, but you cant understand his lectures at all. You'll have to learn by yourself.

In lectures right now, the way he constantly stumbles over his ideas and shuffles through any slides gives me anxiety. listening to the lecture takes patience exercises. But ill hand it to him he does make it clear what's testable, which is the important part at the end.

He's a bit monotonous, but his lectures are very clear and comprehensive. Everything you need to know for his exams are on his slides. His exam questions are straight forward, so if you pay attention during class, you'll do well. Although he doesn't really answer emails, he's willing to take questions during/after lecture. Overall, great prof!

He isn't the most entertaining professor, I had a lot of trouble paying attention to class and we had 2 midterms and an open book final exam. All I had to do for the class was show up and I wrote notes along with his powerpoint slides (which he shared with us), and I did great. I didn't study at all. He's also a nice person and he grows on you! :)

He is definitely not a good lecturer. The lectures seem to organize well but the way he presents materials can be confusing since he always corrects himself. He is very clear in what he will test like what part to memorize. The midterm was easy but the assignment & final are painful to answer. He didn't reply to emails, even during final >:(

Did not answer any of my mails, including the ones for the final, or lecture questions. Never took the time go over materials again to make sure we understood or answer questions in class. Made a fair midterm though, but still concepts were too blurry.

I'll admit that I didn't like him much at first. He grew on me throughout the semester though: he goes at a fairly slow pace so it's easy to follow in class and is explicit about which material is important for the exam. His slides could use some updating though.

Extremely kind and funny prof. He clearly knows his stuff and is very passionate about climate systems. The course is very straightforward — both in terms of content and grading. I also loved that he brought in guest lecturers!

Great prof with clear lectures and slides, a nice grading schedule that clearly acknowledges that many people are taking this as an easy elective. Prof. Gyakum is clearly passionate about the subject and I have left this course feeling so much more educated on the situation in the world. Everyone should take this class! Excellent prof!!

Super kind prof, you can really tell he cares a lot about teaching and the course. The class has very little homework and few assignments, and he is always willing to answer questions and help you out.

Really great! Every positive review of this class is 100% true. Both of the profs (John and John) are very passionate and knowledgeable. I encourage you to come to class and share any personal experiences with a natural disaster - they will really enjoy hearing about it! Found the TAs good as well. Great and light elective to take.

I love Professor Gyakum! He clearly cares a lot about what he teaches his students and he is so kind! His lectures are super interesting and there has been some really interesting class discussions. I found the workload easy to handle. This class, as well as ATOC185, is amazing and I highly recommend taking his classes!

I love Prof Gyakum! He is the best. I also took ATOC 185 with him and he was great there too. They are seen as bird courses but honestly you learn a lot of cool stuff and it's fun to learn. He is very caring and he makes the content easy to understand. The grading is very fair, and the term papers are simple to do. I 100% WOULD DO THIS CLASS AGAIN!
Super interesting class and great lecturer. The content is very manageable and grading is super fair. I really recommend him for an easy yet fun elective.
Sweetest man ever, when a TA strike arose, he personally took time to review my essay. Nicest Prof I've had so far here.

Prof Gyakum is one of the best profs out there. He obviously loves what he does and just wants to share it with us, which makes his lessons super interesting and digestible. The grading is very reasonable and he wants you to get a good great, so he is always accessible.

His dry humour and deadpan delivery goes well with Prof Stix's silliness. It felt like I was watching a standup routine on the last day during the natural disaster survival lesson. He's smart and passionate about the class, but 90% of his slides were charts or graphs, making it hard to take notes. His voice can make you sleepy sometimes.

Dr. Saba is the cornerstone professor of the Aviation Management Program at McGill. LOTS of interesting PowerPoint slides that he does not share with students, but he does not mind if you take snapshots with you phone from time to time. VERY caring and supportive. TALKS a lot, but very knowledgeable and interesting. CHALLENGING term project.

One of the best profs at McGill. Saba is a great guy who actually cares about students. He may seem like a typical serious prof but he's actually quite nice and approachable. Slides are fun and very colourful but you need to take down notes like mad. Although he can be a bit verbose but this is still my favourite class, learned so much! Thumbs up!

One of the most boring classes I've ever taken. Each lecture, he shows you zillions of slide but does not upload them on mycourses. Sticks to the textbook but goes deeper than the text with his slides. Attendance mandatory. I'd say do not take it.

Super interesting course with Saba. He tries his best to make his class everything but boring. Smart guy, teaches with loads of examples. Group project paper had B+ (we only started it a few days before deadline) You can easily ace that paper. Attendance secures u a 10% of ur final grade. Midterm: MC questions. Fair grader, got an A- final grade.
Show up to class to get attendance marks and some of his examples in the final will be pulled straight out of in class examples. Other than that read the book, understand it and you'll get an A.
A course. Prof knows his stuff. Many cases and examples. Motivating. You will ike the team project the most. Take this course if you want to learn something useful
Amazing class. Well organized. worthwhile. my favorite class and prof. Go to class. take good notes. read the book.
Go to lectures, write notes like mad. If you do, most of the material will stick to your head. The project isn't too hard. MAKE SURE YOU GET GOOD TEAMMATES. Easy A.
Too hard to keep up with this teacher. He is way too fast paced and does not post slides online. In order to pass his class, read the book and do the MYECON lab and hopefully you will pass the class.
Amazing-Learned much-Excellent prof-Highly recommend
Favourite prof at McGill by far!! Biggest fan
john and john are my goats. you don't HAVE to go to class, but i really recommend it because these two are hilarious and wonderful.

100% take this class. Most entertaining classes if you do attend, and the slides are exactly what you need to succeed, so attendance is not needed, but definitely go if you want since they are so fun. Watching the John's together is a live tv show - truly the best duo alive. Really care about students!!!

His silly humour goes well with Prof Gyakum's dry humour. It felt like I was watching a standup routine on the last day's lesson. 90% of his slides were charts or graphs, making it hard to take notes. He can be a bit unclear with his explanations sometimes. The MC online final had some really convoluted questions, one of which was opinion-based.

John and John are so amazing! They genuinely want their students to learn and care which is sometimes rare in big lectures. They are always accessible after class and give genuinely helpful feedback. The class consists of a two part term paper, and activity quiz questions which you have unlimited tries to complete. Would take again!!!!

John and John are AWESOME. One of the best courses I've ever taken at McGill. The content is very enjoyable and light, two online exams and a final paper. It's not difficult to get an A if you write good notes from the lectures! All lectures are posted online for your convenience and class time is scheduled for extra material that won't be tested.

The Johns are amazing! Stix is so passionate, and he actually loves Natural disasters; the midterms and finals were take home and relatively easy if you see all the modules and make notes. Papers are graded by TAs so that's a different story. I love these guys. Best elective I will probably take in McGill ever.
THE NICEST PROF. made class so much fun to go to, and made everyone really care about a class that most people take just to boost their grades. if you're given the option you MUST take this class.

John was amazing, very funny and caring and clearly passionate about the subject. Make sure to write down everything they say during prerecorded lectures because there are specific questions during the exams. The research essay was great, TA's gave really good feedback! Overall great class, definitely took a little stress off of the first semester!

You can see his great passion for his area through his teaching. He made a course generally taken to boost GPA very interesting. He didn't put a time limit for the activity quizzes, and the way he organised the class with 5-10 minute videos on every topic made it super easy. He gave a second chance to those who didn't do the quizzes on time.

Dr. Hanrahan is a good lecturer and can help students fully understand a concept. He answers all his emails and is really good at clarifying topics. Always there for students and very helpful if you have questions.
Not a good guy to deal with.
He's a really nice guy and a good lecturer, but his exam questions are very specific. Make sure you know every minute detail.
Very friendly and relaxed in lectures. Obviously works out. Make sure you know the details for his exam questions.

Lectures can be dull, but he clearly knows so much about Canadian history. He genuinely cares about his students and encourages participation/comments/questions. Very passionate. Come to class because power points arent enough to study for tests since lectures are posted. Tests are easy if you study a little.

Very caring professor, he encouraged discussion and questions. Attendance is not mandatory but lectures are not recorded and slides are not all-encompassing/uploaded in a timely manner so showing up does matter (and participation in conferences is graded). He gave really helpful feedback and clarification.

An expert in his field, classes with Dr. Zucchi are incredible. He makes the topic thoroughly engaging and discussions are equally insightful. So much intellectual freedom on assignments while also rewarding academic creativity. Participation matters, but the prof makes it easy to speak up. Would recommend!
Professor Zucchi is one of the kindest professors at McGill. The class itself is very manageable so long as you reasonably keep up with the readings, and Prof. Zucchi is a very kind marker.

By far the kindest professor at McGill. If you show up to class, participate in discussions, do the readings, and genuinely engage in the material you will get a good grade. Super knowledgeable and a great teacher. Cannot recommend highly enough.

I had HIST399 with him, an honours class, & he was great. Because the classes were discussion based, it was us who would lead the discussion every week and he would chime in with his own questions every so often. He is a very fair grader, & you could tell he really cared for his students. Instead of twice a week like scheduled, we met once a week!

The best prof at mcgill, so nice and genuine. He really knows the material and enjoys discussions and listening to students. The workload is super manageable and grades are fair. He takes the time to write comments on assignments and gives very good feedback
Very kind and understanding professor, passionate about his material! Discussions matter and will help you with the assignments so attendance is key.
A really nice and genuine teacher, he is older so his teaching style is very by the book which some might find dull. He is very clear and the work is very reasonable.
John is a really amazing dude who taught a really interesting an enjoyable class. You could tell he was extremely passionate about the topic and really cared about his students.
One of the best teachers I had at McGill. I was uninterested in the material, but he made it more interesting.
Really good prof and he has funny stories about all his summer jobs. He explains very clearly and is willing to answer questions.
Great prof! Material can be a bit boring, but he's funny and easily makes lectures very engaging. Always accessible outside class and gives great feedback. Would definitely recommend taking him.
Really good prof and JP made the zoom lectures engaging. Fair grading.

He is incredibly caring of his students, always ready to listen and try to accomodate us. Always takes feedback and tries to improve his lectures. Also very open to discuss with you outside of class, and perhaps boost your grade if you believe you deserve more. Would 100% take again.

Prof. Britt is super knowledgeable and I found the content of PSYC211 really interesting, it's just dense. He would sometimes ramble or go off on tangents, but he's clear about what you need to know for the exam vs extra info. He's also very available for questions and some of the TAs are helpful.

I loved Prof Britt! the material is very heavy and requires alot of studying but he is so knowledgable in the topics he covers and is always available to answer questions. He does not try to trick you in the midterms or finals, but you have to know the material well. its also a very interesting class that i enjoyed!

Content-heavy (30–40 slides/lecture). Big jump without a psych background (U0; one of my most stressful classes); lots of critical thinking on biological mechanisms. MC exams + quizzes, highest score counts. Lectures are fast, monotone, and skippable since slides cover all. Memorization-heavy; no written components. DON'T take as an elective.

This is a required psyc class, but i really recommend you guys to wait as long as you can to take it cause it's NOT EASY. I recommend you taking perception, cognition before so you can grasp the content a bit better. The midterm and finals were BRUTAL. This prof has a monotonous tone during the lectures, not very engaging…
Goat lecturer, super boring voice. Watch the lecture recordings over and over.

Honestly felt super thrown by how hard the final was, not impossible at all but definitely more confusing and complicated than the midterms. The class is insanely dense lecture-wise. It's not doable at all to cram last minute there's just too much info. Prof is honestly amazing, lectures are interesting, slides are clear, loved this class :)

INCREDIBLE PROFESSOR. Genuinely cares about students success, weight midterms & finals for optimal results, provides a plethora of practice materials (e.g. practice midterms, quizzes), always engages with students questions. Bonus points for TA Madeleine for giving the best review conferences EVER. Loved this class, 10/10 would recommend!

While there was a looot of things to remember for the exam, the teacher was very clear on his slides about the subject and what is important. Certain words will be in blue when they're very important to know and overall pretty much everything is on the slides. I really enjoyed his straight-forward teaching style.

Shortened version of a MUCH longer review I will post on the McGill subreddit:
TLDR: Extremely clear lectures, top-tier PowerPoints and recorded classes. Straightforward, predictable exams with generous bonuses. Warm, approachable prof. Memorization-heavy but fair: if you do the practice exams and stay on top of anatomy, you'll do great.

Really interesting class, lectures were really well organized and structured, but the material was quite heavy. Be ready to not just memorize but actually understand the material and how to manipulate it. Tests are meant to test your understanding, so the wording of questions is meant to mislead you. Very nice and knowledgeable teacher too.

Exams are quite difficult, but Prof. Sakata is a great lecturer. He is extremely interesting and passionate, really tries to encourage class participation and is quite energetic. He jumps around in class a lot, fun guy.

Jon is the best professor ever. He cares so much that his students understand and takes feedback to improve his teaching. I learned so much from his section of the course, and BIOL 205 has been one of the best classes I have taken at McGill.

BIOL205 won't be tough in his section. He usually spends 20~30% of time in the lecture to make students discuss. One thing you will need to take care is his powerpoint is always long (like over 55 pages), but his lecture only takes 50 minutes. Since there is discussion time, he usually finishes the powerpoint really fast.

Chill dude, lectures are engaging and he makes bats and birds sound very interesting. He's cares about answering people's questions and involving the students in the lecture. Tests are hard, but do not weigh too much so there's plenty of opportunities to up the grade.

Please prof Sakata if you're reading this, please please please move the mic a little further from your mouth or remove it when you keep drinking water. I'm rewatching your lectures and I cannot take the sound of gulping anymore every 2 minutes... Good teacher though for the rest reading this and wondering.

He's an AMAZING professor and he cares about his students. There's some prelecture videos that you have to watch but they help a lot in understanding his content beforehand. In class, he goes over the concepts again in so many different perspectives and encourages a lot of class discussion. His section was the hardest but his questions were fair.
big cheeseburger yum yum
hi jon sakata you are very cool
L
cheeseburger

Prof Unruh is very very smart and definitely knows what he talks about. the content itself, though, is pretty boring. midterm and final are long and time consuming but online and not graded too harshly. If you do whats asked you will score well.

Great class for people who enjoy lecture heavy courses. Covered a vast variety of topics relevant to development studies from conflict, the peace process, land tenure, famine to climate change. The group project policy brief was also interesting and fun to work on. Easy enough exams but research heavy.

Professor Unruh was really nice and engaging during class and accessible outside of class. His lectures and guests lecture as well were all well rounded. 
Really clear grading criteria, would recommend the class!

I loved this prof. He clearly is an expert in his field, and that translates well into the lectures. They have rich, concrete content that is captivating while also feeling very useful. Highly recommend this course.

Professor Unruh is an all-around great teacher. The work he does in international development is very interesting, his lecture schedule is concise and grading is straightforward (Two take-homes and a group project). Would highly recommend this class to anyone, especially IDS students.

Prof Unruh is a really nice guy and was very easy to get in contact with. He was extremely understanding of COVID-19 and how some students were struggling. His lectures were randomly spaced out but very engaging. The grading was very fair and the group project was interesting. I hope to take more classes with him as he is a top notch guy.

The class was very informative and pragmatic about intl development practice which is enjoyable. However, the readings were sometimes disconnected from the lectures. Also, Prof Unruh brings up a lot of unanswered questions/dilemmas which can be confusing. Overall though, he made the course engaging and diverse.
Great Prof. Very knowledgeable

I like him as a person but not as a professor. One of the worst classes I've taken. The final had to be curved since it was so hard. I do not recommend this class. The topic is too vague and the lectures are very messy

Professor Unruh is a great person and is always looking out for his students. He'll tell you what will come out in the exam throughout his lecture. The material of the course is very interesting for people interested in international organizations. He mixes things up with group activities every now and then (which are fun). One of the best prof!

Jon Wild is easily the most disorganized professor I have ever interacted with. He is constantly overextended, and struggles with time management. I would expect better from someone who has been teaching here for so many years. Although he is extremely knowledgeable, his expertise are completely overshadowed by his poor organization and planning.

Really great lectures. I actually found it a lot of work to stay on top of everything but he was motivating and it felt worthwhile at the end. He seemed to care about our experience, a couple of times he modified assignments on the fly if he thought it was going to be too much work. The TAs did all the grading, I think.

While I'm sure Prof. Wild is a great person, his disorganization and messy lecture materials meant that almost all of our lectures ran overtime, along with other issues like late grades and unclear instructions. He consistently keeps us 5-10 minutes past the allotted time for this class, and makes small comments when people start packing up.
Nothing but love for Jon Wild

Totally recommended for the course "Topics in Tonal Analysis" which was great and unlike any other course I've ever taken. He found really cool repertoire and gave us lots of freedom in our projects. Asked for lots of work but it was enjoyable.

Fantastic music analysis teacher. We spent a lot of time on each piece and looked in depth at how the music worked. He has passion for music & theory & for sharing his understanding, and his enthusiasm was contagious. Feedback on homework was done in class, not so much individually (but he was very helpful outside of class when I asked questions)
He was THE most Amazing Professor in my first semester in McGill. I really miss his kindness and genuine integrity. The course was brilliant.

I had no background in music theory, and yes the class was more involved than I thought. But this is such a smart guy, I appreciated his lectures so much. I did well & want to learn more. I recommend J.Wild very highly but this isn't a bird course. Not much use of the textbook apart from problem sets- he made a lot of his own materials, it seemed.

If you have no previous music knowledge, the class is very difficult. He gives a lot of assignments, so as long as you do those, you can get a decent grade with some effort. Fair warning though, this is NOT a beginner's course, at least, not with this professor.

He is soooo hot!I've trained in piano for over 10 years but lack knowledge in theories. This course is very helpful but when it comes to final, it gets harder and boring. overall i like the pro!!!He is always there to help. TA hold tutorial all the time.

He's a nice, pleasant, and personable guy. He's knowledgeable about the course material, and wants you to succeed and learn physics. 

However, he was uneffective at teaching. He spends too long showing python code & assigning it as homework -- interesting, but confuses people more than it teaches. He assumes more prereq knowledge than people have.

He is very nice. He literally votes on when you want to take the midterm. He is very cheerful and clearly knows the subject very well. You can get a lot from him if you read ahead and ask him questions about it. However its very hard to learn from his lectures. He has lecture notes that dont cover the entire material

He is extremely nice and clearly knows a lot. BUT, he is extremely unorganized in his teaching. He is EXTREMELY difficult to follow even if u did read the material beforehand. He posts "lecture notes" here and there on his github which is additional material that doesnt include what he actually covers in class. I learnt nothing from this course

Like others already said: the worst handwriting EVER. I learned all the material from Griffith, didn't watch any lectures. Griffiths is an amazing textbook, so at least you're saved with it, and most of the assignments are from it. However, his own questions are extremely confusing and poorly worded. Doesn't seem like a bad guy though.

Interesting man. He's a genuinely nice person but God I hated taking notes in his class. Like others have mentioned (and he mentioned himself) his handwriting is extremely poor, on the verge of unreadability. All he has to do is take a week or two to typeset his notes and all his classes will love him. But he doesn't care since we have Griffiths.

Terrible handwriting but if you read the book in advance then you can get a lot out of the classes. He also listens to feedback so if you have any questions after class he is happy to answer. Not for everyone but you need to be on top of your stuff.
His assignments are often messy and the questions complicated for no particular reason, often with paragraph-long introductions and very poor wording.

Probably the worst prof ever met. The whole blackboard was like a scribbling paper for him--very disorganized and extremely messy. Literally learned nothing from his lectures. Just teach yourself by reading the textbook if you take his course. HW was extremely hard. Exam questions were written in paragraphs......

He cant explain EM to save his life, and his poorly-worded problem sets were the cause for so much strife. What did he just write is that a 0 or a v? Thats super messy, if you ask me. Read the damn book because Griffifths knows how to deliver, but be ready for confusion while with Prof Sievers.

Didn't come prepared for class. Went over the same examples multiple times since he wasn't clear the first time. Handwriting on the blackboard was completely disorganized and impossible to decipher (which became a class-wide joke by the end of the term). Assignments were long and hard. Without the book I wouldn't have learnt anything with this guy.

I absolutely LOVED Jordan's class. He was super funny and very open to questions. He's a little hard to keep track of cause he paces everywhere but it's part of his personality. Not hard to get an A, just make sure you watch and grasp the interviews and do the readings. Intergroup was really fun to take, and very interesting.
Great and engaging lecturer who cares about the subject matter and his students. Highly recommend taking his course as I learned a lot. Tests aren't very difficult.

Prof Axt is a wonderful lecturer, clear in explaining the materials. This class is one of my favorites I've ever taken. The content is very applicable, fascinating and reflective. Prof is a big fan of Duke Basketball lol. Its funny, he tells you how to do well in the class on the first day and he's right: go to class, do the readings, and study.

The clearest and most effective lecturer I've had in my Psychology degree. Exams are fair to class content, but you do need to pay attention and do the readings to succeed. Would absolutely take him again!

I really liked this course. The prof was engaging in his lectures and made class fun. He makes jokes from time to time and creates a good atmosphere. This class was not an easy A but a very feasible one. I did my readings and watched the interviews 2 times (once after class and once before exams in 3x). I studied the content in depth and got an A.

Great researcher, interesting lectures. The material isn't that difficult and there's A LOT compared to other 300 psych courses, but the exams were a nightmare. The questions are very subjective, ambiguous and application based. You won't get away with just memorizing. I learnt a lot from this course and can explain but exams were not reflective.

There are assigned readings and videos, and they don't overlap much with lecture (unlike some other psych courses). If you do all the assigned work, go to class, and are generally interested in the subject, you will get an A. I consistently got 80s on exams and with the curves, easily got an A. Unfortunately he was not approachable outside class.

Contrary to other ratings, I enjoyed PSYC 331 and found the evaluations to be fair. I think that to succeed in the exams it was important to understand and be able to apply the information rather than memorizing. Definitely had to adjust my study methods to succeed, but if you put in the work it will pay off!

I thought the exams  were on par with other psych dept mcq exams. Yes, it is a lot of content, but he is clear on this from the beginning. I looked forward to going to class and even studying for the exams. 100% worth it if you're interested in the topic and willing to put in the work

Class seemed easy enough, interesting. But god, the exams are horrendous. Will ask random questions that are unverifiable (the opinion of someone long gone on a modern thing), will base exams off interpretation and subjectivity. This classes ruined my gpa.

The content is manageable so long as you actually keep up with it and practice b/c it takes time to get comfortable. Prof Correa is good about trying to answer any questions and he's considerate of the class (he let us out early sometimes cuz everyone was tired - apologies prof, it wasn't you, I swear). Explains things well plus lots of examples.
excellent lecturer
Great lectures, accessible outside of class and very caring. Totally recommend!
Helpful lectures with clear order. So many questions in the homework but not so difficult. Allow using formula sheet in the final examination which helps a lot.

Prof. Correa noticed I wasn't doing well in his class and reached out to me. I am not a math person but I would take this class again just because of him. He took the time to schedule zoom calls to go over concepts & made sure I was staying caught up. He truly cares about his students. One of the best profs I've had in my 4 years at McGill.

Had Prof. Correa for Math203 in the summer. The class is super easy to begin with but it is important to do the assignments to practice the material. Read over the lectures and do all the assignments and you're good to go! Slides are sufficient, no need for textbook.
Lectures are easy to follow. Explains concepts clearly. Notes were thorough.

Was quite good at explaining the concepts and I thought the assignments provided good practice. The midterm was quite fair (maybe even easy) but the final was very hard. The final ended up being curved to make up for the difficulty.
He's a really chill prof. As long as you go to lectures and take notes, there's no reason you shouldn't do well.

Took MATH204 with him and I have to say that it was a lot easier than I expected. He writes notes on the board and posts solved problems online. Both midterm and final were easy if you read the notes and looked over the solved problems. All the assignments were long but doable. Really easy to get an A.

He does not care about teaching. His lecture slides were not clear and lacked important explanations. You have to pay a lot of attention during his lectures since he expected you to answer questions from what he said. His exam questions were not fair. Even If you believe you understand and show your knowledge, he still gives you a bad result.

Nice prof, goes over concepts pretty clearly despite slides with very minimal text! Pretty enthusiastic and provides a really nice overview of the virus from its historical perspective, pathology and replicative cycle. Questions on midterm are straightforward as well.

Really great prof! His slides don't contain much text, but if you pay attention, he goes over the concepts and material really well. Also provides historical context/background info to the viruses in his lectures. His lecture structure can be repetitive, but still very clear.

He's ok professor. Attendance is mandatory due to unpredictable lecture recording system at the common lecture hall (otherwise, lecture recordings are mandatory). The slides alone aren't enough for the material taught, so be sure to listen in. A fair professor if you study all details.

HE IS THE BESTTTTTTT!!! literally the kindest and most caring prof in the HISP department. i'd even argue the best at McGill period. if you're doing a HISP minor or major take his classes! he's way more passionate in his 300/400 level courses more than in civilization.

These lectures are so engaging. There is a lot of content throughout the slides but his tests are fair, so if you take the time to study you should do well. He also offers extra credit, and even though it may seem like an overwhelming amount of content at first, stay in the class it will probably become one of your favourites of the semester.

lowk i didn't really show up to any of the classes but he makes his powerpoints pretty comprehensive so use that to study! class consists of three tests, all multiple choice. he's really nice and clearly knows his stuff, you can tell he's pretty passionate about it too! i recommend this prof

This prof was so amazing. He didnt overload us with readings, it was perfect amount. If you attend his class, you dont even need to do the readings. He seems to love what he is teaching us which makes it even better and his tests are very straight forward, and ALL MULTIPLE CHOICE. He posts all his slides and they provide a ton of information. 10/10
I love him. 10/10. I recommend him.

you dont need to go to any class or do any of the readings he puts everything in his slides, hes a great prof but the questions on the exams were most of the time hard, all his exams were multiple choice but still there would be random questions on things we never read. literally only study the slides like A LOT and youll pass

he's a sweetie. genuinely wants students to succeed and exams are fair game if you study the lectures. for the final, it's online and open book, but there are questions related to videos and readings, so make sure to have at least skimmed and taken some decent notes. he makes lectures dynamic and often makes jokes, so it helps you focus!

Jose is an amazing prof, very caring and likeable. The class was much easier than expected for being 400 level--tests were reasonable, participation graded generously, and final paper was not bad. It wasn't as interactive as other HISP classes; a lot of class time was spent watching plays so it wasn't always super engaging but overall I enjoyed it!
This prof is so great, he is so passionate and wholesome.

Attendance isn't mandatory, and Prof. Martin knows a ton about the subject and genuinely loves the topic. His classes are definitely important to go to, as the three exams are almost all based on slides. There are readings/videos for homework, but they're not graded, and in my experience, they're for your understanding only.

I loved her section of the course, it was interesting and different from the lectures we usually have. The exam was really fair: short answer question based more on "what would you do if you were in this situation in the lab" than parrot back what you know. I really enjoy this part of the course.
Goes over a lot of details not required for the final, but a good lecturer all the same.

He's amazing! Lectures are always interesting as he includes lots of examples and funny anecdotes, so it's entertaining even if you're just watching recordings at home. Exams are super fair and straightforward, as well as all online and non-cumulative (including the final). He's always open to questions and is very knowledgeable, would recommend!
Birdiest class at McGill. Nice prof, recorded lectures, and a free A
the freest possible A in history

Tests are made extra hard to account for the fact they are online. Each question is worded in a way that might as well be 4 questions. There is almost always a “none of these is correct” option and the rest is worded ambiguously. There is no amount of studying that will get you a good grade just refine your note searching skills and pray.

It says it's an easy class. But guys, taking the tests is stressful, and there are a lot of very specific questions. Guys we have 3 hours to complete 90 questions, WHICH IS NOT A LOT. So be prepared to be a bit stressed, and to have some tricky answers to the MCQ sometimes....And honestly I would say it's not the easiest A.

a great class to take as an elective. learned a lot as a non-stem major and it really doesn't require that much effort to do well. the only thing i will say is that he gives 3h to do the exams but it is very crammed considering there's like 90 questions.
Way to left for me pushing agenda. . Very interesting lectures.

Prof. Schwarcz's lectures are engaging, though a bit disorganized at times. The exams are challenging but manageable if you take good notes and use study tools like Unstuck study. Overall, it's a decent elective.

I took both chem 181 & 183, such a quirky man and he had entertaining lectures. But I cannot stress this enough: TAKE DETAILED NOTES!! Exam q's sometimes based on the most specific/irrelevant topics, including random graph interpretations. Was time consuming to take notes, but worth it if you want an A. Don't leave them til the last minute!!

I lovve prof. schwarcz! His lectures are fun and he showed us his rubber ducky collection. My only complaint about the class is that your entire grade is based on two midterms (30% each) and a final (40%), so if you do badly on any one of them then your grade will suffer. All u have to do is watch the lectures and take good notes and youll be ok :)

Super unapproachable. Always looked disgusted when you had questions. Not helpful. Material was confusing and he did not offer any stable office hours (and nobody asked for help because he was unapproachable) and his slides were confusing. He talked too quickly. His practice questions did not help for the final exam. Avoid this class if possible.

He is the meanest professor I have ever had. I asked him a question after a class about his section in the final exam and couldn't even bother to look at me. I even emailed him and his response was so condescending even though my question was very simple and straightforward. He is horrible at teaching. His slides suck and he barely explains.
lot of content that was just droned about to you, not particularly engaging
Great lectures and notes, make sure you do all the practice questions and understand the logic behind them before the exam and you'll be fine.

This prof is obviously super smart and fair. It's up to you to prep and post-lecture work. The slides and lecture notes make a lot more sense if you review them a lot. Go to lectures prepared. Re-listen to the earlier lectures. He really wants you to succeed  - he answers our questions; he puts up clicker questions; and even a review session.
Confusing slides

loved his section, behavioural biology/neuroscience is fascinating. I actually had fun writing the final:  it's 95% logic questions where critical thinking >> memorization. memorizing neural circuits for the final is a waste of time–just know it well. Everything on the final is figure-outable. Very sharp guy, but not the friendliest.
He seems not to be "present" when he lectures, almost as though he is somewhere else in his head. I thought that his name should be changed from "Prof Dent" to "Prof Dead".

Lectures are very boring, he doesn't really seem to care. The slides aren't helpful and you need to watch recordings to study for exams. His questions are long and frustrating, but he really doesn't emphasize memorizing on the exam in a bio class, so that redeemed him a little.

Awful professor. Worst teacher I've ever had at McGill. His slides have little to no text, only graphs that can't be understood unless you write down word for word what he says and his exam questions are only based on the graphs presented in class. His neurophysiology section was bad too, barely any problem solving examples done in class.

His style of teaching is definitely not for everyone, and I personally hated it. Very slow teaching, spends hours talking about examples and his personal life sort of related to the topic covered, very weird sense of humour.. This material could be easily understood in half the time Prof Cox takes to teach it. The class is very easy.

Very simply, Professor Cox is by far the best teacher I ever had at McGill. He mixes genuinely humour and knowledge in a way that you actually enjoy his class. Being a practising lawyer, he uses his own anecdotes to explain the course content, making his class delightful. BUSA You can get easily an A by reading the book and attending his class.

Bob was extremely knowledgable. He teaches 3 hour lectures that go by very fast and he speaks freely. He uses anecdotes well to get complicated ideas across easily. He is quite repetitive but thats only for your best interest. There is a LOT of reading, do the reading and go to class and you'll be fine.

Sit a few rows back, because he's very loud. To pass, read all of the readings and be prepared to explain any legal jargon that you may use. It's not enough to write jurisprudence, explain it as well. When I asked him for clarification, it was as though he didn't listen and had already loaded up an answer before I said anything. Does not do email.

Bob knows his stuff, yes he is arrogant. but he speaks clearly and is passionate about his teachings. If you get offended easily probably not the best prof for you. take it with a grain of salt and soak up the tools and information he gives you.
very interesting professor you will learn a lot from his classes! I graduated two years ago and I can still remember most the material he taught me, this does count for something!

Prof Cox is a practicing lawyer, and comes off pompous. Paranoid about technology... says he will answer e-mails but never gets around to it. However if you talk to him one on one, he is very helpful and makes sure you understand the material. Not out to trick students on exams but make sure you know your stuff.
Had an outdated syllabus and then proceeded to not use it.

Charismatic teacher, great delivery. A little pompous at times, but he knows his material. He's also a practicing lawyer, so he is up to date on all cases and events in the legal world. Very interesting material, however Cox needs to get more organized!! Sometimes he was all over the place...

Terribe. More interested in stroking his ego (and telling the class that they're never going to get into law school) than actually teaching anything useful. The course material was super interesting, too bad he barely touched on it.

I don't think Prof Sullivan is a bad prof, I just think his teaching style just didn't really click with me. The course is very difficult, and it takes a while to memorize concepts from the slides, textbook and additional (mandatory) readings. I found it a little excessive in terms of content. Take this course in a lighter course load semester.

Although this class was more on the difficult side the professor is truly excellent and the material fascinating. I failed the first midterm, but got As on the second midterm and final, so if you put in the work and familiarize yourself with his style of testing, you'll be fine. He is very engaging and good at explaining concepts, READ THE TEXTBOOK

You need to know the textbook, lectures and studies well and apply the concepts, not just recall simple definitions. Several of his questions were unfairly specific, but he was willing to adjust the grading after our complaints. Overall, the class was engaging, and he's very kind- his anecdotes were helpful too.

Psychopathology is a complex and challenging class regardless of the professor, and while some of his exam questions felt ambiguous, the material itself is demanding. That said, Prof. Sullivan is cares about his students and brings real-world experience and personal anecdotes, which makes the lectures engaging and genuinely interesting.
honestly loved him, his exams were not easy but i studied a lot and got good grades but it takes hard work. he is a great guy tho and the class is so interesting

Great professor and engaging lectures. The midterms were manageable, focusing only on the "findings" from the papers (I scored ~90% on both). However, the final was BRUTAL—covering 40+ papers and requiring memorization of findings, methods, hypotheses, etc. I scored 62%, and most people ended up with 50–70% (possibly after curving).

He seems like a good guy who cares about his students and is very experienced. However, his exams are awful. They test on random details from 30+ full-length research articles from class which he says you just need to know the "main ideas" of. Content is too broad for exams to cover / boring lectures. Awful class - I just know he can do better.
Great lecturer but that final was genuinely insane. Content was also not equally distributed across chapters as he said it would be.

The final exam which was worth 50% was VERY hard and unfair, testing you on extremely specific details from like 40 different lengthy readings and random things that weren't on the slides. Overall kind of disappointing because the class itself was pretty interesting.

Great professor, engaging lecturer, very interesting content. The exams are fair, but always have some very tricky questions. The final was cumulative and you were expected to learn details from 39 readings (which was only announced a week prior to the final) making it very challenging.

Worst professor I've had in my 14 years of being a student. Context: I am a deans honor list student.
1. Testing grading is nonsensical, directly contradicts his lecture slides
2. Retaliatory if you point out grading mistakes
3. Extremely slow/inefficient, 1hr+ lines in OH
4. Uses own grading scheme (never good)

Only take co-instructed!

Beware that he uses alternative grading scheme, and doesn't tell us until the last test... So even if you get above 85%, if it's below 91% you still get A-. However, people who got 75% can still get A-. It feels unfair, truly. And it was graded subjectively too, some TA grades harshly while others grade easily. Overall the class was disorganized.

Overhated for sure, he's fine. He just talks veeerrry slooowwlly, so if you can stay on top of it I *strongly* recommend ditching the lectures and watching the recordings so you can speed him up. At 1.75x speed, he's a fine lecturer. Co-taught w Jacob Errington when I took it, overall good experience.
The lectures are quite confusing and useless, but on the bright side, the assignments are straightforward, and the final is very generously graded as well.
His lectures are... fine, his assignments are... fine, his exams are... fine. He's very accessible outside class and is overall a good prof.

Took him with prof kopinsky. both good teachers but a bit disorganized. lectures can be better but tbh the material is boring. assignments/midterms are fair, final was fair but kinda hard imo. you're responsible for reading all slides even if not mentioned during the lecture (if something is mentioned for one slide you still need to know it well).

Most disorganised course I've ever taken. Due dates always shifting, unclear assignment requirements, often losing marks for not having things that are clearly present in my work. Some topics never covered in class, no slides, no textbook, but expected to know what to do and/or explanation hidden in an old  forum reply. Miserable teaching. Avoid.

Beware of unforgiving assignment grading scheme. No partial marks are given so your grade can only be either 0%, 50%, 75% or 100%. Keep in mind even if everything is correct, if even one minute criteria is not met you automatically get dropped to a 50%. Good luck
Great guy! Can be boring but the grading scheme was very good and assignments were doable.

probably the laziest and most boring prof. i've had at mcgill. assignments are super vague, and he doesnt check the discussion board often enough. he was also unclear to TA's, so they would give clarifications on assignments and then after they were due he would contradict the answers given by TAs. easy grader though.

Arrogant, condescending and daunting. Encourages you to think first and then refutes what you say. Doesn't know how to respect others' opinions, any opinion other than his is just "wrong". Excellent professor and excellent course. Material is interesting, and the prof makes it even more interesting. He's very engaging, and there is a small class. Not a difficult course either, A's are easily attainable. I highly recommend taking this first year seminar.

one of the most intelligent, interestingly eccentric, open and influential professors in my time at the university. Deeply recommend any class he's teaching.
Great guy. Strange, but great. Knows a ridculous amount about everything, but doesn't really expect you to. Sign up for one of his classes, it'll be good for a larf.

Professor Gregory elucidates his assigned reading with clarity, and poise. His number one concern being whether students comprehend him, he therefore seeks to emphasize important points and takes the time to respond to students queries. An excellent professor!

Professor Gregory elucidates his asigned reading with clarity, and poise. His number one concern being whether students comprehend him, he therefore seeks to emphasize important points and takes the time to respond to students queries. An excellent professor!

Awesome professor. He has an amazing rapport with the classroom, is an excellent speaker that gets his points across clearly and is a fair marker. He's a new prof, but he's destined to be a great one.

Amazing professor. Lectures are coherent and organized. Discusses material from the coursepack and readings in class and synthesizes with his own input. Immensely helpful and very approachable. Love this class and Professor Manaugh, who is kind, funny, and engaging. This is a must-take for urban studies students, and you WILL make friends in this class. Do the 4 short assignments diligently, as they count for 30% of your grade, and it is doable to get 95+ on these. Strongly recommend!
Nice guy, clearly interested in the subject. Grading was fairly lenient. Just go to class and listen to the key concepts. Readings are a bit longer but other than that the class was fairly easy.

All hail King Kevin. Envr 201 is a great intro to Envr classes. The grading for Envr 201 is incredibly forgiving. Midterms are worth 12.5% each and the final is worth 25%. The Perusall readings can seem overwhelming at first but they are very managable when spread out. I had such a good time in this class, I highly reccomend it.
This class was exciting. However, lectures are intense, and it's hard to stay focused for an hour and a half as it's pretty monotone. You learn lots of things, so I still recommend it 100%.

The lectures are clear and organized, and the slides are posted in advance. The tests are solely based on the lectures, there are no bad surprises with content not covered. Always willing to provide more explanations. The attendance is monitored using slido.

Nice chill guy for a McGill prof. Monotone lectures make you fall asleep. Makes us do way too many mandatory 10-20 page readings with graded annotations, which is extremely time-consuming and why I wouldn't take his class again. Unclear instructions and inconsistent class structure frustrated us, making the energy in the classroom pretty negative.
He's a chill guy, but his lectures were kind of just reading off slides, which is why I much preferred the other prof. Take ENVR201 if you can!
I didn't like this class that much as we did a lot of economics. However Mr Manaugh is nice.
Unclear assignments and unrelevant (very old) readings. Not easily reachable outside classroom but overall nice
Very nice guy and an awesome + knowledgeable prof.
Great professor, exams are a little hard.

This teacher looks nice at first with his jokes but his exams are hard. The average for each exam is really low. There are only a few questions so every time you have 1 wrong info, you can lose 20%. Professor Wade was one of the best teachers I had at McGill. He has an in-depth knowledge of his subject, answers in class questions with a lot of detail, and encourages group discussion.
