Questions on tests are fair, but not necessarily easy. His lectures are interesting and very clear. Funny

He's great! Teaches Animal Science intro course that is clear, his test questions are fair, but make sure that you made the connection. He records all his lectures and puts them online for us. Really helpful especially because his slides are only up after class.
Straight forward material  test questions reward those that review it You get what you give into it and you don't need to give much

Very kind and passionate about geology. Lecture presentations contain all the content and are posted online, so they are easy to do remotely. She goes through the lectures quickly and there is a LOT of content, so prepare to write a lot.
Great professor and well-prepared class!

Looooove Professor Chung! Super sweet and passionate about what she talks about. Classes are very interactive and open to conversations. Cannot recommend her enough! TONS of readings tho, and going to class is mandatory.

For an intro 200 level class, it was way too much reading to be expected of students. It rivaled my other honours and 400 level class readings in its amount. I DO appreciate that she gives a study guide to the quizzes, but theyre very short so the lost points raise quickly. attendance is taken randomly throughout the semester.

Though Professor Chung is clearly very intelligent, I personally feel that there are many issues with this course. In addition to assigning a heavier reading load than some of my 400-level courses, 50% of your final grade is based on 2 short quizzes completed in less than a full class period. Grading for these was harsh & some MCQs were unfair.

Great professor who is very knowledgable about the subject matter. Very clear about assignments and what's required to do well in the class. The content is interesting, even to people new to the topic of Korean studies. As long as you read what's required and listen in lectures, the quizzes aren't too bad.

Professor Chung's class was engaging and fairly easy. If you participate, complete the weekly response postings and go to her for advice before writing your final research paper, you will definitely do well. She's very flexible and wants you to succeed.

Dr. Chung is by far my favourite professor at McGill. She is sweet and caring and her lectures are engaging and summarize the readings perfectly. Just doing the readings and taking notes in class will almost guarantee an A.
My favourite prof and favourite class! Hope to have her again!

Prof Chung is a wonderful person & her engaging lectures spark intense discussions. However, the final presentations were an unprofessional mess. Students had 10 minutes but were only timed after the 4th day. Even then, Prof. Chung would ignore the timer to allow further questions. Students showed graphic content with inadequate warnings.

Prof Chung was really nice and she summarized the readings really well during lectures. The content was really interesting and I learned a lot in her class. There are a lot of articles to read (often 20-40 pages per class, 3x a week) and you need to know details to get an A on the quizzes. If you do the readings and take notes, you should be fine!

She was just absolutely amazing! She was very caring, TA were also very nice! She was able to make every class an interesting one. I would just recommend to read the readings, and to pay attention in class. I think its the best way to succeed in her class.
Sweetest prof ever

Prof. Bevan is one of the best profs in Engineering, although Mime 262 is a difficult course by nature with a massive amount of concepts, he explained everything clearly and was helpful. The exams are challenging, but the key is to do many past exams. I really enjoy talking with him before and after each lecture and he's a really nice person.
Prof.Bevan is quite a nice and helpful person! Be prepared for quantum physics.

MIME 262 material is rather hard and requires you to not fall behind. But the prof is pretty good, he explains the material very well. The assignments are very long (even though he gives you the solutions), but do them, they help for the midterms/final. Take him

One of the best proffs mcgill has to offer for a course like Mime 262. You attend his lectures and the course is like a walk in the park, only and only if you are consistent. Very sweet guy, cares for his students. The material itself is a bit tedious but he makes it better. TAKE HIM.

Overall he is a good prof, take him over nate. Nate sucks, he tries to fail you, where as Bevan really gives challengin exams but you will pass if you study ( max 3 days) . His exams are all mcqs. Boring class but you'll get through it. Go to class for the pop quizzes and do your homework (he gives you the solutions): they're basically free points. The good thing is he posts up all useful notes so going to class is not mandatory except to a very easy Quiz once a week,you can just take answers from your friends. I did not find his exams easy .He seems really interested in what he teaches. He can be very boring in class and spend 10 mins drawing a diagram , falling asleep is almost inevitable.

I don't think she likes teaching 1Ls. Her teaching style is really boring and for a 3hour course, you'll want to fall asleep, which is part of the reason why I stopped showing up to class. AWOL outside of class. Lectures borderline meaningless because of her French and the content of the course, and the slides are just random photos. Professor Anker knows, for the most part, the materials she is teaching and she's not a terrible lecturer. Her teaching was fine, however in her exam feedback she said that she personally could not agree with my thesis and gave me a below average grade. She does make it known that she knows more than you.

She gets Indigenous law in theory but in practice she has a long way to go - she is super rigid and kind of mean, so when she tries to be "intentional" or "spiritual" or whatever, it feels pretty fake. he doesnt care about his teaching and the exam was extremely careless: the format, the flipping pages.... and his assignments are full of typos even if he uses the ones from past years. PLEASE AVOID!

5 people in the class. No lecture recording, no cheat sheet, midterm and exams online.

Lectures were a bit boring indeed but they weren't that bad. Exams were a bit hard but doable/fair if prepared, questions were similar to the lectures/assignments/past exams. He's also very caring and he's not that bad honestly. I don't understand all the bad reviews...

Prof. Von Schutz is organized and direct, but I personally found the class hard to follow. Be ready to have homework due for every single lecture. Tough grader with really unclear assignment instructions and poor feedback. Also, poor knowledge of the engineering profession. poor feedback for a tough grader. AVOID!!!
High standards, but with a lot of work, an A is achievable. She speaks very fast but cares a lot about her students and wants you to succeed. She also has a sense of humour.

Out of the 3 professors for this class, he was the best. He is quite enthusiastic but goes off on many tangents and his slides are most pictures. However his unit for this course wasn't that complex, therefore it wasn't that bad.

idk what everyone is on about. this guy is not bad for mime 250, better than the other teachers. he does ask mulitplt times if u understnd and re explains in different ways. it is very theory based but the quiz was more calculations based (which looked exactly like the practice problems we did in class) overall hes pretty good

Not sure I understand all the negative ratings... had him for both 250 and 341. Biggest issue is the lack of assignments to prepare for tests. Had to find my own example problems. Lectures are good, though a bit hard to follow in 341 (big lecture hall). Tests are fair. Its really just algebra.

what he teaches is not what he test, the equation he teaches in class does not apply to test, he tests the laboratory equation but never mentions he will do so prior to the test. Be nice to your self, just avoid it.
have fun learning everything by yourself because this guy is absolutely useless

Also known as the dragon of the department. She is tough and a bit cold, but she is definitely a good teacher. She has no teaching ability. Sometimes she has no idea what she's talking about and reads off of outdated slides. Other times she tells you to "know ____" with no explanation at all.  Luckily there's a lot of guest lecturers. Exams are long, focused on details that were not always taught.

She is tough, but she is clear and straight forward. I enjoyed every single of her guest speakers, and she is a good lecturer too. she's cold..has the goal of destroying what's left of  students' confidence after her initial butchering...

She will say we arent doing well on assignments and say to do better. Im far enough in my education to know that I should be graded on mastery of things i was taught in class

Professor Han is a real gentleman. He is extremely caring towards his students and their learning. He treats his students with great respect and care. 

I loved every single one of his lectures.

Mr. Han is a super nice prof who really cares about his students. He isn't too enthusiastic but knows his material well and always answers questions in great detail. His exams are fair. He is always available in office hours and answers emails promptly. I really appreciated him as a prof.

lots of lecture, can be dull but the prof is super nice. also be prepared for 2 assignments, 2 reports and 2 exams. but moderately easy

really great prof

Very nice professor that cares a lot about students and their wellbeing. Very knowledgeable too.

Tough grader & assessment criteria weren't always clear. Sometimes the Prof. was disorganized. Often he seemed inflexible and rigid in grading, but other times he was fair. I really enjoyed the content of this course! Def wasn't as easy as people make it out to be.

Great class, great prof! We got to create a blog on any topic we like, as long as it could be related to digital culture. A good mix of individual and group work. Lectures were engaging and tied well to assignments, and the readings were not too heavy. Kyle genuinely cares about his students' success and gives helpful feedback to improve writing.

Kyle Kubler was an amazing professor! I learned so much about how to write more "unconventional" papers. kind, serious, honest, and supportive. Although she checks book when teaching to see stuff like how to play ornaments.

Amazing professor!! Her lectures are very easy to follow, and she appreciates it if you do the readings as well. Although the readings can be long, she's very reasonable and open to criticism. Basically, put in the effort and you'll get a good grade.

Laila is such a great prof with a genuine concern for her students. So friendly and she has such a great attitude. Her lectures were really interesting and organized well. I will go out of my way to take a class with her again.
One of the best professors at McGill! The material was really interesting, take-home exams and there were pop quizzes but just to see if you've done the readings! Highly recommended!!
Amazing professor. Incredibly knowledgable and well spoken. Highly recommend.

One of the best teachers I have ever had! She is such a brilliant woman, and so insightful. She teaches the course in such a comprehensive yet intellectually stimulating way. Her TAs were awesome as well- REALLY recommend taking her class

she is amazing

Prof. Braitstein is the cutest, most sweet prof you will ever meet! She really takes the time to cover the material slowly and patiently, making sure everyone understands. Prof. Braitstein makes lectures feel like you're at thanksgiving and your cool aunt is teaching you about something she really loves. Professor Braitstein was very engaging. I really loved the assigned papers, which involved discussing how the Buddhism that is lived out today relates to foundational Buddhist themes and doctrines. I recommend this course.
This teacher does not convey concepts clearly and her impatience shows easily. She does not show the average student rhetoric respect and maturity they deserve.
Graded on a paper (30%), final (60%), and participation (10%). Very sweet teacher and interesting course. However, teacher does not response to emails.

I had Prof Khoury for torts in 1L and have also taken another of her classes since. While she didn't start torts off great (online), after soliciting feedback and changing things the rest of the class was great. Logical structure to classes and really wants you to understand.

Took her in French and she was great. Reminds of a kindergarten teacher in that she seems to really care but still has a lot of sustenance to what she's saying. If you ask a question that's too far ahead of the class, she will shut it right down. Also, not the class to try test out your French writing.
Extremely condescending and combative outside the classroom. Very unpleasant memories of engaging with this professor. Avoid.

Prof. Khoury is lovely. Her lectures are clear and she covers a whole range of issues thoroughly. She uses many non-legal sources which is refreshing. She has high expectations and so her grading is pretty tough, but overall she prepares you well for the assignments. She is very helpful in office hours & she gives good feedback!
I had this professor while on exchange and found her very difficult to learn from mainly since she does not provide patient answers to students and often speaks to them as child
Ineffective communicator. This prof has little respect for her students

I found Khoury very difficult to engage with as a professor. She often explains concepts in ambiguous terms and becomes easily impatient with students. She may mean well but often micro-manages the classroom which leaves students feeling constantly on edge. Unfortunately I did not enjoy her teaching style compared to other McGill professors.
Talks down to students.

Lessard, apart from his reputation (banquet), is not the best lecturer. MECH210 has two 50-minute midterms and the grading scheme is inflexible (25 Midterm 1 / 25 Midterm 2 / 50 Final). He is dismissive during office hours, and essentially reads off the slides, but I will say he is somewhat entertaining and does some fun activities in class.

A very easy-going prof. He took his time going through the content and had examples and solutions right on his slides. I would have liked for him to write out the solution to better understand the steps but it is not a deal breaker. The only graded content is the 2 midterms and the final so be sure to do the optional assignments to prepare.

Very kind and chill guy. Fair exams, and pretty straightforward on how to do well. Only grievance was that one of the midterms and the final both had a question that was ambiguous/had an impossible situation, which a lot of us wasted time on (later removed). Was a bit frustrating considering 100% of our grade was based on the 2 midterms and final.

Cool guy, really respected in the faculty. From what I know, he does insane research. Teachingwise though, this lectures aren't the best, or even moderately good. Had a tougher grading criteria than the other prof. Still my favourite first year course though thanks to the AMAZING content I learnt from him. Man's also going on a bike tour at 62.

Such a great prof!! His lectures are not boring at all if you like the material. His exams are rough (and he takes off a lot of points for small mistakes) but if you practice you'll be fine. His feedback on assignments is useless. He is very friendly and will help you at the end of class if needed.
First midterm is pretty difficult but then you get used to it and will do better on midterm 2

Heavy on projects and if you do everything well material wise in the project, he'll kill you on small technicallities. Like font size for one word is different. Really minor stuff to bring your grade down as much as possible. Our project got a B+ and material wise we got a 100 but 60 on report organization.

His midterms are brutal. After the midterm he redoes it in class and it takes him longer than the time allowed to do it with the answers right there and cutting corners. How do you expect students learning the material to do it faster than the teacher literally just copying the answers down.

Very clear lectures and good flow to the structure of the material. The derivations for composite materials are pretty tedious but he made the class interesting nonetheless. Assignments are fun to complete and not frustrating. Lecture slides could use a revamp

Probably the worst lectures I've attended, extremely boring and does not explain well. Do not rely on his slides for revision, use the textbook instead. He may be funny at times, but you do not want him as your Prof - avoid if possible. I believe that feedback shouldn't be given based on a prof's personality or jokes, but on his teaching ability.

She makes it very clear what's important to know for exams. She's very sweet and loves in-class discussion, perhaps to a fault. Sometimes, when she responds to student questions, she turns the question back on the class, which can make her seem unconfident or as if she doesn't know the answer, which is unfortunate because it's obviously not true.

Very nice Prof. She knows her part in BIOL202 is extremely difficult to explain, tries her best and interacts a lot with students to answer questions. Really the only way to truly understand is to do the exercise because conceptually its hard to grasp. Her question on the final were fair

Her lectures are useless. She explains things superficially and speaks slower than anyone I've ver met (she sounds normal at 1.5-1.75x)...honestly just watch the lectures at a sped up rate and read/make flashcards from the textbook.

She seems like a lovely person who cares about students and is very passionate about genetics. However, she struggles to explain tough concepts and is not coherent throughout her lectures. She would probably be better off teaching easier subjects than the conceptually the hardest part of Biol 202.

Her section is very challenging conceptually at times, however, she did her very best to explain it as well as she could. Some concepts really require you to consider outside of the class as well, so make sure to do all her weekly and textbook exercises. She was the most available professor for office hours and questions in general.

So so kind and helpful, by far my fav BIOL202 prof. Clearly wants everyone to succeed. Her material is challenging and honestly if you want to do well, you need to go to her office hours. Her exam questions are fair but require a decent amount of work outside of class to understand the material.

I wasn't prepared for Prof Nilson's style of lecture, which I would say could best be described as "spaced out". It is almost as through she rushes through the difficult stuff she tests us on because because she herself can't deal with the complexity.  Sometimes I  wondered if she is overwhelmed by it, or perhaps "high" on something or other.
Very nice lady but she speaks super slowly and never finishes the slides. Her content isn't difficult though and final exam qs this year were more than fair. Best to watch recordings at 2x.

horrifyingly difficult, confusing, you think she is nice but she comes around to bite you so hard on the exams. just avoid at all costs. 

Professor Nilson, get better.

DO NOT rely on her lectures! STUDY FROM GRIFFITHS! Her lecture content fantastically glosses over the important details and concepts needed for exams. I am grateful I heeded the advice of previous RMP posters.
Thank you, Dr Pavelka, for a great term !!

I strongly disliked this course. While the instructor was kind and provided many useful practice problems, the flipped format did not work well. Learning from unclear videos that skipped steps made it very difficult to understand concepts, especially as a beginner in organic chemistry.
The man the myth the legend. I love Pavelka, she made org so fun and she really wants you to do well. Lenient grading scheme. Fair exams.
She's pretty awesome
My all-time favourite professor. Her class is super organized, and you always know what you need to do. She cares about every student. The best!

Super kind and caring and the course is so well organized. Adjusting to the flipped format is tough at the beginning, so just use all the resources she provides (Khan Academy links, tutorial problems, workbook questions, etc.) and you'll be fine. The content is fun once everything comes together.
Very good lecturer, well paced and clear. It's a flipped course though. Grading is very lenient and exams are easy.
She's super kind and funny, and you can tell she genuinely tries her best to help as many students as possible. The course is structured very clearly and she explains the material very well.
Uses a flipped classroom format. Not my favourite, but at least the lecture recordings are understandable.

Her flipped format gives a lot of room for practice which is great but her actual lectures are awful. She doesn't explain anything. The class isn't that hard just don't watch her videos alone. Supplement with MasterOrganic Chem textbook. The exams were fair, usually just one harder question on it the rest are straightforward. Lots of practice avail

Prof. Pollock was a great professor and always was willing to answer any additional questions I had after class. She is very nice and showed enthusiasm for the subject, and she released clear rubrics and coordinated lectures with labs. the course content is pretty easy, so just stay on top of weekly lab assignments and papers.

Laura is so sweet and and great professor. The material she teaches in BIOL206 isn't too hard and her instructions and grading for the final presentation were very clear. Her lectures were easy to follow and the slides were clear.

Amazing prof, great speaker, class work is well organized. I loved him, I didn't go to all the classes but the ones I did go to were a lot of fun. It seems like he gives a lot of work cause there's a lot of essays to write, but they're super short and take like 15 minutes to do and you'll get above 95%.
Excellent class
Chen is an amazing prof. As he states in the first class, it is quite difficult not to get an A. The course is extremely organized. He is a very easy grader, and the assignments are made to be fun.
Fun but unnecessary lectures
very nice guy who seems passionate. bird course
The reflections and assignments are tedious, I do admit. Still, sit back and enjoy the ride because everyone gets an A in the class. I went to class twice but still made it, thanks to my group mates!

Prof. Chen made this introductory and frankly filler class as fun and interesting as it could be. Really caring and funny too. 
However, beware that this class has excessive assignments for a 1 credit course, which although aren't hard, take up lots of time. Most are group projects
His assignments are super easy, he's a really nice guy and explains things clearly.

Inverted class is not good. Asking to spend 30-45 minutes 3 times a week watching videos to prepare for the lecture. In class he is not spending enough time to explain the heavy content.
And even if you spend this time to watch the videos, there are still 2 papers per week to submit (his worksheet and reflective papers). On top of quizzes 1 week/2
Worst professor ever
He has no rubric and will just write down a number as your grade, he has no clear feedback and is quite unfair when marking. Also he does not believe in any opinion but orthodox.

This professor is so bad. Nothing in the class makes any sense, and he is not approchable at all. He didn't stick to any sort of syllabus and was didn't respond to an emails from the class during final exams. He didn't have any sort of grading criteria, and when you asked about your papers, he couldn't explain his critiques. Nobody liked him.
As everyone knows, he is a genius and famous scholar. He is a little hard to follow, but he will try to be helpful and give you a fair grade.

This professor will change your life, if you let him. Don't expect to understand everything he says, but when you are able to follow his train of thought your mind will be blown. I highly recommend all of his classes, but only for those who are willing to take the challenge in order to experience genuine learning from a true genius.
A little hard to follow but among the most prominent professors of Jewish Studies worldwide.  Fair grader and pretty helpful.
He is very unorganized and hard to follow. He is a difficult marker and I tell everyone not to take his classes

Here's the scoop on J-Law: Kaplan will never agree with you and it is veeeery hard to do well. However, you can get away with not paying attention (dont worry hes very incoherent) not doing a single reading before the day before and still do moderately well- B range. J-Law is a big regret for me because I learnt absolutely nothing :(

3 things to consider prior to taking Jewish Law with Lawrence Kaplan...1) Do you care about getting an "A" - because you can't. 2) Do you care about learning anything useful - because you won't. 3) Do you want to laugh uncontrolably at a ridiculous "teacher" - because that's all you will do. Only take with a bunch of friends you can laugh with.

Prof Kaplan is a very intelligent man. He was assigned to teach this course at the last minute and it was clearly not his field of expertise. His lectures were unclear and he usually didn't answer questions (avoided/forgot?) the question in his answer. Hard marker; just read the textbooks and ignore the lectures and you'll be fine. Avoid if possibl

Will venture on McTavish to find his students when too many of us are late, his scholarship is his world and his joy, he loves the material so much that he often forgets we the students are there. Only take him if you're interested, but its really worth it.
interesting content, pretty clear and super fair exam questions
love this guy so far, his slides are amazing, he explains things so well!!
Prof Kazak is very cool, takes time to explain the material in different ways, and makes sure everyone understands. His material isn't too hard, and his exam questions were very fair.
His content wasn't too demanding, and he explained concepts pretty well. He tells you what you need to know for the exam, and his questions aren't too tricky. He's a pretty funny dude as well.

a very humbling experience overall. along with long hours winter night mental torture lectures (torture is an exaggeration though) but barely survived and did not even need the course but it was too late to back out

For strong engineering background! advanced stats, mathlab, classworks, assignments, group presentations. lecture-heavy, no tutorials. save cgpa, take lighter 3-credit.15% grade before withdrawal deadline & 30% midterm a day after deadline. guide did not relate to exam. 
Prof's advice: do better next time. someone got 100% so i'm doing it right.

The prof teaches well but the tests and assignments are harder and requires great level of matlab programming and using NC file. Its better not to take if you fear your grades will go down due to this course

This is a CIVIL engineering course, do not consider the course description accurate. It's basically a climate statistics course on Matlab. Evaluations are Matlab graphs... we discuss adaptations in terms of increased capacity, not design. Prof Sushama has clearly limited knowledge about what she is teaching due to her background in Civil
Meh at best. Material is fairly easy but exams are hard.

I only had one class with Lea but she was disrespectful to students and expected us to know way too much for a beginner course... maybe if you have some background in Hebrew you'll be fine though. She just seems mean and is hard to understand as well.

She is to her core a tough but caring immigrant Grandma.
She teaches very well, and managed to get me in one year from zero Hebrew to a pretty good level.
She is very caring, she always did everything she could to make sure we would LEARN, was always kind and accommodating, creating a very nice class environment 
But it is a Language course... hard
Was warned about taking her by the previous ratings but she is honestly amazing. She created a huge bond with all the class and WE ALL loved her. Would certainly take her again.

She loves to hear herself talk. She doesn't care to actually challenge students and is incredibly unclear about her expectations. I would definitely not recommend to take a course with her, though you will likely get an A. Waste of time and money if you care to actually learn.

Giveret Lea, or the 'intellectual' as she prefers to be called, but who goes to the bathroom to clean her tachat like everyone else ... and even after 30 years in the beautiful province of Quebec, she still does not speak a word of French ... as bad of a person and teacher as her husband ...

Awful teacher, but more importantly, horrible person. Rude, nasty, evil - the look on her face is always bad, and a good reflection of her very bad nature. Avoid this course and as much as possible - many people have already said that she is a very bad person, and having tested her, she very much confirms her bad reputation.
Rude and very arrogant (for nothing), and this, for only teaching entry level Hebrew at the university level. Giveret Leah should teach an entire class emphasizing only one word: chutzpah.

Hebrew is her native language, teaches elementary Hebrew at the university level ... so naturally easy work for her ... but then also vents about her salary. However, and for the more than 30 years here, still does not speak a word of French ... one extremely arrogant and nasty person ... without any sincere goodness whatsoever ... one big B ...

Lea is quite impatient with students who either don't understand or don't remember words. Buckle up, you're still going to have to work quite bit to get those words down but overall she's nice in her own way, quizzes and makes sure you can speak as well as write and you get to learn hebrew!

really good prof! i never saw her be mean, the assignments were really interesting and relevant and she marks very easy. all you need to do is participate and she will like you, she's pretty relaxed if you cant finish an assignment and gave a lot of extensions. take her class!
very harsh grader
Participation really matters in the conferences, you have to prepare in advance. He is a great lecturer, very engaging and clear.
amazing Prof - super knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. he's a very fast speaker but takes the time to make sure everyone understands. grading scheme for papers was very reasonable.

Great lecturer! His class was super engaging and very helpful. He was also accessible and helpful to talk to to discuss things I didn't understand. The grading could be quite tough, particularly for the essay. I would also recommend that you attend lectures before doing readings because they're easier to understand after the prof explains them.

Amazing course, interesting and grading is based on 3 papers. TAs are kind and graded lightly, was easy to do well and writing the papers was quite fascinating cause a lot of the writing requires extra research.

Easiest class ever, take it. He's so funny and caring. The TAs are super generous and nice with their grading. The midterms and final are essays at home. I know at first it might seem like a lot of reading but! The midterm allows u to choose your question with the readings you wanna choose. So no need to read them all. Conferences are helpful

Challenging class with hundreds of pages of readings and tough grading on papers and exams. The professor is funny and engaging, but the TA—following the professor's instructions—uses conferences primarily to assess whether students have done the readings, rather than to facilitate learning.

Only complaint:1 TA was so trash at grading 200 level papers +unprofessional/unhelpful. Kinda just gassed up her conference into thinking she was chill then hit you with a v mid grade. She no bueno for those trying to build a base in poli. thankfully I had a way around her grading me, but beware if yo TA seems too chill to be true she may just be:0

Take this class if you want to be challenged, this Prof is extremely knowledgeable. Yes the readings are heavy, yes the lectures require constant attention but by the end of the semester you will have learned a lot about international trade and Bretton woods institutions. He will seriously engage with your questions in office hours.

Papers are graded harshly by the TAs- you'll lose 20-30 points for a slightly unclear structure or bad thesis. Class itself is good, lectures are clear and engaging and course content isn't particularly difficult.

Incredibly difficult to follow along in lectures, reads straight off of PowerPoints that are filled with too many words. Made the mistake of taking this class when it was not mandatory, ended up being just about the hardest class I've taken at McGill.

Need to counter all the negative reviews! This was my first Econ course and I found it very fair/easy. The prof is friendly, she thoughtfully answers student questions during lecture. Her slides are detailed (no need to buy the textbook), and even though she reads from them, it's still worth going to class to avoid falling behind on the material.

Very sweet but boring teaching style and very exam-heavy course. Slides did not cover all of the math concepts, so buying the textbook was very helpful. The final was worth 70 percent, but was very reflective of the lecture content.

For a class with a final exam worth 70%, it wasn't the most fair or caring. The weekly problem sets are very long with lots of variety in types and difficulties. There were good questions to practice with, but also very time consuming. I would be better off knowing which topics and difficulty to expect, the course materials are very spread out.

I took this as my first economics course and found it hard to follow. Lectures mostly repeated slides, and explanations weren't always clear for beginners. The course is graded 30% midterm and 70% final, so exams matter a lot. Better suited for students with some econ background.

She's nice but essentially just reads off the slides, which are taken from the textbook. Gives problem sets weekly which is helpful. Grade is 30% midterm & 70% final, which is pretty harsh for an intro class. After the first few weeks basically 10 people were actually showing up for the lectures. Not ideal class set up if you've never done econ.

Seems sweet, but lectures are unhelpful. Exams were more difficult than other professors' classes. Textbook is also not much help, she uses her own problem sets for practice and exam questions, which are very long, complex, and detailed compared to lecture material. Expectations are unclear since there is no study guide for the midterm or final.
lectures were super slow and difficult to understand - it was honestly easier to self teach this class than to go to lecture. I think this was her first time teaching 208 but lord was it rough.

From what I've heard, she is the best 208 prof, she provides lots of practice problems for each unit, and most will be on the exams. However, you are only graded on the midterm and final, so prepare for them well. She explains the material in-depth and doesn't hesitate to ask questions as she will answer them no matter how long it takes.

baumann is a cutie but her lectures were pretty dull. was essentially just reading straight off the slides. the only reason i was able to bag the A is because i bought the textbook and used the problem sets it gives you to self study (for both the midterm and the final). cannot recommend doing that enough!! easiest way to do well in the class.

IFA2 is a hard class no matter who teaches it. I'm glad I chose Zvi. He knows his stuff. Just print out the slides and take notes. Also try to do ALL of the end of chapter questions (I'm not kidding). Only read the book if you don't get what he taught in class. Exam questions are based on what he taught in class. Also be warned, IFA2 is fast paced!

Tough class but without a doubt an excellent professor. Professor Singer knows his stuff and will take his time to ensure you understand if meet with him. There are a lot of topics to be covered with limited class time.

Tough class, which may explain some of the comments here. He puts the resources out there and he's available after classes and office hours. Just be prepared to work yourself hard and you'll do well. Assignments could be graded much easier though

Zvi's class will either be pretty easy or your worst nightmare. It depends on whether you take the time to meet with Zvi after class. There is a lot of material to cover in the course and not a lot of time for Zvi to teach it thus his lectures are often rushed. Meet him after class and he is more than willing to go over as many examples as you want
good luck with this teacher and the way that he teaches and marks. extremely hard assignments. study really hard otherwise u should repeat the class.

IFA 2 is a hard class to grasp, especially with Zvi teaching it.  He tries, with his jokes, but his teaching is horrendous. Examples straight from the textbook and very unclear at answering questions.  Have homework every week, 3 assignments, insane midterm and final which he said was "reasonable".  If you can, take this class with ANYONE but him.

This is one of those classes you'll carry with you long after graduation. It's engaging, inspiring, and truly eye-opening. I'd recommend it to anyone, no matter your program, the skills you gain go beyond faculty expectations and change the way you think about Canadian institutions, history, and power dynamics.
Unfortunately, the lectures did not keep my attention. I had trouble focusing in class, but the material is interesting! The lectures are important to go to, but I fell asleep a few times.

The professor is funny, with great and interesting lectures. There are no PowerPoint slides or posted recordings. Lectures mainly build on expanding the broader + more detailed ideas from the assigned readings, helping deepen understanding rather than introducing entirely new material. Great elective to take but LOTS of reading to do.
incredible, engaging, enrapturing lecture. everyone should take this class regardless of faculty or degree!
the most underrated class and prof at McGill. everyone should take this class if they can, the content is so important esp as a student in Canada. I'd take this class 100x times again
take this class if u can!

Les was a great prof, definitely one worth taking a class with. He is is very unconventional and has no tech policy, but assignments are just journal entries with use of a reading or two. His whole view is that learning comes from personal growth within, not tests/research papers. A great intro to indigenous scholarship for non-indigenous students.

If you have a chance to take a class with Prof Les you must. Most insightful course at McGill and for a new Prof he is incredibly dedicated and a wonderful lecturer. . Readings are a little dense but are so important to do and assignments were very fair. A respectful and genuine professor, super understanding. Can't say enough good things

Professor Sabiston is a new professor, but an amazing lecturer. His lectures and readings are incredibly insightful and encourage introspection. If you get the chance to take his course, I would! Very human, relatable professor and presents course material in a very engaging way.

For just beginning a professorship at McGill, Les is a great prof! He is incredibly organized, while being understanding and flexible with students. Assignments (mainly essays) heavily focus on the themes of reflection and positionality. Very available for one-on-one meetings. Gives detailed feedback and encourages participation in class.
He is so nice. Very generous with grading. His notes are a little disorganized but everything you need is in the textbook anyway and his lectures are clear so not a big deal.
love this guy. lectures not necessary but he's fun

Not a really good teacher, hard to understand what he explains. However he is a really nice person. The problems sets are really hard to do but are exactly what you will have on the exams so you can get a good grade by knowing how to do the problem sets. Grading is fair.
Awful experience, lecture slides are incoherent and incomprehensible.

had his micro in 2017.his Chinese accent was strong and some explanations weren't clear. But he was one of those professors who actually cared. Like, he'd answer emails in time, and if students needed help, he'd stay late after office hours without making a big deal about it. If you just put in the work on assignments, you could get solid grades.
Great prof I love him

Decent prof. Goes very quickly on the mathematical part of the course and very (sometimes comically) slowly on the theoretical. Does explain the material decently and doesn't mark assignments. Also curves generously.

Very unorganized lectures. This prof is all over the place. He's extremely intelligent and knows his material well, but the way he lectures makes it so confusing. Relying on lectures will make the course harder for you, it definitely did for me.

Professor Xue had a way of taking simple concepts and making them more difficult to understand. Besides this, he does care about his students and tries to explain the material as best he can. The lectures, however, are difficult to pay attention to. I got a good enough grade just attending the lectures and reading the textbook while he yapped away.

Professor Xue is very knowledgeable about the content, but it is often difficult for him to "dumb it down" for students who do not understand his initial explanations. His lectures are kind of dry, but good for anyone interested in theory. You can re-teach yourself the whole sem in like 20 hrs before exams. Problem sets look exactly like exams.

Professor Lapointe is one of the kindest professors at Desautels. She is always available to help and creates a very supportive learning environment. Her three-hour classes go by quickly, and the assignments and projects are engaging and interesting. Overall, a great experience and a professor I would recommend.

She was a good professor, but she marks your papers and group projects very unfairly. If you're not on her good side you won't get a good grade. I started off liking the class and ended up being so disappointed with the professor. I wish she was more fair.
Really great course!  Wonderful prof.  She is unique!

As I am leaving town after graduation, I wanted to pay a tribute to the best prof I had at McGill. Prof. Lapointe you rock!! She is really terrific. And she can be so funny at times! But don't try and mess with her because she can be a tough cookie as well... Thanks for a great semester!
She is great!  Funny and I learned a lot.  She seems to truly care!!
She's really great   I learned a lot and had a great time  She is very experienced
Very useful, nice , passionate, fair excopt for that TA guy

Fun lecturer, very passionate. Fair grading, however as presentations are not done all at once, students who present later get to improve/improvise their slides, which she did not take into account. Great Prof overall.
Lacks professional experience. Very academic. More like a school teacher. Very judgmental.
She's a real good prof. Interesting, knows her stuff well. She knows how to keep the students' attention. I wish they were all like her!

Really caring and approachable professor. One of the best in ECE Department.
Took course 688 (now ECSE 561) which is really good if you like Software Testing.
Its not too difficult and really fun as you'll never feel burdened with deadlines.
She also makes courses very fun and easy to score good grades with bonus points on assignments
Great prof. Great course. Take her!!
Great Prof and Lecture!
My best professor ever!
Caring, Interesting and responsible
Good Professor with perfect lectures and really generous in grading. Easy pass course with interesting content in software testing. Reasonable workload with enough time for working on them.
Very kind. Very prepared class. Funny demonstration by herself

Childress is very kind, passionate, and will answer any question you have. She gives opportunities to get extra points. However, she assumes that everyone has the same physics background as herself. Without doing physics in high school, you are screwed. The only reason I did well in the class is by spending hours every week with a tutor reviewing.

The professors vocabulary use took away from the main points that I felt like were important. I spent so long trying to decode what she was actually saying that I couldn't understand the main concepts. I found it overall an extremely challenging class, but she provides lots of opportunity to do well.

One of the nicest profs, clearly really passionate about the material. However, her lectures were formatted quite differently where its mostly in class polls of conceptual questions testing material that you learn yourself over the weekend, personally I did not gain much from attending lectures.

Lilian is a super nice person but not very good at teaching. The people that do well in PHYS101 are people who've already seen the material in highschool - if you've never taken a physics class before, get a tutor. The course is fast and is hard to keep up with when teaching yourself the content. She is super passionate but wouldn't take again.

Lilian teaches physics in a very different way, and it's pretty daunting for a 1st year. Not that her approach is bad, but I personally struggled a lot with it coming from highschool physics. Other than that, her lecture notes suck so it's best if you go to the lectures.

Professor Childress is very well-spoken, kind, engaging and clearly passionate about the content she teaches. She has an amazing ability to explain difficult concepts in a clear and concise way. During class, there is a mix of lecturing and practice problems pertaining to the concepts being taught.
No Comments

She's a really cool teacher, can talk to students really easily and responds to emails really fast. Very fair marker, but you get better marks if you write your papers in French. Exams aren't hard, just memorize lecture slide info, which is sometime common knowledge anyways. Don't worry if you're taking a class with her, she's awesome!

Great professor! Her test are exactly like the examples given in class. The final exam is exactly like her quizzes and practice exams, like if you do her practice problems there is a high chance the problem will be on the final exam.

She's an amazing prof: lectures are super clear, well-structured, & very helpful at office hours. Posts clear lecture notes too. The grading scheme is forgiving but the exams are deadly. Midterm average so bad she introduced a new grading scheme. Lowest poss. weight for final is 50%. Content is really difficult, defo the hardest class I've taken.
She very clearly explained everything and broke everything down into simple terms. Exams were fair and webworks were helpful practice, but not overly difficult. Overall, a great prof!
Great lecturer and very forgiving grading scheme. Assignments and especially the final were very long and time-consuming but graded generously.

Great lecturer. 1.0 difficulty for the grading scheme, not the course material. Assignments are basically free 100s because you get to resubmit after seeing the solutions. You get the better grade between midterm/quizzes for 30% (both of which had high averages). Hard final but only worth 40%. Got an A and I barely understand the course material.
Her outfits are awesome.

One of the best lecturers at McGill - very easy to follow, organized, great handwriting, follows her posted lecture notes. Gives great intuition.

The assignments were very long, but graded generously after corrections. Quizzes are easy if you know what concept she's trying to get at. Online finall but BRUTALLY long, a real killer - 19 questions!

By far the most amazing course i have taken in McGill. She is extremely orginized, and the hand-writing is awesome. Assignments are hard but they help you learn. However this is definitely not an easy course (Honors Analysis 3), she goes through materials super fast and some proofs are way too long. But in all I realy enjoy the course.
The GOAT of the math department. She's awesome, very smart, and also someone to look up to.
Excellent teacher. The assignments are helpful since the students get to correct their own assignments when provided with the solutions, very effective for learning from mistake.

extremely boring lectures that are like watching paint dry and somehow get more confusing the more she explains. Exams are fair compared to problem sets. In office hours she is incredibly patient and reassuring however it can take some time to actually extract the answer to your question as she goes on tangents.
lecture is useless, and just read the textbook and you will pass the exam.

Linda Reven can't teach. Unfortunately she is one of the most helpful, caring and accommodating professors in the chemistry department. However, like most professors, she lacks the ability to successfully transfer information onto students. The homework was fair as were the exams.
She is a great individual. She may not be the best prof but she is extremely helpful when you go to her office.

Very boring prof.  Textbook is mandatory.  Do every problem she assigns as the exams are the same exact questions for the most part.  Didn't really learn a whole lot from lectures, she isn't in touch with the class very well.  Over all disappointing.  Avoid if possible.

Very monotone. Have a cup of joe before going to class because she will likely put you to sleep. In terms of material, she wasn't very effective at explaining the notes. However, she follows the textbook very closely. Fair exams and fair marker.
BORING TEACHER!!! I never listened to a word she said... study from the book and her assignments.

No point in going to class. Just read the book and you'll do fine. Honestly, there is no point in going to class. Her assignments are pretty easy but her midterm and final were somewhat difficult but not impossible.

Every day I would go home and read the book, do the problems and come to class understanding the material. Every day she would open her mouth and I would leave class VERY confused. This is the worst teacher I have ever had.
She gets better as the semster move along.

Grades are assigned at random. Teacher goes on rants the entire semester explaining what could could all be summed up in 2 weeks of lectures. The material is boring and redundant. She does not respect her rubrics and pulls marks out of her ass. I have emailed her several times and she does not answer. Would never take her again.

She is nice, but she makes you work way too hard, and her grading is pretty random, even though she says otherwise. She doesn't like when people get As in her class, which is outrageous and so UNFAIR lol. I have gotten As everywhere since my first semester, and this is the first class where I'm considering using the S/U option AVOID IF U CAN
Very good teacher! Tests fairly and very enthusiastic when teaching!
Very basic content, pretty boring
SHES THE BOMB
great teach  very enthusiastic
put in some effort and get the A
Did not enjoy her teaching or way of organizing her classes - in fact they were quite disorganized.
Lacks communication skills and organization. The positive reviews are outdated. Students have a hard time learning with her.
Disorganized and lacks communication skills. Does not reflect McGill's reputation and intellectual rigor.
She is confusing to listen to. I feel like I was tricked by the good reviews on rate my prof.
Other than her funny personality, she is a hard prof to listen to. Her way of explaining things is so disoriented and unorthodox that she can make simple concepts hard to understand.

Hilarious person - threw chocolate bars at us to showcase an example. Pop-up quiz (10%) pretty chill if you work a minimum, same difficulty as the midterm (30%). Both online in class. Final exam was fair.

IDK why people glaze her. I did not learn very much and she makes you do ridiculous things like skits in class. If you want to actually learn about econ, don't take her. Also, her final was way tougher than I thought it would be! Not sure why people think she's super easy.

Professor Zhang is very kind and genuinely cares about her students. However, her teaching methods do not measure up. Her lectures were quite disorganized, rambling, and difficult to follow. I relied heavily on the Pearson textbook and practice problems, and ended up teaching myself all the course content. Do not rely on the lectures to pass.
She's super sweet and caring but her exams were a bit on the harder side... Her final had questions that were never seen in class but enough to figure out during the exam...

really unengaging lectures. assigned a group project right before finals started, and after we did the project we also had to write an essay on it, and the essay was due the SAME DAY as the final. would not recommend
Lots of reading, but genuinely so kind and ready to help.
Boring lectures that you actually can learn by your self.

Although the readings can seem like a struggle, if you sit down and comprehend the basics, she'll fill in all the gaps and answer all further questions in class.  She's always there if you have questions or need guidance and truly wants you to succeed

Lisa Barg is such a nice lady.  Though the lectures can be a little boring, she wants you to learn and wants to help you.  If you actually do the readings, they are extremely interesting and helpful.  She deserves more credit.

Prof. Barg shows great interest in her work and is super enthusiastic about it. Her only problem is a lack of presence while lecturing and struggling to strike a balance between holding the class's hand with simple, leading questions and not explaining what she means thoroughly enough. She's getting better though from one class to the next.

My favourite professor of the prerequisite year. Though she doesn't have the kind of arresting presence that makes you want to listen if you weren't interested before, her classes are always interesting and worthwhile.

This teacher has absolutely NO pedagogical skills. Although she does show some interest in her subject, she fails miserably at delivering it. As you can see, I did manage to pull an A, and was probably not alone. Just know that you can't rely on her, you'll have to do so much work because her lectures are USELESS. The T.A.'s were good though...
Messy slides. Lots of long reading assignments. Attendance to tutorials is mandatory. Take S/U option if you can.

Please refrain from taking this class if you are in engineering. The workload is exagerated for a 200 level course open to various faculties and the marking is unfair. There are so many readings and they are boring but WILL be on the exam. If you are interested in the material take it pass/fail. I made a mistake thinking it was going to be easy.

Great class! The professor was extremely clear and engaging, and she really knew the material. I really felt like the readings, the exams and her papers allowed me to learn A LOT.  The workload really isn't that large, take the class!

Very boring class, after a full semester I have no idea what the course is about. Definitely a waste of time, too much work for a complementary course. Marking for essays relies more on English rather than content, exams have nothing to do with the many LONG readings. Stay away from this class!
Gives fair tests and interesting assignments. Great teacher, knows her stuff and expresses it well. Definitely one of the best classes i've taken at McGill.
Great teacher, but don't expect any grades to be returned to you until 4 or 5 weeks after submission. Very interesting lecturer and has lots of experience to feed off of.
No Comments

The best class I ever took.  She presents the material clearly and is very knowledgable in her field.  She has worked all over the world and brings good examples into class.  Nothing bad at all to say about her.

Lisa is a fantastic teacher who evidently loves what she does and genuinely cares about each student. The readings that she assigns are pertinent, the in-class discussions are insightful, and the class structure as a whole felt more collaborative rather than lecture-heavy. I would wholeheartedly recommend taking her class(es)!
Don't take the grading personally because she definitely never gives 100%. I learned a lot from her class and the material is very practical.

You will learn a lot from Dr. Lisa, her stories, and her experiences. She is the pillar of McGill's Music Education Department. Expect to do papers and readings each week but it's not unreasonable and her assigned materials are actually interesting. She will teach you many things on how to become a great music teacher.
Lack of communication skills. Comments in assignments sometimes sound judgmental. Unclear grading criteria. Poor in class material.

Dr. Munter is a fantastic professor. Exams are fair and relevant -- typically focusing on big ideas rather than tiny details. Emphasis on application in the class, such as a drug target discovery project and an oral exam, among other activities like a "treasure hunt". She is fun and keeps things engaging. Makes me want to be a pharmacologist.
Great prof! Her class is really interesting and well taught. It's also graded extremely fairly.
I enjoyed this class!

She takes forever to mark things. We didn't get literally any marks back until December. She is easy though, the course content was never really in depth to begin with. I'm not sure if that's the nature of her teaching style or the "survey" nature of the course.
Dr. Munter is such a nice prof! Super clear lectures, and the best section in the 562 course! I wish I had taken 503 given how she teaches!

Values education over grades! You will be reminded of how much you like learning about new things. Very clear and is more than happy to provide more clarity if needed. Very organized, I really liked the schedule given at the beginning of the semester with weekly lecture material, assignments, and due dates.

She is passionate about what she teaches and her research. She is not the most tech savvy and she is always sick, so, multiple classes were cancelled. Everything is extremely disorganized. The instructions for the material and projects (podcast and especially poster) were unclear, so ask questions. She was unresponsive for emails.

This class and professor Overholtzer are honestly ridiculous. Assignments are incredibly vague and makes them seem as though they are open-ended although they are not and there is a tight scope of what is acceptable. Lectures and lecture slides seemed a bit disorganized. I do not recommend taking Anth 201.

Super vague guidelines for projects and the methods part of the course was rough. Overall, it is very clear that she is both informed and passionate about archeology. Some have said that she talks abt her own research too much, but like, duh. She balances it well with assigned readings that give an insight to the various subfields of archeology.

Dr. Overholtzer is so kind, and passionate about what she does, which shows through her teaching! The theory is so interesting, a very intersectional approach. Conferences were useless and not informative, which is unfortunate because most were confused and did not feel well equipped for the rather odd and unclear final project.

Do not recommend taking this prof if you want to have a good semester. Harsh grading, inaccessible outside class, lectures were boring and useless and didn't provide any knowledge or insight on how to do the assignments. Very disorganized and unreasonable - again I do NOT recommend

ANTH 201 is definitely an easy course. Lectures are engaging, she is clearly super passionate and caring. 
Too many comments criticizing how she talks about her own research - I feel like this is gendered criticism, her research is relevant to the class and shows her passion and expertise, I personally love when she integrates it into lecture!

She is disorganized and totally inaccessible outside of class. You cannot connect with her for help or interest. You need to cc others like the dean if you want a response. Ironic as she boasts about "pedagogy" in her syllabus. It's discouraging to be ignored constantly, if I were still in school I'd avoid her classes.
The class has high expectations, but the professor doesn't hold herself to the same the standards.

Honestly, she is an amazing professor. Easiest class to get an A in because most of the grade is completion based (attendance, conferences, etc.). Weekly quizzes are very reasonable with unlimited time. She can be difficult to get ahold of by email but if you just talk to her at the end of the class, she's very helpful.
Good prof I would take her again. The assignments are a little wacky but the content is interesting and she is definitely passionate about the subject.

Professor Lloyd is great to talk to during class hours, but has an uncomfortable energy during office hours. Homeworks are stressful because, and although there are clear grading criterias, it almost feels like the grade you receive is random. I received criticism multiple times for not tackling points that weren't even on the homework guidelines.

Prof Whitesell gave super engaging lectures, and this course was incredibly interesting overall. He was super caring and understanding with his students, and grading criteria was very straightforward. I would absolutely take a class with him again :)

Great professorclearly knows his material (this course is absolutely fascinating, btw), stays accessible w/engaging lectures (lots of A/V) & doesn't take himself too seriously. Does grade papers a bit hard but always gives feedback, & if you show critical thinking (& add in some fancy words), he also gives out As. We had 3 papers & a final exam.

This was among the better electives I've taken. So interesting, you barely need the coursepack, and lectures are really fun. Professor Whitesell is super nice and funny. It's a pleasure to come to class

Lloyd was a good lecturer and knows his stuff about music history.  He made critical thinking interesting with the topics he picked.  Although he's a bit of a tough grader (i.e. the Midterm that never ended) he's worth it in the end.

Such an amazing professor! Absolutely loved his class, he is very passionate about film music which made his lectures so much fun. Tests were a bit tough and he marks papers kinda hard but you can do well if you go to him for advice and ask questions!
My favorite prof from McGill! He is upbeat and fun. His notes are to the point and he dances a bit too! :) A definite must-take!
He's very good at what he teaches and doesn't beat around the bush when answering questions. Plus, he's funny and plays piano very well! Easy course if you go to lectures and take notes.

best prof ever. he is so funny! he gets really into the music and cracks jokes that aren't really funny but you are compelled to laugh anyway. this was my favourite class this semester! plus the course is an easy A as long as you go to/listen to the lectures.

Amazing. He is so enthusiastic, and clearly loves what he does. Exams are really easy IF you go to class and take good notes. He tells you exactly what to study for the tests. Highly recommended if you have an interest in music history.

I like Luthi and his lectures, but he finds his interpretation of the Cold War to be monolithic. He presents an argument for a specific region/country, then provides information as evidence rather than presenting evidence and allowing students to argue their position.Once you know what he wants to hear, the course is quite reasonable and enjoyable.

Prof Lüthi's take on the Cold War is so refreshing and interesting that you'll find yourself reading his textbook for fun. Lecture can be monotone and some complain they can't understand his accent, but I never found that to be a problem. Essay was tough, very specific criteria wanted, midterm and final were easy if you knew what he wanted

I didn't like him at first, he can also be hard to understand at times, but he has genuinely become one of my favourite profs ive had in my 3 yrs at McGill. The essay was long, but instructions were very clear and exams were fair. Give him a chance, he's actually pretty cool

Prof. is the best I've had at McGill, exams aren't hard, but to get an A go to conferences to get 3 bonus points + helps you study and hear other points of view 

Lectures aren't necessary but super interesting, read his book --> class is based on it. If you read it and skim it a second time its hard to get below A-

Very kind man with a good sense of humour. The course asks are very fair, with generous marking. His accent can be hard to understand at times, but he always makes sure everyone can hear him. Strongly recommend this course and Luthi to anyone!

HIST218He IS a tougher grader than other profs, but not impossible. In weekly papers, the highest you could get was an 85, and I found the essay portion in exams grading tough. He explicitly said he made the final exam's multiple choice section harder bc the class did well on the section for the midterm. His accent is hard to understand sometimes.

Best Professor I've ever had at McGill. He knows so much, is so passionate about what he teaches, and is adorable. His lectures were such a treat to go to, and he's a great story teller. This is the most fufilling class I've taken at McGill, and I would encourage everyone to take one of his classes even if they aren't in HIST. I LOVE YOU LUTHI
Very interesting course. Lectures were a bit unorganized and he has a reputation as a tough grader but I did pretty well.

Hardest but most rewarding class I've taken at McGill. Lectures and readings are dense but what matters is figuring out how to derive the big themes/connections from the Cold War and being able to apply them to essays and exams. Lüthi is engaging, clearly passionate, and accessible outside of class. Would absolutely recommend if you love history.
Honestly, I loved this prof. He is very caring for his students and clearly passionate about what he teaches. Lots of readings and class is not recorded, so I would recommend to go to every lectures.

Good lectures, nice guy, but the final for 356 did not at all reflect what we did all semester. I have no idea why closed-book exam questions are so much harder than assignment questions. Scope of the course was huge, and he didn't give any guidance to prepare for the final. Edit: curved to a 62 avg, got an A but final was unreasonable, still a 3.

I took Prob with Louigi during F23. I thought his lectures were engaging, his homework relevant, and his grading on the HWs/MT generous. However, his final exam was inappropriate, unfair, and misrepresentative of every lecture and evaluation previously given. It was apparently written by Paquette, who has no relation to the course. I felt duped.

Louigi is one of the best profs I've encountered. All lectures were thoroughly prepared and organized, and he was always very helpful. It is clear that he cares about his students and takes his job seriously. In addition, he KNOWS the material and is able to convey it. 
The course is pretty hard, though; the final was indeed brutal.

Good professor. I initially had trouble adjusting to the style of proofs and motivations presented in class and in his typed lecture notes, which he admits certain students may find "terse". The final covered a lot of material and many students claimed to find it hard. Personally won't be taking his classes again but worth taking at least once
Very clear and nice!
Gotta love Louigi
No-nonsense professor that expects a lot from his students. If you aren't ready to put in 100% you should stay away from his classes because he puts in his 100% for the lectures. The exams are tough.
Good Professor that explains the material clearly. The course is a bit hard but he is here to help when necessary.
Very difficult assignments and exams but not a bad instructor.

He is the sweetest prof you will meet, makes you want to go up and give him a hug. The class is really tough imo. It's more of a test of intelligence than hardwork but he makes lectures bearable. He is really patient with his students and genuinely cares for them.
She's GREAT, if you REALLY WANT TO LEARN, TAKE HER CLASSES!! She gives Fantastic advises, not only for school, but as well for professional level!
The best teacher I've ever  had. So professional and helpful!
The lecture notes prepared me well for the exam questions.

He is a great professor. He clearly knows his stuff, but is interesting. I really love his CRISPR talk. He has genuinely impacted the field of molecular biology in a positive way. I am happy that I was in the same room as such a powerful human being.
SOmebody tell this mans to chill on the foreigns. But fr fr, amazing prof like hes got the street and book knowledge. 100!

Started off the semester without knowing how to dress, but suddenly showed up with a ton of drip and made the course very interesting. Would reference a lot of popular music and really knew his things! Great Teacher and can't imagine how good of a father he must be!

He's really got some big drip. He knows his material really well and its a joy and pleasure to watch me give a lecture. The way he describes protein synthesis is like a father explaining the birds and bees to a child. Ya'll capping if you say the opposite.

His section was really intense, but he was the best lecturer in 312. Crystal clear, and amazing slides. As the reviewer below me mentioned, the exam questions were difficult but they were fair (unlike some of the other profs' questions).

He did a decent job in teaching the material but his exam questions are SUPER SUPER hard and focused a lot on the application of the knowledge. so have to know the material from the bottom of the heart. OMG, I am so worried about my grade.
difficult materials, explanations not clear
hes not in micobiology lol, but hes got mad drip so its chill
great
good

She greatly cares about and is interested in the well-being of all her students. She does help you to learn proper technique, but the most important thing for her is expressive communication in your playing. The complainer below didn't stay long enough to realize she will let you follow your own musical ideas once they are convincingly developed.

I studied with her for 3 years back in the late 80s.  My technique at the time was weak and she worked me like a dog.  She is a great technician, and a good teacher for those lacking discipline and/or technique.  She's tough but like previous poster said, cares much about her students.  I don't know how musical/creative she is.
She's tough but she cares very much about her students.  Obviously the person below is a biased jerk.
beware of this woman, she will try to suck you in and break your soul. her students are all wimps with awful technique. AVOID AVOID AVOID
An excellent piano teacher. She is talented, knowledgeable, and really cares about her students.

He speaks pretty quietly and the notes he writes on the black board can be unclear, but he's clearly very knowledgable and can be funny at times. The scribed notes were a lifesaver. His assignments are challenging and time consuming. The lectures are often theory heavy and packed, but the grading is pretty nice and the exams get nice curves.
Luc Devroye is the best and everyone loves him. I miss him and his lectures. Now, I will go and remember him by playing "I'm just a gigolo" on repeat

Very difficult to understand during class, often mumbles and writes way too fast on the chalkboard. That being said, he's very accessible outside of lectures and the scribed notes are a godsend. The material is VERY difficult, but pretty interesting and the grading is generous.

Goat professor. Lectures interesting, although very confusing at times, but with the typed notes provided it's very easy to catch up. Assignments very hard but graded very generously. Go to his office hours, he's a very interesting guy who is extremely knowledgeable on things, even outside of CS and just advice in general. Would 100% take again.

Really great person but his lectures can be confusing with him mumbling the end of half of his sentences. Lectures notes are golden even if they tend to complexify concepts that you can learn in a 3min ytb video. Assignments are really heavy but grading is very generous. Best of luck to anyone taking this class.
Good

Confusing lectures are remedied by amazing notes on his website and great Office Hours. My main criticism is that Luc doesn't give enough time for really long assignments; that being said, I did actually learn a lot because of the challenge. The content is hard but the grading is among the most generous I've ever experienced (both assgn and exams).
Curves

The course was challenging and covered lots of materials. He went pretty fast during lectures, but answered very nicely to students' questions. His class is very interesting as long as you don't care too much about the grade. But he actually gave a big curve on the final, which was really a life saver.

Had a great time in his class. Assignments are hard but interesting and were graded very nicely. Plus you get partners so he really just wants you discussing the problems. Really wish I'd gone to office hours more than just once because he is great and explains everything. Final and midterm were a lot of memorization but had nice curves on them.
Awful boring lecturer. Just reads the slides and doesn't explain examples much. Tests were fair, but he gave extra marks to the few people that attended lectures.

This professor's teaching style is very poor. He is monotonous, his hand writing isn't clear and he doesn't post note solutions. You have to go to class as he only solves the note problems in class. Goodluck for M2 and final exam, because most of the questions are unrelated to assignments and tutorials.

Lectures are useless, professor is unprepared and struggles with solving problems in slides. Notes are disorganized screenshots full of typos. Assignments takes a week, you need to study from books or YouTube. Exam are unrelated and also full of typos. Mentally and physically draining. No official course evaluation, the university knows it's bad.

Overall a good professor. Found that his lectures are pretty dry, but if you can manage to pay attention there's a lot of good stuff in there. Told us very clearly what content would be on the midterms and final. Was perceptive to student feedback and changed the assignment format accordingly.

teacher is lowkey really boring and there are quizzes at the end of class which u get 100% for if you write ur name. you can tell he knows what hes teaching but his class lacks clarity in terms of notes and solutions. he curves sometimes but nothing crazy to be honest. he told us exactly what questions would be on the final so that was pretty bless

His lectures were not very clear. He couldn't figure out how the projector works, so resorted to putting his iPad under the projector instead of connecting to the computer. His handwriting is also very messy. Solutions he wrote are basically undecipherable, even the TAs couldn't solve some of the problems.

He teaches at a painfully slow pace. Pretty boring lectures. Whenever a midterm of final is coming up, he releases old exams with incomplete solutions. The solutions are very messy and extremely hard to read. A huge problem that I've experienced is the lack of response to emails. He will rarely ever answer them. Even during an online midterm.

Midterms were challenging and had questions that were a lot harder than the examples he goes over in class or the assignment questions. Do the hardest questions from the textbook to prepare yourself. The final went terribly for everyone, but don't worry because he usually curves a lot.

Gave very good notes and first and was very clear. Then at the second part of the course the notes were super unclear and it was as if he didn't care. Doesn't look up from his desk and you have to shout if you have a question. Final was super hard. Midterms were OK. Do the practice problems.

You're going to want to sit close when attending lectures because it is VERY difficult to hear. He clearly knows the topic well and does many practice problems. However, the ones that appear on the exam are more difficult so consider doing the harder problems in the textbook and finding problems that mix several of the topics together
Mumbles, delivers confusing information, and responds inappropriately to questions.
Would rate 0/5 if I could, the class is only super hard because of this terrible prof.

Unbelievably confusing. No structure in his course whatsoever. Very unclear slides. Does not follow the textbook. Goes from chapter 3 to 5 back to 2, in the same lecture. For some reason, this semester the tutorials were replaced by graded quizzes. So no tutorials. Therefore not him or the tutor explains practice problems in depth.

The lectures are disorganized and filled with errors. The prof mumbles through class and the notes are impossible to follow. Assignments are unhelpful and disconnected from exams. The exams contain material that was never covered in class. Overall, this course is poorly taught, poorly structured, and extremely frustrating. waste of time and money

Poor lecturer, made mistake on his own exam solutions, expects you to make Matlab assumptions during exams. The textbook is just as bad as he is. I wish you luck if you are taking him, avoid at all cost. Undeniably the worst experience I've had at McGill by far.

Worst prof at McGill, I am literally writing this review as we are in class. This guy couldn't teach a fish how to swim and I put that on G. O. D. Please McGill care for your students this is genuine insanity.
So bad，the notes was in the mess and give a bad grade
Very unorganized. Unclear end of year project that was expected to be completed very quickly during last week of classes.
he is a disorganized professor and his lectures are monotonous, avoid if you can. the exams will be hard but he s lenient in the correction.

This prof is by far the worst I've had, midterms were very difficult and didn't reflect class material, I studied a week straight and still got a 47. He gives incorrect information during exams and refuses to adjust grading to accommodate. Don't bother with regrade as he gaslights you about his policy to avoid regrading. Avoid

Prof. Silva is too disorganized to be teaching a class with such nebulous subject matter. Anth of Meaning would be very interesting if it weren't for her disjointed lectures and incomprehensible PowerPoint slides. That said, I'm sure she was trying her best given the situation. Some of the lectures were interesting (like four or five).
