Her lectures are unorganized and barely discuss the readings that are needed for the assignments. I am confused the entire time I listen to her lectures and she never answers questions clearly. It is really difficult and almost impossible to follow what she is saying and does not do a good job of explaining any of the content of the course.

Professor Silva is great - she's a little skittish but trying her best! She really cares about her students success and is super understanding. Lectures can end up jumbled sometimes, but she does her best to explain everything well. There are 3 papers for this course, they're largely based on assigned readings, fun to do and easy.
Genuinely the most disorganized and ineffective prof I have ever had. Avoid taking all classes with her or if you do, don't bother going because none of the assignments are related to the lectures.

She is enthusiastic about what she teaches and is nice. But she is not good at phrasing things so sometimes it was hard to understand her. The term papers are not directly related to the lectures, but are related to the course readings. They are easy to do though, I was consistently getting 90s on my papers. So do the readings!!

She was a little nervous at first as she was still getting comfortable with teaching, but by the end of the semester her class and teaching improved a lot. The readings we had to do were really text heavy, difficult, and took a very long time to do each week. There was no midterm, and 3 papers throughout the semester which were fun to write.
Easy A, interesting assignments that seldom relate to class material. Lectures are a bit jumbled, but you don't need to attend to do well.

The readings can be a little dense, but Professor Silva tries her best to unpack them all in a way that makes sense for us. As an engineering student taking this course as an elective, I would highly recommend, for the small workload and the essays are honestly pretty enjoyable to write. There is also only 3 essays in the whole semester.
This class makes absolutely no sense. I do the readings and they don't make sense, I go to lectures, she doesn't make sense. DO NOT take this course!!! Awful class and prof.
Shes really trying her best and I love her for it

Bad teacher honestly. She forgets that this is clearly a beginner level course, treats all students as though they are all fluent. She has no remorse when it comes to grading. She will pick on you randomly. I would not recommend taking this class if you dont speak spanish already with this teacher. dont take this class if you love yourself pls

Very kind, funny, accessible prof. I took AP Spanish and got a 4 before this and still struggle in this class, it definitely focuses on grammar that I feel can be overlooked in lower level Spanish classes. Lectures are not bad and easy to review, quizzes, compositions, and projects are more difficult. Content is interesting albeit difficult.

She graded way too hard for a beginner-level course. Didn't seem to care much about her students and only worked at her own convenience. Not a prof that I'd recommend if you don't already have knowledge in Spanish.

Lucia is an amazing professor and person, very approachable and caring! For me, the content was pretty easy but the online quizzes and compositions were harder. She gives great feedback though and not too much homework. Would love to take more classes with her!

Since it's a lnaguage class, there are many subtilities to learn and the flow of material seen is really continuous so don't think about craming everything last minute. You have to put the effort but you get out with a good spanish level and wide vocabulary at the end if you actually work for it.

Lucia's an all round decent professor from who you can learn a lot but she has a tendency to be impatient and rude at times with her students, which just made for an uncomfortable atmosphere. Some people really like her, some people don't. I couldn't say she was my favorite but she wasn't the worst either. I'd give her 3.5 if i could.

Lucia is an excellent professor! She is incredibly kind and cares a lot about the success of her students. You will learn a lot in her class and thanks to her intensive class, I can officially claim Spanish as one of the languages I speak. I would take her classes again and again. She makes us interact with others which is great for practice
I was quite surprised by the ranking. I loved Lucia! Show that you care and she will reciprocate <3

As long as you participate, show up to 95% of classes, and show some effort it's a pretty easy A. Lucia is an amazing professor, and I would gladly take another class with her. Tests are definitely easier than the essays.

She is very caring and very passionate about what she is teaching. Señora Chamanadjian is definitely a professor that I would recommend to those who are very willing to learn Spanish. Sure, there were tons of homework but they helped me improve my Spanish in a short amount of time. Great and very kind professor, take her if you can!

Miss Lach was knowlwdgeble yet very set in old ways. She often talked about reflexivity but was the most unflexable prof I have had. She never handed back assignments on time, and on several occasions lost students assigments. Some students lost marks on assignments for not following her path of knowing. THere was no room for forward thinking.
great but very tough compared to other social work classes
Beyond helpfull and very invested in her student's success.

Lucy is organzied, responsive to students, helpful, thorough, experienced and passionate about the subject area, her research and teaching. She is one of the very few profs who took a genuine interest in the students and modified her material to suit a wide variety of needs. She's tough but helps students learn how to achieve excellence!
Lucy is passionate, organized, knowlegeable, helpful and very encouraging.  She's the only prof I really learned from last year!!!!
This prof really has a zest for what she does. Her passion, professionalism and the course content made me love this course.
No Comments
very helpful.
off the wall weird

This class was approached with real interest and each topic was given ample time. Going to lecture was an engaging conversation each week and much more helpful than the textbook (which is self-written and confusing). He was very approachable before/after class and a super friendly guy. This was an easy A if you like linguistics.

Luis is very nice, but not the best professor. His lectures are good, he answers questions and re-explains when needed, but he sometimes goes on tangents that are hard to follow. Don't rely on the textbook like he tells you, it's so hard to read. Attend class, stay engaged, and you'll be fine. (he also has a tendency to cancel office hours)

LING260 is definitely not an easy course, however, Luis was amazing. His textbook is confusing, I think it's unfinished, but he teaches the material well in class. Quizzes and assignments are very doable with the help of the textbook. He is also super helpful during office hours. The final was super fair, and he answers questions generously :)

Fantastic prof – really engaging, energetic, and funny, making the class feel welcoming. He loves participation and genuinely wants to hear every student's take. The explanations were very thorough and clear, leaving no room for misunderstanding. And he makes sure everyone understands, often using walk-through exercises.

very sweet and caring. can be confusing tho, I've lost track of what he was saying SO MANY times. also has a strong accent so it makes it even harder to understand what he's saying (on top of the confusing material). but very accessible outside of class and always happy to help and go over the  same question a thousand times if you don't understand

i was optimistic this class would be fun but my dreams were crushed. he taught out of the nonsensical textbook that he wrote so it was impossible to study outside of lecture. in a very bizarre move he banned us from taking notes and then got mad when anyone asked a question. everyone who knows me knows the trauma i sustained from this experience.

His lectures, textbook and quizzes are all very inconsistent. He wrote his own textbook that is full of typos and confusing. It's hard to understand what it's going on. Very few resources available to interact with the materials. Gets mad at students that don't understand his confusing material. Overall hard!

He's very dynamic and wants you to understand the content, but at the same time can trail off and it's very easy to lose complete understanding of what he's trying to teach. His book which was the reading for this class is equally as hard to follow and not finished, which pierces through the writing... But very sweet and accommodating.

LING260, while interesting, was not what I expected. The concepts are difficult to understand, even if u attend class/listen to lectures. Shouldn't be a 200-lvl class, and you should not take it without prior knowledge of linguistics. Prof is kind and accessible, but does not explain concepts well at all and can be annoyed if you don't understand.

A prof that explains simple concepts in a way that is extremely difficult to understand, but if you read his handouts that's basically all you need to pass the class so you don't even need to attend. If you're a LING student this course would definitely be a bird course for you (as it was for me).
So much info on the slides and very unclear what info should be known and what info is unnecessary
Dr. Whyte knows his stuff and shares max of it. Encourages in-class discussion. Uses science and logic. Easy-going. It really felt like he enjoys his job. Would love more courses lectured by him!

At first I disliked his teaching style I thought he was too intense. As the term went on, my opinion improved as I realized his energy was meant to try to help us understand the content. His final was challenging (choose-all-correct-answers multiple choice) but fair. He seems to be pleasant and the type who wants students to succeed.

Prof Whyte is a good prof but gives students way too much info. His exam was difficult because of how much information you have to learn and memorize. Overall, you are provided with all the information you need and if you study WELL you will do well. Not an easy A but definitely not the worst prof.

Super knowledgeable on the topic, some might find that he speaks too fast, but I think he only speaks fast when he's reading information on the slide. Very humorous, some people did not appreciate the humour for some reason. No textbook required, all course information can be googled. Professor is available outside class in person and by email. 3

Taught the second part of this course; reads off slides, does not offer any other information. Interesting topics and field trip to water plant which was fun. Very pro-science and not interested in hearing any other opinions. No textbook, all info in slides. Would never take again!
No Comments
The most outstanding lecturer, full of wisdom, friendly, caring, and charming.

Such a kind and caring Professor. There is a lot of reading but she also does great and diverse in-class activities. All graded assignments were group assignments. Attendance is mandatory because she asks for reflections after class. Grading criteria are not always clear.

Parts is a fantastic prof who knows what she is talking about, leads great class discussions. The class was graded on three very short papers, which had pretty clear outlines as well as a discussion on MyCourses. If you don't do the readings, you will think this class is very boring but they are really great readings and short! Participate!

All my classes with Professor Parts have been incredible. She leads class discussions in such a thoughtful and meaningful way, allowing you to engage with the text on a really deep level. Always do your reading, as otherwise you just won't get as much out of it! She rewards interest and improvement, and is always available in office hours.
she is so awesome...just discuss war and peace for 1.5h....what more could you want. she is articulate, kind, and incredibly understanding.

I've taken several courses from Professor Parts and I think she's a fair grader, has a lot of passion for the subject/ also love her coldness and dry wit. Best course of hers would 100% be the supernatural and absurd in russian lit.

No idea why people are giving bad reviews, Prof. Parts is great! We read War and Peace for the whole semester so reading was very manageable. Yes she does not usually have slides and classes are mostly discussion, but she directs it in a productive way; I learned a lot. Creative assignments were fun; love her dry sense of humor. I had a great time!

She is lovely! There are a lot of readings but they are very enjoyable and the class discussions were wonderful. Beyond that, not much work. She is passionate about the subject but engages with student ideas. She can be snappy if you don't seem to have read or aren't paying attention, but she is very kind. You have a lot of freedom with essays.
Very passionate professor. Totally changed my perspective on Russian Short Stories and Anton Chekhov. Super knowledgeable and loved the conversation style classes.

The professor is very competent and engages with interesting and thought-provoking ideas throughout the course. She can be a little hard to understand because she is sometimes quiet. She also asks us to do a LOT of readings and requires us to buy a lot of different books.

Professor Parts is a great professor for Russian Literature. She is very well-versed in the subject matter and gives incredible in-depth lectures that analyze the text in nuanced ways. She is a tough grader, only gives marks above 90% if you come up with a revolutionary interpretation she has not seen before. However, she will reward improvement.

The course itself is very reading heavy. If you do not do the readings and go to every lecture, you will not do well. Prof Parts veers the conversation to one interpretation and is very blunt when she doesn't like yours. My advice is really try to get into the TA Alex's discussion group, his slides were engaging and made content digestible!

Such a sweet man; he was passionate about the course content. His lectures were nice, just very note-taking dense, beware if that's not for you. He'll answer your questions if you email or talk to him after class. He isn't the most tech-savvy, but he was very accommodating with Zooms and recording lectures during metro strikes.
A genuinely interesting and interested professor. He is incredibly knowledgeable and his course is a wonderful intro to the how, what, and why of policy in the world of environmental planning.
When one writes a 200 word response and gets all checkmarks and a smiley face and then gets a 2/4, should they be okay with that?

He is nice and caring, always willing to answer questions and help outside of class. While the content was interesting, his tone made the lectures hard to focus on and boring. I had a hard time listening because the lectures were not very engaging. Plus, the whole course is graded only on exams (2 midterms 1 final) which was stressful.

Took this class for my first semester and I HIGHLY recommend. It was my favorite class and the one I did the best in because it was really easy to go to lectures as they were interesting and clear. He has a bit of a tendency to repeat himself or go on tangents but they are genuinely interesting and the exams were pretty straightforward.

Overall hard class. I didn't expect it because it was "common sense" until you go into your midterms and realize you must listen to everything he says. Lectures are very boring because once again it is common sense but with so many extra complex ideas that go into it. The exams are pretty tricky make sure to study!

he clearly cares and is a smart guy, but is getting old and it shows. i would fall asleep in class sometimes. exams are mostly essay based, a few multiple choice and then like 5 short answer questions on the midterms. also whole grade was based on 2 midterms and the final
Get ready to read a lot, get extreamly bad grades (SUPER TOUGH GRADER) and just sleep during classes
Great prof but he really needs to stop yapping during the middle of a mid-term... that was extremely frustrating. Also that M/C was brutal.
He just talks so much about the same thing over and over. 1.5h for 3 slides is insane. My brain just stops listening after 15 min.

NOT RECOMMEND!!!!!! We spent tons of time on the group project, and got SUPER LOW GRADE. I got A- because I study hard for in-person exams. They care about human right, care about every human in this world but their students.

One of the best Profs I've ever had! He is so passionate about what he teaches, so real, so knowledgable, it doesn't even feel like a class but like a TedTalk. As an undergrad, I was initially scared to take the class because it's a 500-level course, but it turns out to be not challenging AT ALL. I genuinely encourage everyone to take that class.

This class changed my life. Dr. Pai is such an inspirational speaker and he brought in guest speakers who brought the same intensity. This class covered much of global health topics and I feel I left this class a better and more well informed person then when I came in.
Madhu is the most caring, inclusive, and knowledgeable professor I've had at McGill. It's been an honour to be in his class.

He's very nice and he wants everyone to do well. He tended to explain and write theorem definitions before doing examples which often left me to play catch up during the lectures. He writes A LOT of words and the definitions are wordy and confusing. Difficult lectures if you haven't taken calc. Final was very hard

Very good explanation in class and he's easy-going, go ask as more as questions after class, he will answer all of them patiently. 
He made me not hate math.
he's a nice professor who wants you to succeed. he takes time to explain concepts if you don't get it and records his lectures but sometimes he overestimates how much his students already know

Amazing teacher! Magid truly cared about the success of all his students and was very open to questions in class to make sure everyone understood the material. Just follow his approach and what he suggests doing (extra problems and exercises from the textbook), and you'll do great.

Best professor!!! Class was still challenging even having already taken calc before, but do all of the suggested questions and you can get an A (final is harder than the midterm though). Office hours are definitely a great resource he is always super helpful and approachable, and genuinely wants everyone to do well in the class.

Magid was an amazing prof. He was kind, caring, and always wants the best for his students. He can definitely teach. However answering questions is not his strong suit as sometimes he will gaslight you into thinking he answered your question. Overall he was fair, funny, respectful, and very good at doing his job. Thanks!

Worst class ever, and the prof barely taught the class in the lectures. He would use the chalkboard and, unfortunately, had illegible handwriting, so in a 400+ lecture hall, it made it incredibly difficult to follow. Definitely knows what he's doing, but not good.

Amazing lectures. Engaging style and manages to explain complex concepts in a way that is systematic and easy to follow. Very clear about what to study for midterm, provides many resources outside of class for students who are struggling. Really cares about his students.
was a very difficult class. would talk very fast and went through concepts very fast. writing is very messy and did not write big enough so make sure you get a seat in the front.

Awesome teacher! Even though this course was very challenging, he made the class enjoyable.

Reminder: If you take this class, don't fall behind! Review your notes every day… or you might not get a very good grade (been there, done that 😅)
exam questions are tough ,set beyond the scope of the curriculum and not covered in the lectures. material conflict between diffrent professors for the course
His questions this year weren't too hard. They required some thinking but it was very intuitive. Extremely helpful and sends long detailed emails in reply to your questions!

Really friendly and helpful. Read his lecture notes that he posts on WebCT- they're super helpful. His final exam questions are killer though and are by far the most difficult on the exam. Know all the little details!

Prof. Abisaab is very kind and is clearly passionate about what he teaches. However, he does have some organisation problems (his slides and use of my courses) and not very tech savvy. I would take him again tho because he was very funny and cared about his students.

I took history 240 in my first semester of university, and can honestly say that what i learned in this class has stayed with me. Although Abisaab will ask leading questions with only answers he could know he is very kind outside of lectures and incredibly knowledgeable. The readings for this course are interesting and definitely necessary

The only problem I had with this course is that he isn't very well organised. The lectures don't have slides, so it is sometimes a bit hard to follow and it demands a lot of focus. But once you do focus, you can see that prof. Abisaab is very intelligent and passionate about his subject. The course averages to 100/200 pages of readings per week tho

Great professor! It was a rough start because I could not understand his answers to our questions, but as the course continued, we better understood his requirements. Be prepared to read 30-40 page in-depth readings weekly and remember details (25% of the grade is participation, doesn't accept waffling, only details). He appreciates those who care!

Professor Abisaab was one of the most kind and caring Profs I have had at McGill. The class was always engaging and I really enjoyed the reading selection he chose for the course. I recommend taking one of his courses or specifically this course.
In the begininng I thought he may be very strict, but honestly a great prof who posesses a lot of knowledge. Also  was kind enough to give me extensions due to personal issues.

Prof.Abisaab is a great human being and you'll surely enjoy his classes. However he can seem tough and his lectures (him reading a text) are quite hard to keep up with. Fairly easy to get a good grade with quizzes and confs. He's also extremely unclear and unreliable on what he wants from us in essays/papers - hopefully a good TA makes it clear.

Professor Abi Saab makes it clear that he does not care about his students. I was on the brink of an A- (0.5% away), which would have determined me to get into my dream masters program, and he shooed me away when I asked if I could do anything. I got rejected. He likes those who already know the history. Never again.

contradictory, meandering, quasi-deaf. obviously very intelligent but somewhat lacking in terms of translating that intelligence to those around him. very caring, lovely human being on a personal level who's available to help but my god the term paper was utterly infuriating and impossible to follow what he wanted us to do

Great choice for PoliSci and History students. his conferences are dynamic and interesting while his lectures leave much to be desired, he doesnt use powerpoints, instead a word document with the subjects of the lecture written on it. Talla gets straight to the point. He skips the unnecessary filler and spends most of the time going over what will ACTUALLY be on exams. He is super chill which gives anxiety to some--just trust that he is working for YOU.

This professor 100% ruined operations management for me. He has no idea how to explain even the most basic concepts, shows up late to classes, and his exams make no sense at all (multiple choice math based questions where longer questions count for more with no part marks???)
Professor is super fast in writing the Java code. He explains the program logic while writing a program. A lot of class exercise. Overall, a great learning experience.

Don't take MGCR 331 with this professor for your own sake. He doesn't teach, he just plays a video made by ANOTHER PROFESSOR which explains the lecture. That's it. I didn't really learn anything from him; I had to self-teach myself the entire course. Yes, he's a nice and respectable guy, but his "teaching" isn't acceptable.

Prof. Talla writes programs in class. You practice writing of the same programs without looking at them. You will start enjoying the program writing part. You should also do the quizzes that prepare on program logic of program written by some one else. It's a good practice, but needs a lot of effort. Good luck if you take this course.

The GOAT. At first glance, he may not seem like the best teacher. This is a common misbelief amongst bad students who skip and complain. When you really start to attend every lecture with your full attention, you see a mentor instead of a professor. He's the light we need during a time where modern education can be so alienating and discouraging.

Talla didn't care about teaching the course and was not trying to hide it. Obviously improvising in his lectures, and cancelling multiple classes, he described teaching as a "hobby". Expectations for the midterm and final exams were clear but not for MCQs. Little to no engagement in class, despite his frequent requests for questions.

The learning curve is too steep under his teaching style. I self-taught this class by reading the textbooks. I didn't like the quizzes, which were mostly giving you a bunch of codes and asking for output. You can type them in the IDE and run, I don't see the benefits of doing that, but students seemed to be fans because it was brain-dead.
He is the G.O.A.T.

Mr. Talla cares about students. After explaining, he asks questions back to make sure of concepts. He works out programming exercises in real time spontaneously. He also explains different coding styles, data structures and memory like stack, heap and static memory etc. which are not in the PPTs. Very informative. He is an experienced programmer.

Tough grader. Three 1 page responses worth 5% each were eviscerated. What would have been easy marks in any other class were lost here.
Puts too much emphasis on peer evaluations for essays.
Lots of readings each week. Prepare to discuss.
Essays were graded brutally. Definitely not a GPA booster.

Favorite class last semester - his lectures could be clearer but he explains concepts very well outside of class so definitely go to office hours! The textbook is helpful for practice problems and concept explanations but not strictly necessary as all info is available on the slides. Make sure you know how to apply the concepts.

He is clearly way too advanced to be teaching this course and his explanations of course content are very lacking and require you to do a lot of learning on your own.He also makes a lot of mistakes in his lecture slides. Midterms were pretty hard but the final was fair. Not terrible, but he still needs to learns how to teach an undergraduate class.

He is a very intelligent person but this course is too introductory for him to be teaching. The class slides are disorganized, confusing and often incorrect. From his attitude towards students he clearly does not want to be teaching, which is completely fair but makes this course hell.

Loved this class! Lectures could be a bit clearer but he's available outside of class for questions and will answer those well. Grading scheme is very fair and as long as you pay attention in class and make sure you understand the concepts you should do well.
Test content is slightly harder than weekly quiz content so be aware of that!
Very clear explanations. His questions on the final were nice and easy.

He was so arrogant and smug. If professors like Phil Gold can be so humble and respecting of students, why can't someone like Marcel Behr do the same? He certainly is not at Phil Gold's level of esteem. His class is find, I'd just avoid talking to the guy on a one-to-one basis
Very interesting and charismatic lecturer.
Exam questions were really easy and he himself is a great lecturer

He is very difficult to understand when he speaks. I would spend a lot of time during lectures to decipher what he would write on the board/what he is saying. He also does not seem to care for his students that much, I missed a week of classes due to illness and asked for the notes and he refused to share them to me.
I liked him. He focuses on the topics that you will be tested on. It might be hard to understand him sometimes but overall a very positive experience.
I think he is a great prof. You can see that he enjoys teaching this class and his lectures were much clearer than in the recorded section.

Honestly this course will humble you. I have never had a class this hard in my life, midterm was incomprehensible just pure bs for 4 questions i felt like I was here to prove his thesis. Mumbles during lectures, his handwriting felt like i had taken Egyptian hieroglyphs decipher 101, i'm in awe. The other prof is worse, goodluck
speechless

I like him and it would be fun to research with him. Very engaging lectures and motivates definitions well. The proofs weren't always clear though. I also found the earlier evaluations super hard (even for the honours/graduate level), but grading was kind. Final exam was fair and final project was a free 100, so my opinion softened near the end.

The lectures were fast and he covered quite a few difficult topics but it was all worth it for the final. I was also watching videos from the other section and we covered much more exam-related material, which was super helpful.
he was chill but sometimes the way he explains stuff is confusing, not bad tho.

I found his lectures difficult to follow because of a lack of explanation. A lot of the in class time was spent on proofs that did not come up on the final exam. About halfway through the semester his lectures became a lot more understandable. Tricky class overall, prof sabok does do a decent job at preparing you for the final.

I have never been so unbelievably astounded at a persons inability to explain and teach. He was extremely unorganized in his lecture structure, and could not convey any of the material clearly. He was rude to people that would ask questions in class, and spent the majority of the lecture time going through proofs that were not needed on the exams.

Said to be one of the hardest classes in the English department, but I loved it and would absolutely take it again if I could. She's an amazing lecturer which is good because attendance although not mandatory outside of conference is crucial if you want to get a decent grade. Hard grader but she really pushes you to do your best!

this prof will take everything out of you. mandatory attendance, graded (relevant) participation, SO MUCH READING, tough essays. somehow she makes it worth it. i would build her a shrine and name my firstborn child after her

Prof. Kilgour is great at lecturing and made the heavy reading load so worth it. She is very considerate of her students, and her grading criteria and instructions were clear. Keeping up with the readings is essential to pass this course, and attending the lecture, though not mandatory, is necessary if you want to do well in the exams.

One of the best professors at McGill. She is very intelligent and approachable and frames her lectures in an interesting way...I always looked forward to coming to class! As long as you keep up with the readings (which are very dense) and take detailed notes in lecture, you will do fine: her tests are very fair. You will learn so much!

i loved learning about Milton but the prof made it SO hard to enjoy coming to class. if you miss class, she makes you memorize 20 (+) lines and is very strict and weird on attendance, like a highscool teacher. She's a nice woman but made my semester very hard. i appreciate her passion, but would have appreciated some compassion from her. :/

This class is very demanding but it will make you smarter!! The midterm and term paper were really tough, but prof. Kilgour is always happy to discuss your work with you in office hours. This may be the most difficult undergrad ENGL course at McGill, but I sincerely came out of it a better student. No regrets about taking this course :)

Taking this class with prof Kilgour is a rite of passage for any English major at McGill. She's extremely knowledgeable and gives great lectures. However, the readings are numerous and often very dense. She's strict about class averages as well, so if you want a good mark you need to go above and beyond.  Go to lecture!

ENG202 with maggie was the hardest class i've ever taken at mcgill (physics included) but i would do it again. she is incredibly intelligent and verbose; you shouldn't miss a word of her lectures. grading is very rough, this is a high commitment class. VERY heavy reading. no attendance in class, but yes in conference. very tough exams.
Passionate and engaging, Maggie makes class interesting! I got humbled by the grading and suffered through the amount of readings, but I would take her class again without hesitation.

Highly recommend avoiding if possible. I took her for ENGL 202, which is not formatted as a intro course and it has encouraged me to drop the major that I was once very passionate about. Extremely hard marking and the exams are insanely focused on the smallest details of hard texts.

honestly cannot recommend this teacher, get ready to get recked with the APA, she will ALWAYS find ways to deduct points on APA or any other criteria. the whole class could have been a workshop, you spend more time working on the formatting of your paper than on your ideas.
Her's was the clearest, best presented part of this class. From having had to discuss with her on other issues, very helpful indeed.

Dr. Purden is an excellent instructor for this course. She is knowledgeable, kind and most importantly, APPROACHABLE. Provides constructive criticism and helpful suggestions. She has a passion for research that is inspiring. Course pack contains helpful articles, but readings are not mandatory.
No Comments
Professor Kalacska is really kind and approachable. But this course is not easy for those who don't familiar with physics, especially the first two sections. Going to lectures and labs are essential.
Knows her stuff and is an alright lecturer but doesn't seem to put the effort in to be accessible to students outside of the bare minimum.

for one, she never answers her emails when you ask her a question. if you have questions, make sure to flag her down in class! the final project requires you to use remote sensing and analyze an area of your choice, but she doesn't teach the class well, so creating a whole project that you need to present and understand is very, very difficult.

Prof. Kalacska is extremely kind and approachable, she wants to help you! Her lectures are not super-engaging, as she seems shy; however, the content is very interesting and useful. Labs require lots of work, but the TA is usually helpful. I don't know why people say that she's not reachable outside of class - she responded on all my emails!

Prof. Kalacska is completely unaccessible outside class (and did not show up to a few lectures as well). The lab grading is confusing and the workload is insane considering lack of actual learning. If you are an independent learner who thrives with quantitative work - it will be meh, but if you are anything else - do not take this class!

Genuinely one of the worst profs I've had at mcgill. The entire course is taught by the TA. This prof is completely absent, doesn't respond to emails, doesn't show up for all the lectures. You can tell she doesn't want to be teaching this course. Doesn't provide any information about projects and tests you on things she hasn't covered in class
feeling like a very unsupervised class right now :/

Absolutely incomprehensible. Provides no materials or slides with which to study. Lectures are rare, too fast, and entirely uninformative. Labs are mandated with very little guidance, as TA seems just as confused as students and overall frustrated. Do not take this course if at all possible. A shame, as it seems it could be interesting, if taught.

Great prof, clearly an amazing remote sensing scientist. The class was interesting, but the grading scheme was very strange. 4-5 Assignments that are fairly challenging, but a midterm that took months to get feedback on, and while I thought I did well I nearly failed until the curve gave me a B+. The final project was interesting, but tough.

Without a science background was difficult at first but time I learned remote sensing can be fun and very applicable to my major. The labs took longer than expected and were harder than most other classes.

Prof. Deslauriers explains every reading so clearly that you don't even need to do the readings, just skim over them to find quotes for the final. Her lectures are the only ones I bothered going to last semester. Might not be the easiest elective but you will enjoy the class so much you won't really think of it as work.

I took this class as an elective and ended up with an A at the end of the semester without having done all of the readings nor attended every lecture. It's honestly interesting, she is not a boring lecturer. I recommend reading every text she gives and do a little 'fiche' about it so you're not too surpassed for the final (which is pretty easy).

She is iconic. Engaging and funny, she is a great way to start a philosophy career. Readings can be dense, but her lectures dissected them and made content feel manageable. The weighting was tough. I didn't do well in the assignment (40% of grade), which tanked my overall grade, despite doing well on my final. Love her, not the structure.

MY SHAYLA. She's a legend. Your grade basically depends on the final and an assignment, and her lecture style is not for everybody, but she has a great sense of humor and is incredibly passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. The readings will change your life. Go to her office hours and chat! She's very approachable.
Tough grader, make sure to go to office hours for feedback. It's tough to know exactly what she is looking for.
Love her. Iconic class. Amazing woman. I love her.

the materials are very interesting. It's a pity though that the professor can't explore them in depth. The texts are really difficult, but she doesn't spend enough time on each, which means they are only explained in a general way.

She is a great professor and the content was fascinating. I strongly recommend this course and professor but definitely not a bird course - you will have to read quite a bit and the assignments are graded relatively harshly. But the interesting content makes studying fun :)

Take this life-changing class with Prof. Deslauriers if you want to rigorously analyze your philosophical and feminist convictions. Expect tough readings, but the engaging lectures and Unstuck AI make studying more manageable. Endure the harsh grading - it's worth the effort!

Professor Deslauriers is exceptional. Her lectures are well organized with outlines, and she always stops to make sure the class understands and uses real-world examples to clarify. The PHIL 242 material was interesting and varied. Grading was SO HARSH however so make sure to get TA feedback.

Incompetent teacher with no consideration for her students, takes days and weeks to respond to her emails even though she is responsible for the program, often respond with condescending tone. However, very easy to pass her class because no subject is taught.
Overall, the course was pretty easy. You were obliged to come to class and the lectures weren't recorded but if you did all the homework and read the slides, it was an easy A.

she just wants you to agree with her. if you say something that she doesnt like or agree with, end of convo. her students just regurgitate the same stuff that she says and are not actually thinking for themselves and making their own critical opinions about the content.

Wouldn't recommend this class/professor. Lectures were super boring she just read off a paper. The reading load was absurdand grading was unclear. Prof Hwang is an incredibly smart and kind instructor. I had her for GSFS 200, and in this class it felt as though the lectures dragged and lost direction, often becoming incredibly mundane. Overall a solid prof who I would recommend, but not the most engaging lecturer.

In a world where critical thinking is rapidly disappearing, Prof. Hwang widely encourages it. I have never met a prof so dedicated to her students and her craft. Very flexible, and willing to work with you on just about anything.

I feel so lucky to have had Professor Hwang. She works tirelessly to encourage students, takes no breaks, and is always available. She gives fantastic lectures and is a fair grader. GSFS 305 -- being a critical race theory class -- is incredibly difficult to teach, and yet she always made the class feel safe and special!! Amazing prof & researcher

Prof. Hwang was one of the best teachers i had at McGill. As an engaging lecturer, she conveys the complexities and paradoxes of social issues with a profound humanity. Amazing teacher, if you want to truly master Russian this is your girl

Maria Vladimirovna is an awesome prof, she really wants everyone to do well. Maria Ivanova was one of my favourite professors at McGill. Her class isn't easy, but she goes above and beyond to make it fun and make sure you succeed--and she's a very generous grader. Prepare to work hard, but it's a 100% worth it

The RUSS department is a hidden gem at McGill and Maria contributes a lot to that. Excellent professor. Homework assigned after every class, but always to the benefit of your language skills and never anything outrageous. Recommended 100%.

I loved her so much. A great professor! Gave clear explanations and cares about each student. Good teacher and a nice person.

prof is caring, clearly passionate, EU simulation and film reviews were enjoyable, but slow grading (missing Jan grades), low midterm averages, lots of readings (easily 100p/w). Professor Popova's class was one of the best 200 level Poli classes I took. She is truly inspiring and the midterm and final was fairly easy if you did the readings and lowkey just memorized the slides.

Professor Popova is a great teacher, but POLI210 isn't her thing, you can feel it. She does her best to relate the content to her research, providing concrete examples. Maria Mascaro was by far the best teacher ive had at Mcgill. I took both hisp218 and 219 with her and learnt so much!! the course was definitely content heavy - which is to be expected for intensives- but she is a very generous grader and if you put in the work you will do well.

Maite is a great language teacher. Her lectures are engaging and she tells lots of funny stories. terrible lecturer. doesnt explain anything in depth and jumps all over the place during lectures and is impossible to understand.

take every class taught by her, very interesting personality but free 40% and 2 openbook quizzes.

I learned great deal from this course, the Prof is super listening and really intrusting.I have never been so engaged or learned so much from a course.

Fun, flexible grading, great Professor, organized class, structured myCourses, exposure to real consulting was appreciated,
highly practical, professor MJ is literally the best prof i've ever met.

MJ is an excellent teacher. In all her classes I find myself leaving with new knowledge that is highly applicable to the real–world.

very very kind and caring prof. who made university feel approachable for my first semester. lots of homework though- easy, but sometimes tedious if left to the last minute. overall a generous grader who really wants her students to succeed and understands that none of us were perfect. would 100% recommend
Super sweet and caring professor, helped me get through my first semester.

Terrible, i wish i could say dont take him but he teaches mandatory classes. Worst teacher in the department.
heavy french accent, learn which protozoa in which group n of course the diseases n cycles

Not sure why people hate him so much, he's a good and engaging lecturer. Not amazing vibes as a person and his exams were brutal, but I would take him again tbh. A lot of (boring) readings to do, which you are quizzed on every week. Classes are discussions with peers.

Martin Robillard, a.k.a. St. Martin, stands out for his idiosyncratic grading system. A beautifully crafted enigma that managed to simultaneously frustrate students and himself. Years have passed, yet the trauma of his exams and textbooks lingers like a bad WiFi connection—always present, always annoying.

It's a self-study kind of course, but do ask for help from the prof if need be. I couldn't go to lectures, just kept up with the readings and made detailed notes. Key is to do it often and little by little. Textbook, exercises and assessments are really good, only critique is that the book is too focused on 1 context, understandably so.

Everyone says bad things but I found the course good. Textbook was free, with free additional exercises and solutions. Lectures were unusual, but if you did the readings they were a great way to apply what you learned in coding context. If you kept up to date the exercises online and read the book, getting an A wasn't unreasonable at all.

You have to read his entire textbook and its not really written like a textbook. There is barely any clear step-by-step for how to do things, only long paragraphs with snippets of code. We had 4 lab tests that were pretty easy. Average on the midterm was like 55 and like 50 for the final. He didnt answer questions on ed ever.

I think the class isn't terrible. The lectures aren't that bad, I did follow them though I stopped going to them at one point. Would be great if he recorded them or shared his code he writes in class.

His exams have terrible averages. I cried when I saw my midterm mark. I had been so confident! His final sucked because he added a JavaFX question.

If you take this course right after 206/250 or haven't done a lot of personal projects it will be very tough. Exams are all open-code pencil and paper. The barrier is being able to write Java code by hand (and a lot of it). If you can approach a mid-size project on your own / spent reasonable time outside school coding, the course is fine.

HEED my warning: Approach the exercises as a courter, tenderly and wholeheartedly, until they resonate with your essence. Delve into the book of knowledge, for its pages hold the key to your survival; Neglect it, and the shadows of failure will claim you (Read the textbook and grind the GitHub exercises if you wanna pass the course with this prof).

"Ultraviolet (UV) LD is typically employed in the analysis of biological molecules, especially large, flexible, long molecules that prove difficult to structurally determine by such methods as NMR and X-ray diffraction." -Wikipedia   This is actually very relevant, thanks Dr. Schmeing.

Great instructor and good sense of humour. Tests are very fair and he makes his expectations clear...Latin is just a difficult language to learn! The constant quizzes and tests were super helpful to stay on top of the material and made the final a lot more manageable. Go to class and you will be fine. Love Professor Sirois!

The expectations are challenging enough that you have to put in the work and actually learn, but still consistent/fair so it doesn't feel like he's out to get you or anything. I did bad but I had poor attendance, go to class consistently and you'll be fine. His passion for the material really shows, and he has a good sense of humour!

Super cool guy who obviously cares about his students. Quizzes almost every class, which were annoying but good review, did okay with about a half hour of studying for each one. All of the quizzes and tests are fair, as you know what to expect on them. The final was tough but graded pretty kindly. Awesome teacher overall.
Really great prof but the workload is alot. The quizzes are overwhelming sometimes but I think they were a great way to get students constantly reviewing the language for tests and the final.

I thought he was a great professor, explained everything clearly, gave appropriate homework, etc etc. Everyone LOVES to get mad about the pop quizzes, but they really do motivate you to study and you'll do better because of them. He was really funny and cared about his students success, I genuinely don't think I could have asked for a better prof.

Prof. Sirois was the first prof I had at McGill, and I went on to have him for both beginners latin classes as well as intermediate 2. While his classes are work-heavy and intensive, he is also funny and remarkably caring. I highly recommend him to anyone who wants to genuinely improve in Latin and who is willing/able to work hard for it.

Expect a quiz 2/3 classes/week. Each quiz is worth 2%, so do good on them. Although there is a lot of material, the prof made it very digestible. If you're disciplined enough, you should be fine. Although this was the most enjoyable course I have taken at McGill so far, if you're not mildly interested in the material, I would suggest not taking it.

Mr. Sirois is a tough but a fair grader. The exams are definitely difficult but the quizzes prepare you well for it. It is important to show up to class because you have to do 15 quizzes and you do not know when he will hand them out. Overall, great teacher and funny man.

When it came down to grading the quizzes, he is VERY strict. Even when you answered the question and what you said was true, he'll will not be satisfied. And it's weird when the reading responses are very open and can have multiple answers, but the answers for the quizzes has to be EXACTLY what he wants or else you lose marks.

Prof. Sirois is easily one of the best professors Ive ever had. Quizzes are frequent and often come without warning, but this helps to make sure you understand the material and gives you incentive to actually do extra exercises. So long as you do the work the exams and quizzes are easy. He is kind and jokes around, making classes very fun.

He certainly gives the impression that he cares about his students and our success, not only in understanding the content; with clear lectures and requests for feedback, but also in the grading scheme. The weight shift from the final to the midterm was very kind. I really enjoyed this class!

Honestly one of the best professors in the CS department. Grading scheme is very generous and there are a lot of resources to do well on his exams. He's a hilarious guy and on top of that he really cares about his students. He took 2 hours from his weekend to record and post a review lecture before our second midterm. G.O.A.T
very kind and fair, i can tell he genuinely cares for his students and wants us to succeed.

Very caring, responsive professor, fair exam. Homework is meant for helping you practice the materials. Easy grading scheme, designed for you to succeed. Put some effort and can succeed, because that is what he designed for you to do. Nothing bad to say about this course, everything designed perfectly.

Great prof. Clearly giving the materials need to study for test and exams. Assignment were interesting and enjoyed the MIPS. Almost missing all the lectures but still got an A because of the clear lecture recordings watched before the tests. (maybe i am a bit biased on the material? idk, but still very great prof, clear, transparent, ...)

I will never let anyone hate on prof Mathieu. He's always super transparent about how everything is graded and what material we need to focus on. His grading scheme is absolutely goated and I don't see how anyone (who studies) could get below A- in this class. It might even be too good so I think he might change it loll

Amazing and very caring!!!

I (stupidly) forgot to write the MCQ answers on the scantron section, but I had the answers circled on the booklet part, though. I failed the exam because the scantron wasn't graded, but I emailed Mathieu about the situation, and he was caring and empathetic. He deducted 10% (Valid), and I passed the class!

GOAT!!!!!!!!

Incredibly detailed slides; at times overwhelming but lots to say about the material. Amazing prof, so kind and generous with his time. He will spend hours with you in his office making sure you understand. COMP273 is a hard course but if you study, you are certainly rewarded without a doubt.

He was a little bit disorganized (understandable, it's his first time teaching this course), but still managed to relay the info. I think he prepared us very well for the midterms and the assignments were clear. His grading scheme is very forgiving and he's a super understanding prof! Def recommend him if you need to take this course.

He really loves what he teaches, he even manually compiled C code into machine code. The assignments have pretty clear steps and his grading scheme can shift the entire weight of the final onto the class tests, or the other way around. Great teacher.
Had him for 200 and 331. Amazing lecturer and fair exams! One of the best profs for EE. Attendance is mandatory because he doesn't post notes

He is clearly a very knowledgeable person and keeps the class engaged. I just did not see why he was treated like a deity by most students and found him overhyped. He is very loud and somewhat obnoxious at times. He also often goes off on tangents for extended periods. That said, I am definitely in the minority on this opinion, so yk.

In my opinion, he is very overrated. The course material is very easy. He has weekly tests that are graded harshly, and he also has a "lab test" worth 10% of the grade. This test can be very easy to mess up in, and 1 mistake means you get 50%, and two mistakes mean 0%. This is a class you can get a bad grade in even if you studied well.

Funny entertaining guy with great charisma. Weekly quizzes are easy as long as you spend 1-2 hours preparing for them. Labs are easy as well. Gave a 4 star instead of 5 because: 1) He doesn't post any slides so showing up is indirectly manditory. 2) He posts the quiz practice material 2 days before the quiz (not a big deal though).

Good lectures, prof has a very good sense of humor and remembers each of us well. Easy weekly quizzes for each week starting the second until the end of the semester. Final was a bit harder but overall fair game. Labs are mostly easy with the exception of the lab exam

funny guy and good teacher, lectures are engaging. weekly quizzes help to stay on top of things and are pretty easy. final was a little harder than the quizzes but still easy, and labs are basically free marks
Funny guy, engaging lectures, provides enough practice material. Weekly quizzes kept me in check enough that i didnt have to study much for the final.
Overrated. Teach course well, but quizzes are exceptionally tough.
Great lecture. Easy course overall. Maybe too easy.

the goat
got 100% in my final
quizzes are there for you to practice
no worries if you don't do well in them

She is not the nicest professor. She has a great understanding of marketing, but fails to translate it to the next level. She grades very tough and is very picky. I don't think she intentionally does this but she definitely finds things to dock you for. Personally I would not take this professor again.

Creates a positive, welcoming class environment. Cracks jokes in lectures. Kind, approachable. Wonderful woman. I loved her, will seek out another class with her.

Hack: You don't need the textbook much but she loved when I would cite it in projects. I didn't read it, I would just command F for something I was going to talk about anyways.

Amazing professor. we had 2 midterms during the term and the MCQs were very specific. She's not very demanding on the long answer parts, I always got full marks for them. However, I noticed that she graded a bit more severely group project.

Professor Dellar is my favorite professor at McGill! She is earnest, knowledgeable, and pleasant to be around. She is the only professor I have ever felt completely comfortable with when raising a concern about a course. She is discerning, provides excellent feedback, and works with her students to help them succeed, although effort is required.

Took Brand Management with her and absolutely loved the material but loved her delivery of the material even more. A real gem of a prof who truly cares about her students. If you have the opportunity to take a class with her, do it.

Mary is amazing. Always uplifted my mood and had a smile on her face. Class itself was great and the group project throughout the semester was so fun. But emphasis on MARY. She's amazing. Take a class with her if you can for sure

They call her Stellar Dellar for a reason. It was a real PRIVILEGE to learn from someone as passionate and smart as her. Had her for 3 courses and wish she was able to teach me more! Anyone who has the opportunity to take one of her classes should be honored.

I had Prof Dellar for two classes this past semester. She was awesome and made classes interesting. I would definitely take her classes again. The only flaw was that it seemed that she was only willing to give out 75-79% on the written work (talked to others in the class who assumed the same). I got a B+ in both classes. Otherwise, she was amazing!
Had Dellar for 2 courses in my degree. (I LOVED services!) Among my favorite profs who gave me a lot of direction on career. One of the classes that has some practical value at Desautels.

I would not recommend this professor. The amount of work assigned is insane. There is a case (oral and 12 page report), individual assignment, two quizzes (the prof has the most useless and specific questions, and she does not teach anything in class), final group project (oral, 20 page report) and class participation.

I wish the lectures were recorded- would've made things so much easier cuz she gives a lot of info during the lectures which made it difficult for me to study. She's super sweet and knowledgeable but grades kinda harshly (at least in my opinion) it's my first art history class and I won't be taking anymore simply cuz it's not my passion.

I thought Dr. Hunter was extremely fair with assignments and an engaging lecturer. Her passion for French art is contagious and I left the class with knowledge I constantly apply now, both at museums and outside. If you follow her criteria, the assignments are not too hard and can be fun if you pick an interesting topic for the final paper.
Super engaging lectures and is very sweet during her office hours. I would take any and all of her classes!
LOVE this prof. So engaging and helpful. Great course as well. Take the time to get to know her personally and ask good questions

This was my first art history class and I'm glad that it was with her.  She made me love the subject and I'm actually minoring in art history now! She was really helpful during her office hours. If you have questions or any problems go and talk with her! She is really helpful and understanding.
She is amazing
Professor Hunter is great! I would definitely take a class with her again. Her lectures are clear and interesting. If you attend class and do the readings, then you'll do fine.

Overall, she's a great professor. Her lectures are clear and thought-provoking, presenting Realist and Impressionist works in a way which focused at times more on her own, medical-related research and the issues therein. Professor Hunter is also approachable and respectful, and communicates with her students promptly if anything comes up.

Very clear lecture, but she tends to divert questions/requests to the TAs. Not really sure what she looks for in exam essays and essays but if you regurgitate the lecture notes and readings you'll do fine. Short essay (5 pages) for the class makes it rather nonchalant.
She is an AWESOME prof. Her lectures are very clear and interesting. I wish she would teach more courses!

She is an awful teacher and is always unsure about herself and the content she is presents during her lectures, which is very unsettling. Cleary just here to do research and does not care about the undergrad courses she teaches at all.
Honestly a pretty hard class and not the best course if you don't care about hydrology but at least she cares enough to make an exam where you can get enough points to pass the class.
horrible

Prof. Blais is very caring about his students and is always available outside class to answer questions. A quiz each week, and a lot of time to do it and a MyEconLab final.

Oh boy, I self-taught myself to an A in this class He posts pre-recorded videos every week, with weekly quiz and a final on MyEconLab. Lectures were just him reading off the slide, its like watching a Youtube video rather than being in a McGill class.

Was disappointed by this course. The professor just had asynchronous lecture recordings where he read off the slides and then the rest of the course was entirely my econlab, even the final. I felt like we covered so many topics that I wasn't able to get a strong understanding of most of them. He does not seem very passionate about teaching.

Literally the worst professor I've had at mcgill. complete disregard for the fact that we're literally in the middle of a pandemic, still had mandatory attendance to lectures. barely does any teaching , just expects you to show up once a week and answer extremely specific questions about data/ results from readings. doesn't actually teach anything

Literally reads the PowerPoint. The textbook, although not mandatory, taught me more than his lectures. Monotonous professor who seems bored himself by the subject. Makes statistics even more dull (if thats even possible).
Unclear most of the time. She just reads from the slides and does not provide any extra insight. Do yourself a favour and stick with the chemistry department for any materials science course.
She's an ok prof, but teaching and grading style is not good - definitely not suitable for everyone. The guest lectures were interesting, however.

Grading was based on a team project which was not clear at all. She did not provide feedback on the project, and there was no discussion after presenting. Unfortunately, we didn't get grading details. Overall, communication was not satisfactory during the course.

Emailed us 2 days before our projects were due saying she had turned the course into a pass/fail grading system. Made everyones motivations drop. The last day of classes once everyone finished presenting, She changed her mind and said she will turn the course back into a marking system and we should expect a grade. Sabotaged all of our grades.

Dr. Tabrizian is an interesting character. Her material is very useful if you consider studying/working in biomaterials. However, she is not always clear, reads from slides and be quite stubborn with her policy. However, she is very sweet if you take the time to see her after class with questions or concerns. Pushes you to do well, but tough.

When I looked back the moment now, she was working so hard for stubborn and arrogant students. Dear Students,I wish you to have an amazing moment with her. I wish everything is well with profound learning helper, Dr. Tabrizian as well.

Even though I understand Professor is busy, and McGill is a research intensive school, she just read slides. Professor Tabrizian did her best in her first lecture only to help students learn(before the course add and delete deadline). For more objective options, I recommend asking students' response(at least 34people who have taken this before).
Is not very clear about what she expects in terms of project and presentation.  Very very hard marker. Class is boring since lectures are on power point and all she does is read the slides

Lots of practice that is representative of the exams and you will do good if you put in the effort. Sometimes it was unclear if we actually needed to know the content he was sharing or if it was just for fun which made studying a bit difficult. Often asks really specific examples so your best bet is memorizing everything you've seen!
Org God. Clearly explains everything. Tells jokes sometimes. Fair exams that are a bit challenging, but you'll get decent marks with some effort.
Organic god, smart and funny. Made me love org

This class is hard. I definitely struggled to learn the reactions and mechanisms, but Dr. Damha is so fun to listen to that I didn't really mind. Memorize the practice problems and the quizzes!! Before my exam I studied so hard I was doing reaction mechanisms in my sleep. I did feel like I was going crazy but I did well on the test so...

Exams fair (0 suprises); a grade of A required high/constant effort. For future CHEM 302 students if you have him you are super lucky. Make sure to study your slides from the lectures as this will be the main information covered on the exam (I handwrote my notes) and do the practice questions that are given because they also appear on exams.

Make sure to perform well from the start; he doesn't really give you a chance to redeem yourself if you screw up. Fully understand his slides, try his suggested questions from lectures, and do his problem sets twice over. Though, the final required slight critical thinking...

Professor Damha is everything a professor should be; his lectures were clear, concise, interesting, and well organized. I loved CHEM 302 and wish he taught more classes (I would sign up for another Damha class in a heartbeat).

He is a really respected prof. Good handwriting and his exam are not hard and the material is easy to understand. Pay attention to the slides and know the material, you will be fine with his content. Do the practice questions
Just knowing literally every detail of the lecture notes is all you need to do well on a Dahma exam

Damha  clearly enjoys teaching and the content that he presents. He's a nice guy who likes to make his lectures fun and sneaks in the odd joke and funny comment. Notes are pretty clear cut and fairly easy to understand with a bit of application. The only problem I had was that his practice questions didn't seem representative of the actual final

1) lectures are sometimes hard to follow, sometimes a symphony, depend on day.

3) assignments are representative of final (although tough). If understand all of them you should be fine. 
Motivates material well. Tells good stories and makes good jokes.
symphony of math, motivates course well, sometimes lost in sauce.
Absolute genius

No lecture slides and he doesn't follow the lecture notes schedule. He usually writes on an online whiteboard or scrolls through handwritten notes which are hard to read. I would recommend reading the textbook, doing all the questions you can, and taking the time to understand assignments. Exams are fair, he drops the worst question on the final.
Lectures are difficult to follow. Assignments are long. Course is overall very reliant on the textbook. You can succeed with him, but expect to put in a lot of work. At least his grading is generous.

Honestly, I didn't find the lectures helpful and had to rely on the textbook to get through the course. The assignments are super long, so be ready for that. You can get an A, but not from the lectures—more from the textbook and maybe office hours if you go.

Unfortunately he sidetracks a lot during his lectures and his personal notes can be hard to follow, so just use the textbook to study. But he's really sweet and wants the class to do well. Average was a B+, so not necessarily an easy grader, but if you really deep the textbook you'll do well

Very interested in the material he teaches and it shows in his lectures. He often provides examples of real world applications of the material and is very interested in developing the critical thinking skills of his students. Keep up with textbook readings and attend lectures. Assignments can be long but are not hard. Exams are fair.

super kind in office hours and genuinely loves his subject. lectures were alright, just a bit hard to follow a long derivation of some result, and his handwriting can be hard to read. the textbook is a must. do every single textbook question (even the ones marked with asterisks as hard) and you'll be well-prepared for the exams.
He's nice, but he goes on tangents and doesn't explain very clearly. The course material could be presented better, it seems like his teaching ability has declined a bit in recent years

I found his lectures to be boring, he spent the whole class explaining basic concepts, which did not help with the much more difficult homework questions. He does allow crib sheets, but the in-class practice wasn't at all useful. He under-explains the biological concepts in this class, and over-explains basic computer science and math.
Great Prof, explains hard concepts very clearly. The exams were also fair.

Great teacher. Material is just challenging enough to be interesting, but is very clear and starts from the basics so every subject he discusses (no matter the complexity) is accessible for students. Tests were very fair, and assignments were interesting and just hard enough.
Great Prof, Great Lecture, clear instructions, interesting assignment.
Wish he taught more of comp 204. He is very clear and direct and I feel like I understood 110% of everything he explained. Super nice as well

Very clear notes and lectures. He makes it easy to stay engage with the material. Exams are open book and if you pay attention in class the difficulty isn't too bad. Assignments were a bit time consuming but incredibly interesting. I honestly really enjoyed the course and his teaching style, which I was not expecting for a 400 level comp class.

I took this class as an elective and loved it! He is really good at teaching the basics without giving too much info or overly complicating things. This class did have a lot of quizzes and assignments, as well as a midterm and a final, but grading was fair, and assignments are a real grade booster if you put the time in! Take this class if you can!

I thought I wasn't going to like this class but it ended up being my favourite class this semester. Mathieu is so patient and caring and often stayed after class to answer extra questions. The assignments can be challenging but they are also fun and really help with understanding the material! If you're a newbie, this class is perfect.

He is so good at dumbing down the basics of programming for complete beginners. The class was also very well structured. The best thing about him is how much he cares to make his class as good as possible, which was especially noticeable during the transition to online classes. Great guy, and great prof, at least at the beginner level

Great lecturer who made introductory compsci super interesting and easy to understand. Assignments were fun and really helped gain familiarity with the material. Prof. Blanchette was accessible outside class for clarifications and help. Would recommend taking this course with him if you can.

He is a knowledgeable professor with various experiences in both research and industry. His interactive lecture is quite helpful to improve the understanding on the fundamentals of the material science, however, his expectation is extremely high. If you want to challenge yourself to improve your understanding, take his course, but tough to get GPA.
Hard, but you pass

The class itself is very interesting. If only you were tested on what you learned in class. States that we should be able to figure out  things from concepts learned in class, but truthfully forget about it. It is almost as if he will not say important things in class just to have you "figure it out" on the exam. AVOID IF YOU WANT A GOOD GPA!!

A good teacher, although he sometimes moves very quickly and fails to emphasize topics he finds important or any details involving tests/assignments. He is easy to understand and his tests are usually challenging but always fair. I recommend mime 560, interesting class!

This prof is just a genius.Its a problem just as much as its a good thing.He expects too much of u and the workload for his course is as much as 2courses.very demanding and another problem: yes he has interesting lectures but then in the exam he smacks you with the hardest most unclear twists you will start wondering if you are an idiot.Good luck!
This guy does not know how to teach at all.  Why is he at McGill?  He is a real menace: It is time to force him into anger management rehab, urgently.

He knows the stuff VERY WELL. And he teaches VERY WELL. He answer questions CLEARLY. Tries to link with actual industry situation, which is very helpful. Tries to make us "thinking" engineers and be creative. BUT, he is very demanding. Extremly tricky exam. Getting an A is extremly hard. Take him if you wanna learn. Dont, if you want easy garde.

Great Teacher. The class was interesting. The material was a little tricky at times, but he explains it very well. Knows ALOT about the material, and loves it. Going in to talk to him is very informative.

Not a bad guy, but he really cannot teach. It follows that it cannot make up an exam either. Ambiguous question after the other...its a pain! He's really knowledgeable though.. He's worked in the industry and has a learned quite a bit there seemingly. Avoid him as a teacher if you can though...

Not the greatest teacher, but definitely among the better ones I've had.  I'd say in terms of easiness, he's fair - if you follow the notes, read the text, it's pretty easy; the opposite is also true.  His notes could be a little clearer (detailed), but other than that, he's OK.

I took her research method class (I think she gives many different INTD397) and it was the most practical course I have taken so far. There are practical group assignments every week and some of them are a lot of work but she talks a lot about the reality of field research so it was a good class.

I took her course on human development and really enjoyed the way she shares her experiences of the field. There are case studies every week and participation points are given based on short group assignments. It helped connecting theory and development practice.

Simply put, it's not worth your time. Grades harshly for lack of detail and I later understood that basically you need to copy and paste all of her lecture notes to get high grades. Although the course material might sound interesting, it is very obvious and logical and I didn't learn anything really useful

The main problem is that she grades very harshly. She does not provide a lot of information about the assignments and does not provide a lot of feedback after either. She restricts the papers to very few pages, which seems ideal and easy, but then gives really bad grades because it is not detailed enough. AVOID if she does not have a T.A.

I was in her M&E course in Fall 2019. She is caring and wants her students to learn and focuses on the practically of things. There were a lot of group projects, the midterm was fairly easy as she pretty much gave the questions in advance. 1 thing: she is somehow a 'tough grader' bc she doesn't believe in (the importance of) 'grades'. Good overall
lectures were all on slides so attendance wasn't mandatory, group projects were marked really easily so i'd say i got a super easy/good grade for not attending much

This is her first year teaching at McGill, and I can see that she definitely wants her students to do well. The course is not easy but she is very patient and helpful during office hours. Several practicums can prepare you for the final assignment. Would like to take another course with her!
Not engaging lecturer, and some lecture material isn't very well explained. Grading scheme is not very forgiving (50% midterm and 50% final).

Honestly, Prof. Roy's Perception class is awesome. He makes the material super interesting and easy to follow, even when it gets a bit technical. His lectures are actually fun, and the examples stick with you. The exams are fair, and he is super approachable.

Prof. Roy's Perception course is hands down one of the best classes I've taken at McGill. He explains complex concepts with clarity, and passion, making every lecture genuinely engaging. The material is super interesting. He is also incredibly fair and transparent when it comes to grading.

In all honesty, i loved psyc212 with Prof.Roy. He is clearly passionate about what he teaches, which makes his content-heavy lectures enjoyable. He is one of the sweetest teachers ive had at Mcgill and he  really cares about the success of his students. His exams can be challenging but he is a fair grader and will curve accordingly.
If you care abt ur GPA, literally run. seems like a nice guy but bad bad bad class. makes zero sense. my gpa is high and i struggled like crazy. be sure to avoid at all costs.

At first, I had trouble understanding the course and its material. As I went along the semester, I began appreciating his sense of humour and teaching style. He's a really nice guy and does his best to explain the material in a digestible way. You can tell he knows his stuff too.

Don't understand why people say Roy fails to explain clearly. I found he made a concerted effort to slowly walk us through conceptually tricky material + often takes time to reword/reexplain. Some questions can be hard but he curves grades if necessary, very fair. Passionate and brings in the coolest guest lecturers. Really loved him/this class.

Roy is very sweet and funny! Warning- his explanations can be confusing but the TA review sessions are very helpful. These review sessions were recorded and revealed what will actually be tested. His evaluation methods are standard for psyc courses (50% midterm 50% final) however I wish he added weekly quizzes to lower the weight/stress of exams.

overall pretty chill prof. he's defo not the greatest, but also defo not the worst! can be funny and guest lectures were really cool. his exams aren't great per se, but they're fine. average class, if you have to take for psyc, and he's absolutely not the worst prof to have it with

I never went to class and I don't like psych but anytime I was there he had so many silly little jokes and I regretted not going more. Would recommend if you care about ganglion cells. Overall nice guy, but I hate that he's blond.

Matissa is a very sweet person, but it feels her teaching was quite lacking. Her lectures were painfully boring, difficult to stay focused on and far too theoretical. There was far less discussion than I expected, and her group project was incredibly disorganized and the guidelines were confusing and messy.
Very accessible and passionate professor who gives very clear guidelines. Enjoyed all the classes I took with her

Matissa is an amazing professor! She cares deeply about seeing her students succeed. Although sometimes her grading can appear "tough", she takes the time to give everyone extensive details on what could be done better next time. She is also super smart, so take in as much as you can learn from her. Can't recommend taking her enough!!!
