Great professor, caring, demanding but very flexible and listens to students needs. 3h class block/week with small assignments every week + 5 quizzes, so weekly/bi weekly evaluations. Be ready to study consistently the whole semester. Live negotiations each class. Very unfamiliar class format compared to other classes at Desautels, I loved it.

Matissa's course is very interesting, but beware of grading; if you're taking this for an easy A don't! The assignments are not very difficult and you have the option to complete them with a partner, so take the course with a friend you trust because you'll both get the same grade. Overall, the course is quite a bit of work but very cool!

Super impressed. Matissa is incredibly knowledgeable and her exams were very fair but always really tested understanding (can't just memorize, really have to listen and try to comprehend concepts). Great feedback and one of the smartest profs I've been taught by at McGill - would recommend if you're willing to put in quite a bit of work
very much supportive and helpful, always gives extra info and help, super knowledgeable and willing to share
Her classes are interesting, but she doesn't give a mark above B+ (so basically her classes will drop your gpa).

Very nice prof. She cares about her students and helps you do well. In-class assignments are open book. Gives you clear steps on how to write good papers while allowing flexibility. Would take her again!

Really great professor that cares about what she's teaching and cares about her students. The material she teaches is fascinating and the assignments are assigned strategically to put theory into practise. She's awesome !

Dr. Bezabeh was a great lecturer who was engaging and enthusiastic when teaching the course. If you practice solving all the group assignment questions, and attend classes, you will be able to do well on the midterms and final exam. The exams were very fair and representative of what was taught in class and practiced on assignments.

I worked so hard in this course - but it was worth it. lots of homework. lectures were just plain fun. covered the material (quickly) then focused on quirks that are hard to understand. doing the reading in advance is essential

Wow. If I could have all my courses with Prof Dobbs, I would. Entertaining lectures, clear explanations of concepts, and he clearly enjoys what he does. Treat yourself with this class if he's teaching it, it's worth waking up at 6AM and commuting and then some.
My favorite class at mcgill. ever.

best way to wake up in the morning - astronomy story time with Prof. D! 
And super willing to go the extra mile - wrote a letter for me for VISA issues. Thanks Dr. D!

Fun and engaging. The standard model is hard work. He was able to step back and make me appreciate the big picture when I was lost in the equations. My field is not particle physics, but I walked away with a great interest in it.
My favorite course at mcgill, hands down.

so good! I chose this course thinking it'd be easy science credit. Had to attend class to understand the material, but I loved it! walked away energized after every lecture. (and fell behind if I skipped a class because he won't record lectures)
He has unstoppable passion for astronomy and it is contagious! He also loves to receive questions from students. Taking this course was an excellent decision, a great elective!
Take his class if you want to think critically. Great professor who is passionate about his field.

Terrible. So difficult to stay awake in class when Prof Dobbs is lecturing. Grading for the group project was extremely harsh, and 3 hour in person final for level 100 physics is ridiculous. Avoid this class, so many better electives to choose from.

I am trying to take him again because he was such an amazing professor. Caring, passionate, and focused on engaging students. The material can be at times boring, but it was rare. There's a lot of in class discussion, and be prepared for long readings every week, but you get a lot of free points and the midterm and final are take home!

Wonderful prof, the class discussions are always so fulfilling. I took this class as an elective but it might be the only one I looked forward to attending every week. Fair grader, you need to do your work and show up to class but if you have interest in Renaissance literature and philosophy its a must take!!

Prof. Soranzo's a nice guy, but not the best pedagogue. His Dante class often feels like a history class (as opposed to a lit class), and at its worst moments, he seems to reduce Dante to a series of footnotes. Sure, you will be knowledgeable about The Divine Comedy by the end of his class, but I question if any of that knowledge has much value.
Super sweet guy and very chill class! When we discuss poems he is very open to all points of view and never makes anyone feel stupid

Powerpoints arent very useful. Best thing is to take notes of whatever he says. You must like literature, if not, be ready to work a lot to make up for it. Lots of reading, show to class and youll make it. If not you will miss 10% of free marks and lots of information. Course content is not light, be prepare to put effort for it. Funny accent
Prof. Soranzo is an amazing teacher and person!

Italian Renaissance will remain a fave  in terms of content. You will end this class with a breadth of knowledge on the period that you will be grateful for. Art, philosophy, politics.. Petrarch, Boccaccio, Castiglione, Machiavelli, you will get to know them all. You need to dedicate lots of time and it is entirely worth it. Prof. Soranzo is a gem!

This class was one of my favourites at McGill. We discussed the materials in depth and it was actually fun! The marking scheme consisted of 10% Participation, 40% Take home midterm, and 50% Take home final. He is a great prof because he loves new ideas and is open to debates. He is also so knowledgeable and passionate about the subject!
He's a nice guy, but VERY hard and critical marker. Readings are very long, and the assignments are quite hard with not enough time to do them when you get towards the end of the semester.
Professor Sorranzo amazing. He is so passionate about the subject, you can't help to be passionate about it to. He is very helpful and fair. I highly recomend all his classes :)
Easy class, exams are expected. super helpful in office hours, just don't fall behind, and it's a really easy class

Matthew is a very knowledgeable professional of his field, but does not synthesize. He glances over material without going into explanations, using Excel files that all mix up with one another as they all look the same. Overall, this teacher can work for some, but not all. He does have good stories though.

This was by far the most disappointing professor I've had. The exams were unreasonably hard and didn't reflect what was covered in class. It felt like we were set up to struggle. I would highly recommend avoiding this professor if you want a fair learning experience.
Absolute worst professor ever. Zero practice problems given. Super difficult exams. AVOID HIM AT ALL COST!!!
Worst professor ever. Incredibly unorganized, makes mistakes on his exams. NEVER TAKE HIM.
Will not respond to emails and is not very helpful even during office hours. Although the grading criteria is clear, he teaches the content very poorly.
Very hard assignments with little to no help. Takes ages to respond to emails. He also didn't take half of the classes this semester and posted 'recorded lectures'

Really smart and really passionate about accounting. So refreshing to have clear slides and lecture recordings available. Office hours easy to book and helpful. He doesn't try to trick you on exams and you'll know the format and types of questions ahead of time
Very smart prof with good lectures and fair exams
Super clear and easy to follow his lectures. He teaches very complicated subjects in such a simple and clear manner.
easy class and a good teacher. I should have gotten an A but I sold
Very good professor, would take him again. Explains well and walks around to help people if we do individual work. Assignment grading is fair and the rubrics are given in advance.

Great prof who cares about the students and wants everyone to succeed. Professor Goodman makes the material (excel, javascript, etc.) easy and digestible for students who pay attention in class. Glad to have taken MCGR-331
The best teacher I've had at McGill! If you follow his work, you'll get a good grade. Everything is explained very clearly, and if you still don't understand, he takes the time to explain it to you.

Great prof, goes through the course very slowly which was helpful as most of the content was really new. I really liked how he went through examples in class and did exercises. Just wish he the solutions to the practice exercises he gave were more detailed but other than that super nice prof. Final was a tad bit difficult but not bad if you studied

I've had very few profs @ McGill provide such detailed rubrics. Efficient and fair grader gave plenty of in-class time to work on group projects. Very chill class with interesting content and fair assessments. A great choice for an elective

Matt was a great prof for INSY 341. It consisted of a few assignments and quizzes with a midterm and final project. He made sure that his lectures were easy to follow along and gave students time to practice coding on they're own with his help. The final project did take quite long but he was always accessible if ever students had any questions!

He's good! Though there's lots of readings, he always discusses them in class and ties them to the concepts and theories covered, which helps grasp the content. Each of the 3 exams is 1/3 of your grade and the bigger portion of each exam are "short" answer questions, so you do need to study well beforehand.

Prof. Lange invited class participation in every lecture, which led to engaging discussions and prompted us to consider a topic from many perspectives. Connected concepts and theorists' views together in a meaningful way that deepened understanding. Course is organized and well-structured. Would definitely take again.

Prof Lange is a great prof. Although his lectures can be a bit dry and sparse with info, it is still an interesting class. Study a lot for the exams as there are only 3 and each are worth 1/3 of your grade. As long as you do the readings and study, an easy grade is definitely achievable.

Discussion-based classes, participation is required but worth it. Prof. Lange is knowledgeable and inspirational. Classes are well organized and you learn and develop a lot. Prof. Lange is easy to talk to yet professional and invites and encourages participation in a respectful way.

SOCI 210 was a great intro class for sociology, I learned a lot and the readings were very interesting! Professor Lange is a very organized and effective lecturer, but make sure to come to class well-rested and ready to pay attention. The exams weren't too bad, but make sure to study for both the multiple choice and free response sections.

Professor makes lectures interesting - he manages to really engage and make what is already an interesting subject material even more so.

He has lots of information on the slides which is helpful for note-taking.

Professor Lange has a bit of a monotonous tone when he speaks (he also admitted this lol) so it can be hard to tell sometimes, but he is actually a sweet, funny, and caring person who is passionate about what he teaches. He is also very wholesome! I enjoyed the discussion I had in his class. He grades fairly as well.

Prof is definitely smart but lectures are monotonous and just reads paragraphs off of PowerPoint. Potentially interesting material rendered boring. Grading was harsh, midterm and final tested random minute details from readings and lectures that are impossible to study. Overall not worth the headache.

I'm surprised this prof's reviews are average at best  I found his exams to be incredibly easy. Lectures are boring since he basically reads off the slides  but it makes missing class not so much of a big deal. I did really poorly on the paper but did so well on the exam that I didn't even care, and its a very fair study-reward kind of class.

Really nice professor who led a great seminar class. Facilitated discussion well and gave assignments that he graded fairly with tons of feedback that made improving much better. He is a bit more serious than some other profs but still really knows his stuff and is very caring and kind (though it won't slap you in the face like w/ other profs)
I found that her classes were very structured--the material was presented with clarity and very systematically which made classes a little boring but was very helpful for writing papers/studying.

Mean, just really harsh and unhelpful. She's obviously very intelligent, and knows her stuff, but she's intolerant of differing viewpoints. Lectures are a little boring and the assessments are pretty hard.

She really knows her stuff and will tell it like it is! She speaks really fast which can make it hard to follow, but I learned a lot from this class! It's too bad that she has a mean streak, she'll call out kids in class for no reason. Take her class, but watch the lectures at home so you can pause them frequently.

Lectures tended to be boring, also completely changed the guidelines for the final paper two days before it was due, citing "computer error" which certainly would not be an acceptable excuse for handing papers in late

Brilliant. Race and inequality in Latin America is where she really shines - she knows her stuff, but lets students figure it out on their own. Very readings heavy but always interesting - willing to include material she doesn't agree with. Very picky about style + hard grader, but always willing to help you outside of class. I recommend this class

Spoke too fast during lectures, often repeated herself, made note taking difficult.Slides are so vague that they are not helpful at all, so you have to go to class. Does not know Africa well. Take-home midterm long (9pgs over the weekend). Final reasonable, but certain topics were confusing. Only take this class if you really enjoy studying Africa.

This is a boring teacher, she is only reading her notes for 3 hours.  In addition, she's very agressive with her own students!  Don't expect to be able to ask her questions for the exam or other work, she will answer with a very closed mind and there is no argumentation possible.

This prof needs to learn how to teach. She just stands at the front reading off her notes all class. She doesn't repeat anything and gets mad if you ask her to slow down. Sometimes she'll cover a whole country in the last 2 minutes of class, this is not a good way to learn. I was very dissapointed. She clearly doesn't care about students.

She was fairly interesting to listen to, though by the end of class one tended to doze. The thing that really irritated my was the arbitrary and unreasonable page limits for the take-home mid term.  But as one of maybe 2 classes on Africa at McGill, it is pretty good.

This professor is unclear in class, uninformed about the topic, unwilling to hear ideas that are not her own.  She dogmatically holds to her preferences (like Harvard-style referencing) as if they're shared by any other political scientist.  Her classes are a waste of time, as is her enormous coursepack that no one reads, since it's all irrelavent.

My absolute favorite professor I have had at McGill. His classes will challenge you, but nothing extreme. The content is interesting, if you like 313 I highly recommend taking 314 with him as well. It is a more in depth version, smaller class size, and more independent projects.

The course was graded by 2 midterms, 1 test, and 2 papers, all of which we were given ample resources to succeed. Chemin delivers lectures well and keeps the class engaged, although lectures were not recorded and assignment descriptions were not always super clear. However, office hours and TA resources were extremely helpful.
That final exam was messed up

The lectures were amazing and inspiring. Clear explanations of the material. Extra points were given at second assignment for grade catching up. The grading was strict but try to attend classes as much as you can, you will be just fine. Definitely would take again.
Super engaging lectures with weekly quizzes. Group projects are graded very easily.

This class was nothing more than neoliberal indoctrination. In terms of grading, he is completely unreasonable. Half the grade was based on group projects where the work is only as good as the weakest member. The other half was 30-minute "quizzes" (really, they were tests) with anywhere from 8-10 dense questions. Avoid Chemin.

Had the most engaging lectures, gave real information from his research projects of Economic Development in Africa, and quizzes were not that hard. Also, bad grades on the quizzes are compensated for my super high group project grades. take this class!

Very coherent syllabus and lecture format. Engaging and very nice, making lectures a pleasure to watch. Obviously enjoys interaction with students and would love to be back in class, which shows (even on zoom) as a good 'vibe' that I appreciated. Good grade as long as you follow class regularly and study for quizzes.

very descriptive - super clear about what he is talking about . weekly quizzes can be hard at times, but balanced with easier quizzes. lots of group projects - which can be annoying but also really boost your grade. you learn a lot about economics, and he is a really good prof for teaching economics to those who hate math.

tbh im surprised at the comments - Econ is an absolute nightmare to me but Chemin made it bearable and even enjoyable! He was very patient, encouraged students to come see him, and tried to explain the material as detailed as possible. I WISH I could take him for 314 :(
created very clear expectations and followed the guidelines she had set for us completely, very easy to talk to as an accommodating professor

Her section of CHEM110 had the most new content to grasp and it is a lot to memorize for the final. She had the most fun lectures out of the 3 profs that taught this course, but she also spent some time talking about non-course material, while the other profs basically only talked about relevant course material during lecture.

Her lectures are engaging and interesting, and she brings in guest speakers and lab experiments that keep things fun and lively. She covers a lot of material but it's manageable if you practice. She's generally just really sweet and tries to be helpful wherever she can be. Great way to end the class :)

She's an amazing professor! Her lectures were extremely interesting and engaging, with all the guest speakers and lab demonstrations. She is super kind and does want you to succeed. Her section was one of the more difficult ones, but she continued to encourage and help us do our best!

Very caring and nice prof, her section is fairly easy if you've done any organic chem before, however it does have a lot of new material and a good amount of memorization. Her lectures are entertaining and she brings in guest speakers and experiments during lectures which is super cool.

Fellow cat-lover who is kind and funny. I had given up watching the videos by the time she was teaching but the content was managable just with slides. Ochem is horrific at first but gets easier. She lets older students perform fun experiments during lectures and even gave a presentation on applying to research positions. She made chem palatable.

McKeague slayed! Made ochem so fun and enjoyable. Every time I had questions she answered them so well. I'm considering rewatching her lecture vids again just so I can see her cats. Def the most entertaining prof that taught 110 this term.

Dude you always get told organic chemistry sucks, and sure it was easy organic chem, but McKeague makes it really fun and her enthusiasm is palpable which just makes things more enjoyable. I thought learning all the new inorganic would be awful too but it really wasn't bad. She gave us lots of example questions to work with. I loved her
She is awesome and actually made me interested in chem, hats off for that.
Prof. McKeague is my favorite professor. She is energetic and hilarious - one of the very few classes that I do not get sleepy.

He is very knowledgeable about the subject and is always willing to answer people's questions (even though he is not a master of tact when giving his answer). I have learned a lot by asking him slightly tangential questions after class. If you get over his introverted nature, you will see that he is a great prof!

He's good at explaining challenging concepts for the most part, and the content is relatively interesting most of the time. BUT, he shows no passion and gives off this vibe that he hates teaching. He's monotonous, and almost seems disappointed if you dare raise your hand to ask a question. His exam questions were tough but not impossible.

Dr. Chacron definitely does not like teaching. His lectures are extremely monotone and boring which is sad since his topics are actually interesting. During class don't even think of asking a question, he will answer it as if it was the stupidest thing he has ever heard. His section is also the only one where the readings are mandatory.
Makes difficult concepts sound really easy and clear. The guy's a genius, amazing explainer, but his questions definitely make you think. Ie, Ie is his favorite word
Very clear lecturer with the least intimidating ppt slides ever. The concepts he teaches are NOT simple though and makes his exam questions fairly tough.
Very clear and easy to follow lectures, but I thought his exam questions were pretty tough.
He provides clear and helpful notes to go along with his lectures and asks straightforward questions on his part of the final.
Good prof, well organized lectures in the 314 section. His questions on the final were really reasonable as well.
Good professor, course is well-structured and you can learn a great deal of IA. Recommend.

An incredible prof that knows his material very well. His final is optional, but please make sure you do well enough on the midterms since the final is quite challenging, and really does not guarantee it will improve your grade.

Great lecturer, but the exams feel unfairly structured. The time limit is very tight relative to the difficulty and length of the questions, including longer written responses. It is challenging to complete everything properly within the given timeframe.

He is definitely the more knowledgeable of the two 206 profs and does a good job relaying the information. That being said, the class does not really teach anything radical and is very similar to previous classes. The homework is probably the best thing to do as far as learning goes; the lectures were not that helpful for me.

I have him for COMP 273, but I can't add a new class. Anyways, he's probably the best computer science teacher I've ever had. He teaches in a way that is very accessible and easy to understand. Exams carry a lot of weight and are not easy, but if you study, you will get a good grade. It's really a class where you get out exactly what you put in.
Homework are badly organized. There are things we haven't learn. Little ppt used.

Hands down the best professor I have taken at mcgill. If you follow the lectures or at least make a reasonnable attempt to do so, you will have a great time with him. The grading scheme is very generous and forgiving. The professor is almost always availble and anwsers the fastest out of every professor I have had. He is very knowledgable too

His lectures are fun to listen to, his assignments are very straightforward, but his exams can get a bit tough. He has a way of explaining things that makes everything he says very engaging, even when discussing the most dull topics.

Also, he plays video games and his background is the master sword.

Prof Max was very attentive to students, answered questions very quickly, asked for feedback on assignments/exams and seemed to genuinely care about the students. I would love to take a class with him again B) (Although two of the assignments took years off my life)
Unorganized assignments. Penalized for TA/prof errors
Clearest lecturer there is honestly. You can't go wrong with Max

Max is certainly an effective, entertaining, and engaging lecturer. I take issue with the tested material—minimal focus on major concepts, midterms asked questions about niche facts, and MCQs were worth 2% of your final grade. Despite generous curving and plenty of available bonus points, an interesting class was made unnecessarily stressful.

He is really responsible, attending every review session and stay until finish to answer student questions. He will tell you what is the key and what can be ignored in class. It is very important to listen carefully! Most questions in the exam have been taught during the class. The relationship between different molecules is important.

The most insensitive, insulting professor who is determined to make students doubt themselves and underperform. There is no other professor I have had in my degree who is remotely similar. Each question multi select, no part marks and worth 2% of your final grade. Every multiple choice option is worded as a trick so be very careful when you read.
Made an interesting class a nightmare. Exams were heavily biased towards minutiae all but skipped over in lectures.

Does not care about his students at all. An interesting course became literally my worst nightmare and grade at McGill. Please avoid at all costs if you can (but you probably can't, as most of us only take this because it is required). Exams are select all that apply and short answer with no part marks - each question is 2% of your TOTAL grade.
Exam format is terrible he makes you doubt everything.

Good lecturer. However, please don't take this class if you can avoid it. Horrible grading scheme. Absolutely unfair questions. Keeps repeating that the class isn't memorization-based, which is honestly a total lie. Still wishing he would curve that ridiculous second midterm.

Max Denis is a mean person. He does not care about the well-being of his students and does not want them to succeed in his class. Mind you, he does not have a lab and only teaches one class a semester, but he will try to fail you. Spends his entire time figuring out how to word questions is a way that will make you question your sanity. Avoid!

I am taking BIOC311 in U3 and he is by far the worst prof I've had at McGill. His lectures are all over the place and he shows very little care for the students' understanding of the material. Whenever I go see him after lectures to ask questions, I leave more confused or he will ask insist that I'm not doing what I can do understand the material.

Horrible professor who's teaching style is terrible terrible terrible. 

I also hated how we tried to convince us that if we're not able to answer his ridiculous metabolism questions we somehow are not meeting the competencies expected of medical doctors...I'm a med student at McGill and they never teach the way he does. He is just terrible.

She does not assign students exercises on the course material. This mixed with the fact the there are very few evaluations makes it that students don't know exactly what to study before very important tests. If you take her, I'd recommend reaching out for exercises because lectures differ a lot from whats being taught when it comes to difficulty.

Lecutre material does not reflect testable content well. Makes concepts seem too easy and then goes far too fast, and leaves everyone quite confused and unable to know where to begin to ask questions.
ECON 347. Chill easy course if you're in econ. Very kind prof. Tests are chill, lectures are interesting.

the professor was clearly passionate about what she teaches but the classes were boring, all she does is read off the powerpoint so you don't even need to go to class. Her explanations can also overly complicate the subjects covered in class. Final was easier than the 2 midterms

LOVE this woman. She is the most caring person I have ever met in my dark and abscessed 21 years of life. Take one of her classes, even if it means getting castrated. Believe me when I say... IT IS WORTH IT. Seriously tho, she's a great teacher, and will go to the ends of the earth to make sure you get the material, and do well in her course.

Econ is not my thing, and I did not do as well as I wanted. But Mayssun is a passionate professer and you can see that in class. She made the class fun, interacted with us, and did not continue until she saw people understanding the information. GET MYLABS, its very helpful and it was the bulk of my studying. TAs were not useful during midterms.
Will not answer any emails and very difficult to reach outside of class time. Will not post your grades in a timely fashion, I'm still waiting for last semester's grades.

Respectfully, I used to find it so tough to stay awake in her class. She's cute and tries her best but she's basically reading off the slides. Good thing the content of the class is easy, otherwise I would've been doomed :) overall, 7/10. Would take again (if its an easy class)

kind and very passionate about the topic, however it was her first time teaching 313 so the lectures seemed a little unorganized. can also be sort of hard to understand. 2 midterms worth 25% and final worth 50%, but they were very reasonable and doable if you prepared. doesn't respond to emails.

Impossible to reach outside of class hours
Slight accent, but manageable
Kinda rambles on
Reasonable exams
Reasonable teaching skills (if you can stay attentive despite the rambling and repeating [and the minor accent])

Personally wouldn't take it again since I had to teach myself most of the material

If your goal is to have an enjoyable experience and a good grade without having to face a lecturer that is not going to repeat the same things with different choice of words and references for an entire semester and expect you to do the same in your answers then don't take this class.
amazing prof, clearly knows what she's talking about inside and out. was receptive to student feedback a really good lecturer who made getting out of bed early in the morning in the winter worth it.

Bradley is absolutely amazing, it was her first time teaching this course but you could have never guessed. While it was very heavy in terms of readings and content, it was extremely insightful and great prep if you are hoping to go to grad school. very clear grading criteria and thus, if you are willing to work you can get certainly get an A

Professor Bradley is one of the best professors in the department. Be warned, she has high expectations and will make you work for it. Getting a good grade is definitely NOT impossible, but you will have to put a lot of effort into it. The good thing is that it is rewarding - POLI 353 was my favourite class at McGill. I learned so much.

A super relevant and interesting class, one of the best in the department. Wish I had taken another class with her (448). Her powerpoint slides are a bit confusing but she is a solid lecturer. Learned a lot in her class. I would recommend this class as well as 355 and 444 with Nuñez-Mietz. The three all together are a triple threat.

Megan Bradley is a really great professor and a gifted lecturer. It was her first year teaching disasters and development, and she made the theory-heavy material accessible and entertaining. Lots of readings though!

She's very irrational, she gives way too many readings. Her readings are long and repetitive, and she expects us to know everything for the exams. She's extremely annoying. She gave us a useless peer-review for participation marks with the possibility of only losing marks, but not gaining points if we do it. Overall, it's better to avoid this prof

Wonderful prof, wonderful lecturer, wonderful course. Prof. Bradley is engaging, kind, and downright brilliant. POLI 353 is by no means easy, but it is doable so long as you read and pay attention in lecture-i.e, she isn't out to trick you. Prof. Bradley's standards are high, but she makes her expectations clear and helps students meet them.

Disaster & Development. This class is pure suffering despite the interesting topic and seemingly nice professor. The lectures only cover surface of the material. The evaluations are based on specific details of readings, which are impossible to keep up with throughout the semester. This class is a marathon, be ready to be out of breathe.

This class was more than misfortune. Both the Prof and the TA are extremely severe graders and show no mercy. Only got a B+ for participation despite attending every single conference and speaking several times in each one. Midterm and final were focused on extremely specific details about readings, rather than understanding of core concepts.

Really caring and accommodating professor! Made the course really interesting; also, the grading scheme was really flexible. Overall, an interesting course and easy to do well in. She wants her students to succeed.

I really enjoyed taking Dr. Clayards class! She's a super kind person and is very helpful. It's clear that she wants her students to succeed. Her lectures were interesting and clear, and her assignments weren't too difficult and actually kind of fun to do. Quizzes and exams were also pretty fair and not too difficult!
I LOVE THIS PROFESSOR! he made engineering so fun, genuinely everyone take his class :)
His feedback is never good nor clear, he gets caught up in details. He is a very harsh grader, and even though the amount of feedback changes, the grade stays more or less the same.
Amazing, clear about what is expected, cares deeply about the students!

Prof. Dagdoug is a rare find in the math department. He rebuilds intuition at the start of each lecture so definitions click instantly. Couldn't attend in person, but his slides, recorded lectures, and assignments cover everything you need. Would 100% take again.
awesome and so caring!!!
He makes material more complicated than it is, explain things in a difficult way. Also a lot of mistakes in his lectures and notes, he doesn't realize it until you point it out

I'm astonished by the good ratings here. Mehmet has a lot of improvement to do as a teacher. His notes are a mess, every single assignment had mistakes, final had mistakes in it, every single example in class had mistakes, what the heck is even happening. His explanations are extremely confusing, and I know this class from my undergrad already!

Doesn't show dedication to students'. Remarked to students that their questions were too "boring"

There were many errors in the teaching slides in-class. Graded assignments did not include complete solutions.

Practice Exam over reading week did not have complete solutions until less than 24h prior to exam.

Unreachable during exam for questions.
Great professor. Accessible and well-prepared for his lectures. He does need to have a higher standard for TA though. Never had I seen any TA make THAT many mistakes.

A little difficult to stay awake in the lecture, but it's very important to pay attention. His tests and assignments are based on his lectures. He offers a good amount of support and practice questions. If you do your due diligence and do those questions, you will at least get an A-.
Great communicator/lecturer. Makes the topic seem easy. Sets clear expectations for the exam. Provides good preparation materials. Can't ask for much more.

At first when you hear him speak, he doesn't seem special.  However when you have him as a teacher, you realize how good he is. He makes the material seem easy. Although he has an accent, he speaks in a clear and crisp manner that makes us all understand.   One of the best professors I've had at McGill.
The best professor at mcgill. Highly recommend you to take him!
Really breaks down material well and explains it very concisely. Solves problems in class in the most detail possible which really helps with the learning.

Amazing professor! Incredibly knowledgeable about the course material, but also has professional experience in the subject area.  Prepared and motivated for every class, very helpful and clear in answering questions and responds to emails immediately! Would definitely recommend this prof!

i took her for another class before & i was disappointed in this one. the instructions for assignments are very clear but there is no grading rubric to follow! the final exam is basically an essay with no notes allowed. take only if you have to...

Dr Ghazanjani is one of the best profs I've had at mcgill— incredibly knowledgeable and lectures are clear, structured, and genuinely engaging. Grading is fair and expectations are transparent. I honestly don't get the complaints here. Loved her class so much I'm already taking another course with her.

She assigned a group essay with a rubric that didn't make sense, then changed it 3 days before it was due only after students pointed out her own confusion. Was extremely rude and snarky during the STM strike (shamed students who couldn't attend) and compared MMIW to her childhood memory of reading a story about a duck.

Do not ever think about taking her. The class is her reading off slides and adding jargon until even she sounds confused (and often is). Heard her admit to a student she used AI, which we all suspect is in her slides and exams. Everything is overcomplicated, lacks context, and you're graded on understanding confused AI writing. Truly disappointing.

She is very sweet, but unfortunately, her lectures are very long and not very engaging. Very heavy lectures with a lot of information, and we barely touch on the readings, which you are expected to mention in papers. She is clearly very knowledgeable, but I unfortunately could not get myself to be interested in her classes.

I took her last semester, and it's an amazing class. She is so passionate about what she teaches and so open to conversations. Sit in front so she can recognize you! Definitely a tough grader but her remarks are pretty useful. Readings are important - youll have to incorporate them in exams
She's very passionate about what she teaches

Super vague project details. The class content was difficult to understand and I ended up teaching myself most of the material. She seemed annoyed when you asked for clarification or questions in class. She said she had a lot on her plate with another full time job and teaching multiple classes, but the student's are the ones who paid for it.

This was for INTD 398, the class content itself was very interesting, but I feel the grading was way too harsh for a 300 level class. The level of analysis she expects out of her students is not what anyone was able to achieve for a timed essay and I don't know anyone who got an A. She is a good lecturer, but quite old school and strict.

The grading criteria were not clear and what she expected on the midterm and final was not clear. She also expects many elements in your answers but will never explicitly ask for them in the question... She had to curve both midterm and the final. Go talk to her and ASK questions in class because else you are cooked.
I use to hate history class until I got this teacher. Everything is very clear and easy to understand. It is still a University class so be ready to study !
Great teacher! My favorite one so far!

Great passion and enthusiasm for teaching, genuinely cares for the students. May be a little young (i.e. inexperienced and slightly unorganized), but it's clear that he recognizes this and will only improve with time. Highly recommended.
Best accounting prof at McGill. Super nice and supper accessible outside of class.
Great prof. She's very caring and explains everything very well in class. We do a lot of exercises in class on excel. Would recommend
best accounting prof.
Tough class but great prof. Super accessible during office hours as well.

Professor Marginson's classes are very structured and clear, she really explains the concepts well. There was no final for this class, only 2 midterms and one final project. She was very caring and wishes her students to do well. If you do all the practice questions and listen well in class, you will do great.

Great professor and nice person. She explains very clearly, but you will still have to do a lot of practice problems to do well. The fairest exams you will ever take, not too easy not too hard without any unexpected surprises and fair grading.
Love Prof Marginson. Always available outside of class. Also she teaches in the CPA so she is really good at giving practical advice. Couldn't recommend more!
Definitely the best accounting prof. Nice and smart. Knows what she is doing. Exam are tough.
Not easy, but doable if you really do the work. What I really liked is how available Melissa is. She has lots of office hours and she is really helpful.

Prof. Marginson is the best accounting teacher at McGill. She makes difficult material easy to understand by simplifying concepts and explaining clearly. Her enthusiasm makes classes engaging. She gives clear feedback, replies quickly, and genuinely cares about her students' success. Highly recommend!

Rarely takes up entire length of lecture, quick and effective with lots of examples to illustrate concepts. Lots of material to prepare for exams. 
Also had her for ENVB222 and loved the class & big project but hard grader on final report.

Very passionate professor that really thinks about how she presents the material to the class in order to be highly accessible to everyone. Makes lectures interactive and enjoyable and provides plenty of practice material to prepare for quizzes and tests. However, writing assignment preparation was a miss for me.

This professor clearly cares about the content being taught in an effective way to each student. The lectures were informative and interactive, making online class much more enjoyable. Frequent assessments followed the lectures. The assignments were unfortunately off the mark. They were not related to the lecture content and were unforgiving.

The worst professor ever. Made us write a quiz on the syllabus, only to change it multiple times throughout the semester. Her lectures were far from engaging, and she made one of the most interesting courses feel like a chore to get through.

By far the best course I've taken at McGill. Yes it is hard and a lot of reading, but it has truly changed how I approach history as a discipline. Dr. Shaw can be intense, but is very kind and caring and wants to help students succeed and is so encouraging of students ideas, often providing methods of research or sources that can be used.

Professor Shaw may come across as strict or harsh initially, but she is one of the most caring and considerate professors I have ever had. Not only that, but the course content was fascinating. Professor Shaw is so smart and her research is groundbreaking. It was a lot of reading, but definitely worth it. I would 100% take again.
RUNNNNNN!!!!!! NEVER TAKE HER CLASSES FOR YOUR MENTALITY!!!

DON'T take this class if English isn't your first language bc you WILL struggle. She reads only from a pre-written text and she reads FAST so it's very hard to keep up. Slides aren't helpful at all. The tests are hard + she takes so long to grade them (grading method? nonexistent) If you value your life don't ask her any question for your own sake.

One of the worst academic experiences I've ever had. Lectures were uninspiring, and the classroom was often tense due to the Prof's unwelcoming attitude. One on one interactions were unhelpful and curt. Grading was inconsistent (though TA grading was quite fair) and sometimes lacked feedback. Her class will leave you feeling poorly about yourself.
Bad class, boring teacher. Do not take as an elective.

Not to toot my own horn but I know US History fairly well. However, it was of no use in this class. The format of the first exam she deemed to be "too easy" when students did moderately well, and so she decided to abandon her syllabus (which she claims is the ends-all document of her class) to add more questions to an already overbearing exam. Ugh.

The lectures were lightning fast, the exams were incredibly difficult, the instructions were very unclear, and the syllabus changed multiple times after add/drop. I learned a lot from the readings, but the lectures were awful. Too difficult for first years, should have a higher course code.

2 weeks into the semester she has take a quiz based on the syllabus to make sure we understood it. There were still things not clear and when we would ask about something, she'd tell us to reread the syllabus rather than reword what she meant. She's incredibly condescending and rude. Please put the Tin Man on sabbatical until she gains a heart.

Vollrath is so highly regarded and I honestly don't understand why. She's mediocre at explaining things, she's so monotonous, and her exam questions are HARD. I had her for phgy 209 and 210, and her questions are consistently difficult. Her slides are really good, though and she's a nice person. But otherwise, I genuinely don't understand the hype.
Despite everyone saying about how good she is, I just don't see it. Always reading of the slides which is unbearable, and makes you fall asleep.Her questions are hit or miss
Her questions are kinda hard but shes a great teacher

Dr. Vollrath taught the GI section. Her slides had little information on them, so definitely go to class and rewatch lectures to understand the content. She is mostly clear in her explanations and her questions on the final were also fair. That being said, her part has a lot of content to know.

Her slides aren't great so make sure you attend lectures or watch the recordings. She tends to be monotone but overall she is a caring teacher, explains the subject well and her exam questions are fair.

Melissa Vollrath is an absolute angel. Her slides are very organized and she makes sure to go over things in great detail. She is always accessible for questions and emails. She wants you to succeed and her questions are never meant to confuse you.

She is awesome!You feel that she wants you to do well vs. someone like Mandl in the course who designs a structure that will likely fail you! 
Vollrath gives clear lectures and her tests resembles the practice questions and her expectations of the course content from you!
This woman is an angel and the content is pretty interesting but man are the slides ugly.

Mellisa is a great prof and a really kind person. She is always there for extra help if you need and her lectures a very clear. Def keep up with the lectures and don't be shy to ask her questions after class!

Hi everyone, USCA here. Those lecture slides are actually from Dr. Ann Wechsler, who was teaching the GIT section of PHGY 210. Dr. Vollrath is just a sub for Dr. Wechsler, so the slides aren't really her fault. Same thing for PHGY 209 immunology section, Dr. Gold was teaching the section and the slides are from Dr. Gold.

I had her for GEOG 272, and i was worried to take a upper 200 geography class, because i've only taken GEOG 216. But she was amazing, very clear and played music during her classes which was a nice addition. Her grading criteria and exam instructions/guidelines are very straightforward and she structures her class so you can succeed.

Omg just take Mette Bendixen. One of the best profs I have had. The lectures are engaging and you can tell she likes and knows her stuff. She gives really good feedback and is really organized and clear.

most amazing prof ive ever had. clearly understands subject matter and cares about students (literally learnt all 200 of our names). very smart lecture structure: goes over previous class, new material, sums up new material. also brings in guest lecturers for specific topics studied. will look for more of her classes that i can take

Lectures are good, slides are amazing. Very helpful after class. The only thing is that since this is an intro class, there's tons of stuff to memorize, so get ready for that. Exams are ok, just make sure to study the terms well.

Very friendly and caring! Clearly loves to teach and interact with students. Lectures are easy to follow and exams are clearly formatted and fair. Go to class bc there are "pop in-class assignments" where you have to come to class to get credit for unannounced in-class assignments, but they're like a participation grade. I recommend the class!

Take the class - I'm writing this halfway through the course but the midterm was easy. HOWEVER, Prof Bendixen is very cold and stern. She seems like she is fed up with her job and is not friendly with students. Awesome TAs though.

LOVE THIS PROFESSOR!! I changed to geog major after taking this course. Amazing lectures, very fair grading schemes, interesting materials, and super caring. She reviews key points of last lecture at the beginning of every lecture, so you have a sense of what's important and what is more likely to be tested on (hint hint wink). TAKE THIS COURSE!
Worest prof with terrible attitudes. Talked to multiple students in the department and we share the same view. Strongly suspect that those positive reviews were written by tillmann himself.

Prof. Blome-Tilman is one of the best philosophy professors I've had. He also has all of the qualities you want in a philosopher: clear, precise, and immensely knowledgeable. He is very quick on his feet and engages sympathetically with opposing perspectives, both from authors who disagree with him and from other students. Just a pleasure.

He's a great lecturer and he clearly makes an effort to make the class as engaging and interactive as possible. In addition, he truly cares about the success and well-being of all his students. He's very available and he will do whatever he can to help you succeed in his class. You honestly couldn't ask for more from a prof.

Took Epistemology and Phil of Lang with him. Both courses are reading intensive so go to lectures! His ability to extract only the relevant information is impressive. Tough grader but gives good feedback. Class can get dry but he is approachable outside of class. Initially a little cold, he's sweet and genuinely cares about his student's success.

Honestly? I see lots of negative comments to do with his 'negative attitude' when frankly he's just very funny and a little bit sarcastic. Prof. Tillmann doesn't have time for students who want to stroke their egos and will shut them down categorically. Personally, I love it, and the coursework is easy enough as long as you sit down and shut up.
self-righteous to an intolerable point

The worst. This class is only suitable for people who boast of themselves. No real substance there, only egos. Every class is a joke to see your classmates trying so hard feel good. You can do better by not signing up for this class and learning some real skills (or taking a beauty nap).

Class is unorganized and I don't think he actually prepares for the course as well. Would be more fruitful if you buy the coursebook and read it yourself, presumably more fun. You rarely see a hypocritical professor but you get one with Tillmann, he would lie into your face. Learn to protect yourself when dealing with this prof.
Somethings wrong with him. Wants his class to have good attitudes but hes the one with the worst attitude.

ridiculous. this course is difficult only because of his inability to explain the materials and bad comprehension skills in understanding others' opinions. not a good person either: his level of hypocrisy is as high as the level of hypocrisy of the whole course. thinks that he's a linguist but is bad in english. unfair. nobody likes him in class.
Best English teacher ever

PHIL201 was challenging but super interesting - recommend for mathematically-inclined students looking for an intellectually stimulating introduction to logic. Definitely possible to do really well in this course if you apply yourself!

The most difficult class I've taken and I took it first year. Please please if you don't have to don't take this class. The content was so difficult and he is probably the most boring person ever in the whole world. He always started halfway through a slide set and never finished it any class, even the last day. Everyone had NYTimes games up.

Hallett tries his best to explain the course material, but loses his train of thought at least 25 times per lecture. Lectures cure insomnia. Watch his tutorials on 2.5x speed, read the textbook, go to conferences. Expect to teach yourself. Lectures are confusing. The final is reasonable, and extra credit is available for a number of assignments.
Genius. I love Hallett and his british accent.

Prof Hallett seems nice enough, but his lectures for PHIL 210 are torturous. He says about 1 useful word per minute and goes into way too much detail about irrelevant topics. If you have to take this course, though, do not give up hope. I failed the MT like crazy but finished the class with an A because I'm pretty sure he curves the final hard.

Review is more about PHIL 210 than it is Hallett - avoid the class if you can because the content is so difficult. He definitely doesn't make the course any easier and lectures are kinda useless, just read the textbook and practice. Despite this, he's nice if you talk to him and accommodating

the thing is that micheal hallet is a cute old man and has sometimes funny things to say. however, this man cannot teach any deductive logic for the life of him. im sure he's better in smaller setings, but have a class of over 300 people is clearly not for him, and most of the people i know barely passed or failed the final. watch out for this one

Believe him/TAs when they say you have to practice. The textbook, slides, conferences, and online practice are enough to earn you an A in the class. Don't check out after the first assignment (it gets much harder). Lectures are boring but he clearly cares about the topic. Seems annoyed with questions though lol. Studied a lot and got an A!

This class is awful. Please run away from this class and literally take ANY OTHER CLASS for your degree. This class destroyed me and my will to live. I switched majors after finishing this class, so at least I won't have to retake it if I fail it.
Awful. Reads off slides as if he is slowed down to 0.1x. Lectures completely unclear and rarely show what you are actually tested on. Doesn't respond to emails. Don't take this.

He's nice. Seems to enjoy teaching. He's not very good at it. The lectures & course were not very well thought out. It is evident he doesn't plan his lectures. No textbook was used, and the lecture notes were way too brief and similarly not well planned (eg, random unmentioned changes in notation). Exams were not really similar to homework/class.

learn python before you take this class with him. do not make my mistakes! the assignments are sometimes very coding-heavy, and prof hilke WILL tell you "ask chatgpt" if you ask for any direction or assistance. he's a very nice guy, but both of his midterms were horrible. had to defer the final for a family emergency but heard it was also bad...

Nice guy, god awful professor. 
Lectures are incomprehensible. The assignments are often very unlike the lecture material. The exams are disconnected from both the assignments and the lectures. It felt like the exams were for a different course entirely.
Due to exorbitant curving the class average was fine, but it was a gruelling ride. Avoid

His lectures were so incomprehensible and he'd literally stand in front of the board blocking everything he'd written down. Assignments were difficult. As a person he seems lovely, but he isn't the most effective professor. He gets bonus points for repeatedly bringing a blowtorch to class though.

Phys 558 taken fall 2024. 
Prof.Hilke is clearly passionate about physics as well as teaching. He can talk quite fast and therefore is sometimes difficult to follow. He is very approachable, however, so it's easy to ask for clarification. Overall a very intelligent, thoughtful and caring professor. I had a great time taking his class.
He will make you hate Physics and question your decision to study at McGill. Had the worst semester because of this course alone. What a waste of money.
Ruined my semester. A cool person but a terrible professor in every sense of the word. Buckle up

He is a super nice person, but his lectures make no sense and are impossible to follow. The assignments are an arbitrary mess of questions which for some reason contained highly weighted coding questions in a physics class with absolutely no coding prerequisites. Asked a question after class and the response was "use ChatGPT," not even kidding.

He's one of the nicest professors I've ever had, but oh god is he awful at explaining stuff. Every single one of us came out more confused than ever rather than being clarified. The exams and assignments felt like a bunch of random mess, and the assignments were always incoherent with the class lectures.

This course gives you an easy A but makes you learn nothing at all. Unorganized lectures. Weird conceptual questions involved in quizzes and exams. Last year he took screenshots of three ratings that gave him low scores on ratemyprof, and he literally talked about that in class.
COMP546 Not good class. Huge regret taking it. Would not recommend. Run.
run away at all costs

Tests are pretty difficult but is very lenient when grading. Lectures are good and is very accessible outside of class to help any students with questions, online and during office hours. Cares about students

If you are not religious, pick a religion and pray. I feel like he could be a good prof the only problem is that he worries too much about people not cheating and what not. I want to learn and all he worries about is other stuff. Not my cup of tea, and the exams are actually really hard.
Just run, all that has to be said
Actually not a good prof, I went once to Chads class much better. Don't take comp 208 with him , take it with Chad the goat . To busy worrying about grades doesn't actually teach anything

Average professor, classes can get a bit boring. Lecture recordings introduce the topics and lectures in person go into more detail, so attend to review and understand. Assignments are long, but great practice material. Midterm and final were hard and heavily coding-oriented, prepare well with previous exams.
Great guy, super approachable and is passionate about his field. Go to the lectures even if it is a flipped classroom, you learn a lot more than if at home.

Final average = 30/50, Midterm =13/22. Exams are hard and graded on few pts (make one mistake, - 5% straight away). Heavy curving does occur. Assignments take 10hrs, yet they deduct 2% for style pts (y= x vs. y = x). I learned tremendously though, Langer is a great professor, super clear, kind, and answers questions 24/7.

The class slides are excellent and his explanations are clear and intuitive. Assignments are interesting. Exams are relatively easy with almost no curveballs and focus on the most central concepts. Quizzes take up a lot of time despite not being very useful or important. I found the class pretty easy, though I already had basic Python knowledge.
He is strong teacher, who gives a lot of useful information and a lot of homework. The lessons are interesting and helpful. It is hard to pass the course and it seems he marks down the grades.

Michael is an extremely well organized, serious, strict and punctual teacher and the time you spent in class with him never go wasted. Lots of homework for sure but if you follow the pace, pay attention to his feedbacks and work on your weaknesses .. you are good to go .. !!!

He is well organised, you do not waste a minute during his class, so he expects the same attitude from his students.  Lot's of homework, lot's of new useful information. You do not have a choise but to study hard otherwise you will never pass the exam.
This teacher is serious,strict,udjust,his class is hard to pass.There are many students faied the exam in his class.

I learned a lot from this course. Michael is an excellent professor. He is a good entertainer and a very good organizer. He's decent with the grades. I would definitely recommend the students to have him for teaching.
Best music prof at McGill. Highly recommend. Very experienced, inspirational and good at teaching. Cares about every student.

Michael is the most caring and invested prof at McGill. He treats each student well, and does his best to take us from our current level to the next. His professional insights are invaluableand he has a good sense of humor. Widely respected and loved.
Michael mcmahon is one of the best professors at McGill. Many pianists like myself have been inspired by him to pursue accompaniment further.
phenomenal
master of the subject material. knows how to suggest other alternatives instead of making negative statements. inspirational.
Great prof. skillful musician and teacher.
Excellent teacher! No BS, straight to the point. Can make difficult concept easy to understand.

He does not respond to emails nor have office hours. Doesn't seem prepared for questions or lectures.  His grading is 
unfair and from his feedback you realize he doesn't take his time to mark his numerous assignments. If you want to be stressed out for low grade then go for this course!
Never replies emails, he even treats replying email as a joke. Unorganized exam, not planning ahead for lecture and assignment. Very disappointing class.

This is the worst class in my entire degree. He puts zero effort into giving lectures and adds extra work at last minute. Never replies email ,very low efficient, and super hard to approach. Also, grading is unfair.

A phenomenal waste of time. I would consider a different program had I known this waste of time was going to be part of my graduate studies experience. He rudely critiques students in front of all their peers, goes on tangents that make no sense, claims climate change is a religion and not science, and provides no feedback before marking. Horrible.
Most horrible teacher encountered in my whole life. He doesn't do any work or put any effort in teaching. He never replies emails.

The BREE seminar series of classes are a monumental waste of time. Nothing like paying to see the entire department present for 5 minutes about something they just learned for an hour and a half every a week. We have enough presentations in our regular classes to "learn how to present".
few things useful in the class, but too many assignments and reading are required after class

Very unclear, seems to purposefully waste time in class. His material is a lot of filler. There is a useless lab due every single week that is graded quite hard. Sometimes we haven't even learned the material that is covered in the lab, and most of the lab time is spent trouble-shooting the equipment. Very incompetent prof.  Huge waste of time.

Dr. Ngadi made a number of efforts to make this class interactive and interesting. He introduced changes that reduced the amount of paperwork required of each student. He was respectful towards students at all times . Public speaking can be stressful and his feedback and humour made it less daunting for the students presenting.
He was rude, disconnected, and relatively aloof towards students. Ngadi's class was disorganized and poorly organized. Although, fairly easy, it was a sensational waste of time.

MVD is a great lecturer in addition to being funny, knowledgeable, and reasonable. He makes the material interesting and wants you to do well. Lots of assignments, so lots of opportunities to get your grade up. Very accessible outside of class, gives great feedback if you ask him in OH. I am not interested in Middle English but I loved his class.

Could not recommend Prof Van Dussen enough. Took all his courses I was able to. Grading is fair. Participation is mandatory, which can be a turn off for some shy students, but he truly cares and gives good feedback of where to improve.

A caring, intelligent professor who marks tough but reasonably. I was expecting to make a case for the guy here, but no, it seems the critics agree; MVD is an exceptional professor. I have taken two classes with him, both have been thoroughly engaging and genuinely inspired me to pursue more education in the English/Medieval/History field.
My favourite prof at McGill. Mandatory participation and attendance with tough grading but really cares about you. Would highly recommend taking his classes
Engaging, funny, clear and handsome lecturer. He is kind but his classes are quite stressful because of mandatory participation. He has high expectations but is also a lot of help.

One of those profs that actually cares about their students. Great lectures. Material is already interesting but he makes it even more so. Would highly recommend taking this course. Not particularly easy but if you ask for help to improve, he will absolutely help you out. Pop quiz translations are a bit difficult early on but get easier. Great prof
One of my favourite professors of uni.

One of the best classes I have ever taken! He is very clear about his lectures and notes, and expects you to put effort in the class. But that's okay because you want to put effort and do a good job. He has great humour and often has funny slides, creating his own memes to discuss Medieval knowledge. He's super sweet and I would take him anytime!
My favorite class

Before Van Dussen's class, I had very little interest in the subject matter. But his clear lectures, his humor, and his obvious zeal for the subject made learning about Middle English a blast. It doesn't matter which subject he teaches- take a class with this man.

He is a tough grader and doesn't give very clear instructions for his assignments. However, if you go to his office hours he is very helpful. He's also very passionate and knowledgable. Assigns a lot of reading, but you can get away with not reading it all. His classes are more suited for literature students, don't take it as an easy elective.

He doesn't use a single visual aid, he blabbers on for the entire lecture, it's so hard to stay interested. He is super snobby and uptight, when you ask questions he is often rude, short, condescending. He is an EXTREMELY tough grader, I got points removed for punctuation, and for words that he "personally didn't think fit" Don't take his class!!!

I admit I should have seen Biron for appointments-- but despite having gone to all of the lectures, I found that they were not engaging. The content was so enormous (16 novels) that I expected the exams to have open-ended questions, but they were very precise. His style of teaching needs fixing. The few in-class discussions we had seemed useless.

Asks for too much content and hard to understand whenever there are no slides. He's not considerate for those that are non-French speakers and just there to complete their minor.  Also, would prefer to have additional written assignments rather than 2 test and a final worth a lot each.

The prof provides a ridiculous amount of context for the texts but doesn't specify whether or not he will actually test you on this material. I explicitly asked if he was going to test us on a list of authors he wrote down (without discussing the authors almost at all) and he said no. He lied. You MUST be fluent in French. Lowest grade I've gotten.

Very interesting class?I took this as a U1 student even though he insisted that is was ment for U3's, and enjoyed every lecture despite my low grade. He's a great lecturer, really knows his stuff well, very clear, easy to follow. He's quite demanding though, so be sure your French is in order and you've taken a class in French Lit before.

Biron is great!  He really knows the subject matter and is very passionate about it.  I am from the States, but I still found Qcoise lit interesting.  The class however is a bird course for the Quebecois who have taken it in CEGEP, so they are all talking in the back while the non-quebecois are struggling to take notes.  tough exams, but very fair
Great class, easy stuff if you do the work, and Pr Biron made it very interesting even if a little... endormant... in his way of talking. But overall, very good prof
His litterature class is interesting, he seems to like it very much. He is a really nice teacher, always willing to help you plus, he is really good looking.. (those blue eyes!)

wonderful classes, a pleasure to attend and has some very interesting insights into various questions if you've got the time... if you're fluent in french-- take this class!!! it's easy AND interesting. it doesn't get better than this.

one of the most engaging and entertaining lecturers I've had. Has an uncanny ability to involve the class in discussion, where most other profs would have to deal with 90 minutes of hushed murmurs from their students. Beyond that, a really pleasant guy. Always make an effort to greet him in the hallways.
Professor Lefebvre is truly a humorous professor and makes every lecture interesting; he also makes sure to convey the lecture materials well to the students. Would take his class again.

Really enjoyed this class! Pretty funny and has a great insight into the hierarchies of the science discipline. I enjoyed the material a lot. I think all science students should take this course. You really understand the way science works. He repeats the main concepts a lot, so pay attention and you'll do well! Have to go to lecture though!

Great professor! He is funny and entertaining, can be sassy but it's all with a good heart. He is REALLY repetitive so if you go to class you will know what is going on. Exams are fairly straightforward, again, he mentions everything in class so if you take notes you will be fine! Would take his class again.

Interesting class. Lectures are stimulating and clear.I don't think it is an "easy A". The tests are "easy" but you have to know a lot of details, so even if you go over all his lectures, you still cannot be sure that you can do well. Also, the final focuses too much on "statistics". The knowledge you think is important will not be on the tests.

Wasn't interested in the class, hardly went to class - which I really, really don't suggest anyone doing, I got lucky by getting notes from a kind soul. That being said, the midterm was ridiculously easy. The few times I did go to class Lefebvre was funny, answered questions clearly and is obviously very intelligentinvested
Absolutely loved him! I'm planning on reading his books!

Lefebvre is truly a breath of fresh air in what could have easily been a very boring class. He valued students who were interested in the subject and who made an effort to be active in class. Also, really helpful in office hours. He's really funny and makes an effort to be entertaining. Not a difficult class, can can be confusing at times.

Funny, funny guy. Super interesting class, easy to follow as long as you go to class. No need to do the readings, just follow along and study for the exams because he wants quite specific answers. Still easy to get an A though.

This teacher is funny and very helpful. He speak french too! So, it's very nice for francophone's student at McGill. His exams are easy, but you have to read and understand his material. It's easy to get an A.
Great lecturer, interesting, talks quickly

He just didn't care. For this past year, he used another professor's slides in order to teach his section for 300D1 and 311. He didn't understand why certain things were  in a certain order. He emphasized the volume of content we had to learn over understanding it and that resulted in him being fast and semi-coherent. He was very unprofessional.
unclear, nver state clearly the purpose of each step. there is a gap between the students' knowledge and the knowledge he thought the students have, seems he is talking to graduates.
Grrrrrrrr, that's all I gotta say!

Prof. Hartman is a literal gem. She is the best prof I've had, and when I see her around campus she is quick to recognize me and start up a conversation. She took time to get to know her students, and most of the assignments were fun and group projects. Participation does matter, but her lectures are easy to follow and she is extremely intelligent

Professor Hartman was literally one of the best teachers I've ever had. Shes engaging, well-educated, and so incredibly sweet. The assignments ranged from infographics to reflections to podcasts, all having clear guidelines and feedback while also being enjoyable. She cares and wants her students to succeed. If I could I would take her class again!

Prof. Hartman is so passionate and intelligent and cares a lot about her students. She does not give exams, but you must be engaged in the material to succeed. Great TAs, Very interesting readings. Very easily accessible, she replies very quickly. One of the weekly classes becomes a conference. Wish there was sometimes more lecture content.

This professor will not prepare you for the course, although he is nice and his notes are organized they do not align with the material tested. The exams are written to test the most difficult things and are completely unfair. It is not based on your comprehension of the course, you basically need to be a genius to get a good grade.
Goated lecture notes. Hard and proof based course though. Final was quite difficult but manageable

Amazing lecture notes. If you miss a lecture or find yourself struggling with a concept his notes are very easy to follow. He explains the subject with the patience and structure you'd expect from someone teaching first-year students. Also a very understanding and nice guy (definitely the best out of the three instructors).
the best lecture notes you will ever have. Take him if you can

His notes are super organized and he is always very kind and funny and tries to engage with students and make sure they're comfortable with the material. I had him in the morning and his energy was always a nice way to start the day. Some of the concepts toward the end of the course are more confusing but he tries his best to answer any questions.

Very beautiful and organized notes, they are very clear and if you miss a lecture you can easily learn by reading through the notes. Near the end of the course some stuff became confusing, but overall he explains well. He's super friendly and kind. A very chill guy, I enjoyed having him for my 8:30.
Miguel is awesome! has the cutest notes and really helps when you ask for help. Exams are fair, and it is easy to prepare for them.

Math 133 is my first ever math course at McGill and his notes are super organized and easy to read. It is better to attend the classes but I also taught myself most of the content through Youtube. But overall he explains nicely and creates a comforting environment for students to ask questions and gives useful advice!

I was looking forwards to this class... but her lectures are horrible; reads off a powerpoint that is posted anyways. Also, the class is supposed to be in-person, we have a lecture room reserved, but she wants to be online because (????) The frequent technical difficulties are entertaining however
she is a really nice prof, but the lecture let you fall asleep with her mono-tone. Not write her exam yet but everything before the exam is doable.
Everything before he final was doable, the final was literally impossible. Shes boring, but at least you can go into the final with a good grade.

a very sweet and understanding lady. the classes are extremely borrrrr...zzzzzzz (snore)..woops sry, thinking about the monotone voice put me back to sleep. Anyway as mentioned, she's clear, it's all in the slides. not a difficult class by any means but there's a lot of material and her midterm was fair but her final was insane in the membrane!!

She is very nice. Speaks in a mono-tone which makes it REALLY hard to stay awake. Dont need to go to class or buy the book cuz its all on her slides. Just keep up with the 2 lectures a week and dont let it pile up to the end. Lots of info to absorb, midterm to final not cumulative. Exams are not the easiest tho.
She's the NICEST prof ever! And her slides are AMAZING! You don't even need to buy the textbook or go to class. everything is on the slides! The midterm was HARD though... :) :) :)
Just awful. Teaches a class that may as well be a trivia course. Cant understand when she talks because she's so quiet but will stop class to make you pay attention.  Awful.
No Comments
Very easy exams, do the homeworks and practices and you see the exact same questions on the exams. Great profand explains stuff well but the french accent doesnt help.
The Goat for math 223

His lectures are a bit hard to follow along due to his INTENSE French accent, but follow what he writes on the board and you'll be fine. His exams and tests are very fair, no surprise material, he teaches what he tests on. Is a bit hard to reach, but will stay after class and answer any question you have. Accepts feedback well

One of the best professors I have ever had. He explains the material very clearly, and his notes are extremely detailed with relevant exercises that truly help prepare for exams. He genuinely cares about his students and is an excellent lecturer. I highly recommend taking his class.
Lectures are clear, lecture notes are posted and very helpful, exams are fair and a bit more chill than assignments

Material was very easy, the posted notes are a 10/10 so you can definitely skip lectures. Exams were easy , but homeworks were tough. Prof teaches very well with lots of examples, but he does repeat himself a lot (but not too much). The notes are really really great and super thorough.
I found his lectures to be very disorganized and hard to follow, but he posts really good typed lecture notes that are easier to learn from. His exams are very fair.

Pichot's exams are very fair, all problems were seen in either class or tutorial. Lectures were good, although not recorded. Notes are posted and very clear + easy to understand. Wish I had Pichot for more classes!

There was a textbook for this class, barely touched it. Understand the proofs and do the tutorial problems and you should be set for the very fair exam. Homework was sometimes challenging because we would learn the material close to the deadline. Love Pichot, take his class if you can!!

His lectures are a bit repetitive but he's very helpful during office hours. Will tell you what to review and how to review. The exam was a bit too easy and I think the class average was too high too.

Bauer is a very sweet and caring man. A bit awkward and traditional, but nonetheless kind. I got to say though this class was a bit bland and it really has the potential to be AMAZING. Like such a cool topic that didn't feel engaging at all. Everything he taught could have really been boiled down to half the semester, lots of repetition.  Very easy
Okay overall nothing to write home about, just a bit of an old-fashioned guy.

Dr. Bauer is one of my favorite profs at McGill. His lectures are easy to follow and his grading schemes are straightforward. If you don't mind writing essays and find the course material interesting, his classes shouldn't be too difficult.
