He let us give our presentations casually, which made us feel a lot more comfortable. Highly recommend!

workload is light; only three short essays and 1 final essay. I feel they are graded a bit harshly, and the grading criteria isn't very clear as well. Attending class isnt a must but its important to do the readings so you get a good grasp of the material. But if you like anime and manga you'll find his class interesting for sure.

Really enjoyed this class! Nice grading scheme, just three take home tests and one final essay. Prof Bauer really knows his stuff and lectures are very easy to follow. Would highly recommend if you're interested in Asian religions.
If you like anime and manga, this class is meant for you. Awesome professor.
Good prof, I like his lectures and I can see he enjoys the subject too. He seems like a very interesting person, I would have liked to meet him; too bad everything is online.

Dr. Bauer was one of the best professors I have had at McGill. He is both knowledgeable and passionate about the material. He adapted tremendously well to the COVID term and provided fair assessments. His lectures were all recorded, but very content-heavy and were required to do well on the assignments and final. He cares about his students a lot.

The course content was super interesting and the grading was all clear and fair. Prof. Bauer had a fantastic response to COVID-19, was understanding and accessible, and throughout the course used myCourses and technology to enhance the experience. Great prof and class!

The material of this class was quite interesting, but the grading scheme was horrible. We were only graded on 3 quizzes and a final. There was barely any feedback received on the quizzes/no feedback on final and the grading was really harsh. The TA's wouldn't change your grade even if you tried to prove to them that you deserved a higher grade.

Gave no practice problems after second quiz in preparation for final. Final was extremely misleading and impossible. Very unfair teacher wanting to see students fail. Not pleased with grading scheme either since very test heavy. Does not curve.

Prof Maric is a good instructor with no doubt. His lectures are amazing, I bearly missed his classes. His grading is excellent, he will give u points if you have written down the right equation even though your values are incorrect.
BUT, the final. AWFUL!!! I have done all problems that he has provided. Exam questions I have NEVER seen them before.
Genuinely very kind professor! Tests are challenging but partial marks are very generous and if one understands the material and work hard they can do well. Favourite prof at McGill :)

Professor Maric is genuinely one of the kindest profs I have ever had. He wants all of his students to understand the material and do well in the class, and he puts in extra time and effort to make sure that his students feel supported in their learning. His tests are fair, weighted appropriately, and the class is designed to aid in success!
Lectures were not clear. You learn 1+1 in class and he asked you to do data science.

I learnt almost nothing from the class. He pretended to be nice but he didnt give us feedback on our projects and gave all of us B. I emailed him afterwards asking for breakdown of my assessments. He never replied. A waste of my time. Our team consulted him and did a lot of research in our projects. He didnt even try to learn about that.

His lectures in class were not extremely clear, but you could get a very good grasp of material based on his uploaded lecture files before class. There are also a lot of resources online/YouTube, like LearnChemE) which cover the material. He is an extremely caring prof and very accessible outside of class. Exams were long but not extremely hard.
Awesome teacher, I've had him in three classes and he gives such fair exams every time. If you work for it you'll get your A if you don't you'll be close to failing.
Excellent prof, always here to help and to answer your questions, actually one of the few profs that care about his students and is here to hear them. VERY TOUGH exams though!!!
He is a great prof but for 200 level course he might not be the one. His exam is very hard and strangely after the exam when you get home and do them again it seems doable.

This teacher is very sweet and tries to do her best for the students, unfortunately I feel like she is not great at being clear and explaining the material. The grading is quite limited (45% midterm and 55% final). You can have up to 3% extra credits which helps tho. She also provided us with 2 practice finals which looked quick like our final!

Dr. Miocevic is very smart and kind, but really isn't great at organizing class material. She spent the entire semester focusing on the calculations, when the final was 90% theory. All her practice questions were also focused on the calculations. She also assumes a lot of things are common knowledge but she'll try her best to explain if you ask her

She seems sweet and knowledgeable but she's the most boring and unengaging lecturer I've every had at McGill. I fell asleep every class. Very limited practice materials, which is unfortunate in a math class where the midterm is worth 45% of your grade. I would not recommend.

She is obviously very knowledgeable. My main issue is that she spends more time focusing on calculations during the lectures yet her finals are 80% theory which I personally found difficult for a stats class. She does drop the lowest midterm grade so that helps!

Dr. Miocevic is incredibly good at explaining concepts in a simple to digest manner, she is probably one of the best profs I have had thus far at McGill. Doing all the practice provided and focusing on understanding the material rather than plugging and chugging will guarantee you a good grade in this course.

Class focuses on theory more than calculations. Be prepared for exams, since they are hard and detailed. Professor Miocevic is lovely and intelligent, but I found her lectures to be extremely confusing. She often used terminology without providing definitions and I felt like she contradicted herself a lot.

Professor Miocevic is nice however her ability to teach clearly was often hard. She would use complex terminology and often poorly explained topics leading to more confusion than an understanding. One of the main things about this course is that it is much more theory based than actually doing calculations.

I absolutely loved Dr. Milica. She is an eloquent lecturer and made me discover a passion for statistics in psychology. Her lectures are clear and you learn a lot. Tests were reasonable and she emphasizes theory over calculations, which I like.

Background knowledge is key, if u took 204 [take Dr Flake] take this class right after to make things easier. She tries to explain but I found sometimes she complicates things. Very monotone, had to watch lecture recordings on 2x speed to stay engaged. I taught myself everything with lecture recordings. Do practise probs & put effort = you'll pass

I really liked prof Miocevic. I have very little math background and my last statistics class was 2 years ago so I was really stressed for this class. Prof Miocevic was so straightforward and clear in her teaching that I ended up doing better in this class than all my other classes. Highly recommend, especially if you're struggling with statistics

Hes kind but I did not enjoy his lectures. He would start a sentence, then instead of finishing it, he would restart it but go in a different direction. He also overcomplicated the material instead of explaining it in the most straightforward way. Not hard material tho, and possible to do well in the class.

Fairly straightforward class, be very sure to fully understand the terms as Professor Brocic defines them for you, as those definitions will come up on the tests. Could have gotten an A if I had gone further into depth on the numerous readings. Counts towards Urban Studies major but most Urban Studies students will find this class unhelpful.

It shows Professor Brocic enjoys the material, he's an engaging lecturer. Exams require you to know the readings and lectures very well, so be ready to write a lot because it's mostly essay questions, but he is pretty clear on how the exam is formatted. There's group assignments and discussion posts that are pass/fail and an essay that's kinda fun.

He's a good professor with cute jokes sometimes coming from out of nowhere.. ppt is pretty clear but I recommend to attend the class since sometimes what he said can be helpful to set the guidelines for exam.
BUT his TAs can be really tricky (they don't give over 90 out of 100) so use your office hour wisely if you HAVE TO take this class

Prof Brocic is a great lecturer, super knowledgeable, chill, and gives out fun assignments. His classes are enjoyable BUT if you take him for soci330 specifically just know he does not give out As. I had to fight for my life for an A-. We were graded so harshly it barely made sense (got nothing but good feedback but still didn't get an A).

nice guy tbh but ta's super super bad. they graded our work like we were doing our post-doc or smt...hope to see the grades curved a bit at least. i have a great gpa and struggled the whole semester here. fingers crossed final grade curved

Prof is great, TAs are incompetent and a nightmare. AVOID AT ALL COSTS IF YOU CARE ABOUT GPA. I have a near 4.0 GPA, studied like crazy and had to contest every grade. For instance TA gave me a 70 and prof reviewed it and gave me a 90. TA flat out told me nothing was wrong with one of my grades (80) but I was already way above average.
Very very very very hard to do well in this course

While he seems like a nice prof, the class is really poorly managed. TAs very inconsistent in grading and assignments graded way too harshly. For many, this class is an introduction to a bunch of new theorists in the field and considering the level we're at, expectations are astronomically high. We're not Phd level. Hope the final grades are curved

I appreciate the way Professor Brocic engages with the course. He is always available for questions and answers emails pretty quickly. The content itself is not difficult, just heavy. Exams require you to have a good understanding of the material so you can write about it (short essay questions, definitions, and identifying quotes by thinkers).
Amazing! Informative and fun class!

Mindy is super kind, caring, and understanding. A drama course can be intimidating, but she made everyone feel so at ease and turned the class into a comfortable, judgment-free zone. I would highly recommend her.
Loved her class. Absolutely would take it again.

I LOVE MINDY! She is the best. Her class was such a breeze. It was an intensive class and I did not realize how fast 4 hours can go. We had so much fun. Made so many friends. Her teaching methods are amazing! She cares for her students and really wants the class to enjoy every bit of it. We had a blast. Can't wait to take another course with her
Best prof I've had at McGill! She is a fair grader and genuinely wants all of her students to succeed. Definitely would recommend taking any of her classes!

This is my second class I've taken with Mindy. She is super charismatic and caring. Her classes really allow you to be creative and take risks. She is a very fair grader and she allows you to decide how you would like to be evaluate on selective assignment. Would definitely recommend her as a prof!

She is so sweet. I had her for Theories of the Text and Poetics. Her instructions can sometimes be unclear, but this is because she's open to you structuring your essays to how you best see fit or would prefer, and is very accessible/open to discussing and clarifying things with you. Lots of reading for 322, though, but lectures go over everything.
Lectures were incredibly engaging and well-taught! Lectures and readings were dense, but very informative and interesting.

Nice lady and extremely bright. However, her lectures are very boring and she just puts paragraphs of the texts on her slides. Her instructions are unclear and not straight to the point. The final was ridiculously long and tedious, it was so absurd I never experienced that before. Lots of essays that are graded fairly and with lots of feedback.

So kind and so thoughtful in her teaching. She is super enthusiastic about the material and incredibly well-spoken in lectures, and gives very detailed feedback for assignments. ENGL322 is a lot of reading, quite hard to keep up with, and multiple essays - the take-home final was really lengthy.

This professor is truly one of the kindest professors at McGill! You can tell she deeply cares about the material and the students. I was not incredibly interested in the readings but she makes it more engaging through her lectures. The course was not intimidating.
Hickman is very sweet but sometimes rather dull. I don't know if in a smaller setting she'd be better?

The absolute GEM of the English Department and possibly the nicest human being I know at McGill. She always encourages her students to talk in class, and she gives great feedback. Definitely take her class if you can! SHE IS THE BEST

Absolutely stellar! She's a very engaging prof with incredible insight. Her feedback on papers is amazing. She encourages students to engage in the material and always works to engage your points in discussion. I always left her office hours feeling more encouraged than I did going in - 10/10 prof.

Hickman is one of the best profs in the English department. She encourages her students to participate in class and is genuinely interested in their ideas. She is very fair in grading too. Would for sure take more classes with her!

Great class and great prof. Encourages students to share their ideas and is super accepting and open to all different types of interpretations. I felt a lot more comfortable participating in her class than I have in others because of her kind demeanor. Really gives students the opportunity to be creative and explore their ideas.
talking to him feels worse than talking to a brick wall
nothing to say other then the fact that he is just plain rude. likeeee bae not a good look.

He ran the lab component for this course, so I only interacted with him a little, as the students primarily work with the TAs. However, I found the experiments interesting, and he was very kind and helpful the few times I had to ask him questions. The workload was reasonable and mostly contained to the lab session, and grading was tough but fair.
He managed the lab component of CHEM 110 pretty well during the pandemic. Answers questions in a timely manner.
Tough grader.

Arrogant and full of himself, does not help at all when you ask questions, thinks he knows it all. He's a first year lab director, how cocky can you get ?!
Rude and will not help you solve your problems.

Hout is a detailed and busy man. He's very direct and can come across as rude over email. But this man has one of the best designed online lab set ups. He's super well-organized, responsive, and all around puts a lot of effort into making in-person and online labs that are user-friendly. He's a busy guy, so don't waste his time.

The most infuriating professor I have ever had to the displeasure to encounter. He will not help you. When you ask questions, he will tell you to go read the lab manual (duh, we've all done that) or will tell you that your questions are not appropriate. An arrogant, rude man. To be avoided.

If you don't do the lab exactly the way he wants you to (which is hard since he gives vague instructions, always contradicts himself, and refuses to elaborate) or if your results don't match what he wants, he will gladly take off marks to bring your mark below 50%. His stubbornness makes him refuse negotating marks, even when he's being irrational

Prof Huot is a rude person who does not care about his students. He will also not answer your questions helpfully. As other said, he never gets to the root of the problem.

He was only there for the last laboratory on the Resting Membrane Potential. It was very hard to understand what he was saying as he has a very strong accent. However, he is very knowledgeable and his explanations are exactly the type of questions he asks you. He was not very accessible during the lab, however, the TA's and others were still there.
He is very interesting when you get to know him. Great knowledge and experience. Nice person and very helpful.
Very helpful. Speaks with an accent. Everything else OK.
He doesn't even speak English! Impossible for a physiology class to understand

One of the best professors at McGill. He presents the material clearly and with great passion. If you listen carefully in class, you will be more than ready for the midterms and final. The tests are very representative of the types of questions found in the assignments. My main advice would be to manage your time carefully during exams

Professor Alobaidi is one of the kindest and most caring professors I've had! I feel lucky to have taken three classes with him. He's super approachable, supportive, and always willing to help. His classes are engaging, and he regularly seeks feedback to ensure a positive learning experience for everyone.

A highly knowledgeable professor who prioritizes his students' success. He is very clear and interactive in his lectures and provides a comprehensive understanding of what will be required in assignments and exams, making expectations very clear.

An excellent lecturer and professor who genuinely considers his students' needs. He makes sure the material is well understood. He consistently provides clear explanations of course expectations and ensures students are well-prepared for exams by outlining key topics to focus on.

Very good professor, really takes his time in class to explain concepts to make sure students understand. He's also very accessible outside class hours and acommodating to student needs. Very keen on answering any and all curious questions a student might have. Very passionate about his subject and overall pleasant lectures.
Great professor

Dr. Mohammad is an amazing teacher. He Takes the time to explain difficult concepts. His slides are very helpful, he goes through the derivations to see where these equations come from and how to use them. Easy to reach him by email. His exams are very fair. He is very caring about his students. One of the best civil engineering prof at McGill.
Best prof I've ever had at McGill, really does everything to help his students out and is very understanding. Highly recommend taking a class with him !!

One of the best engineering professors at McGill. He is very passionate about the subject. He can easily communicate difficult concepts to students with ease. He is very caring and easy to reach him by email. His exams are fair. Overall, he is an amazing teacher.
Best professor in McGill
He just don't know how to teach
Extremely hard to understand in lecture, speech is a grammatical nightmare

A decent prof, nothing crazy though. His lectures are a little sluggish, but he does provide some clear explanations on topics he wants you to know for exams. The slides by themselves were enough to study from, and his abundance of practice questions makes it easy to review simpler concepts and topics. Overall good experience.
Yes he is monotone, but he is a great prof. The content was enjoyable, and the slides contained everything we needed to know for exams. The grading for this class is great.
He is very monotone and impossible to listen to in lectures. Very easy midterm and paper but impossible final.

Professor Darainy's content was the most interesting I've experienced so far! As a prof, he is kind and always willing to help. Even though our classes were until 5:30pm on a Friday, Professor Darainy kept us very entertained with his jokes and interesting real life examples and demonstrations for topics discussed in class.

I had to read the textbook to understand this class because this prof is simply too boring to actively listen to for 1.5 hours. Maybe it's because of my stupid tiktok brain, but I could not focus in his lectures at all. He's very monotone, but clearly well meaning and exams aren't too hard, but weighted very heavily.

He simply reads off slides that he got from another professor; creates barriers to make himself inaccessible to students; grades more harshly if you are already sufficient in the information by nit-picking details. All-in-all, he's a typical faculty member that only teaches because his boss tells him to do so.

He is a good professor, has a sense of humour, and uses good examples that help you understand the contents. I thoroughly enjoyed the course, it is content-heavy though, so be prepared to learn a lot of stuff

very meh prof&class. assignments &final project are annoying/tedious but easy. easy-ish midterm but final was quite difficult- only worth 25%tho. prof seems to Care and takes a lot of time for student questions, but his explanations dont really add anything beyond what's on the slides.
Amazing prof who is super passionate about what he is teaching.
Great professor, really caring for his students and is passionate about his subjects - I learned so much, loved this class :)

Really cares about his students and spends a lot of time clarifying concepts. Can be mildly confusing at times but genuinely wants his students to be engaged, have fun and learn. 413 is a great class for anyone who is looking to take it and learn a bit more about parasitology.
he is so nice!!!

okay prof, pretty confusing imo, doesn't really explain the basics and just kind of expects us to understand (?????); also heavyish accent which makes it really hard to discern what he's saying at times - on the other hand, very passionate man who wants his students to succeed

I took her for COMP421 where she teaches the first half of the course. I actually found her quite easy to follow in class. My only complaint is the pace was a bit too slow, but I had no trouble doing the assignments, in-class quizzes (worth 0%) and projects. She definitely knows what she's talking about. Her slides are also easy to self-study.
I feel like you have to pick one between mandatory attendance and being a bad lecturer. The stuff in class doesn't even begin to cover what's on the homework but you have to go. Literally a joke.

Not a good lecturer, the way she speaks and explains things makes it hard to follow in class. However she does care about her students. Had to teach myself a lot of things outside of lectures since many things were unclear, but overall getting a good grade was achievable especially since the grading scheme is generous. HWKs help for midterms.

Chill prof but lectures were near-impossible to follow and so scarcely prepared you for the assessments and homework (at least self-studying's easy). What rly irked me tho is that going to class = grade drop since I wasted valuable time going to lectures I couldn't understand, yet skipping to actually study/understand = grade drop due to attendance

She's sweet, but her lectures were tough to follow. I hope she develops the ability to keep people engaged in class, because I couldn't pay attention for the life of me. I do think her slides are decent though.
Also, I think using Discord for all class-related announcements is ridiculous. I hope that changes the next time she teaches this course.

She's nice, but her lectures were often hard to follow and didn't prepare you for the application based homework assignments well enough. The homeworks were good preparations for the midterm but I ended up teaching most of it to myself.

Terrible lecturer, incredibly unclear. Spends too much time on things that don't matter, and then the things that do are typically glossed over, yet you are expected to know them for exams. Assignments are handed out irregularly despite a published release schedule, in general COMP206 felt poorly organized and generally a headache to navigate. Bad.

Awful slides. She's very kind and seems to be trying her best, but sincerely, I do not know how I'm making it until the end of this semester in this class. She reads the slides and does not go much further than that; explanations are not very good, and the amount of assignments we have to submit leaves us with no time to actually study the content.

Not a good lecturer, but in a way that makes it very clear she's a new prof, not like she's inherently bad at it. Had her Fall 2024, she's probably gotten better. Assignments and exams were reasonable, and her notes/slides were p good, esp for the MIPS half of 273. I would neither jump at nor avoid a course bc she was teaching it.
There are a lot of accommodations in this class, she is trying to help students do well. She's not good at explaining the material and lectures are boring and confusing.

Had her for 141 - she can be passive-aggressive when you make mistakes and struggles to explain certain tests/assignments, but overall, she prepared us well for future musicianship classes and warmed up to us by the end of the semester.

Monica tries to be a good teacher and is available if you need help, however she doesn't always explain concepts very well and if you are struggling with something, she'll put you on the spot and force you to redo things.
Took three courses with her. Amazing instructor. Cares about students and always want to offer help so that student ended up with a good grade.

She literally yelled at me in front of the class because she taught us something wrong multiple times and I asked her why she was inconsistently teaching. In general, she did not even teach and just yelled at students who couldn't figure things out the first time around, and refused to explain or help.
Great prof!

Monica really wants you to succeed in the class, and it's made evident from day one.  She prepares you for everything you'll need to pass the class and if you actually sit and do the work (aka practice) you'll fly by the class.

She made a usually tedious class fun and challenging. She really cares about her students and will go out of her way to help them. Even if you're hopeless in solfège and/or dictation, she really values professionalism and effort. McGill is lucky to have somebody like her :)
Easy if you follow her rules. But you won't learn anything you can apply elsewhere which is a huge frustration.
Outstanding! the best teacher ever!

I've ran the gambit of Musicianship teachers here, and Monica is definitely the best one. She puts in so much for her students and is always clear about the material, deadlines, etc. For the first time in six semesters, I look forward to Musicianship!

She was one of the best professors of this course. She explained everything well and clearly and tried her best to make sure everyone understood by doing in class demonstrations. Her final exam questions were very fair aswell. She does not deserve the reviews she currently has
hi sishodnocas

I felt bad for Professor Zetka because I felt like she didn't want to be there. Like others have said, take the class as if there's no lecturer. Even when asked specific questions in class on the material she sometimes wouldn't answer. She often dazed off and stopped speaking for even a minute at a time.
If you do choose afternoon session, work as if there's no lecturer.

OK, I'm going to throw her a bone here. Maybe she's not the best teacher but if you do the readings before coming to class, you'll be fine. The material is interesting so the reading aren't that bad. You can tell that she's trying and she's welcoming of questions and listens to you when you try to explain your thinking. Give her a shot.

The only really bad professor I have had at McGill. Most of the class is wasted with her staring at her slides figuring out what she wants to say about them and not being able to articulate it. She seems like a knowledgeable scientist who is NOT cut out for teaching. My main tip would be to read the textbook and study from her slides.

Good teacher but only once you've understood the material. Best way to study for this class is to do the corresponding readings & take notes,& simply review them a couple times for the midterm. Midterm wasn't hard at all;no specific questions, broad. Don't depend on her to learn the material, but rather as a revision class of what u already learned

She is the worst prof I have had! Her lectures don't make any sense, and most of the time is spent fielding questions from students. There are people audibly saying "What?" in her lectures! Textbook is not mandatory to read, but it kind of is bc you won't know what she is talking about

She is a very interesting and knowledgeable  prof., she may not be the best at explaining but one-on-one she is very helpful. She is really excited about what she researches and happy to share and help you understand better.

Zetka is definitely the worst professor I've ever had in my life. She comes to class seemingly high usually or at least seems like she's talking to spirits or something. She is very inaccessible to email. Her test questions are overall extremely confusing. She holds no office hours, and her lectures really have no structure whatsoever. TERRIBLE

Great prof. This class was awesome, easy A. However, I would not recommend this class if you aren't good at scientific writing/coming up with a hypothesis and a research plan to answer said hypothesis
Not helpful at all. Very demanding.
Nice professor, clear and concise, wants you to succeed. This class is work intensive, but it's very consistent workload throughout the year and there's no final. Good class, good prof.

PPTs are very detailed. Still, pretty hard, if you read the textbook with the PPTs, before or after the lectures, you're good. Especially for the first few modules. Nice prof though, lectures interesting enough.

You will hate your life. The class was heavy and stressful. The teacher and the TAs were not helpful. He was in his own world and did not simplify anything. He changed the material 2 days before the exam. He gave us no warning and no practice. He royally screwed us. Worst teacher, and course. Get ready to fend for yourself. We understood nothing.

The class itself is tough. The midterm was great and was based on the homeworks, quizzes and things we studied but the final was things we did not cover to that depth. Homeworks are difficult and quizzes are easier. He is not very approachable on zoom and in person.

Prof Sonderegger is a fantastic professor who is clearly passionate about what he teaches. He is accessible outside of class, his lectures are funny and informative, and he is available to chat with about anything linguistics outside of class. Definitely inspired me to pursue linguistics further, highly recommend!!

easily my favorite first year class i took. incredibly charismatic and cares that you understand the material. midterm and assignments were clear, fair, and consistent. grading was excellent. TAs perfectly chosen. i had no complaints about this course at all, would definitely recommend.

Professor Sonderegger seems like a really nice guy and his lectures weren't bad, but as somebody who took this class because of an interest in linguistics, I struggled with the class. As an intro course, it's quite confusing if you have no background in linguistics and therefore it's easy to fall behind. He's a nice prof, but a bit confusing.

i think my issue was with the course itself: i'm an essay writer humanities kid and i STRUGGLED in ling 201. morgan himself is great, really knows his stuff and has an interesting background, but beware to anyone considering taking 201 as an "oh looks interesting" elective: if you're like me, this might be a very difficult class for you.

Lectures were easily understandable but often repeated stuff if you had done the readings. Problem sets and quizzes were representative of the material covered. The final was more difficult but not super hard. Overall it's an interesting subject to learn about.
Morgan was a great prof! He taught material very clearly. Can sometimes be a bit monotone, but the material is very interesting if you are interested in linguistics.

Overall good prof, but his lectures could stand to be clearer, and keep in mind that you have to pay as much attention to the textbook as to lectures. Pretty frequent assignments but if you get the material you'll be fine, and groupwork is allowed for these assignments.

Best poli sci prof at McGill. Fun lectures although he does go on frequent off topic tangents. Clearly very passionate about what he teaches, responds fast to emails, and is supportive of all students. content can be hard but he teaches it well and grades fairly.

Edit because I put the wrong class: Katul is the best and kindest poli sci prof I've encountered at McGill. He's funny and keeps his lectures interesting, there were a lot of readings but ultimately he was ALWAYS available to help students even if it inconvenienced him. He genuinely cares for his students, I'd take every class with him if I could

Prof. Katul is the best and kindest poli sci prof I've encountered at McGill. He's funny and keeps his lectures interesting, there were a lot of readings but ultimately he was ALWAYS available to help students even if it inconvenienced him. He genuinely cares for his students, I'd take every class with him if I could

Dr. Katul is the best professor in the Political Science faculty at McGill. He is extremely accessible outside of class, knows everyone's names, and actually cares about the students learning the content and achieving a high grade. Go to office hours and get to know him, he's a really well-read and interesting guy.

Hands down one of the best Poli Sci profs at McGill. He goes above and beyond to help us, and even held office hours on weekends. The class is reading-heavy, but his midterm and final are SOOO fair. His goal is clearly for us to understand the material and succeed. He's hilarious and an amazing professor, take him if you can!

he genuinely cares about his students and wants what's best! i did find his midterm hard bc it relied heavily on the readings but his questions were fair. he also has weekly "homework" to get more points and review the material, which i found helpful. his teaching style is disorganized but he is hilarious and engaging!

Professor Katul is an incredible lecturer, super engaging, and also funny. POLI 444 with him was by far my favourite course at McGill. He is incredibly knowledgeable and cares deeply about his students. He goes above and beyond to ensure students not only understand the content, but how it actually applies to the real world beyond just theory.

Prof is absolutely amazing and caring. Really funny. Readings are intense but enlightening. As an European, this course changed my perspective on lots of things. Midterm was hard to prepare for, lots of readings, content, but general and fairly graded questions. Slides were sometimes dense, hard to follow. Don't neglect the readings!!

Mounir Katul is one of the best professors I have ever had at McGill. He truly sees students as people and cares about them so much. Very responsive and open to help you. Exams are also super fair, and so is grading. He is also extremely funny. Love him!!

Professor Katul is extremely considerate and cares about his students. His exams and assignments were fair , grading criteria was clear and concrete. He is determined to see students which is really nice . Would definitely take his class again

The lecture is clear. The assignments are long and time consuming. The exams focus on the contents taught in the lectures, so attending classes or going through all the recordings are recommended. Overall nice professor with clear lectures.

I heard a lot of bad things about this class before taking it. But i ended up enjoying it very much. This class does require tons of work, but prof explains the material clearly! Learned a lot by taking this class. Just make sure you have enough time to focus on reviewing for the exams and doing assignments.

The lectures do not prepare you for the assignments. Assignments require high comfort level of C, which is not taught. The slides have countless typos, are generally confusing, and are just not enough to answer certain exam questions.

Assignments are really heavy and take a long time. Lectures are a bit boring but I think he realized the weight of the tasks and made 1 assignment and 1 midterm optional(this helped a lot). Note: I think the exams were heavy on memorizing everything, not that much creative application.
Lectures are quite useless for the exams and assignments. This class has some important and interesting material but I did not enjoy this class at all.
This course was death

Ridiculous Assignments. 
"It's normal you don't know how to do it" -Mahesh

Do not take this course unless you have a strong background in C and are willing to spend dozens of hours debugging your assignment with little to no guidance. The course covers a lot of interesting topics, but the lectures are only meant to explain these topics conceptually. Exams are unreasonably difficult and assignments are unreasonably long.
completely unreasonable

Learned a lot. Never showed up to class because it was online and recorded. The three midterms were the only reason I stayed caught up to date on lectures. Had a couple hard questions on midterms but he curved to account for it. Assignments take a lot of work but taught me lots of useful C skills.
He was passionate about his subject and very respectful of students.

I LOVE him. He is passionate, kind, well-spoken, very knowledgeable, and approchable. He has created an effective class and although it's intensive, I have been enjoying it. Very practical methods and resources are being presented and it is easy to see that he cares about his subject and about his students.

Dr. Boudreau is an inspiring and engaging prof. He has a wealth of knowledge and is very wise. He is an asset to the Faculty of Education and I have always enjoyed having him as a prof. He has a special way of sharing his stories and everyone can learn a lot from him.  He is indeed one of my favorites in the Faculty. Keep up the good work !

Maybe it depends on one's interest in the subject matter but I enjoy going to his class, I enjoy his stories and appreciate that he has arranged for so many guest speakers. He clearly cares about the subject matter and that comes through when he is teaching. Understanding of our needs as students in my opinion.

I have a friend who took Math 133 and Math 223, and he told me what I learned was absoluately not what he did in Math 133, instead he taught more like Math 223 stuff or something, focusing on abstract proofs and theorems instead of applications. It is quite confusing for beginners. Overall the teacher is nice though.
Prof Jo always loves to engage with students, class lectures always. It was fun at his class.

Very nice Prof, always trying to make jokes and make people laugh, genuinely very sweet, but unorganized and very unclear grading criteria. Class content was completely useless and very repetitive, so just go to class for the attendance and talk so he knows your name. Overall, pretty easy to get a good mark.

While it is true that the teacher is vague on his grading criteria, I honestly think that the key to having an A is to be consistent, go to every class (or as much as you can), participate so that he knows your name, ask questions, show interest! When writing your essays, go in-depth and show that you did a lot of research. He is super sweet!!

He has a lot of bad reviews, which I get because he is disorganized, doesn't answer emails, and won't hand out grades even when asked, but this lack or organization was almost refreshing in the Desautels faculty. It fostered a very chill environment, where I never felt stressed. He is super funny too. Super easy class.
The class I've least learned from in McGill. Not clear grading criteria with projects. However, it is quite an easygoing class.

Provides poor feedback on assignments.
I am honestly disappointed at how little learning there was in this class.
I would say the same regarding another class I had with him in Market Research.

While the lectures hold little relevance to course assignments, participation is graded. If he likes you, you're gonna do great, but don't be offended if he doesn't learn your name all semester. He gives very little feedback and everyone gets the same marks; and he ends the semester without revealing your grades on most assignments. Easy class tho

Prof. Jo made an effort to memorize everyone's names even with masks. He will cold call you during class and most of the answers will need to be looked up online, but it forces you to pay attention. There are no real readings and the class is mostly graded on essays and presentations. Best prof I've had at McGill so far.

Class was a group project with barely any explanation+ quizzes. The prof will not answer emails + will have you chase him down for office hours/questions regarding grading. Quiz grades are based on specific words that must be included and you will not see the correction/your paper no matter how many times the prof says he'll "bring it next class".

Funny professor. Low work class; very easy. Don't learn much in class though. And his grading criteria is not that clear, leading for it to be unclear why you didn't get an A. Take this class because it's easy and low work, not because you want to learn about international business.

Teacher reads off slides. Packs too much information into one lecture. Defensive when students give feedback. However, easy class to pass. Unfortunate that we cannot choose our teacher for this class because it has interesting topics.

she is so incredibly unorganised and boring. couldn't finish her lectures on time. CONSTANTLY contradicting herself. I had her for biology of behaviour, she spend like 30 minutes explaining how we shouldn't anthropomorphise animals and then went on to anthropomorphise animals every other lectures. also can't answer questions at all

Overall nice enough. They are extremely disorganized and often contradict themselves. Unfortunately these contradictions lead to incorrect information and you may find in future years, this prof did not prepare you for future work.

Easiest section of Biol 216 - the exam for her section had an average in the 90s. Extremely kind, though a bit disorganized/unclear with instructions for conferences. Very clear lecture content and slides, and was pretty clear about what was expected on assessments.
She is a very nice prof and wants her students to succeed. Content is the easiest of the 3 sections of biol 216

She was so disorganized and seemed to have no idea of what she was lecturing about. I was disappointed by her midterm and from people I talked to a lot got around a 60%. Overall, she sucks at lecturing and her test questions were not fair.
TOp 15. good prof too, goodcourse

Highly recommend avoiding at all costs. Big on students being in class even with all lectures posted, goes as far as refusing to allow students to retake quizzes even with proper documentation of illness. Avoid avoid avoid

I enjoyed her lectures at first, but she literally cites Twitter threads and Vanity Fair articles as "scientific evidence" in a class that emphasises the scientific method. Big into conspiracy theories like China leaking the COVID 19 pandemic from their labs...
Nagissa is a really good prof and explains things really well. The format of this class is quite tough though with a 50% final that covers a wide range of topics.

Najib is awesome and explains everything thoroughly. Everything tested on the midterm and the final reflected the content in the zyBooks chapters, so studying for the exams is rather straightforward. I like that he connects some of the concepts to his work at Air Canada and he loves to answer any question—no matter how basic. Assignments are easy.
Goated prof, will answer all your questions and make sure that you understand everything. Might seem fast on the lectures but when you pay attention its awesome.
Goated prof, big s/o naj
very very good.
very Solid guy. Teaches well and is well-rounded.

Prof. Najib is great at teaching! He is always willing to help during office hours and gives detailed lectures, always making sure that students understand the material. Both the midterm and final were composed of multiple choice questions, so look through the material carefully. Do pay attention in class, as lectures are fast-paced.
Easiest class I've had so far. Good prof too.

Best lecturer I had this semester. Explains everything in detail and easy to follow if you pay attention/keep up with the material. Midterm is easy, final is fair but not extremely easy. He is happy to answer questions inside and outside class. Some advice: go over short exercises/labs shortly before or after material is covered to stay updated.

Great professor overall. Lectures can be a bit tedious at times but he explains all the concepts clearly and in depth. Midterm isn't too hard and gives at least a week to complete both assignments. At first seems very serious but he's actually very chill.

Professor Mozahem is very knowledgeable and explains concepts well. I had him for MGCR 331 and learned a great deal from him. His group assignments were a bit challenging but fairly graded and he is willing to help and support us. Going to class and keeping up with the exercises are key to success.
Worth having her as a prof to see the outfits alone.
She is OK, depends on your style you might love her or not.
comme ci comme ca

The Rule of Law and Development is a particularly interesting course. Prof. Ramanujam is excited about the topic, available out of class, and has done a great job of putting together a set of insightful readings.
Very kind and encouraging. Solid amount of grammar review for an intermediate class. Cold calls. Can be a homework heavy course.

I took intro to ancient greek, i'm actually traumatized. When people asked questions she would rant about how we need to study more, is a really nice person not a very patient prof, it was very difficult, lots of homework and 2+ quizzes every week, beware she chooses people to participate in class. I advise you find another class to take
(for CLAS 308) Generous grader! Interesting lectures and great personality. Enjoyed attending class.
Lots of essays and exams are pretty tough. Cool class though

I recommend this course 100%. If you are interested in Ancient Greece at all, take this course. It consists of one or two quizzes every week, two tests and a final exam. If you're good at learning languages, this course should be an easy A. Prof. Kaloudis does a great job at explaining the tough stuff. Textbook material is super interesting too :)
Really great class, the language is a hard one to learn but she does a good job of making it understandable. Studying for quizzes is very important!

You should not take a class with this professor, she is genuinely rude. Whenever we ask questions she is always annoyed and explains really badly. She expects her students to know everything in two seconds and her classes are not productive. Overall very bad experience and would avoid her.

Overall a solid professor who gives insightful lectures. You are expected to attend and participate in conferences, but getting full participation marks is easy. The writing assignments are simple, but some prompts are poorly worded. Memorization is key to doing well on the exams.

Best class I've taken so far! If you're interested in Greek Mythology, I recommend this class 100%. Professor Kaloudis is a great lecturer, helpful, and caring. If you take notes, you should be fine for the tests. I personally found the microthemes very fun and the conferences were very engaging.

Dr.Kaloudis is an amazing lecturer. The Microthemes may be graded harshly depending on your TA, however, you should contact them and ask a lot of questions to maximize your grade. If you take notes during the lectures and take time to review, read the fun stories, I can't stress how EASY the exams were. Conference participation is free marks.

Professor Subramanian is among the best professors at McGill. He truly cares about his students succeeding and is very accessible outside of the classroom. If you are interested in the South Asian region or politics of ethnicity, take a course with him as he is incredibly knowledgable about the field. Grading scheme and exam format was also clear!

Despite the content (civil rights, caste system) being inherently interesting, this prof lectures very slowly and muddily, and is not at all engaging. There is an unbelievable amount of readings. Luckily he offers the midterm / final main questions a week or two beforehand so you can formulate your answers in advance. Would generally not recommend.
Interesting topic and good prof but speaks slowly and lectures can be a bit long.
Poli 322 was a nice class to take, lectures are recorded and midterms were open book exams. Nice prof too
A very nice guy and patient when it comes to answering questions. Lectures can be a bit long at times but the content is interesting & he knows his stuff!!

Subramanian is a great guy but his lectures can be incredibly boring. I really enjoyed him in POLI 321 but this class has an exorbitant amount of reading, and incredibly lengthy exams that are entirely based on memorization.

Subramanian is incredibly knowledgeable on South Asia and beyond: there seemingly was not a question he was not able to answer with impressive depth and nuance. He really challenges you to think critically about class material - and there is a lot of it. His class is very rewarding if you commit and are willing to spend some time with the readings.

If you're deeply into South Asian politics, this could be an amazing course, Professor Subramanian is very knowledgeable. If you are not passionate or from the region, do not take. Lectures are way too content-heavy, and way too specific. TAs are terrible and won't help you. The professor is a tough grader who won't give you any proper feedback.

very tough but rewarding course, a great professor and so knowledgeable on the material, but the lectures are dense and its hard to keep up, the fact that lectures were recorded made up for it and he patiently answers questions, TA expected a lot from students when grading midterms and its reading heavy, but i really gained a lot from this course

This class was one of my favourite poli classes I took. Prof Subramanian is very knowledgable and his lectures are content heavy for sure, but it is very interesting if this is a topic that intrigues you. The only thing is there is quite a lot of memorization. Highly recommended if you are into South Asian politics.
One of the top profs in ECE, excellent lectures with bonus points, and very fair exams. Hope can take a course with her again.
She is clearly super knowledgeable in AI and that comes through in her lectures.
She was the best, kind and compassionate, she can explain in very simple way and her teaching method is excellant

Prof. Narges was really kind throughout the course. She took time to explain each and everybody's question, though I didn't ask any. But she didn't reply my email regarding MP2. Perhaps she was busy. Apart from that, she was an excellent instructor. If I am given the chance to do a PhD under her supervision, I will definitely take it.
Her explanations are very clear and she explains all the material in depth. In addition, she really has a passion for what she's teaching which makes the class very enjoyable.
Armanfard goes through problems step-by-step, takes time to answer questions in depth, and makes herself and her TAs available for office hours. Truly wonderful.

Good lectures. There are room for improvements in the lecture notes, but they are well informative. Online quizzes and class polls are moderate to easy. You need to ace the projects with lots of tests and experiments and explain them well in the reports. There are a few tricky questions in the final. Make sure you explain them properly.

She consistently took the time to answer questions with thorough detail, showcasing her extensive knowledge. Her presentation of the course material was exemplary, effectively conveying complex concepts.

I strongly believe that she is an excellent teacher. Their ability to explain complex concepts in a clear and concise manner is truly remarkable, and their passion for the subject matter is contagious. I feel incredibly lucky to have had the opportunity to learn from such an inspiring and knowledgeable teacher.

I learned a great deal from her. Her engaging and interactive teaching style encouraged critical thinking and creativity. Her passion for the subject matter was evident, and her expertise and knowledge were impressive. Her approachable and patient attitude towards answering questions made the learning experience enjoyable and valuable.

Amazing professor. Passionate about what she's teaching and gives very engaging & clear lectures. Grading is very generous and she is very open to helping her students. Her office hours are extremely helpful and it's super clear that she cares about her students. Be aware that this course is INTENSIVE; you need to do the work to do well.

Overall good prof, has a tendency to prefer the "French" dialect of teaching the French Language. If you care about doing well, make sure to attend office hours and avoid letting homework build up. Find a good partner for the class, and do not be late or skip, as active participation is key.

Professor Wanis is by far the best French teacher I've ever had and is someone I learned so so much from. She speaks French the whole time without ever switching to English which helps a lot to learn the language. She gives good feedback and is always available if needed. Genuinely going to miss this class.

I personally really liked her, she's firm but fair and explains things very well. She is also really helpful and can meet outside of class to explain things. I don't know why she has such a low rating on here

Good lord do not take this course with Wanis if your GPA matters. I wish I S/U'd it. No matter how hard you work you won't improve and this course will take the time away from your other courses. You will be teaching yourself and she only gives pointers to students who are already doing well so if you start slow you're basically screwed.
Course is online and fairly straightforward. Professor posted everything we needed up front, so overall a very pleasant experience.

Her online pre-recorded lecture videos are easy enough to follow, and contain all the information you need to pass the quizzes. She responded to questions on the myCourses discussion board fairly quickly and helpfully. Not much more to say since I barely interacted with her.
The course itself is pretty short, and is self-directed most of the time. I didn't have any personal interactions with her, but she seems to answer questions on the discussion board pretty quickly.
she made a 0 credit class painful. not clear at all. not flexible whatsoever

Took her for FACC100, Definitely take her!!!! Only one "paper" and it was 500 words. Polling questions are just for participation and you have around 7 easy group activities. Easy A for sure, final is super easy and no need to study if you have other exams.
She rushes through the lecture at the end of the class. Articles are boring. They repeat themselves.

Mme. Liakina is amazing. She cares deeply about her students and even will take an interest in your personal life if you tell her about things that you've done outside the classroom, especially if they are related to French! She is very accommodating and wants to make sure that you succeed, so reach out to her if you need help, she'll never say no!

Prof.Liakina can always provide you good way to practice and help you improve a lot. You will find it joyful to learn and speak French if you follow Prof. Liakina and practice hard and you will be surprised that you can easily speak French spontaneously. Her office hours are always helpful.

Liakina is an incredible professor, and she really wants you to succeed/improve your French. I highly recommend taking her classes. She now even teaches FRSL 325, an intensive course, and teaches it incredibly well based on my experience. She is also very happy to meet outside of class to answer questions and work through problems you may have.
10/10 human being. So caring and so prepared. Even apologizes for arriving 5 minutes late when she has another class before. Natallia has my respect and please treat her well.
Natallia Liakina is the best French teacher Ive ever had in my many years of the language. She is empathic but also great at encouraging improvement in students. Definitely an amazing professor!

Professor Liakina is really understanding and accommodating. She encourages you to meet with her to review grammar or pronunciation or anything you need. The class isn't easy, but she grades fairly and helps you succeed. She helped me speak french spontaneously, improve my pronunciation and my oral comprehension. If you can, take a class with her!
Best French teacher at McGill hands down, if you have the oppertunity to take a class with her do it. Actually wants you to learn

This prof is awesome. One of the best classes I've taken. She really wants you to do well and not wreck you. She's accessible outside of class and really nice. Wish she taught more classes! Go to class and be engaged because participation matters in a language class. She doesn't grade too harshly at all but at the same time gives you feedback.
She is the most organized professor I've ever met at McGill. She prepares so well for every class and she is always there if you need any help. Highly recommended
Madame Liakina is a wonderful instructor, she also applied a lot of  research on language learning to the teaching method, very impressive!

I had Professor Nathalie Tufenkji in 2024, and the experience I had with her was very irritating to say the least. I am aware that the class is 1 credit, but being unable to penalize students that do no work in a team is beyond my understanding. Please take your class seriously and I'll do the same.

I don't have many negative things to say other than she makes the content of the course long and boring. after the first month more than half the the students didnt show up anymore. While her class is not difficult at all, it can be really dreadful if you have a bad group for your group projects/assignments. Overall an easy grade for those who try.

She is textbook definition of I dont care about students or your circumstances, I'm here being a lecturer because its a requirement to continue funding for my research. The content of the course inherently is boring, so I can't blame her at all for that, but her character is stubborn, she will never make an effort to make student's learning better.

The slides lacked clarity with excessive text, leaving us uncertain about exam expectations. Although she doesn't ask tricky questions, she expects you to learn all the other equations that aren't provided. Despite recommending manual reading, her slides merely duplicate its content. Regular Slido quizzes are part of each class.

There were little to no examples given to practice content, and the grading/weighting of the course on the tests is very strange - a whole unit was one MC questions where one slide was a long answer worth 30%. The slides are crammed full of text, and very hard to decipher due to the use of technical terms that are never fully explained.
Class is interesting and she does an alright job teaching it. It's her way or the highway. Don't even bother going to see her, she's always right.

This course was offered for the first time in Fall 2015. The material was easy to understand. However, the assignments are too long and require you to read a couple of papers for each one. There's also a presentation. You can easily get a good grade.
easy as long as you are listening. Exams are fair and heavily based on student presentations.
Material is fairly straightforward and she teaches with a good attitude. However, the structure of the class needs work, and tests were mostly MC, which was unfortunate.

She had no idea what she's talking about most of the time. Repeats herself, and if one is still not convinced, might change her mind. Her TAs are the worst, some aren't even engineers to begin with. Her exams were relatively straight forward, just know how to do a non-pinch question on the final! She won't answer if the question was on the final!!

Pros:

-Presence is not compulsory.
-Assessments guidelines are clear (no surprises)

Cons:
She jumped into conclusions very often, and she is judgmental of her students.
Sometimes you know that she has not prepared her classes as she runs quickly through the presentations slides.

Overall, an average performance, do not expect too much.
Good teacher, knowledgeable. Tough tests, does not give enough time to complete them.

Great teacher! She makes class lectures interesting, listens to your opinion or explanation on her questions and gives positive and constructive feedback. Course outline is clear and concise, documents and quizzes are explained and very accessible. I had her for OB and currently in Change, very knowledgeable in every topic that she is teaching.

Nathalie was great! No hidden agenda, no judgment on students, genuinely wants you to pass. Is incredibly understanding (and thats saying a lot for a uni teacher) 10/10 would take a class of hers again

I absolutely adored the Talent & Performance Management course with Mrs. Sylvain. During the classes, she was very witty and she used a lot of personal experience examples to make us understand the topic easier. She was a tough grader, but she was very fair. It's important to listen to what she says, as she gives all of the answers during classes.

awful professor. develops opinions of her students way too early, doesn't get to know them. you can try as hard as you can, if she doesn't like you form the start don't except for her to change her mind.
Absolutely loved class with this professor.

I adored Nathalie for CORG 557. I was so surprised at the ratings she received, and how hard she was made out to be. But honestly if you listen, do the readings and study, it's a normal McGill class. The group projects were hard because you dont pick your team members (I was stuck with 2 who barely spoke English). I got 90 on both Cases + midterm
Great prof! You need to go to classs though or you will lose a lot of points
Seems nice at first but actually isnt. Tough grader for presentations and final. Final average was 64 ( for a relatively easy beginner class like MGCR 222) and she did not curve
His section was quite short, but he was a very nice guy and always open to questions.

Super chill prof, usually just gave short lectures about like random chemistry history lessons about psychedelics or pasteurization before tutorials started. Always shows up to class in sunglasses, usually with an orange fanta. Taught one lecture while Pavelka was away and it was actually really great, I wish he'd taught the whole course.
Best prof ever!!!!
He always wears his sunglasses.

He is a very good prof in terms of caring about his students, to the point it becomes a fault. He answered too many questions in class, slowing the class down a lot. There are weekly quizzes, but they are pretty easy, and half of them are done in groups. He is also very helpful if you talk to him after class or in OH. Also, MCQ on the MT/final.

There is SOOO much content in this class for absolutely no reason. His quizzes and problem sets are random and he just expects you to have a material eng background as common knowledge. His final was fair and he didn't curve even though he said he would...

Explanations a bit confusing and lectures got derailed by too many questions (particularly the french guy who kept saying “but professor… what is the use of this”).
That being said the course notes are quite good though the textbook is not worth your time.
Insanely hard midterm but the final was reactively super easy.
He's a good prof, but the marking is terrible; just avoid him.
marking is terrible

weekly quizzes worth 22%. 8% is free essentially. He's a really really good lecturer and while it is possible to do well without going (I missed most), you'll make your own life more difficult as the only resources he provides are notes from a past student. Midterm and final are open book, so honestly, makes good grades pretty easily attainable
Weekly quiz based on an entire chapter and quizzes are detailed
Awesome professor!

Pay attention in class and read the chapters of the book and you'll be fine. Getting a decent grade in this class can be done without much work but doing really well takes work. Test grading was tough, it takes a while to get a feel for it. He makes this class which could be VERY boring pretty exciting. He doesn't show up to office hours, though.
good guy . nice class. get ready for RAPID quenching...
This class was boring, unnecessary, and graded very harshly. My TA was genuinely an opp

He seems insecure about the fact that people don't think film is difficult or deep. The class zeros in on convoluted ideas that are largely irrelevant because of this. You can't convince me I will ever use the concept of the "filmmind" to explain something.

A really nice guy, but sadly his lectures are very boring and seem aimless. He spends a lot of lecture time on class participation, which feels unproductive. The positive, though, is that you don't really have to do the readings, and if he's the one who grades your paper, he'll probably give you a decent mark.

Prof Schantz had extremely organized lectures. He also took the time to learn a lot of students' names, considering the class size was pretty big. The evaluations were easy and the grading was flexible, depending on your participation. I wouldn't say it was a life-changing course but I would recommend taking prof Schantz if you get the chance.
10/10 Best professor ever! He is so kind and you can tell he truly cares for both his students and the material he teaches. Stop leaving bad reviews and go to class. Would take again:)

Prof. Schantz is the best! His lectures are very conversational and suggestive. Definitely come prepared with the readings & films watched. He does not appreciate arrogance. He can be selective/exclusive about students he lets into classes. Show up & do the work & be engaged and you'll be fine!
Schantz is passionate and kind. Neither of these things necessarily radiate from his lectures though, so if you do take him, talk with him after class and during office hours.
Really awesome lectures and great material chosen for course.

Prof schantz was great. I would definitely recommend his classes if you like to talk and think. he's old school about notes, handwritten only. He has a way of thinking about movies but isn't pretentious about it.
Good guy. Not the best lecturer but youll learn a lot

He was kinda boring and didn't really engage with the class, he just lectured. I nearly fell asleep every single lecture. He didn't seem to really care about clarifying confusing topics in his lectures. He's quick to respond to emails though. Out of the 3 profs that taught BIOL 215, he was my least favorite.

He gives incredibly boring and droning lectures, but his exams expect you to know every detail that he has given. Pay attention to the details of his lectures and you'll be alright, be prepared that he grades hard for a 200 level eco/evo class.

Has the ability to make you fall asleep no matter how interesting the material he claims to be. Also claims you don't need to memorize this and that and the midterm was all about memorizing. Basically you would fail if you don't remember every single thing in the slides.

I usually fell asleep during his monotone lectures. He seems only half alive when he comes to class and its as though he would rather be any place else. Once after lecture I literally vomited up some blood. Not sure it was his fault though.

He seems uninterested in teaching and drones on about dull things. It is sometimes difficult to tell whether he is still alive or simply some type of robot sent into class to bore people into submission.
very boring, lectures are very unclear, can't teach, zero enthusiasm, avoid at all costs.

Prof Price is such a nice guy. You can tell he cares but online class and technology isn't his strong suit. His final exam questions were pretty tricky and his assignments were difficult. He speaks clearly but he's a little boring to listen to.

This course would be interesting and easy to understand if 1) he talked slower 2) his organization of the lectures made any sense 3)if the material was more cohesive. He's a great guy and researcher, makes you interested untilyou realize you don't understand anything: a pretty bad prof.

His material is very straightforward and simple, so naturally it is hard to do poorly. He is very monotonous and can put himself to sleep sometimes. His lectures lack the energy that allows the students to engage with the material. Other than that, he is okay. His lectures notes are not thorough, but they are pulled straight from the textbook.

Out of the three professors for Biol 215 Prof. Price was the best one. His lectures were always very clear. He posts the slides before class and you can print them out and take notes on them. He speaks clearly and just at the right speed for you to jot stuff down. He is always open after class if you have any questions. Test questions were fair

Dr Dew had an interesting class about Industrial Revolution and Luddism, but if you want to have a class with little reading this is not it, take this class only if you're majoring in history and like to yap, it's about 25 students in the class so it'll be pretty easy to talk to people the class isn't hard but a lot of reading if not in History

Prof. Dew is a wonderful teacher - he is very busy, given that he's head of the History department, but I highly encourage anyone interested in hist of sci/med (especially medieval or premodern) to take a class with him! So knowledgeable, you will def walk away feeling like you learned a lot

Prof. Dew is a very knowledgeable and caring professor and his course content are extremely interesting. However, the ways he presents the material is not the most eye-catching way. Do take a class with him if you are slightly interested in history of science. Warning: He is very disorganized and sometimes does not reply to your emails.

Do not take this course! Does not care about students and sets unclear expectations. No matter how hard you try, you won't get more than B+ based on trivial matters. Prof. Dew made an interesting course dull and uninspired.. And the TAs obviously don't care. The conferences were also a waste of time, did not enrich understanding at all.

impossible to reach. this man does not care about his students and its a shame cause the course material is interesting. he's also super boringand disorganized in lectures. wouldnt take another course with him unless i wanted to feel neglected
lectures are a little boring but he is incredibly smart. anything your graded on is based on the weekly readings for your conferences

Prof. Dew teaches a really interesting course. Sometimes he can spend too much time on an introduction to the lecture or a specific slide which unfortunately means we often didn't get through the lessons he planned. He assigned some very cool readings and its not hard to do well in the course if you put in some effort!

Generally professor Dew seems to be passionate about history but much of the lecture time is him explaining the syllabus or going on tangents and then we run out of class time. Overall I did enjoy the class though and Professor Dew was very nice and was very knowledgeable.

Lectures are really hard to follow. He talks about the syllabus and course schedule a lot. The conference sheets he expected us to fill out were really vague. Overall not an enriching experience. Very meh.

Professor Dew is a really nice prof, gives a lot of readings but they were (mostly) good, I had the privilege to be in his conference section for a massive course and it was great, he always encouraged students to share their own knowledge from a diverse amount of fields, he was kind to allow us to write the term paper on ANY TOPIC within reason

His lectures are great. He's funny and has very useful slides. Make sure to take notes and you should be fine for the midterms/final. You can use the lecture recordings to go over a topic you didn't understand in class. The textbook is not entirely necessary, more like optional reading.

He made an otherwise boring class quite interesting! He really knows his stuff and we can tell he is passionate about what he teaches. He always answers questions really well so dont hesitate to ask! The midterm and final were really fair, however to do well you need to memorize a lot of facts found in the PowerPoints; its easy to overlook stuff!
No Comments
amazing prof!!

Grading criteria and instructions for assignments are often unclear and minimal, so you're really going in blind whenever you're writing something. It feels like the grading is ultimately subjective, so you're fully at the mercy of the reviewer (which is often a peer, who has no more understanding of the grading criteria than you do).

Cowan is a really good prof. PHYS186 is a super easy class (I have a science background though, so your mileage may vary). Has an online component (costs $30) which is really tedious but easy. In class assignments are marked out of 3 which sucks (average grade is 66%) but he drops the 2 lowest marks. Final paper is the usual fair.
Very good professor, passionate about the subject and very good class structure overall. You get the grade you worked for.
Overall solid professor, I found his lectures helpful and the problem sets and practice problems given were structured very similarly to the midterm and final which I appreciated.

Beware that the slides do not paint the full picture of what is being taught in a lecture and if you do not come to class you will have a surprise waiting for you at the midterm/final. I found him to be not be entirely clear in describing concepts, given they are very theoretical and abstract the language barrier does not help but he was engaging.

I don't think this professor is a very well-natured educator or person. Don't take one of his courses.

Very unfair final exams, one of which I felt was worthy of a complaint to the university. You'd be better off in really any other professor's class. 

It seems like he likes to hear himself talk - I wasn't impressed with his research, either.

Good and clear lecturer. He takes time from class to work through problems and is availbale for questions and feedback on the spot, making his lectures very worthwhile. What he teaches in class is what you will get on the tests. Very stylish quebecois man too.

Class content is very interesting; it blends theoretical models to applied econometrics. Beware because slides do not include everything tested on exams; some slides just have pictures with no explanations that WILL BE tested on exams. I recommend going to corresponding empirical paper, and noting explanations for these slides and learning by heart

Kind of dry and sometimes his explanations are not very easy to understand, but it's clear that he cares about the class and the material. Midterm is much easier than the final, as the material gets much more complex, so I'd focus on doing well on the midterm and get 100 on the problem sets to be in a good position.
The best economics teacher in mcgill

Prof is very knowledgeable and kind. If you do the problem sets and pay attention in class, you should be alright. Don't be afraid to ask questions as the material can sometimes be a bit convoluted, but he is good at clarifying when prompted.
He cares about his students and explained all the concepts clearly. Just do all the problem sets again before all the exams, then you will be getting As.

In my experience, his approach appeared insufficiently aligned with recent developments and practical applications in the field, particularly research from less prominent institutions. Some interactions with students seemed unsupportive, there appeared to be a strong emphasis on academic prestige over critical engagement with emerging scholarship.

Liked him as a person, not as a prof. Interrupts, esp his co-lecturer. I like that he challenges us but he was rude & patronizing to students w/ opinions different from his own. My impression was "this guy really likes the sound of his own voice". I came to like his chaotic & fiery personality later on- he means well and cares. But wouldn't retake.

Super unapproachable, but hes very smart and knowledgable regarding his domain. hes engaging and not boring, but hes also not afraid to rip you down for sharing any ideas that are either not fully articulated or not up to his standards, which will definietely lower the engagement in his classes/seminars making for an overall bad learning experience

Nico is an interesting guy, loads of energy which can sometimes be disruptive when the other profs are lecturing. His material in ENVR203 is all economics which is a bit outside the comfort zone of most enviro students and I don't think the concepts were super well explained to suit the audience.

Nico is one of the raddest profs at McGill. If you're taking him for ENVR400 he will most likely be co-teaching, which gives him extra freedom to go hard into his material and philosophical views, which diverge from mainstream academia and are extremely refreshing.

Nico is an amazing professor! I appreciate that he's not afraid to share his opinion and challenge students during discussions. He can seem intimidating but he's very kind and approachable. Lectures are hilarious and entertaining, and our seminars were the highlight of my week. :-) highly recommend!!

I still don't really know what this class was about. He's passionate about what he says in his lectures but the lectures are clearly more whatever he wants to talk about instead of whatever this class was supposed to be. The course is very disorganized, it felt like the teachers really didn't plan anything. Also theres 50ish page readings per class

Kosoy is interesting and captivating, he expects you to contribute knowledge from outside the class. However, we did not receive any graded feedback until after the final paper was submitted. He neglected to provide prompt feedback on our final essay outlines, as was discussed. Ultimately enjoyed his lectures but course was very disorganized.
A professor that is very knowledgeable, but helps students to reach their full potential!
Really passionate about his stuff!  Makes you think!

Prof Moitessier realizes that most people in org2 aren't actually interested by it, and so he makes the class fun by cracking as many jokes as possible while drawing mechanism after mechanism. His exams are similar to his notes and the problems he assigns. Also, listen closely in class because he always hints at what he'll ask on the exam!

Nic is a really nice guy but after having Pavelka for the first part of the course its like a total 180.
