Unclear with mechanisms and often skips steps, will go off on tangents in class and then go through stuff too quickly. Somehow he had a way of making the most simple things seem confusing. Cares about students, just not a great lecturer.
He is a really nice prof with clear slides. Really approachable after class for questions. He definitely knows his teaching stuff. Recommended.

Really nice guy, classes are really interesting and he has a really interesting perspective on stereochemistry and makes some quite funny and interesting remarks on the work on a lot of other chemists. The course is really quite difficult I think and the exams are fairly hard though but I would take it again. Also really likes hyperconjugation...

Very understanding and nice guy. Has very good lectures and wants all of his students to succeed. Don't make the same mistake I did and if you enroll in his class, GO! Much of this material is counter-intuitive without his help and some publications available online regarding the material are inaccurate
This guy is a total bro! He's really nice and more than willing to help.
He is just mad. Don't do a PhD there runaway!

Interesting lectures. He's a prof that really tells you what you need to know for the exam. He goes over hard concepts multiple times because he wants students to understand. His sample questions r very much like his actual exam questions, which are not super easy, but he'll make sure u'll be well prepared by clicker questions and sample sets.

Conducts a good lecture, loves to make sure the students understand the material. Has a great sense of humour and a superb understanding and passion for the subject. Wish all profs were like this, especially the math profs!
Best prof at Mcgill, well organized and helpfull, he really want his students to do well.  entertaining and he gives practice exam which are really helpful.

Lots of homework because of the class itself. Really nice person.
Does a bit of pep talk in class, but this is more than forgiveable.
One of the best professors at McGill!  Lectures are very interesting. Cares about students and always there to help!

She was so prepared for every lecture-- she would print out her organized notes for the class (thankfully she wouldn't make us print them out) and always engage us, often making popular music references which made the class more pleasant (even if I didn't get all the references). Overall, a great prof and I hope McGill respects her.

Really amazing prof! Engages students- my favourite part was when we had to sing in a group(it wasn't graded though for my class) Muar 201 was an easy class with really short assignments to hand in almost every week. Stress-free class.

Biamonte was funny and she is really nice! I feel like this class is an easy A for people who have a background in music. The first half of this class was easy, but for the second half, I felt she didn't do a good job at explaining the harder material. She wouldn't really teach and just gives a lot of examples. Assignments are easy to get A on tho!

Professor Biamonte makes the course lectures interesting by incorporating Pop Music examples into her lectures.  Also she gives you A LOT of examples in her slides.  All material and slides are posted online, and she'll tell you what material to expect on the quizzes.  She's also very approachable if you have questions - she wants you to succeed!

She is amazing and she is my fav in anthropology. The vibe of lecture was amazing. Everyone got pretty active. She is passionate about her own research in Andes. If you go to her office hour, she will explain as detailed as possible.
But I have to say she is a bit harsh on grading. She required a very clear explanation on every concept.

Prof. Couture is super smart and really well-spoken. She is also very approachable, which can be hard to say about many profs at McGill. I would say that the grading on the midterm and final was kinda harsh; luckily the journal marks came in clutch! Otherwise, would take again, she's really sweet!

Really sweet and caring prof who got to know all of us in her seminar well! There is a lot of reading but I found this content very interesting so I didn't mind. I also appreciated how she didn't force anyone to talk if they weren't comfortable even though it was a small class where participation counted.

Couture was knowledgeable, energetic, and funny. She gave many creative assignments (ie. watercolor journaling). Although the course covers a lot of material and she grades tough (but not unfairly), you will do fine so long as you keep up with the readings and read instructions carefully. Entertaining lectures, would recommend!

This was my first ANTH class and I found the grading very harsh. Lectures were straightforward and content-heavy, but the grading followed no scheme, and it was hard to understand what the expectations for each assignment were. Would not take again, too much effort for the grade received.
I love Prof. Couture and ANTH 359 is easily one of my favourite classes I have taken at McGill. She is a caring prof and is passionate about what she teaches. Assignments and expectations were clear.

hope you type fast! very interesting in her lecture, but her quiz and midterm are difficult in the short answer and essay questions. She expects you to use every author learned and to use them with intricate examples, as if you were writing an essay at home with your notes. She doesn't allow extra credit.

comments from a few years ago are wack she must have had some kind of spiritual awakening or identity crisis cause she is absolutely not scary or condescending at all never heard her yell once but to be fair i didnt go to a whole lot of classes super nice sunshiny lady lots of readings heavy on indepth ruins descriptions must skim assignments easy

I really wish I could've taken any other core course. Content is not only incredibly dense, but boring and dated. Nicole assigns several very long readings for each class, with equally as long questions assigned for discussion sections. Taking this class gave me a mid-degree crisis and question my interest in archaeology- I'm happy it's over :")

Prof Couture is interesting, helpful and knowledgeable about the subjects she teaches. I took her ANTH 210 last semester and ended up with a B- so I wasn't sure if to take her again but I did anyways. I'm happy I made that choice because her course on the Incas was one of the best Anthropology courses I ever had. Amazing lectures, meh readings!!
She is a great professor

I really enjoyed Nicole's class. Her lectures were interesting and guest speakers were great. Participation is graded so attendance is mandatory. Big evaluations consist of a quiz, a paper and final exam which were not super easy but not too challenging as well. Recommend taking her and I would take her again.

She's a nice person, but with one-sided arguments. You can read the textbook and pass. Don't skip even though everything is learned in the readings and her lectures hardly skim the surface of the course material. She takes attendance and knows everyone by name. She has guest lecturers often. Material is easy, but she's a strict grader on papers.

Nicole's lectures and interesting and the course covers a lot of intro information to help students get familiar with different groups they might be working with. There are often guest lecturers. You will definitely need to read the whole textbook for the exams but she allows a crib sheet.

Extremely fair marker (some may even say generous) and has clear expectations. Knowledgeable and approachable. Lectures are content heavy so she often doesn't get through them... Read the textbook cover to cover - sometimes she asks tedious questions.

Good class, but a little bit repetitive since we must take Public Social Services as well. Nicole keeps the class interesting by showing us films and getting guest speakers, but it's impossible to stay focused in her class for the whole 3 hours.
Good prof overall but TA marks the essays, beware!

Prof Billou facilitates student debate which is very fun, but ultimately leaves very little time where he actually lectures. This was frustrating when trying to study for the midterm, as I barely had any lecture notes or concepts defined. The group presentations were good, but overall I expected to hear more from a prof with such great experience.
Took this course in the fall of 2016, absolutely fantastic course! Heavy on the readings but all very relevant! Definitely would recommend it!

Best prof! So understanding and cares so much about her students and their learning. She's very accessible outside of class and really wants her students to succeed. There's so much to learn from the class too:) take her!!!!
Does not give much work and the work that is given is easy and straightforward. Lectures are mandatory, but worth it.

Nikki s a warm and thoughtful instructor who goes beyond academic support, creating a welcoming and supportive environment by sharing homemade gifts and baked snacks. She is transparent and open. She provides prompt and specific feedback, ensuring that we learn effectively. Her classes are highly engaging, filled with laughter.
Unclear success criteria, makes negative statements about the department and its students, poor teaching and management strategies.

Professor Provatas was an excellent professor who made the electromagnetism seem straightforward even to those like me, who have no prior physics experience. He gives many options for extra credit and writes tests that are very emblematic of the covered material and are possible to do well on without excessive studying.

Nik is simply exceptional, my personal favourite prof from the U0 Science year so far. Course is structured extremely well and coherently, unlike last semester. He explains concepts very well and posts solutions to ANS assignments, giving clarity on how to complete exam style questions.

PHYS102 is very much you trying to learn the content outside of class. Professor Provatas and the class TAs are available for questions, but most learning is done through going over class slides in your own time. However, this is made up for by the extremely lenient markscheme.
I really appreciated how hard work and participation was rewarded in his class.

Kind guy, but extremely weird assessments. Homework often had critical typos (cm instead of m) and the often midterm tested us on content we never covered whatsoever. It's a "fend for yourself" type of course and overall a huge mess compared to Phys 101. Saving grace is the extremely generous mark scheme for the course and lenient midterm grading.
Very good prof, definitely knows what he's talking about. Clear ppt

The course is very doable and the grading scheme gives lots of opportunities to improve and do well! However, Nik lectures in a way that makes you feel like he is talking down to you. He constantly compares the content you cover to the harder physics class and tries to over simplify all concepts (calling charges flavours etc).
wonderful professor, deeply caring, accommodating.

The way he engages the class and explains concepts had me hanging onto every word and I could tell that other students feel the same. His class promotes such a great learning environment and he honestly wants his students to succeed. He is so accessible and helpful outside of class and so kind.

Amazing professor. Always stays after lectures to answer questions and responds to emails. His lectures are clear and the questions in class help check our understanding. Overall very caring and fun professor!

You have to go to lectures in person as he doesn't post notes but the 5 assignments were super easy, the midterm and the final were fair. He even tells us what's going to be on the midterm and final in advance, so no surprises to be had. Lectures were clear and on point and he teaches stuff that's actually useful.
By far my favourite math prof at McGill. Lectures are clear and interesting. Fair tests and assignments. Would definitely take him again if I get the chance to.

Amazing prof, clear and interesting lectures! Doesn't post notes though, so go to class. 
Assignments and midterm were fair, but final exam was insanely long and tough.
Would definitely take another class with him, he's caring and makes sure his students understand the content.

ok so he doesn't record lectures, nor does he post notes. I also only showed up twice to his class during the whole semester. That being said, his assignmnets and exams are very easy. Despite not showing up and just asking chatgpt to explain the material briefly, I think I'm looking at an A, haven't taken the final yet! love him!!!!
BEST TEACHER EVER I LOVE HIM!!!! Class is super fun, he explains everything super clearly. Doesn't post the notes so you have to go to class but I liked that. Tests are very fair.

A fantastic class, a very caring prof. Assignments were quite hard and technical, but he was extremely accessible and ready to help. Lectures are great, he is an unparalleled artist - the shapes he can draw! The final was incredibly vicious in its difficulty, but his grading is some of the most generous around. I want to be him one day.

THE legend. he does NOT post notes , so it is necessary to attend. Knowing that, he makes his lectures as interesting as possible. Glad i did not drop it when i heard he does not post. cares for each one of the students  makes them feel comfortable and respected when asking questions in class.
 kamran teaches ? TAKE the class.
The legend

Prof. Kamran really made the class interesting. Exams were made very easy by giving us a very precise list of proofs to learn (proofs that we did in class). Assignments can take a bit of time but are interesting.
Caring professor who wants the best for his students. He puts a lot of thought into the presentation of the material in lectures which greatly helps students' understanding.

Very interesting lecturer. However, he is a bit unorganized, and is very vague about his exams. He was not very transparent about what material from the course you should know for exams, and he loves to ask questions about specific details that he maybe mentioned once. Also, make sure you over-explain for his written questions.

I took Nil for PARA 515: Water, Health & Sanitation. He's knowledgeable, accessible, and cares about the intersectional issues in water. He covers the introductory knowledge of multiple water-related topics, including environment, biology, public health, environmental justice, development, and public policy. Class discussions are thought-provoking.
he knows how to make science fun like dr dre
Good examples used in class. Responsive to questions.

Nice person, not a fun class experience. Despite being a HIST course it was mostly Hawaiian language, felt like an ENGL or LING class. Not bad on its own, but each paper had to use so many in class sources many not connecting to the assignment itself. Most writing was spent pulling one liners to hit this minimum, external research felt punished.

Arista is a great prof and super nice. My only qualm is that she takes an Indigenous pedagogy approach to teaching (class discussion, readings are stories, talks about personal experience), but doesn't apply this approach to papers. Her classes are super relaxed, but then the grading criteria are strict. You don't that much freedom to self-reflect.

Good professor! Sadly the class was split between her and another professor who significantly lacks teaching and people skills. I learnt a lot in her part of the course, and felt like I was learning Indigenous Hawaiian history in the most sensible and accurate way possible.

Whoops submitted too soon! :") My full comment was: "Noelani is an amazing person and an incredibly captivating lecturer. Helps students learn and grow beyond getting good grades. As an Indigenous student, I felt safe and had the ability to express myself in class."
Noelani is an amazing person and an incredibly captivating lecturer. Helps students learn and grow beyond getting good grades. As an Indigen

Nice and fun person, easy course content but one of the toughest grader ever met. Lost all marks for a question if one single unit is wrong. Got bad grade even though all other steps are correct and have shown clear understanding of the course. Feel less academic and pretty weird about the grading system.
Prepare to learn the most useful, practical and adequate knowledge in your chemical engineering curriculum

Treat this course as a litmus test. If you enjoy it, you will probably enjoy work as a professional chemical engineer, if not, like me, you future probably lies elsewhere. The course material is EASY, in fact, it is trivial compared to the courses you've had to complete to get here. Norman is nice but a hard grader.

Excellent prof.  One of the best I ever had.  Learned more about engineering from him than a half dozen of the other profs combined.  Has real experience, listen to him learn things you will need when you graduate, much more valuable than a lot of the other stuff you learn and never use after grad. Difficult, but in a good way.
Horrible
No Comments

Shes really nice and respectful. However, she moves so fast with the lecture slides and her lectures often have lots of information which makes it hard for someone to keep track of every single detail. We had 2 tests, the first one was pretty hard (class average 57%), while the second one was fairer (class average 67%) + a tough final project.

She is a really nice teacher but she goes way too fast during her lectures. It is a bit hard to keep up. However, her tests look like the exercises she gives in class, they are very fair. She was very flexible and listened to our needs.

She's only been here for a year and a half and teaches better than professors who have been teaching for 20+ years. Very thorough and takes the time to answer questions. Asks the class if everything is clear before moving on. One of the best professors at McGill. Most importantly, teaches with confidence.
She knows her stuff, honestly one of the best profs at McGill
knowledgeable and thorough

You can feel that Oana took the time to prepare for the lecture. Very helpful during office hours. The lectures aren't 100% (because OS is hard man) but they follow the textbook (OSTEP). Textbook+lecture make the course very clear. Strongly recommend. Assignments are slightly on the easy side but time consuming nevertheless.

accessible outside classes, very knowledgable, and willing to help you when you ask questions until you get it. However, the TAs were not so helpful & didn't had much office hours. The course 310 itself is not the easiest, so I think Oana might be the best choice you could get. The language used was C.Doable assignments, no midterm, harder final

Oana has great lectures that delve into enough detail about the tested materials. First assignment was very easy, but beware of the last two assignments as you will need more than a week to complete either comfortably. Answers every question respectfully, explains topics logically, probably one of the best CS profs at McGill.

Good prof. I waited until winter to take her over Muth. Her slides are clear and she has example problems to help understand and gets that OSes are hard. Only caveat is that the 3 assignments are coding one Shell in C, so if you fail one assignment you'll likely fail the other, and there aren't many ways to bring up your grade. No midterm.

Very good lecturer, she explains material methodically and gives examples/practice questions.

However, I took the class during the first semester they used the GitLab Autograder, which gave me a lot of issues. I am not very familiar with C so the assignments were painful and took dozens of hours each, and the optional C labs did not help much.
Very organised, had detailed schedule for each week and timeline was planned really well. No doubt, the class content is not an easy one but her explanations were pretty clear and pace was okay.

Dedicated, organized, lecture notes are AMAZING for visual students (a LOT of graphics and visual pictures). We had practice exercises for each week and others after each big section of the course. Definitely a great teacher for COMP 310. Would take again any time.

Professor Oana Balmau is a great teacher. She really cares about students and gives students meaningful feedback. She also listens to students' suggestions and make necessary changes to the course. Highly recommended to take her course.

She is a great teacher and teaches a great class. She makes you work the entire semester but it is relatively easy to obtain a good grade if you work for it. She goes out of her way to bring guest speakers so that you have a better idea of the industry. Really dedicated to her class and her field.
Do want to do it again!

She has a bad english which makes it hard to understand what she explains. However, she is very caring for her student. Go see her at office hours for questions and you'll understand much better. Slides are also useful. I had ECSE200 with her, get ready to put a lot of time and energy into this course.

She is a very nice person. I found her lectures very clear and useful; maybe sometimes her accent becomes a source of confusion. However, taking a course with prof. Liboiron means that you will have to work very hard.

She's a really lovely person and impressively understanding (I had to defer a couple of assignments and she gave me as much time as possible). Lectures can be a little confusing, but the slides help a lot. She's also very much willing to help you outside of class. A lot of profs could learn a few things from her.
bring coffee and try not to sleep

She is a very nice person. Sometimes lectures were unclear because there was so much material. You need to keep up with the material before class if you want the lectures to be helpful. Easy/Fair midterm.
make sure you understand the concepts in lectures, Make the best out of the quizzes. final can be tricky; her Office hours are tremendously helpful.

I took Introduction to Computer Engineering with her and I thought she was a very good professor. Slides were helpful, she was nice and explained things very clearly. However, her office hours aren't so useful, but she is definitely a good professor inside class. Midterm and final were both fair and not difficult at all.
She doesn't know how to express herself in English, she never learned to be a good teacher. However, slides are clear and useful.

I really enjoyed the course, however, the format with multiple lecturers was not a fan of. Most of the guest profs were unbearable to listen to, and the only thing that helped was the ability to set them to 2.5x speed on the recordings. Very easy to do well if you have taken a bio course and show some interest.

I loved Prof Hardt as a professor, but the course itself, PSYC 100, was not enjoyable at all. I am still surprised that I ended this class with a B considering we covered SO much material, and somehow got tested on every single bit of it on the final.

pure memorization, makes for a very possible A in the course. Not a fan of the multiple profs, but with recorded lectures and slides posted it is not hard to do well if you put time into the course. Dont even bother going to class, some of the profs are unbearable to listen to. Fine to take if you need to, but wouldnt consider a 'bird' course.

Professor Hardt is an excellent lecturer and truly seems engaged with the material. 20% of your grade comes from creating your own multiple choice questions for practice which I found interesting and an easy way to boost your grade!
if u are not smart when it comes to biology then the midterm will be difficult (it was for me). but is still a super easy course and an A is so doable if you do all the zaps and stuff
He seems a bit uninterested in teaching, but is a funny guy overall. Exams and assignments are very easy and class averages are always decently high.

The semester was incredibly chaotic: 10+ profs, TAs messing up MyCourses assignments, cancelled lectures, & classes switching between online & in person without clearly telling us which was which. I enjoyed the content, but we as students should have been better informed. Sidenote: I saw Hardt hit a student on the head after the midterm...

Hardt is a good teacher. He mostly just reads from the slides, so you could get away with not going to class and just learning the slides on your own. The only issue was how incredibly difficult he made the tests. Questions were very ambiguous and there seemed to be multiple right answers. DO NOT get lazy with the homeworks (the MCQ and zaps).

This dude is really funny but his lectures always somehow relate to male genitalia. This year there were like 12 profs teaching different units but the ones he taught as well as the tests he have given are fair and not hard. For PSYC 100 hes very chill. Be aware of neurology tho if u take this class and are an arts student who hates biology.

If you find his class topics interesting, you should take them. He is a very easy prof, and it is super simple to do well in his classes. HOWEVER, I find his classes incredibly boring. This is not to say he's bad, I just don't like his classes.

His lectures are very easy to follow, readings are provided but you won't be tested on them. Also, he's very accessible in office hours. But it's important to know that the exams are just brute memorization of the slides.

Absolutely awesome prof. So kind and genuinely interested in the material he teaches. Readings aren't necessary but can help with further understanding. MUST attend the lectures as the slides won't have the key words and phrasing you will need for midterms & final. Two 25% midterms & 50% final, beware they are essentially entirely memorization.

I think he's a great teacher, and the lectures were engaging. However, Geog216 will be an unnecessarily difficult elective if you aren't a geography major. Two midterms and a final for the entire grade (especially relative to other course options) makes it irrational to take with a ton of memorization and difficult exams to work on.

Such a kind and caring professor. He is so passionate about what he does and it really shows. Important to attend class as he does not put a lot of text on his slides and you will be tested on info mentioned during lecture, but his lectures were engaging and interesting, so I had no problem getting to his class despite it being at 8:30 3x a week.
Gives really good lectures and is so sweet! Super smart and understandable. He also has so much interest in what hes teaching, definately lecture heavy.

They did not test your general knowledge but very fine details however, once you get the hang of how they test it becomes easier. Professor Coomes was a great professor but could be out to lunch from time to time.

One of the best professors I've ever had. I genuinely learned so much. Granted, it definitely was not easy. Don't take the class if you aren't willing to attend every single one because that's what the tests were based on. I recommend copying down the lecture slides before each class so that you can focus on what he's saying during the lecture.

loved this prof! he was so sweet and gave such interesting anecdotes from his fieldwork. lectures on forest people and deforestation were so good! definitely not an easy class, but it's also not as challenging as people make it seem if you take GOOD notes in lectures. flashcards will be your best friend. don't even bother doing the readings.

Going to lecture and taking notes is crucial as his slides alone don't have a lot of the information, but the lectures are very engaging. The readings were not necessary and the tests should not be too difficult if you are good at memorization. He was also very helpful and willing to answer questions during office hours.

MUST ATTEND, review notes not slides. A large portion of his slides intentionally don't include the testable material. He admitted this when I spoke to him in office hours. His portion of 216 is designed to test on his words, the slides are a pseudo throw off which is kinda cringe. Despite that, great lecturer and very passionate about his stuff.

Im not sure what happened, but I took this class last year and it was terrible.  The class was not difficult, but lectures were painfully boring and uninformative. They were rambling, completely unorganized, etc. Impossible to figure out what we were expected to know.

Excellent teacher. Knowlegeable, clear, funny, organized. A model in the faculty, which is usually more about "being an academic and thinking for the sake of thinking" and not "teaching the rules and then get to academic concerns". Highly recommended.

Godin is one of the best in the Faculty.  Super-bilingue.  A practitioner for years, everything he says comes with a great example.  The man helped build Montreal into a city.  Great lectures, kind man.  Highly recommended.

Get a summary from a past year, he sticks to it very closely.  He is clear and answers all questions.  Sometimes he goes on environmentalist digressions.  He obviously cares about his subject and really wants students to learn and care too.  Be very structured and organized in your exams.
Excellent teacher! He is very knowledgeable. He makes the material interesting and fun to learn. Very clear and precise. Strongly recommended!
The best chem prof, have a great summer Dr. Sirjoosingh!
Best prof this year
Great Prof! I found her content videos were on the longer side, however she is a great lecturer and is great at answering questions
Best prof!
I loved my lectures with Prof. Sirjoosingh. She makes the content very clear and easy to understand, and her lectures are interactive and interesting.
she definitely wants you to do well and clearly puts effort into the concept videos. as long as you dont slack off too much you're gonna get an A
Amazing teacher

Pallavi is great. She teaches really difficult concepts (like intro to orgchem) very well. Honestly, I fell in love with chemistry thanks to Dr. Sirjoosingh! Best chem 110 prof, the model kits are so helpful and can be used on the exam. Please take her class!

An absolute gem of a professor. She's an amazing lecturer and breaks things down to reinforce concepts in class after watching videos beforehand, which helped so much. Will always ask if there are questions. It's super obvious she cares a lot about your learning and understanding. Midterms and final were very similar to the provided practice ones.

Somewhat monotone but one of the sweetest profs at Desautels. If you just get to know her and introduce yourself to her and go to office hours, it will go a really long way. Lots of readings but just put some effort and the course will be really easy.

prob the most boring class i've ever taken + makes us write papers or do projects far more complex than what we seem to do in class. Very tough grader, just wouldn't recommend in general. She is nice though but the topics she talks about are not interesting at all.

Here's the thing about Prof. Perez-Aleman. She is a sweet lady, and while the content can be a bit dry, she tries to engage the class with Slido and discussion groups. The most boring class I've ever taken at McGill. Avoid at all costs. Useless readings that you will have to write about in the final paper, including 10 of them, which have nothing to do with the actual paper itself. Everything is vague.

The quizzes are easy if you have done the readings and the group project is very interesting. However, her grading criteria are very unclear, especially for essays and projects. I expected more out of this class and I think the topics of conversation and readings could have been much more interesting. If I had to do it again, I'd take another prof.
Best class I've taken at McGill. Really interesting lectures and readings, only class I never wanted to skip even though it was at 8:30.

The most interesting course I have taken in Desautels so far. Prof P-Aleman is one of the nicest professors, really helpful especially in her office hours.  Very dynamic class with lots of participation.  She also cares about her students and wants to get to know them, known for giving good advice about what to do next for graduating students.
she puts you to sleep BUT attendance is graded so u have to go. Go to class, occasionally do the readings and read all the material prior to an exam

Amazing professor. Always available for you and helps you for your papers. She nearly sat with me and put my ideas on paper and I left with an outline of my paper. Prof "I know everything"

Great prof, really nice.  Lecture style course. Two assignments, one midterm and one final. You can expect a good grade if you attend the lectures, read the materials and ask questions. all the reviews are true and whoever said this class was easy to grade is not true. The material is too heavy for nonscience students and involves a lot of material for an introductory class. actually horrible. lecture slides are disorganized, lectures are boring (she just reads her messy slides).

just read the textbook and you'll be better off than going to class.

DONT TAKE THIS COURSE ANYMORE

this is the worst prof i've ever had. This class made me completely miserable, i've never hated something more in my life. She is so unclear and just reads off the slides and still makes no sense. The work she gives out are all over the place and do not make sense either. Never take this class

Prof très à l'écoute de ses élèves, s'assure toujours que les travaux/échéanciers conviennent à une plus grande majorité de gens, il est très prêt à s'adapter selon les besoins des élèves. Pas du tout sévère dans la correction.

I don't know how Prof. Brissette has poor ratings on rate my prof, he is such a passionate and caring teacher. Can't recommend Prof. Brissette and his class enough!
I liked this prof! his approach was different (data science and stuff) and he was kind. Going to office hours helped a lot.
Il vaut mieux prendre un cours de littérature québécoise avec Catherine Leclerc, Lauraunce Oullet-Tremblay ou Michel Biron.
Not a fan of this guy. A lot of people in the department aren't either. Steer clear.

One of the most knowledgeable people on the planet on this topic.

A must if you want to work in composites.

Lots of work and the reports are long, but the grading is more than fair. Most people get an A.
super disorganized and doesn't explain any reasoning or derivations behind formulas

Very chill dude, but the exams are very hard. Be prepared to see questions you have never seen before in the tests. Thus, don't leave it to the last minute to complete it!

A very respectful professor in MECH eng specialized in engineering materials. He gave very clear lectures on FEA, and if you are looking for a career in composite material, do research with him! He is one of the best professors in this field.

Very knowledgeable and caring professor but this course is a bit disorganized since he doesn't follow any particular textbook. You are left confused how all the topics tie in together until the end of the semester. Project really helped solidify how everything from the class relates to actual aero structures so good class overall.

Great professor, very receptive and accommodating to students; however, he is a tough grader on projects, so be ready to work for your grade. Pay attention to his hints in class, and schedule meetings.

Very approachable and receptive. Nice class atmosphere but you will have to study well because exams are not recycled. He actually tests your knowledge. That being said, midterms are fair. Gives problems for practice to guide you through midterms. Lectures can feel a bit long when he explains new concepts but that's applicable to any course.

Really nice guy who's super receptive to questions and comments in class. His midterms are very fair and he gives a lot of hints if you go to class. Only downside is he explains new concepts really fast and its hard to follow his logic sometimes

He has the three most important qualities of a good professor. He is very knowledgeable, he has a good teaching methodology, he cares about his students (very approachable). He implemented a project in this course for the first time this semester, it was fun and very interesting. Exams are fair, highly recommended.

I've heard such great things about him and he genuinely seems like a nice guy but MY GOD was this class boring. It was so boring I couldn't bring myself to care. Everytime i walked into lecture my sould died a little. Maybe it was me, who knows!
As long as you do the work assigned, the weekly readings, and engage in class, you will do well as he is big on creating a positive culture and community in the classroom

Hands down one of the best profs I've had at McGill. His lectures are engaging, meaningful, and enjoyable. Participation feels natural, and he creates a caring, comfortable space where even shy students feel confident. He fully remembers every student's name and discussion posts, making work feel purposeful. Not necessarily easy but very rewarding

Professor Khan is such a vibrant and caring professor, I cannot recommend him enough. Classes are discussion-based so participation is a must, but he creates such an open and comfortable space that even students as shy as I am can get an A. The work is not necessarily easy, but it's thoroughly enjoyable. Please take a class with him if you can!

Prof Khan was by far the best professor I've had at McGill. He truly knows how to teach, he makes his students feel valued in their participation. We would have to write commentary on the readings before each class and he would remember the commentaries of every single person in the class (we were around 20 people but still!) Truly caring and open.

An excellent professor who is extremely accessible and caring. Professor Khan will go out of his way to make his students comfortable. He provides an extremely safe space for discussions. He is extremely organized and coherent and I learnt a lot from it. I highly recommend this course.

Although the readings were long at times, all of the texts for this class blew my mind since they were so interesting. He was definitely approachable after class and during office hours! Would recommend his class.

Probably my favorite prof at McGill. He's definitely the most understanding + approachable prof I've ever had, and he really goes out of his way to get to know students and make sure they're comfortable. He does have more specific requirements for meetings and general conduct than most profs, but he's always very clear about his expectations.

He clearly cares about his students and is passionate about what he teaches. However, it was clear that he didn't know how to structure a 200 level course, each week was a new topic covered in little detail so it felt rushed. Also wasn't a big fan of the 40% group project since it was hard to relate it to the course material.

Pasha is funny, caring, and really knowledgeable. He encourages a friendly atmosphere, and employs some of the best teaching methods of any professor I've seen. If you're into Bollywood music, plastic fruit, and cats, his classes are for you (seriously, all of the above are regularly utilised in class). One of the best profs at McGill, for sure.

I was nervous that myfaith woulld be blown away but after the initial shock of the historical critical approaches of the course began to help me in deepening my awareness of both ancient andcontemporary hermeneutics. As a lecturer she is wonderfully skilled and very funny. Beware of the amount of time required to adequately read and write.

The teacher was understanding and caring. We had a small quiz or short essay due every week instead of midterm/final. The prof valued your opinion and critical reflection, so it was interesting to engage with the readings.

Dr Kirkpatrick is clearly an accomplished scholar who loves her subject. Her best teaching is done in dialogue so this is not a course of lectures for those who prefer to remain passive. There is a great deal of reading and writing to do so beware this is not a cake walk.

Professor Kirkpatrick has a wonderful presence in the classroom. She speaks with intention and strength, which makes sense considering that she is an ordained minister in the Anglican Church. As such, the course has a heavy Christian undertone. Unfortunately, on some days, she ended lecture extremely early, either out of apathy or lack of energy.

Definitely someone who enjoys the back and forth of discussion even during her lectures that are formal yet open too digressions if the right questions we posed.
She is not interested in riote memory recall but actually wants to know how and what you think of this or that author. She opened up a world I never knew existed.

Although the lectures are not considered 'required,' you must attend them for the overall course to make sense. This is not a professor who thinks she is filling empty vessels but rather one who actually listens to your questions and thrives on them as a way to teach. Now I want to take some more courses. Too bad this was my last term.

She is probably my favourite professor at McGill. An incredible source of knowledge, always interesting to hear lecture, and funny enough to keep your interest for the whole class. She is caring not only about her students but about the her work, which makes her care about your work too. She will push you but I love every class with PGK

Religious Studies is not my area let alone the Hebrew Bible so this was a bit of risk but what an amazing journey. Do not take this class if you do not like to read or give a critical analysis of certain important topics. Not a course if you are looking for answers! She actually cares about what you think or rather how you think. Excellent lectures

She is awesome! took this course on a whim and really enjoyed it! no midterm or final, just bi-weekly papers and many quizzes. The papers are great and you can freely critique the sources - no strict expectations. with the papers there are conferences which are quite relaxed as well. Overall, I learned a lot and enjoyed this class and both profs!

Not a course for people who do not like to read . Demands you bring a critical perspective to Biblical text. 
Lectures are not mandatory but they sure are interesting even though sometimes it feels like she just thought up the idea.
Always responded to my questions over the internet on the same day. Really liked the learning cells.

Notes are very hard to read and follow in class. Grading scheme options aren't forgiving for a first proof-based course and isn't very accommodating. I also took math242 another first proof-based course at the same time and didn't encounter those issues.

Amazing prof! Enthusiastic and passionate. Lectures are clear and easy to follow. Organized lecture notes and lecture recordings are posted on mycourses. Also, he provides 3 different grading schemes, which is quite generous

These reviews are not accurate. MATH 235 is the first proof-based math course and is known to be difficult, but Professor Allen presented it in the most approachable way possible. Compared to most math professors, he goes above and beyond to help all students succeed.
The high ratings for this class have nothing to do with the reality... avoid.

So much material and homework, and no crib sheet. Exams themselves were pretty straightforward if you remember the theorems proved in hws, just make sure to remember those, and it's an easy 80. Prof Allen teaches quite well, I rarely had questions during lectures or checked other resources. Just be prepared to do a lot of work for this class.

Bad handwriting so i had to take my own notes. Lecture notes and recordings posted, which makes up for it. Hard to keep up in class sometimes, material can take some time to digest, needed second or third looks after lots of lectures. 1st midterm was tough, but made the 2nd midterm and final a bit easier as a result (~ 60 average for both)

First time on RMP; he left such a good impression I wanted to share. He's funny, engaging, caring, approachable & passionate, fueling my passion of math! Definitely not an easy class but he manages to make some concepts easier to grasp. Very knowledgeable and his lectures are interesting. Beware of assignments and the exam which both are pretty painful. But overall a very good prof.

Very hard exams, 0 resemblance between practice exam and the actual one./
Really great at explaining the material!

By far the worst Prof I have had in my 4 years at McGill. Pompous, arrogant, acts as if this is the only class you are taking for the semester. Each assignment took me from 15-30 hours, and they are due once a week.

Dr. Clarke is an amazing supervisor. Would recommend 10/10!!!!! He is very supportive and cares about the work in the lab. There's an amazing team working for Dr. Clarke (look for Helena if she's still there). The rats are adorable.
LOVE THIS GUY 3 3 3

Made me cry. This class made me realize i haven't really understood any math concepts since high school. Makes u apply linear algebra in ways u never thought u could. Prof is so fun! I just really wish i understood and could be as excited as him

unhelpful and condescending

His assignments make me want to cry. Good prof otherwise.
This professor does not teach anything. Basically just reads off the slides. Assignments are just ridiculous and counterproductive for learning.

Clearly very smart and knowledgeable. Has an unfortunate habit of using jargon that is unfamiliar to most students, which can snowball to confusion. Otherwise, an interesting class with reasonable evaluations.

Paul is a good prof. It is totally understandable to have difficulties in this course if you're U1, as he skips over 200-level concepts regularly. This does not make him a bad prof imo. I hated his exams, the lecture is mostly based on computer models when i thought it would be based on biology and neuroscience. and I do not understand how he graded his multiple choice because i ended up with weird marks. Also, i normally do very well in class but I would get bad grades on the exams after thinking i understood the material

Most ridiculous class ive ever taken. His lectures are so confusing and the exams even more so. I probably failed my final yesterday. Insanely abstract explanations and exams, unless you like algorithmic metaphors for psychology (??????) DO NOT take this class

DO NOT take this class unless you want to have a daily mental breakdown. You don't take away anything from lectures, he goes over the slides too fast, very broad and confusing powerpoints... And the exams are not easy even if you study.

My favourite prof. He clings to a very clear and consistent logical and conceptual frame and he focuses on scientific methods to recreate
experiments for key findings. Once you understand you can excel in all his exams. Very low commitment if u like abstract thinking, and very enlightening if u want to go into research. Also very accommodating

This class is one of the hardest classes I've ever taken. A LOT of material and the content is certainely not easy to understand. Please stay away from this class whatever you do ESPECIALLY if you are a U1 student.

His lectures are all over the place. He also never answers emails, so it's next to impossible to get in contact with him. He purposefully made the final exam hard because he said the "average was too high," even though it was at a B-. Mind you, this is supposed to be a 200-level class. Just try to avoid taking his class as an elective!
Really good teacher. Resource Economics can't be more easier. Really good feedback, but he took a lot of time to corrected exams and paper.

A very knowledgeable professor.  Makes the topic interesting and explains any "grey" areas clearly and methodically.  If you like natural resource economics, you will greatly benefit from Prof. Thomassin.
Had him for resource economics. Never returns papers. Unavailable for consultation. Doesnt respond to emails.
knows what he is teaching
This is a show off!!!!

He is simply never available and unhelpful. Although the guy is nice, extremely knowledgeable, great lecturer,and has a world wide recognition, he just doesn't seem to care for is students! Probably to busy caring about his own career and research....
Good and knowledgable prof, but unavailable for consultation, poor thesis supervisor
recommend everyone to take his class. nice and a vry good professor
Very good in teaching and highly available for consultation
Very nice professor. His lectures are  clear and also entertaining.

He is a hilarious professor who cracks lots of dad jokes and tries (and somehow succeeds) to tie all the content back to him playing hockey. He is also very caring and will answer any questions you have during or after class and during office hours.
lots of dad jokes, I found him hilarious and super accessible as a professor in a large intro class

Professor Wiseman is my favorite professor when it comes to the CHEM 120 course. He really acknowledges the struggles of students and shows a want to make sure everyone succeeds. He also shares some funny stories which is greatly appreciated especially during early morning classes.

He always goes over a lot of things "you don't have to know." won't say that until after though, and I was always fully lost by that point. lectures are like storytime, you won't leave knowing more chemistry but you WILL leave entertained. Slides are literally unreadable, it's just badly photographed pencil on graph paper. Do the practice exams.

A kind guy who gets the job done. He'll explain things properly, go at a reasonable pace, and just create consistency in the classroom. He had the kind of lectures where you knew what was going to happen -- methodical, organized, and informative. Pleasant experience, and his midterm was very reasonable. Would 10/10 recommend this professor.

During our CHEM120 midterm prof Wiseman was my examiner. Halfway through the exam a protest smashed the windows to the building of the lecture hall we were in. Very good professor explains very well and is caring.Would recommend!
Explained things pretty well during lectures. Not too bad but not amazing either. Some lectures were a bit too long.

Dr. Wiseman is great! He cares about his students and is pretty accessible. My only issue was that the concept videos he posted were very long especially in comparison to the other instructors and his exams were a bit harder. Regardless, he is a great prof!

For your own sake don't take Yachnin. He uses AI for literally everything and didn't teach us anything throughout the entire semester. My favorite professor. He really encourages you to be engaged and I think he gives a lot of attention to your individual growth as a student. He is also always entertaining.

Paul is a great professor and made this course one of the best I have taken so far at McGill! The course is very presentation-based, and a mix of group projects and individual assignments. He is always available for extra help and super nice during office hours.

I was so excited when I read the course description as 'Theory of ENGL studies: philosophical approaches' but it felt like the furthest thing from it. He's nice and all but his lectures are not engaging and he has a weird obsession with AI and conversing with ChatGPT for EVERYTHING. It was the kind of class where people can get away with saying BS
Paul is awesome! Really caring and knowledgeable

I LOVE Paul, but it's worth noting I'm a drama major and a Shakespeare nerd. He is passionate about the subject and goes beyond the plays to consider historical and contemporary contexts. His lectures are informative but sometimes convoluted. If you're interested in Shakespeare, I highly recommend him!! But if you don't, he's probably not for you.

Professor Yachnin is one of the BEST professors at McGill. His Shakespeare classes are really informative, he himself is very knowledgeable and kind, and, above all, if you seek him out, he will train you to think in a new light about the subject matter, which will last with you. He is an inspirational guide for those studying the Bard!

Best teacher at McGill! He's so clever and the way he engages with ideas allows students to participate rather than him just telling you what to think. Really engaging professor who genuinely cares about his students.
Professor Yachnin is a great instructor, but a tough grader.

Professor Yachnin is charismatic and theatrical - however, his teaching methods end there. There is no real substance to his lectures. A waste of time.

I found his lectures a bit confusing at times but, that could just be my shortcomings. He is super kind and helpful, really wanting to see you succeed. His brain fascinates me and he is quite creative in his approach.

Professor Zanazanian is one of the kindest teachers I've ever had. He's so passionate and cares about his students. His instructions are clear, and if ever you're unsure about something, he's more than happy to help. He truly wants you to succeed!

I'm Paul's #1 fan. He's flexible and cares about student success. Him and his graders give very thorough feedback, so you'll leave EDES 334 with a really solid teaching rationale and set of lesson plans. Definitely the most enjoyable class I've taken at McGill!

One of the best edu profs at mcgill. His instructions are long and a bit unclear for assignments but just ask him and he's more than happy to explain. He genuinely cares about students and is passionate about teaching history. He and his ta's give so much helpful feedback, I would definitely recommend him! He's also pretty funny

Amazing! He is always eager to help students and to have intense discussions about the future of the Education system. I have taken him twice now and would gladly take him again if the possibility were presented to me. He is a fair marker with assignments relevant to your future as educators. WE LOVE PAUL.
I think he was fair in the way that he tested. Don't do the readings (yes they can be long and boring) but then you won't do well on the tests, however, he does make this clear.

This is a fair class. It is a very helpful class. He gives good feedback and he is there to help you when you want. Get ready to work in this class. Be productive and you will get that A. He does not want to fail you. He grades very fairly. The is nothing hidden. If you do a good job and deliver properly, you will get that A.

Great professor, and I think for the course material you couldn't do much better. His instructions are unclear and cloaked in too much fancy rhetoric. Paul does, however, give very detailed feedback.

It definitely isn't easy to get an A in Paul's class.  Paul Zanazanian, however, is a very nice and helpful teacher.  He will always make time for you whether you need to better understand a concept or want to look over a test. For his classes, you must be ready to read a lot !! Im sure Paul guy has good intentions, but his lectures are extremely disorganized, long and filled to the brim with questionably relevant information, the kind of stuff you stuff in your brain for an exam and forget afterwards for its lack of utility (just google it). Worst teacher I have had in my whole academic journey so far. He assumes the worst of his students and is always unorganized. This class is totally disorganized. Nothing is clear. If you ask the teacher for clarifications, he will not answer to your emails. If by chance he does, you can expect for a disrespectful answer. If there is one word I would describe after having him: SPEECHLESS. His lecture is very unorganized, slides loaded with words without any main ideas emphasized. Professor Chouha is a very professional, patient and super kind professor. I am so grateful to have him on this challenge subject: mathematics. He should do something else.

a little dry but the sweetest. he is everything to me
Prof Monaville is great, very clear grading and helpful feedback. Interesting courses and very accommodating to student needs!
Super kind and accessible to students. Lectures can be a bit dry, but he really wants you to succeed and the material isn't difficult to grasp. Highly recommend

In addition to being very intelligent in his field, Professor Monaville is one of the kindest professors I have had at McGill. He is accessible outside of class, is happy to clarify any confusing material, and clearly genuinely cares about his students and wants to see them succeed.

Super nice and caring guy. Interesting course content, doesn't ask too much of the students. 100% would recommend.

Professor Monaville is an overall good professor. Pedro was so sweet and clearly wants his students to succeed. He's a bit of a quiet speaker so in class you have to listen. Overall he clearly loves what he teaches and gives a lot of good insight to the topic. The class was not overly stressful and there was a good array of tests and papers, so there were lots of opportunities to succeed.

Peng Fei is a fair teacher. He admits mistakes when there are mistakes anywhere. I have great admiration for teachers who are not in over their heads.  The lectures in general are not very good, but he does show passion for maths. Overall, I think his class is worth taking if you are ready to put in the work.

i think it's important to take at least 1 (honours) class with him because he has a distinct working style: the math is condensed and sharp (but somehow, not terse). you have to infer what he is doing, beyond all the epsilon-delta manipulations, and this acts as a pretty good guiding exercise.

quizzes often reveal small illuminating tricks

His lecturing is basically impossible to understand — I learned all the course material from posted lecture notes, which were themselves typo-ridden. The assignments are good preparation for the exams but the quizzes are all significantly easier than any exam questions were.

THis rating is for math 254 but had to put into math 249 since they clearly didn't have that option. Good prof, he is kind. Hard to understand so was worried at first as how I would learn the material. Prof. Guan is clearly a genius, that being said this class was not well taught. Feels like you almost need Analysis 1 to enjoy this class. I didn't realize at the time, but this was one of the best courses I've taken at McGill
such a nice professor!! he really like students who attend class but dont listen to his proofs! they'll just confuse you. he is one of my favorite profs he genuinely wants his students to do well

Very knowledgeable and responsible.

Spent a whole class telling us we didn't deserve to be in his class. Also told us we didn't need access to solutions since we were honours students. Keeps complaining about physics students
Awesome prof
Prof. Oh is the best accounting prof at McGill. Clear expectations, come to class, practice his questions, getting an A is easy. Reachable and answers emails instantly, helpful during office hours.
He is amazing and truly cares about his students.

Professor Oh was truly good at teaching this class. Lectures and expectations were clear. This is by far the best accounting teacher at McGill, as he makes the slides digestible and provides the right resources for everyone to succeed. It was truly a pleasure to be his student throughout my time at McGill.

Great professor who will know the name of everyone in the class (if you attend I guess), so be nice with him! Do not sleep on the in-class exercises and the homework and you will do good; very straightforward expectations.
Easy class for accounting. He makes it as easy as possible. Great prof

I found this class to be fair. Midterms and Final are similar to his practice materials. It was annoying that there was a random group final paper worth 4.5% assigned at the end of the term. It was tedious work for something worth so little.
Very good teacher. He cares about his students and does his best to make sure everyone in his class understands the material.
Great guy that cares about his students. The class was pretty content heavy and as far as I know basically everyone got a B+. Exams and homework are fair. Coming to class is important.

Professor Oh is a great professor. 
Introduction to accounting is a difficult class but he makes sure that everyone understands.
He replies fast to emails and has many office hours (stays until 10pm during exam week)
To succeed in this class, I would recommend doing the in class exercises, quizzes, textbook problems, and see Professor Oh :)
Reoriented my life. This was more than a class! Thank you professor!

Truly, Louis was a great professor. He's passionate, and that makes him vocal. Some hate him for it; some truly respect him for it. I'm the latter. He makes you think and feel -- what else can you ask of a course? Take him for a new experience that you wont forget; avoid him if you want the same old, same old. ATTEND THE CLASS TO GET AN A.

Very biased, not even willing to consider other points of view. Assignment throughout the semester is very time consuming and grading criteria is not clear- incredibly subjective. Did not enjoy the lectures, though the guest speakers were very interesting.

Chauvin is the best. To do well in this class, you need to know how to self-reflect and really be introspective about how you perceive the world. If you can't do that, you're gonna have a bad time. Personally I loved the class and found it really easy. He's an amazing guy, great prof.

Would not recommend this professor.  Although the course material is interesting, he solely focuses it on environmental issues - simply showing videos and preaching his views. He is knowledgeable about the issues he raises, but leaves little room for you to develop and share your own (sometimes differing) opinions.

Very good prof. The course material is not the most interesting nor is it intellectually demanding. However, his method is refreshingly original. Just the type of class that these uptight rich kids at McGill need.
Nice person, Cares about the class... be prepared to drink the coolaid if you want a good grade.

Chauvin is a really great prof! By far the most down to earth prof I've met. Not afraid to say things that you wouldn't typically hear in a management class. He gives a different perspective. His class is not for everyone but I really enjoyed it.

I still disagree with almost everything he said, but I have respect for him. By far the most interesting prof in management. I leanred more from him than any other prof at McGill. Meditation, awkward one-on-one chats with other students to start every class, hippie rhetoric...needless to say, this class isn't for everyone. Cute, but as a class, it gets old quick.

Be sure to study well and know all of the concepts properly. The midterm took me by surprise and it wasn't good. But after that I went to most of the office hours to clarify stuff I didn't quite understand and Peter helped immensely that way. It went well for the final! Practice, practice and practice again!

Great prof, really cares about helping students and knows his material very well as he is a significant contributor to the field of control theory. Assignments were tough but the exams are quite straightforward. Overall interesting class and was able to appreciate the material, although it's more of a math class compared to the other EE courses.

He is a very nice and caring prof. The lecture slides posted are a bit heavy since it is mostly math, but they give you the important stuff. The midterm was really fair, final was harder... the assignments are tough! Overall good prof and don't be afraid to reach out to him! He will help you out.

Never take his class. He expects you to buy his 150$ textbook of which he is the sole author (#royalties) and refers to it 20 times/lecture while never going over any equation that you may need. The first assignment was absolutely impossible (no one in class managed to do it) and was due after the first lecture which barely covered anything useful
The assignment is toooooooo annoying!!!!!

The exams were easy, lectures however were hard to understand. Professor Caines spends a lot of time on theory and proofs which you will never use again. There are very few examples in the notes and the assignments are also theory-based. Overall, easy class.
Overall very good Prof! His lectures are a bit hard to understand but the exams were easy. The assignments were challenging but doable.

A nice and helpful person who communicates in an extremely confusing manner. But once you've understood the concepts through tutorials/online resources and go back to his slides, you will find them quite logical and helpful. I guess he just cannot see things from a novice's point of view. Fair quizzes and exams, not a tough grader.

good guy, not a good prof. however, the class was manageable. the first midterm had a 70% failure rate, it wasnt really difficult although a little long. the 2nd and the final were very easy. just do the assignments/old midterms. the notes are overly complicated and filled with notation. he gives you A LOT of old exams to practice which is fair.

I think he is a good person, who is not good at teaching. All of his notes are complicated and even harder than the midterms and finals. I think it is too hard to understand these examples when we learn something new. His midterms and final are pretty easy, some questions are just from the assignments. (I think quizes are harder than final/mid.)

If you do more than simply meet him on campus and have a quick chat (i.e. attend his classes for several years) you will come to view him for what he is: relatively good teacher, yet as as a program director and individual, a hypocritical man that keeps a grudge. The program's management under his watch should be more closely looked-into by McGill.
Met him at Macdonald Campus, where he is at the head of FMT program. Proactive, non-nonsense approach to teaching.
Great guy. This course is very easy, and everyone except one person got an A. Nonetheless it is a very interesting course and I learned a lot. It's his field, and it shows.

He made lectures interesting and he's approachable, but there were occasions where the material was presented confusingly. The textbook is really good though. There were eight homework sets total, which was a pretty manageable workload. Midterms were easier than assignments. The final exam was harder than expected, but graded decently leniently.

This guy is literally a gem. The class was not only really interesting (he's an expert on the subject) but it was super easy (everyone got an A except two bozos who didn't even attempt to turn in work). There's a lot of cool stuff in nanoscience that he goes over. Class is, for the most part, optional but most people go anyway cause it's so cool.
Grutter is friendly and a good lecturer, even though the material can be quite boring. The assignments are usually fairly easy and the midterm was fair, however beware of the Exam, it's a killer.
Very smart guy.  Friendly, but terribly disorganized.  I def. recommend him though.  Great course.  He's really into what he teaches....literally (his laptop is as 'nano' as you can get!)
Like 10 years ago..but the man was hot. And he still is. That dishevelled bed hair makes me crazy! Dang yo! That be a fine man! Smart too.

Interesting class but the tests are way too hard. Even if you study super hard there is no way you will do well, he asked questions about super minor details from the readings. No guidance on what to study for except to reread the course readings. He is definitely very passionate as an archaeologist but should not be a teacher.

actually impossible to study for his tests. not on big ideas, no guidance. you would need a photographic memory to get 100%... not sure how people enjoyed his class. He's a decent lecturer, but very full of himself and pretty boring.

Not a lot of info on slides and lectures aren't recorded, so attendance is mandatory. Tested on lots of details that do not seem obvious, which took some time to acclimate to. You can tell he's very passionate about the subject and a nice guy. No grades are posted on MyCourses.

Lessons are dense and slides are bare, so attend lectures. Readings are decently long, and many exam questions are based on seemingly irrelevant details. Professor Johansen never returned any grades on myCourses (due to the TA strike?), but I took the class S/U. Perhaps if I took the class for a letter grade my experience would have been different.

Professor Johansen's class was awesome! He is very passionate about his subject matter. The lectures are sometimes a little long, but the class projects are super interesting and enriching. There are no midterms or finals, just assignments for every project. Some are more time consuming than others, but totally worth it in my opinion.

His lectures were super dense and covered a lot very quickly. There are no lecture recordings and the slides are bare so you HAVE to come to class. That said, the exams are relatively easy and straightforward, focusing on large concepts instead of small factoids. Focus on the who what where when of each city and you'll be fine.

I know Peter in the capacity of a grad student, but I've experienced enough to say that he is an excellent professor and a very caring and involved mentor. He's passionate about his research and about teaching, and I guarantee you will learn a lot in his courses! Take him if you can!

Professor Johansen is a gem but there are certain things you should know before taking his courses (especially arch methods): there are many group projects, which are to be done out of class time, you must participate in field sessions and go to class to pass, but there are many interesting projects. He reads off notes for lectures (only thing).

I truly love Peter so much as a person, but this class was Very stressful for me. Two midterm exams, a 10-12 page research paper + quiz on the last day of class. So many readings to do and lectures are also very dense. A very knowledgeable and passionate prof, just keep in mind that this course is demanding and weigh your schedule accordingly

Professor Johansen is fantastic. He is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about his work and field and wants his students to be as well. Questions and comments are encouraged and although there is a lot to read and remember, he is very fair when it comes to grading.
Gggggggggggggg

he's amazing! he's fun and tries hard to make lectures engaging. however, there's a heavy amount of reading you need to do before class. although each reading counts for participation, it's a lot. there's also 3 essays throughout the semester, as well as a midterm and final (crib sheets allowed). his class is an easy A in my opinion, def recommend!
Literally one of the kindest and understanding prof ever. His lectures are amazing however it is reading heavy. No exams.
Group work based, the easiest soci prof at mcgill

He's honestly one of the best sociology teachers I have taken. While it was a bit reading heavy, the evaluations and weekly discussions were fair and also fairly graded. He also cares for his students and is very engaging in his lectures. If you can take him as a teacher, I would highly recommend

McMahan is a very understanding and caring professor. His class had a lot of mandatory readings and weekly group assignments, but if you had a decent group and stayed on top of the readings, an A is very achievable. The class was as much about sharing your knowledge and experience as learning new concepts.

Dr. McMahan is one of the kindest profs that I have had at McGill. His class did have a significant amount of reading assignments/group papers that needed to be regularly submitted, but the topics were generally interesting, and I learnt a lot very quickly. He is always willing to reexplain concepts and is understanding with extensions. 10/10!

Incredible prof, though beyond that he is a wonderful person and you can tell that he wants his students to succeed. The topics in class are super interesting too!
