His slides are very unclear, and when I asked him to clarify a concept, he mocked me, even though 5 of my friends had no idea what was the answer. The norm was to study for the final from another teacher's slides from the previous year... Class is useless.
No Comments

I absolutely loved Prof. Willson! I'm currently in my second semester of the program and she has been my favourite professor to have! She is very sweet and kind and her class is really interesting. I totally recommend her and would love to take another class with her.
I love her. She is THE MOST amazing professor.
I just love her

Fantastic professor! Definitely my favorite class. Prof. Willson is very clear and easy to reach, and she puts in effort to make sure students are actually learning. She asks for suggestions from students and then actually acts on them! Very engaging, knowledgeable, and passionate.

I enjoyed his lectures for the most part and he was very engaging. He didn't shy away from clarifying and reexplaining confusing concepts. He was also helpful after class. However, he could be condescending at times. The difficulty of the lectures vs the midterm also did not match up. Midterm was significantly more complex.

He seems like a nice guy, but I was not able to understand his concepts clearly from his lectures. It was confusing and the explanations were not easy to follow or clear. This was also for biol 304 but it wont let me write that.
From listening to his lectures, I'm not sure this professor would do well on his own exams.

Lectures are kindergarten level but the assignments and midterm make you think like you have never taken this class. Never goes over assignments nor practice problems. Takes 1 min to go over the equation and expects that we would automatically know how to solve problems. No office hours and doesn't answer emails.
His lectures are full of obvious things and are boring and dull. Not sure I learned anything I didn;t already know.
Not sure what the last reviewer was thinking?  Did we take the same class even?  I found this teacher confusing and kind of "full of himself".

I enjoyed the class, I liked that he gave anecdotes, however sometimes he spent too much time on them and they made him rush the actual content. Also not everything was super clear from the lectures and could definitely give more examples or highlight specific questions from the textbook. The tests were ok and the material was interesting

The assignments given didn't really reflect what was covered in class. His lectures are really easy to follow but in general there was a serious lack of practice material for his section. His questions are very particular and rely on specific definitions, which is easy to mess up. Read the textbook.
He pretends to know a lot, but I found his lectures shallow and overall, boring. He could use some lessons in teaching too. Expects a lot of students, but doesn't give them what they need to learn.
No office hours, doesn't answer emails, boring, does 30 slides in 1 hour, crams the 30 remaining slides in the last 10 minutes
Avoid if you can!

Overcomplicated the content in his lectures, assignments were confusing, and was barely any help during office hours. The textbook is the only reason I did well in the class, and maybe comp 208 so I could teach myself how to use matlab. None of the content is hard (stats or matlab), he just doesn't teach it so it's up to you.
I took CHEE204 with him during COVID. The Prof was professional, caring and knowledgeable. He introduced me to new ways of thinking and analysis. Forever grateful.

A lot of people did not appreciate professor Hill. However, even though he did over complicate some concepts once in a while, I believe that he was very helpful at his office hours and when you go see him after class. He is very helpful when you do so. His exams are also very fair despite the averages being low.

Prof. Hill is a good teacher but sometimes overcomplicates concepts. Pay attention in class for helpful assignment hints. The textbook explanations are clearer, so read and annotate it thoroughly, as exams are open-book. Focus on assignments and tutorials for exam prep, then lectures. MATLAB is used in a beginner-friendly way to reinforce concepts.

Great professor. The lectures tied closely to the textbook and often included helpful hints for solving the homework. The assignments required basic MATLAB, which professor Hill taught. He was responsive to questions and emails, flexible with deadlines, and the exams were fair, with questions drawn from the textbook, assignments, and lectures.

Prof Hill, along with Prof Rey, are the most knowledgeable profs I have encountered in the department of chemical engineering so far. Prof Hill's insights into the math and physics behind the very hard topics covered in this course are inspiring. Prof Hill will make you work to earn a good grade, but that's supposedly the purpose of grad studies.

Definitely more challenging than it should be in terms of in-class assessments. The last chapter was the most complicated as well as the MATLAB but all in all, it was a fair class. The textbook helped a lot.

I loved prof Hill and found his course really interesting. A lot of my classmates don't agree with me, but I find that he is very open to questions and helps a lot whenever someone is struggling. I understand more from the textbook though compared to his explanation.
Teacher somehow makes simple concepts complicated.

She is knowledgeable but the course sucked! Assignments are vague and poorly explained, feedback is harsh and specific. She made one point all semester and did not advance it or add any nuance or dimension. The content had no theoretical grounding. Frustrating waste of time.
Great professor!

Overall, the professor is super nice, understanding, and accommodating. The work she assigns isn't extreme for a university class. Her lectures are well done and she explains well, she also answers questions to the best of her ability. Though she's somewhat of a tough grader.

I have taken two classes with Dr. Bishop-Stall. She is extremely knowledgeable about her field of study (Indigenous art history, photography, and activism). She is also very kind and accessible. Be prepared, while her political views seemed to barely affect grading, her feedback often encourages students to subtly align their beliefs with her own.

Bishop-Stall is clearly passionate about her area of research. Decent lectures but an incredibly hard grader. I don't know if I'm just missing the mark in her course but I'm being heavily penalized on papers over things that would barely drop me grade points in other courses. Additionally, her feedback is consistently unclear. would not recommend.

"I am so in love with Sean Desjardins" -every girl who took this class. He's organized, clear, funny, super cute, has an adorable old dog, and overall just seems like a super knowledgable, decent guy. There's lots of material to study but the actual exam questions were a piece of cake. Just pay attention and study and you'll have a great time

Solid prof definitely. Very interesting material & he kept the lectures upbeat and moving quickly so even with ADHD I was able to focus w ease. Lots of memorization, but if you put work in you should do fine. Only complaint is that he said the final wasnt cumulative and then there were a couple questions from before the midterm but wasnt a big deal

a gem of a prof! clear lectures, very organized course materials, fair exams. also nice, cute, and helpful. midterm and final are mcq & short answer, lab quiz is mainly identifying fossil specimens. decent amount of course content but overall a really interesting class.

sean is amazing!!! everything is written on the slides so you can just listen (or not show up). i recommend going though!! a ton of memorization but super interesting content + he's a total babe so you rly can't beat that. also brought his dog to class one time which was amazing. gonna miss him next semester!!!
He's a good prof

This is was a very interesting class. The lecture slides were good always posted after class and the labs were super interesting not hard (identifying skulls, differences between anatomically modern humans and Neanderthals, etc..). This class is easy if you enjoy the subject. Grading: 1 midterm 30%, 2 pop quizzes 10%, lab quiz 20% and final 40%

Worst prof in the department. Unnecessarily hard and heavy assignments. Expect students to learn everything on their own. Lectures focused on tech ethics and philosophy while tests extremely heavy on technical coding. Inconsistent and harsh grading. Course not as useful as she claims. Overly proud attitude. Avoid at all costs.
Dr. Sieber was not my supervisor but still managed to provide feedback that was not constructive and unkind. Be prepared to go above and beyond to impress her.

I have learned more with Prof Sieber as my prof than all my other ENVR courses combined. Some expectations can be unclear (but they are always more than willing to help you get to where you wanna go) but if you put the work into the course, you will get earn the grade you want.

Entertaining when she speaks, but her feedback for assignments and presentations lack anything concrete or constructive, instead using words like "meh". She will grade you poorly simply for not liking your work instead of basing the grade on the criteria (which is often not clear to begin with).
Time consuming, but very rewarding experience.

She is the smartest person I have ever met. She's a little quirky, but it only makes her classes better. She's tough, makes you work really hard, but if you put in the work, you can do really well, and learn a great deal. None of her classes are easy tho
Very fablous. Not awkward. Doesn't have a funny voice. It's beautiful.

Her explanations were very engaging. She kept us interested by showing video clips, and by showing us her great sense of humour! I would be glad to have her a second time. Her speech is very clear and easy to understand, as are her explanations. Very intelligent person, yet very approachable as well.

a million times more interesting and engaging than the other 2 profs for the class (Hirose and Ellis). She  is insanely intelligent, and the material is hard, but she makes it sound pretty interesting. her voice might be weird, but at least i stayed awake.
Terrible teacher. Never buy book. Take it when she is on sabbatical. Prof. Sangupta is great.

I stopped attending after the 5th class and still managed to do reasonably well. If you are comfortable sacrificing participation marks and are confident writing strong essays under a three-hour exam format, you can probably get by. That said, I found his teaching style dull and he is dismissive when students expressed views he disagreed with.

Does not, unfortunately, respect or understand student accommodations. Often forgetful and will not remember stuff when it comes to administrative things. Does not allow laptop notes and is very lecture heavy (about 150 pages per week worth of readings)

Provost's "Special Friends" cold call system is daunting at first but in reality it ensures you are prepared for each class - which you NEED to be for his lectures and the final exam. He loves debate, discussion, and is open to hearing critique on readings if they are a little outdated. He is thoughtful and personable, would recommend!

He thinks he knows everything and others nothing. He does not share feedback on your work; if you have not written precisely what he believes is correct, you could expect to fail. He likes to degrade students. Grading is so arbitrary that only teachers' pets get a good grade.

I'm basing my review off of a really theoretical class, so it may not accurately reflect his teaching. That being said, he's the least approachable prof I've had. Rambles on and on about random stuff. I had no notes at the end of class and had to teach myself the subject. Unclear expectations and gets offended when you ask for clarification.
Provost <3

Could b because it was a seminar- sheer pleasure! Great class discussions, interesting readings. A breath of fresh air! Prof was kind to all (students and views) and very available. Does not shy away from pushing boundaries with provocative content and likes debate. Highly recommended!

Smart guy, expects a lot, which is good.  But he gives almost NO feedback on your work during the course of the semester, or in the final evaluation.  This is a necessary part of teaching, but with Provost, it's completely absent.
he picks his favorites early on, and if you are not one them, bad luck. in general, pretty snobbish attitude, and not very approachable. he thinks highly of his own ideas.
Not a bad professor but not a great one either.
Dr. Gruber is one of the most disorganized prof I have ever had!

Inspiring course masterfully organized by Dr Gruber. She's planned it so well and everything fits together perfectly. Awesome that there are guest lecturers because you get an expert presentation on new developments in their field. There was a lot of reading, hard quizzes, and a long final assignment but it's graded fairly so you can get an A.

So disorganized! She only lectured once or twice, the rest was guest lecturers. She is very informed on her topics & seems like a nice & highly intelligent person, but is simply a terrible teacher. The course was relatively easy, but that does not take away from the fact that we were given zERO grades or feedback before the course was already over.

An amazing, inspiring course. Dr. Gruber's lectures were easy to follow, but many of the guest speakers (most of the lectures are given by guest profs) were very fast-paced. Only a strong interest in psychiatry and neuro will get you through these, but all the assignments make a good grade more than achievable.
Class was unreasonably difficult. Unless you're coming into the semester with strong (like, very solid) grasp of the material, save your GPA. Your first term will probably have enough challenges
very good for strong students!!!!

You need to have an interest or background in neuroscience in order to understand a lot of the material, especially for the independent project. You are basically sent to the wolves on this one... The lecture is excruciating, Prof is uninteresting and a weak presenter. Also is extremely disorganized (gets dates mixed up, takes forever to grade)

you have to think, to do some independent research, to present. You can choose how much you invest, but if you take it seriously - it is great. I always wanted to give a presentation, and this course encouraged me to prepare it and present it. It was a good experience and I am more confident now.
excellent course!

Easy course load, having two written partner assignments, no readings, and a single 20-minute presentation but prof herself is a pain. Takes forever to grade, long-winded in all her questions and an awful presenter- the three straight hours of class are awful to sit through. Need to attend class for the peer presentation critiques (for credit)
Took for POLI 452 - great group project and really fun content. Prof is available outside class to help and has a lot of suggestions.

Prof. Brynen is an amazing professor. He remains available for students and provides great feedback and guidance. The game project is pretty content heavy and takes lots of time, I definitely recommend taking this class as it is a interesting class with a unique project but would advise avoiding taking it if you have another heavy content class.

Conflict simulation is one of the most interesting and unusual classes I've ever taken at Mcgill, and perhaps the only one where I felt was really having to apply my poli sci learning to practical challenges. The game project is group work, which I usually don't like, but my team was great. Make sure you start working on your project early, though!

An amazing prof, one of my favs @McGill. So enthusiastic and engaging in lectures even if 1h30, and also very talkative in OH. Very clear on what he expects from students, but the multiple choice can still be difficult. Has it so the paper(s) are worth more than the multi c you can still do well. Class was so enjoyable.
I enjoyed this class, he's super knowledgeable and handled the content with the care it needed. Grading was fair on the midterms (just testing if you did the readings), and generous on the paper.

I really appreciate his efforts to be fair and objective with so much going on in the Middle East. Struggled a bit with the first midterm (there's a lot to read and remember) but second one was interesting, and the research paper topic I chose (Arab youth politics) was really interesting. Very helpful outside class.

Professor Brynen sets you up for success. He makes sure that your chances are the highest they can be. He knows how an in person exam is stressing and how it affects your answers. That's why he wants to make sure you get as much time and stress-free environment for your exam making it take home. 

He's the best there is.

Professor Brynen is knowledgeable and engaging, but the workload is heavy. Lots of readings that are crucial for the exams. Attend class, use the textbook, and try Unstuckstudy AI - it really helped me stay on top of the material.
standards too high.

Prof Brynen is incredible. Hes passionate about what he teaches and is very smart. He talks a lot & fast so its hard to keep up but what he says is interesting. In my experience, its hard to remember all the info for the tests but try to make comprehensive notes for each topic. Overall tho hes super sweet and the class is definitely worth effort.

Honestly, take biochemistry with him at MAC instead of taking the biochemistry equivalent at downtown. He's an amazing teacher, & his exams are really easy (even though the class average was a B). If you're in any intensive science program (biology/pharmacology/physiology, etc.) , you'll finish his exams in 30 min while easily Acing it.
Overall one of the best teachers! Clear explanations, witty humorous response, great lectures. Highly recommended!

Reza is a nice professor who really wants you to succeed. He'll answer as many questions as you have, and keep trying to help you understand. His lectures are fun and his in-class review questions help you gauge if you're on top of the material. His exam was very fair. Doing his suggested problems helps in exam preparation.
Funny, interesting and extremely helpful! One of the best profs out there !
Reza is the man!! I you have him as a teacher, you are one lucky person! Easy exams..questions are straight forward and clear! GOOOO REZA! :D:D:D

I loved this man! He was so sincerely kind and just made you happy! He was a very nice person and was very fair when grading and aking questions on an exam. None of these "all of the above", "none of the above" guys. Straight forward questions, nothing twisted or really tricky

He was a great teacher. Gave example questions and extremely helpful if you needed it. Always answered emails and would forward good questions to the whole class. He really wanted his students to understand the material!
Definately a great teacher. He really wants you to do well and really cares. He takes the time to reply to everyone. One of the best profs i've had so far.

Dr. Nafziger is an amazing lecturer who genuinely cares about her students. Her content matters and is relevant to current global issues. She is educated in her field with great compassion in understanding what her students need. Dr. Nafziger is collaborative and I really enjoyed her class. My experience at McGill has been better with her guidance.

Professor Nafziger is an excellent teacher. She is caring, compassionate, and wants the best for her students. She is knowledgeable about the subjects she teaches and facilitates peer-based learning. Her classes were interesting and engaging, and I highly enjoyed the class. The content made me think deeply and critically, which I appreciated!

A solid mid prof. She's fairly flexible with due dates but lacks organization which proved incredibly frustrating for my cohort. She once gave us 60 pages of readings to complete less than 24 hours before class.... The course is participation-heavy and the readings are often a little dry, but it's easy to get good marks.

Professor Nafziger is one of the most understanding and caring professors. I went through some hard times this semester and out of all my professors she was the most concerned with my well-being and most willing to work with me to accommodate my needs. She cares about her students as people, not just students.

She's a good professor. I was more than dissatisfied with the organization of the class. With no warning, the grading criteria of a project was changed a few days before its due date and the grading was strict. All assignments are to be handed through MyCourses, but with all the mislabeled assignment submission boxes, you eventually get lost.
I really like this prof and would def take again !

i love this professor, she is so knowledgeable and understanding. Her presentations are interesting and engaging. We frequently have class/group discussions and reflections. 
We had to turn in a discussion post every week, but it was barely any work. 
I would def take again !
Good teacher all in all. The only thing that could be better is her input in discussions instead of letting just the students speak.

Dr. Nafziger is no stranger to equity in education. However, you will have to read the material and expect that she will not do an in depth discussion of those materials and will instead ask you about experiences and how you relate to the reading. I wish she would lecture and explain how each of the issues can be resolved in the classroom.
such a boring class- hard and exhausting course-

if you don't want to get bad mark, don't take this class he is a tough marker. he doesn't teach well. he expects you alot. and if you ask him a question. he doesn't know the answer , he never say he doesn't know. he talks about other things that is irrelevant to the question.
Very enjoyable class and knowledgeable professor.
Aerospace materials rock!
Excellent!
Super awesome!
100% the worst prof in the country if not in the continent.
No doubt the worst in the universe. A true shame for the material Dept.
Very mean and unknowledgeable! He is definitely in the wrong place.
I wish Clarity & Helpfulness in this website had minus scores as well. If it was the case his clarity would be -2 and Helpfulness -15 honestly. He is lost big time.

Great experience taking WCOM 250 with him. Kind, caring, and answers emails quick. Attendance is mandatory and lectures are a bit boring. Lots of paper to submit, but his grading criteria is simple and doing well is easy because he gives detailed feedback for each assignment. Would definitely recommend the class!
lots of helpful feedback provided, including both audio and written feedback. learned a lot from this class! :)

if you have the chance to take Richard Cooper, do it. The best experience I had in a class so far at McGill. very knowledgable and understanding teacher. Grades very nicely. Learned a lot about english grammar and writing.

Even if you have a lot of writing experience, CEAP 250 is a great way to improve your grammar and writing skills. Prof. Cooper gave really detailed written and audio feedback for each paper and assignment, and grading was very positive. He was also very understanding in regards to deadlines, and helped give me multiple extensions. Great prof!

Professor Cooper is one of the most caring profs ever. He makes writing fun and looks out for his students. He is very lenient with deadlines and always gives you thorough feedback to improve your paper. Highly recommend!!!

Prof Cooper cares about his students. He reminds you of the deadlines, which reminds me of high school. He gave audio-recorded feedback for most of the projects. Make sure to read the textbook as his test questions come from the textbook exercises.

Prof Cooper was my saving grace this semester. He was always lenient with deadlines, and did his best to make sure every student was succeeding. If you do all the changes/corrections he suggests and actually put in some effort, 2nd drafts will all get 90%+. This class is an easy A if you put in the time to write quality stuff. Strongly recommend!

Actually one of the best profs I've had over three years of uni. Fight to take his class if you have to. A fair grader, but he goes over every point he's looking for in class before assigning each paper (before each test too). Also very considerate of students' workload. Class size is very small so be sure to show up and participate!
He is one of the best profs I have had at McGill!

Prof. Cooper was amazing for CEAP250. Taking this class as a science student interested in academic writing allowed for me to develop my skills. The learning curve is steep if you aren't a great writer, but Cooper will get you into shape in no time. He's super caring and very clear.

Lovely man. One can tell that he genuinely cares about the class. He is constant trying new things and adopting feedback. I have no idea what a tort is though. He also struggles with the concept of a class being one hour and twenty minutes, usually leaving 95 percent of the content for the last five minutes of the lecture.

Prof Janda gives a ton of readings, but he's open to student feedback so he's been cutting them down. He has a very philosophical way of teaching so he often goes off about stuff that's irrelevant for exams/papers. He's known for his long exams so pre-write your essay questions (especially for the final exam). He does explain torts well tho

I don't think you could pay me to take another Janda class. He assumes students have prior knowledge and fixates on very specific, niche things (like the reasoning of one judge's dissent) for the first hour and 10 mins of the class, and tries to cram actual content (related to the lengthy readings he assigns) in the last 5 mins.Very kind man though

Professor Janda is an amazing teacher who genuinely cares. He spends a lot of time on the reasoning behind judges' decisions, which is great if you appreciate nuance. There's a lot of reading, but he hammers in the key points. He's super approachable and gave out a super interesting memo assignment which was a nice practical addition go the class.

I could not name a course in which I've learned so little. It was so bad, I would even say I unlearned business law. 

Aspiring business lawyer? Run for your life!

Professor Janda is an amazing professor. Not only is he one of the most brilliant professors at the law faculty, he is one of the most caring ones. He will do his utmost to accommodate students and try to understand their difficulties. He is hard to reach at times though. Highly recommend for anyone who really wants to learn!

Basically had to teach myself torts. His grading criteria are super confusing and contradictory. Ghosts students. Assigns grades randomly if you ask me (B/B-). Lectures unclear. Always behind. Exams are too long (PRE-WRITE YOUR FINAL ESSAY). Still waiting feedback on my midterm and I've already passed the class...

Janda will ramble about the images on his Prezi and the German Civil Code for 1h15, realize there are 5 mins left and attempt (and fail) to cover the readings for the class in that time. Asks us to critique the law before teaching it to us. Terrible prof, but great guy who advocates for students' rights. Also, you will get a B or a B-.

- Professor is very difficult to access outside classroom. - ghost me for several months without giving me feedback of final exam. - boring lectures. - good for having a casual conversation... but no more. - living proof that to be a professor at McGill you do not need to know how to teach.. you just need good connections and a respectable CV.

Disregard the comments that Janda is an obtuse intellectual out of sync with the real world. I'll tell you a very different story. Janda is an exceptional teacher and mentor. He cares deeply about the success of his students and possesses extraordinary insight. Transformative. Relevant. Enlightening.

If I could take every single one of my psych classes with Richard Koestner I would. He is genuinely one of the best psych profs at McGill. Koestner is so funny and makes such a connection with students and the content he teaches might be the most essential and insightful things you will ever learn.
Very good teacher. Will curve if he feel that the exam was too hard.

If you asked a researcher in this field to take the exam I think they would score at most average. His exams feel like a test of prof's own opinions and not reflecting understanding of academic topics. The amount of readings is also a lot, 3 books around 500pages. Take the exam and get tested on his anecdotes and book one-liners.

The exams are super hard, and the grading scale is structured so that success is almost impossible. He's extremely disorganized, and the lectures rarely seem to connect to each other. He is funny though, if you can stay awake.

One of the most interesting and engaging classes I've taken, with a passionate and knowledgeable professor! I truly enjoyed each lecture I attended, and because the classes are recorded, on days when I couldn't make it to class I listened to his lecture as a podcast which was great. The exams are not overly difficult, lots of material but fair.

This has been by the far, the most important and useful class I've taken  at McGill. Koestner makes this class fun and interesting with his own personal stories and you can tell how much passion he has for what he teaches. We were only graded by two exams, but they weren't difficult and Koestner was open to getting rid of questions that were hard.

This is exactly the kind of class I was expecting when I decided to major in psychology. I found the material extremely interesting and eye opening, it really helps you learn about yourself and your close ones. The required reading wasn't a real textbook but I found that to be even better, everyone should read this book. Exams were hard but curved.

a fairly nice prof, listened to student feedback and the option to shift exam weights and retake midterm were kind. but the exams were ridiculous, questions on the profs tangents, the "textbook" is not in a textbook format, so its hard to review, presents theories that use similar terminology with vastly different definitions, overall often unclear

He is extremely sweet and definitely cares about what he teaches, but the grading and the actual lectures are so unfair. This sem, fall 2025, it was a 50% midterm and a 50% final or retaking the midterm during the final. I'm not gonna lie. I have struggled so bad with this class.

Most disorganized, confusing, unfair course I've taken. He lacked clarity, structure, and basic professionalism. Exams were disconnected from lectures, questions felt arbitrary, and feedback was dismissed. An ineffective, frustrating, and unacceptable experience. The department needs to seriously reevaluate this course. Students deserve better.

Best prof one could ever have in chem eng! Always smiling and so chill. His tests were extremely easy and he used to give lots of partial marks. Just solve the textbook problems he recommends and youll definitely ace them. The simulations though were graded harshly by TAs (which is why I got an A-) but generally the course is an easy A.
Would take again, one of the nicest guys of the engineering department.

Wow best prof ever. His tests were so easy, you just had to understand the material and you were good. Loved him. He always made sure our exams were not with other exams and would change the date if we asked him. The material isn't very exciting.

Great prof!! His lectures were well organized and he did a recap at the beginning of the lecture, so it's really clear and easy to follow. His lectures were clearly linked to the textbook and he suggested certain questions from the textbook for practice. His tests were fair and really similar to the practice exam.

Prof. Leask is probably the best prof one can ever get in chem eng. Lectures are super clear: he follows the textbook closely and recaps what he taught in the previous lecture every time so you know what you are doing. Just by using the class notes, you will be ready for his exams certainly. As of his exams, they are very fair. Easy A in my view.

Best professor at McGill. He is clear, understandable, knowledgeable and truly loves teaching. Not of his exams are impossible--just study your butt off, go to his office hours every week, read the book and you'll do well.

He's the best professor in chemical engineering so far. I'm even thinking that's he's the only good guy in the whole crew! Final was IMPOSSIBLE, so get all your marks from the quizzes, midterm, and lab reports! DO NOT DEPEND ON THE FINAL!

The best prof in McGill. Really helpful. you can ask him whatever u want, n he will answer more than what u ask. his exams are really hard though, especially the final; its impossible. try to get as much as u can from the midterms. an interesting course.
Great prof, final was impossible, felt like i was in the wrong room
great adviser and really helped us understand the material...

Professor Preuss is an amazing professor. Although his lectures are very long and he has readings attached to every lecture which can be lengthy (8-20 pgs), he explains the concepts that need to be explained in class and is happy to answer any questions. His grading can be very tough and he is very picky in what to look for. There is a lot to read.
She's an excellent teacher. The class is not difficult at all if you attend classes and do the practice exams. She doesn't post enough exercises to prepare for the exams though.

The professor tends to make the coursework more challenging towards the end of the semester if the class average is high. Feedback is often slow. Instructions not clear on certain hws (and this supposed to be a math course).
Worst experience ever

Prof. Hariss is very knowledgable and passionate about the course and clearly communicates that with students. The slides are concise and easy to understand which helps with studying! Although participation doesn't count, she often encourages it and seems to be a bit bothered when students don't speak up (this doesn't affect your grade though).

Great professor teaching a very interesting course. Slides are clear, simple and concise while the material is well explained. Exams reflect well what has been covered as well as the given practice questions.
One of the most accommodating professors

I thoroughly enjoyed the lectures in Rim's OM analytics course! I especially appreciated learning about so many different applications of the OM/OR/analytics content that I was introduced to in other classes. HW was fun too. Highly recommend the class!! (But, It would be a tough course if you have a weak coding or OR/OM background)
Genuinely cares about her students and is very highly knowledgeable in the subject she studies. Would highly recommend taking a class with her if you have the opportunity to.
she is such a caring prof!
OM prof who doesn't know what JIT is..
Very good course.
unhelpful, not supportive,she has poor communication skills makes comments that are either very generalized or very picky, or irrelevant;  criticizes your work all the time.

Jukier is knowledgeable and usually interesting, but has no notion of pedagogy. Her lectures are fine, but whenever she tries "something different", it's awful. The purpose of her exams is not to evaluate students but rather to show how clever she is. She looks like she understands French, but she really doesn't. I would take her as last recourse.

Prof. Jukier is great! She is extremely well-organized and provides all of the materials to understand first year contracts completely (she also gives much less readings than the other profs). HOWEVER, her exams are way left-field! You can be extremely prepared, you will not see it coming! Tough grader, but gives good feedback. PREPARE FOR CLASSES.

This professor is purposely confusing. She has derived her own understanding of contract law which detracts from the ""standards". Classes are confusing, and run off on tangents, where concepts presented have little to no applicability in principle. Nice person, but certainly more interested in having her ideas affirmed as opposed to teaching.

Professor Jukier is a fantastic lecturer: clear, organized, dynamic, funny, and innovative. A tough marker with specific expectations, she cares deeply about students.

She's not the worst, but I would hesitate before taking a class with her in the future. Learning objectives not aligned with what was actually taught, and she seemed to give attention in class discussions to a select few in the class at the expense of others. Generally not very approachable, unfortunately.
Not horrible, but not a great intro to the study of law. Confusing to follow at times, and not very approachable.
She is a bit boring, but explains things clearly and exams are easy.

Prof Bagot is incredibly knowledgable and passionate about her subject. Unfortunately her lecture is so incredibly boring. The content is super dense and she goes over it very quickly. It's not that hard to do well but its absolutely brutal to get through.

I stopped going to this class because of how boring it was. Professor just reads off the slides with a monotone voice and looks bored herself. The content could be so interesting if taught by someone else.

I do believe that the content of the course is interesting, given that it's a relatively new field it can be a bit vague and lacking boundaries at times. But the way its taught by the professor makes it SO boring. I heard it used to be a discussion based class, now she just puts quotes from scientific papers and reads off the slides

Dr Bagot is a great teacher. Her slides are nice and clear, and she explains the material in a highly comprehensible manner. She is very approachable and is always available to answer questions after class. I found her course extremely interesting, and not too challenging (as a neuroscience student).

This course has some really interesting content, so its a shame that Professor Bagot doesnt really breathe any life into it. Classes mostly consist of her reading off her slides and adding small explanations here and there. All textbook content is testable, so its best to read chapters each week.

Dr. Bagot reads off her lectures, which is quite boring. All the content is in the textbook so no need to go to class. Really nice and flexible grading scheme and the content is very interesting (makes up for her boring lectures). The only thing keeping me awake is her Australian accent :)

The multiple choice questions were tough but definitely doable in my opinion. I thought he lectured clearly and I didn't find you really needed to know anything other than what was on the slides which was nice.

The MC questions in his exams are so tough. The short answer part is good, but the final is only MC questions which makes it impossible. He does ABCDE with multi-select. Doesn't give many practice questions and no flexible grading like in other psych classes. Final is cumulative for all lectures and all readings, all content distributed equally.

Seemed like a nice guy, but lectures were boring. I have no clue how this is a PSYC class, I felt like a comp sci student. If you're into AI, artificial neural networks, algorithms, etc., this might be the class for you. If not, run. I didn't like the exams and lost respect when he didn't show up to the final!
Charming and helpful prof, but course content is quite difficult.
Save yourself the pain. Don't take it.
The hardest class ever. This teacher gave impossible assignments and incorrect solutions. He made us buy his notes from him at high cost. Don't ever take his course.
OMG! This class rocks.

This class is for people who actually want to learn about ore body modelling. Don't take this as a random elective, dont take this because it fits into your schedule, don't take it because it sounds fun. Take it because the class is unreasonably interesting, and the applications make you all giddy. Seriously, you will fail, and no one will pity you
Suitable for students with strong maths !
Very helpful course in Mining Planning and Optimization
OK - getting lazy. seems to rest on his laurels.
An excellent and enlightening course

His section is pretty much all over the place since it goes over most of the systems in animals and might seem vague at first since he only has one lecture per system/concept. However, he does his best to explain everything. Going over his slides before and after the class helps a lot. His questions are very fair and easy.

Engaging, clear in the lectures, and he's very kind and you can tell he cares about students. Inspirational as well, makes me want to learn more and his passion for what he does shows through! would 100% take more classes with him.
His online lectures are long and sometimes boring to listen to but his quizzes and assignments were an easy 90-100%. Answers can be extracted right from your notes/ lecture slides in BIOL205.

Prof. Barrett's lectures are a little long and strains my attention span but his tests are an easy 100% especially online. BIOL205 has lots of content but it's rather repetitive and manageable. Prof. Barrett gives clear explanations and his lectures are easy to follow.

450 by Rui is Microeconomics in Macro's clothing. But I guess that's just how the modern macroeconomic theory works. So polish up your mathematics and micro theory. His lectures are a compact summary of Williamson's macroeconomics: in fact, quite a bit of his questions (HW and Exams) were straight from Williamson.

His lectures are boring and low-paced compared to the challenging and math heavy content he tests on the midterm and the exam. Going for office hours will be very unhelpful because he always replies with another question, to get you to try to figure it out. The exam was incredibly tough; there was so much math that was never explained.
The class is hard but prof Castro explained the material really well.
exams are ok but needs to go over the notes and lectures carefully. overall he explains the contents well.

This course is definitely not easy, but the grading is kind of easy. Castro is a good professor and always present the lecture in a clear, organized way. Be sure to ask him anything if you get lost in the material.
very rude antisemite prof. Doesn't answer emails and thinks of herself as the smartest person in the university.
Terrible fanatic
Terrible Prof.
very good professor. love the way she delivers her lectures, very rational and well-thought opinions, easy to open conversations with and debate about middle eastern subjects. would 100% take again.

Abisaab is extremely knowledgeable regarding the course material and is also very kind and considerate! The course was extremely interesting and made me want to take more ISLA course. There were a decent amount of readings but completely manageable. There were 3 essays and 2 graded discussions. The class is an easy A as long as you do the readings.
The best prof ever. Rula is very kind and intelligent. for anyone with an interest in Islamic studies or history, I suggest you take her courses. She is really one of a kind. Love her!

Rula is awesome. I don't know what the person below is talking about (and apparently we were in the same class).  I wasn't a particularly arrive student in the class, but with the few questions I did have, she was very helpful- she's also just a really smart lady.  Definitely one of the better profs I've had at McGill...knows her stuff really well.

This is a waste of time! Prof. thinks that she is teaching to undergrads and 100 levels! Lacking in intellectual stimulation, lacking in structure and in organization.  Also, the prof. is not professional.  She would be helpful and supportive to selected students (usually those who bow in front of her), and completely unvailable to others.
excellent prof.

Always 10 min late to class confused half the time WITH HIS OWN SLIDES! Content is straight forward but some of the midterm stuff we never covered. The only reason he isn't getting a 1 is because the trading simulations were fun. If you want to get a taste of trading then take the class but be aware that you will just learn on your own.

Unclear grading criteria changes throughout the semester. Not committed to teaching, takes his phone out in class, doesn't care about content. Has a group project but doesn't commit to helping students form their groups. Impersonal and seems like at every class, he discovers the content he's teaching despite the trivialness of it. Worst at McGill.
lashed out at me for asking a question in class :((

Terrible professor who did not want to be there in any class. Kept talking non stop about how his job is useless and AI is going to replace him. Every sentence has a reasonable beginning and end, but the middle part does not link the beginning and the end. Felt lost after every class and did better when I stopped showing up.
He doesn't teach you some of the stuff you get tested on. Trading is fun and useful
Goyenko structured this class in a way that I still use in real life. Not sure why he gets the hate but he is a chill guy with good market knowledge
One of the best prof I have had at McGill so far, even though he may be unclear from time to time. He actually teaches material that will be useful on the job.

I don't know why this guy is getting so much hate. Yeah Ruslan can be a bit uncleared sometimes but overall he gives out clear instructions and the materials are very straightforward. Trading simulations were a lot of fun and FINE 444 is a class that equip you with actual skills - you get to learn to trade different asset classes and code in VBA.

Professor Goyenko taught this class well. The trading was a lot of fun and not too difficult. We could have had more information on how to properly code for one of the trading assignments but all in all he was a fair grader and the midterm was fair as well.

One of the worst professors I've ever had, horrible at explaining the material. Brilliant professor, but a bad teacher. Stupid questions get nasty responses. Can't ask him to repeat stuff, he will likely just scoff then give a bad explanation. If you have to take him, just show up and try not to say something stupid every class to get the marks.

His exams and assignments were fair. He was nice in terms of extending deadlines. We also got the chance to get 100 on the assignments if we chose to grade them. Only issue I would say is we never got our midterm grade back and he goes kind of fast but he repeats himself a lot so it makes sense later. He's very funny and nice, would def recommend.

Prof Steele takes forever to grade but if you learned nothing that's completely on you and that was the whole point of self grading the assignments, so we could have feedback faster. There's no way you'd get any of the assessments done if you didn't learn anything unless you were cheating. He's very lenient, and exams/assignments were fair.
Learned nothing from MATH523, no feedback on any of the homeworks or exams. This course is meant to be a core course for stats students, I hope someone else can take over this course.

Prof Steele is very knowledgeable, very caring, and an engaging lecture. The assessments were very fair. He does give back grades very late but honestly I'd rather have a good class with fair assessments where I can get an A than have my grades back quickly.  Also anyone who thinks Russell Steele doesn't enjoy teaching doesn't know him at all.

I don't know what the other ratings are up to but Prof Steele is actually one of the nicest and most enthusiastic lecturer at McGill. His class go by quickly and he makes sure his students truly understand. His tests and assignments are very fair. The MAIN drawback is that he is known for grading things late. Our midterm of Oct11th isn't graded yet

Dr. Steele told me he knew non-academic things about me, which I also did. These things were too risky for "Us," meaning the university and that he believes in second chances and that I should work as a research assistant for a year. If you trust him and he violates in any way, and you have read this, it's your fault. Get away from him, quickly..

He ruined my life and got me removed from my program. I spent a lot of money to go to McGill and he made the decision to remove me. I had to go through a period of homelessness and hunger since I moved to Montreal with no support network.

I don't think he enjoys teaching, and only seems to be here for a paycheck. Plus, we don't need any professors who are bigoted and unfair in their support of student progress (perhaps due to identity discrimination?).

Russell is a professor and associate dean for grad students. He is a mathematician who works collaboratively at Canada's highest-ranked medical institution. Trust that his game is psychological with students; don't trust him. If you do after reading this, it's your fault.
Prof. Steele is full of enthusiasm, his classes are interesting and the assignments are easy. You won't regret taking his class. Highly recommended!

2 midterms and a final, each 30% of our grade. 10% online quizzes. Open book class. All exams had multi-select multiple choice sections, where no partial credit was given if, for example, you only selected 2 of the 3 correct choices for a question. Midterms were out of 20 marks, final out of 30. Not a great lecturer, had to rely ONLY on textbooks.

During lectures, the prof just reads off of these horribly dense slides, which are miserable to sit through. He also does not answer questions well. For the multiple select questions on all tests, there is no partial credit.  The tests are ridiculously hard, and they're not curved. DO NOT take unless its absolutely necessary.

People conveniently leave out that take home assignments and in class quizzes were combined 40% of our grade. The class did overwhelmingly well in these easy assignments. It was clear that Rustam wanted to push our critical thinking skills in exams and god forbid a prof wants to make his students think in tests rather than regurgitate information

Worst class I've ever taken at mcgill. Absoloutely terrible and incompetent professor, midterm class average was a 45% (curved to a 67%) and the final class average was a 52% (he refuses to curve the final). Needless to say complete GPA killer, and for no reason. Save yourself and don't take this course with Rustam if you don't have to.

HORRIBLE. Do not take this class, take chem 203. I truly think this course would have been more interesting if it wasn't this prof. He was so so boring and didn't even know his own material. I didn't learn a single thing in this class and the test averages were always failing, mind you it was OPEN BOOK. Ruined my GPA.
Very nice teacher

Amazing prof honestly read carefully his notes and examples, practice lot, go to class. Tough exam honestly a lot of 'think first' question but if you understand the material and attend class you can achieve well.

He is great ! His tests are pretty tough compared to other MATH 264 profs but you will understand the content 100%. His lectures are nice ; he tries to make it fun and interesting. Be prepared to 'think first' a lot and read his lecture notes in detail.

Made a horrible exam and sent an announcement blaming us for our grades? Refuse to hear ppl out or acknowledge his practice exercises were nothing like what we got. What a shame, I really thought he was a nice guy. If a midterm has a low average it's not the students being lazy.

It seems he just wants everyone to do well because even though the content was hard he basically gave us free marks. Would not take again because I'm a bit worn out by the spontaneity and lack of organisation is his lectures. He has a great textbook though.

Choksi was born to be an educator, and he's lovely to listen to, but this class kicked my ass. Never have I felt more hopeless than when studying for 255. His assignments are tough, his midterm is tough, his final is tough, but you'll have the comfort of knowing that it's all just "book-keeping." Worst experience since high school Spanish.

His ability to vulgarize complicated notions is incredible. I was actually excited to go to his lectures, he's very caring to his students, would often give extensions for assignments, and grades very generously.

Prof. Choksi is awesome! Had him for math255 and his teaching is amazing. He cares about the class and students. AND he is funny!! He makes you excited to learn more. He provides course notes which are complete, so you can skip classes, but I really recommend to go to all his classes because you'll regret missing it for the rest of your life.

In the sense of distributions, this is a great prof. He made an excellent textbook for the course (PDE's) and all the assignments come from it as well. He gives a good intro to the equations we see in class and how they relate to real lif through physics. He is really knowledgeable and knows his field inside out!
Assignments and exams are easy.
Gives awesome lectures and really cares that students fully understand everything he is teaching! Definitely prepared me well for future math classes!

Nutrition class? No... If you are ready to learn from your mistakes, he will make you feel worse after going to his desk. His grading is 10x harsher during finals, your grade can go from an A to a B- real quick. I wish that they went back to the original format (multiple choice). I don't even wish this class upon my worse enemies.
Evil evil man.

Genuinely one of the most condescending profs I've ever had. Exam corrections are so strict that you almost have to have a photographic memory to get full points to a question. Only good comment I have is that he explains things well but it serves you nothing unless you dedicate a ridiculous amount of time to studying and memorizing every detail

A misleading course covering nutrition only occasionally and as a side note to biochemistry lectures. He really values small details over understanding. Beware of the flipped classroom format where students quietly share the answers to study questions all class while the Prof listens. No opportunity to improve because of unclear grading.

Some people might not like his teaching style, however, I really enjoyed how thorough his lectures were. I really felt like I learned something and if you are passionate about the subject, I think you will enjoy this class. 

You need to be aware that there is a lot of information to study, so be ready for that and be regular with it.
serious attitude problem, not very helpful and constantly complains about being bothered by student emails

The prof is really knowledgeable about the subject and brought things into class, like her own old French map, yo engage with the students. She doesn't post lecture slides, but as long as you come to lectures, it's easy to understand the materia. She also was really understanding about the date of the midterm.

Hands down the WORST professor at McGill. So unprofessional, disorganized and just frankly a hot mess. I learned absolutely nothing about Caribbean history. She is just so lost all of the time, she doesn't provide any syllabi (which is breaking so many student rights rules). Simply avoid her at all costs, she should not be teaching at this level.

Passionate teacher but not organized, changed syllabus / due dates / assignments regularly,  instructions unclear, no proper lectures (just her talking randomly), lots of readings expected, we only had our grades back after the semester was over, systematically late to class (or sometimes didn't even show up, even brought her kids multiple times)

AVOID. the other reviews are completely right. shes the most disorganized teacher ive ever had, unable to show up to HER own classes on time, + has difficultly even delivering a decent lecture. as of today she has graded 1 essay out of 5 and still no midterm grade. i truly think she came to class not even knowing what to talk about that day. AWFUL

So confusing with assignments/ grading (no MyCourses or rubrics, changing due dates constantly, + adding assignments a lot). I'm not picky, but she is not meant to teach a 200s course. She is just a disorganized person so it made it following along difficult. Also, showed up 10-15 minutes late every single time which I found super disrespectful.

Poorly organized class, prof often 10, sometimes 15, minutes late to a 50 minute class. Inconsistent information regarding assignments and assessments. High expectations for students' time spent outside of class (lots of reading for an intro course) which would be fair but I don't feel her own efforts teaching match these expectations.

Very nice person but the course is very disorganized. *Nothing* is available/posted on MyCourses, classes often start with a 10 minute delay, every information (syllabus etc.) is sent part by part via multiple random emails. No slides (if any were used during the class) get posted, very little material actually being taught during class time.

You will take Sabine only if you do the IMSF. Extremely smart and well spoken, her feedback is very valuable and she makes you really think. However, impossible to reach - whether office hours, email, etc. Not an easy A, it's a B+ / A- class. Grades take forever to get back.
Hard to get below B+, but almost impossible to get above A-

This woman did little in class except show up late without apologies, talked about TV shows she enjoys, and raved about her herself. 
She said listened to presentations while she worked on her laptop (she wasn't), and was incredibly dismissive to everyone else except her preferred students.
Really? Is there a need to speak about yourself so MUCH??

Professor Jafralie's classes were engaging. She explained concepts clearly and was always approachable and responsive when students had questions or needed clarification on assignments, especially at the end of class. I would strongly recommend taking a class with her.

Avoid this class if you can. The professor is unapproachable, rarely responds to emails, and grades harshly with little clarity. Feedback is inconsistent, and her tone often feels rude, creating an uncomfortable atmosphere where students feel anxious and unsure of expectations. Overall, this course creates unnecessary stress for students.

The final was worth 40%, and she posted many different and sometimes contradictory instructions in various sections of the course platform and via email at different times. Several time consuming assignments worth 5%, graded harshly and without much logic.Rubrics were constantly changing, leading to confusion.
Only uses AI to grade work and respond to emails sad honestly. Very obvious too everyone knew it. Gets mad when someone asks for guidance or feedback.

Feedback is clearly written using AI. When a problem is brought up, claims to be addressing your concern but never gets back to you. Many group projects and small assignments. Learnt very little as class was cancelled half the time. Rubrics posted after assignments were. Discrepancy between TA and prof grading. Contradictory to what she preaches.

Gave everyone 75% on participation even if you showed up to every single class and listened, did your work, asked questions and did everything he wants you to do. Brought down everyone's grade extremely UNFAIR.

Nice but unprofessional. Gave way too many assignments- each worth 5% each, tricky, time consuming assignments and then would grade so Harshly on all of them- Including Personal reflections which is not right. Gets upset when you ask questions to help your grades out. Final paper worth 40% and many different instructions posted, very confusing.

Vague when explaining assignments. Spent most of the class not knowing how I was doing academically for how long it was taking her to grade our assignments. We weren't getting feedback for assignments before writing future ones. Told us not to email regarding our grades, only to email us about a problem days before the semester ended.Unprofessional
Best prof at McGill. Hilarious, knowledgeable, super well-spoken. I wish they offered more grad courses with her as the prof.

Tough exams, lab reports were graded well which boosts grade. Slido quizzes almost every class so must attend, but it did help boost grade. To study for exams, make sure you memorize every technique he presents, because he will test on every small detail presented. Attend class and take good notes

Don't get me wrong, lectures were actually pretty stimulating. He's a good facilitator that allows for interesting conversations.

Dude just did not care about grading, or giving us feedback. Which sucks for an essay-dependent class. He 'read' all of our 20-page papers in 2 days. (Spoiler: He definitely didn't read them). Extremely demotivating.

There were so many readings (posted on mycourses) to be prepared for each lecture and you really had to participate to do well. He only hands out 1-2 A's per class (Desautels curve). Really interesting class and good conversation, but a lot of work. 20 page paper at the end of the class without clear guidelines. He is really interesting though.
He didn't give as many readings as other social context profs and they were actually all pretty interesting. You learn a lot from him and the class is really interactive.

I think one should take Saku's class purely on the merit of his unconventional  teaching methods. His lectures are incredibly refreshing, highly interactive, and often find themselves as they go. This was one of the few classes I took early in the morning without falling asleep. I would take it again in a heartbeat.
She's the GOAT, Would take again!!!
Best Teacher Ever! Great Class, Excellent Teacher
She is a great professor..so clear, helpful and concise. she is one of the best professors ...

Participation was worth 35% and he would literally take a note every time someone spoke, which was stressful and made conversations insincere. We had to send discussion questions at 1pm every Sunday (=no weekend break) and every class we would have a 20min super specific quiz on the heavy readings. So yeah super formative on anxiety I guess
Great prof, very sweet person. Comfortable with asking questions in class
Her lectures were interesting and her slides were clear. I liked her section of this class. She only taught two lectures but she seemed like a good prof and her exam questions were fair.

MIMM387 consisted mainly of guest lectures, so Prof. Gruenheid only taught a couple of lectures. She's really kind and clearly just wanted us to learn more about science and industry. Super easy grader; I studied for half a day before the exams and did just fine. Unexpected 300-level bird course
Great lecturer
First lab course I've taken that I felt like I was doing something meaningful! I enjoyed the course.
I had her for MIMM 211, MIMM 212 and MIMM 465. She's so nice and clearly cares about the field. Interesting content and most of the info is on the slides.

I loved microbiology up until I took this course, and then I hated it. Be prepared for memorizing lots of boring material, and this prof doesn't make any effort whatsoever to engage students.  Don't show up late or miss a class because this prof gets angry.

The class was so interesting. The SWI project was amazing. You really feel as if your lab work is contributing to a larger worldwide scale. She has amazing ppt slides and makes an effort to join her students and take part in the work they are doing in the lab. She is really involved in the SWI project and her quizzes (no exams) are very fair.

One of the best profs in the department! The class was super fun, and labs could actually be applied to real life. This was the class that made me really want to do micro. Also, she did a great job at teaching MIMM 211.
Really interesting labs! Not just the typical follow the manual type, really hands on and I learned so much!!

Professor Sameer clearly cares about his students and teaching. The class is informative, and he presents the material in an engaging way. He is also available during office hours, which is very helpful for clarifying concepts. Overall, a positive learning experience.
Amazing PM prof

a great professor who obviously cares about his students and actually enjoys teaching. makes life easy and takes the time to meet with students 1-1 to get your feedback, then implements the feedback! highly recommend taking INSY 450 with him, even if the course content isn't the most interesting

Though the course was a bit boring, professor made it easy. He is very respectful and makes sure everyone is comfortable. I also appreciate him meeting all the students one by one outside of his class. Open book exam helps.
Great prof, super interesting topics, and love the structure of the class. Definitely recommend, you do have to put in the work, but its easy if you attend all the lectures
Do not take him. he is very close minded, and not respectful.

Do not take this prof. He is incredibly biased, picks favorites, and does not respect students or their personal situations. Extremely unfair as a grader and as a person. He also does not know what he's talking about or teaching and often thinks his opinion is the only correct one. 

i would really have enjoyed his class if it wasn't him teaching.
Good class! Content is great. Although sometimes the readings are long, it is a good class to apply knowledge about online communities in real life. Lots of examples!
Highly knowledgeable, makes you think instead of forcing you to memorize.  Great teacher and course.
Read your book! CLass is completely useless, he covers less then 20% of the course content.

This professor is great, hes new to McGill and explains everything clearly! Super nice guy always wiling to help, if you put in the work on the assignments and study a bit for the final youll get a good grade guaranteed.
stay away from this professor
Useless teacher

He is a nice guy but his lectures are boring, he is not making any effort to make it interesting or engaging. The "midterm" was literally one week before the end of the semester and was not really related to his lectures his content.The grading scheme is the only good thing about this class, since there is no final and only one exam worth 33%

Bad prof, he said if we want a regrade of final projects then he would regrade every single assessment we did since the beginning of the semester in attempt to scare us from asking for a regrade, he then said he was on leave until mid march but you could literally see him walking around Wong lol, overall bad lecturer and very LAZY.
Long lectures and boring lectures. The prof is very competent though

Professor Huberman is nice and helpful during office hours. His lectures were pretty content-heavy and a bit hard to follow along with, but if you attended class and reviewed the content you could do well on the midterm. The lab component helped bring grades up and the grading was super generous overall, especially on the midterm.

Content is pretty easy to understand on your own but the midterms are way harder than they should be. Fair grading scheme since there is no final and even if you do not too well on the midterms, the labs and projects can help a lot to compensate.

The midterms always had unexpected questions that we never practiced on. The averages of these midterms were always below 60. I am glad that there was a final take home project because I did not want to do a final exam. The concepts were not explained well but the labs helped us understand some of them.

The course material was not delivered in a naturally flowing way, and it was difficult to make connections between topics. There was no textbook and no tutorials, so going into midterms was practically going in blindfolded. There was a final project instead of a final exam though, so that was great!
Great Prof. Really cares and open to questions and providing help. Just do all practice exams and you'll be fine.
Funny guy! Great lectures, but they do require some supplemental resources outside class.

Sewall's lectures are always entertaining, and the concepts are covered thoroughly. I really enjoyed my time in this course. Testing isn't a breeze but definitely doable if you take the time to study.
he is so funny and takes time to explain if you don't get a concept. try your best and you'll be fine

Sam is great. The first chemistry teacher I've ever had that I can immediately understand what he's talking about. Honestly considered minoring in chemistry for a second there. He's also super funny and I enjoyed his teaching style a lot. Sorry that you got shingles in the middle of the semester Prof., I hope you're feeling better

A super nice and engaging professor. You can do really well if you watch the provided videos before the lectures, since he goes over practice problems in class to reinforce your knowledge. Very clear that he knows what he's talking about and offers a lot of support. Midterms and final were very similar to the provided practice ones.
Such a great lecturer. Clearly cares about his students. Easy to succeed in this course.

He teaches the second section of Chem 120 and is more nonchalant than the previous instructor. He is still a great lecturer who knows the content inside and out. He, too, is incredibly personable and offers a lot of support if you ask.
funny guy, clearly cares about his students, engaging lecturer
never knew what was going on in lectures, just do the practice exams though and you'll be fine

Prof Nelson is very kind and accommodating to students' needs. He extended multiple of our assignments, and the assignments for the course (4 essays) are marked very generously. Classes are recorded, and all the readings are accessible via myCourses. Recommend to anyone as an elective or for your major!

Prof Nelson is one of the best professors at McGill; his lectures are insightful and recorded, so attendance isn't mandatory. The class is essay-heavy - 4 essays around 1000-1200 words, but not graded harshly. The professor is also very open to helping students and gives extensions when needed. Class is excellent, would recommend to anybody.

I love Dr. Nelson! His lectures were interesting and the class was never stressful. He was extremely helpful with the assignments and if you listened to his advice, they were easy to do well on. Very funny and energetic guy. He really makes lectures entertaining and fun. He's very joyful and is very smart (ask him a chemistry question before/after class!). If you sit in the front row he'll come right up to you and pretty much give you a 1on1 lecture. Great prof!

He is good for lower level classes do not take him for grad classes. He is all over the place lost in his material, his slides are not his own, midterm and final have nothing to do with course content our final was 3 read 3 papers, terrible teaching for grad class, no flow to the material and all over the place. As everyone else has already mentioned, GO TO THIS MAN'S OFFICE HOURS. He will talk through your work with you, offer you ideas, and you will leave feeling much better than you did coming in. Prof Carney is an excellent teacher and a very kind person; just be sure to dedicate time to his readings, since they tend to be pretty dense.

Sean Carney is a professor who, though incredibly well-versed in theatre history and theory, never makes anyone feel inferior. As many on here have mentioned, his office hours are very helpful. Very knowledgable, engaging, and kind. Available for individual consultation and will even look at drafts of your papers before submission! I learned a lot from his class. Highly recommended! As other reviews said - visit him in office hours before you submit your papers/do your presentation, incorporate his suggestions, and you will do well. Prof is great and genuinely cares about his students. My grades went up significantly when I took my first class with him because of how much feedback he gave me on my essays. Kind, thoughtful, and passionate. Take one of his classes!!

Prof. Carney is absolutely brilliant and an unbelievably kind and helpful professor, he truly cares about his students and was always helpful when I would seek his perspective during office hours. A wonderful prof I highly reccomend - easily one of the most down to earth at McGill and one of the brightest scholars I've studied with!
One of my favourite teachers at McGill. His classes aren't easy, but they're always interesting and he cares about the subject matter.

Prof Carney is great. I look forward to his lectures because he's so personable and likes to trail off into tangents and funny anecdotes. The material is straightforward and you can definitely succeed if you keep up with readings and lectures.
A brilliant lecturer, always ready to help his students. Prepare to read and be amazed at how good he renders everything!

Extremely knowledgeable prof. It is extremely easy to get help from either the prof of the TAs, and they are always happy to do so. Lots of biology content, which for a class that does not have BIOL 112 as a prerequisite, proves to be quite difficult for some, and gives others an unfair advantage.

He's a nice guy, but the quiz questions are hard to understand exactly what the answers are expected to be. Besides, for just 3 credits, there are too many things to do for this course. Great

Should speak louder for everyone to hear, and I find not being able to hear has significantly impacted my grade because on tests and hw he looks for fine detailed answers. Prof. Hogiu is super kind and really cares about the content matter and the students. The way this course is delivered can be tough, because it covers such a wide scope, but he teaches it well.

The lectures definitely tend to be dry, and it may seem that every lecture is just random info that you have to learn, rather than focusing on one or few subjects. However, the prof cared about his students and the project made the class more interesting.

Professor Wachsmann-Hogiu is a very nice person. However, Bien 210 is not a good course. Indeed the scope of this course is way to broad and we go into very little detail about each topic. Sebastian is a really nice guy, super approachable and really takes an interest in your learning. Bien 210 does not have a final, and is a relatively project heavy class compared to other courses. Lectures can sometimes be a bit dry, but he does his best to keep us engaged which is appreciated
Classes were well organized with practical applications and real good examples. I learned alot and have taken good notes as I want to constantly use in future for my career.
Great. Knows his topics and can explain them clearly. His exam contained some "traps". It requires to remember the exceptions and more than the basic stuff in general.

Best Prof and class I have taken at McGill. You definitely need to be invested in the course, but you will get a lot out of it. Exams are hard, but it's absolutely possible to get an A if you attend lectures, do assignments and practice past finals.

Take this professor at any cost. His lectures build a true understanding of the content, and the evaluations are challenging, but reveal your actual knowledge. The group project was a grind, but it was ultimately very fun, and provides a great opportunity to apply your knowledge.
A really good prof. Good lecture slides and makes you work hard on your group project. Expect a lot of work but it is worth it
Incredible professor. Genuinely cares if you understand the material. Hands down the best Finance professor at McGill. Doesn't smile much but you can tell he's a great guy.

Great professor, clearly cares about his students and is passionate about the material. However, be aware that while the material is pretty straightforward, the exams are extremely difficult. Great professor if you want to learn. He will teach you not only the material, but how to think and tackle real life problems. It's not an easy course, but if your up to the challenge take him, you won't regret it.
Best professor I have had by a long way.
Awesome prof, would love to have again
BORING TEACHING AND MEANINGLESS TESTS. WILL NEVER TAKE BIO COURSE SINCE MET THIS PROF.
Very nice and caring professor. Lectures were recorded which makes the class easy to follow and good for re-watching before exams. Exams are fair. Labs are fun, and overall great class.
Fully online, no final, the labs are fun and most grades came from quizzes.
He is amazing, you understand very well the content. He is amazing at explaining!

Overall great professor! One of the few professors that gave quality lectures during zoom classes. One of my favourite profs so far at Macdonald Campus. You do have to watch lectures to pass the class.

I loved him! He was patient and always very concerned about whether we understood or not. Don't be afraid to ask question he really welcomes them. Also a fun guy to talk to and he's not afraid to joke around. Also lectures are required for mechpath

Faucher is an amazing teacher, funny jokes, clear explanation, office hours and review sessions. The textbook is no need as his slides are complete and clear. A lot of materials to be memorized, but materials on the midterm are not on the final :D Study hard and you can get an A.
Amazing teacher. Super helpful and answers emails very quickly. His notes are very complete so no need to purchase the textbook. However, it was helpful for me to understand some concepts.
Very good prof, amazing power point notes, always answer to emails. He makes the class very interesting and has a great sense of humor.

Just reads the slides, attendance not mandatory and posts the slides, nothing wrong with him or his class since it was interesting to follow just can be a tough grader since my friend and I did really good in his class and still managed to not get at least an A- If you're good to with only 3 big essay assignments this is your class.

really clear slides

hes a great prof very knowledgeable and sweet the classes were recorded so attendance isnt mandatory all assignments including the final were take-home essays, you have to do the readings and pay attention and youll pass. Prof. Kroupa is a very caring and knowledgeable professor, and indeed a great person. The prof is very fair. I was upset that my participation mark was reduced for not showing up in class for a good reason, but got above average marks in all tests and finished class with an A. The class is super-well organized.

Challenging but interesting class. I learned a lot from weekly readings and in-class problems and cases. The course is organized really well. Genuinely makes everything seems so difficult even though its not.

MATH 340: Good lecturer, notes are comprehensive & exams are fair. Had a really fun time in MATH 350. It was a difficult journey but I gained an appreciation for slick graph theory proofs

never reply email and very hard to approach. Do Not have any mercy even in this difficult situation.
