Shane is awesome! He always tries to make the lectures engaging. There's 1 midterm, 2 group projects & 2 reflections. The midterm is all memorization. There are readings to do before each class. There are polls done in class that count toward participation marks, so don't miss too many classes.
Best piece of advice: learn content by heart.

Best prof and best class I've had so far at McGill, and by far the class from which I've learned and retained the most info. Great teacher. I did bad in ECSE 200, really didn't understand. With Sharmistha for 210 and all of the things I was "taught" in 200 are so clear when she explains. She makes learning easy to follow and intuitive taking the time to go through problems step by step two thumbs up

Prof. Lovejoy isn't the worst, but he's also not the best. Although not the best I have ever had, it is clear that he is certainly trying to improve, and it shows. Clear about what you need to know, relatively organized, and knows the material like the back of his hand.

E&M is horribly boring, but it's not entirely Lovejoy's fault. He knows his stuff, and although he could be more engaging it's just the material is mindnumbing. It is however an easy class (he even encouraged us to use the solution manual for the assignments). Exam was somewhat tricky.

He wasn't so bad. The classes were a bit boring, but I guess it is mostly due to the nature of the material... Class taken Fall 1999.

Given how hard the material was he taught it excellently. Highly interactive classes which help you internalize the rhythms and difficult but fair tests. Only complaint was the lack of online material, if you don't remember the names of the techniques from class you won't find them on MyCourses.
Hi barely gave any rubric or criteria for tests and quizzes. And he is a super harsh marker especially for students learning a new instrument a month in.

Really follow his grading guidelines. This class is kind of boring and he doesn't really do much, but it is nice to listen to guest lectures with your friends (most of which were interesting). Its low effort, kind of a nice nap opportunity.

Is able to explain statistics very simply and make them less frightening. Offered generous extra credit at the beginning of the term.

if you don't find the subject interesting, I wouldn't take this class, otherwise it is an easy A. Quizzes are annoying but easy to get good mark if you do them all. Good class for those interested in global health. Professor is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic. Pop quizzes are annoying, the rest is ok.

The material can be pretty dry and she doesnt do much for it, but talks pretty quickly. Shes enthusiastic, but it runs a fine line of being a headache. Fantastic course with a super-helpful and approachable professor. She is quite chatty in class but also leads a stimulating discussion. the group project was definitely unfairly marked and the grade we got was not reflective of how much time we put in. shelley is engaging but can be condescending one-on-one, and sometimes has very problematic attitudes about certain things she presents (ie. gay rights movement used AIDS to destigmatize their identity)

Nice prof and will keep you awake during lectures. Lots of readings but they are helpful for understanding the material. Involves a 7-person group project + presentation, midterm, and a rather difficult final. Make sure to start studying early, and know EVERYTHING.
She's a great professor!

Excellent professor. Gave very clear and engaging lectures and posted full lecture notes on MyCourses. Happy to answer questions during and after lectures. Good amount of office hours. Grading, however, was quite slow.
She's an amazing teacher and knows her stuff super well. Answers all questions in depth and makes sure we all get it. Luv her

She was my TA for Math 133 last semester, so I didn't hesitate for a second taking the class with her. Linear algebra can be too abstract and incomprehensible sometimes, but she makes it understandable. Best Math Prof at McGill when it comes to answering questions. Highly recommended.
She's a great teacher and her online recordings help a lot. Cares a lot about the students and answers questions well.

I found her very understanding and kind. She takes the material seriously and expects students to do the same. Maybe passive-aggressive sometimes, but definitely not rude (or a harsh grader). There are reflections at the end of every week, so make sure you don't miss them.

he is a great supervisor for graduate studies. very helpful and knowledgeable. teaching method is somewhat dry, but compared to other teachers at MAC, he is good.
took him last year. was not too bad...easy class, nice guy

was pretty good

love prof shokry. he is so sweet, kind, and always willing to help if you're struggling with grasping anything in class. lots of homework and very hard content, but that's language-learning! as long as you do homework every day and practice speaking in class you will soar through the exam and final projects. he gen wants to see students succeed!

Professeur exceptionnel, qui veut absolument que nous apprenions. Il est donc très exigeant, ce qui est une qualité ! Il est aussi à l'écoute de nos besoins individuels.

Great teacher. The material is difficult but you're always given the chance to absorb it. As for exams, the criteria is very clear and getting an A isn't something to worry about given how hard the material is.
Shokry is the best professor I've had at McGill. He is willing to give up a weekend to help you, and he is a very good teacher.

one of the BEST prof's ive had at mcgill. so very caring and helpful, goes out of his way to help his students and make their lives easier. Easy to get an A as long as you attend class regularly and keep up with work. course is not hard, work load is high but  pay off is also high. (but also easy to fall behind quickly)

Shokry is one of the nicest professors at McGill! He is extremely helpful and really knows what he's doing. Although there is a lot of work in the class, the work itself is not hard. You can easily get an A in this class as long as you attend classes and put in the effort.

He's like a giant, arabic-speaking teddy bear!  I love Shokry and his smile lights up my mornings.  The only downside to Introductory Arabic is that it's taught by TAs three days a week, and mine was an ice queen. Great class, brilliant prof

Shokry is an amazing prof, not too hard but also challenging enough to motivate his students to learn as much as possible. My only complaint is that he only teaches the class 2 times a week..wish we had him every day!

Shokry's a great professor, very helpful, easy to understand and nice. Introductory Arabic is a lot of work but getting a good grade isn't too difficult if you put in the effort. Don't be intimidated by the high hw load in the first month and the 6 hours of classes, A's are very possible especially with prof. Gohar's help.
Really wasn't a bad class. His assignment was straight forward. His section on the exam was straight forward too, really wish I knew the derivations though. Would take his class again.

Great prof. The material for this class isn't too difficult and it's a good introduction to biomaterials. Prof Nazhat's grading if very fair, he has good humor and is very knowledgeable and approachable. Would take again!!!

He really made an effort to connect with the class as people and, unlike some other profs who require class participation, he actually values what we have to contribute. The grading criteria is clear and fair as well. I would definitely recommend taking this or other marketing classes with him!

One of my favorite professors at McGill. I learned so much from him throughout the course. He is one of the kindest professors as well, he's very understanding and very clear in his expectations and guidelines for our projects. Definitely take his course class for marketing research!!
Ignore the negative review below. Amazing Prof, really loved the course. Super friendly, classes were engaging.

I feel like I need to offset the previous review. I loved having this prof - made MRKT451 my favourite out of the three mandatory marketing courses. Participation matters but it's his way of keeping you engaged and the questions he asks aren't even hard. It encourages you to listen and in the long run that's helpful on tests. Super friendly guy.

had him for 140 and 141, didn't care that average was low and half the class was failing, sent us a rude email and said the final will be harder because that midterm was easy and we should have done better... would not recommend him if you can avoid it
He's the reason I go to therapy
I was convinced.
Great prof, explains everything clearly and his exams are fair. Use his textbook for practice and you'll be more than fine.

Good lecturer and responds to emails quickly. Definitely a bird course, 30% of your grade is webworks and the final is online. If you attend the lectures consistently and take notes, should be an easy A.

This professor was heavily idealised before I started this class, so perhaps I came with high expectations. However, he seemed to overexplain simple concepts learned in high school. He did do a lot of practice problems, which helped to learn. He also tricked us by making the midterm easy and the final disgustingly hard. Very Mediocre Prof.
My goat Sid I cannot praise this guy enough. Do every odd problem in the book and mark his words every lecture! Trudeau away everyone, I was waiting every lecture for him to convince me!

Absolutely amazing prof, motivated me to trek up to mcmed and did not skip a single lecture. He may seem intimidating during lectures but he is super approachable during office hours and really tries to make sure you understand the concept. He made calc so interesting and truly showed the beauty of math. and make sure to do all the odd num ques!

Sid is a very nice professor. He spends most of the class time on exercices, which is great. However, as someone who isn't good at math, his teaching style can be confusing most of the time since he goes pretty fast. The first exam was very fair, the final was pretty bad. He does offer an alternative grading scheme though.

Although he does not take attendance, there is a reason his lectures are always full; he does not post lecture recordings or slides; everything is done in class on the chalkboard. He is old-fashioned, and if you don't understand the material, your grade will reflect it. However, MT/exam questions are directly from the textbook, so study those.

I had Professor Huang's lectures 2 years ago. Although the content was fairly heavy, he explains concepts clearly and thoroughly. He really tried to help you understand and think in depth. He was super caring as well. 5/5 prof
Good professor but not professional outside class

Exams are not easy but himself as a lecturer is great. He explains materials well and usually goes over parts of the previous lecture material when the next lecture starts. Which help the continuity of learning the material.

Fine lecturer, points out important details. Tricky exam questions with lots of words -- hard to analyze and actually get to what the question is asking. Was a better prof in BIOC311 than BIOC312. Seems like a nice guy though, and I'm sure he would help if approached with questions
horrible intense materials that focus heavily on useless details

He does a decent job of lecturing and that by itself would have been fine. However, when you add his accent, his random pauses, and mumbling, his material becomes all the more confusing. It doesn't help that he expects a complete understanding of his material and asks rather tricky questions. All I can say is study is section slowly and good luck.
Great prof! would take again.

He may have a slight accent, but is comprehensible.  His slides were very organized and clear. He taught the urea cycle in a step-by-step, easy to follow manner. His questions on the final exam were fair.

He's really not as bad as people are making him seem. Is his teaching perfect? No. Will you get through this class unscathed if you put in effort? Absolutely. 
I highly recommend watching the lecture recordings. He has a thick accent, but you will get used to it. I still feel like I learned a lot from his section. 
His exam questions were easy.
Lots of unfair ratings. He's entertaining, and he gave us what we needed to do well on the exam.
Does he have Alzheimer's disease?

Alert! Cringeworthy professor. His teaching style is to make things incomprehensible. One has to wonder how McGill lets him teach. I know there are financial problems with the university, but they seem to be scraping the bottom of the barrel with this one.

I learned nothing from his lectures. He seems not to understand the material he teaches. The only way I was able to learn was by watching lectures from other universities and reading the textbook. McGill needs to get rid of the so-called "professor". What a joke!

Hekimi seems like a fraud of a professor in my opinion.  He cannot explain things clearly and you have to wonder whether he understands at all what he is supposed to be teaching. He seems to have no idea how much students struggle to understand his lectures. Do yourself a favour and stay away!!
Please for the love of Christ take away his teaching license. He couldn't speak clearly if his family was on the line. God speed to anyone taking the class.

You have to wonder how this guy ever got hired as a professor.  He is so unable to teach that I had to rely entirely on reading about the subject. He has a bad attitude too, as though students don't matter and he would rather be somewhere else.
sb Professor, never gets his point out clearly

Literally yaps faster than the speed of light, which makes it hard to write down everything he DID NOT put on the slides, in class. Unclear learning objectives and I literally have no idea what he's saying cause he rambles, hesitates and cannot get to his point. If you wanna understand what he teaches, look at the textbook and watch the recordings.

She made class interesting and engaging, and I love the cog dog. The material isn't difficult by any means, but you will still need to study it and memorize a bit to do well (which is normal for college, idk why people think otherwise). So far it was the easiest psyc class I've taken. Didn't even touch the textbook and still got 95+ on all exams
Very kind! Grading is forgiving since she doesnt count your worst midterm of the 2. Super kind and gives many possibilities of extra credit. Would take again if I could.

After being through the absolute trenches in Bio 200, I almost cried tears of joy after this class. You know what you are expected to know, and the class itself is super interesting! Amazing prof, 10/10
amazing prof
One of the easiest psyc classes i've ever taken and prof makes it really engaging

She's a real one. What you see is what you get in this class—no surprises, no tricks, no tomfoolery. Wholesome and sweet, I recommend this professor to anybody. I appreciate her bonus points in exams and THTUs.

fav prof at mcgill! she's so knowledgeable and always open to answer questions about topics students may be interested in. her class is engaging and she goes out of her way to help students learn as best they can. she's caring and so funny! exam questions are sometimes weird but nothing terrible. + the cog dog is like a celebrity to me i love her

Prof Sheldon makes an effort to make her classes interactive, you can really tell that she cares. Memorize everything, exams can be tricky, and some questions are made to throw you/very confusing. Slides are sufficient for success. Textbook helps but not necessary. Easy bonus questions. Good class!
One of my favourite profs. PSYC213 is super straightforward. Exams are all multiple choice, no trick questions. She is funny and makes lectures very enjoyable.

the sweetest, kindest, and clearest professor out there. also the cog dog is the cutest girl ever I am obsessed with her. all that aside though, Dr. Sheldon's classes are so well done, and well-structured. Exams are so easy if you study even just a bit, and properly listen. i loved cognition honestly, even though I didn't expect to!

The econometrics goat! Silvia is extremely smart and nice. She makes her lectures engaging and is able to explain complicated derivations well. I took this class with very little econ and math background and managed to do well just by showing up to the lectures, taking notes, going to conferences, and reading the chapters. Excellent professor.

When I signed up for Econ 337, I was looking for silver. But with Silvia, I found GOLD. Best prof ive ever had by a landslide. She will answer any question and will spend an UNLIMITED amount of time helping you understand. Grading is extremely fair, and lectures are all you need. It is such a shame she does not teach more Econ classes. An Angel.

The content is difficult and Silvia didn't make it easier to grasp. She would throw random models and concepts at us without explaining how they were linked so every concept felt like a separate course. There was no TA, no tutorials, and limited online resources so her lectures and your preexisting math foundation are your only hope

For an advanced econometrics course, the contents covered in her 469 feel like they lack justification. "Here are some things out there, but I can't tell you how it works" kind of lectures. Still, the course is not easy. It's not the difficulty of the course, but the sheer amount of contents covered that will suffocate you around the finals period.

Prof Silvia is overall a great professor. She is very intelligent and knowledgable in econometrics, and is also a sweet, caring woman. She explains most concepts quite well, and answers any questions students have for her. The material is difficult, and quite mathematically rigorous, however she makes fair/easier exams relative to the material.
decent but you need to work hard

One of my favorite econ classes. Super caring prof always making sure that the students follow her demonstrations and open for questions during lectures. Go to tutorials to learn how to use STATA. My dream would be her teaching 338. If you prepare well for exams, you should do great (the final a bit more challenging than midterm). 100% recommend.

This class isn't easy, but Prof Goncalves explains the material well, and if you don't get it, she'll re-explain until you do. She's willing to write through proofs with you step-by-step so the concepts are clear. It feels like she cares about whether you learn something or not. As long as you understand her slides, you will be fine in the exam.
This course is poorly designed. She put too much materials in this course, so she could not to afford to explain everything well.

Don't take this class if you want to learn anything applicable. This class is entirely on the mathematical theory of econometrics. I don't think we even looked at any data. Overall, this class is dry, hard and a little useless.

Simon is amazing! I found him to be really great at explaining the content and so approachable for questions. Love the way the grades are divided up.. only problem is that it takes REALLY long to get grades back. Really good course for students interested in behaviour.

Simon is a stand up guy but his course needs some work. Classes are boring, with a low attendance rate. We received no marks until late March, leaving us guessing for what they were looking for or how we were doing. Assignment outlines were unorganized and too long, leaving room for misinterpretation. The conferences are boring and don't help.

DONT TAKE THIS. I read reviews saying not to take this class and I didn't listen. i studied and went to class and still got a D. Will most definitely ruin your gpa. GET OUT OF THIS.  interesting material but not worth the risk.

This prof is AWFUL. the class itself is interesting but his methods of evaluation are skewed and he will mark you wrong if you don't reproduce his theories. His lectures are a series of tangents about his own ethnographic research. he never explains his methods of evaluation either so don't take this if you don't have time to learn everything.

Not a very good prof. The material is relatively interesting but the lectures are extremely boring. Relies almost exclusively on the book--lots of terminology, lots of memorization. I would not recommend you take this class unless you absolutely have to!

A very interesting topic; a very boring prof. If you read his book and the coursepack, study well, and have a study group before the midterm/exam, you should be fine. I did'nt go to class during the last month, but if I could have, I would have gone because his repetition of his book makes it seek in. Take it only if you are interested in the topic

The readings are manageable (his book and a course pack) but his lectures confuse you. He manages to make the materials extremely boring. Does not even tell you what would be on the exams. HIGH RISK OF FAILING. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

The social evolution class revolves around his book. I really do not understand why people find this class confusing it really is a classic anthropology class which refers to traditional notions like kinship, exchange, and leadership. He is very open to questions, it is true however that his answers might not always be very concise.

I really, really like this professor. He's got a good sense of humour and tells funny anecdotes and strange (but endearing) jokes. His material is really involved, lots of terminology, but if you do the reading and pay close attention in class you'll be fine. Very friendly and approachable. I found his lectures well structured and interesting!

I really, really like this professor. He's got a good sense of humour and tells funny anecdotes and strange (but endearing) jokes. His material is really involved, lots of terminology, but if you do the reading and pay close attention in class you'll be fine. Very friendly and approachable. I found his lectures well structured and interesting.

This course is extremely hard to listen to and learn from. The lecturer is very poor at communicating what he is trying to say to his class. He speaks great English, however overcomplicates sentences and makes the course VERY stressful. Even if you watch the lecture again online, you'll keep rewinding every second to understand a mere sentence!
TERRIBLE professor. Extremely unclear and boring. His lectures are confusing and contradictory.
Lectures are a little bit boring, but she gives good grades and can be recommended
This prof made me regret my decision to go to Quebec even more

Easy but wouldn't take again. Do not recall learning anything I didn't already know in this class - information was presented in unoriginal/boring ways. Prof Hashemi was disorganized: contradicted herself when it came to assignment guidelines and did not provide helpful feedback. Outdated readings & her lectures are packed with random youtube vids.
Great class and instructor. Would definitely take again.

This course had big potential to be an amazing course to take, however Ms. Hashemi was quite disappointing. We had mandatory class where we would be in breakout rooms all class to discuss her recordings that wren't the best. She takes ages to reply to emails and her grading criteria are all over the place. Super harsh grader too! I don't recommend

Siva is an amazing lecturer who cares about his content and lectures, however he is super harsh while grading, he refuses to curve his course (i.e. if everyone fails, he will fail the entire class), first class average of below 60. However don't let this deter you, it is possible to do well but takes a lot of effort.

Prof Nadarajah is brilliant and engaging, but sometimes moves a little too fast. The cover-content-quickly-and-review-it-later style of teaching works for some, but I can understand the difficulties for others. He does not post lecture notes and 100% of the grade is split between exams and quizzes, so consider this if you are taking 331 with him.

His lectures are great but he goes pretty fast so you might have to look over topics in the textbook. At the end of the day the most important part of this course is to do as many problems as possible. His exams were fair and there were many resources to prepare.

Incredibly knowledgeable and talented lecturer. Course content is a bit disorganized, so you should attend class to know what is and is not important.

Very generous on assignment grades. Exams are challenging in time but not in content. Very fair overall.

Content will be of great value for all sorts of engineers.

Tough prof, the final grade was 100% based on exams. In the exams, if you do not write exactly what he has in mind, you will get a 2/10 on that problem. He always tries to deduct as many points as he can in all his exams. Always seemed busy and impatient in the office hours. Lectures were engaging and clear, but avoid him if you don't want C or F.
Personally I really enjoy professor Nadarajahs lectures. If you're passionate about the field you will too. Exams are really really tough, but grading is reasonably fair.

Great professor, really enjoyed his lectures. He's knowledgable in so many fields as well as being an expert in his own. Really smart guy and I feel he grades fairly unlike other profs. Classes are content heavy but he explains very clearly. Sometimes he overcomplicates simple concepts. Exams are quite hard so you have to dedicate a lot of time.
Great prof!

Unnecessarily overcomplicates the material and only teaches 1/3 it. Expects you to dedicate 100+ hours per week to this class. Extremely hard and unfair exams. Inconsistent grading. I could go on, but character limit. Avoid him. Just the classic McGill engineering class where you just memorize a textbook, but learn nothing somehow made worse.

Heavy lectures and exams can be long, but just be good at time management. Final was very hard, so do well on the midterms and quizzes. There are also after-class questions to answer on MyCourses for a total of 5%. Overall easy concepts, but a hard class with Siva.

He is incredible at what he does. He kept us constantly engaged, treated us as intellectuals, & designed graded work that we could learn from & innovate with (even tests). It never felt like imitation for the sake of easy grading, you actually gained from it. Rare to find a prof who teaches in a way where the concepts become natural, not forced.

Honestly one of my favourite professors I've had a McGill! He's super funny and uses a lot of the time for open discussion, so you're able to provide thoughts or feedback on the content every class. Midterms are super fair, and the content is super interesting. If you get the chance definitely take it.

I took SOCI 235 in Winter 2025 and it was so insightful! My TA gave good feedback for the paper and Prof Wang gave good feedback for the midterm too. Hoping to take more of his classes while at McGill! He is so insightful and kind. For soci 235, participation mattered but was not counted for grades so it removed the pressure of perfection.

TAKE HIM!! Not only does he offer some of the most interesting courses at McGill, but he grades super fairly and created an extremely engaging class environment. He cares about what students think and wants us to succeed. I was excited to go to each class. There was only 1 reading per class so also super manageable. Such a gem!!!!!!

prof wang is the best.. easily one of the most charismatic profs out there.. class was early but everyone was just so pumped to listen to him lecture. the papers are super fun and he makes you think hard about your relationship with tech. midterm was super managable. he is also just so approachable and kind, and POPULAR so good luck with getting in

TAKE ALL OF HIS CLASSES! In all my years at McGill, I've yet to meet a prof who is this engaging, caring and thoughtful... I actually look forward to attending EVERY one of his classes. You don't just learn about sociological theory -- he teaches you how to think and be better at life. I leave every session inspired. 100% best prof I've ever had.

Great prof! The class only had one midterm and two essays. Also, grading is very clear in my opinion and he is an amazing lecturer. Very funny, knows how to engage his students, and is charismatic. Would 100% recommend

I took Intimacy in the Digital Age with him and let me just say...He is outstanding! Literally chillest, interesting, most fun professor I've had in ages. Most of his lectures are just discussion and his assignments are super engaging. If the new gen of professors at McGill are all like him, this school is SET. Strongly recommend taking his class.
I found his course to be very straightforward, with good lectures and assignments. Honestly what every course should be like/ no attendance except for exit tickets but those weren't worth much

The class is super easy, exam in done in class but online, it wasn't too bad if you attend the classes.  4 questions only 300 words each. As a soci student, the class was definitely not reading heavy, max we had was 30 pages but once or twice in the whole semester. He is very caring of his student and super chill. Will take him again for sure!!
Great and passionate teacher, highly recommend.

Super nice, extremely passionate about what he was teaching and very accessible outside of class. Group projects were long but manageable and the midterm was very fair. Final was fair too but there were some weird syntax choices that made some questions confusing. Overall a fantastic prof!

Great teacher. The structure of the class is well organized and straightforward so you won't be breaking your head in this class too much. Lectures are recorded. Assignments are and exams are very fair. Not the most exciting class, but Sol is a good option for this topic. We learn basic Figma/HTML/CSS/JS.
Very solid guy. Quite a hard course if you know nothing about programming, but he is nonetheless a good teacher. Fair assignment grading as well.

Prof. Tanguay is one of my favourite teachers at McGill. His lectures are well-organized, with clear explanations and helpful practice time. He has a great attitude, is very caring, and genuinely wants his students to succeed. He's positive, enthusiastic, and always willing to help. Highly recommend!
he is good

The course content is very manageable in general. Lots of memorization for the Excel component, but the HTML/JavaScript/CSS part was very straightforward. The 2 assignments (group projects) were very long though. Not the most exciting lectures but the class is pretty free I'd say.
Took him for Digital Consulting. Very passionate, engaging and caring prof, would definitely recommend taking the class.

Great energetic professor. Enjoyed his lectures, but I found mgcr 331 really hard. Still did well mostly due to just having to memorize everything. He's a fun guy, but the topics are extremely basic so there's not much he can do to help. You just need to memorize stuff.

I recommend Sol Tanguay, he's a great professor, super nice and accessible for office hours.
Course can be boring, be prepared to do a lot of excel ( learn all the functions and stuff by heart, kinda useless) and coding.


Overall, though he's a nice guy, no complaints.
He also records his lectures.
Nice person but a bit lazy in teaching. Hard final exam.

This professor is the definition of doesn't care about his students. Cannot be bothered to answer an email and the only reason everyone gets an A is because the materials are relatively simple. If you ask a clarifying question about his horribly poor english in assignments / exams though, good luck getting an answer.
Prof Zhao is handsdown the most accommodating prof's I've met at McGill University. This course is challenging, and prof will go miles to make sure that everyone passes. Absolutely recommend.
Really fantastic all round
fantastic professor! easy course, great teaching
He's really passionate to share his knowledge with his students. I mean he is a shy person in general, but you can still feel his passion. Really caring prof.

Very good prof. If you put in the work on assignments and quizzes, the final is only 20 so it is easy to get an A. Good slides, good explanations and lectures. Only gripe is that he sometimes mumbles and it becomes difficult to understand. You can tell he really cares about his students. Late work is not accepted, even a few mins.

Great lecturer, clear expectations and nothing other than the lectures to study. The midterms were definitely on the trickier side but nothing unfair, and the final was a bit more straightforward. Would recommend :)

Krol's classes are super engaging and very interactive! All psyc majors and non psyc majors need this class because it is very therapeutic. This class is easier than 215 because there is no textbook and has a very flexible grading scheme. The exams are straight forward- just make quizlets and make sure you understand the moderators of each theory.

I love prof Krol and I think she is so underrated. Her lectures are not only clear and straightforward, but they are often hilarious too. I have taken her for PSYC 304 as well, and while they can be lecture heavy, if you put the work in and study you can get good grades! (I got A-). Exams are also straightforward too!

The lectures were very interesting. She is a sweetheart and really interested in the topics taught. The only downside is that her questions are very application focused and there is no exams practice. So, make sure you are comfortable with the material. There is also a lot of memorization, so don't leave everything to the last minute.

Dr. Krol is incredibly intelligent and the most captivating lecturer I have witnessed so far as a McGill psyc student. Her lectures are clear, entertaining, and thoughtful and somehow keep the classes attention despite being 3hr 1/week. Very fair tests, with active participation with the content you will surely get an A.

Prof Krol is awesome. Despite being 3 hours, her lectures are super digestable and the midterms were easy. My only complaint was the book we had to read for the class, as it felt redundant after her lectures and there were so few actual studies explained in it - would have preferred a real textbook.

Clearly has a passion for child development and somehow made those 3 hour lectures fly by. Exams were very doable if you prepare. Her excitement in teaching and description of all the studies (plus cute videos of babies) made it very easy to retain information! It's definitely very memorization heavy and the grade is based only on exams.

This prof fully deserves the 5/5 on rate my prof. Her lectures are clear, her exams are fair and she answers questions in class with patience and respect. The book is now mandatory for the class, and I found it a little challenging to study for, but I'm sure she will adjust her strategy as it was the first time she had it. Also, FLEXIBLE grading!

Prof. Krol is amazing--this class was super interesting and the material was presented really well. Her exams were more difficult and detailed than you would expect, but it wasn't too hard overall because of the flexible grading scheme. You'll learn a lot about yourself and others--definitely had therapy vibes at times (which is an added bonus!)

Took 333 with her because 304 was a breeze. However, this course turned out to be a LOT MORE difficult! Interesting material, but brutal exams. Her questions require integration of class material, and exams can be 25 pages long. Nevertheless, she gives clear lectures and presents the material well. Study well and you should be fine!

Class topics were interesting and for the most part easy to understand. However, on the more difficult topics I found she made them more complex than needed, YouTube videos did a better job in learning some of the topics. 2 midterms and one final exam. Overall I would recommend taking this course.
xx

Topics were relatively interesting, but she spends too much time on simple and self-explanatory while rushing through more complicated concepts (math especially) because they are "intuitive". Not an easy class, requires a lot of studying and concentration as lectures go by slowly. She's nice though but I wouldn't take another one of her classes

Professor Laszlo is a fantastic lecturer and knows how to engage students in what may seem like dry subjects on the surface. I've also had her for ECON 313 and will continue taking her courses, because I always get the most out of them.

For this course, three of my four assignments were calculated wrong (added up to a wrong number). Unfortunately, the professor did not apologize for the error. In addition, Professor Laszlo values cost and benefit analysis over the welfare of her students. Her attitude in class does not seem to reflect the way she treats students outside of class.

Very organized + interesting lectures and always looked forward to her class. I have taken her for Econ 313 and 426 - I would just say the exams are pretty difficult, be prepared to study. Usually is helpful, appreciates participation.
Professor Laszlo is an amazing lecturer - even though the course was online, hers was the class I was most excited to attend and found most engaging.

Class questions are usually met with "Sorry I'm not sure I'm going to have to refer you to political science/sociology/demography etc." She resides in the grey area between teaching an entire unit on colonization and economic development and not knowing any colonial history or anything about the million relevant things she labels "other factors".

Lazlo clearly explains concepts and makes economic theory easy to digest. She makes clear what to expect of her assessments making studying for her exams much easier than in other econ courses. I really appreciated that Lazlo provided nuanced and varying perspectives on the politics of economic development and trending concepts like UBI.

Prof Laszlo has been my favourite prof at McGill so far by a lot. She's funny and she clearly cares about her students. She is also very flexible. Her slides and lectures are easy to understand, but if you don't she answers all questions on the spot. Exams are a lot of writing, but I didn't mind that.
anyone know if she's teaching something else this term? debating waiting a sem. to get her again.

I struggle with learning material and she really accommodated my learning style and went over the material with me in office hours in such a relatable way. Lectures are clear enough and engaging but I really struggle with theory readings so the extra help is so appreciated, she really went out of her way to make me understand concepts

I'm currently taking it in the regular term, this is easily one of the BEST profs I've had at McGill. She clearly knows the material and comes up with current examples to make the historical points. She's funny and engaging, she answered my emails within hours, and I got great feedback on my assignment (even tho I got a B). Learning SO much!
Funniest prof I had at McGill, super accessible and made the material fun, even the boring stuff (Kittler!). Always made time and answered emails within a day

He's nice and knowledgeable. Slides are a little boring (black writing on white background, few images) and classes not super engaging but the material itself is interesting. Exams are quite specific but study the slides and you'll be fine.

He is a very very good man! His lectures are interesting but a bit repetitive. There are two presentations and one literature review. He allows students to go free style when it comes to presenting or handing in an assignment. I still have to see if that lands me a good mark!

A lot of info in this course, and his notes are very detailed and long to read. However, knowing the main points for each slide is enough, as his tests make you list say 4 out of 8 mechanisms presented ect and the main points  Long answers are easy, multiple choice are tricky, so study well!  overall, not bad!

IF YOU CAN AVOID HAVING HIM AS A PROF THEN DO.  0 help, comes out as a nice prof but as soon as you need answers for your questions, good luck getting an answer. Grading is hella weird. exams are apparently the same and he never adjusts to match different types of students. Lectures are BORING wich is such a shame cause the material is p intresting

His notes are necessarily wordy. He will present a tremendous amount of material in his notes and also say extra things in class which are not on the slides. The slides are supplemented with extra notes in the bottom, probably written by the TA. Looks overwhelming, but all you really need to know are the fundamental concepts in bold.

Really nice and helpful man. Paying attention in class is hard, and since lectures are recorded, everyone skips it. There are 3 exams comprised of MC and short answer. MC is EXTREMELY confusing (a and b, non of the above type). Lots of list questions and detail memorization. Marking criteria is awkward. Course is interesting, though.

Material is very intresting, the way the lectures are given is very poor, reads of the slides. Attending is a good idea cause yes lectures are recorded but one might get tired after the first 30 minutes and just give up. he says somethings during class that are not on the slides and are on exams. exams are tricky and grading is weird

Explains material clearly, however course material is unnecessarily wordy and there is a lot of it. Lecture style isn't very interesting, you don't really have to go to class (lectures are recorded). Exams can be tricky but they're fair; you need to be well-prepared for them.

Professor Kubow is one of the profs that teaches (Koziris is the other). I found this class to be really interesting as you learn all about proteins, vitamins, fats, etc. in foods you consume. He is easy to understand and knows what he is talking about. Always was able to answer students questions. Non accumulative mc exams, easy assignments.
Excellent prof, answers all questions very clearly, but course content gets boring after the first midterm.  Exams can be tricky but manageable.

I love him, best professor YOU'LL EVER have, the amount of knowledge and experience this man possesses is truly a colossal milestone for an accomplished tenor, he is as good as you can get, cares deeply about his students, and knows how to decode your teaching/learning style.

This professor is one of the best teachers not only within music teachers but in general. He is so kind and caring, and generally cares for your success and wants you to improve. He has a colossal amount of experience in the subject. He taught me so much in a short period of time and is such a good teacher that he could improve my signing so much.

Persistent and clear.  Has a vested interest in the success of any and all students who come to his studio. Teaches solid technique that gives students the ability to have a long, healthy career. His own healthy voice is a testament to the technique he has to pass on.
Charismatic and well-organized lectures.  Concept and theory-based.
Nice teacher, easy to sleep during his class...
The meanest teacher I have ever had!
The lectures are delivered online. The prof is nice but the midterms can be harder. Overall, it's okay and labs are fun.

Went to all his classes prior to test 1, got C+. Stopped going to his class and studied on my own, got A on the 2nd test. Enough said. Classes are boring as hell, my advice is to listen to Jassim's lectures on webct, of course if you can't attend Jassim's lectures because of the time conflict.

you have to take this class.you cant run, you cant hide. i personally didnt like it. took all the terminology in finance and management, and condensed it in one class for engineers. TOTALLY USELESS. no outcome from this class.
Good prof, but killer tests. They need to help us a bit more to expect us to do well.

He is boring as hell. BUT, if you can stay awake (and pay attention) in class, then the material is EXTREMELY easy to understand. He goes very slow, but then you won't have to work hard outside class. Overall, I found that he was way better than his counterpart Professor Jassim (who is more popular among the students).
He's OK.  You just need to work hard.

Too laid back to teach. He won't bother teaching you anything beyond his slides (so why bother going to class?) which basically means you're screwed for your final. Out of two mediocre prof that teach this class, you're better of with Jassim (sad but true).
stupid one. he looks nice, but actually not !!!!!!!!!! having a fun in the class, but dead in the tests

Even if I am sitting in front of the row, and that he is standing next to me, I can't stay awake..I am really sleeping. Don't know why, I really wanted to learn and be awake, but it was a heck of trouble!!!

Nice guy.  Very fair.  However this course is horrible.  Examples in package are long and confusing.  Exams are always different from previous years.  Worst of all, class is useless.  Expect to fall asleep.  Better spend time reading the slides on your own, rather than going to class.
Very Boring and confusing-Do not waste your time, you willlearn nothing-Good for a good sleep.
Super laid back and doesn't expect egregious amounts of work from students (like many profs). Attend the lectures, skim the textbook for non-overlapping content, and it should be an easy A/A-.
Funny and passionate, super laid back. Textbook is important, the final had some textbook exclusive and niche questions.
I LOVE THIS PROF every time I see him teaching one of the classes I'm enrolled in, I shed a tear of joy. King gaskin. Watch the lecture recordings and study class slides for an easy A

I've taken this prof for Intro to Personality, Child Dev, Hormones and Behaviour, and Perception. As long as you read the textbooks (which are always clear), it is super easy to do well in his classes. Even though he sometimes goes off on random tangents when teaching, he is so passionate and makes any class with him fun and very understandable.

Took him for both Personality and Child Development, very nice prof who brings anecdotes into lectures and generally interesting content. Also, tests are pretty straightforward and not trying to trick you, as long as you go to class and read the textboo,k you are guaranteed to succeed

I can understand how people may enjoy his classes, because he is quite funny and laid back. However, his lectures are painfully stretched out, to the point where he sometimes spends an hour or more on less than 5 slides, rambling about simple topics for too long and going on many tangents. His exams were straightforward and easy, though.

I have taken three of his classes, started with perspective and was unsure at first but did so well in all his classes because he explains things in a simple manner. He talks to the class like a friend, makes learning hard concepts easy. Exams are super easy even with minimal studying. Wish I had him for every class! Take his classes!! love him

I had this professor for PSYC 212 and PSYC 332. He was engaging and made the material interesting in both courses. Exams focused on textbook content, but key concepts were explained in class. He sometimes got sidetracked during lectures, but he always took the time to explain things clearly and used real-life examples to help us understand.

I love prof Gaskin. I have taken him for PSYC 212 and 332. While I do not attend the lectures because I find them not necessarily helpful, the textbook is great for studying for the exams. His classes usually follow a grading scheme of 2 mid terms and 1 final. The exams are pretty straightforward and I always get good grades in his classes!

This is my third class with Gaskin, and while his lecture slides can sometimes be confusing, he is such a great prof. He is genuinely so caring and was very generous with rounding. He was very clear with what we needed to know for exams and gave us in-depth outlines of all the units/content we needed to know. He's super silly and makes class fun.

A month after finishing his 3-lecture section, 3 shining and obviously fake reviews are published SIMULTANEOUSLY. Am I implying that a man who described himself as "internationally renowned" as he does wrote 3 reviews to appear competent, rather than accept that his teaching methods are as effective as greased wheels on ice? Perchance.
He gave a great intro about his research. Its amazing to see how the stuff you learn in class is actually being studied in the lab!! Points out what to study for exam. Nice guy!
Good professor. His material is interesting and straighf-forward, not that hard, but detailed. Says what to study from the detailed notes.
I enjoyed the inspirational and passion he has for science. He gave great lectures and it was the first time i heard of transcriptional elongation. I enjoyed the lectures.

He began class with an extensive list of his accomplishments and self-praise, which, while impressive, made the transition into what he had the audacity to call "lecture slides" all the more jaw-dropping. I would expect only a man as accomplished as he describes himself to be to perfect the craft of making something so preposterously unintuitive.

I don't usually give negative reviews, but I don't think McGill should be letting this guy teach. His slides make no sense (it's like a dense disorganised list of things) and he just reads them monotonously without explaining anything. I don't think I should be googling my way through the class and taking 8+ hours to understand 45 mins of lecture.

I absolutely loved her course, it felt like it opened me up to a whole new world. Most of the content is just interesting insect information, and is very understandable. There is a lot of info to memorize. In labs you learn insect ID from amazing specimens from the Lyman Entomological Museum. The prof is super kind and helpful too.

One of my favourite classes! Lectures are super interesting. She will notice if you don't go to lectures. Exams are very memorization heavy, and there are two finals. You learn so much in such a short time. Prof is super sweet and accommodating! Would definitely recommend.

This is genuinely the best class - even if you hate bugs she will make you love them. It is SO fun and fascinating, and you will learn a ton in a really short time. Not an easy class per se, but absolutely worth it. She is incredibly sweet and helpful as well. Just get ready to study since the exams are pretty tough and memorization heavy

This class is not for the faint of heart: it's a lot of material and a lot of memorization. But she is very engaging and tries to share her enthusiasm with everyone. You will learn a lot and no longer find yourself wondering why someone would want to study bugs for their entire life.

She is super passionate about what she's teaching, and you can clearly feel it! The class has one big assignment, and she seems to love looking at themgrading them. The tests were tough though, a lot of memorizing. Definitely made me more interested in the subject.
Wonderful lecturer (ie- enguaging and interesting material), good sense of humour, patient, and ridiculously hot.  We need more profs like this!

Dr Chevalier has interesting lectures. This class is content heavy, however it is possible to do well. She is practically unreachable outside of class so make sure to be in class to ask your questions. Exams are very straight forward, however grading scheme is very nit picky (big on details!). Know your stuff and the concepts and you will do well.

If you have the chance to take this class, please do - one of the most interesting, well explained and interesting classes I have ever taken. Dr. Chevalier is the only professor in my university experience who made me understand nutrition. I got an A by re-listening to all the recordings because her explanations are so good.

Generally the professor is incredibly friendly and interesting. Lectures are long and material is fascinating. The challenge: the amount of material and the fact that material is expected to be practically memorized for all 3 exams. Grading is very strict and deviation from grading schemes results in no partial marks. The final was brutally long.

Dr. Chevalier was a great prof, wouldn't have wanted to take clin 1 with anyone else. Make sure you study well in advance and use the textbook as a reference or ask her questions if you don't understand something, and it is definitely possible to get an A.

Brilliant lecturer, explains everything well, takes time to go over things again. No-nonsense and straightforward. exams are pretty straightforward as well if you've studied well, MCQ very tricky. Definitely possible to get an A

It is definitely not impossible to get an A with Dr. Chevalier. I loved the lectures, they are super interesting. Exams are quite specific and you need to know a lot, there is TONS of material in the class. Overall, the tests are not ridiculously tough, just sometimes too specific and tricky (MCQ especially!)

Dr. Chevalier is a great lecturer with lots of clinical experience and real common sense (unlike others). She is really concerned with students learning, and while the course contents are challenging, she is always there to answer questions no matter how stupid (people tend to abuse this). Best teacher in the department in my opinion.

If you like philosophy you should definitely take this class!! The topics were very interesting and I would gladly take this class again. She made the lectures interesting as we had to always discuss with our classmates some questions that she made (which gave us extra credit).

She summarizes the assigned readings pretty well, and answers questions decently. The course itself was on the harder side since there were only three papers, so each one is weighted heavily. The grading was also inconsistent among TAs.

The grading criteria is extremely unclear; therefore, it is very difficult to achieve high grades. Even though, I took an appointment with the TA before submitting every paper, I still received low grades. I believe this class is extremely hard and unless you are very passionate about the topics, it is difficult to do well.

I know a lot of the commentators are saying she's engaging but that wasn't my experience - the reading materials are interesting to compensate. TA's suck and are inconsistent. If you don't like or are new to Phil, and this class turned me off it, take P/F if you really want to. I wanted to drop the class for something else. Particpation = EC.
She's so nice and always wants her student to participate. Her TAs are nice too

Unapproachable and rude. She's very intolerant of non-liberal perspectives. She also gets angry when you don't address her strictly as "Professor Leary." Also, the grading criteria is not as clear as other commenters make it seem like. When I asked her what "good writing" was, as mentioned in her rubric, there was no clear response.

Very structured lectures that complemented the readings. Super interesting topics and great required readings. She was very flexible about the subjects, for example if you were uncomfortable about a section of the course she did not require you to write about it with no questions asked. Would definitely take this course again if I could.

Prof Leary is really good at explaining and the readings gave varied takes on the subjects. I understood the material on the first paper but still didn't do well but that's because I didn't go to office hours - they will sometimes read your whole paper and tell you what to fix! Learned a lot about the material and how to write a philosophy paper

Stephanie Leary was a nice teacher and she presented the controversial issues as best as she could. However, her TAs grade VERY inconsistently. Be ready to get 90 on one paper and 60 on the other with very minimal explanation.

The mixed reviews on Leary seem to be due to the controversial nature of the subjects she teaches. Leary was the best prof I had for the online format this year with very clear lectures and great video quality- the content was clear and easy to follow and the readings really weren't too bad. She uses thought experiments and polling regularly!

I thought she was an excellent prof. The class itself was great. The guest lecturers chosen were engaging and the class format was awesome (not midterm or final! just a couple quizzes which were very easy if you did the reading). Would recommend this to anyone!

she's alright as a prof, but not a great teacher, and she definitely has her favourites. She is somewhat helpful with suggestions but selectively responds to emails; if she doesn't want to provide you with information, she won't. Not the greatest class tbh, but many found it easy. I just found it annoying.
Killed my confidence and love for writing...

the experiences I had in this call was nothing like what others were saying. The reading is not that much honestly compared to other courses, 3 books across a semester plus some theory. was respectful of other opinions, and really only asked you to back up what you were saying. There is no more final essay, only an exam. No midterm either.

Her lectures may seem unclear at first, but she teaches exactly what she tests you for on the final. I started off the semester not liking her teaching style and thinking she was a harsh grader, but quite frankly her feedback as well as many office hours meetings helped me immensely to succeed in her class. I would for sure take her class again

She assigns way to much work given the fact that this is a seminar, but more importantly she is just not an intelligent person. I had second hand embarrassment sitting in her class because she just had no idea what was going on or what she was teaching. She also just tries to make everything fit into her views, even when it does not.

As a person, she is such a nice lady, but as a professor, I had the worst experience with her. Everything about this class having the workload of a 400-level course is extremely true. Far too much reading and work for a 230 level class. Her lecturing style is more rambling than lecturing. Easily the worst class I have ever taken.

Instructions are vague in the name of "open-endedness and creativity," but she is actually looking for very specific answers that reflect her beliefs. She is an incredibly harsh grader. She mumbles a lot and goes on unrelated tangents. She never actually gets to the point in the lecture, so you never get the conclusion of any aspect of the lecture.

Her grading is very difficult and she expects a lot out of her students. She is grading and giving papers as if her class is a 400 level- which it's not. She rambles in her lectures and doesn't seen to make points. Her final is 4200 words with so many different prompts and expects you to pull from lectures, which aren't recorded.

The material in this class was interesting, it is just SO much work. I took this class ignoring the comments here but if you are taking this as an elective, DO NOT. Attendance was mandatory and affected your grade. Grading was awful, no feedback. SO. MUCH. WORK. I spent 12 hours a week doing readings as prep for class or else grade was affected.

Participation is mandatory, I was anxious every class. Her lectures were difficult to understand because she would mumble at the end of her sentences. This made taking good notes difficult in class (super unfortunate because your notes are essential for the exam). I wouldn't recommend this class to anyone with learning difficulties or anxiety. :(

Avoid at all costs. Prof Posthumus needs to take a course or two in pedagogy; She calls out on students to participate but is not receptive to any opinions or point of views which deviates from her own. The final is a 4000-word long assignment worth 40% of the final grade; I don't know why her department has allowed her to do that...

Menn is a one-of-a-kind professor who really embodies Philosophy and Plato. He eats, breathes, sleeps, and lives it. He's tough; you need to participate, go to class, and try to understand the material. He's actually a very nice guy, but he can be intense and intimidating. But most of all, you have to TRY and not phone it in; he will know.

Menn is a unique professor. Seems cold and tough, but cares about students and wants to see success. Will never fail you if you try. Lectures are slow and sometimes irrelevant but that's just the nature of philosophy.
His pedagogy is just not my cup of tea. If you want to just regurgitate the readings the entire class then, by all means, take him. I commend those who charm him
He's a fantastic professor. I learnt a lot from him. He strokes his beard sometimes when he ponders ideas and it's just the cutest thing!

BEST COURSE EVER! the first few weeks were intimidating but as soon as we got through the beginning it became a chill discussion class everyday. YOU MUST DO ALL READINGS AND TALK IN CLASS! if you go to most classes and participate that is an easy 20% and there are 2 outlines that must be done sufficiently (another easy 20%) there are only 2 essays
genius. & i want to nestle in his beard. i looooooove him

Menn is a great guy, he's really socially awkward and can be hard to get talking, but if you show an interest in something he's concerned about he really opens up.  He also genuinely wants his students to do well and to understand the material.

Prof Menn was my teacher in a ancient greek philo class. He also supervised my honors thesis in philosophy and was absolutely unhelpful. I actually had to go to other teachers in other departments to get help and feedback regarding my research. He seemed absolutely unintersted in what I was learning

This guy is incredible. Stained clothes, unwashed hair, big beard, in his office 'til 9 at night.  Unpersonable, but it's understandable given that he seems to live philosophy.  Don't be intimidated, it's worth taking this class, he'll make you interested.  Mandatory attendence, though.

lordy does this man love greek philosophy...i don't dispute though that he is extremely intelligent and is well-prepared for class...if you keep up with the readings and attend lectures, you will learn alot...on the downside though lectures are excruciatingly boring
Need a 8% on final to pass, after doing his exam I don't think 8% is possible. Feels a certain pleasure failing students . Good luck
Need 8% on final to pass, now I don't think it's even possible to get 8% after doing his exam. He Feels a certain pleasure by failing students. But u can't avoid him so good luck

I am glad I ended up with him being my supervisor in grad school. Fun and kind, but at the same time really smart and knowledgeable in his field, with a unique perspective over it. He gives you the time and space to produce results without pressure, and he is reachable when needed to discuss any matters.

This prof is just way too goofy with his lectures; the in class lectures are a mess and the slides look like they were built in google space. The grading throughout the semester is overly generous but it's impossibly hard to get a good grade on the final.

Nice person, terrible professor. His course is extremely disorganized (we didn't even get a syllabus) and his lectures are all over the place. His exams are fairly straightforward, just asking you to recall what he said in his lectures (which are also posted online). He's not a bad marker (class average B+) but you end up leaving not knowing much.

very unorganized lecture, used same final questions every year. Ours were closed-book in person, while others were online openbook. Truely unfair, tough grading, final class average was like 30%. Terrible prof!!!
Worst professor at McGill! Really low class average and not able to pass this course.
Classes are fine, not much work to do either. Exams are brutal you wouldn't believe the grading.
He's too freaking goofy. Nice guy, not able to teach. Very early concepts were only explained at the end of this course, pretty badly organized.
The WORST professor ever in McGill! I believe he feels certain pleasure from his students failing his course.

Maiya is an inspiration, her class was one of the best PHIL classes I've ever had. While she isnt an easy grader shes clear on what she expects from you and is accessible outside class. Actually do the readings, go to lectures and participate, and talk to her about your work (ie. do it early and go to her). It won't be an easy A but its worth it.

I hated these lectures. They were incredibly repetitive and almost too straightforward, while the readings themselves were hard to follow. The midterm quiz was entirely based on anecdotes mentioned in class. Conferences were quite dry
Excellent prof. Final exam was very fair and overall a very caring professor with good TAs. Learned a lot from this course!

Professor Greenwood is brilliant and kind. Super generous and understanding of students, while having the course remain intellectually challenging. The TAs picked were also very insightful and provided good feedback. The only issue I noticed was that lecture recordings were often posted quite late.

Caring, understanding, and very flexible to meet the needs of students as long as they are communicated. Open book midterm. Multiple choice final with a crib sheet. If you pay attention during lectures and take notes, you will easily excel in this course. Highly recommend taking advantage of your TA for guidance with the essay

DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH PROFESSOR GREENWOOD!!! Very nice guy, but he presents his own opinions as if they're objective, when they're not. If you disagree with anything he says, you'll lose points. The course content was absolutely irrelevant and will honestly make you dumber. Don't know about his other classes, but avoid this one! I feel betrayed.

Amazing professor. His lectures are engaging, and funny (due to his interest in pop culture). He cares about his students and he wants you to do well. While lectures can be fast-paced, they are recorded and slides are descriptive. Permitted index card on final. I definitely recommend people to take this course!!!

Super kind prof, lectures can have a lot of material but as long as you pay attention and take good notes it'll be fine. He's very caring, and makes sure to thoroughly explain concepts so that students understand them. He also records all lectures and clearly wants students to succeed.

Really great professor! Very caring, understanding, and willing to make accommodations for students who communicate their needs. Genuinely tries to help each student succeed and cares about the material he teaches. Provides lecture recordings and posts all the readings online for students who can't be in-person or work better at home.

Swell guy & good professor! Super clear instructions on the essay (instructions were literally longer than my actual essay). Really detailed feedback on essay - which I appreciate. Though I don't 100% agree with everything taught in class, I respect the Professor for actually upholding his strong viewpoints and taking action on them.

My fav prof! He started off the class by telling you how to write essays for his class, makes sure that the class is not too heavy for anyone, and if you just listen to lectures and you will get an A on quizzes for sure. For essays, just go see your TAs for feedback before submitting. He lectures quickly, but everything is recorded.

He's very knowledgeable in his content, but unfortunately, his lectures ramble a ton and don't make clear sense. I succeeded by reading the textbook and heavily relying on TA review sessions. Most students were incredibly stressed for tests/quizzes as we didn't know what to expect despite being given review sheets.

Extremely poor teacher, mumbles, doesn't finish sentences, goes on useless tangents. Crazy hard quizzes, with choices of 40 symphony movements, by heart, no notes allowed, starting at random. This means 7.5 hours of nonstop listening at home to learn everything per quiz, and none of the symphonies are presented in class. Avoid him like the plague.

⚠️Worst prof I have ever had at McGill. It's painfully obvious Huebner writes his own reviews. Not fooling anyone. He says “I repeat things a lot!” whenever asked any question :) Doesn't finish his sentences, doesn't teach! DO NOT TAKE ANY COURSE WITH HIM!!!!! His research pubs don't even substantiate this guy being vetted, a shame on Schulich.

This professor often mumbles and typically doesn't use full sentences while speaking which makes it difficult to follow and take effective notes. In our first listening test we were expected to identify the symphony and movement of a random 30s excerpt from over 4 hours of music. Some people got it but most didn't and fully failed.

I really enjoyed his teaching style.  He covered a lot of ground and repeated things a lot. Lectures were varied.  My TA was good too.  Study Guides for tests were really helpful.  Course is heavy with a lot of content.

With all due respect, this was the most frustrating course I have EVER taken. Study material was heavy and unclear, the prof's delivery during the lectures was poor, though wonderfully knowledgeable, he would often just mumble to himself. If you're considering taking this course as an elective, spare yourself. MUHL 186? The bane of my existence.

Prof is extremely knowledgeable, but omg his teaching style is so disorganized. He would go on tangents and not finish sentences. You'll only really learn the content for tests by READING THE TEXTBOOK. Tutorials provide some help, but textbook is the key. So many terms to study for tests. Extremely content-heavy. Only take this class if needed.

His class was totally unorganized and he basically read things on PPT. His quizzes were extremely hard. He expected us to know everything in the textbook. And he never followed that study guide he gave to us on exams. He had a tough grade evaluation rule and so do TAs. If I had known these, I would definitely not take this course.
Really excellent teacher. Lots of good music. Repeats points a lot.

He had by far the most Inconsistent grading. I got a 36 on a test worth 15% and a 90 on the final. 

He'll often start sentences without finishing them and he tends to go off topic.

He's a lot more concerned about arbitrary points like where Mozart was born instead of the music he composed. We spent weeks on liturgy and one lecture on Bach.

SO AWESOME!! He made the insanely content heavy section of NSCI he teaches really interesting and easier to learn than most could, and showing all the optical illusions to demonstrate what we had just learned was a cherry on top. 10/10 would take this class just for those lectures

BEST PROFESSOR IVE HAD AT MCGILL. He only guest lectured for 4 lectures as part of NSCI 201, but I had to make a review because he was an exceptional teacher and funny as well. Wish he could teach the rest of the class. Extremely clear and inspiring and interesting lectures on difficult concepts 10/10!!!
bad teacher. doesn't solve numerical problems in class. tough assignments.
Bad teacher. Tough assignments. Limited support. No solved problems done in class.
Make a easy course really hard. Close-book midterm and final. Tons of slides to memorize. AVOID HIM IF YOU CAN
Fun Assignments. Good knowledge of the subject.
He knows the subject very well. His exams are tricky :)
GOOD: available for questions, helpful slides, knowledgful & motivated. BAD: very tricky tests, makes you work your ass off to solve assignments UGLY: having to look down, to talk to him.
Class notes are awful, unclear. Workload is unfair. Don't know what's going on in the class.
nice teacher
gg
It's hard to respect a professor who has to ask a student to pull down the prjector screen for him.

Original chill guy. Almost fell sleeping during Farran's lecture. Very fun person, but his lectures were boring even if he is deeply passionate. Has the good guy role in HIST 209's co-teaching but I am pretty sure he is as tough as his co teacher.

Readings in the beginning of the course I found boring and confusing, but for the later section of the course they were more interesting. He is a good and funny lecturer, lectures draw heavily on the readings so sometimes felt a bit repetitive. Didn't love this course as it surveys such a long period. Final was not bad, 100% free response.

He speaks quite slowly, gives outdated readings and has a tendency to fall asleep during oral presentations. Is incapable of using other students' chosen pronouns. Overall did not really take the class seriously, which in turn did not inspire much effort from everyone.

An absolute chiller - so chill in fact that I've seen him dose off during his colleague's lecture. Still, he's an engaging lecturer and quite a funny guy. If you're lost, just wait until he says "as a consequence," and you'll know what point he's trying to make. Tough grade though, so I heard. Pretty sure Prof. Farran did that part of the course.
Good guy - very interesting if you take the time to analyze his material.
The first time a professor has fallen asleep while listening to graded presentations…

Professor Basu is a great and caring guy, seems to be extremely knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches. Lectures can be a bit dry and difficult to follow, but i have found myself learning new and interesting perspectives. Highly recommend if you are of South Asian heritage, as he provides much needed nuance to our history and politics
hes a super nice person. he's funny and outgoing. a bit of a harsh grader but overall, good.

I loved all of Prof. Basu's lectures for this course and can't wait to take more courses with him. He is very self-deprecating about low lecture attendance and boring people - he did not bore me. Prof Basu is funny, knowledgable, and delivers content effortlessly at a great pace.

Great professor, I was in his class where he taught HIST209. The lectures were clear and were easy to follow if you take notes. There is a lot of reading and weekly discussion questions but I found them to be very manageable. The assignments are not too difficult and as long as you pay attention in class.

Sujata is a fantastic lecturer with great energy and presence. That said, her grading is extremely unreasonable. Your midterm and final are graded by U2/U3s and the grading scheme does not give much partial marks so if you make one mistake but the rest of your work is logical you get 2/15. Exams are designed to lower averages with 1 hard question.

Grading felt arbitrary and poorly explained. Even with strong effort throughout the term, the final mark didn't reflect the work submitted, and there was no real transparency around how it was calculated. The class is also far too easy and won't prepare you for IB recruiting. Take Vadim instead. Also she is fake.. does not care and does for awards
Fake teacher, she is fake to your face and does not care for any of her students its all an act and show one of the worst human beings at mcgill.

Sujata is a great prof. She loves her students and cares about them, and makes the 8am class not feel so bad. She makes difficult concepts easy to understand and provides a lot of exercises for them. HOWEVER, the midterm and final are WAY more difficult than the practice she gives us, and I dont feel prepared from just the class and textbook.

Sujata's lectures are pure gold! She prepares you for the finance world, teaches you the actual reasoning behind stuff instead of just showing formulas, and her courses are such a good time! She knows her students' names, her tests are very fair, and it is very clear she cares deeply. If I could take her for every class, I would!

The GOAT! Professor Madan is the best professor at McGill. She cares so much for her students, and she makes class fun. I always went in with a smile, because I knew it would be a great time! Finance can be challenging, but she breaks down concepts so you understand the “why” behind everything you learn. McGill is so fortunate to have her.

Sujata is probably a staple of Desautels. She knows every student by name, and her lectures are very interesting. Her lectures are simpler compared to the exams, so you need to make sure you study on your own a bit.

Although this professor is kind, the courses are not at all at the same level as the rest of Desautels. It might be a fun high-school class, but if your goal is to learn stuff that will be useful for you afterwards, DO NOT take this class. Half of the time is wasted chatting with others, which I agree is nice, but not really useful.

Professor Madan is sweet and makes the class easy, but it may not fully prepare you for advanced finance. Lectures can be tedious with group work. Unstuckstudy was a great study aid alongside the free textbook.
Sujata is a one-of-a-kind professor. She's inspiring, caring and skillful. She had our class standing up and applauding her. Just incredible! She's a superstar!!!

Really good prof, you can tell she cares for her students! She is a very fair grader and is an expert on the topics she teaches. Her evaluations are fairly structured and properly test the concepts taught within the scope of the lecture. The final examination is also very fair, consisting of theory only and saving us from coding by hand.

I have had her all year for intermediate German and she is amazing! definitely one of the best professors, let alone teachers, that I have had! German is a great language and I highly recommend taking a course with her!

Frau Kim is such a caring professor. I took the 202 class as an elective for two semesters (D1/D2) and loved the small classrooms and engaging lectures. The class is not an "easy A" per se, as there is a decent amount of homework and exams, but you will do well if you put basic effort into the class. Would definitely recommend!
Always prepared to answer questions. Even gave suggestions for personal research and interest related to German literature studies (despite I am not an Arts student).

Fantastic professor! She is super caring and is very helpful and patient when explaining anything to you. Lots of homework, but you will have the same amount for any language course at McGill (I speak from experience). Her lectures are always engaging and entertaining. Would 100% recommend.

Prof. Kim is always ready to answer questions (even the dumb ones) in a clear and inspiring manner. She even invited us to discuss more sophisticated etymological questions, despite our complete ignorance in these topics. She is always able to have her students enjoy the lectures.

Dr. Kim is a great professor. She has a lot of respect for her students, especially in the upper level German classes. The class is definitely not easy and has a ton of homework but you always end the class feeling like you learnt something. She cares a lot and you can tell it in her teaching. She even inspired me to take a German language minor.

Amazing prof, one of my favourites at McGill! She is super kind, enthusiastic and her class was always a blast. We got homework quite regularly, but it's usually not very difficult and is great for practice. She is great at getting people to participate and have fun and as a very shy person myself, I always felt comfortable participating in class.

This was my third term with Professor Kim and I have not regretted one second of it. She is dedicated to the success of her students and to the passion she bears for German.
