It is very homework heavy but very doable - just be ready to work. I miss my class dynamic, I had a great time. I also improved a lot. I recommend 100% !

I loved Dr. Kim! She definitely surpassed my expectations for this class. I very much enjoyed the challenging aspects of this class, even though it felt like there was a tad too much homework. But this is a language course which will always come with more than usual workload. Overall, she is an extraordinary teacher and very understanding. :)

Dr. Kim is the most caring prof I have had yet at McGill. She is quite tough but she actually wants you to learn and will go out of her way to help you learn. She wants all of her students to success and fosters a class environment of mutual respect. She values participation, so speak up!

Great course. The reading load is lighter in the summer session than in the fall, and the exams weren't as hard as I expected--she even said what passages would be on them. Jen is easy to talk to outside of class, and she gave quick, helpful advice about the term paper by email. Sure she's a bit quirky, but once you get that it's part of the fun.

I took the class because one of my profs who I assumed knew what he was talking about told me that she was some kind of superstar. I'm sorry, I don't see it. I thought that she had an okay grip on the material, but as a teacher and person, the comments below are right on target. Avoid. Avoid. Avoid

Prof or not a prof doesn't matter.  Anyone that's had a conference with Colin, or John-Christian, or Medrie knows that a Grad student can teach a whole lot better than a Prof. Jennifer was just full of herself and on a power trip.  Terrible. Nasty. Avoid.

She's not a prof., so why don't we put that notion to rest right off.  She's still a student herself.  Basically, I thought she was OK, except a bit nutty at times.  Not my taste, I'll admit that, but she doesn't deserve all the criticism I see here.

absolute psychopath! Completely unreasonable cow! She's an ok lecturer and her exams were also fair enough, but she's an impossible essay marker. Dont try disagreeing with her, either!! Avoid her like the plague!!

Rigid and full of herself; has no clue how to really teach and reach out to her audience, which requires far more than smarts.  Out of touch with students' concerns.  Do yourselves a BIG favour:  A.V.O.I.D.

not really that unapproachable. i talked to her a lot during break and after class. the final exam was easier than the mid-term once i got the hang of it and i was glad we only had to know the parts from the lectures. imagine if we had to know the whole play!

Very unapproachable. She had way too high expectations on students, and assumed we all should have known material cause she did. Very tough marker, and appeared to have enjoyed her power over the class too much..It showed in her marking and response to comments/questions
I didn't think that she knew her stuff.  What she didn't know, she made up.
she knows her stuff but she is an extremely hard marker. it's not worth the headache!!!
Prof Ballinger's course was not the easiest but she was very supportive and answered emails quickly. I learned a lot in this class.
Huge assignments with unclear rubrics, but grading with personal preference.
Lots of chances to express your ideas with group work. Amazing professor. But need to read before classes or you will be excluded from the others' discussion.
Very interesting course with relevant readings and relevant assignments. Professor was very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject matter.
Average at best :(

Took her for 2 classes. Nice person, but you can tell she's a researcher and not a teacher. Her assignments were vague and unclear always had to come back with clarifications. She could have made the class much more than what it was content was not applicable to helping new teachers, purely research based
Miss Ballinger's lectures were sometimes pretty interesting even though its not the most interesting subject. Her feedback on our final project was really helpful.

Very nice teacher although she needs to be more confident and in control of her class. I do enjoy having her but she does not make the class as interesting as it can be ... I feel she can do much better in teaching and having classroom control.
Very nice teacher. Interesting, fun class. Was always available to offer help but could have given more feedback on assignments.
Very nice teacher and always here if you need more help but not does not have a lot of experience in teaching at Uni level.
Overall a good course for 4 credits. She has very good understanding of the course and the class experience was very engaging.

She doesn't know the material well. In class, she tries solving problems but can't find a solution. she grades all the exams herself, so she rushed through grading meaning she doesn't look at your process in depth. Her grades are mostly based on final answer and the diagram you draw.

She is a very passionate teacher and lenient grader as she gives points even for answers that are a mile off  from what the right answer/steps are. Her midterms are difficult, which lead to her having to curve the grades The final exam was ridiculously difficult but as mentioned she curves it with grading schemes/ bonuses.

Prof Gaskin is the most caring professor I have ever seen besides being a great lecturer as far as u study throughout the semester and making her see all ur efforts. Her grading is fair, her lecture is enjoyable and fun, her exams are fair as long as u pay attention to what she says during the lectures and she is always willing to answer all ques.

Great prof, very knowledgeable and she explains super well. She also grades really fairly, and listened to our feedback. Just remember that CIVE 428 is a tough class and it had a lot of long assignments plus a VERY time consuming design project. The experience is worth it tho, and u definitely learn a lot. But there are easier options available.
This is a pretty challenging course but she does her best to make it easier for us. Her explanations are clear, but her handwriting can be hard to read.
The course was pretty hard, but she tried her best to make things easier on us. Her explanations are sometimes hard to follow, but she genuinely cares about her students succeeding.
This course is really hard but professor gaskin is a good professor, she is very knowledgeable and available for questions during and after class. Her grading is also fair and she often curves.

She was a good prof overall. She covers all of the theory in class and solves conceptual problems to illustrate the concepts. Her assignments can be difficult at times, but they are representative of type of questions you'll see on her exams. Her grading scheme is really fair, you can earn a lot of points by simply drawing the diagrams correctly.

Goes over the theory in lectures, and does it really well. But to pass this class, you'll need to understand how to use the theory. And there are plenty of assignments to facilitate this, but they're hard. Get ready to work really hard. The professor is incredibly interested in water resources, and this passion shines through, making class fun.
Terrible mic quality + a little bit of accent + fast and slow speed + many mistakes when talking about the materials  good treatment for low blood pressure.
She's a poor instructor overall; I found that she does not make her expectations clear and handles misunderstanding/conflict very poorly. I wouldn't take a class with her unless required.

She is awesome by presenting materials in an organized and clear way. Even though cytoskeleton is not my favourite topic, she makes everything smooth to go through. Her addition of new research and animations really helps students to understand. Her questions were probably easiest for this course on tests.
Her section was a lot of fun! She does an amazing job conveying her passion for the cytoskeleton.
Very organized and enthusiastic about what she teaches. Her lectures are clear and she is explicit about what she tests on.
Great lectures Well organized and gives good insight into current research (well simplified)

CHEE 456 is supposed to be an easy A for everyone, but he definitely gives some people a harder life. Didn't care much when students asked for the rubric/content of report but turned out giving a very low mark. I don't like his style.

He is a good lecturer.BUT he very harsh in grading, you cannot review your marks coz he will humiliate you and make you feel like you are retarded and know nothing. He thinks he is a good and talk to you in a condescending way, I really do not like him. Very unprofessional

AMAZING. Easily the best prof in the department. His exams are usually difficult and require a very good understanding, but his teaching skills are excellent. Very good prof! His exams test your understanding thoroughly so make sure you get the concepts... Very just in marking, give you the marks you deserve ...
Good prof, interesting lectures and demonstrations.
Very Helpfull and friendly teacher. Marking style: Hard. Tests a lot on concepts. But I certainly enjoyed the course!!! Enjoy :)
good prof!
has a great influence of his personality on teaching

geog 311 is not as bad as others make it out to be, but it def takes effort to succeed. you should attend lectures bc he drops "hints" and the tests are knowledge vomit. you have to study for sure, but it's not hard to understand. i didn't do any readings they're not necessary imo. breau is open, conversational, and welcoming in office hours :)

This class was very hard, much harder than I anticipated. It is reading and specific term heavy. There are lots of complex concepts that will require a lot of your time to wrap your head around. If you are a Geography or Urban Studies student, there are better 300-level classes to take.

Professor Breau is a fantastic lecturer, and definetly a morning person to bring that much energy. The class was really interesting, but sometimes it felt like it delved into unneccesary information. Great lecturer! Funny, engaging, really brought the energy at 8am. Definitely brought the energy for an 8:30. Super passionate & kind. Midterms and final are entirely memorization with an emphasis on key words in lectures. Detailed slides too. Great class overall.

he's clearly a very knowledgeable professor, and he's very welcoming during office hours. The material is interesting, although sometimes a little shallow. Prof. Breau is a very good lecturer, he's also very accessible. Took this class as an elective but you definitely have to study a decent amount.
Great lecturer that is very understandable. Has extensive knowledge on topics and is very intelligent

This professor is truly excellent! Breau is an amazing prof. Grading is hard, make sure you overexplain yourself on tests. Lectures are super engaging and you learn a ton. This is maybe my favourite 300 lvl Geog class I've taken content-wise. He's also supper easy to talk to in office hours and is super nice.

DO NOT TAKE. prof all over the place in lectures, the final was insanely long, we never received our grades for 70% of the course. only ever got back our midterm grade and then overall grade on minerva. when asked for a grading breakdown got told that the prof "chose not to disclose grades therefore we cannot tell you"

Professor Paul repeatedly interrupts students, cutting them off mid-sentence and dominating discussions. During a presentation today, his constant interjections overshadowed the student's work. He is an expert in his field but he does not know how to structure a course. He'd assign over 200 pages of reading per week. Lectures are okay, but rambly and have no slides. He didn't do any of his own grading, and grading criteria was totally unclear. He is unresponsive to emails. His expertise is not worth putting yourself through this.

Pros: funny prof, interesting lectures, knowledgeable in his subject

I thought Professor Paul was really nice and knowledgeable. His class was very interesting and although yes there is only one slide per lecture, if you focus you will be able to follow. I really enjoyed myself and learned a lot.

Mr. Paul is a pretty piss-poor lecturer. His lectures are essentially bizarre lists of poorly articulated incomplete thoughts. He fails to explain the significance of anything he says. The theoretical framework between the "points" he attempts to make is never clear. Extremely tedious to follow.

Pr Paul is very nice and knowledgeable, he is honestly a brilliant man. However, he goes really fast during lectures, it is very hard to follow and write down everything. Also the slides are not sufficient at all so come to lectures or you will have a hard time during exams. The tests were pretty also heavy. It is an interesting class though !

Although Professor Paul is knowledgeable in his field DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS! His lectures are very hard to follow and his powerpoints are useless and don't help us understand the structure of the class. His exams were also graded very harshly and the final exam was way too long (8 single-spaced pages in only 3 days) considering we have other exams.

Professor Paul is a sweetheart, I don't get why people have a problem with him. Yes the lectures might be a bit disorganized and there may not be enough slides to rely upon, but the content is extremely interesting and if you do the readings and focus in the conferences it's an easy A. He's also brilliant - it was a pleasure being taught by him.
POLI 360 with Prof. Paul was great! His lectures contain a lot of definitions and important info but it really helped in order to get good grades in other classes. Great prof and great content!

Professor Taha was an excellent intro to Python professor (MGCR 233). The online textbook provides very clear explanations of concepts and has good practice questions for the midterm and final exams. Prof. Taha is extremely patient and understanding and I've learned a great deal through his course!

Best IT prof at Desautels. Super caring and accessible, will answer your emails within 5 minutes without exception. It is important to watch the videos before class to stay on top of the content, but he always tries to make everything as easy as possible. (He curves to the max). Best prof

Flipped classroom format- short video to watch before class time, which was treated as a lab. Attendance taken every class with some leniency, extremely helpful during office hours, exams were challenging but graded very fairly, overall would recommend!
He cares about what he does and he is tech savvy. You have to watch a video before every class. Good prof if you pay attention, but very easy to get behind.
Professor Havakhor keeps up with current trends in IT and really tries to prepare you to use tech tools present in your future job. Overall, the class is good if you keep up and he grades generously.
I sincerely ask for refund please
hard to understand the material

Worst experience in McGill University ever! The assignments are very very hard and overloaded. And you are expected to finish all by your own. The worst is there is no TA and every time if you ask the professor Tal, she won't care at all. She won't spend time with you and answer your questions! Also the lecture is monotonic and difficult!

Prof Arbel is a very caring and a great person at heart. When it comes to 415, the course is structured so poorly. Professor Arbel is a great professor and really cares about her students. She is clearly passionate about what she is teaching. The assignments are not hard but they are very long.

Professor Arbel is now one of my favorite profs at McGill. She is very well spoken and her lectures are very captivating. The assignments are fairly time consuming but very fun to do. I highly recommend taking ECSE415 with prof Arbel.

Can easily tell that she puts minimal effort in making this course. Slides are taken directly from textbook (full of random images with little explanation) , tutorials are source code that can be found online. Course material is really interesting but not a good instructor overall.
good prof but not very friendly or helpfull
good prof ..makes u want to go to class :)
I just love this prof! Very clear explanation, very concern about the students, and overall, very nice! Exam is quite hard, but if study well from the slides, A is not impossible.
Not great in teaching a class. Picks specific students and Embarrasses them infront of the class. Had the worse experience.

Took cancer epidemiology with Prof.Malagon. It was a very small class. Grades on exams and presentations are super harsh. They gave you very low grades on presentation for no reason. In addition, it seems Prof.Malagon only wants students to focus on selected topics on cancer epi. The location is very far. I would not recommend taking the course.
Not recommended
slides are hard to understand, annotated but her hand writing is terrible. She is good at explaining however i'd say the other prof (first half of the course) was much better for BIOL115
Best 201 prof. Her section was the easiest. Her questions are very fair and easy if you understood the concepts well.
Sang a biology parody song on the first day of class. Content isn't too difficult if you do the textbook problems. She slays.

Prof Western is a great choice! Very fun prof and makes the best out of online school. Her material isn't too hard but you should definitely do the practice questions because she might throw a bit of a curveball on the midterm. She's also great at answering questions during office hours.

Prof. Western is energetic and tried to make the best out of online school. Her material in BIOL202 isn't too hard but her exam is trickier as it's based on your ability to apply knowledge to solve problems, not memorization. She answered questions really well if you saw her during office hours and her lectures were clear and easy to follow.
Prof. Western is very engaging and her class examples are a great way of reviewing course content. She explains the concepts very well and posts fun videos before class, I love her!
Dr. Western is amazing. She was the head of the FSCI research projects and taught us so much.

Super nice and well-organised professor! She really enjoys teaching and it shows, she came super motivated for every class. Her content is easy and her teaching is clear, which makes this section of the course a breeze. Very funny and enthusiastic, 100% would recommend.

Prof. Western is so nice and caring. Her lectures are fun too, and I love her cute passion for genetics. She loves punnet squares and so do I! She inspires me to consider going into genetics.

She is very sweet and clear about course material. Her lectures aren't extremely heavy, she gives good notes, and is really clear about how to solve the problems in her notes. However, these are not enough and textbook problems are mandatory to do well on the midterm!!

The most uninspiring professor ever. Her slides explained nothing. I'd taken physics in high school and the lenient grading scheme saved me but the midterm was impossible. The final was fair but overall she is not fit to teach this class at all.

This was a hard course, not because of the subject matter, but because of Tami. I'm sure she's a nice person, but she should not be teaching first-year physics. Her lectures are disorganized and she had to apologize for making the midterm too difficult. Tami is very knowledgable, so she assumes difficult things are easy. Her lectures and solutions were often hard to follow because she skipped steps/explanations; lectures weren't helpful. Tami's lectures are poorly organized. I understand that she is very educated in her own right, however there were some lectures where she appeared confused by the very subject shes trying to teach. Overall interesting course, other than the fact that we had an incredibly difficult midterm. I didn't mind her teaching in the beginning of the course when I already knew the content from high school. When it came to the topics I didn't already know, lectures felt rushed and unclear. Physics is already rough enough. She's very kind and is willing to take constructive criticism, but can't explain hard concepts well. Every explanation left me even more confused.

Hated this class. Her lecture style is extremely boring and the course content is even worse. Got absolutely nothing out of qual. research methods, was a total waste of time because you can get a 70 with almost no effort

The assignments are doable and 2 of them(#3 and #5) are relatively easy. She was helpful when TA was not, and adjusted grades marked too harshly by the TA. The extra credit is relatively easy so long as you take them seriously. She is extremely approachable, sweet, and caring. If you take her and her course seriously, you'll find it rewarding.

The lecture style is quite dry and can feel dull. The professor seems to focus on engaging students who are already interested, rather than trying to make the material accessible to everyone. Assignments are generally doable, though grading can feel somewhat arbitrary.

Professor Tania Islas Weinstein is a great, kind and committed professor. pop quizzes so must go to class. need to read a lot. interesting lectures but does talk a lot. not clear grading guidelines. kind and inspiring though.

Professor Islas Weinstein is one of those life-changing professors who transmits her passion and critical thinking in a very effective and profound way. Professor Islas Weinstein is admittedly a bad lecturer (enthusiasm, volume), but she is really smart and passionate about what she teaches. The assignments are really unique. You learn a lot from them and they aren't too difficult.

This teacher is by far the most interesting teacher I have ever had. He makes the lectures exciting and informational at the same time. You can't just show up and pass but it is worth the effort to be in his class. Despite his hard grading, I LOVE this teacher.
He's an awesome prof! Very funny and up-to-date. Very helpful too. Overall this is a great class and a great prof!

She was very nice and accessible outside of class. Her lectures are very clear and gives you lots of resources to study from, which are similar to the exams. Overall a great professor who clearly knows what she's doing.
BEST TEACHER EVER AND SO SWEET!!!! nicest prof i've ever had at McGill and the midterm was just like the practice - she is the best take her!!!

A very sweet person, seems like she really knows her stuff and wants you to succeed. She's good at giving feedback, replies to emails quickly, and though her lectures can be monotonous at times, she really tries hard to help. Would take her again!

Sweetest prof ever, lectures are very fast paced but everything is well explained. Slides and examples are super helpful. Professor Sidthidet is well-organized and passionate about the material. Her clear lectures and practice exams are very helpful. Attendance is key, and unstuckstudy is a great study tool alongside the course resources.

She can be hard to understand sometimes, and she explains the material in a way that makes it seem harder than it actually is. Her slides and practice questions are perfect, and they are all you need to do well in the exams.

This prof is well-organized which really makes the class easier, all chapters have assigned questions and solutions. Great summer class. He really knows the material and made it engaging--not an easy task when analyzing exclusively Mozart, Haydn and Beethoven. 10/10 would recommend.

Took POLI 424 with Prof. Owen back in Winter 2020 and it was an amazing class. The material was very much in touch with current issues in media technology & politics. Dr. Hebert is an amazing prof. He's the sweetest little teddy bear, there is no other way to explain it. If you have the chance to take his class, I highly recommend. :)

Best prof. He cares so much about his students and their success. he is a great lecturer and you can see that he is passionate about his studies. If you can take his class, do it. It is an amazing experience and you will learn so much from it.
Professor Hebert is an excellent prof, highly recommend!

Professor Hebert is very nice. He answers all questions fast and is patient. His assignments are mostly readings, so prepare to read papers a lot. Strong-Wilson is an amazing professor. She is passionate about what she teaches and she cares about her students. She offers in-depth feedback that is super thoughtful and constructive. Do the readings, participate during lectures, put in the effort and don't use your phone in her face. She clearly has many years of experience in the field and she has a lot to share! The assignment guidelines can sometimes be confusing, but she's there to answer questions. Be kind and respectful and she will do the same.

Lectures are monotone and confusing. The whole class has to communicate to figure out the instructions for assignments and the various due dates. Old-fashioned in that she requires 100% attendance with a doctor's note and prior notice if you're planning on being sick, and hates that some students like to take notes on their computers while attending a lecture. Instructions for assignments are unclear and she manages students as if they're children (in the worst way). Very patronizing.

Prof. Strong-Wilson is very sweet, but can be strict. She has specific criteria yet does not give harsh marks. This was a very social class with frequent class discussions and group projects. Participation fro most things is not mandatory. This is an excellent class for anyone to take as an elective, but especially pertaining to k/elem majors.

Created an account just to rate her. I've never had SO MANY assignments in one semester. They all took HOURS to complete, and were worth from 2%-15%. She gives feedback through long emails instead of using a rubric. She will take the full 3 hours every time. Instructions are always extremely unclear, but somehow way too detailed? Avoid.

This is my first year in Mcgill as an undergraduate but I still want to say she's the best prof ever. Great prof! She takes the time to give you detailed feedback after each assignment and is willing to help you if you need it. This class was taken online due to the pandemic and she adapted very well to the online format! To be honest, she was the teacher who was the most at ease with technology..! Be prepared to read, but overall good course!

Professor Strong-Wilson is awesome, gives you detailed feedback for every assignment and group works. She respects every student and takes care of them. Normally, you need to read one book every week and do a group project related to the book at class. if you love children's literacy and want to create your own book, take it! Highly recommend!

She is very quiet and the lectures are very boring. All of the assignments are not well explained and when she tries to explain them she just makes it more confusing for the students. She is sweet and overall it's not hard to get a good mark but the class is very very annoying.
Best prof at McGill without a doubt. Great human.
Terry is the best teacher you could have. He truly marked me as a student. I hope to have him again.

He teaches at UdeS too and he is one of the best teacher.
He really cares about his students and he takes time with them. He is super interesting and always makes his classes so fun.
He has a passion that others rarely have.
the sweetest prof ever and super creative, impossible to fail his class
Terry really cares about his students! Definitely one of the greatest teachers I have ever had! i was always looking forward to his class.

He is truly the best prof i've ever had. the three hour lectures would fly by and everything he taught was so useful and interesting. he is a caring prof and wants the best for his students. he is really understanding and easy-going. he answers emails quickly and his feedback is meaningful and useful. i hope to have him as my prof again !

Terry is the best professor I have had at McGill. He is a great lecturer and makes the content very easy to understand. His grading is fair and is created in a way that encourages students to succeed. His feedback is extremely helpful, as well. He is so incredibly kind and personable. Every education student I know who has had him LOVES him.

By far the best professor I've ever had. He is so understanding, and truly wants the best for his students. As long as you pay attention in class you will do great because he is a great lecturer. I would 100% recommend taking one of his courses if you can.
Terry is the best teacher I've ever had!! He gives extremely elaborate feedback on every assignment, and genuinely cares about his students' success.

BEST TEACHER EVER! if you have the chance to take him don't hesitate, his classes are soooo fun, and he is the most considerate teacher i've ever had. He made sure we knew everything before any exam and gave as much time as we needed for it. His explanation are soo good and he was just the BEST teacher!

I enjoyed having Professor Nadarajah, his lectures were clear and even if he got lost he would get back on track. He also provided bonus quizzes to boost our final mark. I deeply enjoyed having Professor Nadarajah, I found his lectures to be quite clear and he was very generous in giving bonus quizzes to boost your lowest grade. Slides/lectures were hard to follow esp for new content, he would sometimes get confused by them. Nice guy though and gave quizzes for extra credit. I found the final to be pretty fair
very boring lectures, lots of opportunity for extra credit, openbook midterm, tough final
A very caring professor.
55% is free, final not that bad. #Tmoney
He clearly cares about his students and is kind. As long as you study you will get a good grade. Lectures are well organized and homework designed to prepare for the exam / midterm is very useful.

Dr. Nadarajah is very kind, but is NOT a good teacher. His slide shows for this course are genuinely incomprehensible. I felt like I was trying to parse out hieroglyphics every time I tried to study. ppl complaining probably don't go to lectures or watch the recorded content. big mistake because he drops critical hints about exams there. not the best at teaching stats but like most math courses 90% of learning happens outside the course.

super engaging, clear delivery of content!

lectures are unclear and unneedlessly difficult to understand. I find that he is very arrogant and egotistical, especially as you talk to him more in office hours outside of class. boring

Excellent prof who is knowledgeable about the material. Learned a lot. Tests are easy if you study.

Super chill class, guaranteed an A if you go to lectures and do the optional problem sets. Awesome lecture notes.
Great teacher!

Material is tougher than Sujata but he's a great prof if you don't mind putting in the work. Plus he changed the grading scheme in order to bring class avg to a B+. Really interesting material and he ties it to current events/news. Replies to emails very quickly.

Great professor, make sure you go to his class, show you're interested, do not get behind though. I always sent him plenty of email instead of going to office hours and he answered them extremely fast. He's nice and clear to understand. Best finance teacher at mcgill!
Tough class but truly cares about his students. Very responsive and understanding over email. Attendance is important.

Great professor! Explains complex concepts very clearly and doesn't belittle you if you need clarification. Always there to lend a helping hand and is accommodating with office hours or questions over email.

I regret taking his course.

He teaches the concepts very clearly. Though class material can be challenging at times, midterm and final was very similar to practice questions. The course is nice but lectures were just boring, and accent is thick so it can be a bit difficult to follow sometimes if you are not paying attention, also there is no conference in this course. he's only the second half of the semester

Schlich is an awesome prof, incredibly knowledgeable about his field and without question an expert in the discipline. Lectures are very well-structured and discussions are also great, highly recommend!

Professor Schlich is hands down the best professor I have had at McGill. Not only is the content being taught interesting but he is a very engaging teacher. very boring lectures, he is nice and organized but you will fall asleep.
accent is thick.
attendance is not mandatory and you can do fine on the three papers if you just look at the slides, but he is very uninteresting. 
nice enough but not a super easy grader.

Caring and always ready to answer questions. There was really nothing wrong with him, but he always sounded really sad and quiet or maybe bored? He's very knowledgeable and helpful though. Graded by three papers, if write well and can use sources you'll do fine. Readings are pretty much optional but very interesting, so you should do them.

Seems to be nice and cares about the material. He tries to engage the students and make sure they understand what's happening. The lectures can be dull but he is good at explaining the content. As long as you do the readings for the papers, you can easily get a B.
Very nice guy, but sometimes lecture can be dull. He went through the final exam format (take-home) with an example. Asks questions to the students to make sure you understand stuff.

The course extremely boring and slow when he lectured. He needs to be way more clear. Reads off slides rather than explains. His accent was annoying a bit. He'a a very knowledgeable prof he's not engaging, and the course itself wasn't very interesting. The final wasn't good and you have to teach yourself a lot of things.

Not as good a lecturer as Professor Wallis, but a fantastic, clear writer. I have re-used his material for other medical history classes to great effect. Very endearing, very knowledgeable, and he led a great latter half of the class!

Long readings felt excessive for a 200 level, and being held to extremely strict deadlines while Prof Soehl would extend them for himself when returning marks was frustrating. I personally found the no electronics policy made it much easier to focus in class, and I also enjoyed the group work. Would take him again but it's definitely not easy.

Extremely disorganized lectures, constantly jumping between slides and topics, making it hard to follow. NO electronics allowed; all notes are handwritten. Very reading-heavy course, with exams based on 30+ readings and lecture material. If you don't fully understand, you won't pass. Very strict grader. Long, difficult exams. Not recommended.

Professor Soehl does go all over the place when he does lectures, but he is very open to student participation, which makes for good conversations. Lots of group work which is relatively easy. Exams rely a lot on the readings so just make sure to understand them well. Also, memory aid allowed for the final exam, which was very helpful!

He has a tendency of going all around the place, lectures were chaotic and missed to follow a precise guide line. HOWEVER, readings were really great, I learn a lot with them. You need to expect to read a bit and do every week group-projects

SOCI 212 was an interesting but quite hard and very time consuming class. Lots of heavy readings. The teacher is passionate but not very clear and goes really fast. Many graded group projects. Final exam based on readings' content. I would consider this class a 300 level rather than a 200.

The worst professor. Does not care about his students or helping them succeed in his class. He tried to go to office hours for more help, and he laughed and gave no feedback. Lots of reading which makes no sense, and harsh group work grading. Does not actually lecture but rather rambles and gives no information. Tests impossible.

The material for this class is amazing, but professor Soehl is not. He is extremely unreasonable in his quiz grades, especially given the fact that its a 200 level course. Do not take this class if you don't like group projects. Expect to get one letter grade lower than what you usually get if you take this class.

I loved this course! It isn't difficult to succeed if you're interested in the topics. However, if you're taking it as a credit filler hoping for an easy A, stay away from this class. I personally find prof. Soehl's class is quite confusing and boring. He only cares to elaborate a little on the slides when he feels like it (only on the topics that he cares about). Please stay away from Prof.Soehl's classes.Some say he's a "hilarious lecturer" : I can't vouch for that, his lectures are extremely boring, long, he has a bunch of slides but only let us catch a glimpse (we took picture of the slides on our phones to actually be able to note down the content, but even so, hard of the slides don't make any sense).
He is amazing

Best prof! Hes very passionate about the material, so he makes it very interesting. He goes over heavy theories, breaks them down and makes them seem simple and intuitive. His slides are clear and up to the point. And finally, his grading scheme is fair. Overall, this was an awesome course!
great prof with great humor. fair final but weekly quizzes
Favorite class. Lectures are helpfull and since there are weekly quizzes, you should go to class unless you can keep up on your own with the posted slides. Final was a breeze.

Very enthusiastic and also hilarious. Makes the lectures very interesting and simple/straightforward. Just do well in weekly quizzes. All profs at mcgill need to be like him!

Caring, helpful and extremely well spoken - on top of being an easy grader. Eases you into theories with clear explanations and relevant examples. Rather than immersing you in math, he gives you actual insight into the physical nature of circuits. Labs are fun and nicely organized.
Amazing professor as a whole. Final exam for 2018 was super easy. enjoyable class. Study for the quizzes every week and youll nail the course.
Good first insight into GIS. Tim is nice and always happy to chat.

The exam wording is so unclear that even if you study, you're stuck trying to decode the questions instead of showing what you know. Dr. Elrick is a wonderful individual and really tries to make the content engaging. I personally wasn't so interested in the material but his lectures were enjoyable to attend. I don't know how can you not like Prof. Elrick! Extremely funny, cool, approachable! Prof does everything to make sure his students do well. Labs were fairly easy, quizzes were online, and final project was a breeze if you did well on the weekly labs. Course content was dry at points but Elrick was overall a great prof.

Very caring and intelligent professor. While the content of the class lectures was dry at times, I found the lab assignments to be interesting. Overall the class was enjoyable enough and pretty straightforward, with two midterms, lab assignments, and a final project.

Tim Elrick is very kind and an easy grader, but I hated this class. Cares a lot about students, nearly every test has been curved. There's about 1 lab/week and they tend to take an hour or less. The info can be a little dense and you might need to rewatch lectures to fully understand him, but it's easy to do well in this class.

Tim was one of my favourite math professors. The course was challenging, but he explained concepts very clearly and made the material much easier to understand. His well-written LaTeX notes were great for reviewing and catching up, and his lectures were interactive, engaging, and funny.
Would not recommend this course. My advice: drop it.

His lectures are pretty nice, and the lecture notes are also good. But the feedback is disgusting, and when you ask him a question, he makes sure you understand how dumb you are for asking it.

Charismatic professor with hard assignments and amazing lectures. Might be a little "theorem lemma proof" heavy but what pure math course isn't. Ridiculous grading. I got all the midterm questions right but a 60% and he wouldn't tell me why. Professor Warren is not only one of the best professors, but also one of the best people I had the honor of meeting. Great guy who knows his stuff. Although he doesn't seem very receptive to negativity. Overall, fair professor who wants you to learn, not jump through hoops.
Great teacher, easy class not too demanding, he is not the typical hippy dude

Amazing teacher. Eloquent speaker- very inspirational. Challenges the very foundations of everything you've learned in your lifetime. Really takes the time to help you because he cares. Down to earth. Fair marker-if you pick something you're passionate about for projects, you'll do very very well. Take this class. Changed my life.

Ikeda Sensei is the best Japanese teacher! This class is tough because there's a ton of homework and quizzes, however we can feel that it's worth it. She makes the class active and not boring at all, she's really sweet and is really accessible outside of class if we have any questions or worries. I definitely recommend taking a class with her!
Amazing prof, she is so sweet and caring. If you can please take ur class with her. I sucked at Japanese but she was very understanding and was happy I tried.

Ikeda sensei is the best, sweetest prof I ever met in Mcgill.The class is not hard but get ready for the weekly quiz. Go to the class, review, and do all the homework after class, and you'll get an A! Her class was pretty chill, she asked the class to email Japanese music and played it every Friday class. Definitely recommend her to everyone!
Ikeda Sensei is a great prof, but get ready to work hard for your grade in this class. There's homework due every class, quizzes, group presentations, and tests throughout the year.

She is sweet, nice and caring. There are 6 tests and lots of quizzes throughout the year, you really need to put effort into studying. Her lectures are clear and useful, what she tests are exactly what she teaches in class. She is always accessible outside the class. I learnt a lot from her. Strongly suggest taking classes with her.

powerpoints a bit bare-bones, with minimal explanations, not enough to prepare for grammar on exams or short texts. textbook is better. work graded very harshly even for low levels. you will learn more with self-study in less time, and be better able to understand the particularities of the language.

Hands down the best professor I've ever had in university. She is extremely caring, sweet and organized. Always accessible online/offline, truly wants you to learn and have a good time in her lectures. I would most definitely re take her classes. Wonderful experience.

Easily the best teacher I've ever had in my life. Always there for you when you need help. Extremely patient with anyone. If you're interested in learning Japanese during the summer, I highly recommend that summer course. Can be a bit intense, but if you're into it, it'll be a lot of fun!

Ikeda sensei is extremely patient, so you can feel comfortable asking her questions during and after class. She is strict with class regulations and homework corrections, but it is to help the student learn as much as possible. If you do your regular homework and prepare for small quizzes, it would be hard for you to fail.

Ikeda sensei is very helpful in and out of the class. She is super patient and  open to questions. There are many quizzes and presentations marked so there are plenty of chances to get grades up. She is strict with details so be sure to pay attention in class and do all the homework. Hard work in this class is required but worth it.

takano is the goat, simply. good slides, good explanations, really generous exam questions, super kind person. literally a textbook perfect prof. no more needs to be said. if u can take her class, take it. she will be awesome
She truly made this course bearable. Her questions were amazing and she explained super well.

Takano taught the renal section of PHGY 210. She explained her part very clearly and her questions on the final were very fair if you understood the material. She is a gem of a prof in an otherwise quite difficult class! Her section was a breath of fresh air compared to the others.
Her slides are so minimalist yet effective. She goes at a perfect pace in class and makes topics very digestible. Incredible teacher and clinician, there is a lot to learn from her !

Great lecturer! Favorite part of PHGY210 this year by far. Very clear and simple slides to explain the important parts of renal function. Appreciated the addition of common diseases and stories to remember the material.
She's ADORABLE. Her renal section might seem very confusing at first but she explains it very well and goes at a really good pace. Her questions were fair as long as you understood the concepts well.

Dr. Tomoko Takano is the best prof out of all the phgy 210 profs. She explains her material in a very clear way, and it is very easy to understand. Her exam questions are very fair unlike another section (cardio...).
Nothing ever unclear in her lectures, she makes complex stuff easy to understand.

She is super clear-cut, explains things very well, and her lectures have a very good structure. Her exam questions are fair - nothing insane or unexpected will pop up. Watch the lectures, know her slides well and it should be no problem.
amazingly clear

This class is tough and not easy to be taken as elective. Even though a Crib Sheet is allowed both for the midterm and final, exams are hard, long and not straight forward. Overall, this class is too difficult to be taken as elective. Avoid

The good reviews below are obviously written by TA's or herself. Both the midterm and the final are crib-sheet allowed, but the focus is on super small specific details that you might not even think of writing down, rather than obvious generalities you could easily deduce with common sense. This is not an easy A class by any means. B+ avg says it.

Prof Webb speaks about astronomy in a way that makes you really want to invest more about the topic. It is very clear that she loves the topic she is teaching and she does her best to share that love. Her assignments are pretty easy to complete, but her exams are very in-depth. However, you are allowed a crib sheet for both the midterm and final.

Tracy is amazing. The midterm was a bit tricky, but the multiple-choice questions are very straightforward, straight out of the slides. Weekly quizzes really do help. The final was all mcq and was pretty easy. Crib sheets are permitted for both the midterm and final. The term project is pass or fail, pass if you complete it (10% of final grade).

Great course, especially easy for stem majors. Her exams are so easy and you get a cribsheet. The lectures may be a bit boring but she's so kind and passionate so it's all good. They are recorded too. I stopped going to lectures and just wrote a great cribsheet and aced the midterm with no studying. Lots of easy grades too so not just midterm/final

Tracy is a great lecturer who cares about her students. She posts all of her slides, records her lectures and posts weekly quizzes so there are a lot of resources to succeed. Although some lectures are a bit formula-heavy for non-science students and can be confusing at times, her passion for the subject makes it engaging. Cool elective overall.

Tracy Webb is a good prof. who clearly cares about the subject. She is available by email. She posts all lectures and slides. The class sometimes goes way in depth about math/science concepts for a course aimed at non-science students. Some lectures are wildly boring. Some are cool though, and I'm sure for a STEM major it is a true bird course.
great prof and an easy class if you have basic knowledge of physics prior to taking the course

Great lecturer and available outside of class. The course is easy going, and coding labs are very practical and useful (code is reusable is many other contexts). Small classes, so you get what you put in (participation). Definitely recommend!

A most pick course and prof!!! Tracy is so lively and joyful which brightens your day so much. Her Milky Way Inside & Out course is super interesting and is definitely one of the best course I have taken so far. The material is very easily digestible and the midterm and final aren't difficult. Take if you have elective space. You won't regret it!!
GOAT prof in my book.

Your grade basically depends on annotated readings and short responses that are graded pass/fail, so it is very easy to do well. No midterm or final. Lectures and course material is interesting, but I felt like Professor Bruce had a bit of an attitude sometimes...he is funny but in an intimidating way. That being said, he is nice in emails...
Wonderful Professor, very easy but I loved the subject material, would take again

I would suggest taking this course for anyone who wants to study history since time is spent at the beginning of the course introducing the discipline of history. Prof. Bruce is an excellent professor. There is no final exam, you don't have to attend lecture since it typically isn't relevant to what we are assessed on and there are heavy readings

Professor bruce is an amazing lecturer, not a lot of reading compared to other classes, no final, however there is a group project, absolutely no need to go to lectures after the first few weeks, as long as you do the assigned reading youre all set.

Professor Bruce organized this class so well. Even though there were no exams/quizzes, I feel like I learned so much more than I did in my other classes with exams, as the perusalls weekly really helped my understanding. Its nearly impossible to not get a 100% on all conference writings/perusalls. I really enjoyed the course content and structure.
woooooooooooooooooo

At first, I didn't like him too much. But I've grown to love him; he is my favorite history professor at McGill. He will totally change how you see and do history and prepare you for any other history course. You have to "adjust" to him, but lean into it, reach out to him, and you will learn a ton. Don't be soured by his sassy personality.

I only say this class was difficult just because the content is very theoretical and is all new concepts that are a little hard to grasp at first. We did two perusalls weekly, and while those were long and often hard to understand, they enhanced my learning and were the basis of each weekly discussion. Overall a great class and a great professor.

Super great professor and is definitely not condescending at all. I found his grading fair and his lectures were super interesting and funny. I would definitely take this class again, except beware of the perusalls (not bad at all, just a lot of reading).
Approaches brass in a beginner friendly way and has a great understanding of how to get results. Essays are straightforward, just follow the directives and you're gold.

Brass Tech with Trevor was great!! He was really helpful and explained concepts clearly.  If you're not getting something in class, he'll work with you individually right there until you get it.  Also not that much work involved, just prepare for playing test and you're golden - he's very straightforward with what he wants.
Sweet
Damn, some sweet.
No Comments
No Comments

Trevor is the bestest teacher ever.  He always has time for his "favorite" students.  While I don't know why he likes Discovery Channel so much, I hope that if I play my instrument well, or maybe his, that I can get into his good books.  Did you know that Scott is turning 40?
Trevor's the best because he just says it like it is.  Great player, great sound, and such a sexy ass!

Do not take. Trust me.

Professor Ponech is an awesome teacher - not sure why his ratings are so low? Slightly intimidating, but he makes himself very available, gives extensive feedback/help on assignments, and is a generous grader. He's super passionate, and is encouraging if you choose to participate in class. One of my favourite professors at McGill.

I would not take this class unless required; if not, at least take it P/F. Thought the topic seemed interesting but only screwed up my GPA, we unfortunately do not receive feedback for many assignments making it difficult to understand his grading scheme.

The class is once a week, lectures are long, hard to follow without a good visual aid. His slides, if used at all, are either a huge block of text or one sentence linked to the general discussion. He takes months to grade (out of 3, 4, or 8, limiting chances for high grades). Despite being an elective, the lowest grade I've received at McGill.

Harsh grader while giving no feedback throughout the semester so there's no way to improve. His lectures are inaccessible and repetitive. While he seems to care about the topic, it was very difficult to be engaged in the class. Overall, he was ok but I would not suggest taking the course unless you have to.

Clearly favours male students. Lectures are filled with irrelevant rambling. Course material pulled from white male authors with little diversity or modern relevance. Grading is subjective, quick to shut down ideas instead of accepting other perspectives. Gives little structured direction on assignments, yet extremely critical when grading.

I think Ponech is a great professor. He makes himself available outside of class, and very approachable / personable in my opinion. Can be a harsh grader, but not without reason. Out of all the English profs I've had at McGill, he has by far given the most tangible and helpful feedback to improve my writing. Would definitely take him again!

I took this course alongside two 400 level courses yet he grades harsher than the teachers of the 400 levels! Does not allow for extensions etc, so be careful about not turning assignments in, however trivial they may seem. Class concept and content is super interesting but three hours of straight droning on and on is not...
Very very very harsh grader. Failing the course even though I have a 4.0 GPA. and SOOO uninteresting

He is nice but extremely mediocre as a prof. Also, he is super deceitful in the way he grades: tells you to do one thing then grades completely different and unnecessarily harshly. Waste of 3 credits.

ANAT262 is incredibly boring. Overall, I hated this class and Dr. Stochaj was one of the worst profs in it. Unreasonable with her grading guidelines during covid (it was written answers), her slides are messy and she gets super defensive
She is a pretty easy prof but shes mean and not helpful at all. avoiddddd
Very unclear with instructions and does not care about her students. Avoid at all costs!
Lectures are incredibly boring. Overall a bad prof. At least her exam questions are easy.

She has a strong accent with slow speaking speed which is fine to me. The materials she presented were not interesting but she made it logical. However, I found her questions hard to answer since she always tricks students with either small details or confusing written. Her part on final is almost unrelated to what she presented. She is nice tho

Crystal clear. She really made the material interesting by linking it to diseases. She goes through everything slow and often gives summary charts and animated slides for protein transport. It is really easy to remember, lots from bioc212 (like OXA and TIM/TOM complexes etc). Her questions are not as easy as Presley, but still really doable.
I love her accent ! Really clear, and organized and at the end of the day, when you review the material, it's crystal clear. One of the best prof of ANAT 262 with Kollman !
pretty straightforward and interested in teaching. besides all she taught is from her own research and very useful. :)
she has the best english accent i have ever heard.
a professor who can truly teach. in all honesty, the material is quite dull, but shes probably the only cell biology prof who makes the learning so engaging!
Fantastic!
I'm loving this class!
You will learn a lot! Prof. Madej-Krupitski is very passionate about the material and gives great lectures. I found her very helpful during the office hours.

Heavy course material but she makes it easier to digest and comprehend, learned a lot in the course that was not covered in high school, content was very interesting, one midterm, 2 papers, conferences (every other week, mandatory participation and attendance), gave back all assignments including midterm, highly reccomend
I loved this course! She is a great professor! I would take it again.

she lectures well and is knowledgeable + the material is interesting, but lectures aren't recorded so attendance is mandatory (unless you have friends that can send you notes). downside is she never answers emails and office hours aren't useful, so getting questions answered isn't easy. lots of readings, but i feel you can do okay without them.

Absolutely a fantastic professor and person. Her lectures are very engaging and do not include any of the typical reading off of slides. This also means that to succeed, you must go to the lectures but with Prof. Madej-Krupitski, you'll want to. She is an incredibly smart person who wants her students to succeed. Would take her class again!!

Great class. Lectures were always super interesting and engaging and Professor Krupitski is one of the most knowledgeable profs I've had at Mcgill. Grading criteria for the essays could be unclear at times but the TAs were always accessible and willing to help.

This class is easily one of the most interesting classes I have taken at McGill so far. Professor Madej-Krupitski is passionate and caring, and I loved attending her lectures! The class in itself requires a decent amount of work, but is 100% worth the time and effort. I would strongly recommend this professor and this class. :)

Amazing & caring prof. Accessible outside of class and genuinely wants to help her students succeed. Get ready to put effort into this class - mandatory conferences, in-person test which requires a lot of memorization, 2 essays.
Very dry lectures but the tests were fair and he graded the assignments/project very generously

Vadim explains concepts relatively well, but in an extremely dry way. I had trouble focusing at times. He does grade pretty forgivingly on assignments, but his exams are all multiple choice, so part marks are not possible. While I did appreciate his explanations, I feel he was lacking in concrete examples at times
Great prof, who gives lots of materials to succeed. Exams all fair, lots of resources and extra help to succeed.

Straight to the point. He prepares you for the assignment, midterm, and final and excludes extra material not relavent to helping you pass. If you do not understand in class then there will already be extra help in his my courses so you can always keep up or catch up.
Good clear lectures. Kind grading. Good feedback.
Nice prof and the course is quite interesting, but you do need to practice a lot

The lectures drag on a lot and can get boring, but he's a nice guy. Not very engaging but for MGCR 341 you will mostly just be doing his practice problems which are identical to the exam questions. During lectures he will speed through things, but if you need help just ask, and he'll explain things better.

Vadim is the goat. Lectures can be boring but cover the material very well. All you have to do is start reviewing the practice problems well before the midterm and final respectively, and you are good to go. Tests are very straightforward, all multiple choice, and are based on the practice problems.

Vadim is a good teacher. He explains concepts well, goes over a sufficient amount of practice problems, and is always open to helping students and going over a concept again if required. Graded by few things but the assignments are a joke and the fests are fair. Only downside is his lectures can feel like monologues, but overall hes a good prof.
This guy is writing his own 4 and 5 stars review comments.
Great professor, but above all person. Quite possibly the most down to earth person at McGill and a very talented person at explaining difficult subject matter.

Terrible professor, you must be good at teaching yourself to succeed in this class as what she will test you on will be leaps and bounds different from what is taught in class. She forces herself to give tons of part marks bc no one ever comes to the write answer on the tests bc of how much more advanced the qs are then what is shown in class.

She's a very sweet person and understanding, doesn't berate you even if you have a dumb question. Tests are open-book but don't let that make you think you don't need to practice or thoroughly understand the concepts though.

Decent lectures but the in-class examples are what will get you through the class. She is a very generous grader but that won't save you because the tests are really hard. She gives a lot of assignments but everybody cheats of them sooo.
She's a kind professor and she really does understand the properties of food materials. A good instructor too.
I loved the professor's ways of teaching.
very very sweet but not very knowledged

Subject matter was very dry, it was hard to pay attention in class. BUT no textbook, exams were a breeze (most problems were JUST like those in class -- so write the solutions down! The tests are open book!). She's also really nice and happy to help you out. Also the project for that class was neat actually.
No Comments
No Comments
Mind blowing.

Very interesting and entertaining lectures. Nice and sweet professor. TAs in this class are excellent. Not a very demanding class in terms of work (only 1 midterm and 1 assignment) but a lot of reading.
Conferences are so important for this class, they make the lectures so much clearer.

Muniz-Fraticelli is a very knowledgeable and talented professor. He is extremely charismatic and his lectures are  funny and interesting. He has a distinct passion for jurisprudence and the study of ancient societies (ex. roman and Greek history). Be ready to read a lot and be able to compare different political thinkers for assessments.
He's a really good teacher however, he sometimes spends 3/4 of the class contextualizing the reading, which is not necessary for the exams

This course is very philosophical, the prof doesn't use slides or notes or anything, so you really need to pay attention during lectures. He's very funny and engaging, and keeps the course entertaining. There are a lot of readings, but you can honestly get by without doing them and just grasping the main ideas. GO TO ALL CONFERENCES AND LECTURES

Very interesting prof, and (mostly) captivating topics/readings covered, but lectures were not very useful for any kind of studying as they were mostly context and background information  and not elucidation on the readings. Conferences were great though!
really passionate prof, amazing TAs, but lacks structure in his lectures + no slides. Get ready to google most of your info

lots of heavy and long readings. no visual support for lectures, he just talks for an hour without clear indications (often more about context/author than the material). conferences + TAs save this class imo. 1 midterm (not hard), 1 writing assignment (long and unclear), 1 final (lots of writing, expected to know all readings)
don't take this

An academic of the highest order, Prof Muniz-Fraticelli is what one idealises when considering attending a first rate University like McGill. An authority on countless political theorists, crossed with biting sardonic humour to keep you on the edge of your seat every lecture. If you want spoon-feeding and overly friendly BS go back to prep school.
Such a harsh grader for no reason. As a prof he does a great job at having entertaining lectures and teaches the concepts well, however your papers will rarely be above a B+ and the TAs are no help.

he is so obviously well-versed in the subjects, but the lectures sometimes do not relate to our readings at all. readings take very long to do, and are sometimes very hard to understand, and the lack of focus on them from the lecture does not help. ta quality varies greatly. grading is also very harsh. only take if you really enjoy plato, locke etc

Great prof! Class isn't super easy if you don't have a physics background, but is if you do. She does class demonstrations every week or two, usually on Fridays. There is a textbook but its completely optional and you don't need it at all. She's very nice, she even makes slides with cute puppies and kittens on them to keep people engaged lol. 10/10

this prof is very lovely! however, i found the course material was far more difficult than what it was advertised to be sometimes, given that phys 181 was advertised as a basic physics class for art students. she definitely was very passionate and helpful, but i felt a bit misled by the course introductions and found it difficult to keep up.

I am SO happy I got to take this class. Kaspi is the sweetest professor and her class was super interesting. It wasn't necessarily an easy class but if you watch the lectures and put some good thought into the quizzes, it is completely doable. I really wish I could have taken this class in person but so glad I got to take it regardless.

Wow I can't really express how incredible Professor Kaspi is. She is the pinnacle of an incredible professors. Not only is she extremely caring she is also so passionate. Everyone at McGill should take a course with her. I will say though the online format of this course was tough, but with Kaspi you feel like anything is possible.
I had Dr. Kaspi for PHYS 183. It was a few years ago, but I still remember her and I really liked her class. I thought of writing this here because I think everyone else would enjoy this class too.
She is a great professor. Clearly loves what she does and it makes you enjoy the class even more.

Altough this class says it has no prerequisites I definitely struggled to get good grades. Prof. Kaspi however is always cracking jokes and making us laugh during the lectures. She explains really well and will not hesitate to repeat as many times as needed for everyone to understand. She is passionate about the content of the class and I loved it!
Best prof at McGill!! She is so passionate about what she is teaching and makes it so interesting. I really enjoyed the class and I hope I can take another class with her.
What more can I say, she's the best. Please do yourself a favor and just go to class, she'll make you wanna study astrophysics for the rest of your life.
She is really really passionate about astronomy and the universe. The course is very intriguing as well. I feel sad for people who don't show up to lectures. You missed a lot of good stuff.
In his mid 80s, time to pass the torch. Seems likes he's minimizing teaching as much as possible with these one lecture every two week bs

Pretty good professor. The class had a hybrid structure, with more challenging content taught online and supplemented with good resources. Same exams as the other class section which were fair. Only annoying thing was the group project which was marked fairly tough (not a guaranteed 85+). Average for the project was probably around an 80.
Honestly probably the worst prof in desautels. Avoid at all cost.

Had no clue 2008 was upon him. When I mentioned that the US was doomed he gave me an F.  I guess my F stands for alot more than his education ever quoted. What do you think now professor?  Still buying into the garbage that you are teaching!
brilliant man, makes you figure things out yourself. excellent course
"Don't bother me... don't call me... no emails...no questions...no office hours..." No Professor!!!

A very tough grader with content-heavy slides. The class consists of three difficult midterms (30% each) and one group project. This class is interesting in terms of content, but his exams are so difficult that it is impossible to enjoy.

Taught animal biotechnology and all of the material covers recently published work in the field which is amazing and super interesting. He happily answers all of your questions and has flexible office hours. He is extremely helpful and patient and he truly cares about his students. You are evaluated on 3 midterms and 1 project. Take this class!

Here for only 2 lectures, but somehow the worst 2 lectures in the whole course. It's like he interrupts himself at the start of every sentence, and can never finish his thought. Have to rely completely on chat or the textbook to learn his content.
one word: "nachurallie"
He did a "cameo" in the course and his exam questions were easy if you learned what was on the slide

Professor Astvansh's course and teaching methods were very disorganized and misleading. He had many instances of having unclear expectations and being mad when students did not fulfill them. He was rude to students and misleading. This course and dealing with him was quite annoying and something I would strongly recommend against experiencing.

Probably the most consistently uncomfortable class I have ever had. Professor Astvansh does the complete opposite of fostering a supportive environment conducive to learning. His expectations are unclear and the course's organization and delivery were far below McGill/Desautels standards.

She is overly harsh with grading, gets mad at you for asking a question. Like she will genuinely get frustrated/surprised that you are asking a question out of confusion. Puts people on the spot as well (for being late, for answering a question in general or on a quiz incorrectly). Hard to succeed in this class.

She is really mean, but I liked how she encouraged students to pronounce and read out loud. She also doesn't really explain things well, and when you ask her about something, she just repeats it without really helping.
You will definitely learn some French, but I probably should've listened to the rest of the reviews when I was deciding whether or not to stay in the class early on...
Really tough grader, expectations for french speaking ability were extremely high considering it's a beginners french 101 class. She kinda just yells at people in class instead of properly teaching.

she's funny and nice but can be really intense---might yell at you for asking a question. Her grading was harsh especially for an intro to french class, but this also might've been because of the language department standards. she has a tough attendance policy, telling us we needed a doctors note 5 days in advance to get a test rescheduled

Avoid this class at all costs. She may appear witty but is actually just impatient. She is an extremely harsh marker despite teaching absolute beginners French. Real example: We had to write a paragraph of 80+ words marked out of 20 on a test. She took 1 mark away for EVERY typo/error. Her class' averages hover around 52-65%... Leave while you can!

Insults students, does not explain linguistic terms before using them at all, is very impatient, requires you to buy a disorganised 50-dollar textbook and grades ridiculously hard for a 101 course. If you do not have French experience and/or experience learning a second similar language, she will not like you.

I took FRSL 101 and 102 with Prof. Kwan-Lock and got an A in both. It seemed like many people thought this would be a bird course, which reflected the effort they put in. The effort you put in dictates what you get from this course. If she sees you are participating in the class and trying your best, she will be more inclined to help.

Funny and witty personality, but extreeeeemely tough grader. I took FRSL 101 with a different professor, and with the same effort put in, I got much better grades compared to FRSL 102. I definitely suggest S/U'ing the class because with this professor, it would be a real GPA killer. Very likeable character tho.

If this class isn't for your major or minor, don't take it. If you don't come with prior knowledge she will not like you, and if she doesn't like you she won't teach you. She yelled at me for asking to see her in office hours, then when I did come see her she scolded me for asking questions from “old content”. Just don't take her class

Prof. Narain only presents one side of cases/arguments which takes away from the "audi alteram partem" we are supposed to foster. More of a sociology course than a law class. We only really covered 3 sections of the charter. She showed a marked lack of respect for students, and would cut them off while they were speaking. would not take again

She's an incredibly funny and caring professor. Exam was ok (choice between multiple questions + 3 days to do it), but she gives a lot of readings. Her class clarifies the reading; you could pass by doing them and minimally attending. Will tell students to shut up (or answer "in three words only") when necessary, which is refreshing

She is a kind soul and very accessible outside of class. Do the readings as lectures build on them. You are expected to have read your cases, understood them and be able to critically engage with them and other materials in class. Pay attention to her ppts as questions on the slides will be on the exam.

Although she is very sassy, I will take a bullet for her. I barely attended the class as a 1L due to exhaustion and still found that it was easy to catch up. Her  midterm was more like a reflection question, super easy!

Professor Narain is exceptional. Her seminar is highly engaging. She goes above and beyond to include videos, guest speakers, and thought-provoking in-class exercises. Her sense of humour is absolutely unmatched. She is available in office hours and provides detailed feedback in a timely manner. Her compassion and care for her students is clear.
Highly proficient in her field and exceptionally compassionate! She incorporates numerous discussion exercises, creating a refreshing learning environment that caters to various learning styles.

She's great and cares about the wellbeing of students even though her first impression might be a bit intimidating! She doesn't give high grades, but it's possible to get a decent grade with little effort. She's passionate about the subject matter and encourages a lot of discussion. I'd recommend her class!

A really kind prof, who will even check up on you if you miss many classes but also supports asynchronous learning if you choose. The class is extremely easy. Pretty sure the only grades she gave were B-, B and B+. Didn't attend at all in winter term + only studied about 5 hours for the exam. Essential class as it allows you to focus on other work.

Prof Narain is great. She's a very interesting lecturer who clearly knows what she's talking about in constitutional law. There is quite a bit of reading, which is too be expected, and she doesn't really go over the facts at hand. She clearly wants her students to succeed by setting aside class time for revision. Don't try to follow the powerpoint.

great guy! very open to student meetings and discussion, big on in-class participation and discussion. his quizzes can be difficult but the prompts for papers make up for it, very clear and a wide range to pick from. excited to take more with him :)

Took Prof. Kirby several years ago for a graduate seminar on Augustine's City of God. Among the most memorable professors I had while at McGill, Kirby remains in my top 3. I remember his course as being rigorous and invigorating (he is not for the faint of heart or the weak of mind), and I remember Kirby as approachable and extremely knowledgeable.

Class is purely discussion based. He appears to rely on the students as guiding the class time based on where the discussion goes. He does no lecturing. At times, that is not a helpful thing. Kirby can be quite encouraging though and is very willing to help when needed.
You could do better at McGill....
He certainly thinks a lot of himself...
This guy is not worth taking classes from

LOVED this course! So much interesting topics are covered and interesting guest speakers. It is such a well organized class with an amazing professor. Highly recommend!

I love this man. His explanations are somewhat muddled but his post-lecture review slides provide all the information you need. Do the assignments, and the tests are easy. The only complaint I might have is that we had no time for the midterm, but it was only worth 0-10 percent.
the most human professor

Great teacher. He posts all the slides which contains a lot of vital information. Pretty fun labs with cool TAs. I've really gotten a better intuition for electronics out of that class. He talks pretty fast, so just ask him to slow down if you didn't catch something.

Reisner is the most adorable prof you will ever have. He is very very prepared for his lectures, which he makes extra easy and presents the material with nice and clear presentations. Well prepared lectures. He is not always clear during the lectures, but his notes are clear (despite the bad hand-writing and the omnipresent mistakes). He really wants to help, but he doesn't have it. His hand-writting is really hard to read. He teaches the class since about 6 years and still have at least 4 typos per slides. The assignments are confusing and hard to understand. WHEN YOU RECEIVE YOUR GRADED EXAM, GO SEE HIM AND ASK WHY YOU LOST MARKS, AND YOU WILL REGAIN MANY POINTS!

Lectures are organised ok but he writes using a tablet on powerpoint, and his handwriting is very hard to read. His assignments are often messy and the questions complicated for no particular reason, often with paragraph long introdutions and very poor wording.

I love his lectures. He gives clear instructions and fun lectures
Best professor I have ever had, great lectures, very clear, very reachable, faster person to respond to emails, very funny. I wish I took every class he ever taught

He is one of the best profs at McGill! He is so fun to listen to and so knowledgable! You will learn a lot if you take this class, especially with him. Amazing prof. Very good lectures, examples and stories make the course so much better. Very good explanations, clear guidelines as to what is expected from us. 10/10 would recommend.

When I registered to this class I only did it because it was mandatory, now I am seriously thinking about taking more classes of Information System. He makes it so interesting, it's crazy ! I 100% recommend taking him.
He is a fantastic teacher who will make you love IS. Explains concepts really well and will be very helpful if you go to his office hours.

Warut is a wonderful prof! He's very passionate and caring. He can remember all of us and our names, which is truly impressive since he teaches so many students in several sections. And he's always available to answer questions.
Such a great prof! Very kind and funny, and makes boring topics very interesting. This class was not easy by any means, but was still very enjoyable.
This guy has a strong accent but it was not too bad. He invested a lot of his effort in the class and I respect him that. The exams, on the other hand, could use some improvement.

Prof. Sossin is a nice guy but he should retire. He seems to have lost his passion for teaching. His lectures are disorganized and he just reads off the slides. Sossin is one of the most genuine profs I've had. You can tell he is passionate about the material and giving students a clear (and real) picture of how research works...including the uncertainties.
