"I know you guys think I'm trying to make this very complicated, but I am actually trying to make it simpler than it is. It actually is really complicated."

Dr. Sossin is a nice person but not a great lecturer... He clearly knows his stuff really well but his lectures are messy and his explanations are often unclear. However, when I emailed him for questions he always replied quickly and gave very detailed answers.

I'm a U1 who hasn't taken molecular biology, and I've found his explanations clear and straightforward. He clearly makes an effort to engage the class, and he seems like a sweet guy. I had prof Sossin in ANAT 365, his lectures were clear, interesting and he was clearly passionate which really inspired me. He puts meme in his slides and they actually made me laugh. He was very available to talk about the essay. Overall a great prof.

I had Dr. Sossin for Neur310, and I thought he was actually quite clear, and made an obvious effort to both pare down the material and to engage the class. His questions on the final were tricky for sure, but he ultimately mostly tested the major concepts taught. People seem to dislike him in Psych, but for a more molecular class he was good!

Wayne Sossin may be the most unclear and disorganized professor at McGill. Teaching a PSYC course from the perspective of biochemistry is not helpful nor appropriate. Difficult concepts but doesn't explain them well. Leaves students with lots of confusion. His exam questions are very hard. One of the few inspiring professors I've had. A very thought provoking and gifted lecturer. Good sense of humor which emerged as the semester went on. Try to take his classes if you can. He's doing good and important work.

Awesome dude. Grading was really odd at times, and the TA grader wasn't introduced until two out of three of the papers had already been submitted with one returned. Fascinating lectures, though he repeats the same things and has no slides with bullets to keep him or the class on track. Very caring, learning everyone's names. Would take again.

Very kind, caring, intelligent and interesting professor. While lectures are interesting, they lack structure and clarity. Also, there is no TA for this class so you receive very little support. The grader for this class graded unclearly and oddly. Would definitely recommend as a professor though. Stellar guy.

Amazing professor. Stellar lectures that completely change your perspective on history. Extremely caring, accessible and thoughtful. Best professor I have ever had and would 100% take him again.

Not too much reading and only 2 assignments throughout the sem.

He is a really nice and smart man. His lectures were engaging but, they could be more structured to make note-taking easier, especially since he insists on handwritten notes in his class. Even though it was an intro class, I felt like we were expected to come in with prior knowledge which made it difficult. He prepares you well for the exams.
I loved 224. What you see is what you get. Prof. Adjetey's passion for the material is palpable. You can do well (if you show him you care about the work)

Professor Adjetey is a really interesting lecturer and is passionate about African Diaspora history. I looked forward to this class every week. It was honestly one of my highlights in the winter term. I appreciate that the professor brought his expertise and passion to each lecture even when he admitted he was feeling tired towards the end.

Prof Adjetey is delightful  I truly enjoyed learning about the history of the African Diaspora. His lectures were engaging and dynamic. The readings were demanding and sometimes hard to finish but I did learn a lot.
i usually don't write reviews on here, but prof. adjetey is the one of the best professors i have ever had. if you have the chance to take him you should, you'll see for yourself !!

I took the comparative medical law seminar, which is actually a bioethics class. Strange worldview
Somerville can be abrupt at times, but is absolutely brilliant.  She really challenges you to think outside the box.  She's very well known in her field AND a generous marker.

Prof. Folkerth is passionate and knowledgeable. His lectures are disorganized, but his enthusiasm keeps you engaged. Wes is genuinely an amazing professor. His lectures are engaging, passionate, and presented in a way that makes you excited to discuss the studied material in conference. Seems like a really sweet guy. He will remember your name. Lectures are a little disorganized and most of the exam material comes from them. Go to class to do well. Lots of reading but super sweet, knowledgeable, and cool guy :)

Very engaging prof, who makes Shakespeare's plays accessible. The tests are pretty tough, and good knowledge of the plays is necessary. But he does not want to trick students and there are no surprises if you attended class.
Fantastic. Very accommodating.

Wes Folkerth is a super sweet guy, but I did not enjoy this class. The lectures were boring and semi-disorganized, and the exams were unnecessarily difficult for a survey-level class. Such an amazing prof! he is hilarious and extremely passionate about the subject matter. he is a bit timid at times, but he definitely makes an effort to be engaging. midterm was tough (esp those passage ID's). listen in class & take thorough notes.

One of the nicest profs I've had. Very understanding and accommodating. Passionate about the content, although I sometimes wished we'd gone more in depth on a few of the texts. He does expect long essays for a 200 level class.

Good teacher overall. Difficult exams. Requires a lot of preparation. Use the textbook and do the modules. My only complaint is regarding AI use in exams. Not my favourite since we have to correct it. Overall I would still take this class again.

It's pathophysiology (aka quite a heavy subject). He tries to keep it interesting. No group work, no oral presentations (that was a plus for me). The exams are not easy, but there is ample tutoring time and office hours where either he, the other professor or the class mentors explain the material.
Heavy content, question doesn't reflect what is seen in class.

Look down. You see the two legs god has given you. Now use those legs to go to a library because this course will have you in shambles. You have to teach yourself. Also don't bother going to the lectures because it's an absolute waste of your time.

Honestly, one of the best profs Ive ever had! Knows what hes talking about, lectures are very enjoyable, he is passionate about what he teaches and is very caring towards his students. Minarik is an angel on earth, so lovely, passionate + caring, makes sure to reach out and make sure we were ok during the pandemic. He has cool rock collection.

Fantastic teacher, by far the best classes I have taken at McGill were with Prof. P. Interesting classes and wants you to learn something. Fair grader and fair exams, expects you to know the material, rightly so. Would definitely taken again.

Second class I've taken with Polushin. Easily my favorite courses in my business degree. There is no doubt he is a stickler for details and wants students to grasp the fundamentals. Some may dislike him, but listen intently in class and he will drop major hints for what will be tested on the exams.
Great prof!

Each class features a different old white man that gives a recycled presentation on a specific Asian country. Boring lectures paired with a lazy prof made the class a sleep fest. It had so much potential.

brilliant, knowledgeable, insightful. great speaker. best prof in desautels

This professor's judgement is very questionable.

Roberts is one of the best profs at McGill. Pretty difficult to understand during class, but it's not too bad if you study the material beforehand. Exams are relatively straightforward, just memorize and understand the topics he says are important in the slides/notes. Might be the sassiest prof on Ed I've ever seen.

Lectures are disorganized and very difficult to understand. No practice exams or practice problems are given, which makes it so hard to prepare for the exams.
I learned almost nothing and never felt engaged by this class.

This is a terrible class, the worst I've taken at McGill. The professor is impossible to understand and provides no practice questions for the exam at any point during the semester. Unless you learn by memorizing notes, stay away!

People like to complain about this class but his notes are the best and they have literally all the material you need to know. Assignments are not hard or long. A really nice and caring professor. Useful lectures with detailed explanations. One of the best prof I met at McGill.
Very passionate！

He gave really useful review sessions that prepare you sosososos well for midterm and final. Even though there is homework every 2 weeks, they are useful and he teaches very well. All the materials on midterm and final are from his slides!

Really great prof. Took his Comp 350 and Comp 540 in a row this year. The course materials for Comp 540 were pretty hard, but useful at the meantime. The final was much easier, although still require some effort. Overall, he was one of the best prof I've met in McGill.

took in fall 23. comp350 was very easy. notes had everything you need for the homeworks and exams. class was mostly matlab and matrix stuff. He is knowledgeable and tries his best to expand our horizons. The lectures include a bunch of areas in the food industry and some advanced technologies. The exam is in the form of multiple choice questions and the difficulty level is reasonable.
Really poor prof. Teaches with unorganized, unclear handwritten notes. Takes concepts that are relatively simple and massively overcomplicates. Not taught with the audience in mind.

Refuses to post lecture notes on the course page after 3 weeks of classes, and then wonders why the class average dropped down to 38% from 76%. Be ready to learn on your own, a lot.

Don't take this class with this prof, waste of time and energy.
The material itself isn't hard to understand and she did a good job explaining, but be ready to grind for quizzes/assignments every week.

Clear delivery and helpful feedback. Would definitely recommend this professor. 4 assignments, 1 small project (which is basically like the 5th assignment), plus a take-home exams (72-hour time window). I have no background in power systems but Prof. Wang has been extremely responsive and helpful.
I have no background in power engineering but this Prof. delivered great lectures and also offered additional materials for me to understand the matters better.
Just do what she asks of you, tests are not tricky as long as you study. Take her, power is easier with her

I have done very little physics in my high school and classes which are far from being related to electric machinery, the prof makes it very simple and easy to understand her lectures. Dr. Zhao is very passionate about the material. His passion is infused into his lectures which inspires wonder. Super nice teacher, just test are hard. Lots of material

to get an A, you have to know everything inside out. don't skip anything in his notes cuz even a tiny part on one slide can be on his exams. This class felt like a waste of time. If you want an easy A go for it, but at the cost of your morality. Google her name before taking her course. I wish I had.

She is a much better JWST prof than ENGL prof- but if you participate it is easy to do well. Make sure to engage in the material, she will appreciate it. I have had good experiences with her but it goes on a person-person basis (some people do not like her methods).
Her lectures were scattered and not prepared well. She was also very unpredictable, she blew up at me in front of everyone over something that wasn't a big deal.

Prof. Halevi-Wise is great! She just wants you to participate and try and if you do that you're good. She said she wanted everyone to get As by the end (idk if that happened). Side note: if you're doing 325 in the future sorry from our class we said she should add an essay.

I took this class purely because I thought it would be interesting and it absolutely was! ton of reading but very engaging class

Professor Halevi is very sweet and knowledgeable. I always enjoyed our class discussions and her selection of works. Professor Halevi did a great job of teaching online. Prof. Halevi-Wise is a real gem, in both the English Department and also McGill on the whole. I took POLI 368 With Prof Allard-Tremblay and was disappointed. The course content is great, but the professor is unfortunately not. One of the best professors I've ever had. While his material isn't the easiest, his passion for the subject makes it engaging and accessible. Great as a prof and very personable as well. Definitely knows his stuff and he lectures very well. Grading criteria was very clear and honestly assignment were not too difficult, but that said, I still feel like I learned a lot about democratic theory. Would 100% suggest taking one of his courses.

Amazing class but very work intensive if you pick the A bundle (grading is done on a bundle pass/fail basis). Once you understand the expectations it is straight forward.

I would recommend everyone to take INDG 200. Prof. Allard-Tremblay provided important insight to the material and while the lectures weren't super engaging, the readings, movies, and topics covered were great. With the bundle specifications grading, it is easy to get an A as long as you put in the work and stay on top of assignments.

I took INDG 200 at Mcgill with prof AllardTremblay and his lectures were by far the best I've ever had. He is extremely knowledgeable and you can really tell how much he cares. The work load is a lot but the assignments are interesting and I felt it was worth it considering how much work he puts in. I would highly urge everyone to take this course!
Class is non-mandatory but very interesting. Tremblay really makes you think and has immense knowledge within the field.

Amazing class and professor, and extremely necessary information to learn as a person residing in Canada. For fall 2021 we had 'specifications grading.' There were a series of assignments associated with a given grade, and if you complete all of them in the way he asks you too you get that grade. The assignments were thoughtful and engaging.

Not a harsh grader at all! Not sure what the other comments are talking about. Very generous grading scheme. If you do the work and study for the tests, you'll get an A. She brings candy for us every week. She's so accessible and helpful to students, she wants you to succeed. Strongly recommend the class!
She tries to control how you think.
She is not opened minded and tried to impose her thoughts to me. Didn't like her for that. Her Japanese was native and good.

A little homework each class. You don't learn new material everyday, lots of repetition. Though, revise kanji and vocab at home to keep up, kanji are tough and minor mistakes count. Very kind, very fun classes.

Intense class, but Senoo sensei cares a lot! Strict grader (b/c it's a language class) but gives good feedback. Accessible outside of class. Japanese is my favorite class of the day - very relaxing despite its intensity because Senoo sensei and the other students create a fantastic learning environment. Awesome prof!

Professor Senoo is a very sweet person and makes you feel comfortable in her class. She is a tough grader, but considering it's a language class, all of her corrections are productive and useful- she doesn't grade harshly just for the sake of it. She's also lenient with assignments and willing to work with you on anything you may struggle with!

Despite this year's class being held entirely online, Senoo-sensei was organized, kind, and caring. However, taking Japanese with her is a huge commitment. She is an extremely tough grader and will make sure to point out even the smallest of errors. If you're serious about learning Japanese and want a fun but tough teacher, look no further!

Senoo sensei is a good teacher, and she cares for her students. however, if you're expecting this to be an easy A, it won't be because she's quite strict on grading. She will deduct points for minor errors. Attendance is also definitely mandatory, and she expects full attention from her students. Overall, a good class!

Very very knowledgable and extremely organized. Class time is always used wisely and all expectations are clear. However, if you forget homework etc, don't give her excuses - she is not receptive when it comes to even misunderstandings. Tests are graded very straightforwardly but a bit harshly - make sure to spit out the textbook on the tests.

I don't know why the other reviews were so good. I took her property class on priority but honestly the class is presented in a confusing way with heavy focus on civil law. She doesn't seem to acknowledge when students are confused and gets defensive rather than finding a clearer way to answer. Her quiz questions were found to be ambiguous by many.
Clear, structured class material. Accessible for questions. Fair grader.
Somewhat boring at times but incredibly clear and structured. You can tell she's making an effort to be a bit more engaging
Her lectures are very dull and she doesn't delve much into cases or encourage class discussion. There were no comments or feedback on exams. Very continental approach-- memorize and regurgitate.

Fair marker, crystal-clear lectures and no b.s. Teaches you exactly what you need to know, then tests you on it. Doesn't let class discussion stray too far from the lesson (which is a good thing) and doesn't play favourites (also a good thing). Great class to take in French if you're an anglo. Best prof in 1L.
I had her in Torts. Very organized and clear, great use of powerpoints. I wish some teachers could model her way of conveying the course material.

The clearest and most fair prof you will find in McGill. There are no qualms, no frills, just pure comprehensible teaching, fair grading and great introductory exposure to law. Great prof to take in French if you're an anglo!!!
Great prof! Very clear. Exams are fair. Doesn't make things uselessly complicated.
Great professor! Very clear and organized. There is not a lot of readings. I suggest to do the optinal paper because the exam is long, but fair.

Took this class a couple of years ago. I believe I found that doing the homework really boosted my exam performance. The class had a relaxed vibe, and the professor was really approachable and friendly. Overall, it was a positive experience.
the prof is very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject, explains complex concepts in a way that's easy to understand overall the class is engaging and easy to do well in

Professor Simine was always helpful and approachable. Many of the teaching methods and labs were extremely engaging and the CHEM204 group on Slack made it very simple to reach out to her and other students if we had any questions.

Professor Simine was very clear when she taught in class and during office hours, but it was a flipped class and I studied mostly from her videos and the textbook. The minecraft minigame towards the end was a nice touch. The entire class was definitely worth it.

This was the only physics-related class I took last year but it may have been one of my favorite physics classes I've taken since. Professor Simine really cares about her students and she goes out of her way to help us and answer any questions that we have.

This class had of the best grading scheme with lots of easy marks to collect during the semester so the final didn't feel like there was a lot riding on it. I don't personally care about thermo but the prof was did a good job overall, her office hour immediately after class helped a lot.

I found Dr. Simine very easy to work with. She set up a Slack channel for our class and was always available to answer questions or provide helpful feedback/advice on classwork and assignments. I also found the presentation aspect of the class to be a fun and quick way to understand the topics we were discussing.

I found Prof. Simine's lecture notes easy to follow. The homework problems were fair, and always somewhat related to the topics covered in class. Even if some of them were more difficult, she was easily accessible outside of class to answer my questions, responding to emails and messages in a timely manner, which was very helpful during the term.

The absolute worst professor I have ever had. Makes an incredible amount of errors in both uploaded notes (that are both incomplete and unhelpful - have nothing to do with any graded material) and her classes. You must teach yourself any material that is to be graded - she even admits this. Avoid at all costs.

I cannot stress this enough. If you see Lena Simine's name, avoid that class. Take it at another term with a different professor. I have never seen a less competent teacher. She really does not belong to McGill. She would not even be suited to teach high school sciences. She might be a good scientist, but a horrible teacher.

Very nice professor. Class is tough so attendance needed. You also need to work regularly to follow up and start assignments early. Very caring and willing to help for course project/assignments! Highly recommand.

Very nice professor, caring of his students and answering/grading extremely quickly. Helps a lot for the research project/assignments. Tough class so you have to work regularly and attend the lectures.
Prof was great, I learned a lot of skills for doing research, need to put in effort in the research part.
The course title is misleading!

Very unclear. He tries to fit in too much depth for such a broad intro course. Also, classes and book are not "mandatory" but good luck understanding anything or doing assignments without them! Yi loves what he's teaching, but he fails to explain clearly, probably because of the shear amount of material he's trying to get across in each lecture.

Well...No one can deny his enthusiasm to meteorology and his effort to be funny, but he obviously over-estimates our ability for this introductory 200-level course. He is helpful, but his class is dull, filled with equations deriving. Assignments and exams are hard.

Explains content well, hard to follow along unless you annotate slides, as he moves through content very quickly. Hard to deal with outside of class, exams are extremely difficult, refuses to curve. Class average was below a 50 on the final. Take him if you have the time to spend multiple hours on practice problems every week. Harsh grader.

He is a super nice guy who gives good lectures and genuinely wants the students to succeed. It is very clear he wants us to understand the material, and he teaches in a way so we can apply it in exams. He also gives out lots of little quick assignments and HWs that are pretty much free marks. His exams are quite tough, but overall great prof.
This guy is goated. The material is hard, but he teaches super well. Exams are fair but hard and toughly graded but there are chances to offset this with labs, hw, and a few bonus credits.
really wants students to succeed. Really want us to understand the materials and always provide help. definitely would take  again

Decent lectures but great notes regardless. Only prof who gives 5 mins before starting class for you to settle in. Can be a bit hard to understand but not bad. Lots of little HW assignments but nothing crazy
Inspiring professor, very passionate and patient in teaching.
Great professor
The midterm was fair and enjoyable. The group discussions help the learning
Attendance matters, because you need to be able to be ready for pop quizzes, which are either really easy or impossible.
Great teacher, very kind and supportive

She talks too fast but slow at the same time, and it is also hard to catch up as she teaches the slides. It is much better to learn by yourself although she is there to help. Only came for Vevoxes, no class participation done though so that was nice.

Professor Yin Zhu was truly a great teacher. She made the basic concepts very accessible for people new to accounting and gave very clear explanations and examples in class to help us understand. Very accessible outside of class and super caring for our success. Just do all the exercises and listen well in class, a good grade is guaranteed.

Her slides and assigned textbook questions cover all the material on the midterm and final. If you understand those, you'll be fine. As for her lectures, she mostly just reads off the slides, so I found them unhelpful.
She doesn't know how to teach……..
A course without exams.
hes very nice ! and you can tell he really cares about the student. If you show up to class and do your work, you will do very well.

Dr. Wang is friendly and responds to emails very quickly, always available to help students even on the weekends and late at night or early morning. He focuses on student success and your grade will be distributed fairly among various assignments and a final term project. NO EXAMS!

Very helpful and replies to my emails quickly. He just goes through example problems in the textbook during class and exams are very similar to the examples. Class attendance is not necessary if you can solve the problems on your own. Go to 1-on-1 session if you're having trouble!
The teacher is nice
Dr. Wang is really nice and alway available for help. He genuinely cares about students. His class is fun and he never tricks you in the exam. Highly recommend!
Super nice
Dr. Wang is one of the best professors I have had during my four years of university. He is easy to talk to, and his course material is very informative.

Rao's lectures seemed incomprehensible while you're in them, but after reviewing for the final they actually weren't bad at all. He doesn't use slideshows which is annoying at best, but his topics were pretty simple. He doesn't do a good job of emphasizing what is important, what the key topics are, and what you should take away from the lecture.
Worst professor ever at McGill. Moves fast through lectures and does not care to explain in response to questions
Just average, not great
Not your best option for MGCR211. Take it with a diff prof.

Prof Roh was one of the best profs I had at Mcgill! He is so kind & supportive, and really cares about his students in and outside of class. Definitely go to office hours if ur struggling with the course & put effort in class. I went into the course nervous but ended up loving accounting, and I would say having him as a prof played a big part!

Prof. Roh is one of the best professors I've had so far. His lectures are clear and he's available outside of class to help. There are questions in class for participation credit and HW is graded based on effort. He is also honest about the difficulty level of exams. I have nothing bad to say about him. Highly recommend.

Prof. Roh is able to give clear and detailed lectures! Two midterms and a final, I recommend doing the sample exams given as they are the clearest representation of the exam. Questions given in class for participation credit, homeworks are graded based on effort.

Highly recommend Professor Roh! He holds regular office hours, but apart from that, he is very quick to respond to emails and gives detailed answers. He is also honest about the difficulty level of exams compared to the samples (e.g., the first midterm was more challenging than the sample, the second was easier, etc.). HW is graded based on effort.

The best prof for this course! It's a tough class but he explains every concept very well, is available outside of class to help, and has a good sense of humour which makes the lectures engaging. You have to put in a lot of work to get a good grade as it's a content heavy class, but if you do, then it's a lot of fun.

His explanations are always clear and logical, and the course is very well structured, which makes complex concepts much easier to understand. He is also approachable, responsible, and has a great sense of humor, which makes lectures engaging.

One of the best introductory courses I've taken. Highly recommend.

Prof Roh is just amazing! I genuinely have nothing bad to say. I am so so glad I decided to take accounting with him, it ended up being my favourite class at Desautels so far! His lectures are clear & office hours are amazing. He's caring and wants his students to succeed. You obv need to put in effort but once you do he is there to support you
Confusing slides

Genuinely had to teach myself the entirety of her content for this course she was so unclear and didn't really cover anything relevant to the exams. I have to admit she was hilarious and often called people out in class or had some pretty good one-liners but overall I would avoids her if I could.

It was quite clear that this class wasn't one of her priorities, which is a shame, because she gives clear feedback during Q&A in class and she is very dynamic. There were many gaps in content in her lectures. For her section, it was far more helpful to finish the workbook questions and do the practice midterms, as well as use 3rd party websites.

Terrible. Had to learn ALL post-midterm content outside of class. Lecture slides were filled with random information about the synthesis of bioorganic molcules that had no relevance to OChem1. If you have her for 212, use websites outside of class to practice — the style of questions on the final are similar to midterm and is manageable.

I did not attend her lectures after the first week and relied on the OERs which was far more helpful. I am not sure how she can get away with creating such a negative, unorganized environment, especially after Sirjoosingh does so much to help us out. Clearly super knowledgable, just incredibly belittling and disrespectful.
I was doing so well in this course until she started teaching.

Clearly very smart but her teaching skills are lacking. Flies through content with confusing slides. Would always snap at students just asking for clarification, saying they are not watching the lecture recordings and should pay more attention. Scared to ask her anything! Made an unwelcoming environment and was difficult to learn content from.

This is one of the worst profs I've had in my life. She does not know how to teach, she is always yelling and seems visibly annoyed when students ask questions. She acts as if we are a burden to her and also gives no practice. She claims that the in-class practice is enough. Her annotations on the slides look like a toddler scribbled on them.

Slides make no sense and have no explanations for her practice questions. She cannot explain concepts; you will leave every lecture confused, guaranteed. Will also snap at you if you ask a question she doesn't understand. She treats teaching CHEM 212 as if it were a chore your parent asked you to do growing up.

Its obvious she's very smart, but she's NOT qualified to be a prof. Her lectures makes no sense, she goes on tangents ALL the time,never fully explain processes, gets annoyed when people ask questions for clarification and even her practice problems answers barely explain why/ what the process is.I see why she wasn't teaching this class for 10years

Professor Ma is a very kind and cares about his students. He delivers lectures with extremely clear slides that have all relevant information on them. He explains the lessons in depth and goes through example applications of the concepts. He is always willing to answer questions and is also very funny. The class was very well organized.

Professor Yu is an expert in the subject he teaches. Marketing analytics is such a useful course to any marketing student. The class is content heavy but the professor does a great job explaining everything in the lecture. The class is very fast-paced, but the professor is highly accessible outside of class and he has a great sense of humour too!

Ma is unfriendly and unclear during lectures. This class is made unnecessarily difficult when the content is not inherently hard. Super low midterm average. Your grade is almost arbitrarily decided by a confusing game you play. Once you mess up in the game, youve practically stuck yourself with a bad grade in the class. Avoid if possible.
the best cs teacher in McGill, very clear organized, everyone should take his comp551, that did help

Great prof great course. He explains things clearly and seems like he cares about his students - class was given multiple extensions for assignments. This is a 4 credit 500 level course so there is a lot of content - be ready to work hard for this class

5/5 lectures. Hard to rate difficulty. Assignments took me ages but have 95 averages. Exams are weird: about 60% is stupid easy and about 40% is pretty tricky, no "medium" questions. It's a bit tough to get an A (but still common), and it's super easy to get a decent grade. Overall this course took me more time than most cs courses, so I gave a 4.

Li is the best cs prof I have had a McGill. Lectures are dense,  but I came into the class with 0 ml knowledge and left with a strong basis. Midterm and final are a bit tough and completely open book- ended up printing all the slides and using them on the final. Assignments are more data sciency and you work in groups of 3, but doable to do alone.

Really good course but an absolute fire hose of material from the jump. Course is hard to fail due to tests making up so little of your grade. Assignments are much more like a lab than a traditional computer science assignment. Also tests are open book so legitimately bring all the slides printed out bc there's just too much material too have down.

This is easily the best Professor I had in McGill so far. Everything is well organized, he does all the minute details to make sure the students can understand the concept (repeating questions, explaining every operation in proofs, giving lots of examples, etc..).
Prof Li is a great lecturer, super considerate of his students, and overall very kind. His exams were quite fair despite the difficulty of the content. Highly recommend him for COMP 551!
It's hard to explain complex things in simple words and this Prof knows how to do it. Highly recommended!

tbh those giving him bad ratings in for comp 551 are just mad they didn't do well in this class. Its a 4 credit 500-level class, of course its not easy and a lot of work. His lectures are great. He has really nice slides and he is always available. Overall, great teacher. Just a really hard class.

machine learning comp551 is a very useful course but also very difficult , but he explained the concept very well . 
the midterm was a bit tough.
One of the nicest profs at mcgill. Super sweet, very easy A

Prof. Furuhata is very kind and it is evident that she cares a lot about her students. The class was moderately reading-heavy, but her lectures were incredible and I came away mindblown each time. An A is totally doable if you keep up with the material, but don't take 212 as a "bird" course - it's not. However, it was 100% worth the effort imo!!
Professor Furuhata's classes are interesting and very straight forward in every aspect. I strongly recommend!

Tbh this class shouldn't be called "introduction to asian media studies". The stuff is certainly NOT intro. It takes time to digest in class and is quite hard even for an Asian student honestly. Lots of things to memorize and understand. It involves heavy on history and philosophy. The prof is fine but the accent is not easy to follow sometimes.

Really good prof. Her lectures are really interesting and fun to attend. Some readings to do fo every class but it's doable if you don't start at the last minute. Attendance taken 5 times and taken into consideration for the final grade. Non cumulative quizzes, not that hard if you took good notes during the lectures and understood the readings.

Really nice professor who is really passionate in what she is teaching. She tries to entertain and make everyone smile and happy at the end of each class. The questions on the exams, are a bit tricky to answer but also not impossible. If you study the for the exam enough, you'll pass. Not an easy A, but fair.
Very caring and kind professor. Passionate, well-organized, and worth visiting in office hours.

Prof. Furuhata really made the most of a difficult three-hour time slot. She included lots of pictures, video, and references to pop culture in her Powerpoints. She was very approachable and encouraged class participation. The readings / quizzes were pretty cumbersome, though, so be careful. Overall, awesome class!
Great course with an interesting "hands on" component you don't often see at McGill (a film making project). Furuhata is funny, kind, and extremely intelligent.

One of my favourite undergraduate courses. EAST 250 was a well rounded introduction to east asian media studies, spanning from pre-modern technologies to sprit media, idol groups, futuristic architecture, and new media. I loved this course and the way the work was assigned.
Simply one of the best and most understanding teachers I've met during my entire education, on top of being an excellent and engaging lecturer! The kind of teaching experience you'll remember forever

I found prof. Winter's lectures easy to follow because he goes slowly so you can tell from which point he is going on to the next. You need to attend lectures so you can participate in conferences. There were only 2 assignments and they were worth A LOT but the readings weren't heavy. He was one of the best POLI profs I've had.

The only thing that made this class more challenging is the lecture recordings. In other words, you wouldnt know exactly when the professor is going from one idea to the next. Readings were heavy, but veey interesting. Class participation and discussion really helped to understand the topic being studied. TAs were more helpful in my opinion.
amazing professor who truly cares about his students!
My favorite professor at McGill and so incredibly smart! He's an amazing lecturer and always makes his courses super interesting. Totally recommend! A lot of work for sure, but you will learn a lot.

Really great lecturer but has incredibly high (unrealistic?) expectations for papers (3 papers are worth 90% of grade). Tons of reading since it's political theory (ranges from 50 to 200 pages per lecture). Really interesting course material.
He is really kind and professional

If you think ECSE420 could be interesting, well its not when professor Zeljko is teaching. After the first class maybe 5-8 people showed up to class (out of 300). He seems nice, but his teaching style sucks. Slides are horrible, but class is relatively easy as long as you do the labs and assignments. Its an easy class, but you won't learn a thing!
Prof. Zilic is very kind and understanding. He will provide with what you need to get through with your assignmnets and peojects

I was expecting to learn about VLSI-Testing, but surprise! the course was about Android Programming! But at the first lecture he cleared that out and I think in the coming years it would be a separate course!  But I really liked the way he taught us and I personally love doing projects instead of exams and this course was all about doing projects.
Nicest engineering prof and passionate about the subject. Too bad I went to class only once.
Don't attend the lectures, it's a waste of time. Textbook was also useless. The midterm was fair (questions were similar to the assignments) and the project was straightforward.
Great course and really nice professor. The material taught was extremely useful for microprocessor design. Definitely a "must do" course!
The closest material to what I need now that I started by well-paid job. The nicest professor at ECE.
No Comments

This lab course gets you all imporant material you need to know as EE or CE. I got to appreciate that only when hit with the real world job, where just about all the exercises from this course were right on.
a very very nice and patient teacher! recommend everyone choose his courses!
His powerpoints are very clear and helpful for studying. He explains in detail the content. The exams are fair and cover well the material covered in class.
Strongly recommend his class, a lot of assignments but really helpful in the final exams
Great guy. Lectures are a bit stale but good enough. Exams are not too hard. Assignment heavy. overall great professor.

Prof. Qi is a great guy! However, his lectures are long and are very focused on deriving the equations we use in the many homework assignments. I wish there was more time on lecturing and less time writing out equations. He prints out hand written equation sheets that are very useful. Good guy, but the class needs some work in my opinion.
One of the best profs at McGill! She explains things very clearly and really encourages you to practice your Russian skills in class.
Prof Kadyrbekova is fabulous, maybe a little intimidating at first, but she is genuinely the kindest professor I've ever had.
Favourite professor at McGill so far. Super caring!

Zora is very reliable and understanding. She's quite demanding, there is a lot of homework and the pace of lessons is fast. My one issue was that her lessons were really boring and repetitive, she follows the golosa textbook to the letter and never really encourages you to speak Russian outside of narrow grammatical questions.

Zora is a true gem. RUSS 210 was my hardest First-Year course but also the most rewarding. The class seems extremely difficult and impossible at the beginning, but with focus, practice, and Zora's help, anyone can do well. I learned more Russian in than any other course I took beforehand. Zora is charismatic and extremely caring about her students.

Zora is an amazing prof with an organized and well-prepared class. I took the class as an intensive class during summer - without any prior knowledge of the language and I'm not gonna lie, it was the hardest class I've ever had. We basically did one chapter a day and I had to study countless hours on my own. Very rewarding but be prepared to work
took 400 and 401 with her. she is fine, very understanding, easy on grading too.

Had her for Elem.1 and for two advanced courses. Loved it. Be prepared to work, but - be prepared to learn a lot as well. SHe's fun and very knowledgeable, if can't answer a question, will always get back with an answer. Outside the class - always available & ready to help w/anything. Very understanding. Wish could take other classes with her.

Prof. Kadyrbekova is an excellent instructor. She explains grammar very clearly and is organized. As demanding as she can be, she's very understanding & will help u every step of the way. Bc she demanded so much, I learned more in her class than in all preceding classes combined. Def. would recommend & would take a class with her.

I had Zora for my Elem. Russian, too. She is a great teacher. It's true she is demanding, but she is there to help you with everything. Very understanding. Her high expectations can really inspire and push you to learn more. She can also be funny. Explains everything clearly and a very fair grader. Offers extra credit which can really help.

He is nice but BORING. I honestly could not go to class after 1 month just to listen to him read his slides in front of us. Midterm was graded toughly, TA's not an easy grader..but the final was fine. Get ready to learn everything about Quebec's history in 4 months. It's doable to succeed in his class if you're consistent with your work.

His a very reachable and a good lecturer. Sure he is boring but he explains well the subjects. I did not like that all our grade was based on two essay exams. No need to do all the readings just he tells you which ones would be needed for the exam (long readings tho).

He explained everything very clearly and gave hints of things to study for the exams. If you're from Québec this class will be easy, most of the stuff covered is either events we learned in highschool or basic facts of QC politics. Only downside: it's only graded on 2 exams, but you get 2 chances for midterms and only the highest grade is kept.

Prof.Bélanger is a great professor! Very clear lectures, leaving space for debate and often asking for students' opinions/questions while teaching. He's very caring and provided space for students to get involved in his research chair on democracy multiple times. Despite seeming (and at times being) monotonous, he's very accessible and passionate.

went to class like twice currently failing 36% on midterm do not take this class if u are lazy, readings are horrifically long, i had this class at 8 in the morning and oh my god this is not a class u can take at 8 in the morning his monotone voice and blank expression had me zzzing if ur into quebec sure why not but im not rly so idk why i took it

His lectures are amazing and to the point. I was excited to go to class. He allows for a lot of conversation where you can give your opinion about the topics. It is hard to get good grades because you have to be specific in the exams and in the paper but the grader also makes errors and you can get a lot of points back by asking for a regrade.

Disappointing overall. Students led the entire class, readings were outdated, and he seemed rather apathetic generally. Very monotone. He's clearly very intelligent, it just seemed like he couldn't care less.

My experience may be different because this class is a small seminar-style one as opposed to the larger POLI 2XX courses that people are saying he gave dull lectures in. But in this setting, I thought he was a super nice professor who lead great discussions and assigned very interesting readings, and a chill workload. Big recommend for POLI 336.

Wow I've never had a more boring professor. He speaks entirely in monotone, mutters, and is vaguely standoffish as well. I took his class on Quebec provincial politics and couldn't stay awake, even during his Zoom lectures. However, I'm not a francophone and I'm not from Quebec, so I'm not the normal demographic for this class.

I found Prof. Belanger very dull. No powerpoints or class material to work off of. His lectures are him reading hand-written notes. Very monotonous voice, tough to follow because it gets boring. If you put in the work you'll get a decent grade -- very niche.
